hypotheses.mechanism: Src tyrosine-phosphorylates TβRII and this phosphorylation enhances TβRII kinase activity (derynck2019:findings:013), while TGF-β signalling in TCR-transgenic CD4+ T cells blunts IFN-γ (and IL-2/IL-4) production and imposes antigen-specific unresponsiveness without increasing apoptosis (chen2003:findings:002), an IFN-γ-suppressive state that is transferable to other T cells in vivo (chen2003:findings:019). If Src sets the gain of TβRII, then Src activity should be rate-limiting for how strongly TGF-β suppresses IFNG, making SRC an inverse regulator of IFNγ output; Src is a highly active tyrosine kinase whose activity is directly reportable and manipulable in cells (gest2024:findings:208).
hypotheses.prediction: Inhibiting or removing Src kinase activity in CD4+ T cells should reduce TβRII tyrosine phosphorylation and downstream TGF-β signalling and thereby restore IFN-γ production and proliferation in TGF-β-treated cells (partial rescue of the TGF-β-imposed IFNγ block), whereas expressing constitutively active Src should deepen IFNγ suppression at sub-saturating TGF-β; in the absence of TGF-β, Src manipulation should have little effect on IFNγ, making the effect TGF-β-dependent rather than a general activation defect.
hypotheses.test: Stimulate cultured CD4+ T cells (or an IFNG-reporter T cell line) through CD3/CD28 with a TGF-β dose range while (i) treating with a Src-family kinase inhibitor or vehicle, (ii) knocking down SRC by siRNA/CRISPR, and (iii) expressing constitutively active versus kinase-dead Src; read out IFN-γ by ELISA/intracellular staining, and in parallel immunoprecipitate TβRII and blot for phosphotyrosine and for phospho-SMAD2/3. A Src-dependent shift in the TGF-β dose–response for IFN-γ that tracks with TβRII tyrosine phosphorylation supports the hypothesis; unchanged TβRII pTyr and unchanged TGF-β dose–response with preserved PMA/ionomycin-driven IFN-γ would rule it out.

citations.title: Src phosphorylates Tyr284 in TGF-beta type II receptor and regulates TGF-beta stimulation of p38 MAPK during breast cancer cell proliferation and invasion.
The Src family kinase inhibitors PP2 and PP1 block TGF-beta1-mediated cellular responses by direct and differential inhibition of type I and type II TGF-beta receptors.
Inhibitors of Src-family tyrosine kinases favour Th2 differentiation.
TGF-beta abrogates TCR-mediated signaling by upregulating tyrosine phosphatases in T cells.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the mechanism in plain words (Src tyrosine-phosphorylation of TβRII enhancing TGF-β receptor activity), the entities together (Src/SFK inhibitors + TGF-β + CD4 T cells + IFN-γ), and the prediction (SFK inhibition or SRC knockdown restoring IFN-γ in TGF-β-suppressed T cells, including CRISPR-screen literature). The upstream half of the mechanism is well published outside T cells — Src phosphorylates TβRII on Tyr284 and thereby redirects/enhances receptor output (PMID 17440088), and Src-family inhibitors PP2/PP1 block TGF-β1 responses, though largely by directly inhibiting TβRI/TβRII rather than via Src (PMID 21395548). I found nothing stating that SRC acts as an upstream gain-setter for TβRII in T cells to enforce an IFN-γ-low state; the nearest T-cell work runs the other way, with SFK inhibitors reducing IFN-γ and favouring Th2 (PMID 10209068) and with TGF-β itself suppressing Lck/Fyn/ZAP-70 via phosphatases (PMID 11236902), so the specific prediction and the corpus-to-corpus connection are unpublished.

hypotheses.statement: CDK1 directly phosphorylates canonical ERK-consensus proline-directed sites, making it a bona fide cross-reactive kinase for ERK substrates (including the Cdc25-derived EKAR peptide) rather than a kinase with fully disjoint specificity from ERK.
hypotheses.mechanism: gest2024 states that the Cdc25-derived substrate peptide used as the ERK readout in EKAR is phosphorylated by Cdk1, and that only two engineered substrate mutations (EKAREN4/5) separate the two activities, which implies CDK1 acts on the same acceptor site ERK is assayed on; bekkerjensen2020 defines the ERK1/2 motif as Px[s/t]P, a proline-directed motif of the same class CDK1 recognizes, and sang2022 shows Cdk1 will phosphorylate peptides lacking its primary specificity determinants (P53 S9/S37, RPS6 S235/236) when its local concentration on a substrate is raised. Together these imply overlap at the level of individual phosphoacceptor sites, so ERK-motif sites are directly available to CDK1 whenever CDK1 activity is high or co-localized with the substrate.
hypotheses.prediction: Purified CDK1/cyclin B should phosphorylate the unmutated EKAR/Cdc25 peptide and other Px[s/t]P ERK-consensus peptides in vitro, and in cells a CDK1 inhibitor (or CDK1 depletion) should reduce a fraction of the FRET signal reported by original EKAR/EKAR-EV — particularly in G2/M cells — while leaving the EKAREN5 signal and pERK(T202/Y204) immunostaining essentially unchanged; conversely, MEK inhibition should collapse the EKAREN5 signal fully but leave a residual CDK1-dependent component in original EKAR.
hypotheses.test: Side-by-side in vitro kinase assay with recombinant CDK1/cyclin B and active ERK2 on synthetic wild-type EKAR (Cdc25) peptide versus the EKAREN4/5 mutant peptide and a set of Px[s/t]P peptides, read out by phospho-specific blot or radiolabel incorporation; then in the same cell line express EKAR-EV and EKAREN5 in parallel and image FRET during titration of a selective CDK1 inhibitor (e.g. RO-3306) versus a MEK inhibitor, with matched pERK immunofluorescence as the kinase-independent control.

citations.title: Quantifying single-cell ERK dynamics in colorectal cancer organoids reveals EGFR as an amplifier of oncogenic MAPK pathway signalling.
Distinct pools of cdc25C are phosphorylated on specific TP sites and differentially localized in human mitotic cells.
CDK2 activity crosstalk on the ERK kinase translocation reporter can be resolved computationally

novelty.note: I searched for EKAREN4/EKAREN5 and CDK1 cross-reactivity, for CDK1/ERK overlapping proline-directed substrate specificity, and for the Cdc25C T48 site used as the EKAR substrate. Ponsioen et al. (Nat Cell Biol 2021, the source of EKAREN4/5) explicitly state that the CDC25C-derived substrate sequence in EKAREV is phosphorylated by CDK1/cyclin B, show an ~80% mitotic FRET rise persisting under MEK/ERK inhibition, show RO-3306 collapses that signal in G2/M, and show two substrate mutations (K424P, K426W) reduce it to ~11% while preserving ERK responsiveness — i.e. the hypothesis's mechanism and essentially its in-cell prediction are already published. The in vitro arm is also covered: purified Cdk1/cyclin B phosphorylates Cdc25C T48 (the EKAR acceptor site, also reported as an ERK2 site), and a 2025 Cell Systems study generalises CDK-on-ERK-reporter crosstalk, documenting the prior CDK1 reports and the absence of such crosstalk on EKAREN5.

hypotheses.statement: CDK1 activity directly attenuates ERK pathway activation, imposing a cell-cycle-dependent brake that contributes to the intrinsic on/off pulsing of ERK.
hypotheses.mechanism: good2011 shows that Cdk1 phosphorylation of the Ste5 MAPK scaffold's membrane-binding helix blocks scaffold recruitment to the plasma membrane and attenuates MAPK signaling once cells commit to Start, i.e. CDK1 can switch a MAPK cascade off by acting on a scaffold upstream of the MAP kinase. albeck2013 shows that ERK activity in growth-factor-saturated cells is nonetheless intermittent, with pulsing preserved under saturating EGF and therefore generated by intracellular machinery rather than ligand fluctuation, and that ERK pulse length changes systematically with position in the cell cycle in sister-cell pairs. A CDK1-imposed, cell-cycle-phased inhibition of receptor-to-ERK coupling would supply exactly such an intracellular, cycle-correlated off-switch.
hypotheses.prediction: Acute CDK1 inhibition or CDK1 knockdown should increase the fraction of time ERK is 'on' (longer pulses, shorter dormant intervals) and raise the pERK-positive fraction at fixed EGF, with the largest effect in G2/M cells; conversely, driving CDK1 activity (e.g. WEE1 inhibition) should shorten ERK pulses and lower the pERK-positive fraction without changing EGFR surface ligand availability.
hypotheses.test: In MCF-10A cells at steady-state EGF, treat with RO-3306 or siRNA against CDK1 and measure ERK activation directly by pERK(T202/Y204) high-content immunofluorescence (bimodal fraction and 'on'-peak intensity) plus EKAREN5 FRET time-lapse to score pulse duration and interval, in each case co-staining a cell-cycle marker so the effect can be assigned to CDK1-active cells; follow with an in vitro kinase assay testing whether CDK1/cyclin B phosphorylates the membrane-binding region of the mammalian ERK scaffold KSR1 and whether that phosphorylation reduces its membrane/Raf association in a pull-down.

citations.title: Cdc2-mediated inhibition of epidermal growth factor activation of the extracellular signal-regulated kinase pathway during mitosis.
Phosphorylation of MEK1 by cdk5/p35 down-regulates the mitogen-activated protein kinase pathway.
Cell cycle dependence of ERK activation dynamics is regulated by PI3K and PAK1 signaling.

novelty.note: I searched for CDK1/cdc2-mediated attenuation of MAPK signaling, for cell-cycle-dependent ERK activation dynamics in single cells, and for any link between CDK1 and intrinsic ERK pulsing. The mammalian version of the mechanism is already published: Dangi & Shapiro (JBC 2005) show EGF fails to activate ERK in mitotic cells, that Cdc2/CDK1 phosphorylates Sos-1 and Raf-1 (i.e. acts upstream of MEK1, not downstream), and that CDK inhibition with roscovitine restores EGF- and PMA-induced ERK activation — essentially the predicted direction of the CDK1 inhibition experiment; CDK-family phosphorylation of MEK1 Thr286 (cdk5/p35, JBC 2002) is a further published instance of CDK-to-MEK/ERK inhibition. What I could not find is any source connecting this brake to the intrinsic on/off pulsing of ERK or to cell-cycle-phased pulse length; the nearest work on cell-cycle dependence of ERK dynamics (Sci Rep 2025) attributes it to PI3K/PAK1 and reports ERK becoming more sustained in S-G2M, and makes no CDK1 claim, so the specific pulsing prediction and the good2011/albeck2013 connection remain unstated.

hypotheses.statement: PTEN directly negatively regulates mTORC1 activity, acting as an upstream suppressor whose lipid (PIP3) phosphatase activity is required to keep the TSC2–Rheb–mTORC1 axis in the off state.
hypotheses.mechanism: PTEN is characterized as a PIP3 3-phosphatase opposing PI3K (manning2017:findings:002, maehama1998:findings:003) and, when expressed in cells, reduces exactly the subset of Akt-dependent TSC2 phosphopeptides that insulin/PI3K signalling induces and increases TSC2 electrophoretic mobility (inoki2002:findings:008, inoki2002:findings:007). The mTORC1 side of the corpus states that Akt-mediated phosphorylation inactivates the TSC1/TSC2 Rheb-GAP, stabilizing GTP-bound RHEB and activating mTORC1 (laplante2012:findings:002, haeusler2018:findings:027), and that persistent mTORC1 output is what sustains signalling in PI3K-pathway-mutant cells (fruman2017:findings:010). Taken together, loss of PTEN's lipid phosphatase function (the activity selectively destroyed by G129E, balla2013:findings:045) should leave TSC2 phosphorylated and mTORC1 constitutively active, making PTEN a direct negative regulator of mTORC1.
hypotheses.prediction: Re-expression of wild-type PTEN in PTEN-null cells will lower mTORC1 substrate phosphorylation (phospho-S6K1 Thr389, phospho-4E-BP1 Ser65, phospho-S6) and shift TSC2 to its faster-migrating, hypophosphorylated form, whereas the lipid-phosphatase-dead G129E (and catalytically dead PTEN-CS) mutants will not; conversely, acute PTEN knockdown in PTEN-intact cells will raise mTORC1 substrate phosphorylation and render it partially insensitive to growth factor withdrawal, while leaving amino-acid/methionine-dependent inputs (e.g. SAMTOR-mediated, gu2017:findings:011) intact.
hypotheses.test: In a PTEN-null cell line (and in isogenic PTEN-intact cells), doxycycline-inducibly express wild-type PTEN, PTEN-G129E (lipid-dead, protein-phosphatase-intact) or PTEN-C124S, then serum-starve and restimulate with insulin and immunoblot a time course of phospho-S6K1 Thr389, phospho-4E-BP1 Ser65 and phospho-AKT, plus a TSC2 mobility shift (± λ phosphatase) and FLAG-S6K1 immunoprecipitation kinase assay; pair this with siRNA/CRISPR PTEN loss-of-function in PTEN-intact cells, and epistasis controls (TSC2 knockout, or constitutively active RHEB) to test whether PTEN's effect on mTORC1 is abolished when the TSC2–RHEB step is bypassed — no suppression by wild-type PTEN, or equal suppression by G129E, would rule out the proposed PTEN→mTORC1 inhibitory relationship.

citations.title: Enhanced sensitivity of PTEN-deficient tumors to inhibition of FRAP/mTOR.
Identification of the tuberous sclerosis complex-2 tumor suppressor gene product tuberin as a target of the phosphoinositide 3-kinase/akt pathway.

novelty.note: I searched for PTEN loss causing constitutive mTORC1 activation, for PTEN re-expression lowering S6K1/S6 phosphorylation, and for PTEN/TSC2/Akt epistasis. Neshat et al. (PNAS 2001) directly state the explanation: PTEN loss correlates with elevated S6 kinase activity and rpS6 phosphorylation, PTEN overexpression blunts serum-induced S6 kinase activity, and myr-Akt activates S6K in an mTOR-dependent manner; Manning et al. (Mol Cell 2002) show Akt-dependent tuberin phosphorylation is constitutive in PTEN-/- cells, completing the PTEN→Akt→TSC2→mTORC1 link. The hypothesis is therefore long-published rather than novel; only the specific G129E lipid-dead comparison at the mTORC1 readout is a detail variation.

hypotheses.statement: TGFBR2 (TβRII) kinase activity is directly required upstream for TGF-β-induced STAT3 tyrosine phosphorylation and STAT3-dependent transcription, placing TβRII as an activator of STAT3.
hypotheses.mechanism: TGF-β-induced STAT3 activation is reported to occur through JAK1 constitutively bound to TβRI, independently of Smads (derynck2019:findings:034), yet TβRI only becomes signaling-competent after transphosphorylation by a kinase-active TβRII, since no downstream effector association occurs with kinase-defective type II receptors (macassilva1996:findings:001) and TβRII autophosphorylation at Ser213/Ser409 is essential for signaling while Ser416 phosphorylation is inhibitory (hata2016:findings:002). If the ligand-proximal kinase step resides in TβRII, then the JAK1–STAT3 arm branching from TβRI should inherit a strict dependence on TβRII catalytic activity and on its activating autophosphorylation sites.
hypotheses.prediction: TGF-β should induce STAT3 Tyr705/Tyr705-equivalent phosphorylation and STAT3 reporter/target-gene activity only in cells with catalytically active TβRII: TβRII-deficient or TβRII-depleted cells, and cells reconstituted with kinase-dead or Ser213/Ser409-to-Ala TβRII, should lose the rapid Smad-independent p-STAT3 wave (while retaining IL-6-driven p-STAT3), whereas the phospho-mimetic/activating TβRII forms should restore or amplify it; a Ser416 phospho-mimetic should blunt it.
hypotheses.test: In a TβRII-null cell line (or TβRII-knockdown fibroblasts/hepatic stellate-like cells), stably re-express wild-type TβRII, kinase-dead TβRII, S213A/S409A, and S416D mutants, then stimulate with TGF-β and immunoblot for p-STAT3 (with p-SMAD2 as a pathway control and IL-6 as a TβRII-independent positive control) alongside a STAT3-luciferase reporter and qPCR of STAT3 targets; co-immunoprecipitate JAK1/TβRI complexes in each background, and confirm specificity with a JAK1 inhibitor and with TβRI kinase inhibition to separate the TβRII requirement from TβRI catalytic activity.

citations.title: Transforming Growth Factor-β (TGF-β) Directly Activates the JAK1-STAT3 Axis to Induce Hepatic Fibrosis in Coordination with the SMAD Pathway.
Regulation of TGF-β receptor activity.
Loss of transforming growth factor-beta type II receptor promotes metastatic head-and-neck squamous cell carcinoma.

novelty.note: I searched for TGF-β-induced STAT3 phosphorylation with receptor-kinase requirements, for the JAK1–TβRI–STAT3 axis, and for TβRII (TGFBR2) manipulations (knockdown/knockout, kinase-dead, Ser213/Ser409/Ser416 autophosphorylation mutants) tied to p-STAT3. The component mechanisms are published separately: Tang et al. (JBC 2017) show a rapid Smad-independent STAT3 phosphorylation driven by JAK1 constitutively bound to TβRI and show it is abolished by TβRI knockdown or SB431542, while reviews state that TβRII kinase activity transphosphorylates and activates TβRI and that Ser213/Ser409 autophosphorylation is essential and Ser416 inhibitory — but no retrieved source tests TβRII-deficient, kinase-dead, or Ser-mutant TβRII for STAT3 Tyr705 phosphorylation or STAT3 reporter activity, and the nearest in vivo TβRII-loss work associates TβRII deletion with (rather than loss of) STAT3 activation. Hence the specific prediction and the TβRII→STAT3 connection are not established.

hypotheses.statement: mTORC2 directly suppresses proteasomal catabolism of AKT: by co-translationally phosphorylating the AKT turn motif (T450), mTORC2 keeps nascent AKT in a compactly folded state that is a poor substrate for 26S-mediated degradation.
hypotheses.mechanism: manning2017:findings:010 states that mTORC2 constitutively phosphorylates AKT T450 co-translationally and that this event is required for proper folding of the nascent AKT polypeptide, and manning2017:findings:021 shows T450 phosphorylation is a distinct mTORC2 output separable from S473. Independently, collins2017:findings:001 states that efficient 26S degradation requires not only ubiquitin but also a loosely folded region in the substrate, and collins2017:findings:010 shows that forcing a substrate (DHFR) into a tightly folded state blocks its degradation at the committed-engagement step without preventing ubiquitin-dependent binding. Taken together, the folding state that mTORC2 imposes on AKT is precisely the substrate property that determines whether the proteasome can engage and degrade it, so loss of mTORC2 activity should convert AKT into a degradation-competent, loosely folded proteasome substrate.
hypotheses.prediction: Loss of mTORC2 (rictor/mLST8 knockdown, ATP-competitive mTOR kinase inhibition) or a non-phosphorylatable AKT T450A mutant should shorten AKT protein half-life and increase its polyubiquitylation, with the accelerated loss rescued by proteasome inhibition and with accumulation of the unfolded/detergent-insoluble AKT species; a phosphomimetic or otherwise stabilized turn-motif AKT should resist this, and the effect should be specific to newly synthesized AKT rather than to the mature pool.
hypotheses.test: In cultured cells, compare AKT half-life by cycloheximide chase in control versus rictor/mLST8-knockdown cells and in cells expressing AKT wild type versus T450A, each ± MG132 or bortezomib; in parallel, immunoprecipitate AKT under denaturing conditions and blot for ubiquitin, and score folding state by limited-proteolysis sensitivity and soluble/insoluble fractionation. A reconstituted arm — in vitro ubiquitylation of recombinant T450-phosphorylated versus unphosphorylated AKT followed by degradation by purified 26S proteasomes — would show directly whether the mTORC2 mark, and not an indirect signalling consequence, changes the degradation rate; no change in half-life, ubiquitylation, or in vitro degradation between conditions would rule the hypothesis out.

citations.title: The mammalian target of rapamycin complex 2 controls folding and stability of Akt and protein kinase C.
mTORC2 can associate with ribosomes to promote cotranslational phosphorylation and stability of nascent Akt polypeptide.
Essential function of TORC2 in PKC and Akt turn motif phosphorylation, maturation and signalling.
The turn motif is a phosphorylation switch that regulates the binding of Hsp70 to protein kinase C.

novelty.note: Searched for AKT T450/turn-motif phosphorylation with stability, ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation, for cotranslational mTORC2 action on nascent AKT, and for turn-motif folding/chaperone links. Facchinetti et al. (2008) show mTORC2-dependent turn-motif phosphorylation facilitates C-terminal folding and stabilizes newly synthesized Akt, with unphosphorylated Akt vulnerable to degradation (Hsp90-dependent rescue), and Oh et al. (2010) show mTORC2 phosphorylates nascent Akt at Thr450 cotranslationally specifically to prevent ubiquitination of the nascent chain. Together these state the same explanation — mTORC2 turn-motif phosphorylation imposes a folded state on nascent AKT that protects it from ubiquitin-proteasome degradation — including the newly-synthesized-pool specificity; only the explicit 26S 'loosely folded region/committed engagement' framing is additional.

hypotheses.statement: GSK3β directly phosphorylates STAT3 on a primed serine site and thereby negatively regulates STAT3 nuclear accumulation and transcriptional output.
hypotheses.mechanism: The GSK3β claims show it is a phospho-priming-dependent kinase (johnson2023:findings:003) that acts on already-activated transcription factors: it phosphorylates the R-Smad linker to block Smad nuclear accumulation and create E3-ligase sites (hata2016:findings:024), phosphorylates C/EBPβ downstream of ERK/MEK in a manner correlated with reduced target-gene induction (gaffen2014:findings:030, li2019:findings:008), and drives phospho-dependent turnover of PHLPP (haeusler2018:findings:007). STAT3 is exactly this class of substrate: it is a tyrosine-activated transcription factor whose activity is switched off by serine phosphorylation, since PKCδ-mediated Ser727 phosphorylation inhibits its DNA binding and transactivation (heinrich2003:findings:023), and its output depends on nuclear entry, which can be blocked by cytoplasmic sequestration (heinrich2003:findings:018). A directed GSK3β→STAT3 phosphorylation event would provide the same kind of inhibitory, priming-dependent brake on cytokine-driven STAT3 target genes such as the α2M promoter (heinrich2003:findings:016) and Il17/Il17f/Il23r (gaffen2014:findings:013).
hypotheses.prediction: Recombinant GSK3β should phosphorylate STAT3 in vitro, preferentially when STAT3 is first primed by a second kinase (e.g. pre-phosphorylated at Ser727 or an adjacent S/T), on a serine C-terminal-proximal to the priming site; in cells, GSK3 inhibition or GSK3A/B knockdown should raise the nuclear pool of activated STAT3 and increase IL-6-induced STAT3 reporter and target-gene output, while GSK3β overexpression or expression of a GSK3-resistant (Ser→Ala) STAT3 mutant should do the converse — loss of the inhibitory phospho-site making STAT3 hyperactive and insensitive to GSK3β.
hypotheses.test: Two-part in vitro plus cell test: (1) incubate purified recombinant STAT3 (untreated versus first primed in vitro with a priming kinase or using a phospho-Ser727 mimetic/phosphopeptide substrate spanning candidate GSK3 consensus S-x-x-x-pS sites) with recombinant GSK3β and [γ-32P]ATP, reading incorporation by autoradiography/Phos-tag shift and mapping sites by phosphopeptide LC-MS/MS, with a GSK3 inhibitor (CHIR-99021) and kinase-dead GSK3β as controls; (2) in IL-6-stimulated HepG2 cells, compare vehicle versus CHIR-99021 and GSK3A/B siRNA for STAT3 phosphosite occupancy (site-specific antibody or MS), cytoplasmic/nuclear STAT3 partitioning by fractionation and immunofluorescence, and α2M-promoter luciferase plus endogenous target-gene qPCR, repeating the reporter with wild-type versus Ser→Ala STAT3 to show the GSK3 effect is lost when the mapped site is removed.

citations.title: Glycogen synthase kinase-3 enhances nuclear export of a Dictyostelium STAT protein.
Differential regulation of STAT family members by glycogen synthase kinase-3.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the plain-language mechanism (GSK3 serine-phosphorylates an activated STAT and blocks its nuclear accumulation/transcription), the entities together (GSK3β + STAT3 + Ser727 + priming/in vitro kinase assay), and the prediction (GSK3 inhibition or knockdown raising nuclear STAT3 and IL-6 target-gene output). The general mechanism is published for a STAT orthologue: GskA/GSK-3 directly phosphorylates a serine cluster (the GPR) in Dictyostelium Dd-STATa after its tyrosine activation, driving CRM1-dependent nuclear export and reducing nuclear accumulation (Ginger et al., EMBO J 2000). For mammalian STAT3, however, no source states a direct GSK3β phosphorylation event or the predicted inhibitory direction — the nearest mammalian work (Beurel & Jope, JBC 2008) reports the opposite: GSK3 is required for IL-6/IFN-induced STAT3 tyrosine phosphorylation, DNA binding and nuclear accumulation, and GSK3 inhibitors did not markedly change STAT3 Ser727 phosphorylation, and canonical Ser727 kinase lists (ERK, p38, JNK, CDK5, mTOR, PKCδ/ε) omit GSK3. Hence partial: mechanism class published, this specific mammalian STAT3 connection and prediction not.

hypotheses.statement: EGFR directly tyrosine-phosphorylates the cytoplasmic kinase domain of TGFBR2 (TβRII), thereby enhancing TβRII kinase activity.
hypotheses.mechanism: The TGFBR2 evidence states that tyrosine phosphorylation of TβRII — whether by autophosphorylation or by the tyrosine kinase Src — enhances TβRII kinase activity (derynck2019:findings:013), identifying TβRII as a substrate whose activity is set by an external tyrosine kinase of Src-like substrate preference. Independently, the EGFR evidence shows that EGFR phosphorylates a Src-directed reporter substrate as efficiently as Src, Abl and Lck did, i.e. EGFR's catalytic preference overlaps that of Src on the same peptide sequence (gest2024:findings:208). If TβRII's activating tyrosines lie in such a Src-type context, active EGFR should be able to phosphorylate them directly, making TβRII an EGFR substrate and coupling EGFR kinase activity to TβRII activation.
hypotheses.prediction: Purified active EGFR kinase domain should phosphorylate recombinant TβRII cytoplasmic domain on tyrosine in vitro (with sites overlapping those phosphorylated by Src), and in cells EGF stimulation should raise TβRII tyrosine phosphorylation and its Ser213/Ser409-type autophosphorylation/kinase output, both effects abolished by an EGFR kinase inhibitor and by mutating the targeted tyrosines to phenylalanine, without requiring TGF-β ligand.
hypotheses.test: Run a cell-free kinase assay: recombinant active EGFR kinase domain plus purified GST–TβRII cytoplasmic domain (kinase-dead TβRII to exclude autophosphorylation) with ATP, read out by anti-phosphotyrosine immunoblot and LC-MS/MS site mapping, with Src as a positive comparator and EGFR inhibitor plus no-kinase controls; then in cultured cells co-expressing tagged TβRII, immunoprecipitate TβRII after EGF ± EGFR inhibitor and blot for phosphotyrosine, and assay immunoprecipitated TβRII kinase activity on a generic substrate, comparing wild-type with tyrosine-to-phenylalanine TβRII mutants to confirm that the EGFR-dependent activity gain requires the mapped sites.

citations.title: Src phosphorylates Tyr284 in TGF-beta type II receptor and regulates TGF-beta stimulation of p38 MAPK during breast cancer cell proliferation and invasion.
Crosstalk between TGF-β and EGF receptors via direct phosphorylation.
HER2 phosphorylation induced by TGF-β promotes mammary morphogenesis and breast cancer progression.

novelty.note: I searched for EGFR directly phosphorylating TGFBR2/TβRII, for tyrosine phosphorylation sites of TβRII and their kinases, and for TGF-β/EGF receptor crosstalk via direct phosphorylation. Published work establishes that Src phosphorylates TβRII at Tyr284 and that TβRI/TβRII phosphorylate EGF-family receptors (HER2 Ser779; TβRI→HER2), i.e. the reverse direction; a 2024 JCB commentary explicitly leaves 'does HER2 also phosphorylate the TGF-β receptors on specific tyrosines?' as an open question. No source states or tests EGFR directly phosphorylating and activating the TβRII kinase domain, so the claim is unpublished rather than refuted.

hypotheses.statement: GSK3B directly phosphorylates MEK1 on a site whose phosphorylation requires prior ERK1/2 priming of MEK1 Thr292, adding a second, GSK3-dependent layer to the feedback inhibition of MEK1.
hypotheses.mechanism: lake2016:findings:010 establishes that MEK1 itself is a phosphoprotein substrate in this pathway, carrying an ERK1/2-phosphorylated Thr292 that suppresses MEK1 catalytic output and its binding to ERK2, so MEK1 acquires a pre-phosphorylated Thr in exactly the configuration GSK3 requires. johnson2023:findings:003 states that GSK3 is a phospho-priming kinase family that selects a phosphorylated Thr as the preferred residue at a fixed motif position, meaning an ERK-generated pThr292 creates the local determinant GSK3B reads. That ERK-primes-then-GSK3β-phosphorylates sequence is the same arrangement the corpus already reports on a shared substrate, where MEK/ERK and GSK3β activity are both required for C/EBPβ phosphorylation (li2019:findings:008, gaffen2014:findings:030), supporting that GSK3B acts on substrates within the MEK/ERK module rather than only in parallel.
hypotheses.prediction: Recombinant GSK3B will incorporate phosphate into MEK1 only after MEK1 has been pre-phosphorylated by active ERK2, and not into unphosphorylated MEK1 or into a MEK1 T292A mutant; in cells, GSK3 inhibition or GSK3A/B deletion will reduce the ERK-dependent MEK1 phosphopeptide signal (at a Ser/Thr positioned four residues N-terminal to T292) and will prolong or elevate MEK1 kinase activity and downstream phospho-ERK1/2 after EGF stimulation, mimicking the stronger serum activation reported for T292A.
hypotheses.test: Two-step in vitro kinase assay with purified components: incubate recombinant MEK1 (wild type vs T292A, and a kinase-dead MEK1 to exclude autophosphorylation) with active ERK2 plus or minus cold ATP, inactivate/remove ERK2, then add recombinant GSK3B with [γ-32P]ATP and score incorporation by autoradiography, mapping the modified residue by LC-MS/MS; in parallel, EGF-stimulate HeLa cells expressing FLAG-MEK1 WT or T292A treated with a GSK3 inhibitor (e.g. CHIR99021) versus vehicle, immunoprecipitate MEK1 for phosphosite MS and an in vitro kinase assay toward recombinant ERK2, and immunoblot phospho-ERK1/2 — loss of the GSK3-dependent MEK1 phosphosite in T292A or upon GSK3 inhibition, with a corresponding rise in MEK1 activity, confirms the direct relationship, while no GSK3B incorporation on ERK-primed MEK1 rules it out.

citations.title: Negative feedback regulation of the ERK1/2 MAPK pathway
Glycogen synthase kinase-3 is a negative regulator of extracellular signal-regulated kinase.

novelty.note: I searched for GSK3-mediated phosphorylation of MEK1 with T292 priming, for MEK1 T292 ERK feedback phosphorylation, for direct GSK3/MAP2K1 kinase-assay evidence, and for GSK3 inhibition prolonging ERK signalling. Published work documents ERK-dependent inhibitory MEK1 T292 phosphorylation (Lake 2016 review) and GSK3 as a negative regulator of ERK, but the latter acts via MKP-1/PI3K crosstalk rather than by phosphorylating MEK1 itself; no source states or tests a GSK3B site on MEK1 primed by pT292, and none reports a negative result for it.

hypotheses.statement: Proteasomal degradation directly negatively regulates TAK1: the K63-linked polyubiquitin conjugates that activate TAK1 also make TAK1 a 26S proteasome substrate, so proteasome-dependent catabolism terminates TAK1 kinase activity and its downstream JNK/p38/NF-κB output.
hypotheses.mechanism: The TAK1 claims state that TAK1 activation is driven by polyubiquitylation — TRAF6 binds the activated receptor, is K63-polyubiquitylated and promotes TAK1 association, polyubiquitylation and activation (zhang2009:findings:007), and free K63 chains alone suffice to activate TAK1 (komander2012:findings:037). The degradation claims state that efficient 26S degradation requires a ubiquitin chain plus a loosely folded region (collins2017:findings:001), that degradation rate rises with the number of attached ubiquitins while a single ubiquitin contributes little to proteasome binding (collins2017:findings:007), and that proteasome-associated Usp14 competes with degradation by trimming conjugates and shortening dwell time (collins2017:findings:014). Taken together, the same chain-length-dependent conjugation that switches TAK1 on should hand activated TAK1 to the proteasome, making degradation the off-step and making Usp14-type chain trimming a rescue that preserves active TAK1.
hypotheses.prediction: After receptor stimulation that polyubiquitylates TAK1, total TAK1 protein should fall with a half-life in the range reported for ubiquitylated substrates, and this loss should be blocked by proteasome inhibition, which should cause accumulation of high-molecular-weight polyubiquitylated TAK1, prolonged TAK1 autophosphorylation and prolonged JNK/p38 signaling; conversely, forcing longer chains (or removing Usp14-mediated trimming) should accelerate TAK1 loss and shorten signaling, while trimming chains to one or two ubiquitins should leave TAK1 stable but poorly activated.
hypotheses.test: In cultured cells expressing tagged TAK1/TAB1, stimulate the pathway and follow TAK1 levels by cycloheximide-chase Western blot ± MG132/bortezomib, with parallel anti-K63 and anti-ubiquitin immunoprecipitation of TAK1 to show that the proteasome-blocked condition accumulates long-chain conjugated TAK1; then reconstitute the step directly by incubating TRAF6/E1/E2-polyubiquitylated recombinant TAK1–TAB1 with purified 26S proteasome plus ATP and measure TAK1 disappearance and residual kinase activity (MKK-phosphorylation assay) as a function of chain length, using the Usp14 inhibitor and a deubiquitylase-trimmed conjugate as the two arms that should shift degradation in opposite directions.

citations.title: TAK1-TABs Complex: A Central Signalosome in Inflammatory Responses.
XIAP as a ubiquitin ligase in cellular signaling.

novelty.note: I searched for TAK1 proteasomal degradation as a signal-termination step, for K63→K48 ubiquitin editing on TAK1 (Itch/CYLD, XIAP), and for chain-length/Usp14 control of TAK1 stability. Published work establishes the general claim that TAK1 is ubiquitylated and degraded by the proteasome to terminate JNK/p38/NF-κB output — but via a K48 (or K63-to-K48 edited) degron installed by Itch–Cyld or XIAP, not via the same K63 conjugates that activate TAK1; nothing found tests chain-length dependence, in vitro 26S degradation of polyubiquitylated TAK1–TAB1, or Usp14 trimming as a rescue of active TAK1. Hence partial.

hypotheses.statement: MAPK pathway activity directly activates MTORC1, with MAPK effector kinases (ERK1/2 and its substrate RSK) acting as upstream positive regulators of mTORC1 catalytic output toward S6K1/4E-BP1.
hypotheses.mechanism: The mTORC1 side of the corpus states that TSC1/TSC2 is a Rheb GAP and that ERK1/2 and RSK1 directly phosphorylate and inactivate TSC1/TSC2, thereby stabilizing GTP-Rheb and activating mTORC1 (laplante2012:findings:002; haeusler2018:findings:027 for the TSC2/RHEB step). The MAPK side independently shows that Ras/MAPK activation drives RSK1/2 to phosphorylate ribosomal protein S6 at Ser235/236 and promote cap-dependent translation, i.e. MAPK output terminates on the same translational effectors mTORC1 controls (cargnello2011:findings:034), and that EGF stimulation of cells produces high-occupancy, dynamic phosphorylation across RTK/MAPK signalling (bekkerjensen2020:findings:014). Taken together, an acute MAPK input should propagate through the ERK/RSK–TSC2–Rheb node to raise mTORC1 activity rather than merely running in parallel to it.
hypotheses.prediction: Acute MAPK activation (EGF, or expression of constitutively active MEK1) should increase phosphorylation of the mTORC1-specific substrates S6K1 Thr389 and 4E-BP1 Ser65 together with inhibitory TSC2 phosphorylation, and MEK/ERK inhibition should lower these mTORC1 readouts even with amino acids and insulin present; the increase in S6K1 Thr389 should be lost in TSC2-null cells or in cells carrying a constitutively active RagA Q66L/RagC S75N heterodimer, and rpS6 Ser235/236 should still rise under rapamycin (RSK-driven) while S6K1 Thr389 does not.
hypotheses.test: In cultured HEK-293T or RPE1 cells, serum-starve and then stimulate with EGF (or induce CA-MEK1) ±  MEK inhibitor, ± rapamycin, and immunoblot a time course for phospho-S6K1 Thr389, phospho-4E-BP1 Ser65, phospho-rpS6 Ser235/236 and phospho-TSC2; repeat in TSC2 knockout cells and in cells expressing the dominant-active RagA Q66L/RagC S75N pair to test epistasis, and confirm the kinase step in vitro by incubating immunoprecipitated TSC1/TSC2 with purified active ERK2 or RSK1 and assaying subsequent Rheb-GAP activity, with FLAG-mTOR immunoprecipitates from stimulated versus MEK-inhibited cells assayed for intrinsic kinase activity on recombinant 4E-BP1.

citations.title: Phosphorylation and functional inactivation of TSC2 by Erk implications for tuberous sclerosis and cancer pathogenesis.
Tumor-promoting phorbol esters and activated Ras inactivate the tuberous sclerosis tumor suppressor complex via p90 ribosomal S6 kinase.
RAS/ERK signaling promotes site-specific ribosomal protein S6 phosphorylation via RSK and stimulates cap-dependent translation.
ERK1/2 phosphorylate Raptor to promote Ras-dependent activation of mTOR complex 1 (mTORC1).
Single serine on TSC2 exerts biased control over mTORC1 activation mediated by ERK1/2 but not Akt.

novelty.note: I searched for ERK/RSK phosphorylation of TSC2 driving mTORC1, for the Ras/MAPK–TSC2–Rheb–S6K1/4E-BP1 axis, and for the rapamycin-insensitive RSK→rpS6 Ser235/236 prediction. Multiple primary papers already state exactly this explanation: Ma et al. (Cell 2005) show ERK phosphorylates TSC2 (Ser664), dissociates TSC1–TSC2 and relieves inhibition of mTOR signalling; Roux et al. (PNAS 2004) show RSK1 phosphorylates TSC2 Ser1798 downstream of phorbol esters/activated Ras to inactivate the complex and raise mTOR/S6K1 signalling; Roux et al. (JBC 2007) show RSK phosphorylates rpS6 at Ser235/236 in an mTOR-independent (rapamycin-insensitive) manner while stimulating cap-dependent translation, matching the stated discriminating prediction; Carriere et al. (JBC 2011) add direct ERK1/2 phosphorylation of Raptor promoting mTORC1 signalling to 4E-BP1, and Reynolds et al. (LSA 2022) dissect an ERK1/2-biased TSC2 serine. Only the Rag-heterodimer epistasis detail appears untested, which does not change the status of the core explanation.

hypotheses.statement: Ligand-activated EGFR directly engages STAT1, recruiting it through its SH2 domain to EGFR phosphotyrosines and phosphorylating STAT1 on Tyr701 to drive its dimerization and GAS/SIE binding.
hypotheses.mechanism: Independent evidence shows that EGF treatment causes tyrosine phosphorylation of Stat1 and appearance of Stat1-containing SIE/GAS bandshift complexes distinct from the IFNγ-induced complexes (darnell1994:findings:022, darnell1994:findings:023), and that the activating STAT1 site is Tyr701 whose phosphorylation is required for SH2-mediated dimerization and DNA binding (darnell1994:findings:009, darnell1994:findings:015). Separately, EGFR carries phosphotyrosines — notably the promiscuous Y998 and Y1016 sites — that recruit many SH2/PTB-domain proteins with high affinity and become still more promiscuous at lower affinity thresholds and high receptor levels (jones2006:findings:009, jones2006:findings:011). Since STAT1 activation requires an intact SH2 domain (heinrich2003:findings:007), the simplest reading of the EGF-induced STAT1 phosphorylation is that STAT1's SH2 domain docks directly onto an EGFR phosphotyrosine, making EGFR the kinase acting on STAT1 Tyr701 rather than a distal upstream trigger.
hypotheses.prediction: In EGF-stimulated epithelial cells, STAT1 should co-immunoprecipitate with EGFR in a phosphorylation-dependent, transient manner and acquire pTyr701; recombinant STAT1 SH2 domain should bind EGFR phosphopeptides (strongest for pY998/pY1016) but not their non-phosphorylated counterparts, and EGFR kinase inhibition should abolish EGF-induced STAT1 pTyr701, dimerization and GAS/SIE binding without affecting IFNγ-induced STAT1 activation.
hypotheses.test: Two coupled in-vitro assays in a standard cell/biochemistry lab: (1) direct interaction — immobilize synthetic EGFR phosphopeptides (pY998, pY1016, and other EGFR pTyr sites plus non-phospho controls) and measure binding of purified recombinant STAT1 and an SH2-domain-dead STAT1 mutant by pulldown/fluorescence-polarization Kd determination; (2) direct enzymatic and cellular coupling — incubate purified recombinant STAT1 with active EGFR kinase domain plus ATP in vitro and blot for pTyr701, and in EGF-stimulated cultured epithelial cells (e.g. HeLa or MCF-10A) perform reciprocal EGFR/STAT1 co-IP and pTyr701 blots ± an EGFR-selective kinase inhibitor and ± JAK inhibitor, with STAT1 gel-shift on GAS/SIE probes as readout; loss of EGF-induced STAT1 pTyr701 and DNA binding under EGFR inhibition together with direct phosphopeptide binding and in-vitro phosphorylation confirms the direct relationship, while absence of binding or of in-vitro phosphorylation rules it out.

citations.title: Phosphorylation and activation of the DNA binding activity of purified Stat1 by the Janus protein-tyrosine kinases and the epidermal growth factor receptor.
STAT activation by epidermal growth factor (EGF) and amphiregulin. Requirement for the EGF receptor kinase but not for tyrosine phosphorylation sites or JAK1.
Identification of both positive and negative domains within the epidermal growth factor receptor COOH-terminal region for signal transducer and activator of transcription (STAT) activation.

novelty.note: I searched for direct EGFR phosphorylation of STAT1 Tyr701, JAK-independent STAT1 activation by EGFR, STAT1 SH2 docking on EGFR phosphotyrosine peptides, and EGF-induced GAS/SIE complexes, then retrieved the NCBI records for the top hits. Quelle et al. (1995) show that purified/immune-complex EGFR directly phosphorylates purified Stat1 at Tyr701 and thereby activates its DNA binding, and David et al. (1996) show EGF-induced STAT1/3/5 activation requires the intrinsic EGFR kinase but not JAK1; Xia et al. (2002) map multiple EGFR C-tail phosphotyrosines (notably pY1148 for Stat1) as STAT docking sites. The core explanation — EGFR as the direct kinase for STAT1 pTyr701 driving dimerization and GAS/SIE binding — is therefore already published, although the specific docking assignment to pY998/pY1016 is not supported (David et al. even find autophosphorylation sites dispensable, and the mapped Stat1 site is Y1148).

hypotheses.statement: ERK2 directly binds the CAGA-box element of the TGF-β-responsive PAI-1 promoter and, in a kinase-activity-independent manner, represses TGF-β-driven transcription from that element until stimulation clears ERK2 from the promoter.
hypotheses.mechanism: plotnikov2011:findings:000 establishes that ERK2 is itself a sequence-specific DNA-binding protein that occupies short AT/G-rich promoter motifs and directly suppresses discrete transcriptional elements (e.g. the GATE), with suppression relieved when stimulation depletes ERK2 from those promoters; dennler1998:findings:000 establishes that TGF-β induction of the human PAI-1 promoter is carried by three copies of a short defined element, the CAGA box at -730/-580/-280. If ERK2's promoter-occupancy repression extends to this element, ERK2 bound at the CAGA boxes would hold the TGF-β-responsive unit silent in the absence of ligand, and chen2003:findings:011 shows that TGF-β restimulation acutely activates the Smad2/3 arm that must act on such elements, providing the stimulus that would displace ERK2.
hypotheses.prediction: Recombinant ERK2, including a catalytically dead mutant, should bind CAGA-box oligonucleotides in vitro; in unstimulated cells ERK2 should occupy the CAGA-containing region of the PAI-1 promoter and be lost from it after TGF-β addition; ERK2 knockdown should raise basal CAGA-reporter activity and blunt the fold induction by TGF-β, while ERK2 overexpression should lower basal and TGF-β-stimulated CAGA-reporter output without changing Smad2/3 phosphorylation.
hypotheses.test: In HeLa or fibroblast cultures, run (i) EMSA/biotinylated-oligo pulldown with purified wild-type and kinase-dead ERK2 against wild-type versus point-mutated CAGA-box probes, and (ii) ChIP-qPCR for ERK2 across the -730/-580/-280 PAI-1 promoter region before and after TGF-β treatment, paired with a 3xCAGA-luciferase reporter assayed under siRNA depletion of ERK2 and rescue with kinase-dead ERK2; direct binding plus derepression on ERK2 loss supports the relationship, while absence of EMSA binding and ChIP signal and no reporter change rules it out.

citations.title: Profiling the human protein-DNA interactome reveals ERK2 as a transcriptional repressor of interferon signaling.
Phosphorylation or Mutation of the ERK2 Activation Loop Alters Oligonucleotide Binding.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the mechanism in plain words (ERK2 as a kinase-activity-independent DNA-binding transcriptional repressor cleared from promoters by stimulation), the entities together (ERK2 + CAGA box + PAI-1/SERPINE1 promoter + ChIP/EMSA), and the prediction (ERK2 knockdown derepressing basal CAGA/Smad3 reporter output without changing Smad2/3 phosphorylation). The general mechanism is published — Hu et al. (Cell 2009) show recombinant ERK2 binds a G/CAAAG/C motif directly, represses GATE-containing interferon-γ-responsive promoters independently of catalytic activity, and is depleted from those promoters upon IFN-γ; McReynolds et al. confirm direct ERK2–oligonucleotide binding in vitro including with catalytically impaired ERK2 variants. However, no retrieved source extends ERK2 promoter occupancy to the AG(C/A)CAGACA CAGA boxes of the PAI-1/SERPINE1 promoter or to TGF-β/Smad3-driven transcription; literature on ERK and PAI-1 concerns MEK/ERK as a positive kinase input or Smad linker phosphorylation, not direct ERK2 binding at the CAGA element, so the specific connection remains unpublished.

hypotheses.statement: MEK1 activity negatively regulates STAT3 activation, such that inhibiting MEK1 increases STAT3 tyrosine phosphorylation and STAT3-dependent transcription in growth-factor-responsive epithelial cells.
hypotheses.mechanism: The MEK1 evidence shows that MEK1/2 activity sustains an inhibitory feedback arm on receptor signalling — MEK1/2 inhibition reduces phosphorylation of the EGFR feedback site T669 and increases EGFR/ERBB3 activity, and B-Raf mutant cells respond to Raf/MEK1/2 inhibitors with immediate upregulation of EGFR activity (lake2016:findings:025, lake2016:findings:023). Independently, STAT3 is a direct readout of EGF-driven receptor signalling: EGF treatment of epithelial cells induces STAT3 phosphorylation and STAT3-containing SIE bandshift complexes (darnell1994:findings:023). Combining these, loss of MEK1 kinase output should raise receptor-proximal signalling capacity and thereby raise the phospho-STAT3 pool, making MEK1 a negative regulator of STAT3 rather than an activator; the narrow MEK1 motif preference for the ERK TEY site argues against MEK1 phosphorylating STAT3 itself (johnson2023:findings:009).
hypotheses.prediction: Pharmacological MEK1/2 inhibition (or MEK1 knockdown) in EGF-responsive epithelial cells will increase basal and EGF-stimulated STAT3 Tyr705/Tyr705-equivalent phosphorylation, increase STAT3-containing SIE bandshift complexes and STAT3 reporter activity, with the increase appearing over tens of minutes to hours (feedback-relief kinetics) rather than immediately; conversely, expression of constitutively active MEK1 will dampen EGF-induced phospho-STAT3. Ser727 phosphorylation of STAT3, which suppresses its DNA binding, should not increase in parallel, so DNA-binding activity should rise at least as much as total phospho-STAT3.
hypotheses.test: Treat serum-starved epithelial cells (e.g. A431/HeLa) with PD0325901 or U0126 — inhibitors validated for cellular MEK1/2 blockade (cargnello2011:findings:003) — or with MEK1-targeting siRNA, then stimulate with EGF for 0–120 min and immunoblot for phospho-ERK1/2 (pathway control), phospho-STAT3 Tyr, phospho-STAT3 Ser727 and total STAT3, with a parallel SIE electrophoretic mobility shift assay and STAT3 luciferase reporter; a reciprocal arm transfects constitutively active MEK1 versus kinase-dead MEK1. Increased EGF-induced phospho-STAT3/SIE binding under MEK1 loss and decreased phospho-STAT3 under active MEK1 supports the negative-regulation relationship, while unchanged phospho-STAT3 despite full phospho-ERK1/2 suppression rules it out; an in vitro kinase assay with recombinant active MEK1 and purified STAT3 (ERK1/2 as positive-control substrate) distinguishes any residual direct phosphorylation from the feedback mechanism.

citations.title: Repression of Stat3 activity by activation of mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK).
Drug resistance via feedback activation of Stat3 in oncogene-addicted cancer cells.
STAT3 serine phosphorylation by ERK-dependent and -independent pathways negatively modulates its tyrosine phosphorylation.

novelty.note: I searched for MEK/ERK-mediated negative regulation of STAT3, for constitutively active MEK1 versus EGF-induced STAT3 tyrosine phosphorylation, and for feedback STAT3 activation upon MEK inhibitor treatment. Jain et al. (Oncogene 1998) directly state the explanation: ERK2 activated by MEK1 represses Stat3 transcriptional activity and DNA binding and decreases EGF-induced Stat3 tyrosine phosphorylation, i.e. the MAPK cascade negatively regulates Stat3; Chung et al. (MCB 1997) established that ERK-driven Ser727 phosphorylation negatively modulates STAT3 Tyr705 phosphorylation and DNA binding; and Lee et al. (Cancer Cell 2014) show the predicted feedback-relief arm, that MEK inhibition triggers autocrine (FGFR/JAK) Stat3 activation in kinase- and KRAS-driven epithelial cancer cells. Because both the reciprocal (active MEK1 dampens EGF-induced pSTAT3) and the inhibitor (MEK blockade raises pSTAT3/STAT3 transcription) halves of the claim are already published for growth-factor-responsive epithelial cells, the status is established, even though the specific proposed conduit (EGFR T669 feedback site relief) is not the mechanism these papers invoke.

hypotheses.statement: 14-3-3 proteins positively regulate TGFBR1 (TβRI) by acting as the phospho-dependent effector that releases TβRI-containing intracellular vesicles, so 14-3-3 binding is required for insulin/AKT-driven delivery of TβRI to the cell surface.
hypotheses.mechanism: The TβRI evidence states that insulin and high glucose drive rapid transport of an intracellular TβRI pool to the plasma membrane through AKT phosphorylation of the RabGAP AS160, which relieves intracellular receptor retention (derynck2019:findings:010). The independent 14-3-3 evidence states that AKT phosphorylation of TBC1D4/AS160 at multiple sites works specifically by driving 14-3-3 binding, and that this 14-3-3 engagement is the step that releases vesicle retention (manning2017:findings:044); the same logic of phospho-site occupancy by 14-3-3 converting a phosphorylation event into a change in protein localization/availability is the general mode of action attributed to 14-3-3 (manning2017:findings:015). Combining these, the retention-relief step that controls TβRI surface abundance is itself a 14-3-3-dependent event, making 14-3-3 a direct positive regulator of surface TβRI levels rather than a bystander.
hypotheses.prediction: Blocking 14-3-3 phosphopeptide binding should leave AKT activation and AS160 phosphorylation intact but abolish the insulin- or glucose-induced increase in cell-surface TβRI, with a corresponding loss of the insulin-induced increment in TGF-β responsiveness (Smad2/3 phosphorylation); conversely, 14-3-3 should be recoverable in complexes with the intracellular TβRI vesicle pool only after insulin stimulation.
hypotheses.test: In a cultured epithelial or adipocyte-like cell line expressing tagged TβRI, express the pan-14-3-3 competitive inhibitor difopein (or R18 peptide) versus an inactive mutant peptide, serum-starve, then stimulate with insulin or 25 mM glucose and quantify surface TβRI by cell-surface biotinylation/streptavidin pulldown and by non-permeabilized antibody staining in flow cytometry, in parallel with immunoblots for phospho-AKT, phospho-AS160 and TGF-β-induced phospho-Smad2; complement with co-immunoprecipitation of endogenous 14-3-3 from stimulated versus unstimulated cells probed for tagged TβRI and AS160. Loss of insulin-stimulated surface TβRI despite intact AS160 phosphorylation supports the hypothesis, while unchanged surface TβRI under difopein rules it out.

citations.title: The insulin response integrates increased TGF-β signaling through Akt-induced enhancement of cell surface delivery of TGF-β receptors.
A role for 14-3-3 in insulin-stimulated GLUT4 translocation through its interaction with the RabGAP AS160.

novelty.note: I searched for 14-3-3 plus TGF-β receptor surface trafficking, for the insulin/AKT/AS160→TβRI axis, and for the difopein/14-3-3-blockade prediction. Budi et al. (Science Signaling 2015) establishes that insulin/AKT drives AS160-dependent delivery of TβRI/TβRII to the cell surface but does not implicate 14-3-3, while Ramm et al. (JBC 2006) establishes that 14-3-3 binding to phospho-AS160 is required for insulin-stimulated GLUT4 vesicle release. Each half is published, but no retrieved source states that 14-3-3 phosphopeptide binding is required for insulin-induced surface TβRI or TGF-β responsiveness, so the specific connection remains unmade.

hypotheses.statement: Proteasomal degradation (CATABOLIC_PROCESS) acts directly on ERK2, with activation-loop phosphorylation of ERK2 suppressing its own degradation by eliminating the loosely folded region the 26S proteasome requires to commit to a substrate.
hypotheses.mechanism: Work on the 26S proteasome states that efficient degradation needs not only ubiquitin but a loosely folded, ≥30-residue unstructured region, and that tightly folding a substrate (methotrexate-bound DHFR) blocks the transition from initial ubiquitin-dependent binding to the committed, tightly bound degrading state without blocking binding itself (collins2017:findings:001, collins2017:findings:010, collins2017:findings:011). Independently, ERK2 is reported to undergo a phosphorylation-driven conformational change: Thr183 phosphorylation reorders the C-terminal extension and exposes a hydrophobic surface that drives homodimerization (huse2002:findings:004), and ERK2 also carries a phosphorylatable Ser-Pro-Ser patch in its flexible kinase insert domain (plotnikov2011:findings:010). Those same flexible segments are exactly the class of feature the proteasome needs for initiation, so phospho-ERK2 should be a conformationally protected substrate while unphosphorylated, monomeric ERK2 remains degradation-competent.
hypotheses.prediction: Ubiquitylated unphosphorylated ERK2 should be degraded by purified 26S proteasomes, while dually phosphorylated (MEK-activated) ERK2 binds the proteasome comparably but is degraded much more slowly; in cells, MEK inhibition should shorten ERK2 half-life in a proteasome-inhibitor-sensitive manner, and Thr183-nonphosphorylatable or dimer-interface-disrupting ERK2 mutants should turn over faster than wild type, whereas phosphomimetic/stably dimerizing ERK2 (including SPS-phosphomimetic insert mutants) should be longer-lived.
hypotheses.test: Produce recombinant ERK2, phosphorylate half of it with active MEK1 in vitro, ubiquitylate both pools identically (E1/E2/E3 reaction or a defined poly-Ub fusion), then run side-by-side degradation reactions with purified 26S proteasomes plus ATP, measuring loss of substrate by SDS-PAGE/immunoblot and proteasome binding by pull-down to separate a binding defect from a commitment defect; in parallel, run cycloheximide chases in cultured cells expressing wild-type, T183A, dimer-interface-mutant, and SPS-phosphomimetic ERK2 with and without MEK inhibitor and with and without MG132, quantifying ERK2 half-life by immunoblot.

citations.title: Regulation of Proteasomal Degradation by Modulating Proteasomal Initiation Regions.
ERK1/2 inhibitors act as monovalent degraders inducing ubiquitylation and proteasome-dependent turnover of ERK2, but not ERK1.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the proteasome mechanism (unstructured/disordered initiation region, ligand-induced folding blocking commitment), the entities together (ERK2 phosphorylation, ubiquitylation, proteasomal turnover, MEK inhibition, half-life), and the prediction (T183A / dimer-interface mutant ERK2 stability). The general mechanism is published — Tian et al. show that folding or occluding a substrate's disordered initiation region inhibits proteasomal degradation ~10-fold without blocking ubiquitin recognition — but no source applies this to ERK2's activation loop, C-terminal extension, or kinase-insert SPS patch. ERK2 is documented as a genuine ubiquitin/proteasome substrate, yet the nearest cellular test reports the opposite polarity of the prediction: MEK-inhibitor pretreatment that abolishes pTEY phosphorylation prevented rather than accelerated ERK2 turnover; this is an ERK-inhibitor-driven monovalent-degrader context rather than a direct test of conformational protection at the proteasome, so the claim is unanticipated and untested rather than refuted.

hypotheses.statement: JNK1 directly restrains NFAT-dependent cytokine production, so that loss of JNK1 activity increases and prolongs cytokine output in NFAT-driven immune cells.
hypotheses.mechanism: JNK1 acts as an inducible NFAT export kinase that phosphorylates NFAT2 (and NFAT4) to drive their nuclear exit (hogan2003:findings:005), and NFAT2 is one of the two NFAT isoforms whose combined deletion is required to abolish T-cell cytokine production (hogan2003:findings:013); independently, NFAT is one of the transducers through which SYK/Dectin-1 signalling induces cytokine and chemokine production in myeloid cells (mcsai2010:findings:019). If NFAT nuclear residence is rate-limiting for these cytokine genes, the kinase that evicts NFAT2 from the nucleus should be a direct negative regulator of the amount of cytokine made, without any need for a change in NFAT expression.
hypotheses.prediction: Stimulated JNK1-null or JNK1-inhibited cells will show prolonged nuclear retention of NFAT2 and correspondingly higher and longer-lasting transcription and secretion of NFAT-dependent cytokines (e.g. IL-2, TNF, IL-6/chemokines after Dectin-1 or TCR-type stimulation), whereas cytokines transcribed independently of NFAT will be comparatively unaffected; an NFAT2 mutant lacking the JNK1 target phosphosites will produce the same elevated cytokine output even when JNK1 is intact.
hypotheses.test: In a stimulus-responsive cell line (e.g. Jurkat T cells or a macrophage/DC line responding to zymosan/curdlan), generate CRISPR JNK1 knockouts alongside JNK2 knockouts and parental controls, stimulate, and in parallel measure (i) NFAT2 nuclear/cytoplasmic distribution by immunofluorescence and biochemical fractionation time-courses, and (ii) cytokine mRNA by qPCR and secreted protein by ELISA; then re-express wild-type NFAT2 versus a JNK1-phosphosite-mutant NFAT2 in NFAT2-depleted cells and test whether the mutant renders cytokine output insensitive to JNK1 deletion or to a selective JNK inhibitor — an in vitro kinase assay with recombinant JNK1 and NFAT2 confirms the direct phosphorylation arm.

citations.title: c-Jun NH(2)-terminal kinase inhibits targeting of the protein phosphatase calcineurin to NFATc1.
Defective T cell differentiation in the absence of Jnk1.
JNK1 negatively controls antifungal innate immunity by suppressing CD23 expression.

novelty.note: I searched for the JNK1→NFAT2 export-kinase mechanism in plain terms, for JNK1-null T cells with increased NFAT nuclear accumulation and cytokine output, and for a JNK1/NFAT axis in myeloid/Dectin-1 antifungal responses. Chow et al. (MCB 2000) show JNK1 phosphorylates the calcineurin-targeting (PxIxIT) domain of NFATc1/NFAT2, blocking its nuclear accumulation and target-gene transcription, and explicitly frame JNK1 as a tonic negative regulator explaining why Jnk1−/− T cells display greatly increased NFATc1-dependent nuclear responses; Dong et al. (Science 1998) had already reported that Jnk1−/− CD4 T cells hyperproliferate and secrete excess cytokines in association with increased nuclear NFATc, and Zhao et al. (Nat Med 2017) extend the same restraint to innate myeloid antifungal responses, where JNK1 loss or JNK inhibition raises NFATc1-driven gene induction. The mechanism, the direction of the effect, and the loss-of-JNK1 prediction are therefore already published, so the hypothesis is established rather than novel.

hypotheses.statement: TGF-β directly suppresses the TCR-proximal, Tyr323-dependent activation of MAPK14 (p38α) in CD4+ T cells, and this loss of p38α activation is a proximate cause of the TGF-β–induced anergic/low-IFN-γ state.
hypotheses.mechanism: In T cells, p38α is activated by a TCR-proximal route in which ZAP70/p56lck phosphorylate p38α on Tyr323, triggering activation-loop autophosphorylation and kinase activity (cuadrado2010:findings:006), and T cells that cannot use this route (p38α Y323F) are viable but fail to activate p38α after TCR stimulation and produce less IFN-γ with delayed cell-cycle entry (cuadrado2010:findings:007). TGF-β pretreatment of CD4+ T cells produces a strikingly congruent lesion: unresponsiveness specifically to TCR/anti-CD3 engagement with intact responses to PMA/ionomycin, which bypasses proximal TCR signaling, together with blunted IFN-γ (and IL-2, IL-4) production and no increase in apoptosis (chen2003:findings:002), a state reversible by IL-2 (chen2003:findings:003). The overlap of a proximal-signal-selective defect with the exact cytokine and cell-cycle phenotype of Tyr323-dead p38α implies that TGF-β acts on T cells by disabling TCR-driven p38α (MAPK14) activation rather than by killing cells or blocking distal machinery.
hypotheses.prediction: TGF-β–pretreated CD4+ T cells restimulated through CD3 should show markedly reduced p38α Tyr323 phosphorylation and reduced activation-loop (Thr180/Tyr182) phosphorylation, with correspondingly reduced phosphorylation of the p38α-specific substrate MK2, while p38α activation by PMA/ionomycin or by osmotic/stress stimuli (MKK3/MKK6-driven) remains intact; adding IL-2 during the TGF-β preculture should restore TCR-induced p38α Tyr323 and activation-loop phosphorylation, and forcing p38α activation (constitutively active MKK6) in TGF-β–treated cells should restore IFN-γ output.
hypotheses.test: Culture a human CD4+ T-cell line (e.g. Jurkat) or in vitro–expanded CD4+ T cells with plate-bound anti-CD3/anti-CD28 ± TGF-β for 3–5 days, rest, then restimulate with anti-CD3 and immunoblot in parallel for p38α phospho-Tyr323, phospho-Thr180/Tyr182, total p38α, and phospho-MK2 (Thr222/Thr334) at 0–60 min, using PMA/ionomycin and sorbitol as TCR-independent activation controls and SB203580 to confirm MK2 readout specificity; then test causality two ways in the same cells — immunoprecipitate p38α from TGF-β–treated versus control cells and assay in vitro kinase activity toward MK2, and transfect constitutively active MKK6 (or p38α-Y323F as the converse loss-of-function) before restimulation, scoring IFN-γ by ELISA and proliferation by CFSE dilution. Restoration of IFN-γ by MKK6-driven p38α activation with mimicry of the TGF-β phenotype by Y323F supports the hypothesis; unchanged p38α phosphorylation and kinase activity after TGF-β, or no rescue by MKK6, rules it out.

citations.title: Genetic disruption of p38alpha Tyr323 phosphorylation prevents T-cell receptor-mediated p38alpha activation and impairs interferon-gamma production.
TGF-beta modulates the functionality of tumor-infiltrating CD8+ T cells through effects on TCR signaling and Spred1 expression.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: TGF-β inhibition of p38 MAPK in TCR-stimulated CD4+ T cells, the p38α Tyr323/ZAP70 alternative pathway together with TGF-β and IFN-γ, and TGF-β-induced anergy with proximal TCR signaling defects reversible by IL-2. The alternative TCR-proximal Tyr323 route and its IFN-γ phenotype is published (Jirmanova et al.), and TGF-β is separately documented to blunt proximal TCR kinases (Lck/ZAP70/ITK) and downstream MAPK (ERK) signalling in CD4+/CD8+ T cells, but no retrieved source states that TGF-β suppresses Tyr323-dependent p38α activation or tests MKK6 rescue of IFN-γ; most TGF-β/p38 literature reports TGF-β activating p38 (MAP3K4/MAP3K10) rather than inhibiting it. Hence the components are published but the specific link and prediction are not, and nothing tested and refuted it.

dropped_citations.title: The TGFβ-induced phosphorylation and activation of p38 mitogen-activated protein kinase is mediated by MAP3K4 and MAP3K10 but not TAK1
dropped_citations.reason: title mismatch 0.33: record says 'The decline and rise of coronary heart disease: understanding public health catastrophism.'

hypotheses.statement: TNF directly downregulates TGFBR1 (TβRI) by driving ADAM17/TACE-mediated shedding of the TβRI ectodomain, thereby inhibiting TGF-β/Smad3 signaling in TNF-responsive cells such as fibroblasts and epithelial cells.
hypotheses.mechanism: The TGFBR1 claims state that TACE/ADAM17 cleaves TβRI but not TβRII specifically downstream of ERK or p38 MAPK signaling, that this lowers cell-surface TβRI and down-regulates TGF-β-induced Smad3 activation, antiproliferation and EMT, and that such shedding is how mitogenic and inflammatory stimuli dampen TGF-β responses without changing ligand binding to TβRII (derynck2019:findings:009, hata2016:findings:007). The TNF claims independently establish that TNF acting through TNF-R1 is a potent activator of MAPK-arm signaling and of MAPK-activated kinases in fibroblasts (chen2002:findings:006 for JNK/MAPK output from TNF-R1; cargnello2011:findings:044 for MSK1/2-dependent TNF responses in mouse fibroblasts), i.e. TNF supplies exactly the inflammatory MAPK input that the TβRI shedding mechanism requires. Combining the two independent bodies of evidence predicts a direct, receptor-level antagonism in which TNF stimulation converts surface TGFBR1 into a shed ectodomain plus a cleaved cytoplasmic fragment, making TGFBR1 a proximal negative target of TNF rather than merely a parallel pathway.
hypotheses.prediction: TNF treatment of cultured fibroblasts or epithelial cells should cause a time- and dose-dependent loss of cell-surface TβRI (with TβRII surface levels preserved), accumulation of soluble TβRI ectodomain in the medium, and a blunted TGF-β-induced Smad3 phosphorylation/target-gene response; blocking ADAM17 or the ERK/p38 arms, or expressing a cleavage-site mutant TβRI, should abolish all of these effects, whereas TNF should not reduce TGF-β binding capacity attributable to TβRII.
hypotheses.test: Treat a TβRI/TβRII-expressing fibroblast or epithelial line with TNF, then quantify surface TβRI and TβRII by flow cytometry and cell-surface biotinylation, detect shed TβRI ectodomain in conditioned medium by immunoblot of tagged TβRI, and assay TGF-β-induced Smad3 phosphorylation and a Smad3 reporter/target gene after TNF pretreatment; repeat with ADAM17 knockdown or a metalloprotease inhibitor, with ERK and p38 inhibitors, and with a shedding-resistant TβRI mutant to test whether loss of surface TGFBR1 and the TGF-β signaling defect are causally downstream of TNF-driven ADAM17 cleavage.

citations.title: TACE-mediated ectodomain shedding of the type I TGF-beta receptor downregulates TGF-beta signaling.
Duality of Interactions Between TGF-β and TNF-α During Tumor Formation.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the mechanism in plain words (TNF/ADAM17 ectodomain shedding of the TGF-β type I receptor), the entities together (TACE/ADAM17 + TGFBR1 + ERK/p38 + Smad3), and the prediction (TNF-induced surface TβRI loss with TβRII preserved, soluble TβRI in medium, blunted Smad3). The receptor-level half of the hypothesis is fully published: Liu, Chang & Derynck (PMID 19595713) show TACE/ADAM17 sheds the TβRI ectodomain into the medium downstream of Erk MAPK activation, lowering surface TβRI but not TβRII and reducing TGF-β-induced Smad3 activation — but the stimuli tested were PMA, serum and EGF, not TNF, and TNF is never tested or proposed as the trigger. Conversely, the dedicated TNF/TGF-β crosstalk literature (nearest review, PMID 35069596) attributes TNF's antagonism to Smad7 induction, AP-1/c-Jun interference and proteolytic down-regulation of TβRII — the opposite receptor from the one this hypothesis predicts — and does not mention ADAM17-mediated TβRI shedding at all, so the specific TNF→ADAM17→TβRI-shedding connection and its TβRII-sparing prediction appear unstated.

hypotheses.statement: EGFR directly activates mTORC1 by driving ERK-mediated inactivation of the TSC1/TSC2 complex, making mTORC1 substrate phosphorylation an EGFR-dependent output.
hypotheses.mechanism: Evidence about EGFR shows that ERK pathway output is sustained by EGFR: the live-cell FIRE reporter decays upon EGFR inhibition (albeck2013:findings:000), and EGFR-recruited SOS near the membrane is what confers the apparent affinity needed for observed Ras activation rates (kholodenko2006:findings:002); pharmacological EGFR inhibition with erlotinib likewise modulates p-ERK (chen2016:findings:016). Independently, mTORC1 is stated to be activated when growth-factor pathway kinases including ERK1/2 and RSK1 directly phosphorylate and inactivate TSC1/TSC2, the Rheb GAP (laplante2012:findings:002). Since EGFR is the upstream determinant of ERK activity in these systems and ERK is a direct TSC2-inactivating input to mTORC1, EGFR activity should set the TSC2/Rheb-dependent tone of mTORC1 independently of the amino-acid/Rag arm.
hypotheses.prediction: EGF stimulation of serum-starved, amino-acid-replete cells should raise phospho-S6K1 Thr389 and phospho-4E-BP1 Ser65 (and the TORCAR cyan/yellow ratio) with kinetics following ERK activation; acute EGFR inhibition should lower these mTORC1 readouts, and that loss should be phenocopied by MEK/ERK inhibition and largely abolished in TSC2-depleted cells, which should retain high mTORC1 signalling regardless of EGFR inhibitor.
hypotheses.test: In HeLa or MCF-10A cells held in amino-acid-replete, serum-free medium, stimulate with EGF ± erlotinib ± a MEK inhibitor and immunoblot phospho-S6K1 Thr389, phospho-4E-BP1 Ser65, phospho-ERK and ERK-site phospho-TSC2 over a 0–60 min time course; then repeat in isogenic shRNA/CRISPR TSC2-knockdown versus control cells, and in parallel read live-cell mTORC1 activity with the TORCAR FRET reporter during acute EGFR inhibition. EGFR-dependent, MEK-dependent, TSC2-requiring changes in mTORC1 readouts support the relationship; unchanged mTORC1 readouts after EGFR inhibition, or an EGFR effect that persists without TSC2, rule it out.

citations.title: Phosphorylation and functional inactivation of TSC2 by Erk implications for tuberous sclerosis and cancer pathogenesis.
Tumor-promoting phorbol esters and activated Ras inactivate the tuberous sclerosis tumor suppressor complex via p90 ribosomal S6 kinase.
Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor Cell Proliferation Signaling Pathways.
Single serine on TSC2 exerts biased control over mTORC1 activation mediated by ERK1/2 but not Akt.
Lysosomal EGFR acts as a Rheb-GEF independent of its kinase activity to activate mTORC1.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the mechanism in words (ERK phosphorylates/inactivates TSC2 to activate mTORC1 after EGF), the entities together (EGFR/erlotinib + MEK/ERK + TSC2 + S6K1 T389 / 4E-BP1 S65), and the prediction (EGFR inhibition lowering mTORC1 readouts, TSC2-dependence, live-cell FRET mTORC1 reporters). The explanation is long-established: Ma et al. (Cell 2005) show ERK directly phosphorylates TSC2, dissociating TSC1/TSC2 and relieving mTOR inhibition with EGF-stimulated, U0126-sensitive TSC2 phosphorylation; Roux et al. (PNAS 2004) show the parallel Ras/MAPK–RSK1 input to TSC2 increasing mTOR signalling to S6K1; an EGFR-pathway review states directly that EGFR-driven AKT/ERK/RSK inactivate TSC2 to activate mTORC1 and that EGFR TKIs downregulate ERK; and a 2022 study confirms ERK1/2-driven mTORC1 activation (p-S6K1 T389, p-4E-BP1 S65) is TSC2-dependent using TSC2-KO MEFs. The nearest work on the specific prediction (He et al., Cell Res 2025) actually qualifies it: EGFR also activates mTORC1 kinase-independently as a Rheb-GEF, so erlotinib leaves mTORC1 substantially active while afatinib strongly reduces p-S6K1/p-4E-BP1.

hypotheses.statement: Activation-induced opening of SYK's autoinhibited conformation directly converts SYK into an efficient proteasomal degradation substrate, so that catabolic (26S proteasome-mediated) turnover of SYK is conformation-gated rather than ubiquitylation-gated.
hypotheses.mechanism: Collins2017 establishes that ubiquitylation alone is insufficient for 26S degradation: the substrate must present a loosely folded initiation region of at least ~30 varied, hydrophobic-biased residues, and a ligand-locked tightly folded state (methotrexate-bound DHFR) blocks degradation at the transition to the committed state without affecting ubiquitin-dependent binding (collins2017:findings:001, collins2017:findings:010, collins2017:findings:011). Mcsai2010 shows SYK exists in exactly these two states — a compact autoinhibited conformation that is opened by deletion of the tandem SH2 domains or interdomain A, or by binding of a phosphorylated ITAM, and that BCR-triggered Tyr130 phosphorylation in interdomain A releases SYK from ITAMs into a free, high-activity state (mcsai2010:findings:006, mcsai2010:findings:009). Together these imply that the open, ITAM-released form of SYK exposes the interdomain A linker as a proteasome initiation site, while the compact form occludes it.
hypotheses.prediction: Ubiquitylated SYK in the compact state (or held compact by SH2 engagement) will bind the 26S proteasome but be degraded slowly or not at all, whereas open-conformation SYK (phospho-ITAM-bound in solution, Y130E phosphomimetic, or SH2-deleted) will be degraded markedly faster at equal ubiquitylation; deleting or shortening interdomain A below ~30 unstructured residues will stabilize SYK even when it is open and ubiquitylated, and cellular SYK protein should drop after BCR/ITAM stimulation in a manner rescued by proteasome inhibitors.
hypotheses.test: Reconstitute degradation in vitro: ubiquitylate purified recombinant SYK (wild type, Y130E, tandem-SH2-deleted, and an interdomain A-truncated mutant) to matched chain lengths, then incubate with purified 26S proteasomes and measure degradation rate by quantitative immunoblot/fluorescent-substrate readout, in parallel with anisotropy or pull-down measurement of proteasome binding, ± doubly phosphorylated ITAM peptide to force the open state; a conformation-dependent divergence between unchanged binding and increased degradation rate confirms the hypothesis, while equal degradation across conformations rules it out. Corroborate in a B-cell line by anti-IgM stimulation ± MG132 and cycloheximide chase of endogenous versus Y130E SYK.

citations.title: An unstructured initiation site is required for efficient proteasome-mediated degradation.
Regulation of Proteasomal Degradation by Modulating Proteasomal Initiation Regions.
Tripartite degrons confer diversity and specificity on regulated protein degradation in the ubiquitin-proteasome system.
Loss of syk kinase during IgE-mediated stimulation of human basophils.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: (1) the general mechanism (proteasome initiation regions, folded vs. unstructured states gating degradation independent of ubiquitylation), (2) the entities together (SYK/ZAP-70 autoinhibited conformation + Cbl ubiquitylation + proteasomal degradation, interdomain A as degron/initiation region), and (3) the prediction (activation- or conformation-dependent SYK protein loss rescued by proteasome inhibitors; SH2-deleted or Y130E SYK stability). The conformation-gating mechanism itself is firmly published in generic terms — an unstructured initiation region of ~20-30 residues is required beyond ubiquitylation, ligand-induced folding or antibody/small-molecule occlusion of that region blocks degradation without blocking ubiquitin-dependent recruitment, and degrons are described as tripartite with a disordered initiation segment plus conformational masking/PTM-triggered exposure. Activation-triggered, proteasome-dependent loss of SYK protein after immunoreceptor stimulation is also documented. What I could not find is any source proposing that SYK's own autoinhibited-to-open conformational switch (interdomain A / tandem-SH2 release, Tyr130 phosphorylation) is what licenses proteasomal engagement, i.e. that SYK turnover is conformation-gated rather than ubiquitylation-gated — hence partial.

hypotheses.statement: mTOR kinase activity directly sustains the inhibitory, 14-3-3-dependent phosphorylation of c-RAF (S259/B-RAF S364), so that mTOR acts as a negative regulator of RAF and mTOR inhibition de-represses RAF kinase activity.
hypotheses.mechanism: Phosphoproteomic profiling shows that mTOR inhibitors not only collapse mTOR- and p70S6K-motif site phosphorylation but also dose-dependently reduce enrichment of AKT-motif substrate groups, i.e. loss of mTOR catalytic activity lowers phosphorylation of the same basophilic substrate class that includes the RAF inhibitory site (casado2013:findings:004). Independently, that inhibitory site on RAF is defined as a basophilic AKT-type site whose phosphorylation recruits 14-3-3 and blocks RAF activation and downstream ERK signalling (manning2017:findings:024). Combining the two, RAF S259/S364 occupancy should itself be mTOR-activity-dependent, making RAF a target of negative regulation by mTOR rather than an unrelated parallel pathway — consistent with RAF/MEK-level pathways and PI3K–AKT–mTOR signalling being reciprocally coupled through relief of inhibitory phosphorylation (lake2016:findings:025).
hypotheses.prediction: Acute catalytic mTOR inhibition (TORKi; less so rapamycin) in growth-factor-stimulated cells should decrease c-RAF pS259 (and B-RAF pS364), reduce 14-3-3 co-precipitation with RAF, and increase immunoprecipitated RAF kinase activity toward MEK1 plus MEK/ERK phosphorylation; a non-phosphorylatable c-RAF S259A mutant should show no further activation by mTOR inhibitor, whereas a phosphomimetic S259D should remain inactive regardless of mTOR inhibition.
