Activin receptor-like kinase5 inhibition suppresses mouse melanoma by ubiquitin degradation of Smad4, thereby derepressing eomesodermin in cytotoxic T lymphocytes.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the mechanism in words (TGF-β receptor I/ALK5 kinase restraining IFN-γ in CD4 T cells), the entities together (Tgfbr1/ALK5 conditional deletion, SB-431542/galunisertib/vactosertib kinase inhibition, TCR stimulation, Ifng), and the prediction (loss of TGF-β-dependent IFNG repression when TβRI is absent or kinase-inhibited). Published work already states this explanation: inducible Tgfbr1 deletion in T cells increases IFN-γ upon anti-CD3 stimulation and TβRI expression is the TCR-regulated node setting T cell quiescence versus activation (PMID 29669252), TGF-β suppresses IFN-γ in TCR-stimulated human CD4+ T cells in a receptor-kinase/Smad-phosphorylation-dependent manner (PMID 31530731), and genetic ablation of TGF-β receptor signaling in conventional CD4+ T cells causes excessive Ifng/Th1 output (PMID 23569233). Only the narrow sub-prediction about a GS-domain phospho-deficient or constitutively active (T204D-type) TβRI acting on IFNG in T cells appears untested; pharmacological ALK5 kinase inhibition in vivo has in fact been reported not to alter T cell IFN-γ in one melanoma model (PMID 24127404), so that specific quantitative claim is the residual uncertainty rather than the mechanism itself.

hypotheses.statement: p38 activation directly stimulates mTORC1 kinase activity, with p38 acting as an upstream positive regulator of mTORC1 through relief of TSC1/TSC2 inhibition.
hypotheses.mechanism: The p38 evidence states that p38-alpha activation of MK2/MK3 leads to phosphorylation of RSK on Ser380 and RSK activation, which is offered as the route by which p38-stimulating stresses turn on RSK (cargnello2011:findings:058, cargnello2011:findings:068). Independently, the mTORC1 evidence states that RSK1 is one of the growth-factor-pathway kinases that directly phosphorylates and inactivates the TSC1/TSC2 Rheb-GAP, thereby activating mTORC1 (laplante2012:findings:002). Taken together, an input that activates p38 should propagate into the same TSC2/Rheb node that gates mTORC1, so p38 signalling should raise mTORC1 output rather than being signalling-neutral toward it.
hypotheses.prediction: Acute p38-activating stimuli should increase mTORC1 substrate phosphorylation (S6K1 Thr389, 4E-BP1) together with an increase in inhibitory TSC2 phosphorylation at the RSK/AGC-kinase site; pharmacological p38 inhibition (e.g. SB203580, which is reported to abolish MK2 activation) should blunt both readouts, and the mTORC1 gain should be lost when TSC2 or RSK is absent, while persisting if mTORC1 is already locked on by a constitutively active Rag or Rheb input.
hypotheses.test: In a standard cell line (e.g. HEK-293T or MEFs), stimulate p38 with anisomycin or sorbitol in the presence or absence of SB203580 and immunoblot phospho-S6K1 Thr389, phospho-4E-BP1 and phospho-TSC2 across a time course; then repeat in TSC2-knockout and in RSK-knockdown (siRNA/CRISPR) cells, and in cells expressing a TSC2 phospho-site mutant, to establish whether the p38-dependent change in mTORC1 substrate phosphorylation requires the TSC2 node or is absent altogether — no change in mTORC1 substrates under p38 activation, or an unchanged response in TSC2-null cells, would rule the relationship out.

citations.title: The p38 and MK2 kinase cascade phosphorylates tuberin, the tuberous sclerosis 2 gene product, and enhances its interaction with 14-3-3.
p38α senses environmental stress to control innate immune responses via mechanistic target of rapamycin.
p38 regulates the tumor suppressor PDCD4 via the TSC-mTORC1 pathway.
Phosphorylation of Raptor by p38beta participates in arsenite-induced mammalian target of rapamycin complex 1 (mTORC1) activation.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the plain-language mechanism (p38 as a positive upstream regulator of mTORC1 via relief of TSC1/TSC2 inhibition), the key entities together (p38/MK2 + TSC2/tuberin + 14-3-3 + mTORC1), and the prediction (anisomycin/sorbitol/SB203580 effects on S6K1 Thr389 and 4E-BP1). The explanation is already published: Li et al. showed the p38–MK2 cascade directly phosphorylates TSC2 (Ser1210) and promotes 14-3-3 binding that antagonises TSC2's inhibitory function, and Katholnig et al. showed that stress- and TLR-driven p38α activation raises mTORC1 output (p-S6K1 Thr389, p-4E-BP1) in an MK2- and TSC1/TSC2-dependent, PI3K-independent manner; Fonseca-type follow-up work (PDCD4) restates the same p38→MK2→TSC2→mTORC1→S6K1 axis. The p38→mTORC1-positive relationship is therefore established, though the published route runs through MK2 (and, for arsenite, p38β→Raptor) rather than the RSK-mediated TSC2 phosphorylation posited here.

hypotheses.statement: GSK3B directly phosphorylates MYC on a primed Ser/Thr site, creating a phosphodegron that targets MYC for ubiquitin-mediated degradation and thereby lowers MYC protein levels.
hypotheses.mechanism: The claims about GSK3 describe a single recurring biochemical logic: it prefers substrates already bearing a priming phosphate (johnson2023:findings:003) and its phosphorylation of substrates such as β-catenin creates an E3-ligase (β-Trcp) binding site that drives ubiquitination and degradation (macdonald2009:findings:008), the same degron-generating role it plays for R-Smads and for PHLPP, whose degradation follows GSK3β phosphorylation unless AKT inhibits GSK3β (hata2016:findings:024, haeusler2018:findings:007). GSK3β is also stated to act together with ERK on a transcription factor, phosphorylating C/EBPβ downstream of ERK/MEK to reduce its transcriptional output (gaffen2014:findings:030, li2019:findings:008). MYC is independently described as an ERK effector whose protein abundance is graded and variable with EGF-ERK input (albeck2013:findings:004, albeck2013:findings:019), so an ERK-primed, GSK3β-generated degron on MYC would explain post-translational control of MYC protein level by the same kinase pair.
hypotheses.prediction: Recombinant GSK3β should phosphorylate MYC in vitro, efficiently only after ERK (or another priming kinase) pre-phosphorylation of the adjacent +4 Ser/Thr; in cells, GSK3 inhibition or GSK3B knockout should raise steady-state MYC protein and lengthen its cycloheximide-chase half-life without raising MYC mRNA, reduce MYC ubiquitination, and these effects should be abolished in a MYC mutant lacking the GSK3 acceptor serine/threonine, which should itself be stabilized and insensitive to GSK3 inhibition.
hypotheses.test: Two-step in vitro kinase assay: incubate recombinant MYC (and its Ser/Thr→Ala point mutants) with active ERK2, then with active GSK3β ± a GSK3 inhibitor, and read out incorporation by ³²P/phos-tag gel and site assignment by LC-MS/MS or a phospho-specific antibody; pair this with cells where GSK3B is depleted (siRNA/CRISPR) or inhibited, measuring MYC protein by immunoblot with cycloheximide chase and proteasome-inhibitor-stabilized MYC ubiquitination by anti-MYC immunoprecipitation/anti-ubiquitin blot, alongside MYC mRNA by qPCR, and repeating the chase with the phospho-site mutant to show loss of GSK3 dependence.

citations.title: Multiple Ras-dependent phosphorylation pathways regulate Myc protein stability.
The Fbw7 tumor suppressor regulates glycogen synthase kinase 3 phosphorylation-dependent c-Myc protein degradation.

novelty.note: I searched for the mechanism in plain words (GSK3-created phosphodegron on MYC), the entities together (GSK3 + MYC Thr58 + ERK Ser62 priming + Fbw7/ubiquitination), and the prediction (GSK3 inhibition raising MYC protein/half-life, T58 mutant insensitivity). This is a textbook-established pathway: Sears et al. (Genes Dev 2000) showed Thr58 phosphorylation is GSK-3-mediated and strictly dependent on prior ERK-driven Ser62 priming (+4 residue) and is associated with Myc degradation, and Welcker et al. (PNAS 2004) showed GSK3 phosphorylation of T58 creates the Fbw7 binding site, with Fbw7 directly catalysing c-Myc ubiquitination in a T58- and GSK-3-dependent manner. The hypothesis, including the priming logic, degron identity, ubiquitin-mediated turnover and the T58 mutant control, is therefore fully anticipated.

hypotheses.statement: SRC directly phosphorylates the LAT cytoplasmic tyrosines, generating the SH2-docking phosphotyrosines that drive multivalent LAT–Grb2 assembly and phase separation.
hypotheses.mechanism: SRC-family kinases are shown to phosphorylate up to five tyrosines in the nephrin cytoplasmic domain, creating consensus pY SH2-binding motifs that recruit adaptors (case2019a:findings:011), and nephrin and LAT are described as the same class of pTyr-dependent assembly in which increasing the number of phosphotyrosines lowers the phase-separation threshold (banani2017:findings:008). Since LAT's condensate-forming activity depends entirely on its phosphorylated tyrosines serving as multivalent Grb2/Sos1 docking sites (case2019a:findings:006), and LAT co-partitions with Src-family kinases in the same detergent-resistant membrane fraction after receptor activation (sezgin2017:findings:015), SRC is positioned to act directly on LAT's tyrosines as it does on nephrin's.
hypotheses.prediction: Purified SRC kinase domain incubated with the recombinant LAT cytoplasmic domain should produce stoichiometric multi-site tyrosine phosphorylation at the Grb2-docking motifs, and this SRC-generated pLAT should be sufficient to recruit Grb2/Sos1 and to form micron-scale condensates on supported bilayers, with condensate formation scaling with the number of SRC-installed pTyr and abolished by Y-to-F substitution of those sites or by SRC inhibition.
hypotheses.test: Run an in vitro kinase reaction with purified recombinant SRC (versus a kinase-dead SRC) and His-tagged LAT cytoplasmic domain, then (i) map and quantify phosphosites by anti-pTyr immunoblot and LC-MS/MS, and (ii) load the product onto Ni-chelating supported lipid bilayers with fluorescent Grb2 and Sos1 and score cluster/droplet formation by TIRF microscopy; LAT tyrosine-to-phenylalanine mutants and an ATP-free control provide the negative controls that would rule out direct SRC-on-LAT phosphorylation.

citations.title: Phosphotyrosine-mediated LAT assembly on membranes drives kinetic bifurcation in recruitment dynamics of the Ras activator SOS.
A molecular assembly phase transition and kinetic proofreading modulate Ras activation by SOS.
Phase separation of signaling molecules promotes T cell receptor signal transduction.
Lck promotes Zap70-dependent LAT phosphorylation by bridging Zap70 to LAT.

novelty.note: I searched for in vitro LAT phosphorylation by Src-family kinases, for LAT–Grb2–SOS1 reconstitution on supported bilayers, and for phosphotyrosine-valency dependence of LAT clustering. Published reconstitutions already do exactly what the prediction describes: Huang et al. (PNAS 2016, and Science 2019) tether the His-tagged LAT cytoplasmic domain and the Src-family kinase Hck to supported bilayers, where Hck directly multi-site phosphorylates LAT and the resulting pLAT recruits Grb2/SOS to form macroscopic membrane assemblies (the paper notes ZAP-70 can substitute 'without appreciable differences'), while Su et al. (Science 2016) show cluster formation scales with the number of Grb2-docking tyrosines (2xYYY > YYY > FYY > FFY > FFF). The only respect in which the hypothesis diverges from the literature is physiological: in cells LAT is phosphorylated by ZAP-70, with Lck acting as an SH3/SH2 bridge rather than the direct LAT kinase (PMID 29915297), so Src-family action on LAT is established biochemically but not as the in vivo kinase.

hypotheses.statement: p38 directly phosphorylates MEK1 on the inhibitory ERK-consensus site Thr292, acting as a stress-activated negative regulator of MEK1 kinase activity toward ERK1/2.
hypotheses.mechanism: MEK1 carries a proline-directed, ERK1/2-consensus site (T292) whose phosphorylation inhibits MEK1 catalytic activity toward ERK1/2 and disrupts the MEK1–ERK2 docking interaction (lake2016:findings:010), so MEK1 is intrinsically a substrate of a conventional proline-directed MAPK. p38 is a conventional MAPK of the same family (cargnello2011:findings:000) that is already documented to inhibit a kinase by direct phosphorylation of a single serine, reducing that enzyme's activity (balla2013:findings:022), and ERK2 versus p38 substrate selection is governed by only a small docking patch that can be swapped to interconvert the two enzymes' partner repertoires (cargnello2011:findings:016) — implying MEK1's ERK-directed docking/consensus features are compatible with p38 engagement. Together these predict that stress-activated p38 can occupy the same MEK1 site that ERK uses for feedback inhibition.
hypotheses.prediction: Active recombinant p38 should phosphorylate purified MEK1 in vitro on T292 (signal lost in a MEK1 T292A mutant) and thereby reduce MEK1's ability to phosphorylate ERK1/2, and in cells a p38-activating stress (sorbitol/anisomycin) should raise phospho-MEK1 T292 and lower MEK1-dependent ERK1/2 phosphorylation in a manner blocked by SB203580 and absent in MEK1 T292A-expressing cells.
hypotheses.test: Two-step in vitro/cell assay: (1) incubate purified active p38α with recombinant MEK1 WT or T292A ± ATP, then blot with phospho-T292-specific antibody and quantify stoichiometry by phos-tag/mass shift, and couple the reaction to a second-stage kinase assay measuring pre-treated MEK1 activity on kinase-dead ERK2 (TEY phosphorylation); (2) in HeLa or NIH3T3 cells expressing FLAG-MEK1 WT or T292A, stimulate with sorbitol/anisomycin ± SB203580 and immunoblot phospho-MEK1 T292, phospho-ERK1/2, and MEK1–ERK2 co-immunoprecipitation. Loss of T292 phosphorylation and of MEK1 inhibition under p38 inhibition, with no effect in T292A, would confirm; failure of p38 to phosphorylate MEK1 in vitro would rule it out.

citations.title: p38 mitogen-activated protein kinase-dependent activation of protein phosphatases 1 and 2A inhibits MEK1 and MEK2 activity and collagenase 1 (MMP-1) gene expression.
Phosphorylation of MEK1 by cdk5/p35 down-regulates the mitogen-activated protein kinase pathway.
Mitogen-activated protein kinase feedback phosphorylation regulates MEK1 complex formation and activation during cellular adhesion.
Crosstalk between p38 and Erk 1/2 in Downregulation of FGF1-Induced Signaling.

novelty.note: I searched for direct p38 phosphorylation of MEK1 Thr292, for the T292 inhibitory feedback site and its kinases, and for stress/p38-mediated suppression of MEK1 activity (PubMed, PMC, publisher pages). Published work establishes (a) T292 as an inhibitory, proline-directed MEK1 site phosphorylated by ERK1/2 as feedback and also by CDK1/CDK5 (which likewise lowers MEK1 activity toward ERK1/2), and (b) p38 as a stress-activated negative regulator of MEK1/2 activity — but via p38-dependent activation of PP1/PP2A, not by p38 phosphorylating MEK1 T292; the p38–ERK crosstalk literature I checked attributes p38's direct substrate role to FRS2, not MEK1. So the components are published, while the specific claim that p38 itself phosphorylates MEK1 T292 to inhibit it was not found anywhere.

hypotheses.statement: 14-3-3 proteins bind directly to the Ser/Thr-phosphorylated cytoplasmic tail of EGFR generated by stress-activated p38/MK2 signalling, and this binding controls EGFR internalization.
hypotheses.mechanism: EGFR is itself a direct Ser/Thr phosphorylation substrate of p38alpha, and that phosphorylation is required for clathrin-mediated EGFR internalization after inflammatory cytokines or UV (cuadrado2010:findings:054); the same stress-activated module creates functional 14-3-3-binding sites on other substrates when MK2 phosphorylates them (cargnello2011:findings:073, cargnello2011:findings:077). Because 14-3-3 recognition requires only a basophilic phosphoserine motif with Arg at pS-4 and Pro at pS+2 coordinated in the dimer channel (yaffe1997:findings:002, yaffe1997:findings:009), stress-phosphorylated EGFR tail sites are candidate direct 14-3-3 ligands, making 14-3-3 an occluding partner of the phosphorylated receptor tail rather than only of downstream effectors.
hypotheses.prediction: Recombinant 14-3-3 should bind EGFR cytoplasmic-tail phosphopeptides phosphorylated at the p38/MK2-type Ser/Thr sites with micromolar or better affinity and not their unphosphorylated counterparts; in cells, endogenous 14-3-3 should co-immunoprecipitate with EGFR after anisomycin/UV or cytokine treatment, this association should be abolished by p38 inhibition or by Ser/Thr-to-Ala substitution of the modified tail residues, and loss of 14-3-3 engagement should change the rate and extent of ligand-independent, stress-induced EGFR internalization.
hypotheses.test: Synthesize phospho- and non-phospho EGFR cytoplasmic-tail peptides spanning the candidate p38/MK2 sites and measure binding to purified recombinant 14-3-3 by fluorescence polarization or ITC; in parallel, in HeLa cells expressing wild-type versus Ser/Thr-to-Ala EGFR, treat with anisomycin or UV with and without a p38 inhibitor and assay 14-3-3/EGFR co-immunoprecipitation plus surface-biotinylation internalization, and repeat with the 14-3-3 pan-inhibitor difopein to test whether blocking 14-3-3 engagement alters receptor uptake.

citations.title: Identification of 14‐3‐3ζ as an EGF receptor interacting protein
Stress-specific p38 MAPK activation is sufficient to drive EGFR endocytosis but not its nuclear translocation.

novelty.note: I searched for 14-3-3/EGFR phosphorylation-dependent binding, for p38/MK2-phosphorylated EGFR tail sites and clathrin-mediated internalization, and for stress/anisomycin-induced EGFR uptake with 14-3-3 co-immunoprecipitation. An EGF-induced 14-3-3ζ association with the EGFR cytoplasmic tail (C-terminal to residue 1028) is published, and the p38-dependent Ser/Thr cluster in the EGFR tail driving stress-induced clathrin endocytosis is published, but the published mechanism for the latter runs through the dileucine motif/AP2-σ2 and no retrieved source links 14-3-3 to p38/MK2-phosphorylated EGFR or to stress-induced internalization; the specific prediction is neither stated nor tested.

hypotheses.statement: 14-3-3 is recruited into the activated EGFR receptor complex and acts as a negative regulator of EGFR-proximal signal output by displacing the Grb2–SOS1 module from the receptor.
hypotheses.mechanism: EGF stimulation recruits GRB2 to EGFR at roughly 1:1 stoichiometry at the receptor-bearing endo-lysosomal membranes (itzhak2016:findings:025, itzhak2016:findings:010), and receptor-bound SOS gains 10^2–10^3-fold apparent affinity for Ras purely from membrane confinement (kholodenko2006:findings:002), so whatever controls SOS1 occupancy of the receptor complex controls receptor output. Feedback phosphorylation of SOS1 at S1134/S1161 recruits 14-3-3 and negatively regulates ERK1/2 activity, in the same setting where SOS1 phosphorylation disrupts its association with Grb2 and Shc (lake2016:findings:003). Together these imply that 14-3-3 physically enters and then dismantles the EGFR-nucleated adaptor complex, so 14-3-3 should be detectable on and act directly upon activated EGFR.
hypotheses.prediction: After EGF stimulation, 14-3-3 should appear in EGFR immunoprecipitates with delayed kinetics relative to GRB2 and should be inversely related to receptor-associated SOS1; sequestering 14-3-3 should increase and prolong EGF-induced ERK output and GRB2/SOS1 occupancy of EGFR without changing EGFR tyrosine autophosphorylation.
hypotheses.test: In EGF-stimulated HeLa or MCF-10A cells, immunoprecipitate EGFR over a stimulation time course and immunoblot for 14-3-3, GRB2 and SOS1, then repeat with difopein expression or 14-3-3 knockdown and with the SOS1 S1134A/S1161A mutant; read ERK pathway output in the same cells with the live-cell FIRE reporter, which rises on ERK induction and decays on EGFR inhibition, to test whether removing 14-3-3 engagement raises receptor-driven output while EGFR pTyr immunoblots stay unchanged.

citations.title: Identification of 14-3-3zeta as an EGF receptor interacting protein.
RSK phosphorylates SOS1 creating 14-3-3-docking sites and negatively regulating MAPK activation.
Phosphorylation-dependent binding of 14-3-3 terminates signalling by the Gab2 docking protein.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: (a) 14-3-3 recruitment to activated EGFR and co-immunoprecipitation with the receptor, (b) SOS1 S1134/S1161 phosphorylation, 14-3-3 docking and Grb2/receptor dissociation, and (c) the prediction that 14-3-3 sequestration (difopein/knockdown) prolongs EGF-driven ERK output and receptor-associated GRB2/SOS1. Each component is published separately — 14-3-3ζ is an EGF-inducible EGFR-interacting protein (Oksvold 2004, though the association is described as rapid, is localised at the plasma membrane, and its function was left undetermined with no Grb2/SOS test), 14-3-3 docking on SOS1 at S1134/S1161 negatively regulates MAPK and the S1134A/S1161A mutant modestly increases and extends ERK activation (Saha 2012, which explicitly does not test Grb2 or receptor-complex association and speculates instead about SOS1 catalytic activity/Ras access), and 14-3-3 is known to uncouple an adaptor from Grb2 and hence from the receptor complex for Gab2 (Brummer 2008). No source states the specific proposed link: that 14-3-3 enters the activated EGFR complex with delayed kinetics and negatively regulates receptor-proximal output by displacing the Grb2–SOS1 module from EGFR without altering receptor autophosphorylation.

hypotheses.statement: EGFR directly tyrosine-phosphorylates IRS1, and the resulting bisphosphotyrosine IRS1 motif binds and allosterically activates SHP2, making IRS1 a substrate/adaptor that couples EGFR to SHP2-dependent ERK output.
hypotheses.mechanism: The EGFR-side evidence shows EGFR phosphorylates docking/adaptor proteins such as Shc and thereby alters their receptor affinity, and that among ErbB receptors SHP2/PTPN11 is the one protein binding EGFR phosphotyrosines with high affinity (KD < 500 nM), while EGFR-dependent and RTK/FRS2-dependent cell lines are the classes most sensitive to SHP2 loss. The IRS1-side evidence shows that a bisphosphorylated IRS-1-derived peptide (2P-IRS-1) is the standard allosteric activator of SHP2, engaging its tandem SH2 domains with AC50 values in the 0.2–0.4 μM range and driving the enzyme's catalytic activation. If EGFR kinase activity generates that tandem-pY IRS1 ligand, IRS1 would act as a direct EGFR substrate whose phosphorylation state licenses SHP2 activation in EGFR-driven cells, rather than being confined to insulin/IGF1R inputs.
hypotheses.prediction: Recombinant EGFR kinase domain should phosphorylate IRS1 fragments on the tandem tyrosines corresponding to the 2P-IRS-1 motif, EGFR-phosphorylated IRS1 should stimulate recombinant SHP2 phosphatase activity in a DiFMUP assay with an AC50 comparable to synthetic 2P-IRS-1 (and this stimulation should be blunted by SHP099), and in EGF-stimulated EGFR-amplified cells IRS1 immunoprecipitates should gain phosphotyrosine and co-precipitate SHP2 in an erlotinib-sensitive manner.
hypotheses.test: Two-part in vitro/cell assay: (1) incubate purified recombinant EGFR kinase domain with a purified IRS1 fragment spanning the candidate tandem-pY region plus ATP, read out site-specific phosphorylation by anti-phosphotyrosine western blot and LC-MS/MS, and then add the reaction product to recombinant SHP2 (1–525) in the DiFMUP phosphatase assay to measure activation AC50 versus synthetic 2P-IRS-1, using kinase-dead EGFR and Tyr→Phe IRS1 mutants as negatives; (2) in EGF-stimulated EGFR-amplified cells (e.g. MDA-MB-468) ± erlotinib, immunoprecipitate IRS1 and blot for phosphotyrosine and co-precipitated SHP2, scoring loss of both signals upon EGFR inhibition or Tyr→Phe IRS1 replacement as refutation.

citations.title: Insulin receptor substrate 1 is a novel member of EGFR signaling in pancreatic cells.
The COOH-terminal tyrosine phosphorylation sites on IRS-1 bind SHP-2 and negatively regulate insulin signaling.
Systems-level interactions between insulin-EGF networks amplify mitogenic signaling.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: (i) EGFR as a direct IRS1 tyrosine kinase, (ii) the IRS1 bisphosphotyrosine motif (pY1172/pY1222, the '2P-IRS-1' peptide) as an allosteric SHP2 activator, and (iii) the composite prediction of an EGF/erlotinib-sensitive IRS1–SHP2 complex driving ERK. Both halves are separately published — Takács et al. show EGFR binds and directly phosphorylates IRS1 (Y612, Y896) to drive MAPK, but via GRB2 and with no mention of SHP2/PTPN11; Myers et al. established that the IRS-1 COOH-terminal tandem tyrosines are the SHP-2 docking/activating sites, in an insulin-receptor context; Borisov et al. model IRS together with SHP2 as nodes amplifying Ras/ERK in EGF–insulin crosstalk, but there the IRS phosphorylation is insulin-receptor/PIP3-driven. I found nothing showing EGFR kinase generating the tandem-pY 2P-IRS-1 motif, EGFR-phosphorylated IRS1 allosterically activating recombinant SHP2, or an erlotinib-sensitive IRS1–SHP2 co-precipitation, so the specific connection remains unstated.

hypotheses.statement: EGFR activation negatively regulates IRS1 by driving serine phosphorylation of IRS1 that suppresses its tyrosine phosphorylation and stability.
hypotheses.mechanism: On the EGFR side, ERK pathway output is directly sustained by EGFR: a live-cell Fra-1-based reporter of ERK activity rises up to 7-fold on ERK induction and decays when EGFR is inhibited, so EGFR occupancy sets ERK activity in these cells. On the IRS1 side, MAPK is reported to phosphorylate the IRS1 docking protein alongside Gab1 and FRS2 as part of negative feedback on upstream regulators, and serine phosphorylation of IRS1 (e.g. Ser312 class sites) strongly inhibits IRS1 tyrosine phosphorylation and promotes its degradation. Together these imply that ligand-engaged EGFR should act as an upstream suppressor of IRS1 function, independent of insulin or IGF1R input.
hypotheses.prediction: EGF stimulation alone should increase IRS1 serine phosphorylation and lower IRS1 protein levels, and should reduce subsequent insulin-stimulated IRS1 tyrosine phosphorylation; both effects should be abolished by EGFR inhibition and by MEK/ERK inhibition, and should be attenuated on IRS1 in which the relevant serines are mutated to alanine.
hypotheses.test: In a cultured epithelial line, stimulate with EGF for 0–6 h ± erlotinib ± MEK inhibitor, then blot IRS1 total protein and phospho-serine sites and, after an acute insulin pulse, IRS1 phosphotyrosine (IRS1 immunoprecipitate) and downstream AKT phosphorylation; repeat in cells reconstituted with wild-type versus serine-to-alanine IRS1 to test whether the EGF-driven suppression requires those sites, with no suppression under erlotinib indicating the hypothesis is false.

citations.title: Feedback mechanisms promote cooperativity for small molecule inhibitors of epidermal and insulin-like growth factor receptors.
p38 mitogen-activated protein kinase-dependent transactivation of ErbB receptor family: a novel common mechanism for stress-induced IRS-1 serine phosphorylation and insulin resistance.
Angiotensin-induced EGF receptor transactivation inhibits insulin signaling in C9 hepatic cells.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the mechanism in words (EGF/EGFR-driven IRS-1 serine phosphorylation causing degradation and loss of tyrosine phosphorylation), the entities together (EGFR + IRS-1 + MEK/ERK + erlotinib/gefitinib), and the prediction (EGFR inhibition restoring IRS-1 function and insulin/IGF signalling), via PubMed/E-utilities, PMC and publisher pages. Retrieved work already states this explanation: Buck et al. show EGFR-directed MAPK activity sustains inhibitory IRS-1 serine phosphorylation and that erlotinib lowers it, improving signal flow through IRS-1 to Akt; Hemi et al. show ErbB/EGFR transactivation is the common route to IRS-1 serine phosphorylation (Ser307, Ser612, Ser632, Ser636/639) and insulin resistance, with ErbB antagonists attenuating it and restoring insulin-stimulated IRS-1 tyrosine phosphorylation; Andreozzi-type work in C9 hepatic cells shows EGFR transactivation drives IRS-1 Ser636/639 phosphorylation and proteasomal IRS-1 loss, blocked by the EGFR inhibitor AG1478 and the MEK inhibitor PD98059. Only the specific serine-to-alanine reconstitution test and pure EGF-alone time course remain incompletely covered, so the explanation itself is published rather than novel.

hypotheses.statement: MAPK14 (p38α) directly promotes TNF production by phosphorylating and activating MK2, which post-transcriptionally stabilizes and enhances translation of TNF mRNA.
hypotheses.mechanism: Claims about MAPK14 state that MK2 activation is completely dependent on p38α, which phosphorylates MK2 at Thr222, Ser272 and Thr334, that the two kinases reciprocally stabilize each other, and that deleting p38α in epithelial cells lowers proinflammatory gene expression. Independently, claims about TNF state that MK2 raises TNF-alpha output by promoting translation and/or stability of its mRNA, and that MK2-dependent phosphorylation of TTP creates 14-3-3-binding sites that block TTP-driven degradation of ARE-containing transcripts, contributing to LPS-induced TNF-alpha expression. If MK2's activating input comes exclusively from p38α, then p38α catalytic activity should itself be a rate-limiting determinant of TNF mRNA stability and TNF protein output, independent of transcription.
hypotheses.prediction: Loss or inhibition of p38α catalytic activity in LPS-stimulated cells should reduce secreted TNF protein and shorten TNF mRNA half-life without a proportional drop in TNF transcription, with loss of MK2 activation-site phosphorylation and of TTP phosphorylation/14-3-3 binding; expressing a constitutively active, p38α-independent MK2 should restore TNF output despite p38α inhibition.
hypotheses.test: In an LPS-responsive macrophage-like or epithelial cell line, compare wild-type cells, p38α-knockout/siRNA cells, and cells treated with SB203580 or with CMPD1 (which selectively blocks p38α phosphorylation of MK2 without blocking ATF2 phosphorylation or p38α–MK2 binding): measure secreted TNF by ELISA, TNF mRNA decay by actinomycin D chase with qPCR, nascent TNF transcription by nuclear run-on or intron-spanning qPCR, and immunoblot MK2 phospho-Thr222/Thr334 plus TTP phosphorylation with 14-3-3 co-immunoprecipitation; then rescue with a constitutively active MK2 mutant to confirm that the TNF defect lies downstream of the p38α-to-MK2 step.

citations.title: The p38 MAP kinase pathway signals for cytokine-induced mRNA stabilization via MAP kinase-activated protein kinase 2 and an AU-rich region-targeted mechanism.
Mitogen-activated protein kinase p38 controls the expression and posttranslational modification of tristetraprolin, a regulator of tumor necrosis factor alpha mRNA stability.

Mitogen-activated protein kinase-activated protein kinase 2 regulates tumor necrosis factor mRNA stability and translation mainly by altering tristetraprolin expression, stability, and binding to adenine/uridine-rich element.
Macrophage deletion of p38alpha partially impairs lipopolysaccharide-induced cellular activation.

novelty.note: I searched for the plain-language mechanism (p38 acting through MK2 to stabilize/translate TNF mRNA), the entity combination (p38alpha + MK2 + tristetraprolin + 14-3-3 + ARE), and the prediction (p38 inhibition shortening TNF mRNA half-life, constitutively active MK2 rescue). The p38–MK2–TTP axis controlling TNF mRNA stability and translation post-transcriptionally is a long-established, primary-literature mechanism: Winzen et al. showed p38-dependent ARE-targeted mRNA stabilization requires MK2 (with active MK2 sufficient and dominant-negative MK2 blocking), Mahtani et al. showed p38 inhibition by SB203580 blocks TTP induction/phosphorylation and TNF mRNA stabilization, and Hitti et al. showed MK2 controls TNF mRNA stability and translation mainly via TTP expression, stability and ARE binding; Kang et al. showed macrophage p38alpha deletion selectively impairs LPS-induced TNF. Because published work already states this explanation for this phenomenon, including the isoform-specific p38alpha requirement, the status is established rather than partial.

hypotheses.statement: mTORC1 directly and negatively regulates NF-κB transcriptional activity by sustaining cap-dependent translation of the short-lived inhibitor IκB, so that mTORC1 inhibition de-represses NF-κB.
hypotheses.mechanism: mTORC1's principal growth output in the cited evidence is control of cap-dependent translation through the 4E-BP/eIF4E axis, with eIF4E function acutely rapamycin-sensitive (fruman2017:findings:009). Independently, NF-κB is held inactive by IκB whose short half-life makes its steady-state level dependent on ongoing translation, and global translation inhibition activates NF-κB purely by lowering IκB (costamattioli2020:findings:019); NF-κB's own shutoff likewise requires newly synthesized IκB (chen2002:findings:007). Because mTORC1 sets the rate of eIF4E-dependent synthesis, mTORC1 activity should set the IκB replenishment rate and therefore the basal and post-stimulus amplitude/duration of NF-κB activity.
hypotheses.prediction: Acute mTORC1 inhibition (rapamycin/TOR kinase inhibitor) or expression of non-phosphorylatable 4E-BP1 should lower IκBα protein without lowering IκBα mRNA, increase basal NF-κB nuclear translocation and κB-reporter output, and markedly prolong NF-κB nuclear residence after TNF by blunting IκB resynthesis; conversely, cells with hyperactive mTORC1 (e.g., GATOR1-null-like constitutive signaling) should show higher IκBα and faster NF-κB shutoff.
hypotheses.test: In a cultured cell line carrying a κB-luciferase reporter (or GFP-RelA for imaging), compare vehicle, rapamycin, and a TOR kinase inhibitor, plus doxycycline-inducible 4E-BP1-4A and eIF4E knockdown: measure IκBα protein by immunoblot alongside IκBα mRNA by qPCR, IκBα synthesis rate by cycloheximide chase/puromycin-pulse or 35S pulse-labeling on immunoprecipitated IκBα, and NF-κB nuclear translocation/reporter activity at baseline and over a TNF time course; decisive rescue arm is constitutive re-expression of IκBα from a heterologous cassette, which should abolish the mTORC1-inhibition-induced NF-κB activation if the link runs through IκB translation, while failure to rescue (or unchanged IκBα synthesis) rules the hypothesis out.

citations.title: Translational repression mediates activation of nuclear factor kappa B by phosphorylated translation initiation factor 2.
The TSC-mTOR signaling pathway regulates the innate inflammatory response.
Akt-dependent regulation of NF-{kappa}B is controlled by mTOR and Raptor in association with IKK.
Raptor-Mediated Proteasomal Degradation of Deamidated 4E-BP2 Regulates Postnatal Neuronal Translation and NF-κB Activity.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the mechanism in words (translational repression lowering short-lived IκBα to de-repress NF-κB), the entities together (mTORC1/rapamycin/4E-BP/eIF4E with IκBα, NFKBIA, cap-dependent translation), and the prediction (rapamycin/torin lowering IκBα protein without mRNA change, prolonged post-TNF nuclear NF-κB, TSC2-null/hyperactive mTORC1 giving faster shutoff). The component mechanism is firmly published for the ISR arm — eIF2α-phosphorylation-driven translational repression depletes IκBα without increasing its phosphorylation/degradation and thereby activates NF-κB (Deng et al. 2004) — and the phenomenological direction (mTOR as a negative regulator of NF-κB: rapamycin enhances NF-κB-dependent proinflammatory output while TSC2 deletion diminishes NF-κB) is published in myeloid cells by Weichhart et al. 2008, but that work attributes it to pathway crosstalk/transcriptional regulation and does not test IκBα synthesis, 4E-BP/eIF4E, or IκBα mRNA-versus-protein. No source I retrieved states that mTORC1 sustains cap-dependent IκB translation; the nearest mTORC1-specific work reports the opposite sign (mTOR/Raptor–IKK promoting NF-κB, with IκBα levels unchanged by rapamycin) and the nearest 4E-BP-to-NF-κB work found that increased 4E-BP2 repression *inhibits* NF-κB activity without identifying IκB as a translational target, so the specific link and prediction remain unpublished.

hypotheses.statement: SYK directly activates the Ras–Raf–MAPK module via its phosphorylated interdomain-B tyrosines, which recruit PLCγ1 and thereby drive PKC-dependent Raf/MAPK activation.
hypotheses.mechanism: The SYK evidence states that phosphorylated Tyr342 and Tyr346 bind the C-terminal SH2 domain of PLCγ1 and that these sites are required for ITAM-receptor signalling output, and that SYK signalling downstream of CLEC7A induces cytokine and chemokine production specifically via ERK as well as NFAT and NF-κB. The MAPK evidence independently defines a PLCγ→PKC→Raf→MAPK route in which PKC activation of MAPK is sufficient to switch the module into a sustained active state. Joining only what each side states, SYK's PLCγ1-docking tyrosines provide exactly the upstream input that the modelled PLCγ–PKC arm needs to turn on MAPK, so SYK should act as an upstream activator of MAPK rather than merely coexisting with it; consistent with this, tyrosine kinases can activate MAPK effector kinases and their substrates without engaging the canonical upstream tier.
hypotheses.prediction: In a SYK-dependent cell line, receptor stimulation should produce SYK-linker-tyrosine-dependent ERK1/2 activation-loop phosphorylation and downstream MAPK substrate phosphorylation: SYK inhibition or loss abolishes it, wild-type SYK re-expression restores it, and a Y342F/Y346F SYK mutant that cannot dock PLCγ1 fails to restore it despite retaining kinase activity; the residual ERK signal should be further blocked by PLCγ or PKC inhibition, and sustained ERK output should show a threshold dependence on stimulus strength/duration rather than graded scaling.
hypotheses.test: Reconstitute a SYK-null cultured cell line (CRISPR knockout, e.g. DT40-style B cell or a myeloid line) with vector, wild-type SYK, kinase-dead SYK, and Y342F/Y346F SYK; stimulate the ITAM-coupled receptor and immunoblot a time course for phospho-ERK1/2 (Thr202/Tyr204), phospho-MEK, and a MAPK-dependent substrate (e.g. RSK-mediated rpS6 Ser235/236), with parallel arms treated with a SYK inhibitor, a PLCγ inhibitor, or a PKC inhibitor; co-immunoprecipitate SYK with PLCγ1 in each background to confirm the docking step. Loss of ERK phosphorylation only in the SYK-null and Y342F/Y346F conditions supports SYK as a direct upstream activator of MAPK through PLCγ1/PKC, whereas unchanged ERK phosphorylation across all SYK variants rules the relationship out.

novelty.note: I searched for the SYK linker-tyrosine (Y342/Y346) → PLCγ1 docking → ERK link, for SYK→PLCγ→PKC→Ras/Raf/ERK in B cells/mast cells/platelets, and for the CLEC7A(Dectin-1)→SYK→PLCγ→ERK arm. The explanation is already published: Syk-deficient primary mast cells reconstituted with linker-tyrosine mutants show that Tyr342/Tyr346 are required for PLCγ1/PLCγ2 phosphorylation and for ERK phosphorylation (PMID 15576379, which also dissociates the two, ERK depending more on Y346), Syk is shown to feed Ras/ERK through phosphorylation of conventional PKC isoforms and Grb2/Sos recruitment (PMID 12881490), and PLCγ2 is required for ERK activation downstream of Dectin-1/Syk (PMID 19136564), with PLCγ/PKC input to BCR-induced ERK established in B cells (PMID 11976336). Only the appended bistability/threshold aspect of the prediction is not joined to SYK in these sources, which is not enough to make the core explanation novel.

hypotheses.statement: SHP2 acts directly on GRB2 complexes by dephosphorylating the phosphotyrosine docking sites that GRB2's SH2 domain reads, thereby controlling where GRB2–SOS1 complexes assemble and how long they persist.
hypotheses.mechanism: GRB2 is a single-SH2/two-SH3 adaptor whose recruitment depends entirely on binding tyrosine-phosphorylated partners generated by activated receptors (lowenstein1992:findings:004, lowenstein1992:findings:000), and those pTyr sites dictate its output: GRB2 is the dominant source of stable SOS membrane recruitment (huang2019:findings:003, huang2019:findings:008), while a competing pTyr site on Sprouty1/2 (Y53/Y55) can pull GRB2 away from FRS2 (lake2016:findings:015). SHP2 is a catalytically required, RAS-upstream node in RTK-driven cells — its phosphatase-dead mutant fails to restore p-ERK (chen2016:findings:003) and KRASG12V makes cells indifferent to SHP2 loss (chen2016:findings:004) — and it is itself switched on ~100-fold by engaging phosphotyrosine ligands through its tandem SH2 domains (alonso2004:findings:014), placing its active site on the same pTyr-decorated scaffolds GRB2 occupies. The simplest direct relation consistent with both sets of claims is that SHP2 selectively hydrolyses GRB2-binding phosphotyrosines, releasing GRB2 from non-productive/decoy sites and thus licensing GRB2-dependent SOS loading.
hypotheses.prediction: Purified activated SHP2 should dephosphorylate GRB2 SH2 ligand phosphopeptides (e.g. Sprouty pY53/pY55, FRS2 and EGFR-tail GRB2 sites) and strip pre-bound GRB2 from them in a SHP099-sensitive, catalysis-dependent manner; conversely, SHP2 inhibition in EGFR-amplified cells should increase GRB2 association with decoy pTyr partners, decrease GRB2–SOS1 co-precipitation at the receptor, and lower p-ERK, whereas GRB2 partner occupancy should be unchanged in KRAS/BRAF-mutant cells where SHP2 is dispensable.
hypotheses.test: Two-part in vitro/cell assay: (1) immobilize synthetic GRB2-binding phosphopeptides (Sprouty pY55, FRS2, EGFR C-tail pTyr) on beads, pre-load with recombinant GRB2, then add purified wild-type SHP2, catalytically dead SHP2C459S, or wild-type SHP2 plus SHP099, and quantify released GRB2 by immunoblot alongside phosphate release/anti-pTyr loss — GRB2 release should track SHP2 catalytic activity; (2) in MDA-MB-468 cells treated ±0.25–1 µM SHP099, immunoprecipitate GRB2 and blot for SOS1, Sprouty and EGFR, using A2058 (BRAF-mutant, SHP2-independent) as the negative control.

novelty.note: I searched for SHP2 dephosphorylating Grb2 SH2 docking sites, for SHP2/Sprouty pTyr53–pTyr55/Grb2 release, and for SHP2 substrate selectivity among EGFR phosphosites. Hanafusa et al. (JBC 2004) already state and demonstrate exactly this explanation: Sprouty is a direct Shp2 substrate, Shp2 dephosphorylates its Grb2-docking pTyr in vitro and in cells, Grb2 dissociates from Sprouty, and RTK/MAPK signalling is thereby restored; a 2022 review restates it as pTyr53/pTyr55 dephosphorylation dissociating Grb2–Spry and returning Grb2 to FRS2, which is the corpus link the hypothesis proposes. The generalisation to EGFR C-tail Grb2 sites is the weakest part — published substrate-specificity work shows SHP2's active site selects acidic (−2) contexts such as EGFR pY992/HER2 pY1023 (RasGAP sites) rather than the canonical Grb2 sites — so that portion is cited as the nearest work rather than as anticipation.

hypotheses.statement: NGF signalling directly engages SRC-family kinase activity, and Src activity is required for the sustained ERK1/2 output and ERK1/2-effector coupling that distinguishes NGF from EGF stimulation.
hypotheses.mechanism: The NGF claims establish that NGF's defining feature in PC-12 cells is a long-lived, positive-feedback-supported ERK1/2 activation with nuclear translocation and tyrosine phosphorylation of additional substrates (e.g. the 80 kDa SNT) not seen with EGF (lake2016:findings:016, marshall1995:findings:004), i.e. sustained ERK requires extra tyrosine-kinase input beyond the transient Ras-ERK burst. The SRC claims independently show that Src activation drives tyrosine phosphorylation of RSK2 that stabilises ERK1/2 binding to RSK2 and promotes its activation (cargnello2011:findings:059), and that Src is a broadly active tyrosine kinase capable of generating large numbers of upregulated pY sites when active (bradley2024:findings:002). Together these imply that the NGF-specific sustained-ERK/tyrosine-phosphorylation state is produced in part by NGF-induced Src activity acting on ERK-pathway components rather than by Ras-ERK core kinetics alone.
hypotheses.prediction: In NGF-stimulated PC-12 cells, Src should become activated with kinetics tracking the sustained (not the transient) phase, RSK2 tyrosine phosphorylation and ERK1/2-RSK2 association should rise under NGF but much less under EGF, and pharmacological or genetic loss of Src should selectively truncate the sustained NGF-ERK phase (converting it toward an EGF-like transient profile), reduce ERK1/2 nuclear accumulation and RSK2 activation, and blunt neurite outgrowth, while leaving the first ERK peak amplitude largely intact.
hypotheses.test: Stimulate PC-12 cells with NGF or EGF in parallel and, in a time course over 5-120 min, immunoblot for Src pTyr416/pTyr527, phospho-ERK1/2, RSK2 phospho-tyrosine and RSK2 activation-loop phosphorylation, with co-immunoprecipitation of ERK1/2 with RSK2; repeat under a Src-family inhibitor (e.g. PP2 with PP3 as inactive control) and under siRNA knockdown of Src, scoring (i) ERK activation duration and nuclear translocation by immunofluorescence, (ii) RSK2 tyrosine phosphorylation and ERK1/2-RSK2 co-IP, and (iii) neurite outgrowth at 48 h; loss of the sustained NGF-specific ERK phase and of NGF-induced RSK2 pTyr/ERK binding upon Src loss supports the relationship, whereas unchanged ERK duration and unchanged RSK2 pTyr would rule it out.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: (i) Src-family requirement for sustained vs transient ERK in NGF- and EGF-stimulated PC-12 cells, (ii) Src/SFK inhibitor (PP2, SU6656) effects on ERK duration, nuclear translocation and neuritogenesis, and (iii) Src-dependent tyrosine phosphorylation of RSK2 and ERK1/2–RSK2 coupling. The individual mechanistic pieces are published — Src acts upstream of Ras and is required for NGF-induced neuritogenesis (Kremer 1991), Src activity is required for sustained ERK1/2 activation, ERK nuclear translocation and process formation in PC-12 cells (though shown for MG-132-induced, not NGF-induced, differentiation), and Src-family phosphorylation of RSK2 at Tyr-529 stabilises ERK binding and is needed for RSK2 activation (Kang 2008, demonstrated downstream of EGF, not NGF). However, no source states the composite NGF-specific claim, and the nearest PC-12 work runs partly counter to the prediction: SFK activity in lipid rafts terminates EGF-ERK signalling (PP2/SU6656 make EGF-ERK sustained and pro-differentiative), and NGF produces sustained down-regulation of active Src rather than sustained Src activation — hence 'partial'.

hypotheses.statement: GSK3B directly phosphorylates RAPTOR at sites created by prior (primed) phosphorylation, acting as an inhibitory input to mTORC1 through the RAPTOR subunit.
hypotheses.mechanism: RAPTOR is established as a regulatory phospho-acceptor node in mTORC1: RSK phosphorylates Raptor in the Ras/MAPK arm (cargnello2011:findings:035) and AMPK inhibits mTORC1 specifically by phosphorylating RAPTOR independently of TSC2 (herzig2018:findings:006), so RAPTOR phosphorylation is a general mechanism for setting mTORC1 output. GSK3B is a processive, priming-dependent Ser/Thr kinase that preferentially selects substrate motifs containing an already-phosphorylated Thr/Ser (johnson2023:findings:003) and uses this to mark substrates functionally, as when it phosphorylates PHLPP to trigger its turnover under AKT control (haeusler2018:findings:007). Because RSK- or AMPK-deposited phosphates on RAPTOR would generate exactly the primed acceptor context GSK3B prefers, GSK3B is predicted to add a second, downstream phosphate on RAPTOR that dampens mTORC1 activity, placing an AKT→GSK3B→RAPTOR branch alongside the known AKT→GSK3B→PHLPP branch.
hypotheses.prediction: Recombinant GSK3B will phosphorylate purified RAPTOR efficiently only after RAPTOR has been pre-phosphorylated by a priming kinase (RSK or AMPK), yielding GSK3-dependent phosphosites positioned ~4 residues N-terminal to the primed site; in cells, GSK3 inhibition or GSK3A/GSK3B deletion will selectively lose these RAPTOR phosphosites and raise mTORC1 output (S6K1 and 4EBP1 phosphorylation), while a RAPTOR mutant with the GSK3 acceptor serines changed to alanine will be insensitive to GSK3 inhibition.
hypotheses.test: Immunopurify FLAG-RAPTOR from HEK-293T cells, split it into reactions with and without prior in vitro priming by recombinant RSK or AMPK, then perform a [γ-32P]ATP kinase assay with recombinant GSK3B ± a GSK3 inhibitor and map phosphosites by LC-MS/MS to test priming dependence and identify the acceptor residues; in parallel, treat cells with a GSK3 inhibitor (or use GSK3A/B-null cells) and immunoblot RAPTOR phosphosite-specific signal, RAPTOR–mTOR co-immunoprecipitation, and p-S6K1/p-4EBP1, comparing wild-type RAPTOR with a phospho-site alanine mutant reconstituted into RAPTOR-knockdown cells.

citations.title: GSK3-mediated raptor phosphorylation supports amino-acid-dependent mTORC1-directed signalling.

novelty.note: I searched for GSK3-raptor phosphorylation, priming-dependent GSK3 substrates in mTORC1, and for reports that GSK3 inhibition raises mTORC1 output. The core mechanism is already published: Stretton et al. (Biochem J 2015) show recombinant GSK3β phosphorylates raptor on Ser859 in a manner primed by Ser863 (the hierarchical Ser863→Ser859 relationship having been established by Foster et al., JBC 2010, where Ser863 is phosphorylated downstream of PI3K/Rheb/mTORC1, not by RSK or AMPK), and Inoki et al. (Cell 2006) already established an AMPK-primed, GSK3-mediated inhibitory input to mTORC1 — but at TSC2, not raptor. The hypothesis is therefore only partially novel and its directional prediction is contradicted: GSK3-mediated raptor Ser859 phosphorylation supports mTOR–raptor interaction and GSK3 inhibition or the S859A mutant lowers, rather than raises, S6K1/4E-BP1/ULK1 phosphorylation.

hypotheses.statement: JAK1 activity acts as an activating input to ERK, sustaining ERK pathway output (pulse frequency and downstream Fra-1 accumulation) in parallel with, and not requiring, EGFR stimulation.
hypotheses.mechanism: chen2016:findings:012 reports that cells carrying JAK1 alterations are sensitive to SHP099 while RAS- or BRAF-mutant cells are resistant, i.e. JAK1-driven growth signalling is routed through a node that RAS/BRAF mutation bypasses, placing JAK1 upstream of the RAS-ERK module. albeck2013:findings:013 shows that ERK activity pulses persist under saturating EGF and partial EGFR inhibition, so pulse generation depends on intracellular signalling components rather than receptor ligand supply, leaving room for a non-EGFR kinase input; albeck2013:findings:015 shows that the fraction of pERK-positive cells (pulse frequency) is set by receptor-level activity while amplitude is set by MEK, so an additional upstream kinase such as JAK1 should register specifically as a change in pulse frequency and in the pERK-positive fraction.
hypotheses.prediction: Pharmacological or genetic loss of JAK1 in ERK-reporter epithelial cells will reduce the fraction of pERK-positive cells and shorten/rarefy EKAR-EV ERK bursts (frequency modulation) without lowering the amplitude of the remaining 'on' state, and will produce a graded drop in Fra-1 immunofluorescence; conversely, expression of hyperactive JAK1 (V657F) will raise the pERK-positive fraction and Fra-1 level even at fixed or saturating EGF.
hypotheses.test: In MCF-10A cells stably expressing EKAR-EV and the FIRE/Fra-1 reporter held at steady state, apply a JAK1-selective inhibitor or JAK1 siRNA/CRISPR knockout (with a JAK1-deficient fibrosarcoma-type line and JAK1 re-expression as the complementation arm) at both low (50 pg/ml) and saturating (20,000 pg/ml) EGF, and score by live single-cell FRET the pulse duration, inter-pulse interval and fraction of time ERK is 'on', plus high-content pERK and Fra-1 immunofluorescence distributions; a gain-of-function arm expressing JAK1-V657F is read out the same way. Frequency-selective shifts in the pERK-positive fraction that track JAK1 dosage, persisting under saturating EGF, support the relationship; unchanged ERK pulse statistics under complete JAK1 loss rule it out.

citations.title: SHP2 inhibition displays efficacy as a monotherapy and in combination with JAK2 inhibition in preclinical models of myeloproliferative neoplasms.
Receptor Level Mechanisms Are Required for Epidermal Growth Factor (EGF)-stimulated Extracellular Signal-regulated Kinase (ERK) Activity Pulses.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the mechanism in words (JAK kinase as an activating input upstream of RAS-ERK, via SHP2/Grb2-SOS), the entities together (JAK1 + ERK + SHP2/EGFR-independence, JAK1 V657F + ERK/Fra-1, JAK1-deficient cells + ERK), and the prediction (JAK/cytokine control of ERK pulse frequency, pERK-positive fraction and FIRE/Fra-1 in MCF-10A live-cell FRET). The generic half is published: in MPN models SHP2 inhibition places SHP2 downstream of JAK2 and upstream of RAS-GTP/ERK, i.e. JAK-driven growth signalling is routed into the RAS-ERK module through a node RAS/BRAF mutation bypasses; many cytokine papers also report JAK1-associated ERK/MAPK activation. I found nothing stating the specific connection — a JAK1 input that sets ERK pulse frequency / pERK-positive fraction and graded Fra-1 in epithelial cells in parallel with and independent of EGFR; the closest dynamics work attributes pulse frequency generation specifically to receptor(EGFR)-level mechanisms, and the systematic optogenetic screen of nodes shaping ERK dynamics contained no JAK family members, so the status is partial.

hypotheses.statement: GRB2 binds directly to autophosphorylated SYK, docking via its SH2 domain onto phosphotyrosines in the SYK interdomain B/linker region (the Tyr342/Tyr346/Tyr624 cluster) and thereby coupling activated SYK to SOS1 recruitment.
hypotheses.mechanism: SYK is autophosphorylated on ~ten tyrosines, and the characterized linker phosphotyrosines function specifically as SH2-domain docking sites — phospho-Tyr342 binds the VAV1 SH2 domain, phospho-Tyr342/Tyr346 bind the PLCγ1 C-terminal SH2 domain, and phospho-Tyr624 binds the SLP65 SH2 domain (mcsai2010:findings:008, mcsai2010:findings:012, mcsai2010:findings:013). GRB2 is an SH2-plus-two-SH3 adaptor whose SH2 domain binds tyrosine-phosphorylated proteins in stimulated lysates, and full-length GRB2 captured several phosphoproteins beyond the receptor itself, with the N-terminal SH3 enhancing SH2 binding (lowenstein1992:findings:004, lowenstein1992:findings:005). Since GRB2 is the dominant element for stable SOS membrane recruitment (huang2019:findings:003, huang2019:findings:008), a GRB2 SH2–phospho-SYK interaction would place SOS1 directly on an activated SYK scaffold.
hypotheses.prediction: Purified GRB2, and its isolated SH2 domain, should bind autophosphorylated SYK but not unphosphorylated SYK, with binding recapitulated by synthetic SYK phosphopeptides spanning Tyr342/Tyr346 and Tyr624 and abolished by Y→F substitution of those tyrosines; in cells, SYK activation should yield a GRB2–SYK co-immunoprecipitate that also contains SOS1 and is lost in the phospho-null SYK mutant or upon GRB2 SH2 (R86K-type) inactivation.
hypotheses.test: Autophosphorylate recombinant SYK in vitro with ATP (and a kinase-dead or Y342/346/624F variant as controls), then perform GST pulldowns with GST–GRB2 full-length, GST–GRB2 SH2 alone, and the individual SH3 fusions, immunoblotting bound material for SYK; in parallel, quantify affinity by fluorescence-polarization or surface-plasmon titration of GRB2 SH2 against phospho- versus non-phospho SYK linker peptides, and confirm in cells by reciprocal co-immunoprecipitation of GRB2 and SYK (±SYK inhibitor, ±SYK Y→F mutant) with blotting for SOS1.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: (i) GRB2 SH2 docking on SYK interdomain-B/linker phosphotyrosines (Y342/Y346/Y624), (ii) the entities together (SYK + GRB2 + SOS1 co-IP / direct association), and (iii) the prediction (phosphopeptide binding, Y→F loss, GRB2 R86K) using PubMed, Europe PMC full-text search, PMC and publisher pages. The direct-binding half is already published in general terms: Geahlen's BCR review states that GRB2 is among the SH2 proteins docking on the SYK linker region and that GRB2 binds preferentially to a SYK-derived phosphopeptide modified only on Y346 (offering an explanation for the ERK coupling defect of Y346 mutants), while structural work on this tandem site characterises VAV1/PLCγ1 recognition and notes that GRB2-type SH2 domains lack the second-pocket lysine and do not bind the doubly phosphorylated pY342/pY346 peptide well. I found nothing stating the specific package proposed here — GRB2 SH2 binding to autophosphorylated SYK including pY624, its abolition in phospho-null SYK, and a GRB2–SYK–SOS1 complex placing SOS1 on an activated SYK scaffold; published SYK→GRB2/SOS coupling instead runs through separate substrates (e.g. Syk-phosphorylated PKC creating the GRB2 SH2 site, or BLNK/LAT/Shc), so this is partial rather than established.

hypotheses.statement: TGFBR1 (TβRI) directly but inefficiently engages SMAD1 at the receptor L45–Smad L3 interface, acting as a low-affinity kinase that can C-terminally phosphorylate SMAD1 when TβRI is strongly/constitutively activated, with the Smad1 L3 residues His425/Asp428 being the determinant that normally restricts this direct interaction.
hypotheses.mechanism: The corpus states that swapping just two L3-loop residues between Smad1 (His425, Asp428) and Smad2 (Arg427, Thr430) switches which type I receptor each Smad interacts with and which one activates it (hata2016:findings:012), which implies that discrimination between TβRI and SMAD1 is a two-residue affinity threshold at a shared physical interface rather than an absolute structural incompatibility. TβRI is independently described as recruiting and activating effector Smads in a manner promoted by its own phosphorylation-dependent Lys389 sumoylation (derynck2019:findings:014), and SMAD1 is described as requiring a catalytically active type I receptor for its transcriptional activation, since kinase-defective receptor mutants fail to activate GAL4-Smad1 (liu1996:findings:005). Together these imply that an activated TβRI kinase domain can contact and phosphorylate SMAD1 directly, and that the reported lack of SMAD1 responsiveness to TGF-β in cells (liu1996:findings:006) reflects weak L3-mediated recruitment at endogenous receptor activity rather than absence of a direct receptor–substrate relationship.
hypotheses.prediction: Constitutively active or highly overexpressed TβRI will co-immunoprecipitate with SMAD1 and drive detectable SMAD1 C-terminal SXS phosphorylation above BMP-receptor-independent background, at markedly lower efficiency than SMAD2/3; the Smad1 L3 swap mutant (H425R/D428T) will show strongly increased TβRI co-precipitation and TGF-β-inducible SMAD1 SXS phosphorylation, while a kinase-dead TβRI or the TβRI K389R sumoylation-deficient mutant will abolish or reduce it.
hypotheses.test: In a cell line lacking endogenous SMAD1 signal contribution (e.g. SMAD1-knockdown HEK293 or NMuMG), co-express Flag-SMAD1 wild type or the H425R/D428T L3-swap mutant with HA-TβRI (wild type, constitutively active T204D, kinase-dead K232R, or K389R), stimulate with TGF-β, and assay (i) anti-HA co-immunoprecipitation of Flag-SMAD1 and (ii) phospho-Smad1/5 (SXS) immunoblot of the Flag immunoprecipitate; confirm directness with an in vitro kinase assay using immunoprecipitated or recombinant TβRI kinase domain plus bacterially expressed GST-SMAD1 versus GST-SMAD2 and ATP, scoring SXS phosphorylation, with a BMP type I receptor kinase and a TβRI kinase inhibitor (SB-431542) as specificity controls.

citations.title: Transforming Growth Factor {beta} Can Stimulate Smad1 Phosphorylation Independently of Bone Morphogenic Protein Receptors.
