novelty.note: I searched three ways: the mechanism in plain words (mTOR lysosomal localization gating de novo lipogenesis/SREBP-1), the entities together (GATOR1/DEPDC5/NPRL2 and SAMTOR with lipogenesis, SREBP, FASN), and the prediction (localization-specific manipulations changing lipogenic flux; lysosome-independent mTORC1 activation). Published work firmly links mTORC1 activity to SREBP-dependent de novo lipogenesis and links Rag/GATOR/SAMTOR to mTOR's lysosomal positioning, but I found no source that makes lysosomal localization itself the gating step for lipogenic flux, nor any paired measurement of mTOR–LAMP2 colocalization with lipid labeling under GATOR1 deletion or SAMTOR overexpression; no direct negative test was found either. The nearest published work ties mTORC1 activity (not its localization) to de novo lipid synthesis and to lysosome-dependent lipid remodeling.

hypotheses.statement: CDK1 acts as a direct mTOR-independent kinase for canonical mTORC1/S6K output sites, converging on the same substrate node as mTOR (functional redundancy between CDK1 and mTOR at S6-type sites).
hypotheses.mechanism: Cdk1 recruited to condensates phosphorylated peptides lacking its own primary specificity determinants, including RPS6 Ser235/236 (sang2022:findings:009), and CDK1 is separately documented to phosphorylate a substrate sequence designed for a different kinase, generating signal wrongly attributed to that kinase (gest2024:findings:192) — i.e. CDK1 can occupy other kinases' substrate sites when co-localized. Independently, mTOR inhibition is defined operationally by loss of mTOR-motif and p70S6K substrate site phosphorylation (bekkerjensen2020:findings:016) and reduces p70S6K/mTOR substrate group enrichment (casado2013:findings:004). If CDK1 can phosphorylate S6-type sites directly, part of that 'mTOR-pathway' phosphosignal should be CDK1-generated and therefore refractory to mTOR inhibition.
hypotheses.prediction: Purified CDK1/cyclin B should phosphorylate recombinant RPS6 (and S6K-motif peptides) at Ser235/236 in vitro without any mTOR or S6K present; in cells, a residual pS6 Ser235/236 signal should persist after saturating mTOR kinase inhibition, be highest in mitotic/high-CDK1-activity cells, and be eliminated by CDK1 inhibition or CDK1 depletion, whereas mTOR-only-dependent sites (e.g. 4EBP1-type mTOR-motif sites) should be fully lost with mTOR inhibition alone.
hypotheses.test: Two-part, standard-lab: (1) in vitro kinase assay with recombinant active CDK1/cyclin B plus recombinant RPS6 or S6 peptides, ±ATP, ±CDK1 inhibitor (RO-3306), read out by phospho-Ser235/236 immunoblot and by phosphopeptide LC-MS/MS to map sites; (2) in cultured cells (e.g. HEK-293T or RPE1), treat with Torin1/rapamycin alone, RO-3306 alone, or both, in asynchronous versus nocodazole-arrested populations, and immunoblot pS6 Ser235/236, pS6K, and p4EBP1 — plus siRNA knockdown of CDK1 as an independent loss-of-function control. Persistence of pSer235/236 under mTOR inhibition that collapses only when CDK1 is inhibited/depleted, together with direct in vitro phosphorylation, supports the relationship; absence of in vitro phosphorylation and complete Torin1-sensitivity of the site rules it out.

citations.title: CDK1 substitutes for mTOR kinase to activate mitotic cap-dependent protein translation.
CDK1 couples proliferation with protein synthesis.
Evidence for cell cycle-dependent, rapamycin-resistant phosphorylation of ribosomal protein S6 at S240/244.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the mechanism in words (CDK1 as an mTOR-independent kinase at mTORC1/S6K output sites), the entities together (CDK1/cyclin B + RPS6 Ser235/236 + Torin/rapamycin/RO-3306), and the prediction (residual mitotic pS6 resistant to mTOR inhibition but CDK1-dependent). The general redundancy is published: Shuda et al. show CDK1/cyclin B directly phosphorylates canonical mTOR sites on 4E-BP1 in vitro and in mitosis in an mTOR-inhibitor-resistant manner ('CDK1 substitutes for mTOR'), and Haneke et al. report that CDK1 inhibition strongly dephosphorylates RPS6 Ser235/236 while CDK1's effect on translation is independent of mTOR activity; a separate study documents rapamycin-resistant, cell-cycle-dependent S6 phosphorylation by unidentified kinase activity. However, no source states that CDK1 is a direct kinase for RPS6 Ser235/236, and the specific prediction is partly contradicted in the published work (Shuda report pS6 Ser235/236 is nearly ablated by the mTOR inhibitor PP242 but not by RO-3306; Haneke conclude RPS6 phosphorylation is not directly involved and do not claim direct CDK1 catalysis), so the specific substrate-node claim and its prediction remain unpublished.

hypotheses.statement: Constitutively active BRAF (B-RafV600E) directly suppresses the proteasomal degradation of Sprouty2, so that inhibiting BRAF shifts Spry2 into a rapidly degraded state.
hypotheses.mechanism: In B-RafV600E cells Spry1/2 are functionally engaged as active feedback brakes, since knocking them down raises Ras-GTP levels, implying that mutant BRAF signalling sustains a pool of Spry protein (lake2016:findings:020). Independently, Spry2 protein stability is set post-translationally: phosphorylation of Ser112/Ser121 protects it, whereas Ala substitution of these sites or inhibition of the upstream kinase drives Spry2 degradation (cargnello2011:findings:066), a route that would run through the proteasome, which accounts for at least 80% of protein degradation in growing mammalian cells (collins2017:findings:000). Because the kinase output that writes those stabilizing marks lies downstream of Raf, constitutive BRAF activity should hold Spry2 in its stabilized, long-lived state, making Spry2 turnover a direct output of BRAF activity.
hypotheses.prediction: In BRAF-mutant cells, acute BRAF (or MEK1/2) inhibition should cause loss of Spry2 Ser112/Ser121 phosphorylation followed by a sharp shortening of Spry2 protein half-life and accumulation of poly-ubiquitylated Spry2, with the drop in Spry2 protein rescued by proteasome inhibition; conversely, expressing B-RafV600E in BRAF-wild-type cells should lengthen Spry2 half-life, and phospho-mimetic S112E/S121E Spry2 should remain stable regardless of BRAF inhibition.
hypotheses.test: In a BRAF V600E cell line, run a cycloheximide chase for endogenous and tagged Spry2 (wild-type, S112A/S121A, S112E/S121E) with vehicle, vemurafenib, vemurafenib + MG132/bortezomib, and MG132 alone; immunoblot Spry2 decay curves plus phospho-Ser112/121, and in parallel immunoprecipitate Spry2 under denaturing conditions to quantify ubiquitin conjugates. A gain-of-function arm expressing B-RafV600E versus empty vector in BRAF-wild-type cells provides the reciprocal readout; if Spry2 half-life and ubiquitylation are unchanged by BRAF manipulation, the proposed relationship is ruled out.

citations.title: Regulation of sprouty stability by Mnk1-dependent phosphorylation.
Bimodal expression of Sprouty2 during the cell cycle is mediated by phase-specific Ras/MAPK and c-Cbl activities
Sprouty2 association with B-Raf is regulated by phosphorylation and kinase conformation.
Induction of Resistance to BRAF Inhibitor Is Associated with the Inability of Spry2 to Inhibit BRAF-V600E Activity in BRAF Mutant Cells.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the mechanism in plain words (ERK/MAPK activity stabilizing Sprouty2 against proteasomal degradation, cycloheximide half-life, MG132), the entities together (Spry2 + BRAF V600E + vemurafenib/MEK inhibition + ubiquitin/c-Cbl), and the specific phospho-sites (Mnk1, Ser112/Ser121). The phospho-dependent stabilization arm is already published in general: DaSilva et al. show MEK/ERK- (plus p38-) driven Mnk1 phosphorylation of Ser112/121 protects hSpry2, while the S112A/S121A mutant is tyrosine-phosphorylated, c-Cbl-ubiquitylated and degraded in an MG132-blockable, proteasomal manner; Ras/Raf–ERK activity is also known to set Spry2 levels, though that work attributes it to transcriptional induction with c-Cbl-mediated degradation occurring independently of continued ERK signalling. I found nothing that makes the BRAF-specific claim — no source reports that oncogenic B-RafV600E suppresses Spry2 proteasomal turnover, or that acute BRAF/MEK inhibition shortens Spry2 half-life and drives poly-ubiquitylation; the BRAF V600E–Spry2 literature instead concerns loss of V600E–Spry2 binding and reduced SPRY2 expression in BRAFi-resistant cells. Hence partial.

hypotheses.statement: SHP2 phosphatase activity is directly required for full TNF-induced NF-κB transcriptional output in fibroblasts, acting on the ERK/MAPK-dependent p65 Ser276 branch rather than on IκB degradation.
hypotheses.mechanism: SHP2 is the catalytic node that drives ERK activation downstream of receptor inputs — re-expression of wild-type but not catalytically dead SHP2C459S restores p-ERK (chen2016:findings:003), and Gab1–SHP2 association drives ERK2 while Gab1-deficient fibroblasts show markedly reduced MAPK activity (heinrich2003:findings:010), with a Gab1-PH–active-SHP2 fusion causing constitutive MEK1/ERK2 activation (heinrich2003:findings:011). Independently, TNF-driven NF-κB activation in mouse fibroblasts requires the MAPK-activated kinases MSK1/2 and their phosphorylation of p65 at Ser276 (cargnello2011:findings:044), while the receptor-proximal RIP/IKKβ arm that degrades IκB is MAPK-independent (chen2002:findings:004). If TNF's fibroblast NF-κB output depends on a MAPK branch, and SHP2 is required to make that branch active, then SHP2 should be a direct positive requirement for TNF signalling amplitude in fibroblasts.
hypotheses.prediction: In fibroblasts, SHP2 inhibition or knockdown should blunt TNF-induced p65 Ser276 phosphorylation and reduce induction of NF-κB/TNF target transcripts (e.g. Tnfaip3, Ccl2/Cxcl5-type inflammatory genes), while leaving IκBα degradation, p65 nuclear translocation and TNF-R1-proximal complex formation intact; the defect should be rescued by shRNA-resistant wild-type SHP2 but not by catalytically inactive SHP2C459S.
hypotheses.test: Treat cultured mouse or human fibroblasts with SHP099 (≈0.25–1 µM, the concentration that suppresses p-ERK) or doxycycline-inducible SHP2 shRNA, stimulate with TNF over 0–60 min, and immunoblot p-ERK, p-p65 Ser276, total p65 and IκBα plus fractionate for nuclear p65; in parallel run qPCR/RNA-seq for NF-κB target genes at 1–4 h, and repeat in knockdown cells re-expressing shRNA-resistant wild-type SHP2 versus SHP2C459S to test whether the effect requires SHP2 catalytic activity.

citations.title: Modulation of the nuclear factor kappa B pathway by Shp-2 tyrosine phosphatase in mediating the induction of interleukin (IL)-6 by IL-1 or tumor necrosis factor.
Inhibition of tumor necrosis factor-[alpha]-induced SHP-2 phosphatase activity by shear stress: a mechanism to reduce endothelial inflammation.
Ser276 phosphorylation of NF-kB p65 by MSK1 controls SCF expression in inflammation.

novelty.note: I searched three ways — SHP2/PTPN11 requirement for TNF-induced NF-κB in fibroblasts, SHP2 linked to the ERK→MSK1→p65 Ser276 branch, and SHP099/knockdown effects on TNF target-gene induction. The core requirement is already published: You et al. (JEM 2001) showed IL-1/TNF-induced NF-κB DNA binding and IL-6 output are nearly abolished in Shp-2−/− fibroblasts and rescued by re-expression of wild-type Shp-2, and an endothelial study reports TNF-induced SHP-2 phosphatase activity is needed for NF-κB activation; the ERK/MSK1-dependent, IκB-degradation-independent Ser276 branch is separately established without any SHP2 link. Status is partial rather than established because no retrieved source places SHP2 on the Ser276 branch — indeed the nearest source explicitly found MAPK (Erk/Jnk/p38) activation unaffected by Shp-2 loss and the defect at the level of IκB phosphorylation, the opposite of this hypothesis's branch assignment, and no source tests catalytic-dead SHP2C459S in this setting.

hypotheses.statement: EGFR activity negatively regulates TSC2, driving inhibitory phosphorylation of the TSC1–TSC2 complex that suppresses its GAP activity and thereby de-represses mTORC1/S6K signalling.
hypotheses.mechanism: The EGFR evidence shows that ERK pathway output is directly sustained by EGFR, since a live-cell ERK-activity reporter rises on pathway induction and decays specifically upon EGFR inhibition (albeck2013:findings:000), and EGFR-driven ligand shedding and receptor signalling feed proliferative signalling (cuadrado2010:findings:029). The TSC2 evidence shows that ERK (with RSK) phosphorylates TSC2 at Ser664/Ser1798 to negatively regulate its GAP activity toward Rheb (cargnello2011:findings:035), that growth-factor kinases directly phosphorylate and inactivate the TSC1/TSC2 complex to activate mTORC1 (laplante2012:findings:002), and that lowering TSC2 raises basal and stimulated S6K phosphorylation (inoki2002:findings:004). Taken together, the receptor whose activity sets ERK output should be a proximal determinant of the phosphorylation state and functional output of TSC2.
hypotheses.prediction: In cells with active or amplified EGFR, acute EGFR inhibition (or EGF withdrawal) should reduce phosphorylation of TSC2 at the ERK/RSK sites (Ser664/Ser1798), restore TSC2 GAP-dependent repression of mTORC1 with a fall in pS6K(Thr389) and pS6(Ser240/244), and shift TSC2 to a faster-migrating, less-phosphorylated form; conversely EGF stimulation should increase TSC2 site phosphorylation and pS6K. The pS6K response to EGFR inhibition should be strongly blunted in TSC2-depleted cells, whose pS6K is already elevated.
hypotheses.test: In an EGFR-dependent line (e.g. EGFR-amplified MDA-MB-468) and in serum-starved EGF-stimulated MCF-10A cells, run a time course of EGF stimulation ± an EGFR kinase inhibitor and immunoblot TSC2 phospho-Ser664/Ser1798 (and TSC2 mobility shift, with λ-phosphatase control) alongside pS6K(Thr389)/pS6; then repeat the EGFR-inhibitor treatment in cells transfected with TSC2 siRNA versus control siRNA (blotting TSC2 to confirm knockdown) to test epistasis, and assay Rheb-GTP loading or TSC2 GAP activity from immunoprecipitated TSC1–TSC2 complexes ± EGF to confirm the change is in GAP function rather than TSC2 abundance.

citations.title: Phosphorylation and functional inactivation of TSC2 by Erk implications for tuberous sclerosis and cancer pathogenesis.
Tumor-promoting phorbol esters and activated Ras inactivate the tuberous sclerosis tumor suppressor complex via p90 ribosomal S6 kinase.
Identification of S664 TSC2 phosphorylation as a marker for extracellular signal-regulated kinase mediated mTOR activation in tuberous sclerosis and human cancer.
Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor Cell Proliferation Signaling Pathways.
Resistance to anti-HER2 therapy associated with the TSC2 nonsynonymous variant c.4349 C > G (p.Pro1450Arg) is reversed by CDK4/6 inhibitor in HER2-positive breast cancer.

novelty.note: I searched for EGF/EGFR-driven inhibitory TSC2 phosphorylation (S664/S1798), for ERK/RSK–TSC2–Rheb GAP inactivation, and for the prediction that EGFR/HER2 kinase inhibition lowers TSC2 phosphorylation and pS6K in a TSC2-dependent way. The explanation is published: Ma et al. (Cell 2005) and Roux et al. (PNAS 2004) show that mitogen/growth-factor signalling through ERK (S664) and RSK (S1798) phosphorylates and functionally inactivates the TSC1–TSC2 complex, impairing its Rheb-GAP function and raising mTOR→S6K1 output, Ma et al. (Cancer Res 2007) validate pS664-TSC2 as the marker of ERK-mediated mTOR activation in human tumours, and an EGFR-signalling review states the axis explicitly with EGFR upstream (AKT, ERK and RSK converge to deactivate TSC2 and activate mTORC1/S6K). The narrower experimental prediction is also partly demonstrated: in HER2+/EGFR-targeted breast cancer cells lapatinib suppressed TSC2 phosphorylation and mTOR signalling, and the response depended on TSC2 status, though that work scores the AKT site Thr1462 rather than the ERK/RSK sites after acute EGFR-TKI treatment.

hypotheses.statement: PTEN directly dephosphorylates the MAPK (ERK1/2) activation-loop threonine through its protein-phosphatase activity, acting as a lipid-independent negative regulator of MAPK.
hypotheses.mechanism: PTEN belongs to the VH1-like dual-specificity phosphatase family whose other members include the eleven MAP kinase phosphatases that act on the dual phosphothreonine/phosphotyrosine activation loop of Erk, Jnk and p38 (alonso2004:findings:009), and the Cowden-disease G129E allele shows PTEN's protein-phosphatase activity is genetically and biochemically separable from its lipid-phosphatase activity (balla2013:findings:045), leaving a catalytic function whose protein substrates are unassigned. Removal of the activation-loop phosphothreonine alone is sufficient to inactivate MAPK, as bacterial effectors demonstrate (cuadrado2010:findings:013), and MAPK-pathway profiling has already invoked unexplained 'MAPK phosphatase inhibition' to account for effector-kinase activation without upstream activation (bradley2024:findings:009). Together these imply PTEN's orphan protein-phosphatase activity could act directly on the MAPK activation loop.
hypotheses.prediction: Purified recombinant PTEN incubated with dually phosphorylated ERK2 will remove phosphate preferentially from the activation-loop threonine (loss of pTEY signal, reduced ERK2 kinase activity toward a substrate peptide), with activity retained by the lipid-dead G129E mutant, abolished by an active-site cysteine mutant, and thiol-dependent as for other PTEN-catalyzed reactions; in cells, PTEN depletion will raise basal and EGF-stimulated pERK even when PI3K is pharmacologically inhibited, and re-expression of G129E will restore pERK suppression without restoring PIP3 control.
hypotheses.test: Run an in vitro phosphatase assay with purified recombinant PTEN (wild type, G129E, and catalytically dead C124S) against purified dually phosphorylated ERK2 in buffer with 10 mM DTT, reading out phospho-Thr and phospho-Tyr loss by phospho-specific immunoblot or Phos-tag SDS-PAGE, free phosphate release, and residual ERK2 kinase activity; pair this with a cell-based test in a PTEN-null line reconstituted with wild-type, G129E, or C124S PTEN, measuring pERK by immunoblot after EGF stimulation in the presence and absence of a PI3K inhibitor, plus co-immunoprecipitation of PTEN with ERK1/2 to confirm direct association.

citations.title: PTEN Loss Promotes PI3Kβ Phosphorylation and EPHA2/SRC/p-PI3KβY962 Complex Assembly to Drive Tumorigenesis.
PTEN regulation of ERK1/2 signaling in cancer.
Tumor suppressor PTEN inhibits integrin- and growth factor-mediated mitogen-activated protein (MAP) kinase signaling pathways.
PTEN protein phosphatase activity regulates metastasis by targeting PKCδ.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: (a) 'PTEN protein phosphatase dephosphorylates ERK1/2 activation loop threonine' and in vitro pERK/ERK2 substrate assays, (b) the entity pair PTEN + G129E/Y138L with lipid-independent MAPK/pERK regulation, and (c) reviews of PTEN protein substrates (Shc, FAK, IRS1, CREB, PTK6, PKCδ, AKT, PI3Kβ). The lipid-independent half of the prediction is published: a 2026 Cancer Discovery study reports that PTEN-WT and the lipid-dead G129E mutant reduce pERK/c-MYC while the protein-phosphatase-dead Y138L and C124S do not — but the bona fide substrate there is p-PI3KβY962, not ERK, and ERK suppression is downstream via an EPHA2/SRC/PI3Kβ scaffold. No source states that PTEN acts directly on the ERK activation loop; the standard review of PTEN–ERK1/2 explicitly calls the link indirect (PI3K/AKT, Shc, PKC, Ras, Raf) and Gu et al. note that isolated PTEN cannot dephosphorylate ERK2 in vitro, so the specific direct-dephosphorylation mechanism is unpublished and partly contradicted, while the cellular prediction is anticipated.

hypotheses.statement: SYK acts upstream of p38 MAPK, activating the MKK3/6–p38α module in ITAM/CLEC7A-coupled myeloid cells to drive proinflammatory cytokine gene expression.
hypotheses.mechanism: SYK signalling downstream of Dectin-1/ITAM adaptors is reported to drive MAPK-dependent (ERK) and NF-κB-dependent cytokine and chemokine output in dendritic cells and macrophages (mcsai2010:findings:019), and SYK activation in macrophages requires ITAM-associated receptor engagement (ivashkiv2014:findings:003), placing SYK at the receptor-proximal tyrosine-kinase step of myeloid inflammatory signalling. Independently, p38α is the p38 isoform whose deletion reduces proinflammatory gene expression (cargnello2011:findings:006) and it is switched on only by MKK3/6-catalysed dual phosphorylation of its activation-loop TGY motif (cargnello2011:findings:005), a step that must be supplied by an upstream receptor-coupled kinase cascade. If the SYK-proximal branch feeds the same inflammatory transcriptional output, the simplest direct link is that SYK activity is required for TGY phosphorylation of p38α, with MK2 (whose activation is completely p38α-dependent; cargnello2011:findings:068) serving as a specific readout of that requirement.
hypotheses.prediction: Engagement of ITAM/Dectin-1-coupled receptors on myeloid cells should produce rapid dual TGY phosphorylation of p38α and downstream MK2 Thr222 phosphorylation that is lost when SYK is inhibited or deleted, whereas SYK-independent p38 stimuli (sorbitol, anisomycin, UV) should still phosphorylate p38α normally in the same SYK-null cells; conversely, forced SYK activity should increase p38 TGY phosphorylation without altering total p38 levels.
hypotheses.test: In a myeloid cell line (e.g. RAW264.7 or THP-1 macrophages) compare wild-type, CRISPR SYK-knockout, and SYK-inhibitor-treated (e.g. a selective SYK inhibitor, with an inactive analogue control) cells stimulated with curdlan/zymosan-depleted particles or plate-bound anti-ITAM receptor crosslinking; immunoblot a time course for phospho-p38 (Thr180/Tyr182), phospho-MKK3/6, and phospho-MK2 Thr222 against total protein, and run sorbitol as a SYK-independent positive control. Pair this with a gain-of-function arm expressing the constitutively active SYK Tyr130Glu variant (mcsai2010:findings:009) in the knockout background, and test whether p38 TGY phosphorylation is restored, and with an in vitro kinase assay using purified active SYK plus recombinant inactive p38α to distinguish direct SYK phosphorylation of p38 from a cascade requirement routed through MKK3/6.

Syk inhibitor attenuates lupus in FcγRIIb(-)(/-) mice through the Inhibition of DNA extracellular traps from macrophages and neutrophils via p38MAPK-dependent pathway.
The protein tyrosine kinase SYK regulates the alternative p38 activation in liver during acute liver inflammation.

CR3 and Dectin-1 Collaborate in Macrophage Cytokine Response through Association on Lipid Rafts and Activation of Syk-JNK-AP-1 Pathway

novelty.note: I searched for SYK acting upstream of p38 in Dectin-1/ITAM myeloid signalling, for SYK-dependent MKK3/6–p38α activation, and for the predicted loss of p38/MK2 phosphorylation on SYK inhibition. Published work does place SYK upstream of p38 in myeloid cells — a SYK inhibitor (R406) reduced Dectin-1-driven p38 phosphorylation in human DCs, and SYK inhibition lowered p-p38 (but not ERK/JNK) in FcγRIIb-deficient macrophages/neutrophils — and SYK→p38 has been demonstrated directly in liver, but there it runs through the MKK3/6-independent 'alternative' Tyr323 route rather than TGY dual phosphorylation. No source states the specific claim that SYK drives the MKK3/6–p38α module with MK2 Thr222 as readout in ITAM/CLEC7A-coupled myeloid cells; the myeloid MKK3/6–p38α activator on record is TPL-2 downstream of TLR/TNF-R1, and one primary study reports that Dectin-1/CR3-induced p38 phosphorylation in macrophages is intact in Syk-deficient cells, so the specific link and prediction remain unsettled.

hypotheses.statement: TAK1 (MAP3K7) acts directly upstream of the stress-kinase arm that phosphorylates STAT3 on Ser727 and is therefore required for MKK4/p38-dependent negative regulation of STAT3 transcriptional activity.
hypotheses.mechanism: Independent evidence places TAK1 as the MAP3K that is absolutely required for MKK4-dependent JNK activation and for p38 MAPK activation upon receptor stimulation (xu2009:findings:029; derynck2019:findings:030), while the STAT3 side states that sequential Vav–Rac-1–MKK-4–PKCδ activity is necessary for IL-6-induced STAT3 Ser727 phosphorylation, which inhibits STAT3 DNA binding (heinrich2003:findings:023), and that LPS/TNFα suppression of IL-6-induced STAT3 activation depends on the p38 stress kinase (heinrich2003:findings:015). Since MKK4 and p38 are the two effectors shared by both sets of claims, the kinase that activates them should be the node through which stress signals reach STAT3, making TAK1 a required upstream regulator of the Ser727 modification rather than a parallel pathway.
hypotheses.prediction: Loss or catalytic inhibition of TAK1 should abolish or strongly reduce inducible STAT3 Ser727 phosphorylation and, consequently, restore STAT3 DNA binding and STAT3-dependent promoter activity (e.g. α2M reporter) under IL-6 plus LPS/TNFα conditions, without affecting STAT3 Tyr705-type JAK-driven phosphorylation; conversely, expression of active TAK1 should increase Ser727 phosphorylation and dampen STAT3 reporter output even with intact upstream cytokine receptor signalling.
hypotheses.test: In HepG2 (or fibroblast) cultures, deplete TAK1 by siRNA/CRISPR or inhibit it pharmacologically (5Z-7-oxozeaenol), then stimulate with IL-6 alone and IL-6 plus TNFα/LPS and immunoblot for phospho-Ser727 STAT3 versus phospho-Tyr STAT3, MKK4 and p38 phosphorylation; pair this with an EMSA or STAT3-dependent α2M luciferase reporter, and rescue TAK1-null cells with wild-type versus kinase-dead TAK1 to confirm that the Ser727/DNA-binding shift tracks TAK1 catalytic activity.

citations.title: STAT3 regulates Nemo-like kinase by mediating its interaction with IL-6-stimulated TGFbeta-activated kinase 1 for STAT3 Ser-727 phosphorylation.
Role of the TAK1-NLK-STAT3 pathway in TGF-beta-mediated mesoderm induction.
Interleukin-6-induced STAT3 transactivation and Ser727 phosphorylation involves Vav, Rac-1 and the kinase SEK-1/MKK-4 as signal transduction components.

novelty.note: I searched for TAK1/MAP3K7 as an upstream kinase for STAT3 Ser727, for TAK1 combined with MKK4/p38 and STAT3 DNA binding, for TAK1 inhibition (5Z-7-oxozeaenol) effects on pSer727, and for p38-dependent LPS/TNFα suppression of IL-6-STAT3. The core mechanistic claim that TAK1 lies directly upstream of inducible STAT3 Ser727 phosphorylation (and not of Tyr705) is already published: Kojima et al. show IL-6-stimulated TAK1 acting through NLK to phosphorylate STAT3 Ser727 with STAT3 as scaffold, and Ohkawara et al. establish a TAK1-NLK-STAT3 Ser727 axis requiring TAK1 catalytic activity. However, no retrieved source states the specific version proposed here — TAK1 acting through the MKK4/PKCδ–p38 stress arm so that TAK1 loss relieves Ser727-mediated inhibition of STAT3 DNA binding and restores α2M-type reporter output under IL-6 plus LPS/TNFα; the nearest work on the MKK4 arm (Schuringa et al.) implicates MEKK, not TAK1, and reports Ser727 as positively coupled to STAT3 transactivation, the opposite sign from the prediction.

hypotheses.statement: JAK1's ~100-fold reduced mobility reflects constitutive, high-affinity binding of its FERM-SH2 module to receptor Box1/Box2 motifs, so the diffusing species is effectively the membrane-anchored receptor-JAK1 complex rather than free cytoplasmic JAK1.
hypotheses.mechanism: The cryo-EM structure shows the IFNλR1 Box1/Box2 peptide occupying an extended groove on JAK1 FERM-SH2 with ~1650 Å2 buried and specific hydrophobic insertion (Leu266/Phe268 into a Val194/Phe247/Phe251 pocket) plus a Glu284–His509 salt bridge, an interface large enough to support a long-lived complex. Independently, JAK1 is reported to bind receptor cytoplasmic domains constitutively and in a stimulation-independent manner, and its association is unchanged by ligand. A JAK1 population essentially always bound to an integral membrane receptor would diffuse with membrane-protein kinetics, matching gp130 rather than a cytoplasmic protein.
hypotheses.prediction: FRAP of a JAK1 fusion bearing FERM-SH2 point mutations at the Box1-binding pocket (e.g., the hydrophobic pocket residues) should restore mobility toward that of a free cytoplasmic protein, while wild-type JAK1 remains slow; conversely, overexpressing an untagged receptor cytoplasmic-domain competitor should also increase JAK1 mobility.
hypotheses.test: Perform side-by-side FRAP in cells expressing GFP-JAK1 wild type versus a FERM pocket mutant (and versus isolated GFP-FERM-SH2 and GFP-TK constructs), with and without co-expression of excess soluble receptor Box1/Box2 peptide; verify loss of receptor binding by co-immunoprecipitation and confirm the mutant is expressed at the membrane by fractionation. A receptor-tethering model predicts mobility scales with measured receptor-binding competence; a bulk/oligomerization model predicts the FERM mutant stays slow.

citations.title: Long term association of the cytokine receptor gp130 and the Janus kinase Jak1 revealed by FRAP analysis.

Janus kinase (Jak) subcellular localization revisited: the exclusive membrane localization of endogenous Janus kinase 1 by cytokine receptor interaction uncovers the Jak.receptor complex to be equivalent to a receptor tyrosine kinase.
The Janus Kinase (JAK) FERM and SH2 Domains: Bringing Specificity to JAK-Receptor Interactions.

novelty.note: I searched for JAK1 FRAP/membrane-mobility measurements, for receptor-binding-deficient JAK1 FERM mutants and their localization, and for the structural/affinity basis of FERM-SH2 binding to Box1/Box2. Giese et al. (JBC 2003) directly report that Jak1-YFP and gp130-YFP have equal plasma-membrane mobilities, that Jak1 therefore 'diffuses like a transmembrane protein,' and that antibody-mediated immobilization of gp130 immobilizes Jak1 — i.e. the diffusing entity is a long-lived receptor-Jak1 complex that does not exchange with a cytosolic pool; Haan et al. (JBC 2004) further show the non-receptor-binding Jak1-L80A/Y81A mutant is cytoplasmic rather than membrane-localized, the mutant-based half of the prediction, and Ferrao & Lupardus review the high-affinity bipartite FERM-SH2/Box1-Box2 interface that underpins it. Because the explanation for the slow mobility is explicitly stated in published primary work, this is established rather than partial, although the specific side-by-side FRAP comparison of wild-type versus Box1-pocket mutant and the soluble-competitor experiment were not found.

hypotheses.statement: The poor kinetics on soluble Ins(1,3,4,5)P4 arise because PTEN's true substrate is the membrane-embedded D3-phosphoinositide PIP3, so that presentation of the inositol headgroup without its lipid/interfacial context loses the binding and orientation contributions needed for efficient turnover.
hypotheses.mechanism: Other papers assign PTEN to the phosphatase subgroup that dephosphorylates the D3-phosphate of inositol phospholipids and characterize it specifically as a PIP3 phosphatase opposing PI3K, and the G129E allele that abolishes lipid phosphatase activity while sparing protein phosphatase activity is the one that is disease-causing and that also fails to dephosphorylate IP4 or to down-regulate Akt. This implies the active site engaged by soluble IP4 is the same site used on PIP3, but the soluble headgroup is a truncated surrogate lacking the diacyl/membrane moiety, so it reports a low kcat that underestimates activity on the lipid.
hypotheses.prediction: Purified recombinant PTEN assayed on PIP3 presented in lipid vesicles or as short-chain (diC8) PIP3 micelles should show a substantially higher kcat/Vmax and greater catalytic efficiency than on soluble Ins(1,3,4,5)P4, with activity on the lipid enhanced by phosphatidylserine-containing vesicles, while G129E is inactive on both.
hypotheses.test: Run side-by-side steady-state kinetics with the same purified PTEN preparation on (a) Ins(1,3,4,5)P4, (b) diC8-PIP3 below its critical micelle concentration, and (c) long-chain PIP3 in defined phosphatidylcholine/phosphatidylserine vesicles, quantifying released inorganic phosphate by malachite green and fitting Km/kcat; include G129E and C124S as controls. If interfacial presentation is the missing determinant, kcat rises with lipid/vesicle presentation and scales with vesicle surface concentration rather than with bulk substrate concentration; if the active site is intrinsically slow, kcat stays near 0.5 min-1 in all three formats.

citations.title: Interfacial kinetic analysis of the tumour suppressor phosphatase, PTEN: evidence for activation by anionic phospholipids.
Kinetics of PTEN-mediated PI(3,4,5)P3 hydrolysis on solid supported membranes.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: PTEN kinetics on soluble Ins(1,3,4,5)P4 versus membrane PIP3, PTEN interfacial/surface-dilution kinetics with anionic phospholipid and diC8 presentation, and the prediction of higher kcat on vesicle-presented PIP3. The 2003 Biochemical Journal surface-dilution study states exactly this explanation: PTEN behaves as an interfacial enzyme whose rate depends on substrate surface concentration (mol fraction) as well as bulk concentration, and its kcat for PtdIns(3,4,5)P3 is at least 200-fold greater than for the water-soluble substrate Ins(1,3,4,5)P4, with anionic phospholipids/PtdIns(4,5)P2 stimulating lipid turnover while inhibiting activity on the soluble headgroup. A later supported-membrane kinetics paper reiterates that soluble-headgroup assays fail to capture interfacial determinants and that membrane binding can occlude soluble substrate access, so the mechanism and its central prediction are already published rather than open.

hypotheses.statement: The combination of low Km with very low Vmax reflects an active site optimized for tight substrate binding rather than rapid hydrolysis, i.e. PTEN behaves partly as a phosphoinositide-sequestering protein.
hypotheses.mechanism: One paper reports that catalytically inert substrate-trapping PTEN mutants (C124S, D92A) retain partial ability to arrest cells in G1, and infers that sequestration of phosphorylated substrate may itself suffice for inhibition, while another paper defines PTEN's cellular role as PIP3 removal opposing PI3K. Tight binding with slow turnover would produce exactly the observed kinetic signature — micromolar Km alongside a kcat near 0.5 per minute — and would mean the low Vmax is an intrinsic property of the enzyme rather than an artifact of using the wrong substrate.
hypotheses.prediction: The equilibrium dissociation constant of PTEN for Ins(1,3,4,5)P4 (and for the PIP3 headgroup) should be comparable to or tighter than the measured 98.9 microM Km, and the catalytically dead C124S and D92A mutants should bind these ligands with similar or higher affinity than wild type.
hypotheses.test: Measure direct binding of Ins(1,3,4,5)P4 and of a soluble PIP3 analogue to purified wild-type, C124S, and D92A PTEN by competition filter binding or scintillation proximity against tritiated IP4, and independently by intrinsic tryptophan fluorescence quenching or isothermal titration calorimetry, then compare Kd to the kinetic Km. Tight binding by the dead mutants (Kd at or below Km) supports a binding-optimized, turnover-limited site; Kd far weaker than Km, or no measurable binding by the dead mutants, favors the alternative that IP4 is simply a poor, non-preferred substrate weakly engaged by the active site.

citations.title: Interfacial kinetic analysis of the tumour suppressor phosphatase, PTEN: evidence for activation by anionic phospholipids.
Kinetics of PTEN-mediated PI(3,4,5)P3 hydrolysis on solid supported membranes.
Membrane Association of the PTEN Tumor Suppressor: Molecular Details of the Protein-Membrane Complex from SPR Binding Studies and Neutron Reflection

novelty.note: I searched for PTEN kinetics on Ins(1,3,4,5)P4 versus lipid PIP3 (Km/Vmax/kcat), for direct binding/Kd measurements of soluble inositol phosphates and dead mutants, and for any proposal that PTEN acts as a non-catalytic phosphoinositide-sequestering protein. McConnachie et al. directly compared the same enzyme on both substrates and report catalytic-centre activity for PtdIns(3,4,5)P3 at least 200-fold greater than for the water-soluble Ins(1,3,4,5)P4, attributing the low soluble-substrate turnover to absence of interfacial activation (and PtdIns(4,5)P2/univalent salts stimulate PIP3 activity while inhibiting Ins(1,3,4,5)P4 activity); Liu et al. measure kcat ≈ 11 s⁻¹ on membrane PIP3, over a thousand-fold above the ~0.5 min⁻¹ cited for IP4. These are stated results that the very low Vmax is an artifact of the non-preferred soluble substrate rather than an intrinsic binding-optimized, turnover-limited active site, i.e. the alternative named in the hypothesis's own test; Shenoy et al. do support the subsidiary point that catalytically dead C124S binds PIP3-containing membranes more tightly than wild type while binding PI(4,5)P2 comparably (Kd 0.32 vs 0.4 µM).

hypotheses.statement: The discrepancy arises because cardiac myocytes, unlike HEK-293 cells, contain abundant scaffold (mAKAP-type) complexes that support PKA-dependent phosphoactivation of co-anchored PDE4D3, so activation of the resident nuclear holoenzyme immediately amplifies local cAMP hydrolysis and clamps cAMP below the activation threshold, erasing the fast in-place activation seen in HEK-293 nuclei.
hypotheses.mechanism: PKA phosphorylation of PDE4D3 on Ser13/Ser54 raises its Vmax roughly 3-fold and attenuates local cAMP signalling, and this phosphorylation is strongly scaffold-dependent: in HEK293 cells PDE4D3 is barely phosphorylated when expressed alone but markedly phosphorylated when co-expressed with mAKAP (dodge2001:findings:011, pawson2003:findings:011). In heart extracts the scaffolded PDE actively suppresses anchored PKA activity, since PDE4D3 co-expression lowers mAKAP-associated PKA activity ~40% and rolipram both restores it and increases cAMP sensitivity of the complex several-fold (dodge2001:findings:010, dodge2001:findings:009). Thus the same AC-generated cAMP flux that crosses threshold in a scaffold-poor HEK-293 nucleus would be consumed by feedback-activated anchored PDE in myocytes, making apparent activation slow or absent.
hypotheses.prediction: Reconstituting scaffold-anchored, PKA-phosphorylatable PDE in HEK-293 nuclei should abolish the fast in-place activation kinetics, whereas the non-phosphorylatable PDE4D3 S13A,S54A mutant or PDE4 inhibition should preserve or restore them; conversely, PDE4 inhibition should unmask fast resident-holoenzyme activation in a scaffold-rich cardiac-like cell.
hypotheses.test: In HEK-293 cells expressing a nuclear-targeted PKA-activity FRET reporter plus the nuclear AC, compare cAMP-onset-to-PKA-activation kinetics across four conditions: (i) reporter alone, (ii) co-expressed mAKAP + wild-type PDE4D3, (iii) mAKAP + PDE4D3 S13A,S54A, (iv) condition (ii) plus rolipram; in parallel immunoprecipitate the scaffold and measure PDE and PKA activity in the same lysates to confirm feedback engagement. If the kinetic slowing tracks specifically with scaffolded, phosphorylatable PDE (present in ii, lost in iii and iv), the myocyte failure is explained by scaffold-coupled PDE feedback rather than by diffusion.

citations.title: PDE4 and mAKAPβ are nodal organizers of β2-ARs nuclear PKA signalling in cardiac myocytes.
Control of cytoplasmic and nuclear protein kinase A by phosphodiesterases and phosphatases in cardiac myocytes.
Mechanisms of cyclic AMP compartmentation revealed by computational models.

novelty.note: I searched three ways — the mechanism in plain words (scaffolded PDE4D3 phospho-feedback clamping local cAMP below the PKA activation threshold), the entities together (mAKAP/mAKAPβ + PDE4D3 + Ser13/Ser54 + nuclear PKA + cardiac myocyte), and the prediction (PDE4 inhibition unmasking anchored/nuclear PKA activation in myocytes vs. fast resident-holoenzyme activation in HEK-293) — using PubMed/PMC, Oxford Academic, and eutils. Bedioune et al. (Cardiovasc Res 2018) states precisely this explanation for precisely this discrepancy: PDE4 'insulates a mAKAPβ-targeted PKA pool at the nuclear envelope that prevents nuclear PKA activation', PDE4 inhibition unmasks that activation in an mAKAPβ-knockdown-sensitive manner, PDE4D3 co-anchored with PKA is argued to prevent catalytic-subunit dissociation via the known PKA→PDE4D3 feedback loop, and the paper explicitly contrasts this with the resident nuclear PKA holoenzyme demonstrated in HEK-293 cells; Haj Slimane et al. (2014) independently reports fast cAMP but markedly slower nuclear PKA in myocytes with PDE4 inhibition enhancing the nuclear response. Hence established, with the caveat that these authors' cytoplasmic-PKI data place the PDE-clamped pool at the nuclear envelope rather than in a nucleoplasmic resident holoenzyme, and the S13A/S54A reconstitution in HEK-293 nuclei remains undone.

hypotheses.statement: GSK3B negatively regulates TGF-β-induced growth inhibition: GSK3B phosphorylates the Smad3 linker, which limits the Smad-dependent growth arrest caused by TGF-β.
hypotheses.mechanism: In NMuMG cells, dominant-negative Smad3 or Smad7 blocks about 80% of TGF-β-induced growth inhibition. In BxPc3 cells, loss of Smad4 abolishes TGF-β growth inhibition. So TGF-β growth control depends on Smad signalling. Independently, GSK3β phosphorylates the linker of activated Smad2/3. This phosphorylation creates a Nedd4L recognition motif, which leads to Smad ubiquitylation and degradation, and it also inhibits Smad nuclear accumulation. GSK3B activity should therefore reduce the Smad3 pool available to mediate TGF-β growth inhibition.
hypotheses.prediction: In TGF-β-treated NMuMG cells, inhibiting GSK3B pharmacologically or by siRNA should reduce Smad3 linker phosphorylation. It should also increase nuclear and total activated Smad3 and strengthen TGF-β-induced 3TP-Lux activation. As a result, proliferation should be suppressed more strongly than with TGF-β alone. Expressing a Smad3 linker mutant that GSK3B cannot phosphorylate should mimic this effect and make it insensitive to GSK3B inhibition.
hypotheses.test: Treat NMuMG cells with TGF-β, with or without a GSK3 inhibitor or GSK3B siRNA. Measure thymidine or BrdU incorporation, 3TP-Lux reporter activity, Smad3 linker phosphorylation, and nuclear versus cytoplasmic Smad3 by immunoblot or immunofluorescence. Compare cells expressing wild-type Smad3 with cells expressing a linker phospho-site alanine mutant.

citations.title: Transforming growth factor-{beta}-inducible phosphorylation of Smad3.
A negative feedback control of transforming growth factor-beta signaling by glycogen synthase kinase 3-mediated Smad3 linker phosphorylation at Ser-204.
Ubiquitin ligase Nedd4L targets activated Smad2/3 to limit TGF-beta signaling.

novelty.note: I searched for the mechanism in plain words (GSK3 phosphorylation of the Smad3 linker limiting TGF-β growth arrest), the entities together (GSK3/Smad3 linker/Nedd4L/growth inhibition), and the prediction (GSK3 inhibition or non-phosphorylatable linker mutants strengthening the TGF-β antiproliferative response). Two primary JBC papers from 2009 state exactly this explanation: Wang et al. map TGF-β-inducible Smad3 linker sites, show GSK3 phosphorylates Ser204 (LiCl/GSK3β-null cells), and report that blocking linker phosphorylation enhances Smad target-gene activation and the growth-inhibitory function of Smad3, i.e. linker phosphorylation suppresses Smad3 antiproliferative activity; Millet et al. independently show GSK3-mediated Ser204 phosphorylation (primed by Ser208) is a negative feedback loop, with S204A/S208A mutants showing stronger CBP binding, transcriptional output and TGF-β growth inhibition. Gao et al. establish the Nedd4L linker-phosphomotif degradation arm that limits activated Smad2/3 half-life, so both the kinase step and the consequence for the Smad-dependent antiproliferative program are published; only the specific NMuMG/3TP-Lux framing is not.

hypotheses.statement: ERK2 directly phosphorylates EGFR on serine/threonine residues as a negative-feedback modification that limits EGFR tyrosine phosphorylation, analogous to its direct phosphorylation of FGFR1.
hypotheses.mechanism: EGFR and its kinase activity are required for ERK activation downstream of EGF and LPS (de2015:findings:004, de2015:findings:006), so EGFR sits upstream of ERK. ERK2 directly phosphorylates another receptor tyrosine kinase, FGFR1 on S777, and blocking that site prolongs receptor tyrosine phosphorylation (lake2016:findings:002). ERK2 also directly phosphorylates other upstream pathway components (SOS1, Raf-1, MEK1) to dampen signalling (lake2016:findings:003, lake2016:findings:007, lake2016:findings:010), and the related MAPK p38α phosphorylates EGFR itself (cuadrado2010:findings:054). Together these imply that ERK2 may likewise directly phosphorylate EGFR as part of a feedback loop.
hypotheses.prediction: Recombinant active ERK2 should incorporate phosphate into the EGFR intracellular domain in vitro at one or more Ser/Thr-Pro sites. In EGF-stimulated cells, MEK1/2 inhibition or ERK2 knockdown should abolish phosphorylation at these sites, and alanine mutation of the mapped site(s) should prolong EGF-induced EGFR tyrosine phosphorylation.
hypotheses.test: Run an in vitro kinase assay with [γ-32P]ATP, activated recombinant ERK2 and purified EGFR cytoplasmic domain (kinase-dead, to exclude autophosphorylation), then map the sites by phosphopeptide analysis or phospho-motif immunoblot. Then, in cultured cells expressing wild-type or site-mutant EGFR, measure phosphorylation at the mapped site(s) and the time course of EGFR tyrosine phosphorylation after EGF, with and without U0126 or ERK2 siRNA.

citations.title: Isolation and characterization of two growth factor-stimulated protein kinases that phosphorylate the epidermal growth factor receptor at threonine 669.
ERK-dependent threonine phosphorylation of EGF receptor modulates receptor downregulation and signaling.
Inverse correlation between Thr-669 and constitutive tyrosine phosphorylation in the asymmetric epidermal growth factor receptor dimer conformation.
Negative feedback regulation of the ERK1/2 MAPK pathway.
Feedback control of ErbB2 via ERK-mediated phosphorylation of a conserved threonine in the juxtamembrane domain.

novelty.note: I searched for ERK-mediated Ser/Thr feedback phosphorylation of EGFR, for direct in vitro phosphorylation of EGFR by ERK2, and for the specific prediction that mutating the site prolongs EGF-induced EGFR tyrosine phosphorylation. This is a long-established mechanism: ERK1/ERK2 were purified in 1991 as the growth-factor-stimulated kinases that phosphorylate the EGFR juxtamembrane Ser/Thr-Pro site Thr-669 in vitro, and later work showed EGF/cytokine-induced Thr-669 phosphorylation is MEK/ERK-dependent (blocked by U0126), modulates receptor downregulation and signalling, and that T669A abolishes the downregulation of EGFR tyrosine phosphorylation in the asymmetric dimer — exactly the FGFR1-S777 analogue proposed. A 2016 review explicitly frames ERK1/2 phosphorylation of EGFR T669 as negative feedback reducing EGFR tyrosine phosphorylation.

hypotheses.statement: EGFR signaling negatively regulates TGFBR1 (TβRI) by lowering its cell-surface abundance through ERK-dependent, TACE/ADAM17-mediated ectodomain cleavage, which attenuates TGF-β–induced Smad3 activation.
hypotheses.mechanism: EGFR kinase activity is required for ERK activation: EGFR knockdown or erlotinib blocks ERK phosphorylation, and an ERK-output reporter decays when EGFR is inhibited. Separately, ERK activation causes TACE/ADAM17 to cleave TβRI but not TβRII, which lowers surface TβRI and down-regulates Smad3 activation. Together these claims imply that EGFR activity, acting through ERK, controls TβRI surface levels. Because TACE also sheds TGFα-family ligands that signal through EGFR, EGFR activation could additionally sustain this TβRI down-regulation.
hypotheses.prediction: In cells expressing both receptors, EGF stimulation should reduce cell-surface TβRI and increase TβRI ectodomain release, with TβRII unchanged. TGF-β–induced Smad3 phosphorylation should also decrease. These effects should be prevented by erlotinib, EGFR knockdown, MEK/ERK inhibition, or TACE/ADAM17 knockdown or inhibition.
hypotheses.test: Pretreat cultured epithelial cells (e.g. MCF-10A) with erlotinib, a MEK inhibitor, a TACE inhibitor, or siRNA against EGFR or ADAM17, then stimulate with EGF. Measure surface TβRI and TβRII by cell-surface biotinylation and immunoblot, and detect the shed TβRI ectodomain in conditioned medium. Then add TGF-β and measure phospho-Smad3 by immunoblot. Express a cleavage-resistant TβRI mutant to test whether the EGF effect on Smad3 depends on TβRI cleavage.

citations.title: TACE-mediated ectodomain shedding of the type I TGF-beta receptor downregulates TGF-beta signaling.
Post-translational regulation of TGF-β receptor and Smad signaling.

novelty.note: I searched for ERK-dependent TACE/ADAM17 cleavage of TβRI, for EGF stimulation lowering surface TβRI and Smad3 phosphorylation, and for EGFR-inhibitor blockade of TβRI shedding. Liu et al. (Mol Cell 2009) directly report that TACE sheds the TβRI but not TβRII ectodomain downstream of Erk MAPK, that adding EGF (which enhances Erk signaling) decreases cell-surface TβRI and TGF-β-induced Smad3 activation in T4-2 cells, and that MEK inhibition or TACE inhibition/knockdown restores surface TβRI and Smad3 activation; the Xu/Liu/Derynck review states the same explanation generally. This is the same explanation, so the status is established, although the specific EGFR-directed arms of the prediction (erlotinib, EGFR siRNA, cleavage-resistant TβRI mutant) were not the reagents used in that work.

hypotheses.statement: GSK3B phosphorylates RAPTOR as a secondary kinase, acting on RAPTOR that has first been primed by ERK1/2 phosphorylation at its proline-directed sites (Ser8, Ser696, Ser863).
hypotheses.mechanism: GSK3 prefers phospho-primed substrates (johnson2023:findings:003). In R-Smad linkers, phosphorylation by proline-directed kinases (CDK8/CDK9, alongside Erk MAPK) primes secondary GSK3 phosphorylation (hata2016:findings:024). RAPTOR is directly phosphorylated by ERK1/2 on the proline-directed sites Ser8, Ser696 and Ser863 after PMA or EGF stimulation (carriere2010:findings:004, carriere2010:findings:008, carriere2010:findings:010), so ERK-phosphorylated RAPTOR could present primed sites that GSK3B then phosphorylates.
hypotheses.prediction: Recombinant GSK3B should incorporate phosphate into RAPTOR that was pre-phosphorylated by active ERK1 substantially more than into unprimed RAPTOR or the S3A (S8A/S696A/S863A) mutant. In PMA- or EGF-stimulated cells, GSK3 inhibition should reduce the ERK-dependent phosphorylation or mobility shift of RAPTOR without reducing Ser696/Ser863 phosphorylation itself.
hypotheses.test: Immunopurify myc-RAPTOR (wild-type or S3A) from HEK293 cells and pre-incubate it with recombinant active ERK1 plus cold ATP, or with no ERK. Wash, then run an in vitro kinase assay with recombinant GSK3B and [γ-32P]ATP, with and without a GSK3 inhibitor, and read 32P incorporation by autoradiography. In parallel, treat PMA/EGF-stimulated HEK293 cells expressing myc-RAPTOR with a GSK3 inhibitor or GSK3B siRNA. Assess RAPTOR phosphorylation by Phos-tag SDS-PAGE and immunoblotting, using phospho-Ser696/Ser863 antibodies as priming controls, and assess mTORC1 output by 4E-BP1 Thr37/Thr46 phosphorylation.

citations.title: GSK3-mediated raptor phosphorylation supports amino-acid-dependent mTORC1-directed signalling.
Regulation of mTOR complex 1 (mTORC1) by raptor Ser863 and multisite phosphorylation.
ERK1/2 phosphorylate Raptor to promote Ras-dependent activation of mTOR complex 1 (mTORC1).

novelty.note: Searched for GSK3-mediated raptor phosphorylation, raptor Ser696/Ser863 priming, and GSK3 primed-substrate hierarchies in raptor. Stretton et al. (Biochem J 2015) report exactly this two-kinase arrangement at raptor: GSK3 acts as the secondary kinase on Ser859 and requires prior phosphorylation of Ser863 (shown by loss of Ser859 phosphorylation in the S863A mutant and by GSK3 inhibition reducing Ser859 but not Ser863), and Foster et al. had already established Ser863 as the obligatory upstream priming site for Ser859/Ser855 within a GSK3 consensus cassette. Ser863 is one of the ERK1/2 proline-directed sites identified by Carrière et al., so the priming-then-GSK3 relationship for raptor is published; only the explicit attribution of the priming event to ERK1/2 is left unaddressed in the GSK3 papers, which instead ascribe Ser863 to an amino-acid-regulated kinase.

hypotheses.statement: SRC activity is required for EGF-induced ERK2 activation, acting upstream of the Gab1–SHP2 step that drives ERK2 activation.
hypotheses.mechanism: Src knockdown in HEK293 cells lowered EGF-induced GAB1 phosphorylation and phospho-ERK without affecting EGFR autophosphorylation (borisov2009:findings:011). The SRC-family inhibitor PP2 eliminated EGF-induced ERK phosphorylation (de2015:findings:008). Independently, Gab1–SHP2 association leads to ERK2 activation, and membrane-targeted active SHP2 fused to the Gab1 PH domain constitutively activates MEK1 and ERK2 (heinrich2003:findings:010, heinrich2003:findings:011). Together these imply that SRC promotes ERK2 activation through a Gab1–SHP2-dependent route.
hypotheses.prediction: Loss of SRC activity should specifically reduce EGF-induced activation-loop phosphorylation and kinase activity of ERK2. Expressing the constitutively active Gab1-PH–SHP2 fusion should restore ERK2 activation in SRC-depleted cells, whereas re-expressing wild-type Gab1 should not.
hypotheses.test: In HEK293 cells, deplete SRC by siRNA or treat with PP2 before EGF stimulation. Measure ERK2 activation-loop phosphorylation by immunoblot, resolving ERK2 from ERK1 by electrophoretic mobility. Confirm with an in vitro kinase assay of immunoprecipitated HA-ERK2. In parallel, co-transfect the Gab1-PH–active SHP2 fusion and test whether it rescues ERK2 activation when SRC activity is lost.

citations.title: EGFR-activated Src family kinases maintain GAB1-SHP2 complexes distal from EGFR.
Roles of Gab1 and SHP2 in paxillin tyrosine dephosphorylation and Src activation in response to epidermal growth factor.
Epidermal growth factor-induced DNA synthesis. Key role for Src phosphorylation of the docking protein Gab2.
Participation of both Gab1 and Gab2 in the activation of the ERK/MAPK pathway by epidermal growth factor.
Role of Src family tyrosine kinases in the down-regulation of epidermal growth factor signaling in PC12 cells.

novelty.note: I searched three ways (Src requirement for EGF-induced ERK via Gab1/SHP2; Gab1–SHP2–Src–EGFR–ERK mechanism in HEK293-type systems; and SFK-inhibitor effects such as PP1/PP2 on EGF-stimulated ERK), retrieving abstracts through NCBI efetch and publisher/search pages. The published record already states this explanation: SFKs activated by EGFR sustain GAB1 tyrosine phosphorylation and GAB1–SHP2 complexes whose output is increased ERK activity (PMID 25969544); Src-kinase inhibition abrogates EGF-stimulated Erk activation in the Gab1–SHP2 pathway (PMID 14665621); SFK inhibition (PP1) blocks EGF-induced Gab docking-protein phosphorylation without affecting EGFR phosphorylation, and loss of SHP2 binding to the Gab protein blocks MAPK activation (PMID 12464621), with SHP2 binding to Gab1/Gab2 being the threshold step for EGF-driven ERK activation (PMID 15952937). The specific Gab1-PH–active-SHP2 rescue in SRC-depleted cells and ERK2-versus-ERK1 resolution are not themselves reported, and one study finds SFK suppression prolongs rather than prevents EGF-induced ERK1/2 activation in PC12 cells and Csk-null fibroblasts (PMID 16324154), so the ordering is context-dependent — but the explanation itself is published, hence established rather than partial.

hypotheses.statement: TGFBR2 kinase activity negatively regulates GROWTH, mediating TGF-β-induced growth inhibition of epithelial cells through Smad-dependent signaling.
hypotheses.mechanism: In NMuMG cells, dominant-negative Smad3 or Smad7 inhibited about 80% of TGF-β-induced growth inhibition (bhowmick2001:findings:001). In BxPc3 cells, loss of Smad4 abolished TGF-β growth inhibition while receptor-proximal signaling persisted, so growth control sits on a Smad branch downstream of the receptor complex (bhowmick2001:findings:008). Independently, Smad (MADR2) association with the receptor complex requires TβRI transphosphorylation by a kinase-competent TβRII (macassilva1996:findings:001), TβRII Ser213/Ser409 autophosphorylation is essential for signaling (hata2016:findings:002), and receptor-level signaling drives Smad3 activation and antiproliferation (hata2016:findings:007). Together these imply TβRII kinase activity is the upstream requirement for Smad-dependent growth inhibition.
hypotheses.prediction: Knockdown of TGFBR2, or replacement with a kinase-defective or Ser213/Ser409-to-alanine TGFBR2 mutant, should abolish TGF-β-induced reduction of epithelial cell proliferation and Smad3 phosphorylation. Re-expression of wild-type TGFBR2 should restore growth inhibition.
hypotheses.test: In NMuMG cells, deplete endogenous TGFBR2 by siRNA and reconstitute with wild-type, kinase-dead, or S213A/S409A TGFBR2. Then treat with TGF-β1 and measure proliferation by thymidine or BrdU incorporation and cell counts, alongside phospho-Smad3 immunoblots and 3TP-Lux reporter activity.

citations.title: Positive and negative regulation of type II TGF-beta receptor signal transduction by autophosphorylation on multiple serine residues.
Transforming growth factor beta-induced phosphorylation of Smad3 is required for growth inhibition and transcriptional induction in epithelial cells.
Expression of a dominant-negative type II transforming growth factor beta (TGF-beta) receptor in the epidermis of transgenic mice blocks TGF-beta-mediated growth inhibition.
Inactivation of the type II receptor reveals two receptor pathways for the diverse TGF-beta activities.
Regulation of TGF-β receptor activity.

novelty.note: I searched for kinase-defective/dominant-negative TGFBR2 blocking TGF-β growth inhibition, for TβRII Ser213/Ser409 autophosphorylation requirements, and for Smad3 phosphorylation as a requirement for the antiproliferative response. The explanation is already published in exactly this form: Luo & Lodish showed that TβRII autophosphorylation at Ser213 is essential for TβRII kinase activity, TβRI activation and TGF-β-induced growth inhibition (with Ser409 essential for signaling and Ser416 inhibitory), truncated/nonfunctional TβRII acts dominant-negatively to abolish TGF-β growth inhibition in epithelial cells in vitro and in epidermis in vivo, and C-terminal Smad3 phosphorylation by the activated receptor complex is required for TGF-β growth inhibition of epithelial cells. Reviews of TGF-β receptor regulation state the full chain (TβRII kinase → GS-domain transphosphorylation of TβRI → Smad2/3 activation), so both the mechanism and the predicted mutant phenotypes are anticipated rather than open.

hypotheses.statement: Acute rapamycin treatment increases inhibitory Ser9 phosphorylation of GSK3β in EGF-stimulated cells. The proposed route is loss of S6K1-mediated Rictor Thr1135 phosphorylation.
hypotheses.mechanism: In one study, Rictor Thr1135 phosphorylation depended on S6K1 and was acutely sensitive to rapamycin. A rapamycin-resistant S6K1 mutant made Thr1135 phosphorylation resistant to rapamycin. In a separate study, cells expressing the non-phosphorylatable Rictor T1135A mutant showed more GSK3β Ser9 phosphorylation after EGF stimulation than cells with wild-type Rictor. So rapamycin, by removing Thr1135 phosphorylation, should phenocopy T1135A and raise GSK3β Ser9 phosphorylation. Prolonged rapamycin may act differently, because it reduces Akt hydrophobic-motif phosphorylation.
hypotheses.prediction: In EGF-stimulated cells expressing wild-type Rictor, acute rapamycin should raise GSK3β Ser9 phosphorylation. This increase should be absent in cells expressing Rictor T1135A or rapamycin-resistant S6K1.
hypotheses.test: Use HEK293 cells stably expressing wild-type Rictor, Rictor T1135A, or rapamycin-resistant S6K1. Pre-treat with vehicle or rapamycin for about 30–60 minutes, then stimulate with EGF. Immunoblot for phospho-GSK3β Ser9, total GSK3β, phospho-Rictor Thr1135 and phospho-S6. The hypothesis is supported if rapamycin increases Ser9 phosphorylation only when Thr1135 phosphorylation is rapamycin-sensitive.

citations.title: mTORC1-activated S6K1 phosphorylates Rictor on threonine 1135 and regulates mTORC2 signaling.
Characterization of Rictor phosphorylation sites reveals direct regulation of mTOR complex 2 by S6K1.
S6K1 regulates GSK3 under conditions of mTOR-dependent feedback inhibition of Akt.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the mechanism in words (S6K1→Rictor Thr1135→mTORC2→GSK3 Ser9), the entities together (Rictor T1135 + rapamycin + GSK3 Ser9, including a Europe PMC full-text query), and the prediction (acute rapamycin raising Akt-substrate phosphorylation after EGF). Julien et al. (PMID 19995915) publish the general mechanism and explicitly report that 30-min rapamycin pretreatment markedly increases EGF/insulin-stimulated Akt Ser473, attributing mTORC1/S6K1 negative regulation of mTORC2 to Rictor Thr1135; however their GSK3α/β Ser21/Ser9 data compare only WT vs T1135A/T1135D Rictor without rapamycin, so the specific prediction and its dependence on Thr1135 or rapamycin-resistant S6K1 is untested. Zhang et al. (PMID 17052453) is the nearest contrary context, showing GSK3 Ser21/9 phosphorylation is rapamycin-sensitive (decreased) where S6K1 phosphorylates GSK3 directly, but this is in TSC-null cells and is not a direct test of the Rictor-Thr1135 route, so the status is partial rather than refuted.

hypotheses.statement: EGFR kinase activity positively regulates LPS-induced, NFκB-dependent proinflammatory gene expression.
hypotheses.mechanism: Two de2015 claims show EGFR is required for LPS signalling to NFκB. EGFR knockdown in A549 and OVCAR3 cells impaired LPS-induced NFκB activation, and erlotinib blocked LPS-dependent IKK/IκB phosphorylation, IκB degradation, and NFκB activation (de2015:findings:005, de2015:findings:006). Independently, in IMR90 fibroblasts, impairing p65 phosphorylation went together with loss of inflammatory (SASP) gene expression (dou2017:findings:006), and deleting p38α in epithelial cells reduced proinflammatory gene expression (cargnello2011:findings:006). Together these suggest EGFR kinase activity sits upstream of the inflammatory gene-expression output of LPS/NFκB signalling, not only upstream of NFκB pathway phosphorylation.
hypotheses.prediction: In LPS-stimulated A549 or HME cells, EGFR knockdown or erlotinib pretreatment should lower the mRNA levels of NFκB-dependent proinflammatory genes compared with control cells. Re-expressing kinase-active EGFR, but not kinase-dead EGFR, in the knockdown cells should restore that induction.
hypotheses.test: In A549 cells, deplete EGFR by siRNA (or pretreat with erlotinib) and stimulate with LPS over a time course. Measure proinflammatory NFκB target transcripts by RT-qPCR, alongside an NFκB luciferase reporter and p65 phosphorylation by immunoblot. Include a rescue with siRNA-resistant wild-type versus kinase-dead EGFR to show that the effect specifically requires EGFR kinase activity.

citations.title: Inhibition of Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor (EGFR) Reduces Lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-Induced Activation and Inflammatory Cytokines in Hepatic Stellate Cells In Vitro.
Inhibition of epidermal growth factor receptor attenuates LPS-induced inflammation and acute lung injury in rats.
EGFR kinase activity is required for TLR4 signaling and the septic shock response.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the mechanism in words (EGFR kinase activity required for LPS/TLR4 signalling to NF-κB), the entities together (erlotinib/AG1478 + LPS + NF-κB + epithelial cells), and the prediction (EGFR knockdown/TKI lowering LPS-induced NF-κB target mRNAs, plus kinase-dead rescue). The explanation is already published beyond the corpus paper: in hepatic stellate cells EGFR inhibition blocked LPS-induced NF-κB nuclear translocation and reduced TNF-α and IL-6 mRNA (PMID 30091424), and in human bronchial epithelial cells and rat lung EGFR inhibitors dose-dependently lowered LPS-induced TNF-α, IL-6, IL-1β, IL-8, MCP-1 and COX-2 transcripts (PMID 28460454). The NF-κB-dependence of that output is contested rather than uniformly supported — the lung study found EGFR inhibitors did not reverse LPS-induced IκBα degradation, and in myeloid cells EGFR kinase inhibition spared IKK/NF-κB activation and enhanced rather than reduced TNF-α induction (PMID 26341626) — and the siRNA-resistant kinase-dead EGFR rescue in A549/HME cells remains undone, so only that discriminating control is genuinely unpublished.

hypotheses.statement: p38 (p38α) regulates mTORC1 signaling through MK2-mediated phosphorylation of TSC2 at Ser1210, so p38 activity controls mTORC1 kinase output toward substrates such as 4E-BP1.
hypotheses.mechanism: MK2 activation depends completely on p38α, which phosphorylates MK2 at Thr222, Ser272 and Thr334 (cargnello2011:findings:068). MK2 phosphorylates TSC2 at Ser1210, which promotes 14-3-3 binding and may regulate mTOR-dependent protein synthesis under certain stresses (cargnello2011:findings:077). mTORC1 kinase output can be read directly as 4E-BP1 Thr37/Thr46 phosphorylation and in vitro mTOR kinase activity toward GST-4E-BP1 (carriere2010:findings:015), so a p38→MK2→TSC2 axis should produce a measurable change in mTORC1 activity.
hypotheses.prediction: Under a p38-activating stress, TSC2 Ser1210 phosphorylation and TSC2–14-3-3 binding should rise. Blocking p38α should reverse both and shift 4E-BP1 Thr37/Thr46 phosphorylation and mTOR-immunoprecipitate kinase activity. This shift should be absent in cells expressing a TSC2 S1210A mutant.
hypotheses.test: In HEK293 cells stimulated with a p38-activating stress, compare cells treated with SB203580 or p38α siRNA against vehicle or control siRNA. Measure p38-dependent MK2 phosphorylation, TSC2 Ser1210 phosphorylation, TSC2–14-3-3 co-immunoprecipitation, and phospho-4E-BP1 (Thr37/Thr46) by immunoblot. Also run in vitro mTOR kinase assays on immunoprecipitates using GST-4E-BP1. Repeat in TSC2-knockdown cells reconstituted with wild-type or S1210A TSC2 to test whether the p38 effect on mTORC1 requires this site.

citations.title: p38α senses environmental stress to control innate immune responses via mechanistic target of rapamycin.
The p38 and MK2 kinase cascade phosphorylates tuberin, the tuberous sclerosis 2 gene product, and enhances its interaction with 14-3-3.
p38 regulates the tumor suppressor PDCD4 via the TSC-mTORC1 pathway.
Phosphorylation of Raptor by p38beta participates in arsenite-induced mammalian target of rapamycin complex 1 (mTORC1) activation.

novelty.note: I searched for MK2-mediated TSC2 Ser1210 phosphorylation with 14-3-3 binding, for p38-MK2-TSC2 control of mTORC1/4E-BP1, and for direct tests of a TSC2 S1210A mutant on mTORC1 output. Li et al. (JBC 2003) established that the p38-MK2 cascade phosphorylates TSC2 Ser1210 and creates a 14-3-3 site in a p38-dependent manner, and Katholnig et al. (J Immunol 2013) directly tested the proposed axis: stress-induced p38alpha-mediated mTOR activation was MK2-dependent and required TSC1/TSC2 inhibition, with wild-type but not S1210A TSC2 restoring anisomycin-induced p70S6K activation in Tsc2-/- cells; Braun et al. (2021) restate the same p38-MK2-TSC2-mTORC1 route and show p38 inhibition fails to act in TSC1/TSC2-deficient cells. The explanation and essentially the proposed experiment are therefore already published, so the status is established; the nearest qualifier is that stress identity matters, since arsenite-induced mTORC1 activation proceeds via p38beta-Raptor independently of TSC2 and MK2.

hypotheses.statement: GSK3B directly phosphorylates STAT3 on serine and thereby negatively regulates STAT3 DNA binding and transcriptional activity.
hypotheses.mechanism: GSK3B repeatedly acts as an inhibitory serine kinase on signal-responsive transcription factors. Its phosphorylation of C/EBPβ correlates with decreased IL-17-induced gene expression (gaffen2014:findings:030, li2019:findings:008), and its phosphorylation of the R-Smad linker inhibits Smad nuclear accumulation and promotes degradation (hata2016:findings:024). STAT3 is inhibited by exactly this kind of modification: serine phosphorylation at Ser727 (by PKCδ) inhibits its DNA binding and transcriptional activity (heinrich2003:findings:023). EGF both induces STAT3 phosphorylation (darnell1994:findings:023) and increases inhibitory Ser9 phosphorylation of GSK3β (julien2009:findings:019), so the same stimulus would activate STAT3 while relieving a GSK3B-imposed brake on it.
hypotheses.prediction: Recombinant GSK3B phosphorylates purified STAT3 on serine in vitro. In EGF- or IL-6-stimulated cells, GSK3 inhibition or GSK3B knockdown lowers STAT3 serine phosphorylation and increases STAT3 DNA binding and STAT3-dependent reporter activity. A constitutively active GSK3B (S9A) has the opposite effect.
hypotheses.test: First, run an in vitro kinase assay with recombinant GSK3B and purified STAT3 (wild-type versus Ser727A), with and without a GSK3 inhibitor, and read out phosphoserine by immunoblot or mass spectrometry. Second, in IL-6- or EGF-stimulated cultured cells (e.g., HepG2), use siRNA against GSK3B, a selective GSK3 inhibitor, or overexpression of GSK3B S9A. Then measure STAT3 Ser727 phosphorylation by immunoblot, STAT3 DNA binding by SIE bandshift, and STAT3-responsive (e.g., α2M) luciferase reporter activity. Include co-immunoprecipitation of GSK3B with STAT3.

citations.title: Differential regulation of STAT family members by glycogen synthase kinase-3.
Signal integration and gene induction by a functionally distinct STAT3 phosphoform.
ERK1/2 hijack STAT3 via Thr714 phosphorylation to suppress gene expression

novelty.note: I searched three ways: GSK3β as a direct STAT3 serine kinase, GSK3 inhibition/knockdown effects on STAT3 DNA binding and reporter activity, and GSK3 as a negative regulator of STAT3. The direct-phosphorylation half of the claim is already published but with the opposite sign: Waitkus/Yang et al. (MCB 2014) show GSK-3α/β directly phosphorylate STAT3 at Thr714 and Ser727 downstream of EGFR/PAR-1, and that GSK-3α/β depletion abolishes rather than enhances STAT3-dependent gene induction. Beurel & Jope (JBC 2008) ran essentially the predicted experiment in IL-6-, IFN- and insulin-stimulated cells and report the opposite of the prediction — GSK3 inhibitors reduced STAT3 tyrosine phosphorylation, DNA binding and STAT3-driven gene expression (GFAP, Bcl-3), while not markedly affecting Ser727 phosphorylation — and they co-immunoprecipitated GSK3 with STAT3 as a positive, not inhibitory, partner. Since the specific functional prediction (GSK3 inhibition increases STAT3 DNA binding and transcriptional activity) has been directly tested and contradicted, the status is refuted.

hypotheses.statement: ERBB2 positively regulates AKT activation, sustaining EGF-induced, PI3K-dependent AKT phosphorylation.
hypotheses.mechanism: EGF stimulation activates AKT transiently through a PI3K-dependent route; wortmannin blocks AKT phosphorylation without affecting EGFR tyrosine phosphorylation (borisov2009:findings:008, borisov2009:findings:009). ErbB2-containing heterodimers are the most mitogenic ErbB complexes, and ErbB2 heterodimerization lowers partner endocytosis and increases recycling (yarden2001:findings:001, yarden2001:findings:004). Endocytosis is the principal way ErbB signalling is terminated, so ERBB2 presence could prolong receptor-driven PI3K/AKT output. The chain is indirect and relies on ERBB2 pairing with the EGF-activated receptor, so the proposed relationship is regulatory (receptor-level), not physical kinase-to-kinase.
hypotheses.prediction: Depleting ERBB2 should lower the amplitude and shorten the duration of EGF-induced AKT S473 phosphorylation. Overexpressing ERBB2 should prolong it. Both effects should be abolished by wortmannin.
hypotheses.test: Knock down ERBB2 by siRNA, or overexpress it, in HEK293 or another ERBB2-expressing cell line. Stimulate with EGF over a time course (0–120 min), with and without 100 nM wortmannin. Immunoblot for phospho-AKT (S473/T308), total AKT and phospho-EGFR, and measure surface EGFR retention by surface biotinylation.

citations.title: HER2 stabilizes EGFR and itself by altering autophosphorylation patterns in a manner that overcomes regulatory mechanisms and promotes proliferative and transformation signaling.
Epidermal growth factor-stimulated Akt phosphorylation requires clathrin or ErbB2 but not receptor endocytosis.
ErbB2 expression through heterodimerization with erbB1 is necessary for ionizing radiation- but not EGF-induced activation of Akt survival pathway.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the mechanism in words (HER2 impairing EGFR degradation/recycling to prolong PI3K-AKT output), the entities together (ErbB2 + EGF + AKT phosphorylation + siRNA/wortmannin), and the prediction (amplitude/duration of EGF-induced pAKT after ErbB2 depletion or overexpression). Hartman/Agazie (Oncogene 2013) states exactly this explanation: HER2 expression blocks EGFR Y1045/Y1068 phosphorylation (the c-Cbl docking site), stabilizing EGFR, and yields enhanced and sustained EGF-induced ERK and Akt activation versus short-lived signalling in HER2-negative controls — i.e. the corpus chain (yarden2001 endocytosis/recycling → prolonged PI3K/AKT) is already published. Garay et al. (MBoC 2015) independently show ErbB2 provides a Gab1-PI3K-Akt route for EGF-stimulated Akt phosphorylation, though redundantly with clathrin; note that Toulany et al. found ErbB2 siRNA and trastuzumab did not block EGF-stimulated Akt phosphorylation, so the knockdown arm of the prediction has been tested negatively in at least one context and is context-dependent rather than universal.

hypotheses.statement: EGFR kinase activity positively regulates (activates) mTORC1 kinase activity through ERK1/2-dependent phosphorylation of Raptor.
hypotheses.mechanism: EGFR knockdown or erlotinib inhibition blocks ERK phosphorylation downstream of LPS and EGF, so EGFR kinase activity is required for ERK activation (de2015:findings:004, de2015:findings:006). Separately, ERK1/2 directly phosphorylate Raptor. A phosphorylation-deficient Raptor S3A mutant lowers mTORC1 kinase activity toward 4E-BP1, and MEK1/2 inhibitors completely inhibit mTORC1 kinase activity (carriere2010:context:004, carriere2010:findings:015). Together these imply that EGFR activation should raise mTORC1 activity through ERK-mediated phosphorylation of Raptor, and that this effect should depend on EGFR kinase activity.
hypotheses.prediction: EGF stimulation should increase mTORC1 output (4E-BP1 Thr37/Thr46 and S6K1 Thr389 phosphorylation, and in vitro mTORC1 kinase activity toward GST-4E-BP1), along with ERK-dependent Raptor phosphorylation. Erlotinib or EGFR knockdown should abolish this increase. The part of the EGF-induced increase that depends on EGFR should be reduced in cells expressing Raptor S3A instead of wild-type Raptor.
hypotheses.test: In HEK293 or A549 cells expressing wild-type or S3A Raptor, stimulate with EGF with or without erlotinib, EGFR siRNA, or a MEK1/2 inhibitor. Immunoblot phospho-ERK, phospho-Raptor, phospho-4E-BP1 (Thr37/Thr46) and phospho-S6K1 (Thr389). In parallel, immunoprecipitate mTORC1 and run an in vitro kinase assay with GST-4E-BP1 as substrate to measure its activity directly.

citations.title: Lysosomal EGFR acts as a Rheb-GEF independent of its kinase activity to activate mTORC1.
ERK1/2 phosphorylate Raptor to promote Ras-dependent activation of mTOR complex 1 (mTORC1).

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the ERK1/2→Raptor→mTORC1 mechanism in plain words, EGF/EGFR together with Raptor and 4E-BP1, and the prediction that erlotinib/EGFR inhibition abolishes mTORC1 output (p-S6K1 Thr389, p-4E-BP1 Thr37/46). The ERK-arm is already published: Carriere et al. (JBC 2011, PMID 21071439) show EGF-stimulated, MEK/ERK-dependent phosphorylation of endogenous Raptor at Ser696/Ser863 (plus Ser8) and that phospho-deficient Raptor lowers mTORC1 signalling to 4E-BP1. However, the specific EGFR-kinase-dependence prediction has been directly tested and failed: PMID 40259053 reports that lysosome-tethered kinase-dead EGFR triggers mTORC1 as well as wild type, that erlotinib leaves mTORC1 output (p-T389-S6K1, p-Thr37/46-4E-BP1) substantially intact rather than abolished, and that erlotinib and afatinib suppress p-EGFR/p-AKT/p-ERK1/2 to comparable levels while diverging in mTORC1 activation — an explicit dissociation showing ERK suppression cannot account for EGFR's effect on mTORC1. Hence refuted for the EGFR-kinase/ERK causal route, even though the downstream ERK→Raptor step itself is established.

hypotheses.statement: SHP2 acts directly upstream of RAS in growth-factor signalling, promoting RAS-GTP loading so that RAS-to-ERK flux requires SHP2 phosphatase activity only at or above the level of RAS.
hypotheses.mechanism: Claims about RAS place it immediately upstream of Raf-MEK-ERK, with dominant-negative Ras (N17) and c-Raf inhibition abolishing MEK/ERK activation and defining the crosstalk node as being at the Ras/Raf level (borisov2009:findings:013, cargnello2011:findings:002, carracedo2008:findings:004). Claims about SHP2 show its catalytic activity is needed to sustain p-ERK in RTK-driven lines, that this requirement is bypassed by KRASG12V expression, and that RAS/BRAF-mutant lines are refractory to SHP2 loss (chen2016:findings:003, chen2016:findings:004, chen2016:findings:001). The only arrangement consistent with both sets is SHP2 feeding into ERK through RAS activation itself, so constitutively active RAS renders SHP2 dispensable.
hypotheses.prediction: SHP2 inhibition or knockdown in RTK-driven cells should lower RAS-GTP loading before and proportionally to the drop in p-ERK, and this loss should be fully rescued by expression of a GTPase-deficient RAS mutant but not by SHP2 catalytic-dead re-expression; in RAS-mutant cells RAS-GTP and p-ERK should be unaffected by SHP2 inhibition.
hypotheses.test: In an EGFR-amplified, SHP2-dependent line and a KRAS-mutant line, treat with SHP099 (or induce SHP2 shRNA) over a time course and quantify active RAS by RBD (RAF1 Ras-binding domain) pulldown immunoblot alongside p-ERK; then repeat in cells stably expressing KRASG12V versus vector, and in SHP2-knockdown cells reconstituted with wild-type versus C459S SHP2, to test whether the RAS-GTP change is required for and upstream of the p-ERK change.

citations.title: RAS nucleotide cycling underlies the SHP2 phosphatase dependence of mutant BRAF-, NF1- and RAS-driven cancers.
Molecular mechanism for a role of SHP2 in epidermal growth factor receptor signaling.
Molecular mechanism for the Shp-2 tyrosine phosphatase function in promoting growth factor stimulation of Erk activity.
