Inhibition of SHP2-mediated dephosphorylation of Ras suppresses oncogenesis.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the plain-language mechanism (SHP2 promoting RAS-GTP loading upstream of RAS), the entities together (SHP099/SHP2 inhibition + RBD pulldown + KRAS-mutant insensitivity), and the prediction (rescue by GTPase-deficient RAS, catalytic-dead SHP2 failure). The explanation is explicitly published: Agazie & Hayman (2003) place SHP2 upstream of Ras and show it increases GTP-Ras half-life by excluding RasGAP, Cunnick et al. (2000) map the SHP2 phosphatase requirement to the Ras-Raf-Mek-Erk cascade above Ras, and Nichols et al. (2018) show allosteric SHP2 inhibition lowers RAS-GTP by disrupting SOS1-mediated RAS-GTP loading with p-ERK falling accordingly. Status is established for the core statement, although Nichols et al. also directly tested the prediction's final clause and found that nucleotide-cycling oncogenic RAS mutants (e.g. KRAS G12C/G12D) do lose RAS-GTP and p-ERK upon SHP2 inhibition, so refractoriness applies only to GAP-insensitive/non-cycling mutants.

hypotheses.statement: RAF activity positively regulates mTOR (mTORC1) kinase activity under Ras/MAPK-pathway stimulation, through MEK/ERK-dependent phosphorylation of Raptor.
hypotheses.mechanism: In HEK293 cells, c-Raf inhibition with GW-5074 eliminated MEK and ERK activity, and Raf activates MEK by phosphorylating two serines in its kinase subdomain VIII (borisov2009:findings:013, marshall1995:findings:002). Separately, MEK1/2 inhibition abolished Raptor Ser696 and Ser863 phosphorylation under Ras/MAPK activation and completely inhibited mTORC1 kinase activity. A phosphorylation-deficient Raptor (S3A) lowered mTOR kinase activity toward 4E-BP1 and reduced PMA-stimulated 4E-BP1 Thr37/Thr46 phosphorylation (carriere2010:findings:011, carriere2010:findings:015). Together these imply that RAF sits upstream of the MEK-dependent input that raises mTORC1 catalytic output. This is a regulatory relationship, not a physical interaction.
hypotheses.prediction: In PMA- or Ras/MAPK-stimulated cells, inhibiting or knocking down RAF should reduce Raptor Ser696/Ser863 phosphorylation, mTORC1-immunoprecipitate kinase activity toward GST-4E-BP1, and cellular 4E-BP1 Thr37/Thr46 phosphorylation. Cells expressing Raptor S3A should show a blunted effect of RAF inhibition on mTORC1 activity compared with cells expressing wild-type Raptor.
hypotheses.test: In HEK293 cells expressing myc-Raptor and mTOR (wild-type or S3A Raptor), stimulate with PMA with or without a RAF inhibitor (e.g. GW-5074) or RAF siRNA. Include a MEK inhibitor as a positive control and rapamycin as a specificity control. Readouts: immunoblot phospho-MEK, phospho-ERK, Raptor pS696/pS863 and 4E-BP1 pT37/46, plus an in vitro mTOR kinase assay on Raptor immunoprecipitates with GST-4E-BP1 and [γ-32P]ATP.

citations.title: ERK1/2 phosphorylate Raptor to promote Ras-dependent activation of mTOR complex 1 (mTORC1).
Oncogenic MAPK signaling stimulates mTORC1 activity by promoting RSK-mediated raptor phosphorylation.
Regulation of mTOR complex 1 (mTORC1) by raptor Ser863 and multisite phosphorylation.

novelty.note: I searched for ERK/MAPK phosphorylation of Raptor at Ser696/Ser863, for Raf-level regulation of mTORC1 via MEK/ERK and Raptor, and for RAF-inhibitor (GW-5074, vemurafenib, sorafenib) effects on Raptor phosphorylation and 4E-BP1/mTORC1 kinase output. The MEK/ERK-dependent arm is firmly published: ERK1/2 directly phosphorylate Raptor on Ser8/Ser696/Ser863 and these sites promote mTORC1 activity toward 4E-BP1 (PMID 21071439), oncogenic Ras/MEK signalling stimulates mTORC1 through RSK-mediated Raptor phosphorylation (PMID 18722121), and multisite Raptor phosphorylation including Ser863 controls mTORC1 in vitro kinase activity (PMID 19864431); reviews of the RAF/MEK/ERK-mTOR crosstalk cite this as the pathway mechanism. However, I found no source that tests the RAF step itself — no report of RAF inhibition or knockdown reducing Raptor pSer696/pSer863 and mTORC1-immunoprecipitate activity, and no test of the predicted Raptor-S3A epistasis with RAF inhibition — so the specific prediction is published only at the MEK/ERK level, not at the RAF level.

hypotheses.statement: JNK1 directly negatively regulates cytokine production in T cells by phosphorylating NFATc1/NFAT2 and driving its nuclear export, so that loss of JNK1 activity raises NFAT-dependent cytokine output.
hypotheses.mechanism: Claims about JNK1 show it binds and phosphorylates NFATc1-a/-b at Ser117 and Ser172, suppresses calcineurin-stimulated nuclear accumulation of NFATc1, and thereby strongly inhibits IL-4 promoter reporter expression, with a JNK1-insensitive [Ala117 Ala172] mutant becoming constitutively nuclear and transcriptionally active (chow2000:findings:003, chow2000:findings:010, chow2000:findings:011). Independently, claims about cytokine production establish NFAT as the limiting transcriptional input: combined NFAT1/NFAT2 deletion is required for effective loss of T-cell cytokine production, and conditions that reduce sustained Ca2+-driven NFAT activation reduce effector cytokine production (hogan2003:findings:013, prakriya2015:findings:078). Together these imply that the amount of nuclear NFATc1 set by JNK1 phosphorylation is a direct determinant of how much cytokine a stimulated T cell makes, making cytokine production a direct downstream output of JNK1 rather than only a correlate of shared signalling context.
hypotheses.prediction: Loss or inhibition of JNK1 in stimulated T cells should increase secretion of NFAT-dependent cytokines (notably IL-4, and IL-2/IFN-γ) together with increased nuclear NFATc1, while expression of constitutively activated JNK1 should reduce both; the cytokine change should be abolished when NFATc1 carrying Ala substitutions at Ser117/Ser172 is the only NFATc1 present, and the magnitude of the cytokine change should track nuclear NFATc1 levels rather than total NFATc1 expression.
hypotheses.test: In Jurkat T cells (or primary CD4+ T cells) stimulated with PMA/ionomycin or anti-CD3, compare four arms — control, JNK1 knockdown/knockout (siRNA or CRISPR) or a JNK inhibitor, expression of activated JNK1, and expression of dominant-negative JNK1 — and measure secreted IL-4 and IL-2 by ELISA plus endogenous cytokine mRNA by qRT-PCR, in parallel with nuclear versus cytoplasmic NFATc1 by cell fractionation immunoblot. Decisive arm: reconstitute NFATc1-depleted cells with either wild-type NFATc1-a or the [Ala117 Ala172] mutant; if JNK1 controls cytokine production through this phosphorylation, the JNK1-dependent change in cytokine secretion will be present with wild type and absent with the mutant, whereas retention of the JNK1 effect in the mutant line would rule the mechanism out.

citations.title: Defective T cell differentiation in the absence of Jnk1.
JNK is required for effector T-cell function but not for T-cell activation.
c-Jun NH(2)-terminal kinase inhibits targeting of the protein phosphatase calcineurin to NFATc1.
JNK knockdown enhances CAR-T cell cytotoxicity through elevated NFATc1-dependent transcription in preclinical ovarian cancer models.

novelty.note: I searched for JNK1 phosphorylation of NFATc1 at Ser117/Ser172 with nuclear export, for Jnk1-deficient T cells and IL-4/Th2 cytokine output, and for JNK inhibition effects on NFAT-dependent cytokine production. The explanation is already published: Dong et al. (Science 1998) report that Jnk1-/- T cells preferentially become Th2 and that their enhanced Th2 cytokine production is associated with increased nuclear accumulation of NFATc, and Dong et al. (Nature 2000) report that T cells lacking JNK signalling make more IL-2; these are the phenotypic counterpart of the corpus paper's biochemical mechanism (Chow et al., MCB 2000, PMID 10866678, which itself states that JNK phosphorylation of the calcineurin-targeting domain blocks NFATc1 nuclear accumulation and that JNK1-null cells show enhanced NFATc1-dependent nuclear responses). Caveats rather than refutation: the same Nature paper found effector cytokine production requires JNK, and a 2025 CAR-T study found JNK knockdown enhanced NFATc1-dependent transcription while suppressing helper-T cytokine production, so the direction is context-dependent; the Ala117/Ala172 reconstitution arm appears untested.

hypotheses.statement: EGFR kinase activity mediates EGF-induced tyrosine phosphorylation and DNA-binding activation of STAT1, either by phosphorylating STAT1 directly or by acting as the proximal kinase required for it.
hypotheses.mechanism: EGF treatment of epithelial cells induces STAT1 tyrosine phosphorylation and STAT1-containing SIE bandshift complexes (SIFB, SIFC) that are distinct from the IFN-γ-induced complexes (darnell1994:findings:022, darnell1994:findings:023). Independently, EGFR kinase activity is required for EGF- and receptor-driven downstream phosphorylation events: erlotinib or EGFR knockdown blocks downstream phosphorylation (de2015:findings:006, de2015:findings:004), and the ERK pathway reporter decays upon EGFR inhibition (albeck2013:findings:000). Together these imply that the EGF-triggered STAT1 phosphorylation depends on EGFR catalytic activity.
hypotheses.prediction: In EGF-stimulated epithelial cells, blocking EGFR kinase with erlotinib or depleting EGFR by siRNA will abolish or strongly reduce STAT1 Tyr701 phosphorylation and the STAT1-reactive SIFB/SIFC SIE complexes. IFN-γ-induced STAT1 Tyr701 phosphorylation will be unaffected. If the relationship is direct, purified active EGFR will phosphorylate recombinant STAT1 on Tyr701 in vitro.
hypotheses.test: Treat epithelial cells (e.g., A549 or HeLa) with EGF, with or without erlotinib pretreatment or EGFR siRNA. Include IFN-γ as a specificity control. Measure phospho-STAT1 Tyr701 by immunoblot and STAT1-containing SIE complexes by EMSA with STAT1 antibody supershift. To distinguish direct from indirect phosphorylation, run an in vitro kinase assay with recombinant EGFR kinase domain and recombinant wild-type versus Y701F STAT1, detecting Tyr701 phosphorylation with a phospho-specific antibody.

citations.title: Phosphorylation and activation of the DNA binding activity of purified Stat1 by the Janus protein-tyrosine kinases and the epidermal growth factor receptor.
STAT activation by epidermal growth factor (EGF) and amphiregulin. Requirement for the EGF receptor kinase but not for tyrosine phosphorylation sites or JAK1.
EGFR-STAT1 pathway drives fibrosis initiation in fibroinflammatory skin diseases.

novelty.note: I searched three ways — direct EGFR phosphorylation of STAT1 Tyr701, the requirement of EGFR kinase activity for EGF-induced STAT1 tyrosine phosphorylation and SIE DNA-binding, and pharmacological (erlotinib/gefitinib) block of EGF-induced pSTAT1 — via web search plus NCBI eutils to verify records. Quelle et al. (JBC 1995) show activated EGF receptor phosphorylates purified Stat1 on Tyr701 in vitro and that this phosphorylation is necessary and sufficient to activate its DNA-binding activity, while David et al. (JBC 1996) show EGF- and amphiregulin-induced STAT activation requires the receptor's intrinsic kinase activity and is JAK1-independent; a recent Nature Communications study reiterates direct, JAK-independent, EGFR-inhibitor-sensitive STAT1 activation by EGFR. Both the indirect-requirement and direct-phosphorylation arms of the statement are therefore already published, so the status is established rather than partial.

hypotheses.statement: ERK2 negatively regulates insulin-potentiated Ras/ERK signaling by feedback phosphorylation of SOS1 and Raf-1, which terminates the ERK response that insulin amplifies.
hypotheses.mechanism: Insulin alone is a poor Ras/ERK activator but enhances ERK activation by low EGF doses. This crosstalk acts upstream of Ras and at the Ras/Raf level, and the resulting transient kinetics are attributed to ERK-mediated negative feedback (borisov2009). Independently, activated ERK2 directly phosphorylates SOS1, which disrupts SOS1 association with Grb2 and Shc (lake2016:findings:003). ERK2 also phosphorylates Raf-1, which desensitises Raf-1 and prevents Ras engagement and sustained Raf-1 activity (lake2016:findings:007). Together these imply ERK2 acts directly on the nodes where insulin's amplifying input converges, limiting the duration of insulin-enhanced signaling.
hypotheses.prediction: In HEK293 cells co-stimulated with insulin and low-dose EGF, depleting ERK2 should prolong the Ras-GTP and phospho-MEK responses and should sustain SOS1–Grb2 association. Expressing a SOS1 mutant that ERK2 cannot phosphorylate should have the same effect. Each change should be larger than with EGF alone.
hypotheses.test: In HEK293 cells, compare control siRNA with ERK2 siRNA, and wild-type SOS1 with SOS1 carrying alanine substitutions at its ERK2 phosphorylation sites. Stimulate with low EGF, insulin, or both, and run a time course. Measure Ras-GTP by Raf-RBD pulldown, phospho-MEK and SOS1 mobility shift by immunoblot, and SOS1–Grb2 association by co-immunoprecipitation. A PD184352 MEK-inhibitor arm serves as a control for ERK dependence.

citations.title: Insulin receptor-mediated dissociation of Grb2 from Sos involves phosphorylation of Sos by kinase(s) other than extracellular signal-regulated kinase.
Insulin stimulation of a MEK-dependent but ERK-independent SOS protein kinase.
Insulin-induced dissociation of Sos from Grb2 does not contribute to the down regulation of Ras activation.
Insulin-induced desensitization of extracellular signal-regulated kinase activation results from an inhibition of Raf activity independent of Ras activation and dissociation of the Grb2-SOS complex.
Feedback regulation of mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase kinase activity of c-Raf-1 by insulin and phorbol ester stimulation.

novelty.note: I searched for ERK2 feedback phosphorylation of SOS1/Grb2 dissociation, for insulin–EGF ERK crosstalk in HEK293, and for the specific prediction that blocking ERK phosphorylation of SOS1 sustains SOS1–Grb2 association under insulin. The Raf-1 arm is anticipated: Ueki et al. showed insulin-stimulated, MAPK-dependent feedback hyperphosphorylation of Raf-1 (and mSos) accompanied by decreased Raf MAPKKK activity. However, the SOS1 arm has been directly tested with the exact proposed reagent and reported negative: a Sos mutant lacking all seven canonical ERK phosphorylation sites still dissociated from Grb2 after insulin stimulation (9575148), insulin activates a MEK-dependent but ERK-independent SOS kinase (8552085), insulin-induced Sos–Grb2 dissociation does not shorten Ras activation (8649797), and insulin-induced ERK desensitization was attributed to Raf inhibition independent of Grb2–SOS dissociation (10373477). Because the specific SOS1 prediction is a stated negative result in multiple independent reports, the conjoined claim is refuted even though the Raf-1 component stands.

hypotheses.statement: Src kinase activity is a required upstream mediator of rapamycin-induced ERK (and PI3K/AKT) feedback activation, so inhibiting or depleting Src should block the MAPK rebound caused by rapamycin.
hypotheses.mechanism: Rapamycin relieves S6K1-driven IRS-1/PI3K feedback and activates ERK through Ras-Raf1(Ser338)-MEK1/2, a route that depends on receptor-proximal adaptor phosphorylation (carracedo2008:findings:004, carracedo2008:findings:006). Independently, Src is required for adaptor (GAB1) tyrosine phosphorylation and for downstream ERK and AKT phosphorylation at receptor-proximal nodes, since Src knockdown lowers GAB1 and ERK phosphorylation and the Src-family inhibitor PP2 eliminates AKT and ERK phosphorylation (borisov2009:findings:011, de2015:findings:008). If the rapamycin rebound is routed through this same receptor-adaptor layer, Src activity should be necessary for rapamycin to raise p-Raf1(Ser338) and p-ERK.
hypotheses.prediction: In rapamycin-treated cells, co-treatment with a Src-family inhibitor or Src knockdown should abolish the rapamycin-induced increases in p-ERK and p-Raf1(Ser338) (and the accompanying p-AKT rise) while leaving rapamycin's suppression of p-S6 intact; rapamycin plus Src inhibition should slow growth more than either agent alone, mirroring the rapamycin plus MEK-inhibitor additivity.
hypotheses.test: Treat MCF7 (and a second line such as HEK293) with vehicle or rapamycin for 1-24 h, with and without PP2/saracatinib or siRNA against Src, and immunoblot for p-ERK, p-Raf1(Ser338), p-GAB1, p-AKT, and p-S6 with total-protein controls; a loss of the rapamycin-dependent increment in p-ERK/p-Raf1(Ser338) specifically under Src loss-of-function, but preserved p-S6 inhibition, supports the relationship, whereas an unchanged rebound rules it out. Pair this with a crystal violet growth assay of rapamycin, Src inhibitor, and the combination to test the predicted additivity.

citations.title: Rapamycin induces transactivation of the EGFR and increases cell survival.
Combined SFK/mTOR inhibition prevents rapamycin-induced feedback activation of AKT and elicits efficient tumor regression.
Different patterns of Akt and ERK feedback activation in response to rapamycin, active-site mTOR inhibitors and metformin in pancreatic cancer cells.

novelty.note: I searched for Src as an upstream mediator of rapamycin feedback signaling, for rapamycin/ERK rebound plus Src-inhibitor co-treatment (PP2, dasatinib, saracatinib), and for the specific prediction that Src loss-of-function abolishes the MAPK rebound. Vlahakis/Ehrlich-type work (PMID 19151764) states exactly this explanation: rapamycin increases active c-Src (pY416) and decreases inhibitory pY527, c-Src then transactivates EGFR, and the Src-family inhibitor PP2 — but not its inactive analog PP3 — abolishes rapamycin's ability to raise Erk1/2 and RSK phosphorylation while rapamycin still suppresses S6K, matching the predicted pattern; a complementary paper (PMID 25023728) shows dasatinib completely blocks rapamycin-induced feedback AKT activation, and that a dasatinib-resistant Src mutant rescues the feedback, placing Src upstream. Because the mechanism, the loss-of-function prediction, and the preserved mTORC1 inhibition are all already published, this is established rather than partial; note the second paper found no in vitro additive antiproliferative effect for the combination, so only the growth-additivity portion of the prediction lacks support.

hypotheses.statement: JNK1 directly phosphorylates STAT3 on serine, and this phosphorylation inhibits STAT3 nuclear accumulation, DNA binding and transcriptional activity.
hypotheses.mechanism: JNK1 directly binds transcription factors, phosphorylates them on specific serines, and so reduces their nuclear accumulation and target-promoter activity. Examples are NFATc1-a at Ser117/Ser172 and NFAT2/NFAT4 as an inducible export kinase. Independently, STAT3's transcriptional output is negatively regulated by serine phosphorylation: PKCδ-mediated Ser727 phosphorylation inhibits STAT3 DNA binding and transactivation. Blocking STAT3 nuclear localization also suppresses its transactivation. Together, these claims suggest STAT3 could be another serine-phosphorylation substrate through which JNK1 limits transcription-factor nuclear activity. This remains an analogy, since no cited claim tests JNK1 against STAT3 directly.
hypotheses.prediction: Recombinant active JNK1 should bind STAT3 and phosphorylate it in vitro, with the phosphorylation lost when the target serine(s) (e.g., Ser727) are mutated to Ala. In cells, co-expressing activated JNK1 should reduce IL-6-induced STAT3 nuclear accumulation, DNA binding and STAT3-dependent reporter activity. Dominant-negative JNK1 or a non-phosphorylatable STAT3 mutant should abolish this effect.
hypotheses.test: Run in vitro kinase and GST-pulldown assays with active JNK1 and wild-type versus serine-to-Ala STAT3, mapping the sites by mutagenesis and phospho-specific immunoblotting. Then co-transfect HepG2 cells with activated JNK1 or dnJNK1 plus wild-type or mutant STAT3. After IL-6 stimulation, measure STAT3 nuclear fraction by fractionation/immunoblot and immunofluorescence, DNA binding by EMSA, and α2M-promoter luciferase reporter activity.

citations.title: Serine phosphorylation and negative regulation of Stat3 by JNK.
MSK1 and JNKs mediate phosphorylation of STAT3 in UVA-irradiated mouse epidermal JB6 cells.
JNK1 mediates serine phosphorylation of STAT3 in response to fatty acids released by lipolysis.
Interleukin-6-induced STAT3 transactivation and Ser727 phosphorylation involves Vav, Rac-1 and the kinase SEK-1/MKK-4 as signal transduction components.

novelty.note: I searched for JNK1-mediated STAT3 serine phosphorylation, for JNK plus STAT3 Ser727 with nuclear translocation/DNA binding readouts, and for in vitro kinase and direct-binding evidence, retrieving records via Europe PMC, Semantic Scholar and PMC. Lim & Cao (JBC 1999) state exactly this explanation: JNK induces Stat3 Ser-727 phosphorylation and JNK1 activated by MKK7 negatively regulates Stat3 tyrosine phosphorylation, DNA binding and transcriptional activity, with the effect absent for Stat1; Zykova et al. confirm active JNKs phosphorylate STAT3 Ser727 in vitro, and a 2026 J Lipid Res study attributes STAT3 Ser727 phosphorylation to JNK1 in vivo. Status is established rather than partial because the core claim is published, though I also flag that Schuringa et al. directly tested the proposed HepG2/IL-6 arm of the prediction and found IL-6 does not activate JNK-1 in HepG2 cells and that STAT3 is a poor JNK-1 substrate, excluding JNK1 in that specific setting; the nuclear-accumulation readout remains unaddressed.

hypotheses.statement: EGFR activation positively regulates TGFBR2 (TβRII) cell-surface abundance by driving AKT-dependent transport of intracellular TβRII to the plasma membrane.
hypotheses.mechanism: EGF stimulation induces PI3K-dependent AKT phosphorylation without PI3K inhibition affecting EGFR autophosphorylation (borisov2009:findings:009), and EGFR is required for AKT phosphorylation downstream of stimuli such as LPS (de2015:findings:004). Independently, AKT activation by insulin or glucose phosphorylates the RabGAP AS160, which relieves intracellular retention and rapidly moves TβRII and TβRI to the cell surface (derynck2019:findings:010). Together these imply that EGFR-driven AKT activity should mobilize intracellular TβRII to the surface, as insulin receptor-driven AKT activity does. The ERK-activated ADAM17 cleaves TβRI but not TβRII (hata2016:findings:007), so EGFR signaling would not be expected to deplete surface TβRII by shedding.
hypotheses.prediction: EGF treatment should rapidly increase cell-surface TβRII and AS160 phosphorylation without changing total TβRII protein. Erlotinib, EGFR knockdown, or PI3K/AKT inhibition (wortmannin or an AKT inhibitor) should abolish this increase. The surface TβRII gain should persist even where ERK/ADAM17 activity lowers surface TβRI.
hypotheses.test: In cultured epithelial cells such as HEK293 or MCF-10A, serum-starve the cells and stimulate with EGF for 5–60 min, with or without erlotinib, EGFR siRNA, wortmannin, or an AKT inhibitor. Quantify cell-surface TβRII and TβRI by surface biotinylation followed by streptavidin pulldown and immunoblot, alongside total receptor levels and phospho-AKT and phospho-AS160. Include an AS160 non-phosphorylatable mutant to test whether the EGF effect requires AS160.

citations.title: The insulin response integrates increased TGF-β signaling through Akt-induced enhancement of cell surface delivery of TGF-β receptors.
FAF1 phosphorylation by AKT accumulates TGF-β type II receptor and drives breast cancer metastasis.
Akt acts as a switch for GPCR transactivation of the TGF-β receptor type 1.
Novel permissive role of epidermal growth factor in transforming growth factor beta (TGF-beta) signaling and growth suppression. Mediation by stabilization of TGF-beta receptor type II.
Epidermal Growth Factor Stimulates Transforming Growth Factor-Beta Receptor Type II Expression In Corneal Epithelial Cells.

novelty.note: I searched for EGF/EGFR-driven trafficking of TβRII to the cell surface, for AKT/AS160-dependent TGF-β receptor translocation, and for EGF effects on TβRII abundance. The AKT-dependent arm is firmly established: insulin-activated AKT phosphorylates AS160 to deliver TβRI/TβRII to the surface (PMID 26420907), an AKT agonist alone suffices to translocate TGF-β receptors (PMID 34826189), and AKT raises surface TβRII without changing total receptor via FAF1 phosphorylation, with EGF used as an AKT-activating/pro-metastatic stimulus in vivo (PMID 28443643). However, the published EGF-specific links to TβRII are ERK/MEK-dependent increases in TβRII mRNA stability and total protein (PMIDs 16428382, 31147562), not AKT-dependent mobilization of a pre-existing intracellular pool; I found no study that measured surface TβRII and phospho-AS160 after acute EGF with erlotinib/EGFR knockdown or PI3K/AKT inhibition, and no negative test of it, so the specific prediction is unpublished rather than refuted.

hypotheses.statement: EGFR kinase activity activates NF-κB through IKK-dependent IκB degradation, which in turn triggers NF-κB-driven IκB resynthesis as negative feedback.
hypotheses.mechanism: In HME and A549 cells, EGF stimulation requires TAK1 and TLR4 to phosphorylate IKK and IκB, and EGFR knockdown or erlotinib blocks IKK and IκB phosphorylation and IκB degradation/resynthesis (de2015). Separately, IKKβ is essential for canonical NF-κB activation (chen2002:findings:005), and NF-κB activation induces IκB resynthesis that limits signal duration (chen2002:findings:007). Together these imply that EGFR kinase signalling feeds into the canonical IKKβ–IκB–NF-κB module, producing transient, self-limiting NF-κB activation.
hypotheses.prediction: EGF should induce RelA/p65 nuclear translocation and κB-reporter activity in HME or A549 cells. Erlotinib, EGFR siRNA or TLR4 siRNA should abolish this response. Selective IKKβ inhibition should block EGF-induced p65 translocation without reducing EGFR autophosphorylation. The EGF-induced IκBα mRNA rebound should require NF-κB activity.
hypotheses.test: In cultured HME or A549 cells, stimulate with EGF under each of these conditions: vehicle, erlotinib, EGFR siRNA, TLR4 siRNA, an IKKβ inhibitor, or a non-degradable IκBα super-repressor. Then run a time course measuring (i) phospho-EGFR, phospho-IKK and IκBα by Western blot, (ii) p65 nuclear translocation by immunofluorescence, (iii) κB-luciferase reporter activity, and (iv) IκBα mRNA by qPCR.

citations.title: Epidermal growth factor (EGF) activates nuclear factor-kappaB through IkappaBalpha kinase-independent but EGF receptor-kinase dependent tyrosine 42 phosphorylation of IkappaBalpha.
IkappaB kinase alpha and p65/RelA contribute to optimal epidermal growth factor-induced c-fos gene expression independent of IkappaBalpha degradation.
Erlotinib protects against LPS-induced endotoxicity because TLR4 needs EGFR to signal.

novelty.note: I searched for EGFR-kinase-dependent NF-κB activation via IKK/IκB, for EGF-induced IκBα phosphorylation-degradation-resynthesis with erlotinib in A549/HME cells, and for EGF-induced p65 nuclear translocation with IKKβ dependence. The positive version of this explanation is already published for exactly these cells: De et al. (PNAS 2015, PMID 26195767) report that EGF, via EGFR kinase, TLR4 and TAK1, drives IKK and IκB phosphorylation and IκB degradation and resynthesis, so the hypothesis is not novel. However, the specific IKK/IKKβ-dependence prediction has been directly tested and reported negative: Sethi et al. found that EGF failed to induce IκBα phosphorylation/ubiquitination or IKK activation and that dominant-negative IKKβ had no effect on EGF-induced NF-κB activation (while blocking TNF-induced activation), attributing EGF-induced NF-κB activation instead to EGFR-kinase-dependent tyrosine-42 phosphorylation of IκBα; Ang et al. (PMID 15155743) similarly state that EGF does not engage the classical IKK-directed IκBα phosphorylation/degradation pathway in fibroblasts. Because at least one source tested this exact mechanistic claim and stated it does not hold, the status is refuted, though the conflict may be cell-type dependent (NSCLC/EGFR-amplified lines and fibroblasts versus HME/A549).

hypotheses.statement: MEK1 activity positively regulates (activates) RPS6KB1/S6K1 under Ras/MAPK-pathway stimulation by supporting mTORC1-dependent phosphorylation of S6K1 at Thr389.
hypotheses.mechanism: MEK1/2 inhibitors abolish ERK-dependent Raptor phosphorylation at Ser696/Ser863 and completely inhibit mTORC1 kinase activity toward 4E-BP1 after PMA stimulation (carriere2010:findings:011, carriere2010:findings:015). S6K1 Thr389 phosphorylation is a direct readout of mTORC1 activity (gu2017:findings:002, dibble2009:findings:009), and S6K1 kinase activity rises in response to Ras stimulation (inoki2002:findings:000). Together these imply that MEK1 output is needed for full S6K1 activation when the Ras/MAPK pathway is stimulated.
hypotheses.prediction: In PMA- or Ras-stimulated cells, MEK1 inhibition or depletion should reduce S6K1 Thr389 phosphorylation and S6K1 kinase activity toward S6. Constitutively active MEK1 should increase them. Both effects should be blunted when Raptor is replaced by the S3A phosphorylation-deficient mutant.
hypotheses.test: Use serum-starved HEK293 cells stimulated with PMA. Treat with PD184352 or U0126, or knock down MEK1 by siRNA, or express constitutively active MEK1, each alongside wild-type or S3A Raptor. Immunoblot S6K1 phospho-Thr389 and phospho-ERK. Measure immunoprecipitated S6K1 activity in a GST-S6 in vitro kinase assay.

citations.title: TSC2/Rheb signaling mediates ERK-dependent regulation of mTORC1 activity in C2C12 myoblasts.
ERK1/2 phosphorylate Raptor to promote Ras-dependent activation of mTOR complex 1 (mTORC1).

Pharmacological and genetic evaluation of proposed roles of mitogen-activated protein kinase/extracellular signal-regulated kinase kinase (MEK), extracellular signal-regulated kinase (ERK), and p90(RSK) in the control of mTORC1 protein signaling by phorbol esters.

novelty.note: I searched for MEK1/2-inhibitor effects on S6K1 Thr389, for the ERK–Raptor Ser696/Ser863 axis, and for PMA-stimulated mTORC1 readouts. The upstream mechanism is published: Carrière et al. show ERK1/2 phosphorylate Raptor at Ser696/Ser863 and that MEK inhibition blocks mTORC1 activity, but they read this out only on 4E-BP1 and never test S6K1 Thr389 or the Raptor S3A mutant against S6K1; Miyazaki et al. independently show U0126 suppresses PMA-induced S6K1 Thr389 (~44%) in C2C12, though attributing it to TSC2/Rheb rather than Raptor. Direct tests of MEK/ERK requirement for phorbol-ester-driven S6K1 phosphorylation give cell-type-dependent and partly negative results (dispensable in some systems), so the specific MEK1→Raptor-phosphosite→S6K1 Thr389 prediction is neither established nor cleanly refuted.

hypotheses.statement: RPS6KB1/S6K1 negatively regulates MEK1 activation through a feedback loop, so that loss of S6K1 activity increases MEK1 activity.
hypotheses.mechanism: Rapamycin-mediated mTORC1 inhibition activates ERK specifically through the Ras-Raf1-MEK1/2 route, since U0126 abolishes the effect (carracedo2008:findings:004). A rapamycin-insensitive, constitutively active S6K1 suppresses this rapamycin-induced ERK activation (carracedo2008:findings:005). S6K1 directly phosphorylates the upstream adaptor IRS-1 (dibble2009:context:002). This implies that S6K1 activity restrains signalling at or above MEK1.
hypotheses.prediction: S6K1 knockdown or inhibition should increase MEK1 activation-loop phosphorylation (Ser217/Ser221) and MEK1 kinase activity toward ERK in insulin- or IGF-1-stimulated cells. Constitutively active S6K1 should prevent the rapamycin-induced increase in MEK1 phosphorylation.
hypotheses.test: Use MCF7 cells treated with rapamycin, with or without insulin or IGF-1. Compare S6K1 siRNA, a selective S6K1 inhibitor, and expression of rapamycin-resistant constitutively active S6K1 (E389 D3A/E). Immunoblot phospho-MEK1 Ser217/221, phospho-Raf1 Ser338 and phospho-ERK. Measure immunoprecipitated MEK1 activity in an in vitro kinase assay using inactive ERK2 as substrate.

citations.title: mTORC1 inhibition induces pain via IRS-1-dependent feedback activation of ERK.
Dual PI3K/mTOR Inhibitors Induce Rapid Overactivation of the MEK/ERK Pathway in Human Pancreatic Cancer Cells through Suppression of mTORC2.
Suppression of feedback loops mediated by PI3K/mTOR induces multiple overactivation of compensatory pathways: an unintended consequence leading to drug resistance.

novelty.note: I searched for the S6K1→MEK/ERK feedback in plain mechanistic terms, for the entity combination (S6K1 + MEK1 Ser217/221 + IRS-1 + rapamycin), and for the prediction (S6K1 knockdown/PF-4708671 raising MEK-ERK signalling). An independent study of mTORC1 inhibition in sensory neurons states the general explanation and directly tests part of the prediction: it reports that S6K1 phosphorylates and inhibits IRS-1 thereby restraining ERK signalling, and that the S6K1 inhibitor PF-4708671 and S6K1/2 double-knockout raise phospho-ERK with reduced inhibitory IRS-1 phosphorylation. However, no retrieved source measures MEK1 activation-loop phosphorylation or immunoprecipitated MEK1 kinase activity as a function of S6K1 loss; the two papers that do score MEK Ser217/221 attribute the over-activation to mTORC2/Grb10/PKCα and explicitly dissociate it from the mTORC1/S6K axis, so the specific MEK1-level link remains untested rather than refuted.

hypotheses.statement: PTEN positively regulates GSK3B activity by lowering AKT-mediated inhibitory phosphorylation of GSK3B (Ser9), and this depends on PTEN's lipid phosphatase activity.
hypotheses.mechanism: PTEN is a PIP3 phosphatase that opposes PI3K (manning2017:findings:002), and catalytically active PTEN, unlike PTEN-CS, reduces AKT-dependent phosphorylation of an AKT substrate (inoki2002:findings:007, inoki2002:findings:008). Separately, AKT inhibits GSK3/GSK3β (hogan2003:findings:006, haeusler2018:findings:007), and the state of GSK3β is read out by Ser9 phosphorylation (julien2009:findings:019). Together these imply that PTEN activity should keep GSK3β in its active, Ser9-dephosphorylated state, and PTEN's lipid (not protein) phosphatase activity should be the relevant function (balla2013:findings:045).
hypotheses.prediction: PTEN overexpression should lower GSK3β Ser9 phosphorylation and raise phosphorylation of GSK3 substrates, such as β-catenin at Ser33/37/Thr41. PTEN knockdown should do the opposite. A lipid-phosphatase-dead PTEN (G129E) or catalytically dead PTEN (C/S) should fail to produce these effects.
hypotheses.test: In cultured cells (e.g., HEK293) stimulated with EGF or insulin, express wild-type PTEN, PTEN-G129E or PTEN-C/S, or knock down PTEN by siRNA. Immunoblot for GSK3β pSer9, total GSK3β, AKT pThr308/pSer473 and β-catenin pSer33/37/Thr41. As a further check, co-express constitutively active AKT to test whether it abolishes PTEN's effect on GSK3β Ser9.

citations.title: PTEN inactivation induces epithelial-mesenchymal transition and metastasis by intranuclear translocation of β-catenin and snail/slug in non-small cell lung carcinoma cells.
PTEN contributes to profound PI3K/Akt signaling pathway deregulation in dystrophin-deficient dog muscle.
GSK3 beta mediates suppression of cyclin D2 expression by tumor suppressor PTEN.
PTEN, a negative regulator of PI3 kinase signalling, alters tau phosphorylation in cells by mechanisms independent of GSK-3.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the plain-language mechanism (PTEN → reduced AKT → dephosphorylated GSK3β Ser9), the entities together (PTEN + GSK-3β Ser9 + AKT + β-catenin Ser33/37/Thr41), and the predictions in both directions (PTEN overexpression/restoration vs. knockdown/knockout), using PubMed E-utilities and publisher/PMC pages. The explanation is already published as stated: PTEN knockout cells show elevated pAKT (Ser473/Thr308) together with increased inactive pGSK-3β Ser9 and consequent β-catenin stabilization/nuclear translocation (PMID 30885348), the converse is reported where elevated PTEN lowers Akt phosphorylation and thereby reduces GSK3β Ser9 phosphorylation leaving GSK3β hyperactive (PMID 19264909), and PTEN reintroduction is shown to act through a GSK3β/β-catenin/TCF axis (PMID 17043650). The lipid-phosphatase-dependence arm is the least directly demonstrated for the Ser9 readout specifically; the nearest work overexpressed PTEN with C124S and G129E mutants and attributed effects to lipid phosphatase activity, but concluded its downstream tau effects were independent of Akt and GSK-3 (PMID 16684527), so that sub-claim is adjacent rather than confirmed.

hypotheses.statement: MEK activates MTORC1 in a stimulus-dependent way: MEK activity is required for MTORC1 kinase activity when cells are stimulated with PMA (Ras/MAPK-driven), but not when they are stimulated with insulin or EGF (PI3K-driven).
hypotheses.mechanism: With PMA, Raptor phosphorylation at Ser696/Ser863 depends on MEK, since U0126 abrogates it, and MEK1/2 inhibitors completely inhibit MTORC1 kinase activity toward 4E-BP1. A Raptor mutant that cannot be phosphorylated at these sites (S3A) lowers MTORC1 activity without disrupting complex assembly. By contrast, with insulin or EGF, a rapamycin-sensitive, MTORC1-dependent phosphorylation of Rictor is resistant to U0126 but sensitive to wortmannin. This suggests MEK's input to MTORC1 is confined to the Ras/MAPK-driven stimulus.
hypotheses.prediction: In HEK293 cells, U0126 or PD0325901 should sharply reduce MTORC1 kinase activity and 4E-BP1 Thr37/46 phosphorylation after PMA stimulation. The same inhibitors should leave MTORC1 readouts after insulin stimulation largely intact (S6K1 Thr389, 4E-BP1 Thr37/46, Rictor T1135). Expressing Raptor S3A should reproduce the MEK-inhibitor effect only under PMA.
hypotheses.test: Serum-starve HEK293 cells expressing wild-type or S3A Raptor, pretreat with a MEK inhibitor or vehicle, then stimulate with PMA or insulin. Immunoprecipitate Raptor-associated mTOR for an in vitro kinase assay with GST-4E-BP1 as substrate. In parallel, immunoblot for phospho-4E-BP1, phospho-S6K1 Thr389, phospho-Rictor T1135 and pERK, and compare the MEK-inhibitor effect across the two stimuli.

citations.title: Co-ordinated activation of classical and novel PKC isoforms is required for PMA-induced mTORC1 activation
ERK1/2 phosphorylate Raptor to promote Ras-dependent activation of mTOR complex 1 (mTORC1).

novelty.note: I searched for the MEK→Raptor Ser696/Ser863→mTORC1 mechanism, for stimulus-specific MEK requirement (PMA vs insulin/EGF), and for direct tests of MEK inhibition on PMA- versus insulin-stimulated mTORC1 readouts. Liu et al. (PLOS ONE 2017), working in HEK293 and HeLa cells, directly tested the PMA arm and report that U0126 inhibited PMA-induced ERK phosphorylation by >70% while having only minor effects on mTORC1-dependent S6K phosphorylation, concluding that 'MEK/ERK and RSK are largely dispensable for activation of mTORC1 induced by PMA in our system' and that the MEK/ERK contribution to mTORC1 is cell-line variable; their readout was S6K1 rather than an in vitro 4E-BP1 kinase assay. In addition, the source paper itself (Carrière et al., PMID 21071439) reports that MEK inhibitors and ERK1/2 depletion block Raptor Ser696/Ser863 phosphorylation after EGF as well as PMA, contradicting the hypothesis's confinement of MEK input to the PMA (non-PI3K) stimulus, so the stated stimulus partition is not supported.

hypotheses.statement: MTORC1 activity inhibits MEK activation, so acutely inhibiting MTORC1 should increase MEK phosphorylation through Ras-Raf1.
hypotheses.mechanism: Rapamycin-mediated MTORC1 inhibition in MCF7 cells increases Raf1 Ser338 phosphorylation and ERK phosphorylation. Both dominant-negative Ras and the MEK1/2 inhibitor U0126 block this ERK activation, which places MEK between MTORC1 loss and ERK activation. Because MEK in turn supports MTORC1 activity, the two would form a reciprocal loop in which MTORC1 restrains its own MEK input.
hypotheses.prediction: Rapamycin or an MTORC1-selective perturbation should increase MEK1/2 activation-loop phosphorylation (Ser217/221) and MEK kinase activity in MCF7 cells. This increase should be blocked by dominant-negative Ras (N17) or by Raf1 inhibition.
hypotheses.test: Treat MCF7 cells with rapamycin, or knock down Raptor with siRNA. Measure phospho-MEK1/2 by immunoblot and MEK activity by immunoprecipitation kinase assay against kinase-dead ERK2, with and without co-expression of Ras N17 or treatment with the Raf1 inhibitor GW-5074.

citations.title: Rapamycin induces mitogen-activated protein (MAP) kinase phosphatase-1 (MKP-1) expression through activation of protein kinase B and mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase pathways.
Deconstructing feedback-signaling networks to improve anticancer therapy with mTORC1 inhibitors.
Inhibition of mTORC1 leads to MAPK pathway activation through a PI3K-dependent feedback loop in human cancer.

novelty.note: I searched for mTORC1-inhibition feedback activation of Ras-Raf-MEK, for direct measurement of MEK1/2 Ser217/221 phosphorylation after rapamycin, and for a reciprocal mTORC1-MEK loop. The core explanation is already published: Carracedo et al. show rapamycin-induced Raf1 Ser338 phosphorylation and ERK activation in MCF7 requiring functional Ras and MEK1/2, a companion review states MAPK activation by mTORC1 inhibitors is mediated by S6K-PI3K-Ras and requires Ras and MEK1/2, and a separate study directly reports that rapamycin causes rapid c-RAF Ser338 phosphorylation 'associated with a marked activation of MEK1/2, as indicated by MEK1/2 phosphorylation at Ser-217/221'. One caveat short of refutation: in that latter study a RAF kinase inhibitor failed to block the rapamycin-induced downstream phosphorylation, so the Raf1-dependence arm of the prediction is questioned in macrophages, though not tested in MCF7.

hypotheses.statement: ERK1 directly phosphorylates EGFR on serine/threonine residues as a feedback modification that limits the duration of EGFR tyrosine phosphorylation, analogous to the corpus-stated relation 'ERK1 phosphorylates FGFR1'.
hypotheses.mechanism: EGFR kinase activity is required for ERK activation (EGFR knockdown or erlotinib blocks LPS-induced ERK phosphorylation), so ERK1 is active downstream of EGFR. Recombinant activated ERK1 phosphorylates a receptor tyrosine kinase, FGFR1, on S777, and loss of that site prolongs ligand-induced receptor tyrosine phosphorylation; activated ERK1 also directly phosphorylates other purified substrates in vitro. EGFR is itself phosphorylated by a MAPK family member (p38alpha), which bears on its trafficking, so it is plausible that EGFR is a direct ERK1 substrate in a negative-feedback loop.
hypotheses.prediction: Recombinant activated ERK1 will phosphorylate immunopurified EGFR (or its cytoplasmic domain) on S/T-P sites in vitro. In cells, blocking ERK1 activity will reduce EGF-induced EGFR Ser/Thr phosphorylation and prolong EGF-induced EGFR tyrosine phosphorylation. Mutating the mapped site(s) to alanine will reproduce the prolonged tyrosine phosphorylation.
hypotheses.test: Run an in vitro kinase assay with recombinant active ERK1 versus kinase-dead ERK1 and immunopurified EGFR from HEK293 or HeLa cells, read out by [γ-32P]ATP autoradiography or pS/T-P immunoblot, and map sites by LC-MS/MS. Then treat EGF-stimulated cells with U0126 or ERK1 siRNA, and express EGFR alanine mutants of the mapped sites. Compare EGFR Ser/Thr phosphorylation and the time course of EGFR tyrosine phosphorylation by immunoblot.

citations.title: ERK-dependent threonine phosphorylation of EGF receptor modulates receptor downregulation and signaling.
Feedback control of ErbB2 via ERK-mediated phosphorylation of a conserved threonine in the juxtamembrane domain.
Negative feedback regulation of the ERK1/2 MAPK pathway.
ERK-mediated negative feedback regulation of oncogenic EGFRvIII in glioblastoma cells.

novelty.note: I searched three ways — the mechanism in plain words (ERK feedback phosphorylation of EGFR on Ser/Thr limiting tyrosine phosphorylation), the entities together (ERK1/2 + EGFR + Thr669 + juxtamembrane), and the prediction (MEK/ERK inhibition and alanine mutant altering EGF-induced EGFR tyrosine phosphorylation). The proposed explanation is long-established: EGFR Thr-669, in a PX(S/T)P ERK consensus in the juxtamembrane domain, is the receptor's major Ser/Thr phosphosite and was mapped in 1991 to a growth-factor-stimulated MAP kinase; Li et al. (2008) showed the phosphorylation is EGF-induced, blocked by U0126, absent in a T669A mutant, and that T669A alters EGF-induced EGFR tyrosine phosphorylation and receptor downregulation, and later work (ErbB2 Thr-677, EGFRvIII Thr-402) generalised it across the ErbB family with explicit ERK-inhibitor (SCH772984) dependence. A recent review of ERK1/2 negative feedback states this exact loop, so the hypothesis reproduces published mechanism rather than proposing a new one; one nuance is that loss of the site enhances acute rather than uniformly prolonged tyrosine phosphorylation.

hypotheses.statement: RAF1 (CRAF) activity is required for the MAPK (ERK) activation that follows relief of the S6K1–PI3K negative feedback loop, placing RAF1 directly upstream of that feedback-driven MAPK activation.
hypotheses.mechanism: Rapamycin activates ERK, and together with insulin or IGF-1 it superactivates MAPK. Both effects depend on an S6K1–IRS-1/PI3K feedback, because constitutively active S6K1 or PI3K inhibitors reduce them (carracedo2008). Separately, insulin–EGF crosstalk that amplifies ERK acts upstream of Ras and at the Ras/Raf level, and c-Raf inhibition abolishes MEK/ERK activity (borisov2009). CRAF, but not BRAF, is also required for inhibitor-induced MEK/ERK activation (poulikakos2010). Together these point to RAF1 as the kinase through which the feedback-released insulin/PI3K signal reaches MAPK.
hypotheses.prediction: When RAF1 is inhibited or depleted, rapamycin should no longer increase ERK phosphorylation, and rapamycin plus insulin should no longer superactivate it. Depleting BRAF should have a smaller effect. Rapamycin should still reduce phospho-RpS6, showing that mTORC1 inhibition itself is intact.
hypotheses.test: Treat serum-starved MCF7 cells with RAF1 siRNA, BRAF siRNA, a control siRNA, or the c-Raf inhibitor GW-5074. Then expose them to vehicle, rapamycin, insulin, or rapamycin plus insulin, and western blot for p-MEK, p-ERK, p-RpS6 and total proteins. As a gain-of-function check, re-express siRNA-resistant RAF1 and confirm that it restores rapamycin-induced ERK activation.

citations.title: Inhibition of mTORC1 leads to MAPK pathway activation through a PI3K-dependent feedback loop in human cancer.
The p70S6K/PI3K/MAPK feedback loop releases the inhibition effect of high-dose rapamycin on rat mesangial cell proliferation.
BRAFV600E-dependent Mcl-1 stabilization leads to everolimus resistance in colon cancer cells.

novelty.note: I searched for rapamycin/mTORC1-inhibitor-induced ERK activation via the S6K1–IRS-1/PI3K feedback together with Raf, for CRAF/RAF1 isoform requirement in feedback-driven MEK/ERK activation, and for the prediction (RAF1 knockdown or GW-5074 blocking rapamycin-induced ERK). The full text of the corpus paper itself (Carracedo et al., JCI 2008) already places RAF1 at this node: it reports that rapamycin induces Ser338-Raf1 phosphorylation and that dominant-negative Ras blocks rapamycin-induced ERK phosphorylation, concluding that rapamycin-mediated mTORC1 inhibition acts through the Ras-Raf1-MEK1/2-ERK pathway; an independent study likewise reports that high-dose rapamycin activates Raf1-MEK1/2-ERK through the p70S6K–PI3K feedback loop. The explanation is therefore published, although necessity was demonstrated at the Ras level rather than by RAF1 depletion, and the CRAF-versus-BRAF comparison remains untested (in BRAF-V600E colon cancer cells, feedback-driven ERK/Mcl-1 elevation after everolimus was instead abrogated by BRAF siRNA).

hypotheses.statement: EGFR activity negatively regulates TGF-β-induced SMAD3 activation: EGFR-driven ERK activation triggers ADAM17-mediated cleavage of TβRI, which lowers SMAD3 phosphorylation.
hypotheses.mechanism: EGFR is required for ERK activation downstream of EGF and LPS, and ERK output decays when EGFR is inhibited (de2015:findings:004, borisov2009:findings:009, albeck2013:findings:000). Separately, ERK activation causes TACE/ADAM17 to cleave TβRI but not TβRII. This reduces cell-surface TβRI and down-regulates TGF-β-mediated SMAD3 activation (hata2016:findings:007). Together these imply that EGFR signalling suppresses SMAD3 activation by depleting surface TβRI through an ERK- and ADAM17-dependent step.
hypotheses.prediction: In cells pre-stimulated with EGF, TGF-β should induce less SMAD3 C-terminal phosphorylation and less CAGA-reporter activity, and cell-surface TβRI should be reduced. The opposite should follow EGFR inhibition with erlotinib or EGFR knockdown. The EGF effect should be abolished by MEK/ERK inhibition, by ADAM17 inhibition or knockdown, or by a cleavage-resistant TβRI.
hypotheses.test: Use cultured epithelial cells such as HME or MCF-10A. Pretreat with EGF, with or without erlotinib, a MEK inhibitor, or an ADAM17 inhibitor or siRNA, then stimulate with TGF-β. Read out phospho-SMAD3 and total SMAD3 by immunoblot, cell-surface TβRI by surface biotinylation, the soluble TβRI ectodomain in the medium, and (CAGA)-luciferase reporter activity. Repeat after EGFR siRNA knockdown to test whether loss of EGFR increases TβRI surface levels and SMAD3 activation.

citations.title: TACE-mediated ectodomain shedding of the type I TGF-beta receptor downregulates TGF-beta signaling.
Post-translational regulation of TGF-β receptor and Smad signaling.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the mechanism in words (ERK/ADAM17 cleavage of TβRI lowering Smad3), the entities together (EGF/EGFR + TβRI shedding + ADAM17 + MCF10A), and the prediction (EGF pretreatment or erlotinib altering TGF-β-induced SMAD3 phosphorylation and surface TβRI). The Liu et al. Molecular Cell paper retrieved via PMC states exactly this explanation and already tested the EGF arm: EGF, PMA and serum enhance Erk signalling and decrease cell-surface TβRI, PMA suppresses TGF-β-induced Smad3 phosphorylation, and this is reversed by the MEK inhibitor U0126 and by TACE/ADAM17 inhibition (TAPI-1) or knockdown; a subsequent review frames the same axis as growth-factor (EGF) signalling attenuating TGF-β-induced Smad3 activation via TβRI ectodomain shedding. Because the published work states the mechanism, the direction, and the MEK- and ADAM17-dependence for the specified readouts, this is established rather than partial; only the erlotinib/EGFR-knockdown arm appears untested in these sources.

hypotheses.statement: PTEN negatively regulates MAPK (ERK) activation triggered by mTORC1 inhibition, acting through its PIP3 (lipid) phosphatase activity.
hypotheses.mechanism: Carracedo et al. show that rapamycin-induced ERK/MAPK activation depends on PI3K: PI3K inhibitors (LY294002, wortmannin) reduce it, which defines an S6K1-PI3K feedback loop controlling MAPK. PTEN is a PIP3 phosphatase that opposes PI3K activity, and its tumor-suppressive function is attributed mainly to its lipid phosphatase activity. PTEN should therefore act like the PI3K inhibitors on this loop and dampen rapamycin-induced MAPK activation. Consistent with this, Pten-null prostates show increased ERK phosphorylation after mTORC1 inhibition with RAD001.
hypotheses.prediction: In rapamycin-treated cells, raising wild-type PTEN should reduce the rapamycin-induced increase in ERK phosphorylation, as LY294002 does. A catalytically dead PTEN mutant (C124S) or a lipid-phosphatase-dead mutant (G129E) should not reduce it. Conversely, PTEN knockdown should enhance rapamycin-induced ERK phosphorylation.
hypotheses.test: Transfect MCF7 cells with empty vector, wild-type PTEN, PTEN-C124S or PTEN-G129E, or with PTEN siRNA versus a control. Treat with rapamycin or vehicle, with or without insulin or IGF-1 co-stimulation. Western blot for p-ERK/total ERK, p-AKT (as a PI3K readout) and p-RpS6 (to confirm mTORC1 inhibition), and compare the rapamycin-induced fold change in p-ERK across conditions. Include LY294002 as a positive control.

citations.title: Inhibition of mTORC1 leads to MAPK pathway activation through a PI3K-dependent feedback loop in human cancer.
Pten loss promotes MAPK pathway dependency in HER2/neu breast carcinomas.
PTEN-mediated ERK1/2 inhibition and paradoxical cellular proliferation following Pnck overexpression.
Restoration of PTEN expression alters the sensitivity of prostate cancer cells to EGFR inhibitors.
PTEN status is a crucial determinant of the functional outcome of combined MEK and mTOR inhibition in cancer.

novelty.note: I searched for the mechanism in plain words (PTEN dampening rapamycin/mTORC1-inhibition-induced ERK via the S6K1-PI3K feedback loop), for the entities together (PTEN + rapamycin/RAD001 + pERK; PTEN status + mTOR inhibitor + MAPK), and for the specific prediction (PTEN wild type vs C124S vs G129E and PTEN knockdown effects on ERK phosphorylation). The general half is published: Pten suppression hyperactivates Mek/Erk and endogenous Pten restoration reduces both PI3K/Akt and Mek/Erk signalling (PMID 26929372), and the PI3K-dependence of rapamycin-induced ERK plus raised pERK in RAD001-treated Pten-null prostates is the source paper itself (PMID 18725988); no retrieved work tests PTEN gain or loss on the rapamycin-induced pERK fold change, so the specific prediction is unpublished. Two retrieved papers argue against parts of it rather than confirming them — the lipid-phosphatase-dead G129E mutant still suppressed ERK1/2 like wild-type PTEN while the fully dead C124S did not, implicating protein rather than lipid phosphatase activity (PMID 24552815); PTEN restoration increased rather than decreased pERK on EGF/serum stimulation, mimicking LY294002, with G129E having no effect (PMID 18386291); and PTEN silencing or enforced expression did not significantly alter downstream pathway activation under everolimus (PMID 28220839). Because these are different stimuli and contexts rather than a direct test of the mTORC1-inhibition-triggered claim, this is partial rather than refuted.

hypotheses.statement: 14-3-3 binds GSK3B directly in a phosphorylation-dependent manner, recognizing GSK3B once AKT has phosphorylated its inhibitory Ser9 site.
hypotheses.mechanism: In the corpus, AKT phosphorylation of several substrates (FoxO1 T24/S256, c-RAF S259/B-RAF S364, TBC1D4/AS160) creates 14-3-3 binding motifs, and 14-3-3 binding inhibits or sequesters those substrates. GSK3B is also an AKT target: AKT inhibits it, and GSK3B Ser9 phosphorylation rises together with AKT-site phosphorylation of FoxO1/3a after EGF stimulation. This parallels the FoxO case, where AKT-site phosphorylation is sufficient for 14-3-3 recruitment. By analogy, the AKT-phosphorylated Ser9 form of GSK3B may also be a 14-3-3 client. This rests on a shared-kinase pattern and does not establish that the GSK3B Ser9 sequence matches a 14-3-3 motif.
hypotheses.prediction: Growth-factor or insulin stimulation should increase co-precipitation of GSK3B with 14-3-3. This association should be lost with a GSK3B S9A mutant or under AKT inhibition, and restored or unaffected with a phosphomimetic or in-vitro AKT-phosphorylated GSK3B.
hypotheses.test: Express HA-tagged wild-type, S9A, or S9D GSK3B with Flag-14-3-3 in HEK293 or HeLa cells, stimulated with EGF or insulin with or without an AKT inhibitor. Perform anti-Flag co-immunoprecipitation and immunoblot for HA-GSK3B and phospho-Ser9. In parallel, run a GST-14-3-3 pulldown of recombinant GSK3B before and after in-vitro phosphorylation by AKT, with lambda-phosphatase treatment as a control.

citations.title: 14-3-3 binds to and mediates phosphorylation of microtubule-associated tau protein by Ser9-phosphorylated glycogen synthase kinase 3beta in the brain.
14-3-3 connects glycogen synthase kinase-3 beta to tau within a brain microtubule-associated tau phosphorylation complex.
Ser9-phosphorylated GSK3β induced by 14-3-3ζ actively antagonizes cell apoptosis in a NF-κB dependent manner.

novelty.note: I searched for direct 14-3-3/GSK3β binding, for Ser9-phosphorylation-dependent 14-3-3 recognition of GSK3β, and for the predicted S9A-sensitive co-precipitation experiment. Yuan et al. (JBC 2004) state exactly this explanation: GST–14-3-3 pulls down Ser9-phosphorylated GSK3β from brain and neuronal extracts, in vitro 14-3-3 binds GSK3β only when phosphorylated on Ser9, and in transfected HEK-293 cells the phospho-Ser9 form but not the S9A mutant is engaged — i.e. the discriminating S9A experiment in the prediction has already been performed with a positive result; the earlier Agarwal-Mawal et al. (JBC 2003) paper established the direct co-precipitation, and Zhang et al. (2014) confirmed it by GST pulldown with Ser9 phosphorylated by PKC. The only part not covered by the retrieved sources is the specific attribution of the Ser9 phosphorylation to AKT under growth-factor/insulin stimulation, which those papers drive with other kinases, so the site-level explanation is published even though the AKT-stimulus link is untested there.

hypotheses.statement: RPS6KB1 (S6K1) negatively regulates MEK activation through a PI3K-dependent feedback, so loss of S6K1 activity increases growth-factor-stimulated MEK phosphorylation.
hypotheses.mechanism: In the carracedo2008 claims, rapamycin-induced ERK activation was blunted by a rapamycin-insensitive, constitutively active S6K1 and by the PI3K inhibitors LY294002 and wortmannin. The authors define this as an S6K1-PI3K feedback loop that negatively regulates MAPK. Separately, borisov2009 shows that insulin enhancement of MEK and ERK phosphorylation requires PI3K, placing a PI3K-dependent input at or upstream of MEK. Together, these suggest the S6K1-restrained, PI3K-dependent input to ERK acts at the level of MEK activation rather than only on ERK itself.
hypotheses.prediction: Knocking down S6K1 or blocking it with rapamycin should raise insulin- or EGF-stimulated phospho-MEK. Wortmannin or LY294002 should prevent this increase. Expressing rapamycin-resistant, constitutively active S6K1 should suppress the rise in phospho-MEK after rapamycin.
hypotheses.test: In HEK293 or MCF7 cells stimulated with insulin, run immunoblots for phospho-MEK, phospho-ERK and phospho-S6K1 T389 under four conditions: control vs. S6K1 siRNA; rapamycin alone vs. rapamycin plus wortmannin; and rapamycin-resistant active S6K1 vs. vector. If phospho-MEK does not change when S6K1 activity is altered, the hypothesis is ruled out.

citations.title: Different patterns of Akt and ERK feedback activation in response to rapamycin, active-site mTOR inhibitors and metformin in pancreatic cancer cells.
Dual PI3K/mTOR Inhibitors Induce Rapid Overactivation of the MEK/ERK Pathway in Human Pancreatic Cancer Cells through Suppression of mTORC2.
mTORC1 inhibition induces pain via IRS-1-dependent feedback activation of ERK.

novelty.note: I searched for the S6K1/mTORC1-PI3K feedback onto MAPK, for direct phospho-MEK readouts after rapamycin or S6K1 loss, and for S6K1-MEK regulation. The general feedback (mTORC1/S6K1 inhibition relieving IRS-1/PI3K restraint on Ras-Raf-ERK) is published, but I retrieved two studies from the same group that directly tested the specific prediction with phospho-MEK immunoblots under insulin stimulation: rapamycin and everolimus, at concentrations that fully blocked the mTORC1/S6K axis, produced no detectable enhancement of MEK/ERK activation, whereas active-site mTOR inhibitors did raise insulin-stimulated phospho-MEK in a manner that persisted when PI3K was inhibited (attributed to mTORC2/Rictor, explicitly dissociated from the S6K1-PI3K loop). Because both the S6K1-dependence and the PI3K-dependence of the phospho-MEK increase were tested and reported negative, I record refuted; the nearest positive work shows S6K1-IRS-1 feedback to ERK without any MEK-level measurement.

hypotheses.statement: SYK activates RAS, which is the route by which SYK-dependent receptor signalling (e.g., CLEC7A/Dectin-1) drives ERK activation.
hypotheses.mechanism: One claim reports that SYK-mediated signalling downstream of CLEC7A induces chemokine and cytokine production via ERK. Other claims place RAS directly upstream of ERK: RAS activates Raf, which activates MEK, which phosphorylates ERK. A dominant-negative Ras (N17) also blocks ERK phosphorylation triggered by a separate upstream stimulus. The evidence therefore implies that SYK-driven ERK activation may pass through RAS activation, making RAS a direct downstream target of SYK signalling.
hypotheses.prediction: Dectin-1 ligation should increase GTP-bound RAS in a SYK-dependent way. SYK inhibition or knockdown should abolish this increase. Dominant-negative RAS(N17) should block ERK phosphorylation downstream of Dectin-1 or SYK without reducing SYK autophosphorylation.
hypotheses.test: Use a Dectin-1-responsive macrophage or dendritic-like cell line. Stimulate with curdlan or zymosan, with or without a SYK inhibitor or SYK siRNA. Measure RAS-GTP by Raf-RBD pull-down and western blot. In parallel, express RAS(N17) or empty vector, then immunoblot phospho-ERK1/2 (T202/Y204) and phospho-SYK after stimulation.

citations.title: CARD9 mediates Dectin-1-induced ERK activation by linking Ras-GRF1 to H-Ras for antifungal immunity.
A Ras activation pathway dependent on Syk phosphorylation of protein kinase C.

novelty.note: I searched for the mechanism in plain words (Syk-driven Ras activation feeding ERK), the entities together (Dectin-1/CLEC7A + Syk + Ras + ERK in macrophages), and the prediction (Syk-dependent Ras-GTP loading measured by Raf-RBD pulldown after curdlan/zymosan). Jia et al. (J Exp Med 2014) states exactly this explanation: Dectin-1 engagement initiates Syk-dependent Ras-GRF1 phosphorylation, which recruits and activates H-Ras via a CARD9 complex, and this H-Ras activation is what drives Dectin-1-induced ERK activation and proinflammatory output in antifungal immunity; an earlier PNAS study independently established a Syk-dependent route to Ras/ERK activation (via Syk phosphorylation of conventional PKC creating Grb2/Sos docking sites) in FcεRI-stimulated mast cells. Because the specific claim — Syk activating Ras as the route to ERK downstream of Dectin-1 — is directly stated and supported in the published record, the status is established rather than partial.

hypotheses.statement: JNK1 directly restrains IFNγ production in CD4+ T helper cells by phosphorylating NFATc1-a/b at Ser117/Ser172 to drive its nuclear export, so loss of JNK1 activity increases NFAT-dependent cytokine promoter output.
hypotheses.mechanism: The JNK1 claims establish that JNK1 binds and phosphorylates NFATc1-a/b at Ser117/Ser172, reducing calcineurin binding and nuclear NFATc1, and that this directly suppresses an NFAT-dependent cytokine (IL-4) promoter reporter, with Jnk1-/- TH cells showing increased nuclear NFATc1 and skewed cytokine secretion. The IFNγ evidence shows IFNγ production by T cells is an NFAT-dependent, TCR-driven output: it is blunted by treatments that block antigen-specific TCR signalling while sparing PMA/ionomycin responses, and is suppressed by D-2HG partly through disruption of NFATC1 activity. Together these imply that JNK1-mediated phosphorylation of NFATc1 is a direct negative input onto the IFNγ locus's NFAT-dependent activation in T cells.
hypotheses.prediction: Expression of activated JNK1 in T cells should reduce IFNG promoter/reporter activity and IFNγ protein output upon anti-CD3 or PMA/ionomycin stimulation, while dominant-negative JNK1 or JNK1 knockdown should increase nuclear NFATc1 and raise IFNγ output; the NFATc1-a [Ala117 Ala172] mutant should render IFNγ induction insensitive to activated JNK1.
hypotheses.test: In Jurkat or primary CD4+ T cells, co-transfect an IFNG promoter luciferase reporter with activated JNK1, dominant-negative JNK1, or empty vector, plus wild-type NFATc1-a versus the [Ala117 Ala172] mutant; stimulate with anti-CD3 or PMA/ionomycin and read luciferase, in parallel measuring secreted IFNγ by ELISA and nuclear NFATc1 by cell fractionation immunoblot. A JNK1-dependent, Ser117/Ser172-dependent change in IFNG reporter and IFNγ secretion supports the relationship; equal IFNγ output across all JNK1 conditions, or loss of the effect only for the IL-4 reporter and not IFNG, rules it out.

citations.title: c-Jun NH(2)-terminal kinase inhibits targeting of the protein phosphatase calcineurin to NFATc1.
c-Jun N-terminal kinase (JNK) positively regulates NFATc2 transactivation through phosphorylation within the N-terminal regulatory domain.
Regulation of interferon-gamma gene expression by nuclear factor of activated T cells.
NFATc1 deficiency in T cells protects mice from experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis.
JNK is required for effector T-cell function but not for T-cell activation.

novelty.note: I searched for the JNK1–NFATc1 Ser117/Ser172 nuclear-export mechanism, for JNK1/Jnk1-knockout effects on IFNγ and Th1 differentiation, and for NFAT-dependence of the IFNG promoter (PubMed/eutils, publisher pages). The component mechanisms are published — JNK phosphorylates the NFATc1/NFATc2 N-terminal regulatory domain (Ser117/Ser172 for NFATc1-a, suppressing an IL-4 reporter; Thr116/Ser170 for NFATc2, where the effect is reported as positive rather than inhibitory), and NFAT activity is required for IFNγ transcription (chiefly NFATc2, with conditional NFATc1 loss also lowering IFNγ in vivo) — but no retrieved source states that JNK1 restrains IFNγ by exporting NFATc1, tests an IFNG reporter against activated/dominant-negative JNK1, or tests the [Ala117 Ala172] mutant for IFNγ. The nearest functional work points the other way at the whole-cell level (Jnk1- and Jnk2-deficient T cells are deficient in Th1/effector cytokine production), but that is not a direct test of the Ser117/Ser172-dependent claim, so this is partial rather than refuted.

hypotheses.statement: ERK1 inhibits RAS activation through negative feedback, so that ERK1 kinase activity limits the amplitude and duration of growth-factor-induced RAS-GTP.
hypotheses.mechanism: RAS acts upstream of MEK-mediated ERK1/2 activation (cargnello2011:findings:002; carracedo2008:findings:004). In HEK293 cells, EGF- or insulin-induced Ras-GTP is transient, and the model attributes this to negative feedback that includes ERK (borisov2009:findings:008). ERK1 directly phosphorylates upstream components in ways that shorten signalling: FGFR1 S777, whose loss prolongs receptor tyrosine phosphorylation, and MEK1 T292 (lake2016:findings:002; lake2016:findings:010). Together these suggest that ERK1 activity feeds back to curtail RAS activation.
hypotheses.prediction: Knocking down ERK1, or blocking ERK activation with U0126, should give higher and more sustained RAS-GTP after EGF stimulation. Re-expressing wild-type ERK1, but not kinase-dead ERK1, should restore transient RAS-GTP kinetics. ERK1 and ERK2 knockdown together should have a larger effect than either alone.
hypotheses.test: In HEK293 cells, deplete ERK1 by siRNA (alone, together with ERK2, or with rescue by wild-type versus kinase-dead ERK1), or treat with U0126. Stimulate with EGF and measure RAS-GTP over a 0–120 min time course by Raf-RBD pulldown and immunoblotting, comparing peak and decay kinetics with control cells.

citations.title: Desensitization of Ras activation by a feedback disassociation of the SOS-Grb2 complex.
SOS phosphorylation and disassociation of the Grb2-SOS complex by the ERK and JNK signaling pathways.
Multiple decisive phosphorylation sites for the negative feedback regulation of SOS1 via ERK.
Relief of profound feedback inhibition of mitogenic signaling by RAF inhibitors attenuates their activity in BRAFV600E melanomas.

novelty.note: I searched for ERK-mediated negative feedback onto RAS-GTP loading, for ERK phosphorylation of SOS/Grb2-SOS in the context of transient EGF-induced Ras activation, and for the prediction that blocking MEK/ERK raises and sustains RAS-GTP. The explanation is long-established: MEK/ERK-dependent phosphorylation of SOS1 dissociates the Grb2-SOS complex and desensitizes Ras activation, accounting for the transience of growth-factor-induced Ras-GTP (Waters 1995; Langlois 1996, which shows ERK and not JNK is the responsible pathway; Kamioka 2010 quantifies multiple decisive ERK sites on SOS1), and pharmacological interruption of ERK signalling demonstrably relieves this feedback and increases Ras-GTP (Lito 2012). Only the ERK1-versus-ERK2 isoform partition and the specific HEK293 siRNA/kinase-dead rescue design go beyond what these sources state, so the core explanation is anticipated rather than merely related.

hypotheses.statement: Insulin synergistically enhances EGF-induced activation of RPS6KA1 (RSK1), in a PI3K-dependent way, while insulin alone only weakly activates RSK1.
hypotheses.mechanism: In HEK293 cells, insulin alone is a poor activator of ERK and is much weaker than low EGF even at saturating doses, but it amplifies ERK activation by low physiological EGF. This amplification is lost when PI3K is inhibited with wortmannin (borisov2009:findings:000, :007, :009). RSK1 activation requires ERK1/2-mediated phosphorylation at essential sites including Ser380 and Thr573, and RSK1 translocates to the nucleus upon ERK1/2 stimulation (cargnello2011:findings:023, :020). The insulin-driven gain in ERK output should therefore pass directly to RSK1 activation state.
hypotheses.prediction: Insulin alone should give minimal RSK1 phosphorylation at Ser380 and Thr573. Low-dose EGF plus insulin should give greater and longer-lasting RSK1 phosphorylation and more RSK1 nuclear accumulation than EGF alone. This enhancement should be abolished by wortmannin or by MEK inhibition.
hypotheses.test: Treat serum-starved HEK293 cells with low-dose EGF (about 0.1 nM), insulin (about 100 nM), or both, with and without pretreatment by wortmannin or a MEK inhibitor such as U0126. Run a time course and immunoblot for phospho-RSK1 (Ser380, Thr573), phospho-ERK1/2 and phospho-AKT. As an activity readout, measure RSK-specific rpS6 Ser235/236 phosphorylation in rapamycin-treated cells. Assess RSK1 nuclear translocation by immunofluorescence.

citations.title: Systems-level interactions between insulin-EGF networks amplify mitogenic signaling.
PI3K is required for insulin-stimulated but not EGF-stimulated ERK1/2 activation.
Insulin activates RSK (p90 ribosomal S6 kinase) to trigger a new negative feedback loop that regulates insulin signaling for glucose metabolism.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the plain-language mechanism (insulin amplifying EGF-induced RSK/ERK output in a PI3K-dependent manner), the entities together (insulin + EGF + p90RSK/RPS6KA1 + wortmannin/Ser380/Thr573), and the prediction (synergistic, greater-than-additive RSK phosphorylation and its loss on PI3K or MEK inhibition), using PubMed/Europe PMC, publisher pages and phosphoproteomic surveys. The upstream half is published: insulin is a weak Ras/ERK activator yet synergistically amplifies low-dose-EGF ERK activation in HEK293 via PIP3/GAB1-IRS feedback, and this synergy is abolished by PI3K inhibition (PMID 19357636); PI3K-dependence of insulin-driven (but not EGF-driven) ERK1/2 activation is independently reported (PMID 16406609). I found no source that measures RSK1 Ser380/Thr573, RSK-specific rpS6 Ser235/236, or RSK1 nuclear translocation under insulin + low EGF co-stimulation with wortmannin/U0126, so the specific RSK1-level prediction is unaddressed; notably, insulin alone has been shown to activate RSK appreciably in muscle and liver cell models (PMID 24036112), which qualifies but does not test the 'insulin alone is weak at RSK1' component in HEK293.

hypotheses.statement: EGFR kinase activity positively regulates growth factor-stimulated global protein biosynthesis through its activation of the MEK/ERK pathway.
hypotheses.mechanism: EGFR kinase activity is required for ERK activation: erlotinib or EGFR knockdown blocks ERK phosphorylation (de2015:findings:004, de2015:findings:006), and an ERK-output reporter decays when EGFR is inhibited (albeck2013:findings:000). Separately, MEK1/2 inhibition blocks growth factor-stimulated global protein synthesis (carriere2010:context:000). Together these imply that EGFR sits upstream of a MEK/ERK-dependent increase in protein synthesis. Because MNKs appear dispensable for global protein synthesis (carriere2010:context:001), any such effect would not be expected to require eIF4E phosphorylation by MNK.
hypotheses.prediction: EGF stimulation should increase the global rate of protein synthesis. This increase should be abolished by an EGFR kinase inhibitor (erlotinib) or EGFR knockdown, and also by a MEK inhibitor. MEK inhibition should add no further suppression in EGFR-inhibited cells, and the effect should persist when MNK1/2 is inhibited.
hypotheses.test: In serum-starved EGFR-expressing cultured cells (e.g., HME, A549 or MCF-10A), stimulate with EGF after pretreatment with vehicle, erlotinib, EGFR siRNA, a MEK1/2 inhibitor, the combination, or the MNK inhibitor CGP57380. Quantify global protein synthesis by puromycin incorporation (SUnSET immunoblot) or 35S-methionine incorporation, and measure p-ERK in parallel by immunoblot.

citations.title: Inhibition of growth factor-induced protein synthesis by a selective MEK inhibitor in aortic smooth muscle cells.
ERK1/2 phosphorylate Raptor to promote Ras-dependent activation of mTOR complex 1 (mTORC1).

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the mechanism in words (EGF-stimulated global protein synthesis requiring MEK/ERK), the entities together (EGFR/erlotinib/gefitinib + global protein synthesis + puromycin/35S incorporation), and the prediction (MEK inhibitor abolishing EGF-driven translation, MNK-independence). The component steps are published — a MEK inhibitor blocks growth factor-stimulated global protein synthesis in aortic smooth muscle cells (Servant et al.), and EGF-driven ERK1/2 signalling feeds the translational machinery via Raptor/mTORC1 phosphorylation (Carrière et al.) — but I found no source that states or tests the specific chain of EGFR kinase activity being required for a MEK/ERK-dependent rise in global protein synthesis (no study combining EGFR inhibition/knockdown with global synthesis readouts and epistasis against MEK inhibition), and no stated negative result for it.

hypotheses.statement: SYK kinase activity is required upstream for MAPK (ERK1/2) activation downstream of ITAM-coupled CLEC7A (Dectin-1) engagement in myeloid cells.
hypotheses.mechanism: mcsai2010 reports that SYK-mediated signalling after CLEC7A ligation drives chemokine and cytokine production via ERK. The MAPK evidence establishes phospho-ERK as the readout of MAPK pathway activation (carracedo2008) and shows that tyrosine kinases can activate the MAPK effector kinase and its substrates even without activating upstream MAPK-pathway kinases (bradley2024). Together these suggest that SYK, a tyrosine kinase, is a direct upstream requirement for MAPK activation in this receptor context.
hypotheses.prediction: Yeast-particle stimulation should raise ERK1/2 Thr202/Tyr204 phosphorylation in wild-type myeloid cells. This increase should be abolished by SYK loss or SYK kinase inhibition, and should be restored by wild-type SYK but not by kinase-dead SYK.
hypotheses.test: In a cultured macrophage or dendritic cell line, knock out or knock down SYK, or treat with a SYK kinase inhibitor, then stimulate with yeast particles. Measure phospho-ERK1/2 (Thr202/Tyr204) and total ERK by western blot over a time course. Include rescue with wild-type versus kinase-dead SYK, and use a MEK inhibitor as a pathway control.

citations.title: Syk‐dependent ERK activation regulates IL‐2 and IL‐10 production by DC stimulated with zymosan
Syk-Dependent Cytokine Induction by Dectin-1 Reveals a Novel Pattern Recognition Pathway for C Type Lectins
Dexamethasone induced inhibition of Dectin-1 activation of antigen presenting cells is mediated via STAT-3 and NF-κB signaling pathways.

novelty.note: I searched for Dectin-1/Syk-dependent ERK activation with zymosan and curdlan, for Syk-inhibitor effects on phospho-ERK1/2 in dendritic cells/macrophages, and for Syk kinase-activity requirements downstream of hemITAM C-type lectins. Slack et al. (Eur J Immunol 2007) reports exactly this explanation: zymosan-induced ERK activation in dendritic cells is completely blocked in Syk-deficient DC and unaffected by MyD88 deficiency, attributing ERK activation to the Syk-coupled receptor Dectin-1 and linking it to downstream cytokine output; Rogers et al. (Immunity 2005) established the Dectin-1 hemITAM-Syk cytokine pathway in Syk-/- DC, and a later study shows the Syk inhibitor R406 reduces curdlan-induced ERK phosphorylation in DC. Because the core statement (Syk required upstream for ERK1/2 activation after Dectin-1 engagement in myeloid cells) is directly stated and demonstrated, the status is established, even though the specific wild-type versus kinase-dead SYK rescue comparison was not found.

hypotheses.statement: RPS6KB1 (S6K1) promotes 14-3-3 binding to Rictor by directly phosphorylating Rictor at T1135, which generates a 14-3-3 docking site.
hypotheses.mechanism: S6K1 from insulin-stimulated cells directly phosphorylates Rictor T1135 in vitro in a rapamycin-sensitive way, and knocking down S6K1 (but not S6K2) specifically reduces T1135 phosphorylation in cells. Independently, Rictor's association with 14-3-3 in pulldowns and co-IPs depends largely on T1135 phosphorylation. This matches the corpus pattern in which AGC kinases that can share sites with S6K1, such as Akt and RSK, create 14-3-3 binding motifs by phosphorylating their substrates. Together these claims imply that S6K1 activity is a direct upstream determinant of Rictor–14-3-3 complex formation.
hypotheses.prediction: Rictor–14-3-3 association should fall when S6K1 is depleted or inhibited, for example with S6K1 siRNA or rapamycin, and should rise when Rictor is pre-phosphorylated by S6K1. Rapamycin-resistant S6K1 should keep the association intact under rapamycin, and none of these effects should occur with the Rictor T1135A mutant.
hypotheses.test: In HEK-293E cells expressing myc-Rictor (wild type or T1135A), deplete S6K1 or S6K2 by siRNA, or treat with rapamycin with or without rapamycin-resistant S6K1. Then measure Rictor binding to 14-3-3 by GST–14-3-3 pulldown and Flag-14-3-3 co-IP with immunoblotting. In parallel, phosphorylate immunopurified Rictor in vitro with immunoprecipitated active versus kinase-dead S6K1 and test binding to recombinant GST–14-3-3.

citations.title: Characterization of Rictor phosphorylation sites reveals direct regulation of mTOR complex 2 by S6K1.
mTORC1-Activated S6K1 Phosphorylates Rictor on Threonine 1135 and Regulates mTORC2 Signaling
The role of RICTOR amplification in targeted therapy and drug resistance.
