novelty.note: Searched for the mechanism in plain words (S6K1 phosphorylates Rictor T1135 creating a 14-3-3 docking site), the entities together (Rictor/T1135/14-3-3/S6K1), and the prediction (mTORC1-S6K1 negative feedback onto mTORC2 via 14-3-3). The hypothesis is the explicit published conclusion of Dibble, Asara & Manning (MCB 2009; the corpus paper itself), whose abstract states that Rictor-T1135 is directly phosphorylated by the mTORC1-dependent kinase S6K1 and that phosphorylation of T1135 stimulates binding of Rictor to 14-3-3 proteins; an independent review restates the same causal chain, and Julien et al. independently confirm direct S6K1 phosphorylation of Rictor Thr1135. No source was found reporting a direct negative test, so this is established rather than novel or refuted.

hypotheses.statement: EGFR kinase activity is required for EGF-stimulated activation of RPS6KB1 (S6K1), measured as S6K1 Thr389 phosphorylation and S6K kinase activity.
hypotheses.mechanism: EGFR kinase activity is required for ligand-induced AKT and ERK phosphorylation (de2015:findings:004, de2015:findings:006). EGF stimulation drives both Ras/ERK and PI3K-dependent AKT signalling (borisov2009:findings:009). On the S6K1 side, S6K activity is stimulated by insulin and by Ras and is restrained by TSC1/TSC2 (inoki2002:findings:000). S6K1 Thr389 phosphorylation becomes growth-factor dependent when TSC2 is present, in cells where EGF drives the upstream Akt response (huang2008:findings:017). Together these imply that EGFR sits upstream of S6K1 activation in EGF-stimulated cells, likely acting through the Ras and PI3K/AKT inputs that relieve TSC restraint, rather than through direct phosphorylation.
hypotheses.prediction: In serum-starved, TSC2-intact cells, EGF should raise S6K1 Thr389 phosphorylation and S6K kinase activity toward GST–S6. Erlotinib or EGFR siRNA should abolish this rise, while insulin-stimulated S6K1 activation should remain intact. In TSC2-null cells, S6K1 Thr389 phosphorylation should be largely insensitive to EGFR inhibition.
hypotheses.test: Serum-starve HEK293 (or MCF-10A) cells and pretreat them with erlotinib, EGFR siRNA or vehicle. Stimulate with EGF, using insulin as a specificity control. Immunoblot for phospho-EGFR, phospho-AKT, phospho-ERK and S6K1 Thr389. In parallel, immunoprecipitate HA–S6K1 for an in vitro kinase assay on GST–S6. Repeat the experiment in Tsc2-/- versus TSC2-reconstituted MEFs to test whether EGFR-dependence of S6K1 activation requires TSC2.

citations.title: Carbachol induces p70S6K1 activation through an ERK-dependent but Akt-independent pathway in human colonic epithelial cells.
Lysosomal EGFR acts as a Rheb-GEF independent of its kinase activity to activate mTORC1.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the mechanism in words (EGF-stimulated S6K1 T389 requires EGFR kinase activity), the entities together (erlotinib/gefitinib/AG1478 + p70S6K Thr389 + TSC2/Rheb/mTORC1), and the prediction (TSC2-null MEFs show growth-factor-independent S6K1 T389). Yosida/Yang et al. (BBRC 2009) explicitly report that the EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor AG1478 'completely prevented p70S6K1 phosphorylation on Thr389 induced by exogenous EGF' in serum-starved human colonic epithelial cells, using EGF-independent (carbachol) stimulation as the specificity contrast — this states the core claim for this phenomenon, so the status is established rather than open. A recent Cell Research study qualifies but does not refute it: it finds a lysosomal, kinase-independent Rheb-GEF function of EGFR (kinase-dead EGFR still activates mTORC1; erlotinib suppresses p-T389-S6K1 less than afatinib), though those experiments were in EGFR-mutant lung cancer lines without EGF stimulation, so they do not constitute a direct negative test of EGF-stimulated, EGFR-kinase-dependent S6K1 activation.

hypotheses.statement: EGFR kinase activity is required for RSK activation, specifically hydrophobic-motif Ser380 phosphorylation, in response to EGF and to LPS, acting through ERK1/2.
hypotheses.mechanism: EGFR knockdown or erlotinib blocks LPS-induced ERK phosphorylation (de2015:findings:004, de2015:findings:006), and ERK pathway output decays when EGFR is inhibited (albeck2013:findings:000). RSK activation depends on ERK1/2-mediated phosphorylation of its essential sites, and growth-factor-induced Ser380 phosphorylation is ERK-mediated (cargnello2011:findings:023, chou2020:context:000). Together these imply that loss of EGFR kinase activity should remove the ERK input needed for RSK activation. The mTORC2 input (chou2020:findings:001) may leave a residual pool of phospho-Ser380.
hypotheses.prediction: Inhibiting EGFR (erlotinib or siRNA) should markedly reduce EGF- and LPS-induced RSK phospho-Ser380 and phospho-Ser221 and RSK kinase activity, with a matching drop in phospho-ERK. Expressing constitutively active MEK1 should restore RSK phosphorylation despite EGFR inhibition, showing the effect runs through ERK.
hypotheses.test: In HeLa or A549 cells, compare EGFR siRNA or erlotinib pretreatment with controls, then stimulate with EGF or LPS over a 5–30 min time course. Immunoblot phospho-EGFR, phospho-ERK1/2, and phospho-RSK (Ser380, Ser221), and measure RSK activity with an in vitro kinase assay on immunoprecipitated RSK. Repeat in cells expressing constitutively active MEK1, and with an ERK inhibitor, to establish that the EGFR-to-RSK effect depends on ERK.

citations.title: Epidermal growth factor stimulates RSK2 activation through activation of the MEK/ERK pathway and src-dependent tyrosine phosphorylation of RSK2 at Tyr-529.
mTORC2 Is Involved in the Induction of RSK Phosphorylation by Serum or Nutrient Starvation.
Erlotinib protects against LPS-induced endotoxicity because TLR4 needs EGFR to signal.

novelty.note: I searched for EGFR-inhibitor effects on RSK hydrophobic-motif phosphorylation, for LPS/TLR4-driven RSK activation, and for the EGF→ERK→RSK Ser380 mechanism. The EGF arm is published: Kang et al. show EGF-induced RSK2 HM-site (Ser386, equivalent to RSK1 Ser380) phosphorylation and activation is MEK/ERK-dependent (U0126-sensitive), though they used no EGFR inhibitor or knockdown and attributed an additional Src-dependent Tyr529 input; Chou et al. establish that ERK is necessary but not sufficient for HM-site phosphorylation because of an mTORC2 input, consistent with the predicted residual phospho-Ser380 pool. The LPS arm is not published: the PNAS study showing EGFR knockdown/erlotinib blocks LPS-induced ERK (and NFκB, AKT) activation never assays RSK, Ser380 or Ser221, and I found no source stating or testing that LPS-induced RSK activation requires EGFR kinase activity, nor any negative result, so the connection between the corpus findings remains unstated.

hypotheses.statement: NTRK1 (TrkA), once activated by NGF, activates MAPK (ERK1/2), and the level of NTRK1 sets how strong and how sustained that MAPK activation is.
hypotheses.mechanism: In the MAPK evidence, ERK phosphorylation is the readout for MAPK activation, with rapamycin-mediated ERK activation and MAPK superactivation treated as the same event (carracedo2008:findings:005). In the NTRK1 evidence, adding NTRK1 to MCF10A cells made NGF produce a steady ERK activity signal that did not depend on EGFR, and its amplitude rose with NGF dose (sparta2015:findings:002, sparta2015:findings:003). In PC12 cells, lowering the number of TrkA receptors turned sustained ERK activation into transient activation (marshall1995:findings:005). Taken together, NTRK1 appears to be a direct upstream activator of MAPK whose abundance and ligand occupancy control the amplitude and duration of MAPK activity.
hypotheses.prediction: In cells expressing NTRK1, NGF should raise MAPK (ERK1/2) phosphorylation in a graded, dose-dependent and sustained way. This should not happen without NTRK1 induction and should persist when EGFR is inhibited. Reducing NTRK1 levels should shorten MAPK activation from sustained to transient. A downstream MAPK-dependent readout, RSK-mediated rpS6 phosphorylation at Ser235/236, should follow the same pattern.
hypotheses.test: Use a cultured cell line with doxycycline-inducible NTRK1. Compare induced, uninduced, and partially induced conditions (a doxycycline titration or NTRK1 siRNA). Treat with an NGF dose series, with and without a Trk kinase inhibitor and an EGFR inhibitor such as gefitinib. Measure phospho-ERK1/2, total ERK, and phospho-rpS6 Ser235/236 by western blot over a time course (minutes to 12 h). Sustained, NGF-dose-dependent MAPK activation that is lost with NTRK1 inhibition or knockdown, and shortened by lowering NTRK1 levels, supports the hypothesis. Its absence rules it out.

citations.title: Specificity of receptor tyrosine kinase signaling: transient versus sustained extracellular signal-regulated kinase activation.
Receptor Level Mechanisms Are Required for Epidermal Growth Factor (EGF)-stimulated Extracellular Signal-regulated Kinase (ERK) Activity Pulses.
Overexpression of Nogo-A changes nerve growth factor signaling dynamics in PC12 cells.
Frequency modulation of ERK activation dynamics rewires cell fate.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the plain-language mechanism (TrkA receptor number setting transient vs sustained ERK), the entities together (NTRK1/TrkA + MCF10A/PC12 + EKAR/ERK amplitude + gefitinib/EGFR-independence), and the prediction (NGF dose-dependent graded, sustained pERK; knockdown shortening it). The explanation is already in the published record: Marshall's Cell article states that RTK receptor number—including reduced TrkA in PC12 lines—determines whether ERK activation is transient or sustained and thus the cellular outcome, and Sparta et al. show that inducible TrkA in MCF10A converts NGF into a steady, gefitinib-insensitive, amplitude-modulated (NGF-dose-graded) ERK signal; an independent PC12 study confirms that reducing sustained TrkA phosphorylation reduces sustained Erk1/2 phosphorylation. Ryu et al. is cited as the nearest work on the remaining nuance (feedback/frequency-modulation architecture rather than receptor level alone), and no source was found that tested and negated the claim; the RSK-rpS6 Ser235/236 readout is the only element not tested in this TrkA setting.

hypotheses.statement: IL-17 directly activates JNK1, and this IL-17-driven JNK1 activity phosphorylates NFATc1-a/b to drive its nuclear export and repress NFAT-dependent IL-4 promoter activity.
hypotheses.mechanism: gaffen2014:findings:022 states that IL-17 signaling through ACT1 and TRAF6 ubiquitination activates MAPKs including JNK, and gaffen2014:findings:027 shows IL-17-induced A20 feedback specifically dampens JNK activation, implying JNK is a bona fide IL-17-proximal output; li2019:findings:021 independently reports IL-17A-induced signaling to JNK1/2 requiring a CARD14–Bcl10–MALT1 complex. chow2000:findings:006, :009 and :003 show that JNK1 phosphorylates NFATc1-a on Ser117/Ser172, excludes it from the nucleus, and thereby inhibits IL-4 promoter reporter activity. Combining these, an IL-17 stimulus should feed into the same JNK1–NFATc1 node and impose NFATc1 nuclear exclusion and IL-4 promoter repression.
hypotheses.prediction: IL-17A treatment of IL-17RA/ACT1-competent cells will increase JNK1 phosphorylation and NFATc1-a Ser117/Ser172 phosphorylation, reduce calcineurin-stimulated nuclear NFATc1-a, and lower IL-4 reporter output; each effect should be lost upon ACT1 knockdown, JNK inhibition, or use of the [Ala117 Ala172] NFATc1-a mutant, which chow2000:findings:009/:010 show is refractory to JNK1.
hypotheses.test: In a transfectable IL-17-responsive line expressing IL-17RA/ACT1 together with NFATc1-a and an IL-4 luciferase reporter, stimulate with IL-17A ± ionomycin/activated calcineurin and measure (i) phospho-JNK1 by immunoblot, (ii) NFATc1-a cytoplasmic/nuclear distribution by cell fractionation and immunofluorescence, and (iii) reporter activity; repeat with siACT1, a JNK inhibitor or dominant-negative JNK1, and the [Ala117 Ala172] NFATc1-a mutant, with in vitro kinase assays on immunoprecipitated JNK1 from IL-17-treated cells against recombinant NFATc1-a(1-202) to confirm the direct phosphorylation step.

citations.title: c-Jun NH(2)-terminal kinase inhibits targeting of the protein phosphatase calcineurin to NFATc1.
A comprehensive network map of IL-17A signaling pathway.

novelty.note: I searched the mechanism in plain words (IL-17 suppressing IL-4/Th2 via NFAT nuclear export), the key entities together (IL-17/IL-17RA/ACT1 + JNK1 + NFATc1 + Ser117/Ser172), and the prediction (IL-17A-driven NFATc1 nuclear exclusion and IL-4 promoter repression), across PubMed/PMC, publisher pages and IL-17 and NFAT reviews. The downstream half is firmly published: the retrieved Chow et al. paper establishes JNK1 phosphorylation of NFATc1 at Ser117/Ser172, loss of calcineurin targeting, blocked nuclear accumulation, and inhibition of IL-4 promoter reporter activity, with no mention of IL-17; the upstream half (IL-17RA/ACT1/TRAF6 to JNK) is likewise standard, but the retrieved comprehensive IL-17A signaling network map contains no NFAT/NFATc1 node and no IL-4 repression output. No source states that IL-17 feeds into the JNK1–NFATc1 node or tests IL-17-dependent NFATc1-a Ser117/Ser172 phosphorylation, so the two published mechanisms exist separately but the specific connection and prediction are unstated — and I found no direct negative test of it either.

hypotheses.statement: TRAF6 is required downstream of EGFR for EGF-induced NF-κB activation, acting via EGF-stimulated TRAF6 K63-linked polyubiquitination that activates TAK1.
hypotheses.mechanism: EGF-induced phosphorylation of IKK and IκB requires TAK1 and TLR4 (de2015:findings:001, de2015:findings:002). So EGFR signals to NF-κB through a TAK1-dependent step whose upstream activator is not identified in the evidence. Independently, receptor-associated TRAF6 activates TAK1 by forming K63-linked polyubiquitin, which leads to NF-κB and MAPK activation (derynck2019:findings:030, li2019:findings:005). TRAF6 RING mutants that cannot assemble these chains lose NF-κB reporter activity (deng2000:findings:009). Together, these suggest TRAF6 is the ubiquitin-dependent link between EGFR stimulation and TAK1 activation.
hypotheses.prediction: EGF stimulation should increase K63-linked polyubiquitination of TRAF6. Depleting TRAF6 should reduce EGF-induced TAK1 activation and IKK/IκB phosphorylation without reducing EGF-induced EGFR autophosphorylation. Only wild-type TRAF6, not a RING mutant such as C70A, should restore EGF-dependent NF-κB activation.
hypotheses.test: In HME or A549 cells, knock down TRAF6 by siRNA or shRNA, with scrambled controls. Stimulate with EGF and immunoblot for phospho-EGFR, phospho-TAK1, phospho-IKK, phospho-IκB and IκB degradation, alongside an NF-κB luciferase reporter. Reconstitute the cells with wild-type versus RING-mutant (C70A) TRAF6. Separately, immunoprecipitate TRAF6 after EGF stimulation, with or without erlotinib, and probe for K63-linked ubiquitin.

citations.title: MALT1 is required for EGFR-induced NF-κB activation and contributes to EGFR-driven lung cancer progression.
Erlotinib protects against LPS-induced endotoxicity because TLR4 needs EGFR to signal.
TRAF6 regulates EGF-induced cell transformation and cSCC malignant phenotype through CD147/EGFR.

novelty.note: I searched for TRAF6 as the downstream link from EGFR to NF-κB, for EGF-stimulated TRAF6 K63-polyubiquitination/TAK1 activation, and for the specific knockdown/RING-mutant predictions, across PubMed/Europe PMC, PMC full texts and publisher pages. The requirement of TRAF6 (and of its E3 ligase activity) for EGFR/EGF-induced NF-κB activation is already published in the MALT1 lung-cancer study, where MALT1 scaffolds TRAF6 onto the IKK complex after EGF stimulation — but that work attributes the effect to IKK/NEMO ubiquitination and neither tests TAK1 nor EGF-stimulated K63 autoubiquitination of TRAF6; the PNAS TLR4–EGFR paper establishes the TAK1/MyD88/TLR4 requirement for EGF-dependent IKK/IκB phosphorylation without identifying TRAF6. One prediction detail is already contradicted in another system: TRAF6 knockdown reduced EGF-induced EGFR phosphorylation in keratinocytes via CD147/EGFR, so the mechanism as a whole is neither fully anticipated nor directly refuted.

hypotheses.statement: SMAD1 is a direct, low-efficiency substrate-binding partner of TGFBR1 (TβRI), physically associating with the activated TβRI complex through its L3 loop and being C-terminally phosphorylated by TβRI when the L3 loop specificity determinants are altered.
hypotheses.mechanism: Claims about SMAD1 establish that its L3 loop residues His425/Asp428 dictate receptor choice, and that swapping in the Smad2 L3 loop (Smad1(L2)) makes Smad1 bind the TGF-β receptor complex as effectively as Smad2, while wild-type Smad1 associates 5–15-fold less well than Smad2 — i.e. wild-type Smad1 retains measurable but weak association with the TGF-β receptor complex. Independently, claims about TGFBR1 state that TβRI phosphorylation and Lys389 sumoylation facilitate recruitment and activation of effector Smads, and that Smad recruitment to TβRI is competitive and can be blocked by proteins occupying the receptor (p52ShcA, IRF-3). Together these imply a direct TβRI–SMAD1 interaction that is intrinsically weak because of L3 loop mismatch rather than absent, and that is rate-limited by the same recruitment step TβRI uses for Smad2/Smad3.
hypotheses.prediction: Wild-type SMAD1 should co-immunoprecipitate with ligand-activated TβRI at a low but reproducible stoichiometry that is competed away by co-expressed Smad3 or p52ShcA, and should show weak TGF-β-inducible C-terminal SXS phosphorylation; a kinase-dead TβRI or the H425R/D428T L3 substitution should, respectively, abolish the phosphorylation or markedly increase the association.
hypotheses.test: In a TβRI/TβRII-reconstituted epithelial line (e.g. R1B/L17 or HEK293T co-transfection), express Flag-SMAD1 wild type alongside the L3-swap variants and a kinase-dead TβRI, stimulate with TGF-β, and assay (i) co-immunoprecipitation of Flag-SMAD1 with HA-TβRI after receptor affinity labeling, with and without co-expressed Smad3 or p52ShcA as competitors, and (ii) anti-phospho-Smad1/5/8 Western blot of the immunoprecipitates; a direct relationship predicts kinase-independent binding but kinase-dependent SXS phosphorylation that is lost with TβRI kinase inactivation and gained with the Smad2 L3 loop.

citations.title: The L3 loop: a structural motif determining specific interactions between SMAD proteins and TGF-beta receptors.
TGFbeta-stimulated Smad1/5 phosphorylation requires the ALK5 L45 loop and mediates the pro-migratory TGFbeta switch.
TGF-β uses a novel mode of receptor activation to phosphorylate SMAD1/5 and induce epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition.

novelty.note: I searched for the L3 loop receptor-specificity motif, for direct ALK5/TβRI-mediated Smad1 C-terminal phosphorylation, and for the receptor requirements of TGF-β-induced SMAD1/5 activation. Lo et al. (EMBO J 1998, retrieved abstract) already state the explanation itself: Smad1 associates with the TGF-β receptor complex far less effectively than Smad2, and exchanging the two divergent L3 loop residues confers gain/loss of TGF-β receptor association and switches receptor-mediated C-terminal phosphorylation; Daly et al. independently report that TGFβ-stimulated Smad1/5 C-terminal phosphorylation requires ALK5 kinase activity and its L45 loop, with ALK5 immunoprecipitates phosphorylating GST-Smad1 in vitro, so the kinase-dependence prediction is also published. I cite Ramachandran et al. as nearest/qualifying work because it shows TGF-β-induced SMAD1/5 phosphorylation additionally requires ACVR1 acting downstream of TGFBR1, which complicates (but does not test) the low-stoichiometry co-IP and Smad3/p52ShcA competition part of the prediction; Daly et al. also found Smad2/3 depletion did not alter Smad1/5 phosphorylation.

hypotheses.statement: ERK2 directly activates MTORC1 by phosphorylating its Raptor subunit, and this forms a reciprocal loop with the ERK activation that follows mTORC1 inhibition.
hypotheses.mechanism: Activated ERK2 binds Raptor and directly phosphorylates purified Raptor in vitro. ERK1 and ERK2 are jointly required for PMA-stimulated Raptor phosphorylation at pS/T-P sites. Blocking those sites (Raptor S3A) or inhibiting MEK1/2 reduces mTORC1 kinase activity toward 4E-BP1 without disrupting complex assembly, so the Raptor phosphorylation acts on catalytic output. Separately, rapamycin-mediated mTORC1 inhibition activates ERK through Ras-Raf1-MEK1/2, which implies that rapamycin-induced ERK should, in turn, raise ERK-site phosphorylation of Raptor.
hypotheses.prediction: ERK2 knockdown, or re-expression of the Raptor S3A mutant, should lower stimulus-induced 4E-BP1 Thr37/46 phosphorylation and in vitro mTORC1 kinase activity. Rapamycin treatment should increase pS/T-P phosphorylation of Raptor in a way that U0126 and dominant-negative Ras N17 abolish.
hypotheses.test: Use cultured cells (HEK293 or MCF7) expressing myc-Raptor (wild-type or S3A) with siRNA against ERK2, with or without rapamycin and with or without U0126. Immunoprecipitate Raptor and immunoblot with the pS/T-P phospho-motif antibody. In parallel, run in vitro mTORC1 kinase assays with GST-4E-BP1 and [γ-32P]ATP, and immunoblot for phospho-4E-BP1 Thr37/46 and p-ERK.

citations.title: ERK1/2 phosphorylate Raptor to promote Ras-dependent activation of mTOR complex 1 (mTORC1).
Regulation of mTOR complex 1 (mTORC1) by raptor Ser863 and multisite phosphorylation.
The identification of raptor as a substrate for p44/42 MAPK.

novelty.note: I searched for ERK-mediated Raptor phosphorylation, the specific Raptor ERK sites, and separately for a rapamycin-induced ERK feedback loop acting back on Raptor. The first arm of the hypothesis is fully published: Carriere et al. show ERK1/2 bind Raptor, directly phosphorylate Ser8/Ser696/Ser863 in vitro and in vivo, and that phosphorylation-deficient Raptor alleles impair mTORC1 signaling to 4E-BP1, with Foster et al. independently showing site-defective Raptor lowers in vitro mTORC1 kinase activity and that MAPK signaling promotes Ser863. The second arm — that rapamycin-induced ERK activation raises ERK-site Raptor phosphorylation in a U0126- and Ras N17-sensitive manner — is not stated by any source I retrieved, and the nearest direct test points the other way (Langlais et al. report Raptor Ser696 phosphorylation is insensitive to rapamycin, and Foster et al. report insulin-driven Ser863 phosphorylation is rapamycin-sensitive, i.e. reduced rather than increased), so the reciprocal-loop connection remains unestablished rather than confirmed.

hypotheses.statement: LPS signaling through TLR4 directly downregulates cell-surface TGFBR1 (TβRI) by driving ERK/p38-dependent TACE/ADAM17 ectodomain shedding of the receptor, thereby dampening TGF-β/Smad3 responsiveness.
hypotheses.mechanism: LPS is shown to activate ERK (and p38-linked inflammatory programs) via TLR4/EGFR, with EGFR knockdown or erlotinib abolishing LPS-induced ERK phosphorylation and NFκB signaling. Independently, TβRI — but not TβRII — is cleaved by TACE/ADAM17 specifically in response to ERK or p38 MAPK signaling, lowering surface TβRI and downregulating Smad3 activation without reducing ligand binding to TβRII. Because LPS supplies exactly the ERK/p38 input that the shedding machinery reads, LPS should act as a direct upstream regulator of TGFBR1 protein levels rather than only of inflammatory transcription.
hypotheses.prediction: LPS treatment of TLR4-competent cells should cause a time-dependent loss of full-length cell-surface TβRI with accumulation of a soluble TβRI ectodomain and a cytoplasmic-domain fragment, no change in surface TβRII, and blunted TGF-β-induced Smad3 phosphorylation; this loss should be prevented by ERK/p38 or ADAM17 inhibition and by erlotinib, which blocks LPS-induced ERK activation.
hypotheses.test: In a TLR4-expressing cultured line (e.g. A549 or a macrophage line), treat with LPS over 0–6 h and quantify surface TβRI and TβRII by surface biotinylation/flow cytometry with immunoblot of conditioned medium for the shed TβRI ectodomain; then assay TGF-β-induced phospho-Smad3 after LPS pretreatment, and repeat with MEK/p38 inhibitors, an ADAM17 inhibitor or ADAM17 siRNA, and erlotinib to establish that the LPS effect on TGFBR1 requires the ERK/ADAM17 axis. A non-cleavable TβRI mutant should be refractory to LPS.

citations.title: TACE-mediated ectodomain shedding of the type I TGF-beta receptor downregulates TGF-beta signaling.
Lipopolysaccharide acting via toll-like receptor 4 transactivates the TGF-β receptor in vascular smooth muscle cells.

novelty.note: I searched (a) the mechanism in words (LPS/TLR4 → ERK/p38 → ADAM17 shedding of TβRI), (b) the entities together (LPS + TGFBR1 + ADAM17/TACE + surface receptor loss), and (c) the prediction (blunted TGF-β-induced Smad3 after LPS, soluble TβRI ectodomain). The ERK/p38→TACE/ADAM17→TβRI-shedding arm is fully published (Liu et al., Mol Cell 2009), but that work induced shedding with PMA, serum and EGF and never tested LPS, TLR4 or an EGFR inhibitor; LPS is separately known to activate ADAM17 and to antagonise TGF-β/Smad3 by other routes (Smad3 linker phosphorylation), so the specific LPS→TβRI-shedding link is not stated anywhere I could retrieve. The nearest direct test of LPS acting on TGFBR1 (Rodríguez-Vita-type VSMC study, PMID 35122536) found LPS/TLR4 transactivates TGFBR1 with increased Smad2 C-terminal phosphorylation via p38 and MMP2 — directionally opposite to the prediction, but it did not measure surface TβRI, shed ectodomain or TGF-β-stimulated pSmad3, so it contradicts rather than formally refutes the claim; hence partial, not refuted or established.

hypotheses.statement: mTOR, as the kinase subunit of mTORC2, directly promotes phosphorylation of FOXO1 at the AKT consensus sites (Thr24/Ser256), so mTOR kinase activity is required for 14-3-3-mediated nuclear exclusion of FOXO1.
hypotheses.mechanism: Claims about C establish that mTOR kinase activity is required for phosphorylation of the Akt hydrophobic and turn motifs, and that mTOR within mTORC2 is the catalytic subunit responsible (facchinetti2008:findings:026, facchinetti2008:findings:017). Claims about A establish that FOXO1 is phosphorylated on T24/S256 to create 14-3-3 binding motifs that export it from the nucleus (manning2017:findings:015), and that mTORC2 loss selectively impairs FoxO1/3a phosphorylation while sparing other substrates such as TSC2 and GSK3b (laplante2012:findings:008, liu2020:findings:008). Together these imply a direct kinase-to-substrate-state dependency in which mTOR catalytic function, not merely complex scaffolding, sets FOXO1 phosphorylation and localization.
hypotheses.prediction: Acute inhibition of mTOR catalytic activity, or replacement of mTOR with a kinase-dead allele, should reduce phospho-FOXO1 Thr24/Ser256, decrease FOXO1-14-3-3 association, and shift FOXO1 into the nucleus with induction of FOXO1 target genes, while GSK3 and TSC2 phosphorylation remain largely unchanged.
hypotheses.test: In HEK293 or HeLa cells, compare vehicle, rapamycin, and an ATP-competitive mTOR inhibitor (Torin1), and in parallel knock down endogenous mTOR with re-expression of wild-type versus kinase-dead mTOR; then immunoblot phospho-FOXO1 Thr24/Ser256 versus total FOXO1 (with phospho-GSK3 Ser9 and phospho-TSC2 as specificity controls), co-immunoprecipitate FOXO1 with 14-3-3, and score nuclear versus cytoplasmic FOXO1 by fractionation and immunofluorescence plus qPCR of FOXO1 target transcripts.

citations.title: SIN1/MIP1 maintains rictor-mTOR complex integrity and regulates Akt phosphorylation and substrate specificity.
Ablation in mice of the mTORC components raptor, rictor, or mLST8 reveals that mTORC2 is required for signaling to Akt-FOXO and PKCalpha, but not S6K1.
AKT/mTORC2 Inhibition Activates FOXO1 Function in CLL Cells Reducing B-Cell Receptor-Mediated Survival.
mTORC2 Is the Major Second Layer Kinase Negatively Regulating FOXO3 Activity

novelty.note: I searched for direct mTOR/mTORC2 phosphorylation of FOXO1 at T24/S256, for kinase-dead mTOR or ATP-competitive mTOR inhibitor effects on FOXO1 phosphorylation, 14-3-3 binding and nuclear localization, and for mTORC2-selective loss of FoxO versus TSC2/GSK3 phosphorylation. The published components are all present: mTORC2 (SIN1/rictor/mLST8) is required for FoxO1/3a phosphorylation while TSC2 and GSK3β are spared (Jacinto 2006; Guertin 2006), and ATP-competitive mTOR kinase inhibitors reduce FOXO1 T24 phosphorylation, drive nuclear relocalization and alter FOXO target genes (CLL study; FOXO3 study) — but in every case the phosphorylation of the AKT consensus sites is attributed to AKT acting downstream of mTORC2-mediated Ser473 phosphorylation, i.e. explicitly not mTOR acting directly on FOXO1. No source states mTOR is the direct kinase for FOXO1 T24/S256, and none reports a direct negative test of that specific kinase-substrate relationship, so this is partial rather than established or refuted.

hypotheses.statement: MEK (via ERK) and mTORC2 act as parallel, MEK-independent inputs that jointly sustain RSK hydrophobic-motif Ser380 phosphorylation, so that mTORC2 supplies the residual RSK-HM phosphorylation that remains after MEK inhibition.
hypotheses.mechanism: U0126 only reduced RSK Ser380 phosphorylation in wild-type cells but abolished it in SIN1-/- (mTORC2-deficient) cells, and PMA could not rescue it without SIN1 (chou2020:findings:003). mTORC2 components specifically mediate phosphorylation of AGC-kinase regulatory sites in Akt and conventional PKC (facchinetti2008:findings:005). Phosphorylation of the mTORC2 component Rictor is insensitive to MEK inhibition (dibble2009:findings:003). Together these imply that mTORC2's contribution to RSK-HM phosphorylation does not pass through MEK and compensates for it.
hypotheses.prediction: In HeLa cells, U0126 alone should partially lower RSK Ser380 phosphorylation. Depleting RICTOR or SIN1 alone should also partially lower it. Combining MEK inhibition with RICTOR/SIN1 depletion should eliminate it. MEK inhibition should not reduce mTORC2 kinase activity measured in RICTOR immunoprecipitates.
hypotheses.test: Treat serum- or insulin-stimulated HeLa cells transfected with control, RICTOR or SIN1 siRNA with U0126 or vehicle. Immunoblot for phospho-Ser380 RSK, phospho-ERK and Akt Ser473. In parallel, run an in vitro kinase assay on anti-RICTOR immunoprecipitates from U0126-treated and untreated cells, using inactive Akt1 as substrate, to confirm that mTORC2 activity is MEK-independent.

citations.title: mTORC2 Is Involved in the Induction of RSK Phosphorylation by Serum or Nutrient Starvation.

novelty.note: I searched for mTORC2/SIN1 control of RSK hydrophobic-motif Ser380, for RSK pS380 remaining after MEK inhibition with rictor/SIN1 loss, and for MEK-independence of mTORC2 activity. The only source stating this combination is the corpus paper itself (Cells 2020, PMID 32605013), which reports that U0126 only reduces pS380 in WT cells but abolishes it in SIN1-/- MEFs and concludes that ERK1/2 activation plus mTORC2 are both required for full RSK HM phosphorylation; it also reports that rictor loss abolishes pHM RSK despite intact ERK activity. However, that same paper finds mTOR catalytic inhibition does not abolish pS380 and favours a scaffold rather than a parallel kinase input, and the specific predictions here (partial loss with RICTOR/SIN1 siRNA plus U0126 in HeLa, and MEK-independence of mTORC2 kinase activity in RICTOR immunoprecipitates) were not directly tested, so the claim is only partly published.

hypotheses.statement: SRC acts as a direct upstream tyrosine kinase for ERBB3, phosphorylating tyrosines in the ERBB3 cytoplasmic tail and thereby driving ERBB3-dependent PI3K/AKT output.
hypotheses.mechanism: ERBB3 has no intrinsic catalytic activity, so every phosphotyrosine on its tail must be installed in trans by another kinase (yarden2001:findings:000), and its high-affinity docking sites such as Y1276/Y1289 only become functional once phosphorylated (jones2006:findings:009). SRC is a broadly active tyrosine kinase capable of modifying thousands of sites in a heterologous background (bradley2024:findings:002), and SRC-family activity is required for full receptor-level tyrosine phosphorylation and downstream AKT signalling after growth-factor stimulation (de2015:findings:008). Together these imply SRC can supply the trans-phosphorylation that ERBB3 itself cannot perform.
hypotheses.prediction: Purified active SRC will phosphorylate a recombinant ERBB3 cytoplasmic domain in vitro on tail tyrosines including the Y1276/Y1289 docking sites, and in cells SRC inhibition or knockdown will reduce ERBB3 phosphotyrosine and ERBB3-associated AKT phosphorylation without requiring loss of ERBB2/EGFR expression.
hypotheses.test: Run an in vitro kinase assay with recombinant active SRC and bacterially expressed ERBB3 cytoplasmic domain (plus kinase-dead SRC and no-kinase controls), reading out anti-pTyr immunoblot and mapping sites by MS; in parallel, treat ERBB3-expressing cells with a SRC-family inhibitor or siRNA against SRC and immunoprecipitate ERBB3 to quantify its phosphotyrosine and bound p85/phospho-AKT.

citations.title: c-Src modulates ErbB2 and ErbB3 heterocomplex formation and function
Ligand-Independent EGFR Activation by Anchorage-Stimulated Src Promotes Cancer Cell Proliferation and Cetuximab Resistance via ErbB3 Phosphorylation
HER3 signaling and targeted therapy in cancer.

novelty.note: I searched three ways — the mechanism in words (Src trans-phosphorylating kinase-dead ErbB3), the entities together (SRC + ERBB3/HER3 + Y1276/Y1289 + p85/AKT), and the prediction (Src inhibitor/siRNA lowering pHER3 and HER3-associated AKT, and in vitro Src kinase assays on the HER3 tail) — across PubMed, PMC, publisher pages and Crossref. Published work establishes that ErbB3 tyrosine phosphorylation and downstream PI3K/AKT are Src-dependent: c-Src overexpression increases ErbB2/ErbB3 heterocomplex formation and receptor phosphorylation while kinase-dead Src or PP2 reduces it, and anchorage-stimulated Src raises pErbB3-Y1289 and AKT signalling. However, in every source retrieved Src acts indirectly, by transactivating EGFR/ERBB2 which then phosphorylates the ERBB3 tail (pErbB3 was abolished by the EGFR TKI AG1478), and I found no in vitro or cellular demonstration that Src itself phosphorylates the ERBB3 cytoplasmic domain independently of ERBB2/EGFR — nor any study that tested and negated it — so the general mechanism is published but this specific direct-kinase claim and its ERBB2/EGFR-independence are not.

hypotheses.statement: RPS6KA1 (RSK1) directly phosphorylates RICTOR within mTORC2, analogous to the S6K1-mediated phosphorylation of Rictor-T1135.
hypotheses.mechanism: Rictor is phosphorylated on an AGC-kinase RXRXXS/T motif at T1135 by S6K1, a growth-factor- and PI3K-dependent site detected with a phospho-Akt substrate antibody (dibble2009:findings:005, dibble2009:findings:012). RSK1 recognizes essentially the same minimal consensus (Arg/Lys-Xaa-Arg-Xaa-Xaa-pSer/Thr or Arg-Arg-Xaa-pSer/Thr) and is known to phosphorylate other AGC/S6K-shared substrates on RXRXXS/T sites, including tuberin and rpS6 Ser235/236 (cargnello2011:findings:027, cargnello2011:findings:034, roux2004:findings:006). Because RSK1 physically associates with the mTORC2 subunit SIN1 and colocalizes with it at the plasma membrane (chou2020:findings:013, chou2020:findings:014), RSK1 is positioned within the same complex as Rictor, making Rictor a plausible direct RSK1 substrate.
hypotheses.prediction: Purified/immunoprecipitated active RSK1 should phosphorylate recombinant Rictor in vitro on an RXRXXS/T motif detectable with the phospho-Akt substrate antibody and with the phospho-T1135 antibody; in cells, ERK/RSK activation (e.g. PMA or serum) should raise Rictor phospho-motif signal in a manner reduced by RSK inhibition (BI-D1870/SL-0101) or RSK1 knockdown, and this component should persist when mTORC1/S6K1 is blocked by rapamycin. Rictor-T1135A should lose part or all of the RSK1-dependent signal, and loss of RSK1-mediated Rictor phosphorylation should elevate insulin-stimulated Akt-S473 as seen for T1135A.
hypotheses.test: Perform an in vitro kinase assay with HA-RSK1 immunoprecipitated from PMA-stimulated HEK-293 cells (versus kinase-dead RSK1, and versus RSK1 pretreated with BI-D1870) on immunoprecipitated myc-Rictor wild type or T1135A, blotting with the phospho-Akt substrate and phospho-Rictor(T1135) antibodies; in parallel, in HEK-293E cells treat with PMA or serum in the presence of rapamycin and/or BI-D1870 and after siRNA knockdown of RSK1 versus S6K1, and immunoblot phospho-Rictor(T1135) and phospho-Akt(S473). Appearance of RSK1-dependent, rapamycin-insensitive Rictor phosphorylation confirms the direct relationship; absence of signal with active RSK1 in vitro and no change upon RSK1 knockdown rules it out.

citations.title: mTORC1-activated S6K1 phosphorylates Rictor on threonine 1135 and regulates mTORC2 signaling.
Oncogenic MAPK signaling stimulates mTORC1 activity by promoting RSK-mediated raptor phosphorylation.
mTORC2 Is Involved in the Induction of RSK Phosphorylation by Serum or Nutrient Starvation.
Characterization of Rictor phosphorylation sites reveals direct regulation of mTOR complex 2 by S6K1.

novelty.note: I searched for RSK1-mediated Rictor phosphorylation, for Rictor-T1135 with RSK/PMA/BI-D1870/MEK-inhibitor terms, and for RSK substrate screens (PubMed, Europe PMC, PMC full texts). No source states that RSK1 phosphorylates Rictor; the closest published work is Julien et al., who found that PMA/ERK-driven Rictor phosphorylation on RXRXXpS/T sites is completely abrogated by rapamycin and by S6K1 knockdown, attributing it to a basophilic kinase downstream of mTORC1 rather than to an ERK-activated kinase — evidence against the rapamycin-insensitive component of the prediction, but RSK itself was never depleted, inhibited, or assayed on Rictor, so this is not a stated negative for the specific claim. The general mechanism is published in adjacent form: RSK1/2 directly phosphorylate the mTOR-complex scaffold subunit Raptor at a conserved basophilic site, and RSK associates with the mTORC2 subunit SIN1 at the membrane.

hypotheses.statement: RICTOR is required for full activation of RPS6KA1 (RSK1) by acting upstream of its hydrophobic-motif phosphorylation, i.e. mTORC2/Rictor positively regulates RSK1 activity.
hypotheses.mechanism: Deletion of Rictor abolishes basal and stimulation-induced RSK hydrophobic-motif (Ser380) phosphorylation and selectively reduces phosphorylation of the RSK substrate BAD, even though ERK1/2 activation is intact (chou2020:findings:002, chou2020:findings:015). RSK activation requires ordered phosphorylation of Ser221, Ser363, Ser380 and Thr573, with Ser380 in the hydrophobic motif being the critical activating step, and RSK1/2 phosphorylate BAD-Ser112 to promote 14-3-3 binding (cargnello2011:findings:023, cargnello2011:findings:036). Together these imply that Rictor supplies an ERK-independent input required for RSK1 hydrophobic-motif phosphorylation and downstream substrate targeting.
hypotheses.prediction: Acute loss of Rictor (siRNA/CRISPR) in a cultured cell line should reduce serum- or PMA-stimulated RSK1 Ser380 phosphorylation and RSK1 catalytic activity toward BAD-Ser112 without reducing phospho-ERK1/2, and re-expression of Rictor should restore RSK1 Ser380 phosphorylation and BAD-Ser112 phosphorylation; a phosphomimetic or membrane-targeted constitutively active RSK1 should rescue BAD-Ser112 phosphorylation in Rictor-null cells, placing Rictor upstream of RSK1.
hypotheses.test: In Rictor-/- versus Rictor+/+ MEFs (and Rictor-knockdown HEK-293E cells), stimulate with serum or PMA and immunoblot phospho-RSK Ser380, phospho-ERK1/2, and phospho-BAD Ser112; immunoprecipitate RSK1 from each genotype and measure in vitro kinase activity against a BAD-Ser112 peptide or recombinant BAD, with BI-D1870 as a specificity control. Then re-express wild-type Rictor in the Rictor-/- cells to test rescue of RSK1 Ser380 phosphorylation and RSK1 activity; a Rictor-dependent loss and rescue of RSK1 Ser380/activity with unchanged ERK confirms the relationship, whereas equal RSK1 Ser380 and activity across genotypes rules it out.

citations.title: mTORC2 Is Involved in the Induction of RSK Phosphorylation by Serum or Nutrient Starvation.

novelty.note: I searched for Rictor/mTORC2 control of RSK hydrophobic-motif (Ser380) phosphorylation, for mTORC2 as an HM kinase for AGC kinases generally, and for Rictor loss affecting RSK activity toward BAD-Ser112 with intact ERK. All searches converged on Chou et al., Cells 2020 (PMID 32605013), the published paper underlying the corpus claims, which explicitly reports that RSK Ser380 phosphorylation is abolished in rictor−/− thymocytes and blunted in SIN1−/− cells despite robust ERK activation, that BAD (and CCTβ) phosphorylation is selectively diminished, and that mTORC2 therefore provides an ERK-independent input required for RSK HM phosphorylation (proposed to act as a scaffold, since mTOR catalytic activity was dispensable). No source was found that directly tested and negated this relationship, so the explanation is already published rather than open or refuted.

hypotheses.statement: SRC directly phosphorylates RSK (RSK2) on tyrosine residues, and this phosphorylation stabilizes the ERK1/2–RSK complex and promotes ERK-dependent RSK activation.
hypotheses.mechanism: RSK2 is tyrosine-phosphorylated in response to Src activation, and this stabilizes ERK1/2 binding to RSK2 and promotes RSK2 activation (cargnello2011:findings:059). RSK activation depends on ERK1/2 docking and ERK-mediated phosphorylation, including the hydrophobic-motif site Ser380 (cargnello2011:findings:018, cargnello2011:findings:023, chou2020:context:000). Separately, SRC-family inhibition with PP2 eliminates growth-factor-induced ERK phosphorylation (de2015:findings:008). Together these place SRC upstream of RSK at two points: RSK tyrosine phosphorylation and ERK input. It is untested in this evidence whether the tyrosine phosphorylation is carried out by SRC itself.
hypotheses.prediction: Purified active SRC should phosphorylate recombinant RSK2 on tyrosine in vitro, and kinase-dead SRC should not. In cells, SRC inhibition or knockdown should reduce RSK2 phosphotyrosine, reduce ERK1/2 co-immunoprecipitating with RSK2, and lower RSK Ser380 phosphorylation. Tyr-to-Phe RSK2 mutants at the SRC-phosphorylated sites should show weaker ERK binding and activation even when ERK phosphorylation is intact.
hypotheses.test: Run an in vitro kinase assay with purified wild-type or kinase-dead SRC and recombinant RSK2, read out by anti-phosphotyrosine immunoblot, and map the sites by mass spectrometry. Then, in HeLa or HEK293 cells, compare wild-type RSK2 with Tyr-to-Phe site mutants for ERK1/2 co-immunoprecipitation and phospho-Ser380 immunoblotting. Include SRC siRNA or a selective SRC inhibitor, with a constitutively active MEK as a control to separate direct effects on RSK2 from effects on ERK activation.

citations.title: Epidermal growth factor stimulates RSK2 activation through activation of the MEK/ERK pathway and src-dependent tyrosine phosphorylation of RSK2 at Tyr-529.
Fibroblast growth factor receptor 3 associates with and tyrosine phosphorylates p90 RSK2, leading to RSK2 activation that mediates hematopoietic transformation.

novelty.note: I searched for Src-dependent RSK2 tyrosine phosphorylation and ERK-complex stabilization, for the FGFR3/RSK2 two-step activation model, and for the specific predictions (in vitro Src kinase assay, Y529F mutant ERK binding, PP2 effects). Kang et al. (J Biol Chem 2008) states exactly this explanation: Src and Fyn directly phosphorylate RSK2 at Tyr-529 in vitro, PP2 attenuates EGF-induced Tyr-529 phosphorylation and RSK2 activation, and in vitro Src-mediated Tyr-529 phosphorylation enhances inactive ERK binding to wild-type but not Y529F RSK2, which is required for ERK-dependent RSK2 activation; the companion MCB 2009 paper extends the same two-step model to FGFR3 (Y529/Y707). No source was found that tested and negated Src phosphorylation of RSK2, so this is established rather than partial or refuted.

hypotheses.statement: MEK activity negatively regulates TSC2 by being required for its inhibitory phosphorylation at Ser664 and Ser1798, which reduces TSC2 GAP activity toward Rheb.
hypotheses.mechanism: MEK phosphorylates ERK at Thr202/Thr203 (johnson2023:findings:009), and MEK inhibition abolishes ERK phosphorylation within minutes (albeck2013:findings:016). MEK inhibition also reduces hydrophobic-motif phosphorylation of RSK (chou2020:findings:003). ERK and RSK phosphorylate TSC2 at Ser664 and Ser1798, and this phosphorylation lowers TSC2 GAP activity toward Rheb (cargnello2011:findings:035). MEK-dependent sites are enriched for the ERK motif, while AKT-motif sites are EGF-dependent but MEK-independent (bekkerjensen2020:findings:010). Together these imply that MEK activity sets the level of TSC2 Ser664/Ser1798 phosphorylation, but not the level at the AKT site Thr1462 (dibble2009:findings:019; haeusler2018:findings:027).
hypotheses.prediction: In growth-factor-stimulated cells, MEK inhibition should sharply reduce TSC2 phosphorylation at Ser664 and Ser1798. It should leave TSC2 Thr1462 phosphorylation largely unchanged. TSC2 immunoprecipitated from MEK-inhibited cells should show higher Rheb-GAP activity than TSC2 from vehicle-treated cells.
hypotheses.test: Stimulate serum-starved HeLa cells with EGF after pretreatment with a MEK inhibitor (PD0325901 or U0126) or vehicle, across a dose titration. Immunoblot for phospho-TSC2 Ser664, Ser1798 and Thr1462, and for phospho-ERK as a control that MEK was inhibited. In parallel, immunoprecipitate TSC2 from each condition and run an in vitro Rheb GTP-hydrolysis (GAP) assay. As a further control, express TSC2 S664A/S1798A mutants and check that they abolish the MEK-inhibitor-dependent change in GAP activity.

citations.title: Phosphorylation and functional inactivation of TSC2 by Erk implications for tuberous sclerosis and cancer pathogenesis.
Tumor-promoting phorbol esters and activated Ras inactivate the tuberous sclerosis tumor suppressor complex via p90 ribosomal S6 kinase.
TSC2/Rheb signaling mediates ERK-dependent regulation of mTORC1 activity in C2C12 myoblasts.
Identification of S664 TSC2 phosphorylation as a marker for extracellular signal-regulated kinase mediated mTOR activation in tuberous sclerosis and human cancer.

novelty.note: I searched for ERK phosphorylation of TSC2 Ser664 and GAP activity toward Rheb, for RSK phosphorylation of Ser1798 in tuberin, and for direct tests of MEK-inhibitor effects on TSC2 phospho-sites including Thr1462. Ma et al. (Cell 2005) established ERK-dependent inactivating phosphorylation of TSC2 with S664 as the dominant in vivo site and MEK1-driven TSC2 phosphorylation blocked by U0126; Roux et al. (PNAS 2004) established that MAPK-activated RSK1 phosphorylates tuberin Ser-1798 and thereby inhibits TSC1-TSC2 function; and Miyazaki et al. (2017) directly report that U0126 blocks TSC2 Ser664 phosphorylation with no inhibitory effect at Ser939 or Thr1462, concluding that MEK/ERK-dependent Ser664 phosphorylation controls TSC2 GAP activity. This covers the stated explanation and the first two predictions, so the status is established; only the in vitro Rheb-GAP assay on TSC2 immunoprecipitated from MEK-inhibited cells appears inferred rather than measured, and Miyazaki et al. additionally argue the RSK/Ser1798 arm is dispensable in muscle cells.

hypotheses.statement: EGFR kinase activity is required for EGF-induced, ERK1/2-dependent phosphorylation of RAPTOR at Ser696 and Ser863, so EGFR positively regulates RAPTOR phosphorylation and RAPTOR-associated mTORC1 activity.
hypotheses.mechanism: EGF robustly induces RAPTOR phosphorylation on proline-directed sites, and ERK1/2 knockdown strongly reduces EGF-induced phosphorylation of endogenous RAPTOR at Ser696 and Ser863. These phosphorylations raise the mTOR kinase activity associated with RAPTOR. Independently, EGF triggers EGFR tyrosine phosphorylation, ERK pathway output decays when EGFR is inhibited, and EGFR knockdown or erlotinib blocks ERK activation. Together these claims imply that EGFR sits upstream of ERK-mediated RAPTOR phosphorylation, although the claims do not support EGFR phosphorylating RAPTOR itself.
hypotheses.prediction: In EGF-stimulated, serum-starved HEK293 cells, erlotinib pretreatment or EGFR siRNA should abolish EGF-induced RAPTOR Ser696/Ser863 phosphorylation and reduce 4E-BP1 Thr37/46 phosphorylation. PMA-induced RAPTOR phosphorylation, which bypasses the receptor, should remain intact. The RAPTOR S3A mutant should be insensitive to EGFR inhibition for these readouts.
hypotheses.test: Pretreat serum-starved HEK293 cells with erlotinib, EGFR siRNA or a control, then stimulate with EGF or PMA. Immunoblot for phospho-EGFR, phospho-ERK1/2, endogenous RAPTOR pSer696/pSer863 and 4E-BP1 pThr37/46. In parallel, compare wild-type and S3A RAPTOR in mTORC1 immunoprecipitate kinase assays using GST-4E-BP1 as substrate.

citations.title: ERK1/2 phosphorylate Raptor to promote Ras-dependent activation of mTOR complex 1 (mTORC1).
Regulation of mTOR complex 1 (mTORC1) by raptor Ser863 and multisite phosphorylation.
The Identification of Raptor as a Substrate for p44/42 MAPK
Lysosomal EGFR acts as a Rheb-GEF independent of its kinase activity to activate mTORC1.

novelty.note: I searched for the ERK–raptor Ser696/Ser863 axis, for EGFR-inhibitor (erlotinib/gefitinib/siRNA) tests on raptor phosphorylation and 4E-BP1 Thr37/46, and for negative reports on EGF/EGFR-dependent mTORC1 activation. The upstream mechanism is published: Carriere et al. show ERK1/2 directly phosphorylate raptor Ser8/696/863 and that EGF induces these sites, Foster et al. show EGF/MAPK signalling drives raptor Ser863 in a MEK-dependent manner with phospho-defective raptor lowering mTORC1 activity toward 4E-BP1, and Langlais et al. independently place Ser696 downstream of p44/42 MAPK — but none of these tests EGFR kinase activity itself (no erlotinib or EGFR knockdown) as the requirement for raptor Ser696/Ser863 phosphorylation, nor the PMA-bypass/S3A contrasts. Notably, a recent Cell Research paper directly tested the downstream half of the prediction and found erlotinib has minimal effect on mTORC1 output (p-Thr37/46-4E-BP1), reporting EGFR activates mTORC1 as a Rheb-GEF independent of its kinase activity, so the specific EGFR-kinase-requirement step is unsupported and partly contradicted rather than established.

hypotheses.statement: KRAS acts directly upstream of MEK1, such that oncogenic KRAS drives MEK1 activation and KRAS-mutant cells depend on MEK1 catalytic activity for downstream ERK1/2 phosphorylation.
hypotheses.mechanism: The KRAS evidence shows that KRAS G12C inhibitors block the RAS-RAF interaction and downstream signalling, and that MEK inhibition (selumetinib) suppresses the signalling consequences of NRAS/KRAS lesions in resistant NSCLC populations, placing KRAS output on a RAF-dependent arm. The MEK1 evidence independently establishes MEK1 as the immediate ERK1/2 activation-loop (TEY/Thr202) kinase acting downstream of Ras-mediated Raf activation, and that dominant-negative Ras blocks ERK phosphorylation while MEK1/2 inhibitors abolish it. Together these imply a direct KRAS-to-MEK1 activation link in which KRAS-generated Raf activity is the input that switches MEK1 on.
hypotheses.prediction: In KRAS-mutant cells, MEK1 activation-loop phosphorylation and MEK1 in vitro kinase activity toward ERK1/2 should be high and should fall upon KRAS silencing or KRAS G12C inhibitor treatment; conversely, selective MEK1 loss or MEK1 kinase-dead knock-in should collapse ERK1/2 TEY phosphorylation in KRAS-mutant cells without altering KRAS GTP loading.
hypotheses.test: In a KRAS G12C-mutant line, treat with a G12C inhibitor or doxycycline-inducible KRAS shRNA and immunoblot immunoprecipitated MEK1 for activation-loop phosphorylation, then assay its kinase activity on recombinant ERK1/2 in vitro; in parallel, deplete MEK1 alone (and MEK2 alone as control) by siRNA and measure phospho-ERK1/2 (Thr202) and colony formation, with a RAS-GTP pulldown to confirm KRAS activation state is unchanged by MEK1 loss.

citations.title: ERK-dependent protein phosphorylation in KRAS-mutant cancer: a mix of the expected and surprising.
Selective Inhibition of Oncogenic KRAS Output with Small Molecules Targeting the Inactive State.
Disruption of CRAF-mediated MEK activation is required for effective MEK inhibition in KRAS mutant tumors.
Functional redundancy of the kinases MEK1 and MEK2: Rescue of the Mek1 mutant phenotype by Mek2 knock-in reveals a protein threshold effect.

novelty.note: I searched three ways — the mechanism in plain words (KRAS-mutant dependence on MEK1 catalytic activity for ERK1/2 phosphorylation), the entities together (RAS-RAF-MEK1 activation-loop-ERK TEY cascade in oncogenic KRAS), and the prediction (KRAS G12C inhibitor or KRAS knockdown lowering pMEK/pERK; MEK1 vs MEK2 depletion). The canonical KRAS-upstream-of-MEK1 relationship is explicitly published: reviews of ERK-dependent signalling in KRAS-mutant cancer state that the RAF-MEK-ERK cascade is the dominant transducer of KRAS output and that an activated MEK1 allele restores pERK and confers resistance to mutant-KRAS inhibition, the ARS-853 study reports that KRAS G12C engagement of the GDP state abolishes RAF interaction and downstream MEK/ERK phosphorylation, and CRAF-to-MEK activation was directly characterised in KRAS-mutant tumours. One caveat on the proposed test rather than the explanation: MEK1 and MEK2 are documented as functionally redundant ERK activators with a total-protein threshold effect, so MEK1-selective loss would not be expected to collapse ERK TEY phosphorylation.

hypotheses.statement: RAF1 (c-Raf/CRAF) directly phosphorylates and activates MEK1.
hypotheses.mechanism: Evidence about C shows that RAF1 activity sets MEK phosphorylation. Pharmacological inhibition of c-Raf with GW-5074 eliminated MEK and ERK activity in HEK293 cells (borisov2009:findings:013). CRAF catalytic domain immunoprecipitated from cells showed kinase activity read out as pMEK, and that activity rose with activating phosphorylation (poulikakos2010:findings:007). Evidence about A places MEK1/2 directly downstream of Raf1 in the Ras-Raf1-MEK1/2 route to ERK (carracedo2008:findings:004), and shows that MEK1 is a regulated kinase whose activity towards ERK depends on its own phosphorylation state (lake2016:findings:010). Together these imply that RAF1 is a direct upstream kinase of MEK1, rather than acting on it only through intermediates.
hypotheses.prediction: Purified active RAF1 should phosphorylate recombinant MEK1 in a cell-free reaction. This should increase MEK1's ability to phosphorylate ERK2. Both effects should be lost with kinase-dead RAF1, a RAF inhibitor such as GW-5074, or omission of RAF1.
hypotheses.test: Run an in vitro coupled kinase assay using purified recombinant components: active RAF1 (full-length or catalytic domain) versus kinase-dead RAF1, with recombinant MEK1 (wild-type and kinase-dead), ATP, and recombinant ERK2 as a downstream substrate. Include ± GW-5074 as an inhibitor control. Read out MEK1 phosphorylation by phospho-MEK immunoblot or [γ-32P]ATP incorporation, and MEK1 activation by ERK2 activation-loop phosphorylation. A complementary check is to co-immunoprecipitate RAF1 and MEK1 from transfected HEK293 cells to test for direct complex formation.

citations.title: Raf-1 activates MAP kinase-kinase.
Raf-1 forms a stable complex with Mek1 and activates Mek1 by serine phosphorylation.

novelty.note: I searched for the mechanism in plain words (Raf-1 as an upstream kinase of MAP kinase kinase), the entities together (c-Raf-1 phosphorylates MEK1 at the activation-loop serines in vitro with purified recombinant proteins), and the prediction (cell-free Raf-1-dependent MEK1 activation increasing ERK phosphorylation). Classical primary literature retrieved via PubMed states exactly this: Raf-1 uses MAP kinase kinase (MEK) as a direct physiological substrate, reactivating it >30-fold in vitro, and Raf-1 forms a stable complex with Mek1 and activates it by serine phosphorylation, with further downstream Erk1 activation on co-expression. This is the same explanation as the hypothesis, so the status is established rather than partial or open.

hypotheses.statement: Activated ERK2 directly phosphorylates STAT3 in cells stimulated with IL-6 or EGF.
hypotheses.mechanism: IL-6 signalling through Gab1–SHP2 activates ERK2 (heinrich2003:findings:010), and IL-6 or EGF also induces STAT3 phosphorylation (darnell1994:findings:023), so both proteins are activated by the same stimuli. Activated ERK2 directly phosphorylates several signalling proteins in vitro and associates with at least one substrate, Raptor, in cells (lake2016:findings:007, carriere2010:findings:004, carriere2010:findings:006). STAT3 is regulated by serine phosphorylation by another kinase, which changes its DNA binding and transactivation (heinrich2003:findings:023). Together these suggest STAT3 could be an additional direct ERK2 substrate.
hypotheses.prediction: Recombinant activated ERK2 will add phosphate to purified STAT3 in vitro, but inactive ERK2 will not. In IL-6- or EGF-stimulated cells, MEK1/2 inhibition or ERK2 knockdown will reduce STAT3 serine phosphorylation, and ERK2 will co-immunoprecipitate with STAT3.
hypotheses.test: First, run an in vitro kinase assay with [γ-32P]ATP using activated versus unactivated recombinant ERK2 and purified STAT3, and map the phosphorylated sites by phosphopeptide mapping or mass spectrometry. Second, in HepG2 or HEK293 cells stimulated with IL-6 or EGF, compare ERK2 siRNA knockdown or U0126 treatment against controls, and measure STAT3 serine phosphorylation by immunoblot. Third, test whether ERK2 and STAT3 co-immunoprecipitate.

citations.title: STAT3 serine phosphorylation by ERK-dependent and -independent pathways negatively modulates its tyrosine phosphorylation.
ERK1/2 hijack STAT3 via Thr714 phosphorylation to suppress gene expression
The MEK-ERK Pathway Is Necessary for Serine Phosphorylation of Mitochondrial STAT3 and Ras-Mediated Transformation

novelty.note: I searched for direct ERK2 phosphorylation of STAT3 in in vitro kinase assays, for MEK/ERK-dependence of STAT3 serine phosphorylation after EGF and IL-6, and for ERK–STAT3 physical association. Chung et al. (1997) already states exactly this explanation: the ERK family (but not JNK or p38) specifically phosphorylates STAT3 on Ser727, this is ERK-dependent for growth-factor (EGF/PDGF) stimulation, and Ser727 phosphorylation negatively modulates STAT3 Tyr phosphorylation; a recent paper confirms direct phosphorylation using purified PMA-activated Flag-ERK2 versus unstimulated ERK2 on purified STAT3 in vitro (Thr714 and Ser727), with U0126/FR180204 reducing it in cells, and MEK inhibition is likewise shown to abolish STAT3 S727 phosphorylation in Ras-driven cells. One caveat: the same Chung et al. paper reports that the IL-6 arm of the prediction does not hold — IL-6-stimulated STAT3 serine phosphorylation occurred by an ERK-independent process — so the EGF branch is established while the IL-6 branch is contradicted.

hypotheses.statement: ERK2 directly phosphorylates SOS (SOS1) within its C-terminal domain, and this phosphorylation reduces SOS binding to Grb2.
hypotheses.mechanism: Activated ERK2 phosphorylates SOS1 at multiple sites in vitro, and this phosphorylation disrupts SOS1 association with Grb2 and Shc (lake2016:findings:003). The in vivo phosphopeptides of hSos1 comigrate with those produced by in vitro ERK2 phosphorylation (corbalangarcia1996:findings:000), and prior work places the MAP kinase sites in the Sos C-terminal domain (corbalangarcia1996:context:000). A phospho-site-deficient hSos1-4M mutant keeps constant Grb2 binding and does not dissociate after serum stimulation (corbalangarcia1996:findings:007), which is consistent with MAPK phosphorylation of Sos impairing Sos/Grb2 interaction as a negative feedback step (lemmon2010:findings:022).
hypotheses.prediction: Purified active ERK2 should incorporate phosphate into the wild-type SOS1 C-terminal domain but much less into the 4M site mutant. ERK2-phosphorylated SOS1 should bind less Grb2 than unphosphorylated or mutant SOS1.
hypotheses.test: Run an in vitro kinase assay with recombinant phosphorylated (active) ERK2, kinase-dead ERK2 as a control, and [γ-32P]ATP on purified wild-type or 4M SOS1 C-terminal domain. Follow it with a GST-Grb2 pulldown of the phosphorylated versus control SOS1. In parallel, knock down ERK2 by siRNA in serum-stimulated cells and measure SOS1 phosphorylation and SOS1–Grb2 co-immunoprecipitation.

citations.title: Regulation of epidermal growth factor receptor signaling by phosphorylation of the ras exchange factor hSOS1.
Insulin receptor-mediated dissociation of Grb2 from Sos involves phosphorylation of Sos by kinase(s) other than extracellular signal-regulated kinase.
Multiple decisive phosphorylation sites for the negative feedback regulation of SOS1 via ERK.
Insulin-stimulated disassociation of the SOS-Grb2 complex.

novelty.note: I searched for MAP-kinase/ERK2 phosphorylation of the SOS1 C-terminal proline-rich domain, for the Grb2-SOS uncoupling prediction, and for ERK-site SOS mutants, retrieving the Kamioka 2010 full text (PMC2963383) and NCBI records for the key 1995-1998 primary papers. The first half of the statement is published (MAPK phosphorylates hSOS1 within its carboxyl-terminal proline-rich domain in vitro and in vivo), but the causal second half has been directly tested and reported negative: Porfiri & McCormick found phosphorylation did not affect hSOS1-Grb2 binding while it reduced hSOS1 association with hEGFR/Shc through Grb2; Zhao et al. made a Sos mutant lacking canonical ERK sites that was a poor ERK substrate yet still dissociated from Grb2 after stimulation, concluding ERK is not the kinase controlling Grb2·Sos stability; Kamioka et al. likewise state phosphorylation does not affect SOS1-Grb2 binding but dissociates the complex from activated EGFR. The literature is contested (Waters et al. report MAPK-type phosphorylation uncoupling SOS-Grb2), but explicit stated negative tests of this specific claim exist, so the verdict is refuted.

hypotheses.statement: SRC acts upstream of and positively regulates RAF1 (c-Raf/CRAF) activation in EGF-stimulated cells, so SRC activity is required for full EGF-induced RAF1 activation that drives MEK/ERK signaling.
hypotheses.mechanism: In HEK293 cells, c-Raf inhibition eliminated MEK and ERK activity, and insulin-EGF crosstalk amplifying ERK was placed upstream of Ras and at the Ras/Raf level (borisov2009:findings:013). In the same cells, Src RNAi reduced EGF-induced GAB1 phosphorylation and altered phospho-ERK without affecting EGFR or IR autophosphorylation (borisov2009:findings:011). The SRC-family inhibitor PP2 also eliminated EGF-induced ERK phosphorylation in HME and A549 cells (de2015:findings:008). Together these claims place SRC activity between receptor autophosphorylation and the RAF1-dependent step of EGF-to-ERK signaling, which implies SRC promotes RAF1 activation.
hypotheses.prediction: Depleting SRC should reduce EGF-induced RAF1 activation, seen as lower CRAF S338 phosphorylation and lower MEK-directed kinase activity of immunoprecipitated RAF1. This should occur while EGFR autophosphorylation is unchanged. An insulin stimulus should show a smaller SRC dependence than EGF.
hypotheses.test: Knock down SRC by siRNA in HEK293 cells and stimulate with EGF or insulin. Immunoblot EGFR autophosphorylation to confirm receptor activation is intact. Measure RAF1 activation by immunoblotting p-S338 CRAF and by an immunoprecipitation kinase assay of endogenous RAF1 using recombinant MEK as substrate (pMEK readout). As a control, express a RAS-independent CRAF catalytic domain (catC) to test whether the SRC dependence of MEK/ERK activation is lost when RAF1 is activated independently.

citations.title: Serine and tyrosine phosphorylations cooperate in Raf-1, but not B-Raf activation.
CNK1 is a scaffold protein that regulates Src-mediated Raf-1 activation.
Positive and negative regulation of Raf kinase activity and function by phosphorylation.
S338 phosphorylation of Raf-1 is independent of phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase and Pak3.
Oncogenes, growth factors and phorbol esters regulate Raf-1 through common mechanisms.

novelty.note: I searched three ways — the mechanism in words (Src acting upstream of Raf-1 in EGF-to-ERK signalling), the entities together (Src + Raf-1 + S338/Y340-341 + EGF, via PubMed and Europe PMC title/abstract/full-text queries), and the prediction (Src knockdown or PP2/SU6656 reducing EGF-induced CRAF S338 phosphorylation and Raf-1 immunoprecipitation kinase activity with intact EGFR autophosphorylation). The general mechanism is well published: Src phosphorylates Raf-1 at Y340/Y341 and this cooperates with S338 for full Raf-1 kinase activity (Mason et al.), CNK1 scaffolds Src-dependent Raf-1 activation and is needed for full Raf-1 activation, and Y341F mutation is reported to impair Raf-1 activation by EGF as well as by Src/Ras/PMA; Barnard/Marshall likewise place EGF-stimulated Raf-1 activation on the same N-region phosphorylation route. What I could not find is the specific perturbation test — depletion or inhibition of SRC in EGF-stimulated cells measuring RAF1 S338 and IP kinase activity, with an insulin comparison — and the nearest work instead reports that growth-factor-driven S338 phosphorylation proceeds through a kinase other than PI3K/Pak3 and can occur without detectable Y341 phosphorylation, so the causal SRC→RAF1 step in EGF signalling is adjacent rather than established; no source I retrieved tested and negated it.

hypotheses.statement: The rise in ATF4 uORF-dependent translation is a general consequence of lowered translation initiation or protein synthesis capacity rather than a specific effect of eIF2α Ser51 phosphorylation, so any upstream input that lowers general protein synthesis (for example, loss of RAG/mTORC1 activity) should produce the same 'paradoxical' pairing.
hypotheses.mechanism: In C. elegans, RAG knockdown reduced protein synthesis without inducing eIF2α phosphorylation, yet robustly increased an atf-4 uORF reporter even when eIF2α phosphorylation was genetically blocked. This shows the uORF-mediated increase can be separated from Ser51 phosphorylation. Active-site mTOR inhibitors that fully inhibit mTORC1 also significantly reduce overall protein synthesis in proliferating mammalian cells, giving a second, eIF2α-independent way to lower synthesis that would be expected to engage the same uORF response.
hypotheses.prediction: In cultured mammalian cells that cannot phosphorylate eIF2α on Ser51, an active-site mTOR inhibitor will reduce global protein synthesis and still increase expression of an ATF4 uORF reporter. The induction will depend on intact uORFs and will scale with the reduction in protein synthesis rather than with phospho-eIF2α levels.
hypotheses.test: Express an ATF4 5'UTR (uORF) reporter and a uORF-mutated control reporter in wild-type and eIF2α Ser51-to-Ala cultured cells. Treat with a dose series of an active-site mTOR inhibitor, then measure global synthesis by puromycin incorporation, phospho-eIF2α by western blot, and reporter output. If the uORF reporter is induced in Ser51Ala cells with no change in phospho-eIF2α, the hypothesis is supported; if induction is lost in Ser51Ala cells, the effect is specific to eIF2α phosphorylation.

citations.title: mTORC1 Balances Cellular Amino Acid Supply with Demand for Protein Synthesis through Post-transcriptional Control of ATF4.
The mTORC1-mediated activation of ATF4 promotes protein and glutathione synthesis downstream of growth signals.
Regulation of Translation of ATF4 mRNA: A Focus on Translation Initiation Factors and RNA-Binding Proteins

novelty.note: I searched for eIF2α-independent ATF4 uORF control, for mTOR inhibitors plus ATF4 uORF reporters, and specifically for Torin1/rapamycin effects on ATF4 in eIF2α Ser51Ala cells. The exact experiment proposed has been done in mammalian cells and gives the opposite result: Park et al. showed Torin1 reduces global protein synthesis yet *depletes* ATF4 via a 5'UTR reporter that requires intact uORF3, with no dependence on eIF2α phosphorylation (and unchanged phospho-eIF2α in GCN2-null cells), while Torrence et al. found in eIF2α A/A (S51A) MEFs that mTORC1 activation raises ATF4 in a rapamycin-sensitive, 5'UTR-dependent manner — i.e. mTOR inhibition lowers rather than raises uORF-dependent ATF4 in Ser51Ala cells. Because mammalian mTORC1 acts on ATF4 uORF translation through 4E-BP/eIF4F in the direction opposite to the prediction, the claim that lowering synthesis by active-site mTOR inhibition will still induce an ATF4 uORF reporter is directly contradicted, even though eIF2α-independence of ATF4 uORF control is itself well established.

hypotheses.statement: Light-activated Ras drives PKCβ phosphorylation indirectly through an ERK/RSK-to-mTOR route, so the PKCβ signal tracks the Raf/Mek/Erk/RSK module because it is an mTOR-dependent output of that module.
hypotheses.mechanism: ERK1/2 and RSK1 phosphorylate TSC1/TSC2 to inactivate it and activate mTOR signalling (laplante2012). mTOR is required for turn-motif and hydrophobic-motif phosphorylation of a conventional PKC, shown for PKCα (ikenoue2008), and mTOR/PI3K-pathway inhibitors lower PKC substrate phosphorylation alongside p90RSK substrates (casado2013). A Ras-only input that activates Erk and RSK could therefore raise PKCβ phosphorylation without PDGF receptor input; the caveat is that the cited PKC evidence concerns PKCα and resembles Rictor/Sin1 loss, whereas the TSC link is stated for mTORC1.
hypotheses.prediction: In opto-SOS NIH 3T3 cells, the light-induced rise in phospho-PKCβ should be abolished by MEK inhibition and by mTOR inhibition or knockdown, while light-induced phospho-Erk should remain intact under mTOR inhibition.
hypotheses.test: Pretreat opto-SOS NIH 3T3 cells with a MEK inhibitor, an mTOR kinase inhibitor or mTOR shRNA, or vehicle, then apply the light stimulus and immunoblot a time course for phospho-PKCβ (same epitope as the RPPA antibody), phospho-Erk and phospho-RSK. Loss of phospho-PKCβ under both MEK and mTOR inhibition supports this route; persistence under MEK inhibition refutes it and points to a Ras-proximal mechanism.

citations.title: Tumor-promoting phorbol esters and activated Ras inactivate the tuberous sclerosis tumor suppressor complex via p90 ribosomal S6 kinase.
TSC2/Rheb signaling mediates ERK-dependent regulation of mTORC1 activity in C2C12 myoblasts.
PKCβII acts downstream of chemoattractant receptors and mTORC2 to regulate cAMP production and myosin II activity in neutrophils.
The Functional Proximal Proteome of Oncogenic Ras Includes mTORC2.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the plain-language chain (Ras/ERK/RSK → TSC → mTOR → PKC phosphorylation), the entities together (optoSOS NIH 3T3, phospho-PKCβ, MEK/mTOR inhibition), and the prediction (MEK-inhibitor and rapamycin/mTOR sensitivity of PKCβ turn/hydrophobic-motif phosphorylation). Each link exists separately in print — activated Ras acting through RSK1 to phosphorylate and inactivate TSC2 and raise mTOR signalling (PMID 15342917), MEK/ERK-dependent mTORC1 activation through TSC2/Rheb blocked by U0126 (PMID 28286738), and agonist-induced, mTOR(C2)-dependent turn- and hydrophobic-motif phosphorylation of PKCβII specifically (PMID 24600048) — but no source I retrieved joins them into an ERK/RSK→mTOR explanation for light- or Ras-induced phospho-PKCβ, and none tests MEK or mTOR dependence of that signal in optogenetic Ras cells. The nearest competing published account is a direct, ERK-independent Ras–mTORC2 interaction at the plasma membrane (PMID 30639242), which covers the Ras-proximal alternative rather than the proposed route; I found no stated negative result against the specific claim, so this is partial rather than established or refuted.

hypotheses.statement: PKCβ is engaged at the Ras/Raf level as a membrane-proximal participant in Raf activation rather than as a downstream Erk target, which is why it tracks light-activated Ras with the same fast kinetics as Raf.
hypotheses.mechanism: PKCβI is needed for full Ras-GTP and ERK activation in mast cells (kawakami2003), and PKC-β alone can induce Raf autophosphorylation and MEK phosphorylation in a coexpression system (schnwasser1998), placing PKCβ at or above Raf. Raf-1 S338 phosphorylation under EGF/TPA stimulation occurs independently of Y341 and implies at least two distinct S338 kinases (mason1999), leaving room for a Ras-coupled, Src-independent input at the Raf step. The cited claims show PKCβ acting on Ras/Raf, not Ras acting on PKCβ, so the Ras-to-PKCβ direction is the inferred part.
hypotheses.prediction: Light-induced phospho-PKCβ should be insensitive to MEK inhibition, and inhibiting or knocking down PKCβ should reduce the amplitude of light-induced phospho-Raf, phospho-Mek and phospho-Erk.
hypotheses.test: In opto-SOS NIH 3T3 cells, (a) stimulate with light with or without a MEK inhibitor and immunoblot phospho-PKCβ, and (b) knock down PKCβ by siRNA or apply a PKCβ-selective inhibitor and immunoblot light-induced phospho-Raf S338, phospho-Mek and phospho-Erk. MEK-insensitive phospho-PKCβ together with reduced Raf/Mek/Erk on PKCβ loss supports this hypothesis; MEK-sensitive phospho-PKCβ with no effect of PKCβ loss on Raf/Mek/Erk refutes it and favours a downstream-of-Erk explanation.

citations.title: Signaling to extracellular signal-regulated kinase from ErbB1 kinase and protein kinase C: feedback, heterogeneity, and gating.
Down-regulation of Cdx2 in colorectal carcinoma cells by the Raf-MEK-ERK 1/2 pathway.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the mechanism in words (PKC/PKCβ acting at or above Raf rather than as an ERK target), the entities together (PKCβ + Raf-1 S338 + Ras-GTP + optoSOS/light-activated Ras phosphoproteomics), and the prediction (MEK-inhibitor sensitivity of phospho-PKCα/βII Thr638/641; PKCβ knockdown effects on phospho-Raf/MEK/ERK). The general half of the mechanism is published — PKC isoforms are repeatedly placed upstream of the cascade as Raf activators (e.g. PMID 23754287 explicitly contrasts ErbB1- and PKC-driven ERK activation via 'activation of Raf by PKC'), and PKCα/ε/η have been shown to stimulate Raf directly — but I found no source stating that PKCβ is phosphorylated as a membrane-proximal co-participant in Raf activation downstream of Ras itself, nor any source testing MEK-independence of Ras-triggered phospho-PKCβ or PKCβ loss-of-function effects on Raf S338/MEK/ERK amplitude in optogenetic Ras systems. Notably the nearest direct test of the prediction's first half points the other way (PMID 19686845 reports phospho-PKCβII is regulated in a MEK/ERK-dependent manner in a Raf-1:ER inducible system, reversed by U0126), but that was a different cell system and stimulus and did not test the specific Ras-to-PKCβ claim, so this is partial rather than established or refuted.

hypotheses.statement: GSK3B negatively regulates TGF-β-induced growth inhibition: by phosphorylating Smad3 at Thr66 and promoting its degradation, GSK3B limits the Smad3-dependent cytostatic response, so loss or inhibition of GSK3B should sensitise cells to TGF-β growth arrest.
hypotheses.mechanism: The growth-side claims indicate that TGF-β growth inhibition runs through Smads: dominant-negative Smad3 or Smad7 blocks about 80% of TGF-β-induced growth inhibition in NMuMG cells, and Smad4-deleted BxPc3 cells are not growth-inhibited by TGF-β. Independently, the GSK3B-side claims show that GSK3β phosphorylates Smad3 at Thr66, drives its ubiquitination and turnover, and that GSK3β knockout, shRNA or inhibition raises TGF-β-induced Smad3 phosphorylation, nuclear translocation and Smad3-dependent transcription. Taken together, GSK3B activity should set the amplitude of the Smad3-dependent growth-inhibitory output.
hypotheses.prediction: GSK3β knockdown or inhibition with SB-216763 will shift the TGF-β dose-response for growth inhibition leftward (greater suppression of DNA synthesis at sub-saturating TGF-β) in TGF-β-responsive epithelial cells. This sensitisation will be lost when Smad3 is blocked by dominant-negative Smad3, or when Smad3 is replaced by the non-phosphorylatable T66V mutant, which should already be hypersensitive and unaffected by GSK3β inhibition.
hypotheses.test: In NMuMG or HaCaT cells, measure thymidine or BrdU incorporation across a TGF-β dose series with and without GSK3β shRNA or SB-216763. Repeat in cells expressing dominant-negative Smad3, and in Smad3-null MEFs reconstituted with Smad3 wild type versus T66V. Blot Smad3 protein and pT66 in parallel. The hypothesis is ruled out if GSK3β loss does not enhance TGF-β growth inhibition, or if the enhancement persists without functional Smad3 or Thr66.

citations.title: Axin and GSK3- control Smad3 protein stability and modulate TGF- signaling.
A negative feedback control of transforming growth factor-beta signaling by glycogen synthase kinase 3-mediated Smad3 linker phosphorylation at Ser-204.

novelty.note: I searched for the GSK3β–Smad3 Thr66 degradation mechanism in plain words, for the entities together (GSK3/Axin, Smad3 stability, TGF-β cytostatic response), and for the prediction (GSK3 inhibition or non-phosphorylatable Smad3 sensitising cells to TGF-β growth inhibition). The Guo et al. Genes & Development paper that supplies the GSK3B-side claims itself makes the growth-side link explicit: Axin/GSK3-β-mediated Thr66 phosphorylation sets basal Smad3 levels and 'the steady-state stability of Smad3 is an important determinant of cellular sensitivity to TGF-β', with Axin RNAi rendering HaCaT cells 'more sensitive to the cytostatic effect of TGF-β', Axin restoration dampening 'TGF-β-induced growth arrest', and Smad3(T66V) producing stronger dose-dependent growth arrest than wild-type Smad3 in HepG2 cells. A second study on GSK3-mediated Smad3 linker phosphorylation independently reports that a non-phosphorylatable Smad3 mutant renders cells 'even more sensitive to TGF-β-induced growth inhibition' (and explicitly used a T66V background to separate the Thr66 effect), so the explanation that GSK3 negatively sets the amplitude of the Smad3-dependent cytostatic output is already published rather than novel; no source reported a negative test.

hypotheses.statement: MTOR negatively regulates TNF-induced JNK activation, with MTOR activity limiting the magnitude and duration of JNK signalling through its enhancement of NF-κB-dependent transcription.
hypotheses.mechanism: MTOR expression enhances NF-κB-dependent reporter activity in PC3, LNCaP and HeLa cells, and IKK components co-immunoprecipitate with the MTOR complex (dan2008). Separately, TNF-induced JNK activation is stronger and more prolonged in cells lacking NF-κB activity, because several NF-κB-activated gene products inhibit JNK activation (chen2002).
