Together these imply that lowering MTOR activity should reduce NF-κB output and thereby release JNK from NF-κB-dependent restraint.
hypotheses.prediction: MTOR knockdown or ATP-competitive MTOR inhibition will increase and prolong TNF-induced JNK and c-Jun phosphorylation relative to control cells. This effect should be reversed by enforced NF-κB activation, and MTOR overexpression should shorten or dampen the JNK response.
hypotheses.test: In PC3 or HeLa cells, deplete MTOR by siRNA (or treat with Torin1) and, in parallel, overexpress MTOR. Stimulate with TNF over a time course (0–4 h) and immunoblot for phospho-JNK and phospho-c-Jun, with an NF-κB luciferase reporter as a control for the MTOR effect on NF-κB. Then repeat the MTOR knockdown with co-expression of a constitutively active IKK to test whether restoring NF-κB activity rescues the prolonged JNK phosphorylation.

citations.title: A20/TNFAIP3 Discriminates Tumor Necrosis Factor (TNF)-Induced NF-κB from JNK Pathway Activation in Hepatocytes.
Sustained activation of the JNK cascade and rapamycin-induced apoptosis are suppressed by p53/p21(Cip1).
Rapamycin antagonizes TNF induction of VCAM-1 on endothelial cells by inhibiting mTORC2.

novelty.note: I searched PubMed (eutils) and the web for mTOR/rapamycin/Torin combined with TNF-induced JNK and c-Jun phosphorylation, for mTOR–IKK–JNK crosstalk, and for the prediction phrased as prolonged JNK signalling after mTOR loss; no paper states that mTOR limits TNF-induced JNK by boosting NF-κB output. The two halves are separately published: NF-κB-induced products such as A20 dampen and shorten TNF-induced JNK phosphorylation, and mTOR inhibition alone can drive sustained JNK/c-Jun activation (via ASK1, serum-free, p53-dependent, with no TNF or NF-κB involvement). The closest direct look at the predicted readout is in endothelial cells, where rapamycin left TNF-induced JNK1/2 phosphorylation and IκB-α processing unchanged — an unchanged, not increased, JNK response, but in a setting where mTOR inhibition also did not lower NF-κB activation, so it does not constitute a test of the proposed NF-κB-mediated link; hence partial rather than established or refuted.

hypotheses.statement: GSK3B directly restrains TGF-B signaling output in T cells by phosphorylating Smad3 to limit its stability and transcriptional activity, so GSK3B inhibition should amplify TGF-B-driven responses such as Foxp3 induction and anergy.
hypotheses.mechanism: The GSK3B evidence establishes a direct enzymatic relationship with the TGF-B pathway effector Smad3: GSK3B phosphorylates Thr66 in the Smad3 MH1 domain and the R-Smad linker, driving ubiquitylation and degradation, and GSK3B-null cells show stronger TGF-B-induced C-terminal Smad3 phosphorylation, nuclear translocation and SBE-reporter activity (guo2008:findings:018, guo2008:findings:016, hata2016:findings:024). Independently, the TGF-B evidence shows that TGF-B plus TCR stimulation induces Foxp3 and a Smad2/3-phosphorylation-associated anergic state in naive CD4+ T cells in a TGF-B dose-dependent manner (chen2003:findings:013, chen2003:findings:011). If Smad3 abundance is the limiting node in both settings, GSK3B activity should set the gain on TGF-B responses in T cells.
hypotheses.prediction: Pharmacological or genetic loss of GSK3B in naive CD4+CD25- T cells stimulated with anti-CD3/anti-CD28 should shift the TGF-B dose-response curve leftward — higher Foxp3 induction and stronger hyporesponsiveness at submaximal TGF-B doses — accompanied by increased Smad3 protein and phospho-Smad3 and loss of the pT66 signal, with little effect on Smad2-dependent readouts; conversely, GSK3B overexpression should blunt TGF-B-induced Foxp3.
hypotheses.test: Stimulate primary naive CD4+CD25- T cells with anti-CD3/anti-CD28 across a TGF-B dose series with and without SB-216763 (or siRNA/shRNA knockdown of GSK3B), then measure Foxp3 by RT-qPCR/flow cytometry and proliferation by thymidine or CFSE, in parallel immunoblotting total Smad3, pT66-Smad3 and C-terminal phospho-Smad3; rescue with a Smad3(T66V) versus Smad3(WT) construct in Smad3-depleted cells to test whether the Thr66 site is required for the GSK3B effect on TGF-B output.

citations.title: Glycogen synthase kinase 3β inhibition promotes human iTreg differentiation and suppressive function.
Cutting Edge: Inhibition of Glycogen Synthase Kinase 3 Activity Induces the Generation and Enhanced Suppressive Function of Human IL-10(+) FOXP3(+)-Induced Regulatory T Cells.
Glycogen synthase kinase-3 inhibition attenuates fibroblast activation and development of fibrosis following renal ischemia-reperfusion in mice.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the mechanism in words (GSK3 restraining TGF-β output via Smad3 stability), the entities together (GSK3β + Smad3 + Thr66 + Foxp3/iTreg), and the prediction (SB216763 or GSK3 knockdown shifting TGF-β-driven Foxp3 induction in anti-CD3/CD28-stimulated naive CD4+ T cells). Xia et al. (Immunol Res 2015) already states this explanation for this phenomenon: GSK3β is inactivated during iTreg differentiation, and its pharmacological inhibition with SB216763 or TDZD-8 promotes TGF-β-driven iTreg/Foxp3 differentiation and suppressive activity specifically 'through the TGF-β/Smad3 pathway', which is the same causal claim as the hypothesis. Two caveats keep this from being a complete match rather than changing the status: the 2020 J Immunol Cutting Edge reports GSK3 inhibition lowering FOXP3 MFI while promoting IL-10+FOXP3+ iTregs and explicitly not altering TGF-β expression, and in renal fibroblasts GSK3 inhibitors reduced rather than increased TGF-β1-induced pSMAD3 — so the Thr66-dependence, the leftward dose-shift, the anergy readout and the Smad2-selectivity remain untested in T cells.

hypotheses.statement: ERK2 directly phosphorylates EGFR on a serine/threonine-proline site in its cytoplasmic region, acting as negative feedback that shortens EGF-induced EGFR tyrosine phosphorylation.
hypotheses.mechanism: EGF strongly activates ERK2 (meng2005:findings:001), and activated ERK2 phosphorylates upstream components of its own pathway, including another receptor tyrosine kinase: ERK1/2 phosphorylate FGFR1 on S777 in vitro, and the S777A mutant shows prolonged receptor tyrosine phosphorylation (lake2016:findings:002). ERK2 similarly phosphorylates SOS1 and disrupts its association with Grb2 and Shc (lake2016:findings:003). Separately, EGFR is itself a substrate of a proline-directed MAPK, since p38alpha phosphorylates EGFR to drive its internalization (cuadrado2010:findings:054). Together these suggest EGFR could be an ERK2 feedback substrate analogous to FGFR1.
hypotheses.prediction: Recombinant active ERK2 will incorporate phosphate into the EGFR cytoplasmic domain in vitro on S/T-P site(s). In cells, MEK1/2 inhibition or alanine substitution of the ERK2-targeted site(s) will abolish EGF-induced S/T-P phosphorylation of EGFR and prolong EGF-induced EGFR tyrosine phosphorylation.
hypotheses.test: Run an in vitro kinase assay with recombinant activated ERK2 and purified kinase-dead EGFR cytoplasmic domain ([γ-32P]ATP autoradiography or pS/T-P motif immunoblot) and map the sites by mutagenesis. Then express WT or Ser/Thr-to-Ala EGFR in cultured cells, stimulate with EGF with or without U0126, and immunoblot immunoprecipitated EGFR for pS/T-P and phosphotyrosine over a time course.

citations.title: Isolation and characterization of two growth factor-stimulated protein kinases that phosphorylate the epidermal growth factor receptor at threonine 669.
ERK-dependent threonine phosphorylation of EGF receptor modulates receptor downregulation and signaling.
Inverse correlation between Thr-669 and constitutive tyrosine phosphorylation in the asymmetric epidermal growth factor receptor dimer conformation.
Feedback control of ErbB2 via ERK-mediated phosphorylation of a conserved threonine in the juxtamembrane domain.

novelty.note: I searched for ERK-mediated serine/threonine feedback phosphorylation of EGFR, for the specific proline-directed juxtamembrane site, and for the prediction that site mutation prolongs EGF-induced receptor tyrosine phosphorylation. The mechanism is long-established: EGFR Thr-669 sits in a Pro-Leu-Thr-Pro (S/T-P) motif in the juxtamembrane cytoplasmic region, is phosphorylated in vitro by purified MAP kinase/ERT kinase (Northwood et al.), is blocked in cells by MEK/ERK inhibition (U0126), and T669A abolishes the phosphorylation while enhancing/prolonging EGF-induced EGFR tyrosine phosphorylation and accelerating downregulation; the same conserved-threonine feedback extends to ErbB2 Thr-677. Every element of the stated explanation and prediction, including the proposed assays, is therefore already published, so the status is established rather than partial.

hypotheses.statement: EGFR activates ERK2 in a manner gated by phosphorylation of its Y992 RasGAP-binding site, such that the SHP2 requirement for EGF-induced ERK2 activation reflects SHP2 dephosphorylation of EGFR pY992.
hypotheses.mechanism: EGF-induced ERK2 kinase activity falls by about 80% when Gab1 or Gab2 cannot bind SHP2 (meng2005:findings:001), and targeting active SHP2 to the membrane through the Gab1 PH domain is sufficient for constitutive ERK2 activation (heinrich2003:findings:011). Independently, SHP2 targets EGFR pY992, which is a RasGAP SH2 binding site (agazie2003:findings:012, agazie2003:findings:013). Y992F-EGFR gives higher and more prolonged ERK1/2 activation when SHP2 function is blocked (agazie2003:findings:014). This implies that EGFR output to ERK2 is limited by pY992, and that Gab-recruited SHP2 relieves this limit.
hypotheses.prediction: Y992F-EGFR will produce greater and more sustained EGF-induced ERK2 kinase activity than WT-EGFR. It will also substantially rescue the loss of ERK2 activation caused by SHP2-binding-defective Gab1 (Gab1FF), whereas WT-EGFR will not.
hypotheses.test: Co-transfect cultured cells with HA-ERK2, WT- or Y992F-EGFR, and either empty vector or Gab1FF, then stimulate with EGF over a time course. Measure ERK2 activity by HA immunocomplex kinase assay with MBP as substrate, and in parallel pull down EGFR with GST-SH2-RasGAP to confirm that RasGAP binding tracks inversely with ERK2 activity.

citations.title: A specific amino acid context in EGFR and HER2 phosphorylation sites enables selective binding to the active site of Src homology phosphatase 2 (SHP2).
SHP2-EGFR States in Dephosphorylation Can Inform Selective SHP2 Inhibitors, Dampening RasGAP Action.
Phosphoproteomics-based modeling defines the regulatory mechanism underlying aberrant EGFR signaling.
Requirement of SHP2 binding to Grb2-associated binder-1 for mitogen-activated protein kinase activation in response to lysophosphatidic acid and epidermal growth factor.

novelty.note: I searched three ways — the mechanism in words (SHP2 dephosphorylating an EGFR RasGAP-docking site to permit Ras-ERK signalling), the entities together (Y992/pY992 + SHP2 + Gab1 + RasGAP, via Europe PMC full-text queries), and the prediction (Y992F-EGFR effects on ERK amplitude/duration; SHP099 phosphoproteomics for a negative test). The component steps are published independently: SHP2's active site selectively engages the pY992-EGFR context and dephosphorylation there is framed as dampening RasGAP action, and a Y992F-EGFR line has been reported to show sustained rather than transient ERK1 activation; no source reported a direct negative test. However, no retrieved work attributes the Gab1/Gab2-SHP2 requirement for EGF-induced ERK2 activity to EGFR pY992, nor tests Y992F rescue of SHP2-binding-defective Gab1 — that Gab-dependent literature instead locates the relevant RasGAP-binding substrate on Gab1 itself, so the specific connection remains unpublished.

hypotheses.statement: Rapamycin treatment negatively regulates GSK3B kinase activity in cells, indirectly, by relieving the S6K feedback and raising AKT activity that inhibits GSK3B.
hypotheses.mechanism: The rapamycin claims report that rapamycin increases AKT S473 phosphorylation in PC3 cells and CLL-like cells, attributed to loss of S6K-mediated feedback. Independent claims about GSK3B state that AKT inhibits GSK3B, which stabilises PHLPP and prolongs NFAT nuclear residence. Together these imply that rapamycin-induced AKT activation should lower GSK3B activity toward its substrates, such as Smad3 Thr66, which is reported to be GSK3B-dependent.
hypotheses.prediction: In cells where rapamycin raises AKT S473 phosphorylation, rapamycin should increase AKT-dependent inhibitory phosphorylation of GSK3B and decrease phosphorylation of GSK3B substrates such as Smad3 Thr66. Both effects should be reversed by co-treatment with the PI3K inhibitor LY294002. An mTOR kinase inhibitor that also blocks AKT S473 (AZD8055 or Torin1) should not produce them.
hypotheses.test: Treat PC3 or HaCaT cells with a rapamycin time course and dose range, with and without LY294002, alongside AZD8055 and the GSK3 inhibitor SB-216763 as controls. Immunoblot for phospho-AKT S473, phospho-S6K, inhibitory-site phospho-GSK3B, and Smad3 pT66. Complement this with an in vitro kinase assay of immunoprecipitated GSK3B from treated versus untreated cells on a primed peptide substrate. No change in GSK3B phosphorylation, substrate phosphorylation or kinase activity despite elevated AKT S473 would rule the hypothesis out.

citations.title: mTOR inhibition induces upstream receptor tyrosine kinase signaling and activates Akt.
S6K1 regulates GSK3 under conditions of mTOR-dependent feedback inhibition of Akt.
GSK3 is required for rapalogs to induce degradation of some oncogenic proteins and to suppress cancer cell growth.

novelty.note: I searched for the rapamycin→S6K/IRS-1 feedback→AKT→GSK3 inhibitory-phosphorylation chain, for rapamycin plus GSK3 Ser9/Ser21 with PI3K-inhibitor reversal, and for any link between mTOR inhibition and GSK3-dependent Smad3 Thr66. O'Reilly et al. already report the core step — 1 nM rapamycin raises Akt S473 and GSK3α/β S21/9 phosphorylation in DU-145 cells through relief of mTOR-dependent IRS-1 feedback, with the Akt activity increase abolished by LY294002 and IGF-IR blockade — but no retrieved source ties this to reduced GSK3B kinase activity toward substrates such as Smad3 Thr66, and the two nearest works show the opposite or a much weaker effect: in TSC1/2-null cells rapamycin restores Akt S473 yet abolishes GSK3 S21/9 phosphorylation because S6K1 is the GSK3 kinase there, and in lung/head-and-neck lines rapamycin only slightly raised GSK3 S21/9 in 2 of several lines while rapalog action required active GSK3. Hence the mechanism is published in general form but the specific prediction and cross-paper connection are not, and the direction is context-dependent rather than cleanly refuted.

hypotheses.statement: GSK3B phosphorylates c-Myc in a phospho-priming-dependent manner and thereby promotes c-Myc ubiquitination and degradation, so that GSK3B activity limits the c-Myc protein level set by ERK signalling.
hypotheses.mechanism: The claims about GSK3B show a recurring mode of action: it phosphorylates transcriptional regulators and signalling proteins (Smad3, the R-Smad linker, PHLPP) to trigger their ubiquitination and degradation, it prefers substrates already phosphorylated at a priming site, and it acts after priming by proline-directed kinases such as CDK8/9 alongside ERK. Independently, c-Myc protein is reported as an ERK effector whose abundance scales in a graded way with EGF dose and ERK output. This is an inference by analogy, not a stated link: an ERK-phosphorylated c-Myc would fit the kind of primed substrate GSK3B is shown to destabilise elsewhere.
hypotheses.prediction: Inhibiting or knocking down GSK3B should raise steady-state c-Myc protein and lengthen its half-life without raising its mRNA, and should reduce c-Myc ubiquitination. GSK3B should phosphorylate c-Myc in vitro much more efficiently when c-Myc has first been phosphorylated by active ERK, and blocking MEK should reduce the GSK3B-dependent phosphorylation in cells.
hypotheses.test: In MCF-10A or HaCaT cells, treat with the GSK3 inhibitor SB-216763 or GSK3B shRNA, then measure endogenous c-Myc by Western blot and cycloheximide chase, with qPCR for MYC mRNA and a c-Myc ubiquitination assay under MG-132. In parallel, run an in vitro kinase assay with recombinant GSK3B on recombinant c-Myc, with and without pre-phosphorylation by active ERK, and map the sites by mass spectrometry. Confirm by showing that alanine mutants of the mapped sites make c-Myc stability insensitive to GSK3B inhibition.

citations.title: Multiple Ras-dependent phosphorylation pathways regulate Myc protein stability.
Phosphorylation by glycogen synthase kinase-3 controls c-myc proteolysis and subnuclear localization.
A signalling pathway controlling c-Myc degradation that impacts oncogenic transformation of human cells.

novelty.note: I searched for GSK3-mediated c-Myc Thr58 phosphorylation with Ser62 priming by ERK, for the Sears/Nevins Ras-Myc stability work, and for GSK3-dependent c-Myc ubiquitination via Europe PMC records. The hypothesis is a textbook-level established mechanism: Sears et al. (2000) show ERK-mediated Ser62 phosphorylation primes GSK-3-dependent Thr58 phosphorylation that drives Myc degradation and that PI3K/GSK-3 controls Myc accumulation; Gregory et al. (2003) show GSK-3 inhibition stabilises c-Myc and blocks Thr58 phosphorylation while GSK-3 overexpression increases Thr58 phosphorylation and ubiquitination, identifying GSK-3 as the Thr58 kinase; Yeh et al. (2004) detail the downstream Ser62/Thr58-dependent degradation cascade. Because the specific priming-dependent phosphorylation, the ubiquitination/stability prediction, and the ERK-GSK3 antagonism over c-Myc levels are all explicitly reported, the status is established rather than partial.

hypotheses.statement: GSK3β directly phosphorylates STAT3 on serine/threonine residues and thereby negatively regulates STAT3-dependent transcriptional activity.
hypotheses.mechanism: The claims about GSK3β show it repeatedly phosphorylating transcription factors to restrain their output: Smad3 at Thr66 (reducing its stability and activity), the R-Smad linker (inhibiting nuclear accumulation), and C/EBPβ (correlating with decreased IL-17-induced gene expression). It also often acts on substrates already phosphorylated by a priming kinase. Independently, STAT3 is shown to be restrained by serine phosphorylation, since PKCδ phosphorylation at Ser727 inhibits its DNA binding and transcriptional activity. STAT3 is therefore a transcription factor whose phospho-regulation fits the pattern GSK3β applies to comparable substrates.
hypotheses.prediction: Recombinant GSK3β should phosphorylate purified STAT3 in vitro. In cells, GSK3β knockdown or inhibition should reduce a GSK3-dependent phospho-species of STAT3 and increase IL-6-induced STAT3 DNA binding and STAT3-dependent promoter activity (for example the α2M promoter). A STAT3 mutant lacking the mapped site(s) should not respond to GSK3β inhibition.
hypotheses.test: First, run an in vitro kinase assay with recombinant GSK3β and purified STAT3, with and without pre-phosphorylation by a priming kinase, and map any sites by mass spectrometry. Then, in HepG2 cells, treat with SB-216763 or GSK3β shRNA and measure STAT3 phosphorylation by immunoblot or Phos-tag, endogenous GSK3β–STAT3 co-immunoprecipitation, and IL-6-induced α2M-promoter luciferase activity. Compare wild-type STAT3 with a phospho-site mutant; no in vitro phosphorylation and no change in STAT3 reporter activity on GSK3β loss would rule the hypothesis out.

citations.title: Signal integration and gene induction by a functionally distinct STAT3 phosphoform.
Differential regulation of STAT family members by glycogen synthase kinase-3.

novelty.note: I searched for GSK3β as a direct STAT3 serine/threonine kinase, for GSK3-dependent STAT3 Ser727 phosphorylation in vitro, and for the prediction that GSK3 inhibition would increase IL-6-induced STAT3 DNA binding and reporter activity. Waitkus et al. (MCB 2014) already report that recombinant GSK-3α/β directly and efficiently phosphorylate STAT3 at Ser727 and Thr714 with Ser727 acting as a priming site for Thr714, but the mapped sites and GSK-3α/β depletion are required for — not restraining of — STAT3 DNA binding and STAT3-dependent gene induction, and the Ser/Thr mutants lose rather than gain activity. Beurel and Jope (JBC 2008) directly tested the cellular prediction and found GSK3 inhibition or GSK3β knockdown blocked IL-6-induced STAT3 activation, DNA binding and transcriptional activation, the opposite of the predicted increase; so the phosphorylation half is published while the negative-regulation half has been tested and does not hold.

hypotheses.statement: JNK directly phosphorylates the mTORC1 subunit Raptor and thereby regulates mTORC1 kinase activity, in parallel to the ERK1/2- and RSK-mediated Raptor phosphorylation already described.
hypotheses.mechanism: The mTORC1 claims show that Raptor is a convergence point for Ras/MAPK input: ERK1/2 and RSK phosphorylate Raptor, and loss of the ERK-dependent sites (S3A) lowers mTORC1 kinase activity toward 4E-BP1 without changing complex assembly. The JNK claims place JNK in the same MAP kinase family as ERK, sharing dual-specificity MAP kinase phosphatases, and show it directly phosphorylating a substrate serine (NFATc1 Ser117) in a JIP-1-inhibitable manner. This is an inference by analogy: a sibling MAP kinase may use the same Raptor entry point to mTORC1. The evidence does not state the direction of the effect on activity.
hypotheses.prediction: Active JNK should incorporate phosphate into wild-type Raptor in vitro, with reduced incorporation into a phosphorylation-site mutant such as S3A. In cells, activating JNK (MKK7 plus JNK1) under MEK inhibition should change Raptor phosphorylation and mTORC1 output (4E-BP1 Thr37/Thr46, S6K1 phosphorylation), and this change should be lost with JIP-1 overexpression or the JNK inhibitor SP600125.
hypotheses.test: Run an in vitro kinase assay with recombinant active JNK1 and immunopurified wild-type or S3A Raptor using [γ-32P]ATP. In HEK293 cells, co-express MKK7 plus JNK1 with or without JIP-1 or SP600125, in the presence of a MEK1/2 inhibitor to exclude ERK/RSK input. Then immunoblot for Raptor phosphorylation and phospho-4E-BP1 (Thr37/Thr46) and phospho-S6K1, and measure Raptor-associated mTOR kinase activity on GST-4E-BP1. No JNK-dependent Raptor phosphorylation and no change in mTORC1 readouts would rule the hypothesis out.

citations.title: Osmotic stress regulates mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) complex 1 via c-Jun N-terminal Kinase (JNK)-mediated Raptor protein phosphorylation.
Suppression of MAPK/JNK-MTORC1 signaling leads to premature loss of organelles and nuclei by autophagy during terminal differentiation of lens fiber cells.

novelty.note: I searched for JNK-mediated Raptor phosphorylation, for JNK/Raptor/mTORC1 in vitro kinase assays, and for MAPK-family convergence on Raptor (ERK/RSK vs JNK), then retrieved the primary records via Europe PMC/NCBI and PMC. Kwak et al. (J Biol Chem 2012) report exactly this explanation: JNK physically associates with Raptor and phosphorylates it in vitro, osmotic stress drives Raptor phosphorylation at Ser696, Thr706 and Ser863 in a JNK-dependent manner (abolished by JNK inhibition), and mTORC1 kinase activity is activated JNK-dependently — i.e. JNK regulates mTORC1 through Raptor, in parallel to the ERK1/2- and RSK-mediated sites. A second retrieved paper independently states that MAPK8/JNK1 phosphorylates RPTOR at Ser863 and that JNK inactivation suppresses MTORC1 signaling, so the mechanism is published rather than novel.

hypotheses.statement: SRC acts upstream of ERK2 as an activator: SRC kinase activity is required for EGF-induced ERK2 activation, through SRC-dependent GAB1 phosphorylation that enables the Gab1–SHP2 signal to ERK2.
hypotheses.mechanism: On the SRC side, Src knockdown in HEK293 cells lowered EGF-stimulated GAB1 phosphorylation and phospho-ERK without changing EGFR autophosphorylation, and the SRC-family inhibitor PP2 eliminated EGF-induced ERK phosphorylation. On the ERK2 side, EGF activation of ERK2 was inhibited by about 80% by SHP2-binding-defective Gab1 or Gab2, and a Gab1-PH–active SHP2 fusion was enough to activate MEK1 and ERK2 constitutively. Together these imply that SRC feeds ERK2 activation specifically through the GAB1–SHP2 step, which the SRC-side evidence only measured as bulk phospho-ERK rather than ERK2 kinase activity.
hypotheses.prediction: Depleting or inhibiting SRC should substantially reduce EGF-induced ERK2 kinase activity, and should also reduce EGF-induced Gab1–SHP2 association. Expressing the Gab1-PH–active SHP2 fusion should restore ERK2 activation in SRC-depleted cells. If ERK2 activity is unchanged by SRC loss, or the fusion fails to rescue it, the hypothesis is ruled out.
hypotheses.test: In T47D or HEK293 cells expressing HA-ERK2, knock down SRC by siRNA (with PP2 treatment as a parallel arm) and stimulate with EGF. Measure ERK2 activity by HA immunocomplex kinase assay with MBP as substrate, and measure Gab1 phosphorylation and Gab1–SHP2 co-immunoprecipitation by immunoblot. Repeat with co-expression of the Gab1-PH–active SHP2 fusion to test whether it bypasses the SRC requirement, confirming EGFR autophosphorylation is unchanged as a control.

citations.title: Regulation of the mitogen-activated protein kinase signaling pathway by SHP2.
Shp2 regulates SRC family kinase activity and Ras/Erk activation by controlling Csk recruitment.
EGFR-activated Src family kinases maintain GAB1-SHP2 complexes distal from EGFR.
Differential phosphorylation of the docking protein Gab1 by c-Src and the hepatocyte growth factor receptor regulates different aspects of cell functions.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the mechanism in words (Src requirement for EGF-induced Gab1 phosphorylation and ERK activation), the entities together (SRC + GAB1 + SHP2 + ERK2 + EGFR), and the prediction (whether a Gab1-PH–active SHP2 fusion bypasses a SRC requirement). The SRC→GAB1 half is published for EGFR (Furcht et al. show EGFR-activated SFKs phosphorylate GAB1 and sustain GAB1–SHP2 complexes), but the specific epistatic ordering and the rescue prediction have been directly tested with the opposite outcome: Cunnick et al. built the very Gab1PH-SHP2ΔN fusion invoked here and found its MEK1/ERK2 activation was itself blocked by an Src inhibitor and by Csk, that the fusion activated Src, and that it therefore acts at a step upstream of Src and Ras — so the fusion cannot bypass SRC loss. Zhang et al. independently place SFK activation downstream of SHP2 (via Csk/PAG), with impaired Erk activation in Shp2-deficient cells, reversing the proposed SRC→GAB1–SHP2→ERK2 direction; by the hypothesis's own stated falsification criterion this rules it out.

hypotheses.statement: S6K1 activity downstream of mTORC1 negatively regulates TNF-induced JNK activation, so that loss of S6K1 activity strengthens and prolongs JNK and c-Jun phosphorylation.
hypotheses.mechanism: Rapamycin suppresses IKK activity and constitutive RelA/p65 phosphorylation while also inhibiting S6K phosphorylation (dan2008:findings:017), which ties the mTORC1/S6K state to NF-kB output. Separately, TNF-induced JNK activation is stronger and more prolonged in cells lacking NF-kB activity, because NF-kB-induced gene products inhibit JNK activation (chen2002:findings:006). S6K1 already restrains another MAPK branch (ERK) through a feedback loop (carracedo2008:findings:005), and a rapamycin-resistant S6K1 mutant can separate S6K1-specific effects from other mTORC1 outputs (dibble2009:findings:013). The cited claims do not show that the IKK effect runs through S6K1 rather than another mTORC1 output; that is the inference under test.
hypotheses.prediction: S6K1 knockdown or rapamycin treatment should increase the amplitude and duration of TNF-induced phospho-JNK and phospho-c-Jun, alongside reduced IKK activity and RelA phosphorylation. Expressing rapamycin-resistant S6K1 should return JNK activation kinetics to control levels despite rapamycin. If the rapamycin-resistant S6K1 does not rescue, or S6K1 knockdown leaves JNK kinetics unchanged, the effect is not mediated by S6K1.
hypotheses.test: In a cultured cell line such as PC3 or HEK-293, run a TNF time course (0 to 4 h) under four conditions: control, S6K1 siRNA (with S6K2 siRNA as a specificity control), rapamycin, and rapamycin plus the rapamycin-resistant S6K1 mutant. Immunoblot for phospho-JNK, phospho-c-Jun, phospho-RelA/p65, phospho-IkBa and phospho-S6, and compare JNK activation magnitude and duration across conditions.

citations.title: Inhibition of p70 S6 kinase (S6K1) activity by A77 1726, the active metabolite of leflunomide, induces autophagy through TAK1-mediated AMPK and JNK activation.
Sustained activation of the JNK cascade and rapamycin-induced apoptosis are suppressed by p53/p21(Cip1).
Mammalian target of rapamycin inhibition in macrophages of asymptomatic HIV+ persons reverses the decrease in TLR-4-mediated TNF-α release through prolongation of MAPK pathway activation.
S6K1 deficiency protects against apoptosis in hepatocytes.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the mechanism in words (S6K1/mTORC1 as a negative regulator of JNK), the entities together (S6K1 + TNF + JNK + NF-kB/IKK), and the prediction (rapamycin or S6K1 knockdown increasing amplitude/duration of phospho-JNK and phospho-c-Jun). The core kinase relationship is already published: S6K1 knockdown or pharmacological S6K1 inhibition raises JNK and c-Jun phosphorylation (via TAK1), and mTOR inhibition has been reported to produce sustained JNK/phospho-c-Jun and enhanced, prolonged JNK1/2 phosphorylation in other stimulus contexts; an S6K1-deficient hepatocyte study also links S6K1 to JNK-dependent events downstream of TNF-R1. However, no retrieved source states the specific version under test — that S6K1 activity restrains TNF-induced JNK amplitude/duration, or that the rapamycin effect on IKK/RelA phosphorylation runs through S6K1 — and notably the S6K1-inhibitor paper reports rapamycin itself did not activate JNK, which weighs against the rapamycin arm of the prediction without directly testing it, so the status is partial rather than established or refuted.

hypotheses.statement: TGFBR1 kinase activity negatively regulates GSK3B through the p85/PI3K-AKT arm, so that TGF-β stimulation suppresses GSK3β-dependent phosphorylation of its substrates, including Smad3 Thr66.
hypotheses.mechanism: TGF-β activates AKT in a TβRI kinase-dependent manner, with p85 associating with TβRI upon ligand stimulation (derynck2019:findings:032). Independently, AKT is reported to inhibit GSK3β, stabilising GSK3β substrates such as PHLPP and prolonging NFAT nuclear residence (haeusler2018:findings:007, hogan2003:findings:006). GSK3β phosphorylates Smad3 at Thr66 to drive its turnover (guo2008:findings:018), so TβRI-driven AKT activation would be expected to lower GSK3β output on this site.
hypotheses.prediction: TGF-β treatment should reduce GSK3β-dependent Smad3 Thr66 phosphorylation and phosphorylation of other GSK3-motif sites. This reduction should be abolished by a TβRI kinase inhibitor or a PI3K/AKT inhibitor, and should be absent in cells expressing kinase-dead TβRI.
hypotheses.test: In HaCaT or HepG2 cells, stimulate with TGF-β with or without a TβRI kinase inhibitor, LY294002 or an AKT inhibitor. Immunoblot for Smad3 pT66, AKT phosphorylation and a GSK3 substrate readout such as PHLPP protein level, using SB-216763 as a positive control for GSK3β inhibition. Confirm by TGFBR1 knockdown and rescue with wild-type versus kinase-dead TβRI.

citations.title: Axin and GSK3- control Smad3 protein stability and modulate TGF- signaling.
Type I transforming growth factor beta receptor binds to and activates phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase.
Phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase function is required for transforming growth factor beta-mediated epithelial to mesenchymal transition and cell migration.
Chronic TGFβ stimulation promotes the metastatic potential of lung cancer cells by Snail protein stabilization through integrin β3-Akt-GSK3β signaling.

novelty.note: I searched for (i) GSK3-dependent Smad3 Thr66 phosphorylation and its regulation by TGF-β, (ii) TβRI/p85-PI3K-AKT activation and inhibitory phosphorylation of GSK3β, and (iii) TGF-β-driven stabilisation of GSK3 substrates. Each limb is published separately: TβRI binds and activates PI3K in a receptor-kinase-dependent way (PMID 15657037), TGF-β activates Akt with in vitro kinase activity toward GSK-3β in a PI3K-dependent manner (PMID 10969078), and chronic TGFβ raises Akt-mediated GSK3β Ser9 phosphorylation to stabilise the GSK3 substrate Snail (PMID 27015122, via integrin β3-FAK rather than TβRI-p85). The Smad3 paper reports that Thr66 phosphorylation diminishes on TGF-β treatment but attributes this to Smad3 dissociating from the Axin/GSK3-β complex, and only cites unpublished data that activated Akt lowers Thr66 phosphorylation GSK3β-dependently; so the specific TβRI-kinase/PI3K-AKT causation of reduced Thr66 phosphorylation is not stated in the published literature I retrieved, and nothing tested and refuted it.

hypotheses.statement: Activated TGFBR1 and the Axin–GSK3B complex compete for Smad3, such that TβRI kinase-dependent recruitment of Smad3 drives its release from GSK3β, while GSK3β limits the Smad3 pool available for TβRI-mediated activation.
hypotheses.mechanism: TGF-β causes Smad3 to be released from Axin and GSK3β without disturbing the β-catenin/Axin/GSK3β complex (guo2008:findings:009). Loss of GSK3β increases TGF-β-induced C-terminal Smad3 phosphorylation and Smad3-dependent reporter activity (guo2008:findings:016). Separately, Smad3 association with TβRI is competitive and limiting: p52ShcA and IRF-3 each reduce Smad3 recruitment to TβRI and its activation (derynck2019:findings:029, derynck2019:findings:041). Together these suggest Smad3 partitions between the receptor and the GSK3β complex.
hypotheses.prediction: Blocking TβRI kinase activity should prevent TGF-β-induced dissociation of Smad3 from GSK3β. Conversely, GSK3β knockdown or the Axin-displacing GID-5/6 peptide should increase the amount of Smad3 co-precipitating with TβRI after TGF-β stimulation.
hypotheses.test: In MG-132-treated HaCaT cells, co-immunoprecipitate endogenous Smad3 with GSK3β after TGF-β stimulation, with or without a TβRI kinase inhibitor or TGFBR1 knockdown. In the reciprocal experiment, co-immunoprecipitate Smad3 with TβRI in cells with GSK3β shRNA, SB-216763 or GID-5/6 expression, compared with controls.

citations.title: Axin facilitates Smad3 activation in the transforming growth factor beta signaling pathway.
Axin and GSK3- control Smad3 protein stability and modulate TGF- signaling.

novelty.note: I searched for the Axin/GSK3-β–Smad3 complex and TGF-β-induced release, for competition between TβRI and the Axin/GSK3-β complex for Smad3, and for the reciprocal prediction (GSK3 loss or Axin displacement changing Smad3 recruitment to TβRI). The Guo 2008 study (the corpus source) reports the TGF-β-dependent release and the GSK3-β-dependent limitation of the Smad3 pool but attributes it to Thr66 phosphorylation and proteasomal degradation rather than to competition for receptor binding, and explicitly does not test TβRI kinase dependence of the release. Furuhashi et al. independently show that Smad3 is phosphorylated by activated TβR-I and thereby dissociates from both TβR-I and Axin, with binding requiring receptor kinase activity — anticipating the first half of the prediction — but they report an Axin–Smad3–activated TβR-I ternary complex in which Axin facilitates rather than competes with receptor-mediated Smad3 activation, so the mutual-exclusivity framing and the reciprocal GSK3-β/GID-5/6 prediction remain unstated and untested.

hypotheses.statement: GTP-bound RAS activates mTORC2 kinase activity through PI3K.
hypotheses.mechanism: RAS binding is required for membrane recruitment and activation of p84/p110gamma PI3K complexes (balla2013:findings:034). Independently, insulin-stimulated mTORC2 kinase activity in RICTOR immunoprecipitates is partially blocked by pretreating cells with the PI3K inhibitor wortmannin (huang2008:findings:002), and constitutively active V12-H-Ras is sufficient to drive downstream signalling without upstream input (agazie2003:findings:003). Together these imply that active RAS, by engaging PI3K, could supply the PI3K-dependent input that raises mTORC2 activity.
hypotheses.prediction: Expressing V12-H-Ras in serum-starved cells should raise mTORC2 kinase activity in RICTOR immunoprecipitates (Akt-S473 phosphorylation of inactive Akt1 substrate) above vector control without growth factor. This increase should be abolished by wortmannin pretreatment or by a RAS effector-domain mutant unable to bind PI3K.
hypotheses.test: Transfect HEK293 or HeLa cells with vector, V12-H-Ras, or a PI3K-binding-deficient V12-H-Ras mutant, then serum-starve with or without wortmannin pretreatment. Immunoprecipitate RICTOR and run the in vitro mTORC2 kinase assay with inactive or kinase-dead Akt1 as substrate, immunoblotting for phospho-Akt S473. Confirm equal mTOR-RICTOR association, and confirm RAS activity by phospho-ERK1/2 blot.

citations.title: Evidence for direct activation of mTORC2 kinase activity by phosphatidylinositol 3,4,5-trisphosphate.
The Functional Proximal Proteome of Oncogenic Ras Includes mTORC2.

novelty.note: I searched three ways — the mechanism in words (Ras → PI3K → mTORC2 kinase activity), the entities together (V12/G12V H-Ras, Rictor, wortmannin/LY294002, Akt S473), and the prediction (Ras effector mutants defective in PI3K binding vs. mTORC2 activation). Gan et al. (JBC 2011) state and test exactly this explanation: constitutively active H-Ras (G12V) strongly induced Akt hydrophobic-motif (S473) phosphorylation and 'LY294002 almost completely blocked Ras-G12V-induced HM phosphorylation,' concluding that insulin and its downstream effector Ras stimulate Akt HM phosphorylation via PI3K, whose product PIP3 directly stimulates intrinsic mTORC2 kinase activity. Later work (Kovalski et al., Mol Cell 2019) shows GTP-bound Ras also binds mTORC2 directly and raises its activity in a PI3K-independent manner at the plasma membrane, which qualifies but does not negate the published PI3K-routed explanation, so the status is established rather than open or refuted.

hypotheses.statement: LPS activates SYK: LPS stimulation of TLR4 induces SYK tyrosine phosphorylation and recruits SYK to the phosphorylated TLR4 complex, where it contributes to LPS-induced NF-κB and ERK signalling and cytokine production.
hypotheses.mechanism: LPS signalling depends on tyrosine phosphorylation of the TLR4 TIR domain and recruits the SRC-family kinase LYN to TLR4, creating a phosphotyrosine-rich receptor complex (de2015:context:000, de2015:findings:010). SYK is activated when its SH2 domains engage phosphotyrosine motifs, and its SH2 domains are flexible enough to bind a broad range of tyrosine spacings (mcsai2010:findings:006, mcsai2010:findings:007). SYK also drives cytokine production through ERK and NF-κB, and it is required for the collaborative TNF response that integrates with the TLR/MyD88 pathway (mcsai2010:findings:019, dennehy2008:findings:004); these are the same outputs LPS induces (de2015:findings:004).
hypotheses.prediction: LPS treatment should rapidly increase SYK tyrosine phosphorylation and SYK co-precipitation with TLR4, and both should be reduced by SRC-family inhibition with PP2. SYK knockdown or pharmacological inhibition should reduce LPS-induced IKK/IκB and ERK phosphorylation and TNF secretion. If LPS does not act through SYK, SYK phosphorylation will not change and SYK loss will leave these LPS responses intact.
hypotheses.test: In a cultured macrophage line (e.g. RAW cells) or in A549 cells, stimulate with LPS over a time course and immunoblot for phosphorylated SYK. Immunoprecipitate TLR4 and blot for SYK, with and without PP2. Then knock down SYK by siRNA or apply a SYK inhibitor and measure LPS-induced phospho-IKK, phospho-IκB and phospho-ERK by Western blot, plus TNF by ELISA, against control cells.

citations.title: SCIMP is a transmembrane non-TIR TLR adaptor that promotes proinflammatory cytokine production from macrophages.
The transmembrane adapter SCIMP recruits tyrosine kinase Syk to phosphorylate Toll-like receptors to mediate selective inflammatory outputs.
TLR4 phosphorylation at tyrosine 672 activates the ERK/c-FOS signaling module for LPS-induced cytokine responses in macrophages.
Tyrosine kinase Syk associates with toll-like receptor 4 and regulates signaling in human monocytic cells.
The tyrosine kinase Syk differentially regulates Toll-like receptor signaling downstream of the adaptor molecules TRAF6 and TRAF3.

novelty.note: I searched for LPS/TLR4-induced SYK tyrosine phosphorylation and SYK recruitment to TLR4, for SYK requirement in LPS-induced NF-κB/ERK and TNF output, and for Src-family (Lyn/PP2) dependence of that recruitment. The explanation is already published as the Lyn–SCIMP–SYK axis on TLR4: LPS triggers Lyn-dependent tyrosine phosphorylation of the TLR4 TIR domain and the adaptor SCIMP, whose phospho-Y96/Y120 pair docks the tandem SYK SH2 domains, activating SYK, which then amplifies TLR4/SCIMP phosphorylation and drives LPS-induced ERK/c-FOS signalling and IL-6, IL-12p40 and TNF production; SYK was also shown much earlier to associate with TLR4 and undergo an early wave of tyrosine phosphorylation after LPS in monocytic cells. Hence established, though note the NF-κB/TNF arm specifically is contested rather than uniformly supported (e.g. Syk-deficient macrophages have been reported to show enhanced TRAF6/TAK1-dependent proinflammatory cytokine output, and piceatannol did not reduce LPS-induced TNF in THP-1 cells).

hypotheses.statement: MEK activity positively regulates mTORC1-dependent activating phosphorylation of S6K1 (RPS6KB1) downstream of EGF/PMA, acting through ERK-dependent Raptor phosphorylation rather than through altered Raptor–S6K1 binding.
hypotheses.mechanism: MEK inhibition with U0126 abrogates PMA-induced Raptor Ser696/Ser863 phosphorylation and reduces EGF-stimulated Raptor Ser863 phosphorylation. Raptor Ser863 phosphorylation follows a time course similar to S6K1 and S6 phosphorylation. The phospho-deficient Raptor S3A mutant still binds mTOR and S6K1 normally, so any MEK input to S6K1 would act on mTORC1 catalytic output toward S6K1, not on substrate recruitment.
hypotheses.prediction: In HEK293 cells stimulated with EGF or PMA, MEK inhibition (U0126 or PD0325901) should reduce S6K1 Thr389 phosphorylation and the S6K1-specific S6 Ser240/244 signal, in parallel with loss of Raptor Ser863 phosphorylation. Replacing wild-type Raptor with the S3A mutant should blunt EGF/PMA-induced S6K1 Thr389 phosphorylation and make the residual signal insensitive to MEK inhibition. If S6K1 Thr389 is unchanged by MEK inhibition or by S3A, the hypothesis is ruled out.
hypotheses.test: Serum-starve HEK293 cells, pretreat with or without a MEK inhibitor, and stimulate with EGF or PMA. Immunoblot phospho-S6K1 Thr389, phospho-S6 Ser240/244, phospho-Raptor Ser863 and phospho-ERK. Repeat in cells with endogenous Raptor knocked down and reconstituted with wild-type or S3A Raptor. Confirm with an in vitro mTORC1 kinase assay on recombinant S6K1, using Raptor immunoprecipitates from cells treated with or without MEK inhibitor.

citations.title: Co-ordinated activation of classical and novel PKC isoforms is required for PMA-induced mTORC1 activation.
TSC2/Rheb signaling mediates ERK-dependent regulation of mTORC1 activity in C2C12 myoblasts.
ERK1/2 phosphorylate Raptor to promote Ras-dependent activation of mTOR complex 1 (mTORC1).
Regulation of mTOR complex 1 (mTORC1) by raptor Ser863 and multisite phosphorylation.

novelty.note: I searched for ERK/MEK-dependent Raptor phosphorylation driving mTORC1 output, for MEK inhibition plus S6K1 Thr389/S6 Ser240/244 after EGF or PMA, and for direct tests of the Raptor phospho-site mutants on S6K1. The published Raptor work (ERK1/2 phosphorylating Ser8/Ser696/Ser863; Ser863 as a hierarchical switch) reports its functional readout on 4E-BP1, not S6K1 Thr389, whereas Liu et al. directly ran the predicted experiment in HEK293 cells — PMA stimulation with U0126 at a dose inhibiting ERK phosphorylation >70% — and report only minor effects on S6K Thr389, concluding MEK/ERK (and RSK) are largely dispensable for PMA-induced mTORC1 activation; the RSK inhibitor BI-D1870 likewise had no effect on S6K phosphorylation. Where MEK inhibition does partially lower PMA-induced S6K1 Thr389 (C2C12 myoblasts, 44% decrease), the authors attribute it to ERK-dependent TSC2 phosphorylation and Rheb, and explicitly call RSK-type input dispensable, so the Raptor-phosphorylation route to S6K1 is both contradicted in the stated system and displaced by an alternative mechanism elsewhere.

hypotheses.statement: EGFR activates mTORC1 through ERK1/2-dependent phosphorylation of Raptor.
hypotheses.mechanism: The claims about EGFR show that EGF stimulation induces ERK1/2 activation and that ERK pathway output decays when EGFR is inhibited. Independently, the claims about mTORC1 show that Ras/MAPK signalling activates it through RSK- and ERK1/2-mediated Raptor phosphorylation, that the phosphorylation-deficient Raptor S3A mutant lowers mTORC1 kinase activity, and that MEK1/2 inhibitors abolish that activity. Together these imply that EGFR kinase activity should drive mTORC1 activity through the ERK-Raptor route.
hypotheses.prediction: EGF stimulation should raise mTORC1 kinase activity and 4E-BP1 Thr37/Thr46 phosphorylation. That rise should be blocked by an EGFR inhibitor or a MEK1/2 inhibitor, and blunted in cells expressing Raptor S3A compared with wild-type Raptor.
hypotheses.test: Serum-starve HEK293 cells expressing wild-type or S3A Raptor and stimulate with EGF, with or without an EGFR kinase inhibitor (e.g. erlotinib) or a MEK1/2 inhibitor. Immunoblot for phospho-ERK1/2, phospho-4E-BP1 (Thr37/Thr46) and phospho-S6K1. Then run an in vitro kinase assay on Raptor immunoprecipitates using GST-4E-BP1 as substrate.

citations.title: ERK1/2 phosphorylate Raptor to promote Ras-dependent activation of mTOR complex 1 (mTORC1).
The Ras-ERK and PI3K-mTOR pathways: cross-talk and compensation.
Regulation of mTOR complex 1 (mTORC1) by raptor Ser863 and multisite phosphorylation.
Lysosomal EGFR acts as a Rheb-GEF independent of its kinase activity to activate mTORC1.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the plain-words mechanism (ERK-dependent Raptor phosphorylation driving mTORC1 after EGF), the entities together (EGFR/EGF + Raptor Ser8/Ser696/Ser863 + MEK inhibitor + 4E-BP1 Thr37/46), and the prediction (erlotinib/gefitinib or U0126 blocking EGF-induced mTORC1 activity, Raptor S3A). The ERK1/2-to-Raptor-to-mTORC1 arm is fully published, including MEK1/2-inhibitor sensitivity and reduced GST-4E-BP1 kinase activity with phospho-deficient Raptor, and reviews place this arm downstream of growth-factor receptors generally; Raptor multisite phosphorylation controlling mTORC1 activity toward 4E-BP1 is also published, though for insulin via PI3K/TSC/Rheb. What I did not find is a source stating the specific EGFR-kinase-to-ERK-to-Raptor route or testing EGF stimulation against Raptor S3A plus an EGFR inhibitor; the closest EGFR-specific work instead reports EGFR activating mTORC1 as a kinase-independent Rheb-GEF, with erlotinib leaving substantial mTORC1 activation, which complicates rather than directly refutes the ERK-Raptor prediction. Hence partial.

hypotheses.statement: S6K1 (RPS6KB1) negatively regulates MEK1 activation through a feedback loop, so that loss of S6K1 activity increases MEK1 activity toward ERK.
hypotheses.mechanism: Rapamycin-induced ERK activation is abrogated by the MEK1/2 inhibitor U0126 and by dominant-negative Ras, so it runs through Ras-Raf1-MEK1/2, and MEK1/2 are the kinases that phosphorylate the ERK activation loop. A rapamycin-insensitive constitutively active S6K1 reduces this rapamycin-mediated ERK activation. S6K is also reported to feed back to block IRS-1, with S6K1 phosphorylating IRS-1 S1101, which suggests S6K1 activity restrains the upstream input that activates MEK1.
hypotheses.prediction: S6K1 knockdown, like rapamycin, should increase activating phosphorylation of MEK1 and MEK1 kinase activity toward ERK. Constitutively active rapamycin-resistant S6K1 should blunt rapamycin-induced MEK1 activation. S6K2 knockdown should not reproduce the effect if it is specific to S6K1.
hypotheses.test: In MCF7 cells, knock down S6K1 or S6K2 by siRNA, or express the rapamycin-insensitive constitutively active S6K1, with or without rapamycin and insulin/IGF-1. Immunoblot for activation-loop phospho-MEK1 and phospho-ERK. Also immunoprecipitate MEK1 and measure its in vitro kinase activity toward recombinant inactive ERK2.

citations.title: S6K1 and 4E-BP1 Are Independent Regulated and Control Cellular Growth in Bladder Cancer
Dual PI3K/mTOR Inhibitors Induce Rapid Overactivation of the MEK/ERK Pathway in Human Pancreatic Cancer Cells through Suppression of mTORC2.

novelty.note: I searched for the mechanism in plain words (mTORC1/S6K1 negative feedback relieving inhibition of the Ras-Raf-MEK-ERK cascade), for the entities together (S6K1 + MEK1 + rapamycin + IRS-1), and for the prediction (S6K1 siRNA/knockout increasing MEK/ERK activating phosphorylation, plus S6K2 specificity). An independent study reports directly that silencing S6K1 increases Raf1/ERK1/2 phosphorylation and that PI3K-MAPK crosstalk is mediated indirectly by S6K1 activity, i.e. loss of S6K1 activity de-represses signalling through the Raf-MEK-ERK cascade — the same explanation as the hypothesis; the corpus paper itself already places this feedback on the Ras-Raf1-MEK1/2 route via S6K1-IRS-1. What I could not find published are the specific refinements (activation-loop phospho-MEK1 and immunoprecipitated MEK1 kinase activity toward ERK2 after S6K1 loss, and an S6K1-versus-S6K2 contrast); the nearest work that does assay MEK Ser217/221 after mTOR-pathway inhibition attributes the MEK/ERK over-activation to loss of mTORC2 rather than to S6K1, but it does not knock down S6K1 and therefore does not constitute a negative test of this claim.

hypotheses.statement: GRB2 and SHP2 co-assemble on the same EGF-activated EGFR as an EGFR-bridged complex, in which SHP2's phosphatase activity does not regulate GRB2 docking: SHP2 removes the RasGAP-binding pY992 while leaving GRB2 recruitment to the receptor intact.
hypotheses.mechanism: GRB2 was cloned as a binder of the tyrosine-autophosphorylated EGFR tail via its single SH2 domain, is recruited to EGFR at roughly 1:1 stoichiometry after EGF, and accounts for about 90% of SOS membrane recruitment in reconstitution. SHP2 also engages activated EGFR, but its substrate-trapping mutant singles out pY992 among five tail tyrosines. Neither WT nor C/S SHP2 changes SOS translocation to the plasma membrane, although SHP2 alters RasGAP translocation and Ras-GTP levels. Together these imply both proteins occupy the same receptor in separate arms, with GRB2-SOS recruitment spared by SHP2.
hypotheses.prediction: After EGF stimulation, GRB2 should co-precipitate with SHP2, most clearly with a substrate-trapping SHP2 mutant, and this should be lost with EGFR kinase inhibition or with Y992F-EGFR. The amount of GRB2 bound to EGFR, and GRB2 SH2 binding to EGFR in far-Western, should be the same in cells expressing vector, WT-, C/S- or R/E-SHP2, even though RasGAP SH2 binding differs. If SHP2 instead regulates GRB2 docking, GRB2-EGFR association would change with SHP2 catalytic status.
hypotheses.test: In COS-1 or NIH 3T3 cells expressing vector, WT-, C/S- or R/E-SHP2, with or without EGF, run three assays. (1) Immunoprecipitate SHP2 and immunoblot for GRB2 and EGFR, including an EGFR kinase inhibitor control and WT- versus Y992F-EGFR transfectants. (2) Immunoprecipitate EGFR and quantify co-precipitated GRB2 across the SHP2 variants. (3) Do GST-GRB2-SH2 pulldown and far-Western on EGFR from these cells, alongside GST-RasGAP-SH2 as a positive control for SHP2-dependent change.

citations.title: A new function for a phosphotyrosine phosphatase: linking GRB2-Sos to a receptor tyrosine kinase.
Multiple in vivo phosphorylated tyrosine phosphatase SHP-2 engages binding to Grb2 via tyrosine 584.
SIRPalpha1 receptors interfere with the EGFRvIII signalosome to inhibit glioblastoma cell transformation and migration.
A specific amino acid context in EGFR and HER2 phosphorylation sites enables selective binding to the active site of Src homology phosphatase 2 (SHP2).

novelty.note: I searched for a GRB2–SHP2 complex on activated EGFR, for SHP2 substrate selectivity at pY992 versus GRB2 docking sites, and for any test of whether SHP2 catalytic status alters GRB2–EGFR association (PubMed/Europe PMC keyword and title queries, plus the Agazie/Hayman primary and follow-up papers). Published work establishes the component parts separately: SHP2 selectively engages the acidic pY992/RasGAP context on EGFR, and GRB2–SHP2 complexes exist and co-precipitate with receptor signalosomes — but the published architecture is the reverse of the proposed one, with GRB2 bound to SHP2's own pY584 or bridging via GAB1 rather than the two being independently docked on one EGFR-bridged receptor. I found no source stating the EGFR-bridged two-arm arrangement, and none that tested and negated the specific prediction that GRB2–EGFR binding (co-IP and GRB2-SH2 far-Western) is unchanged across WT, C/S and R/E SHP2 while RasGAP-SH2 binding changes, so this is partial rather than established or refuted.

hypotheses.statement: LPS activates MTOR (mTORC1 kinase activity) via EGFR-dependent ERK and AKT/IKK signalling.
hypotheses.mechanism: LPS induces AKT, ERK and IKK/IκB phosphorylation in HME and A549 cells, and this requires EGFR expression and EGFR kinase activity. Independently, ERK1/2-dependent Raptor phosphorylation raises mTORC1 kinase activity toward 4E-BP1 and is abolished by MEK1/2 inhibitors, while mTOR activity is also promoted by an Akt-dependent IKKα–mTOR/Raptor interaction. LPS therefore turns on precisely the upstream inputs that the mTOR claims describe as positive regulators of mTORC1.
hypotheses.prediction: LPS should increase mTORC1 readouts (4E-BP1 Thr37/Thr46, S6K/S6 phosphorylation, Raptor Ser696/Ser863 phosphorylation) in these cells; the increase should be blocked by erlotinib or EGFR knockdown, reduced by MEK1/2 inhibition, and abolished by Torin1/rapamycin. No LPS-dependent change, or a change insensitive to EGFR and MEK blockade, would rule the hypothesis out.
hypotheses.test: Stimulate A549 or HME cells with an LPS time course, with or without erlotinib, PD184352, an AKT inhibitor, or Torin1, and after EGFR siRNA; immunoblot for phospho-4E-BP1 (Thr37/Thr46), phospho-S6K/S6 and phospho-Raptor (Ser696/Ser863), and in parallel immunoprecipitate Raptor for an in vitro mTOR kinase assay using GST-4E-BP1 as substrate.

citations.title: mTORC1-S6K Activation by Endotoxin Contributes to Cytokine Up-Regulation and Early Lethality in Animals
Activation of MTOR in pulmonary epithelium promotes LPS-induced acute lung injury.
Lysosomal EGFR acts as a Rheb-GEF independent of its kinase activity to activate mTORC1.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the mechanism in words (LPS/TLR4 turning on mTORC1 through EGFR-dependent ERK and AKT/IKK), the entities together (LPS + EGFR + mTORC1/Raptor/4E-BP1/S6K, erlotinib/EGFR knockdown), and the prediction (EGFR blockade reducing LPS-induced S6K/4E-BP1 phosphorylation). The two component halves are separately published: LPS does activate mTORC1-S6K, and full activation requires the PI3K/AKT and MEK/ERK inputs acting together (PLoS ONE 2010), while LPS-induced MTOR activation in bronchial/alveolar epithelium is documented as TLR4/MYD88-dependent with no EGFR involvement examined (Autophagy 2016); the LPS→EGFR→ERK/AKT arm is only reported up to NF-κB, never carried to mTORC1 readouts or Raptor Ser696/Ser863. No source states the joined claim, and none directly tested and rejected it, so this is partial rather than established or refuted; the nearest caution is a 2025 report that EGFR-driven mTORC1 activation is largely insensitive to erlotinib because EGFR acts as a kinase-independent Rheb-GEF, which bears on the erlotinib arm of the prediction without testing LPS.

hypotheses.statement: Tyrosine-phosphorylated IRS1 acts as an allosteric activator of SHP2 that promotes dephosphorylation of EGFR at pY992, reducing RasGAP recruitment to EGFR.
hypotheses.mechanism: Bis-phosphorylated IRS-1 peptide activates recombinant SHP2 with sub-micromolar AC50 in biochemical assays, and this activation is the input that SHP099 competes with (chen2016:findings:005, chen2016:findings:007, chen2016:findings:019). Independently, SHP2 selectively dephosphorylates EGFR pY992, the same residue that serves as the RasGAP SH2 binding site, so blocking SHP2 catalysis increases RasGAP-EGFR association (agazie2003:findings:012, agazie2003:findings:013, agazie2003:findings:011). Because insulin but not EGF generates tyrosine-phosphorylated IRS1 in the same cells where insulin amplifies EGF-driven Ras/ERK output (borisov2009:findings:006), IRS1 phosphotyrosine is positioned to act directly on EGFR pY992 status through SHP2.
hypotheses.prediction: Insulin co-stimulation, or introduction of a bis-tyrosine-phosphorylated IRS1 peptide into cells or lysates, should selectively lower EGF-induced EGFR pY992 and reduce GST-SH2-RasGAP pulldown of EGFR without changing pY1068, pY1086, pY1148 or pY1173; IRS1 depletion should abolish this site-selective loss, and Y992F-EGFR should be insensitive.
hypotheses.test: In a cell-free reconstitution, incubate immunopurified EGF-stimulated EGFR (wild type versus Y992F) with recombinant SHP2 (residues 1–525) plus increasing concentrations of bis-phosphorylated versus non-phosphorylated IRS1 peptide, and quantify site-specific pY992 loss by immunoblot alongside GST-SH2-RasGAP far-Western binding; in parallel, treat EGF-stimulated cells with or without insulin, with and without IRS1 siRNA and with or without an allosteric SHP2 inhibitor, and measure EGFR pY992 versus other EGFR phosphosites and RasGAP-SH2 affinity precipitation of EGFR.

citations.title: Systems-level interactions between insulin-EGF networks amplify mitogenic signaling.
Activation of the SH2-containing protein tyrosine phosphatase, SH-PTP2, by phosphotyrosine-containing peptides derived from insulin receptor substrate-1.
Molecular mechanism for a role of SHP2 in epidermal growth factor receptor signaling.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the SHP2→EGFR pY992→RasGAP mechanism, IRS-1 bisphosphotyrosyl peptide allosteric activation of SHP2, and the insulin/EGF crosstalk prediction (plus a targeted search for any direct test of insulin lowering EGFR pY992). Each link is separately published — Sugimoto et al. showed IRS-1 bis-pTyr peptides allosterically activate SHP2 up to 50-fold, Agazie & Hayman identified EGFR Y992 as the SHP2 substrate whose dephosphorylation blocks RasGAP membrane recruitment, and Borisov et al. (retrieved full text) explicitly models SHP2 bound to phosphorylated GAB1/IRS causing 'dephosphorylation of the docking sites on EGFR, IR, GAB1, and IRS, which are involved in RasGAP binding' as the basis of insulin amplification of EGF-driven ERK. However, Borisov names no residue (Y992 appears nowhere in that text), treats SHP2 recruitment rather than IRS1-driven allosteric activation, and the site-selective prediction (insulin/IRS1-dependent loss of EGFR pY992 with other sites unchanged, reduced RasGAP-SH2 pulldown, Y992F insensitivity) is neither stated nor tested anywhere I found; I found no negative report either.

hypotheses.statement: JNK1 is a required positive signalling component for CBM (CARD–BCL10–MALT1) complex-driven cytokine production in innate immune cells.
hypotheses.mechanism: mcsai2010:findings:019 states that C-type lectin receptor ligation induces chemokine and cytokine production through a CARD9–BCL10–MALT1 module acting on ERK, NFAT and NF-κB, while li2019:findings:021 shows that a homologous CBM complex containing CARD14, Bcl10 and MALT1 is required not only for NF-κB but also for JNK1/2 and p38 activation downstream of receptor engagement. If CBM complexes couple receptor ligation to JNK1 activation, then the cytokine output attributed to these complexes should depend in part on JNK1 itself rather than on NF-κB alone.
hypotheses.prediction: Loss or inhibition of JNK1 in macrophages or keratinocytes should reduce receptor-induced TNF/IL-6 output (and the corresponding transcripts) upon CBM-coupled stimulation, without abolishing proximal NF-κB IκBα degradation, and the JNK1 dependence should be lost in BCL10- or MALT1-deficient cells where the upstream complex is already broken.
hypotheses.test: In cultured macrophages (or a macrophage line) knock down/knock out JNK1 with siRNA or CRISPR, or use a selective JNK inhibitor, then stimulate with β-glucan plus a sub-stimulatory TLR2 ligand and measure TNF/IL-6 by ELISA and qRT-PCR alongside immunoblots for phospho-JNK, phospho-c-Jun and IκBα; repeat in BCL10- or MALT1-depleted cells to test epistasis, and confirm receptor-induced JNK1 activation is CBM-dependent by co-immunoprecipitating BCL10/MALT1 after stimulation.

citations.title: JNK1 negatively controls antifungal innate immunity by suppressing CD23 expression.
The CARMA1-Bcl10 signaling complex selectively regulates JNK2 kinase in the T cell receptor-signaling pathway.
The paracaspase MALT1 mediates CARD14-induced signaling in keratinocytes.
c-Jun N-terminal kinase 1 is required for Toll-like receptor 1 gene expression in macrophages.

novelty.note: I searched for CBM/CARD9-BCL10-MALT1 coupling to JNK, for JNK1-isoform-specific requirements in macrophage/keratinocyte cytokine output, and for the prediction itself (JNK1 loss reducing β-glucan/Dectin-1-induced TNF/IL-6). The CBM-to-JNK arm is published (Afonina et al. show CARD14-induced JNK activation is MALT1-dependent and that MALT1 loss blocks cytokine/chemokine expression in keratinocytes), but the JNK1-specific positive requirement has been directly tested and fails: Zhao et al. show Dectin-1-dependent JNK phosphorylation in BMDMs yet report no significant change in pro-inflammatory cytokines in JNK1-KO versus WT mice or in JNK1-KO BMDMs stimulated with C. albicans, and JNK1 acts as a negative rather than positive regulator of antifungal innate immunity; Blonska et al. provide genetic evidence that the Bcl10-containing CBM selectively assembles and activates JNK2, not JNK1. Caveat: Zhao et al. used whole Candida rather than the proposed β-glucan plus sub-stimulatory Pam3CSK4 combination and did not perform BCL10/MALT1 epistasis, and JNK1 does have positive roles in other macrophage TLR responses (Wang et al., TLR1 expression), so the failure is of the stated JNK1-dependence of CBM-coupled cytokine output rather than of all JNK1 involvement in innate signalling.

hypotheses.statement: EGFR directly phosphorylates and activates STAT1, docking it via its SH2 domain at a receptor phosphotyrosine site.
hypotheses.mechanism: EGF stimulation produces tyrosine-phosphorylated Stat1 and Stat1-reactive SIE/GAS bandshift complexes, and Stat1 activation requires pTyr701 plus SH2-mediated dimerization (darnell1994:findings:022, darnell1994:findings:015), while STAT1 recruitment elsewhere occurs at defined receptor pY motifs (heinrich2003:findings:006). Activated EGFR presents discrete phosphotyrosines that bind SH2 domains directly and site-specifically (agazie2003:findings:011, agazie2003:findings:013), making EGFR a plausible direct docking site and upstream kinase for STAT1.
hypotheses.prediction: EGF-induced STAT1 pTyr701 and STAT1-containing GAS/SIE complexes should require EGFR kinase activity, and a GST-STAT1-SH2 probe should capture phosphorylated EGFR only after EGF, with binding abolished by an SH2-inactivating STAT1 mutation.
hypotheses.test: In HeLa or fibroblast cultures, compare EGF-stimulated cells with and without an EGFR kinase inhibitor or EGFR siRNA by phospho-Tyr701 STAT1 immunoblot and Stat1-supershifted GAS gel shift; in parallel perform far-Western and pulldown with GST-STAT1-SH2 (wild type versus SH2 point mutant) against lysates of cells expressing wild-type or single Tyr-to-Phe EGFR constructs, plus reciprocal EGFR/STAT1 co-immunoprecipitation.

citations.title: Transcription factor p91 interacts with the epidermal growth factor receptor and mediates activation of the c-fos gene promoter.
EGF receptor deletions define a region specifically mediating STAT transcription factor activation.
STAT activation by epidermal growth factor (EGF) and amphiregulin. Requirement for the EGF receptor kinase but not for tyrosine phosphorylation sites or JAK1.

novelty.note: I searched for EGF-induced STAT1 tyrosine phosphorylation, direct EGFR–STAT1 SH2 docking, and the requirement of specific EGFR autophosphorylation sites for STAT activation (PubMed via E-utilities plus web search). Fu & Zhang (Cell 1993) report exactly this explanation: EGF causes rapid tyrosine phosphorylation and nuclear translocation of p91/STAT1, which binds the EGF receptor directly and ligand-dependently through its SH2 domain and is required for the EGF-induced SIE complex on the c-fos promoter; a BBRC 1995 receptor-deletion study further maps STAT activation to the receptor phosphotyrosines Y1068/Y1086 (YXXQ), i.e. site-specific docking. The specific prediction is therefore already published, although David et al. (JBC 1996) directly tested the docking requirement and found EGF/amphiregulin-induced STAT1 activation needs receptor kinase activity but not the receptor autophosphorylation sites (nor JAK1), so the Tyr-to-Phe arm of the prediction is contested rather than supported.

hypotheses.statement: P38 activates MTORC1 indirectly: stress-stimulated p38 signalling through MK2/3 activates RSK, which phosphorylates Raptor and raises mTORC1 kinase activity independently of ERK1/2.
hypotheses.mechanism: On the p38 side, MK2 activation depends entirely on p38-alpha, and MK2/3 phosphorylate RSK Ser380 in certain cell types, which may explain how p38-stimulating stresses activate RSK. On the mTORC1 side, RSK phosphorylates Raptor on Ser719/721/722, and this is required for activation of mTORC1 in vitro kinase activity. Together these independent claims imply a p38 -> MK2/3 -> RSK -> Raptor route by which p38 could positively regulate mTORC1.
hypotheses.prediction: With MEK1/2 inhibited, a p38-activating stress should increase RSK Ser380 phosphorylation, Raptor Ser719/721/722 phosphorylation and mTORC1 output (S6K1 and 4E-BP1 Thr37/46 phosphorylation, Raptor-associated mTOR kinase activity). These increases should be lost on p38 inhibition (SB203580) or p38-alpha/MK2 knockdown, on RSK inhibition, and in cells expressing a Raptor Ser719/721/722-to-alanine mutant.
hypotheses.test: In HEK293 cells pretreated with a MEK1/2 inhibitor, stimulate p38 with anisomycin or arsenite, with or without SB203580, p38-alpha or MK2 siRNA, or an RSK inhibitor. Immunoblot for phospho-MK2, phospho-RSK Ser380, phospho-Raptor (RSK sites), phospho-S6K1 and phospho-4E-BP1. Then immunoprecipitate wild-type or Ser719/721/722Ala Raptor and run an in vitro mTOR kinase assay with GST-4E-BP1 as substrate. If mTORC1 activity does not rise in a p38-dependent, RSK-site-dependent way, the hypothesis is ruled out.

citations.title: The PI3K and MAPK/p38 pathways control stress granule assembly in a hierarchical manner.
Cellular stress induces non-canonical activation of the receptor tyrosine kinase EphA2 through the p38-MK2-RSK signaling pathway.
Phosphorylation of Raptor by p38beta participates in arsenite-induced mammalian target of rapamycin complex 1 (mTORC1) activation.
A role for p38 stress-activated protein kinase in regulation of cell growth via TORC1.

novelty.note: I searched for the p38→MK2/3→RSK Ser380 leg, for RSK-mediated Raptor Ser719/721/722 phosphorylation, and for stress (anisomycin/arsenite) activation of mTORC1 output under MEK inhibition. The upstream leg is published (JBC 2023 shows stress-activated p38-MK2 phosphorylates RSK1 Ser380/RSK2 Ser386 independently of ERK, using anisomycin and osmotic stress, but only to phosphorylate EphA2 — raptor, mTORC1, S6K and 4E-BP1 are never mentioned), and p38 is indeed established as a positive mTORC1 regulator. However, Heberle et al. directly tested the MK2 requirement in arsenite-stressed cells with the MK2 inhibitor PF3644022 and report that MK2 inhibition did not reduce p70-S6K-pT389, concluding mTORC1 activation by p38 is MK2-independent; complementary work attributes arsenite-induced mTORC1 activation largely to direct p38β phosphorylation of raptor on Ser863/Ser771 rather than the RSK sites, and Cully et al. found anisomycin-driven TORC1 activation does not go through raptor Ser863 but acts at the Rag GTPases. The required MK2 step of this specific route therefore has a stated negative test.

hypotheses.statement: RSK1 (RPS6KA1) directly phosphorylates RICTOR on Thr1135, acting as an ERK-pathway-driven kinase for the same AGC-motif site targeted by S6K1.
hypotheses.mechanism: Rictor-T1135 lies in an AGC/RXRXXS-T motif recognized by the phospho-Akt substrate antibody and is directly phosphorylated by S6K1 in vitro (dibble2009:findings:005, dibble2009:findings:012); RSK1 has the matching minimum consensus Arg/Lys-Xaa-Arg-Xaa-Xaa-pSer/Thr (cargnello2011:findings:027) and is already documented to converge on other S6K1 substrates, phosphorylating IRS-1 Ser-1101 (smadjalamre2013:findings:002) and rpS6 Ser235/236 (cargnello2011:findings:034). Because S6K1 knockdown leaves residual basal T1135 phosphorylation and RSK1 loss raises Akt Ser-473 much as Rictor-T1135A does (dibble2009:findings:017, smadjalamre2013:findings:009), RSK1 is a plausible second, MEK-dependent input to this site.
hypotheses.prediction: Immunoprecipitated active RSK1 will phosphorylate recombinant Rictor on Thr1135 in vitro, with no signal on a T1135A substrate or with kinase-dead RSK1; in cells, PMA or serum should raise phospho-Rictor-T1135 in a BI-D1870- and U0126-sensitive, rapamycin-partially-resistant manner, and RSK1 knockdown or dominant-negative RSK1 should lower basal and mitogen-stimulated T1135 phosphorylation while sparing S6K1-dependent S6 Ser240/244.
hypotheses.test: Perform an in vitro phosphotransferase assay with HA-RSK1 (wild-type or kinase-dead) immunoprecipitated from PMA-stimulated HEK-293 cells against immunoprecipitated myc-Rictor wild-type versus T1135A, blotting with the phospho-Rictor(T1135) antibody; in parallel, treat HEK-293 or L6 cells with BI-D1870 or RSK1 siRNA plus PMA/insulin and immunoblot phospho-Rictor-T1135 against phospho-S6K1 controls.

citations.title: mTORC1-activated S6K1 phosphorylates Rictor on threonine 1135 and regulates mTORC2 signaling.
Characterization of Rictor phosphorylation sites reveals direct regulation of mTOR complex 2 by S6K1.

novelty.note: I searched for RSK/RPS6KA1 as a Rictor Thr1135 kinase, for the entity pair (Rictor T1135 + p90 RSK / ERK / PMA / U0126 / BI-D1870), for ERK-driven Rictor phosphorylation in BRAF-mutant settings, and for unbiased RSK substrate screens; no retrieved source assigns Thr1135 (or any Rictor site) to RSK1, and the RSK analog-sensitive substrate screens surfaced report other substrates (RanBP3, PDCD4, IRS2, TRIM33, SORBS2). The closest published work is Julien et al., which shows PMA/Ras-ERK stimulation of Rictor-T1135 that is blocked by U0126 but also by rapamycin and attributable to mTORC1-activated S6K1, and Dibble et al., which reports S6K1 (not S6K2) siRNA robustly reducing basal and stimulated T1135 phosphorylation while leaving RSK levels unaffected. Since neither paper directly assayed RSK1 against Rictor or reported a stated negative for that pairing, the claim is untested rather than refuted, though the complete rapamycin sensitivity of PMA-induced T1135 phosphorylation is indirect evidence against an mTORC1-independent RSK input.

hypotheses.statement: PTEN positively regulates GSK3B activity: PTEN's lipid phosphatase activity relieves AKT-mediated inhibition of GSK3β, so PTEN loss functionally suppresses GSK3β.
hypotheses.mechanism: Claims about GSK3B state that AKT inhibits GSK3/GSK3β, with consequences for its substrates (PHLPP stabilisation, prolonged NFAT nuclear residence). Independent claims about PTEN state that PTEN, but not catalytically inactive PTEN-CS, reduces AKT-dependent phosphorylation of TSC2 just as the PI3K inhibitor LY294002 does, that PTEN loss elevates PI3K signalling, and that a lipid-phosphatase-dead mutant (G129E) exists. Together these imply that PTEN's lipid phosphatase activity sets the level of AKT-imposed inhibition on GSK3β, making PTEN an upstream activator of GSK3β.
hypotheses.prediction: Re-expressing wild-type PTEN in PTEN-null cells should lower AKT-dependent inhibitory phosphorylation of GSK3β and raise GSK3β output (more Smad3 Thr66 phosphorylation, less PHLPP protein). Lipid-phosphatase-dead PTEN (G129E or PTEN-CS) should not do this. Co-expressing active AKT should reverse the effect of wild-type PTEN, and the GSK3 inhibitor SB-216763 should abolish the downstream substrate changes.
hypotheses.test: Transfect PTEN-null PC3 cells with wild-type PTEN, PTEN-G129E or PTEN-CS, with or without active AKT, and with or without SB-216763. Immunoblot for AKT-site inhibitory phospho-GSK3β, total GSK3β, Smad3 pThr66 and PHLPP protein. As the converse, knock down PTEN by shRNA in PTEN-intact cells (e.g. HaCaT or HEK293) and check that the same readouts shift the opposite way and are reversed by LY294002.

citations.title: AKT activation because of PTEN loss upregulates xCT via GSK3β/NRF2, leading to inhibition of ferroptosis in PTEN-mutant tumor cells.
GSK3-CRMP2 signaling mediates axonal regeneration induced by Pten knockout.
PTEN and GSK3beta: key regulators of progression to androgen-independent prostate cancer.
beta-TrCP-mediated ubiquitination and degradation of PHLPP1 are negatively regulated by Akt.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the mechanism in plain words (PTEN loss → AKT → inhibitory Ser9 phosphorylation of GSK3β), the entities together (PTEN + GSK3β + lipid phosphatase/G129E), and the downstream predictions (PHLPP stability, GSK3 substrate output). The core explanation is explicitly published: Cell Reports 2023 (PMID 37210723) states that AKT activation caused by PTEN loss inhibits GSK3β, driving NRF2/xCT output, and a Pten-knockout study (PMID 31453382) shows Pten deletion abrogates GSK3 inhibitory activity on its substrate CRMP2, while an Oncogene review (PMID 16421604) frames PTEN loss as promoting Ser9 phospho-inhibition of GSK3β in prostate cancer; the PHLPP arm of the prediction is separately published as Akt suppressing GSK3β-dependent PHLPP1 degradation (PMID 19797085). Nothing found reports a negative test, and the only unpublished specifics are the particular readout panel (Smad3 Thr66) and the explicit lipid-phosphatase-dead PTEN comparison, so the explanation itself counts as established.

hypotheses.statement: SYK acts upstream of and activates MAPK signalling, with SYK-dependent tyrosine phosphorylation of PKCβI as the proposed link to the PKC→Raf→MAPK cascade.
hypotheses.mechanism: SYK is required for PKCβI tyrosine phosphorylation in mast cells and directly phosphorylates the PKCβI C-terminal Y662 once S661 is phosphorylated. SYK signalling downstream of Dectin-1 is also reported to induce cytokine production via ERK. Independently, the kinetic model places PKC upstream of MAPK through Raf, with a PKC–MAPK positive feedback loop that gives threshold-dependent, sustained MAPK activity. Taken together, SYK modification of PKC would feed into MAPK activation.
hypotheses.prediction: Loss of SYK should markedly reduce receptor-stimulated MAPK (ERK) activation-loop phosphorylation, and re-expression of SYK should restore it. If PKCβI is the link, a PKC inhibitor or a non-phosphorylatable PKCβI Y662F mutant should blunt MAPK activation even when SYK is present. If SYK acts through another route, MAPK activation will be SYK-dependent but unaffected by Y662F.
hypotheses.test: Stimulate wild-type, Syk-deficient and syk-reconstituted RBL-2H3 mast cells through FcεRI and measure phospho-ERK (Thr202/Tyr204) by western blot over a time course. Repeat with a PKC inhibitor and in cells expressing wild-type versus Y662F PKCβI, confirming PKCβI tyrosine phosphorylation by immunoprecipitation and anti-phosphotyrosine blot in parallel.

citations.title: A Ras activation pathway dependent on Syk phosphorylation of protein kinase C.
A requirement for Syk in the activation of the microtubule-associated protein kinase/phospholipase A2 pathway by Fc epsilon R1 is not shared by a G protein-coupled receptor.
Regulation and function of syk tyrosine kinase in mast cell signaling and beyond.

novelty.note: I searched the mechanism (Syk phosphorylation of PKCβI Y662 leading to Ras/ERK), the entities (Syk-deficient RBL-2H3, FcεRI, MAP kinase) and the prediction (Y662F mutant or PKC inhibitor blunting ERK). Kawakami et al. 2003, which is the corpus source paper itself, already states and tests this: Syk phosphorylates PKCβI Y662, the Y662F mutant fails to restore FcεRI-induced ERK activation in PKCβ-/- cells, and the PKC inhibitor Gö 6976 reduces Ras activation and ERK phosphorylation. The published link runs through Grb2/Sos recruitment to Ras rather than a direct PKC→Raf step. Hirasawa et al. 1995 had earlier shown, by manipulating Syk expression in RBL-2H3 cells, that FcεRI-driven MAP kinase activation requires Syk.

hypotheses.statement: RSK1 positively regulates proteasomal degradation of its substrate IRS-1, with RSK1-dependent phosphorylation of IRS-1 Ser-1101 acting as a signal that marks IRS-1 for degradation.
hypotheses.mechanism: The catabolic-process claims describe kinase phosphorylation as a recurring trigger for substrate degradation: GSK-3β phosphorylation of primed β-catenin drives its complete degradation, and Cdk phosphorylation of Sic1 drives its destruction, with the 26S proteasome accounting for most protein degradation in growing mammalian cells. Independently, RSK1 directly phosphorylates IRS-1 on Ser-1101, and dominant-negative RSK1 blocks insulin-induced Ser-1101 phosphorylation while increasing p85 association with IRS-1 and Akt Ser-473 phosphorylation. If Ser-1101 phosphorylation works as a degradation signal in the same way, RSK1's negative effect on IRS-1 signalling would be partly due to faster proteasomal turnover of IRS-1; the cited claims do not themselves report IRS-1 degradation.
hypotheses.prediction: Inhibiting RSK1 (BI-D1870 or dominant-negative RSK1) should lengthen the half-life of IRS-1 protein in insulin- or PMA-stimulated cells, and an IRS-1 S1101A mutant should be more stable than wild-type. Proteasome inhibition should abolish the stability difference between RSK1-active and RSK1-inhibited conditions. If RSK1 acts only on IRS-1 signalling and not on its turnover, IRS-1 half-life and ubiquitination will be unchanged by RSK1 manipulation.
