hypotheses.test: In L6 myocytes or HEK293 cells, run cycloheximide-chase immunoblots of IRS-1 (wild-type versus S1101A) after insulin or PMA stimulation. Compare control cells, cells treated with BI-D1870, cells expressing RSK1-DN and cells expressing constitutively active myrRSK1, each with and without a proteasome inhibitor. In parallel, immunoprecipitate IRS-1 and blot for ubiquitin to see whether RSK1 activity and Ser-1101 phosphorylation increase IRS-1 ubiquitination.

citations.title: Identification of IRS-1 Ser-1101 as a target of S6K1 in nutrient- and obesity-induced insulin resistance.
The CUL7 E3 ubiquitin ligase targets insulin receptor substrate 1 for ubiquitin-dependent degradation.
A novel domain mediates insulin-induced proteasomal degradation of insulin receptor substrate 1 (IRS-1).
Insulin activates RSK (p90 ribosomal S6 kinase) to trigger a new negative feedback loop that regulates insulin signaling for glucose metabolism.

novelty.note: I searched for RSK1/RSK and IRS-1 Ser-1101 together, for Ser-1101 as a degradation signal, and for kinase-phosphorylation-driven IRS-1 ubiquitination/proteasomal turnover (PubMed/eutils, PNAS, JBC, PMC). Phospho-dependent proteasomal degradation of IRS-1 is well established in general — insulin-stimulated Ser/Thr phosphorylation of a distinct degradation domain (aa 386–430) and CUL7/FBXW8-mediated ubiquitination that depends on mTOR and p70S6K activity — and Ser-1101 is documented as an inhibitory site targeted by S6K1 (and PKCθ), but no retrieved source links RSK1 activity or Ser-1101 phosphorylation to IRS-1 half-life, stability or ubiquitination, and the RSK paper itself reports only signalling effects. Because the general mechanism is published while this specific kinase–degron connection and prediction are not, and no source reports a direct negative test of it, the status is partial.

hypotheses.statement: TNF stimulation negatively regulates GSK3B activity through Akt, placing GSK3B as a downstream target of TNF signaling.
hypotheses.mechanism: Prior work summarised in the corpus places Akt downstream of TNF, although the specific finding that Akt directly phosphorylates IKKβ was later challenged. Independently, Akt is reported to inhibit GSK3β after insulin (stabilising the GSK3β substrate PHLPP) and after CD28 costimulation (prolonging NFAT nuclear residence). If TNF does activate Akt, the same Akt-to-GSK3β inhibition should follow, reducing GSK3β-dependent substrate phosphorylation such as Smad3 Thr66.
hypotheses.prediction: Acute TNF treatment of cultured cells should lower GSK3β activity, seen as reduced Smad3 Thr66 phosphorylation and increased PHLPP protein stability. This effect should be abolished by the PI3K inhibitor LY294002, which blocks Akt phosphorylation, and should be absent in GSK3β-null cells.
hypotheses.test: Treat cultured cells (e.g. HaCaT cells or wild-type versus GSK3β-/- MEFs) with a TNF time course, with or without LY294002 pretreatment. Immunoblot for Akt phosphorylation, GSK3β-dependent Smad3 pThr66, and PHLPP levels under cycloheximide chase. Use the GSK3 inhibitor SB-216763 as a positive control for loss of GSK3β activity. No change in these GSK3β readouts after TNF, despite NF-κB activation, would rule the hypothesis out.

citations.title: TNF-α induces epithelial-mesenchymal transition of renal cell carcinoma cells via a GSK3β-dependent mechanism.
TRAF6-mediated regulation of the PI3 kinase (PI3K)-Akt-GSK3beta cascade is required for TNF-induced cell survival.
Vascular cell adhesion molecule-1 expression in human intestinal microvascular endothelial cells is regulated by PI 3-kinase/Akt/MAPK/NF-kappaB: inhibitory role of curcumin.

novelty.note: I searched the mechanism (TNF → PI3K/Akt → GSK3β Ser9 phosphorylation), the entity combination with LY294002, and the specific readouts (Smad3 Thr66, PHLPP stability). Several primary papers already report that TNF inhibits GSK3β through PI3K/Akt-mediated Ser9 phosphorylation and that LY294002 reverses this, in renal carcinoma cells, intestinal endothelial cells and 3T3 cells, so the core explanation is published. No source was found testing the Smad3 Thr66 or PHLPP-stability readouts after TNF, and no negative test of the claim was found.

hypotheses.statement: JAK1 acts upstream of ERK, such that JAK1 kinase activity promotes ERK1/2 activation through a SHP2-dependent step located at or above Ras.
hypotheses.mechanism: Cell lines with JAK1 alterations are sensitive to SHP099 whereas RAS- or BRAF-mutated lines are resistant (chen2016:findings:012). The same pattern holds for ERK: catalytically impaired SHP2 cuts short ERK1/2 activation but cannot block ERK1/2 activation by constitutively active V12-H-Ras (agazie2003:findings:002, agazie2003:findings:003). This implies JAK1-driven signalling feeds into the SHP2-dependent, Ras-upstream route that sustains ERK. It rests on the assumption that SHP099 sensitivity reflects SHP2 dependence, which the cited claim does not state. JAK1 is also required for IL-6 signal transduction through gp130 (heinrich2003:findings:022), which gives a defined stimulus for probing this.
hypotheses.prediction: Cytokine-induced ERK1/2 phosphorylation (e.g. by IL-6) will be reduced in amplitude and/or duration in JAK1-deficient cells compared with the same cells re-expressing JAK1. Expression of constitutively active V12-H-Ras will restore ERK1/2 phosphorylation regardless of JAK1 status. Phosphatase-impaired SHP2 (C/S or R/E) will blunt the JAK1-dependent ERK1/2 response in JAK1-reconstituted cells.
hypotheses.test: Use JAK1-deficient human cells (e.g. U4A) and the same cells complemented with JAK1 cDNA. Stimulate with IL-6 (or IFN) over a 0-60 min time course and immunoblot for phospho-ERK1/2 and total ERK1/2. Repeat with co-expression of V12-H-Ras, and with C/S- or R/E-SHP2 in the reconstituted cells. If phospho-ERK1/2 does not differ between JAK1-null and reconstituted cells, the hypothesis is ruled out. If the difference is there but V12-H-Ras does not bypass it, JAK1 does not act above Ras.

citations.title: Beta interferon and oncostatin M activate Raf-1 and mitogen-activated protein kinase through a JAK1-dependent pathway.
Activation of the protein tyrosine phosphatase SHP2 via the interleukin-6 signal transducing receptor protein gp130 requires tyrosine kinase Jak1 and limits acute-phase protein expression.
Dual signaling role of the protein tyrosine phosphatase SHP-2 in regulating expression of acute-phase plasma proteins by interleukin-6 cytokine receptors in hepatic cells.

novelty.note: I searched for JAK1-dependent ERK/MAPK activation, for the JAK1–SHP2–Ras link in IL-6/gp130 signalling, and for the proposed experiment itself (JAK1-deficient U4A cells reconstituted with JAK1, cytokine-induced ERK, Ras epistasis). Stancato et al. performed essentially this experiment: JAK1-deficient U4A (and JAK1-null HeLa) cells showed no Raf-1/MAPK activation by IFN-beta or oncostatin M, activation was restored on re-expressing JAK1, and OSM-driven Raf-1 activation tracked with Ras-GTP loading (placing the JAK1-dependent input at or above Ras), while Schaper et al. showed with the same JAK-deficient cell panel that JAK1 specifically is required for gp130-dependent SHP2 tyrosine phosphorylation, and Kim & Baumann showed that gp130 recruitment of SHP-2 drives ERK via Grb2/SOS/Ras. The explanation is therefore already published; caveats are that IFN-beta-driven Raf-1 activation was reported Ras-independent, and that full-length catalytically inactive SHP-2 did not reduce IL-6-induced ERK activation in hepatic cells, which cuts against the phosphatase-activity part of the prediction.

hypotheses.statement: PKC activates mTORC1 by driving MAPK-pathway (ERK1/2 and RSK) phosphorylation of Raptor.
hypotheses.mechanism: The claims about PKC place it upstream of the Ras-Raf-MAPK cascade: in the modelled feedback loop PKC acts on Raf and PKC activity raises MAPK activity (bhalla1999:findings:001, bhalla1999:findings:002). Independently, the claims about mTORC1 state that Ras/MAPK signalling activates mTORC1 through RSK- and ERK1/2-mediated Raptor phosphorylation, and that PMA-stimulated mTORC1 kinase activity requires these Raptor sites and is abolished by MEK1/2 inhibitors (carriere2010:context:004, carriere2010:findings:015, foster2009:context:002). Together these imply that PKC activity should feed into mTORC1 through MAPK-dependent Raptor phosphorylation, though the PKC-to-MAPK step rests on a simulation rather than a cell measurement.
hypotheses.prediction: Acute PKC activation should increase Raptor phosphorylation at the RSK/ERK sites and raise mTORC1 output (4E-BP1 Thr37/Thr46 and S6K1 phosphorylation, and Raptor-associated mTOR kinase activity). This increase should be lost with PKC inhibition or knockdown, with MEK1/2 inhibition, or in cells expressing the phosphorylation-deficient Raptor S3A mutant. Amino acid-induced mTORC1 activation should be unaffected by PKC inhibition.
hypotheses.test: In HEK293 cells, stimulate PKC with a phorbol ester or diacylglycerol analogue, with or without selective PKC inhibitors or siRNA against PKC isoforms, and with or without a MEK1/2 inhibitor. Immunoblot for phospho-Raptor, phospho-ERK, phospho-RSK, phospho-4E-BP1 (Thr37/Thr46) and phospho-S6K1. Then immunoprecipitate wild-type or S3A Raptor and run an in vitro mTOR kinase assay with GST-4E-BP1 as substrate. Loss of the stimulated mTORC1 activity under PKC inhibition and in the S3A mutant would support the hypothesis; unchanged activity under PKC inhibition would rule it out.

citations.title: Pharmacological and genetic evaluation of proposed roles of mitogen-activated protein kinase/extracellular signal-regulated kinase kinase (MEK), extracellular signal-regulated kinase (ERK), and p90(RSK) in the control of mTORC1 protein signaling by phorbol esters.
Co-ordinated activation of classical and novel PKC isoforms is required for PMA-induced mTORC1 activation
ERK1/2 phosphorylate Raptor to promote Ras-dependent activation of mTOR complex 1 (mTORC1).

novelty.note: I searched the mechanism (PKC/phorbol ester to ERK/RSK to Raptor phosphorylation to mTORC1), the entities together, and the predicted inhibitor results. The explanation is already published: Carriere et al. showed PMA-induced, MEK-dependent Raptor phosphorylation by ERK1/2 (extending their RSK work) driving mTORC1 activity. Two later studies tested it directly for phorbol esters and found it largely does not hold: Fonseca et al. (2011) found p90RSK not required for PMA-induced mTORC1 activation in any cell line tested, could not detect PMA-induced phosphorylation of endogenous Raptor, and saw MEK dependence in HEK293 but not in MCF-7 or NIH/3T3 cells; the 2017 PLoS ONE study confirmed PKC is required but concluded MEK/ERK and RSK are largely dispensable, with classical PKC/PLD2 and PKCη/lysosomal pathways mediating the effect instead.

hypotheses.statement: EGFR kinase activity activates ERK1 (upstream, via the MEK cascade), so EGF-induced ERK1 activation-loop phosphorylation depends on EGFR and is restrained by the EGFR pY992 site.
hypotheses.mechanism: EGF-induced ERK1/2 phosphorylation is modulated by EGFR phosphosite status: Y992F-EGFR gives higher and more prolonged ERK1/2 activation than WT-EGFR, and ERK pathway output decays on EGFR inhibition. Independently, ERK1 is described as activated after EGF stimulation and as phosphorylated by MEK1 at Thr202. Together these imply that ERK1 specifically, not only the pooled ERK1/2 signal, is a downstream target of EGFR activity.
hypotheses.prediction: Inhibiting or depleting EGFR will abolish EGF-induced phosphorylation of ERK1 at its MEK-targeted activation-loop site. Expressing Y992F-EGFR will raise and prolong ERK1 phosphorylation relative to WT-EGFR.
hypotheses.test: In HeLa or HEK293 cells, stimulate with EGF with or without an EGFR kinase inhibitor or EGFR siRNA, and in cells expressing WT- versus Y992F-EGFR. Resolve ERK1 (p44) from ERK2 (p42) by immunoblot with an activation-loop phospho-antibody, or immunoprecipitate HA-ERK1 and measure its kinase activity in vitro over a time course.

citations.title: Phosphoproteomics-based modeling defines the regulatory mechanism underlying aberrant EGFR signaling.
Molecular mechanism for a role of SHP2 in epidermal growth factor receptor signaling.
ERK1/2 MAP kinases: structure, function, and regulation.

novelty.note: Searched the mechanism (EGFR Tyr992 as a negative-regulatory site restraining Ras/ERK), the entities (Y992F EGFR, ERK1, MEK, SHP2, RasGAP) and the prediction (Y992F prolongs ERK1 activation; EGFR inhibition blocks EGF-induced ERK phosphorylation). A 2010 phosphoproteomics study in NIH3T3 cells expressing WT vs Y992F EGFR reports sustained ERK1 activation in Y992F cells versus transient activation in WT cells, which is the ERK1-specific prediction; Agazie & Hayman 2003 already gives the Tyr992/RasGAP explanation, and the MEK1/2-to-ERK1 activation-loop step is textbook (Roskoski review). No negative test was found; the only unverified detail is that the 2010 page retrieved did not state which ERK1 phosphosite was measured.

hypotheses.statement: TNF directly induces BCL2 expression in an IKKβ/NF-κB-dependent manner.
hypotheses.mechanism: Bcl-2 is described as one of a coordinately regulated set of NF-κB target genes (alongside cIAP1, XIAP, IκBα, cyclinD1) whose transcript levels drop when upstream signalling to NF-κB is reduced. Separately, TNF engagement of TNF-R1 recruits and activates the IKK complex within minutes, with IKKβ essential for TNF-induced NF-κB activity, and the resulting NF-κB program turns on protective genes such as IκB and the cIAPs. If Bcl-2 shares that regulatory logic, TNF should raise BCL2 levels via the same IKKβ-dependent route.
hypotheses.prediction: TNF exposure raises BCL2 mRNA and protein with kinetics tracking IκBα and cIAP1 induction, and this induction is lost upon IKKβ depletion or IκB super-repressor expression, while a control transcript such as GAPDH is unchanged.
hypotheses.test: Stimulate a cultured epithelial or carcinoma line with TNF across a 0–8 h time course; quantify BCL2, IκBα and cIAP1 by RT-qPCR plus BCL2 immunoblot. Repeat under IKKβ siRNA, pharmacological IKK inhibition, or IκBα-SR expression, and confirm promoter engagement by p65 ChIP-qPCR at the BCL2 locus.

citations.title: Transcriptional regulation of bcl-2 by nuclear factor kappa B and its significance in prostate cancer.
NF-kappaB activates Bcl-2 expression in t(14;18) lymphoma cells.

novelty.note: I searched for TNF-induced Bcl-2 via NF-κB, for κB-site-driven bcl-2 promoter regulation, and for IKKβ/IκB-super-repressor dependence of Bcl-2 levels (plus a targeted search for negative results). Catz & Johnson (Oncogene 2001) directly states this explanation: a functional NF-κB site in the bcl-2 P2 promoter, ~40-fold promoter induction and increased Bcl-2 protein in LNCaP carcinoma cells after TNF-α, abolished by NF-κB inhibitors; Heckman et al. (Oncogene 2002) independently shows endogenous Bcl-2 falls upon IκBα-super-repressor expression, which is the second arm of the stated prediction. The specific requirement for IKKβ (versus NF-κB generally) was not found to be directly tested, and no source reported a tested negative result, so the explanation counts as already published rather than open or refuted.

hypotheses.statement: SYK acts upstream of RAS, promoting conversion of GDP-Ras to GTP-Ras after ITAM-coupled receptor engagement, and this RAS activation is how SYK signalling reaches ERK.
hypotheses.mechanism: SYK signalling downstream of CLEC7A (Dectin-1) induces cytokine and chemokine production via ERK, but the step between SYK and ERK is not specified. Independently, ERK1/2 activation is placed downstream of Ras-mediated Raf activation and MEK1/2, and receptor-proximal tyrosine signalling components such as SHP2 are shown to control ERK by acting upstream of Ras GTP-loading. Together these imply that SYK's ERK output passes through RAS activation rather than bypassing it.
hypotheses.prediction: Receptor-induced GTP-Ras accumulation will be strongly reduced in SYK-deficient or SYK-inhibited cells and restored by re-expressing SYK. Constitutively active V12-H-Ras will restore ERK1/2 phosphorylation without SYK. If SYK reaches ERK independently of RAS, GTP-Ras levels will be unchanged by SYK loss while phospho-ERK still falls.
hypotheses.test: Use Syk-deficient and syk-reconstituted RBL-2H3 mast cells, or macrophage or B cell lines with or without a SYK inhibitor or knockdown. Stimulate through FcεRI, Dectin-1 (β-glucan) or the BCR, then measure GTP-Ras over a time course by GST-Raf-RBD affinity precipitation and immunoblot, alongside phospho-ERK1/2 immunoblots. As an epistasis check, express V12-H-Ras in the SYK-deficient cells and test whether ERK1/2 phosphorylation is rescued.

citations.title: A Ras activation pathway dependent on Syk phosphorylation of protein kinase C.
Syk-dependent phosphorylation of Shc. A potential link between FcepsilonRI and the Ras/mitogen-activated protein kinase signaling pathway through SOS and Grb2.
Grb2 and GRAP connect the B cell antigen receptor to Erk MAP kinase activation in human B cells.
The SYK tyrosine kinase: a crucial player in diverse biological functions.

novelty.note: I searched for the mechanism in plain words (Syk upstream of Ras, Ras-GTP loading, ERK), for the entities together (Syk + Ras + Shc/Grb2/Sos + FcεRI, Dectin-1, BCR), and for the prediction (reduced Ras-GTP in Syk-deficient cells, GST-Raf-RBD pulldowns, V12-Ras rescue), using PubMed and Europe PMC. The explanation is already published and explicitly stated: Kawakami et al. (PNAS 2003) — the very corpus paper from which the PKCβI claim was drawn — is titled 'A Ras activation pathway dependent on Syk phosphorylation of protein kinase C' and concludes that Syk-phosphorylated conventional PKC isoforms recruit Grb-2/Sos to the membrane and thereby 'contribute to the full activation of the Ras/extracellular signal-regulated kinase signaling pathway' in FcεRI-stimulated mast cells; Jabril-Cuenod et al. (JBC 1996) earlier reported that Syk-dependent Shc phosphorylation and Shc–Grb2 association provide a Sos-dependent route to Ras activation by FcεRI. Status is established rather than partial because a source states this explanation for this phenomenon, although no retrieved paper performs the specific epistasis test (Ras-GTP pulldown in Syk-deficient versus Syk-reconstituted cells with V12-H-Ras rescue of phospho-ERK), and nothing found tests and refutes it.

hypotheses.statement: EGFR activation by EGF positively regulates RPS6KB1 (S6K1), increasing its rapamycin-sensitive phosphorylation and kinase activity through a PI3K-dependent route.
hypotheses.mechanism: EGF stimulation of EGFR drives wortmannin-sensitive AKT phosphorylation in the same way insulin does, without PI3K being needed for EGFR tyrosine phosphorylation itself (borisov2009:findings:009). Independently, S6K1 is activated by insulin and serum in a rapamycin-sensitive manner, with S6K1 and S6 phosphorylation following growth-factor stimulation within minutes (dibble2009:findings:012, dibble2009:findings:014, foster2009:findings:006). Because EGFR engages the same PI3K/AKT arm that accompanies insulin-driven S6K1 activation, EGFR is inferred to act upstream of S6K1.
hypotheses.prediction: In serum-starved cells, EGF should rapidly (within 5-20 min) increase S6K1 T389 phosphorylation and phosphorylation of S6K1-specific readouts (S6 S240/244, Rictor T1135). This increase should be abolished by an EGFR kinase inhibitor or EGFR knockdown, and by wortmannin or rapamycin, while EGFR autophosphorylation stays intact under wortmannin and rapamycin.
hypotheses.test: Serum-starve HEK293 or NIH 3T3 cells and stimulate with an EGF time course, with or without pretreatment with an EGFR inhibitor (e.g. erlotinib) or EGFR siRNA, wortmannin, rapamycin, or a MEK inhibitor. Immunoblot for phospho-S6K1 (T389), phospho-S6 (S240/244), phospho-Rictor (T1135), phospho-AKT, phospho-ERK and phospho-EGFR. Confirm by immunoprecipitating HA-S6K1 from EGF-stimulated versus unstimulated cells and running an in vitro kinase assay on a Rictor or S6 substrate.

citations.title: Selective inhibition of p70 S6 kinase activation by phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase inhibitors.
p70 S6 kinase is regulated by protein kinase Czeta and participates in a phosphoinositide 3-kinase-regulated signalling complex.
Characterization of phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase-dependent phosphorylation of the hydrophobic motif site Thr(389) in p70 S6 kinase 1.

novelty.note: I searched for EGF activation of p70 S6 kinase with wortmannin/rapamycin sensitivity, for EGFR/S6K1 T389 with inhibitors, and for EGF-driven Rictor T1135 phosphorylation. Abstracts retrieved through Europe PMC show this is long-published: wortmannin prevents EGF-induced S6 kinase activation (1995), EGF activation of p70S6K requires PI3K-dependent signals (1999), and EGF induces the rapamycin- and wortmannin-sensitive Thr389 phosphorylation of S6K1 (2002). The specific Rictor T1135 readout under EGF and the EGFR-inhibitor arm were not confirmed in any page I could open, but the core EGFR to PI3K to rapamycin-sensitive S6K1 explanation is established and no negative test was found.

hypotheses.statement: JNK1 directly phosphorylates the mTORC1 subunit Raptor and thereby regulates mTORC1 kinase activity toward 4E-BP1, as the corpus reports for the related MAPKs ERK1/2.
hypotheses.mechanism: JNK1 is a conventional MAPK in the same family as ERK1/2 (cargnello2011) and is shown to be a direct serine kinase that binds and phosphorylates specific sites on its substrate NFATc1-a (chow2000). Independently, mTORC1 is activated by MAPK-pathway kinases phosphorylating Raptor: ERK1/2 and RSK phosphorylate it directly, and the phosphorylation-deficient Raptor S3A mutant lowers mTORC1 kinase activity without changing complex assembly (carriere2010, foster2009). This implies Raptor may be a regulatory input for another conventional MAPK, although JNK1 does not share every ERK substrate, since it fails to phosphorylate hSos1 (corbalangarcia1996), so the relationship needs direct testing.
hypotheses.prediction: Activated JNK1 will incorporate phosphate into purified Raptor in vitro at serine sites that can be removed by alanine substitution. In cells, activated JNK1 will increase, and dominant-negative JNK1 will decrease, Raptor phosphorylation and Raptor-associated mTOR kinase activity toward GST-4E-BP1 (and 4E-BP1 Thr37/Thr46 phosphorylation), even when MEK1/2 is inhibited. If JNK1 is not a Raptor kinase, there will be no Raptor phosphorylation in vitro and no change in mTORC1 activity when JNK1 is manipulated.
hypotheses.test: Run an in vitro kinase assay with immunopurified or recombinant activated JNK1, [γ-32P]ATP and recombinant wild-type Raptor versus alanine mutants (including S3A), with ERK1/2 as a positive control. In parallel, co-express activated JNK1 or dnJNK1 with tagged Raptor in HEK293 cells treated with a MEK1/2 inhibitor, immunoprecipitate Raptor, and measure its phosphorylation, the associated mTOR kinase activity toward GST-4E-BP1, and phospho-4E-BP1 (Thr37/Thr46) by immunoblot. A GST pulldown of JNK1 with GST-Raptor fragments would test direct binding.

citations.title: Osmotic stress regulates mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) complex 1 via c-Jun N-terminal Kinase (JNK)-mediated Raptor protein phosphorylation.

novelty.note: I searched for JNK-mediated Raptor phosphorylation, for JNK1 plus Raptor plus mTORC1 in vitro kinase assays, and for the specific prediction of alanine-substitutable serine sites, then retrieved the full PMC text of the top hit. Kwak et al. (J Biol Chem 2012) report exactly this explanation: FLAG-JNK1 (including constitutively active MKK7-JNK1) physically associates with Raptor by co-IP and GST pulldown, directly phosphorylates purified Raptor in vitro at Ser-696, Thr-706 and Ser-863 with no phosphorylation of the S696A/T706A/S863A alanine mutant, and JNK inhibition abolishes stress-induced Raptor phosphorylation while osmotic stress raises Raptor-associated mTORC1 kinase activity toward 4E-BP1 and S6K1 in a JNK-dependent manner. This states the hypothesised mechanism and its core prediction for JNK1 specifically, so the status is established rather than partial.

hypotheses.statement: RAS activates ERK1: GTP-loaded RAS is an upstream positive regulator of ERK1 activation-loop phosphorylation (Thr202 in the TEY motif), acting through Raf and MEK1/2.
hypotheses.mechanism: The RAS-side claims place ERK1/2 TEY phosphorylation by MEK1/2 downstream of Ras-mediated Raf activation, and show that constitutively active V12-H-Ras induces ERK1/2 activation that an upstream SHP2 block cannot inhibit. The ERK1-side claims show that ERK1 Thr202 is a highly selective MEK1 site, and that MEK1 probably phosphorylates only four sites, two of them in ERK1. Together these imply that RAS-GTP level should by itself set ERK1 activation-loop phosphorylation, for the ERK1 isoform specifically and not only for pooled ERK1/2.
hypotheses.prediction: Expressing V12-H-Ras in serum-starved cells should raise ERK1 Thr202/Tyr204 phosphorylation and ERK1 kinase activity without growth factor. Dominant-negative N17-Ras should blunt EGF-induced ERK1 phosphorylation in a dose-dependent way. The V12-Ras effect should be lost with the MEK1/2 inhibitor U0126.
hypotheses.test: Transfect COS-1 or HEK293 cells with V12-H-Ras, N17-H-Ras or empty vector together with HA-ERK1, then stimulate with EGF or leave unstimulated, with or without U0126. Immunoprecipitate HA-ERK1 and measure its phospho-Thr202/Tyr204 signal by immunoblot, plus its activity in an in vitro kinase assay on a known substrate such as purified Raptor. In parallel, measure GTP-Ras by GST-Raf-RBD pulldown to confirm the RAS manipulation and relate ERK1 phosphorylation to RAS-GTP level.

citations.title: Ras is essential for nerve growth factor- and phorbol ester-induced tyrosine phosphorylation of MAP kinases.
ras mediates nerve growth factor receptor modulation of three signal-transducing protein kinases: MAP kinase, Raf-1, and RSK.
Evidence for a Ras-dependent extracellular signal-regulated protein kinase (ERK) cascade.
Activation of extracellular signal-regulated kinase, ERK2, by p21ras oncoprotein.

novelty.note: I searched the mechanism (oncogenic Ras activating p42/p44 MAP kinases via Raf and MEK), the entities (V12-Ras, N17-Ras, HA-ERK1, U0126) and the prediction (growth-factor-independent ERK activation by V12-Ras; block of growth-factor-induced ERK activation by dominant-negative Ras). Primary papers from 1992 already state this: dominant-inhibitory N17-Ras blocks NGF/TPA-induced phosphorylation of the 42 and 44 kDa MAPKs (ERK2 and ERK1), Ras is required for stimulation of the ERK cascade (ERK1 and ERK2) upstream of an ERK activator, and oncogenic p21ras activates ERK-family kinases by Thr/Tyr phosphorylation without growth factors. No source reporting a negative test was found; records were read as Europe PMC abstracts because PubMed/PMC pages were blocked, and the U0126 arm was seen only in search snippets, not in a retrieved paper.

hypotheses.statement: ERK1 negatively regulates RAS: ERK1 kinase activity feeds back to limit the amplitude and duration of growth-factor-induced RAS-GTP loading.
hypotheses.mechanism: The RAS-side claims show that Ras-GTP and downstream pathway activation are transient under persistent EGF or insulin, a behaviour the model attributes to ERK-mediated negative feedback, and that the duration of GTP-Ras depends on upstream inputs such as SHP2. The ERK1-side claims show that ERK1 directly phosphorylates a receptor upstream of the cascade (FGFR1 S777), and that blocking this site prolongs receptor tyrosine phosphorylation. They also show ERK1 phosphorylates MEK1 T292 to inhibit it, so ERK1 has demonstrated feedback-kinase activity on its own pathway. This suggests ERK1 activity may shorten RAS-GTP accumulation by dampening inputs upstream of RAS.
hypotheses.prediction: Loss of ERK1 activity should convert the transient EGF-induced GTP-Ras peak into a higher or more sustained one. Because single-isoform knockdown only partially reduced ERK substrate phosphorylation, combined ERK1/ERK2 knockdown or MEK inhibition should give a stronger effect than ERK1 knockdown alone. Re-expressing siRNA-resistant wild-type ERK1, but not kinase-dead ERK1, should restore the transient profile.
hypotheses.test: In HEK293 cells, knock down ERK1 alone, ERK2 alone or both by siRNA, or pretreat with U0126. Stimulate with EGF over a time course of about 2 to 60 minutes and quantify GTP-Ras by GST-Raf-RBD affinity precipitation and Ras immunoblot, normalised to total Ras. Include rescue with siRNA-resistant wild-type and kinase-dead ERK1. If peak height and decay of GTP-Ras are unchanged across these conditions, ERK1-dependent feedback onto RAS is ruled out.

citations.title: Desensitization of Ras activation by a feedback disassociation of the SOS-Grb2 complex.
Downregulation of the Ras activation pathway by MAP kinase phosphorylation of Sos.
Multiple decisive phosphorylation sites for the negative feedback regulation of SOS1 via ERK.
Divergent mechanisms for homologous desensitization of p21ras by insulin and growth factors.

novelty.note: I searched for ERK-mediated negative feedback onto RAS-GTP loading, for the specific entities (ERK1/2, SOS1, Grb2, Ras-GTP, EGF/insulin time courses), and for the prediction that blocking MEK/ERK prolongs the Ras-GTP peak. The explanation is long-published: MEK/ERK-dependent phosphorylation of SOS1 uncouples the Grb2-SOS complex from activated receptors and is shown to be the mechanism desensitizing insulin- and growth-factor-stimulated Ras-GTP loading, with a later quantitative study explicitly constraining its models by the duration of Ras activation and showing that MEK inhibition prolongs Ras activation. Because these sources state the same explanation for the same phenomenon (transient Ras-GTP under persistent ligand caused by ERK feedback acting upstream of RAS), the status is established; the isoform-resolved ERK1-versus-ERK2 refinement is an unaddressed detail rather than a distinct mechanism.

hypotheses.statement: SYK is required for the collaborative TNF response produced when Dectin-1 is co-ligated with TLR4, meaning SYK signalling functionally synergises with TLR4 signalling rather than acting on TLR4 itself.
hypotheses.mechanism: The collaborative TNF response to β-glucan plus a TLR2 ligand is lost in Syk–/– macrophages and in MyD88–/– macrophages, so it needs both the Dectin-1/Syk and TLR/MyD88 pathways (dennehy2008:findings:004). Co-ligation of Dectin-1 with TLR4 produces a comparable collaborative TNF response (dennehy2008:findings:008), and SYK transduces Dectin-1 signals to cytokine production via ERK, NFAT and NF-κB through CARD9–BCL10–MALT1 (mcsai2010:findings:019). TLR4 signals through a MyD88 arm as well as a TRIF arm (fitzgerald2020:findings:010), so the same SYK-dependent integration should apply to TLR4.
hypotheses.prediction: In a macrophage cell line, loss or inhibition of SYK should reduce TNF induced by β-glucan plus LPS to the level seen with LPS alone, while leaving the LPS-alone TNF response largely intact. Re-expressing SYK should restore the synergy.
hypotheses.test: Knock down or knock out Syk (siRNA or CRISPR) in a Dectin-1-expressing macrophage cell line, or treat with a SYK inhibitor. Stimulate with LPS alone, β-glucan alone, or both, and measure TNF by ELISA, with a Syk re-expression rescue as control. Unchanged synergy without SYK would rule the hypothesis out.

citations.title: Syk kinase is required for collaborative cytokine production induced through Dectin-1 and Toll-like receptors.
More Prominent Inflammatory Response to Pachyman than to Whole-Glucan Particle and Oat-β-Glucans in Dextran Sulfate-Induced Mucositis Mice and Mouse Injection through Proinflammatory Macrophages.

novelty.note: I searched for the mechanism in plain words (Dectin-1/TLR4 collaborative TNF requiring Syk), the entities together (β-glucan + LPS synergy, Syk inhibitor, macrophages), and the prediction (Syk loss collapsing β-glucan+LPS TNF to LPS-alone levels), via PubMed/PMC and publisher pages. The corpus's own source paper, Dennehy et al. 2008, states this explanation verbatim in its abstract: 'Dectin-1 signaling through the spleen tyrosine kinase (Syk) pathway is required for this collaboration, which can also occur with TLR4, 5, 7 and 9', with Syk or MyD88 deficiency abolishing collaborative TNF and the two pathways integrating at sustained IκB degradation/NF-κB translocation — i.e. functional pathway synergy rather than Syk acting on TLR4 itself. A later study likewise attributes β-glucan/LPS synergistic macrophage TNF to Syk-associated interactions, though the specific Syk-knockdown-plus-rescue test in a Dectin-1-expressing cell line with LPS (rather than Pam3CSK4) has not been reported; no source reports a negative test.

hypotheses.statement: mTOR (as the IKKα-associated mTOR–Raptor complex) negatively regulates p53 by promoting IKKα-dependent diversion of CBP away from p53, lowering CBP–p53 binding and p53 transcriptional activity.
hypotheses.mechanism: IKKα associates with the mTOR–Raptor complex in an Akt-dependent manner, and mTOR expression enhances NF-κB-dependent reporter activity, which suggests mTOR supports IKKα/NF-κB output. Separately, IKKα phosphorylates CBP, increasing its binding to p65 and decreasing its binding to p53, and CBP/p300 acetylation of the p53 carboxyl terminus is needed for high-affinity DNA binding. If mTOR promotes this IKKα function, mTOR activity should reduce CBP-dependent p53 activation.
hypotheses.prediction: In p53-wild-type cells, mTOR overexpression should decrease CBP–p53 co-immunoprecipitation, p53 C-terminal acetylation and p53-responsive reporter activity. mTOR knockdown or catalytic inhibition should increase all three. These effects should be lost when IKKα is knocked down.
hypotheses.test: In a p53-wild-type cultured cell line, overexpress mTOR or deplete/inhibit it (siRNA, Torin1), with and without IKKα siRNA. Measure CBP–p53 and CBP–p65 association by co-immunoprecipitation, acetylated p53 by immunoblot, and p53-dependent luciferase reporter activity alongside the NF-κB reporter as a positive control.

citations.title: Phosphorylation of CBP by IKKalpha promotes cell growth by switching the binding preference of CBP from p53 to NF-kappaB.
Akt-dependent regulation of NF-{kappa}B is controlled by mTOR and Raptor in association with IKK.
mTORC1 Phosphorylates Acetyltransferase p300 to Regulate Autophagy and Lipogenesis.
Transcriptional cross talk between NF-kappaB and p53.

novelty.note: I searched for the composite mechanism in plain words (mTOR negatively regulating p53 by diverting CBP via IKKα), for the entities together (mTOR/Raptor + IKKα + CBP + p53; Akt + IKKα + CBP Ser1382/1386), and for the prediction (mTOR overexpression/knockdown or Torin1/rapamycin effects on CBP–p53 co-IP, p53 C-terminal acetylation and p53 reporter activity). Each link exists separately in the literature — the Akt-dependent mTOR–Raptor/IKK association that drives NF-κB reporter activity (Dan et al., which contains no p53 or CBP data), IKKα phosphorylation of CBP switching its binding preference from p53 to NF-κB (Huang et al., which does not invoke mTOR, Raptor, Akt or rapamycin), p53/RelA competition for a limiting CBP/p300 pool, and a direct mTORC1–p300/CBP acetyltransferase axis (Wan et al., which does not address p53 or IKKα) — but no retrieved source states mTOR as the upstream driver of IKKα-dependent CBP diversion from p53, and none reports a negative test of it. Hence partial rather than established, open, or refuted.

hypotheses.statement: EGFR kinase activity positively regulates the protein biosynthetic process, with EGFR activation increasing global protein synthesis through its downstream MEK/ERK output.
hypotheses.mechanism: Independent claims about EGFR show that it drives ERK1/2 activation: EGF-induced ERK1/2 phosphorylation is modulated at EGFR pY992, and an ERK output reporter decays when EGFR or ERK is inhibited. EGF also activates Ras-GTP/MEK/ERK alongside PI3K-dependent AKT. Separately, a claim about protein synthesis states that MEK1/2 inhibition blocks growth factor-stimulated global protein synthesis. Together these imply that EGFR activity is an upstream positive regulator of global translation through MEK/ERK.
hypotheses.prediction: EGF stimulation should increase the global protein synthesis rate in EGFR-expressing cells. EGFR inhibition or knockdown should abolish this increase to a similar extent as MEK1/2 inhibition. An EGFR variant with prolonged ERK activation (Y992F) should give a larger or more sustained increase than wild-type EGFR.
hypotheses.test: In serum-starved MCF-10A or HEK293 cells, measure nascent protein synthesis by puromycin incorporation (SUnSET immunoblot) or 35S-methionine labelling after EGF stimulation. Compare conditions with and without an EGFR kinase inhibitor (erlotinib) or EGFR siRNA, and with and without a MEK1/2 inhibitor, monitoring phospho-ERK in parallel. As a gain-of-function arm, compare WT-EGFR and Y992F-EGFR transfected NIH 3T3 cells. The hypothesis is ruled out if EGFR inhibition does not reduce EGF-stimulated puromycin incorporation.

citations.title: The activation of eukaryotic initiation factor (eIF)2B by growth factors in PC12 cells requires MEK/ERK signalling.
Resistance to EGFR-TKI can be mediated through multiple signaling pathways converging upon cap-dependent translation in EGFR-wild type NSCLC.

novelty.note: I searched for EGF/EGFR-driven global protein synthesis, for MEK/ERK dependence of growth-factor-stimulated translation, and for EGFR-inhibitor effects on translational output (puromycin/cap-dependent translation). Kleijn & Proud (FEBS Lett 2000) directly report that EGF activates protein synthesis in PC12 cells and that this activation, together with activation of eIF2B, requires MEK/ERK signalling and is blocked by the MEK inhibitor PD98059 — the same explanation as the hypothesis (EGFR ligand engagement raising global translation via MEK/ERK). A separate NSCLC study confirms that EGFR signalling is coupled to activation of cap-dependent translation machinery and that erlotinib collapses this coupling in sensitive cells, though it measures eIF4F/4E-BP1 rather than global synthesis rate, so it is cited as the nearest work for the EGFR-inhibition arm.

hypotheses.statement: GSK3B negatively regulates NF-KB transcriptional activity, so that AKT-mediated inhibition of GSK3B is one route by which AKT promotes NF-KB-dependent gene expression.
hypotheses.mechanism: Independent claims state that AKT inhibits GSK3B (stabilising PHLPP, prolonging NFAT nuclear residence) and that GSK3B restrains transcription factors by phosphorylating them (Smad3 Thr66 driving its turnover, NFAT nuclear export, C/EBPβ phosphorylation lowering IL-17-induced gene expression). Separately, NF-KB reporter activity in PTEN-null PC3 cells depends on PI3K/AKT2, falling about 70% with AKT2 knockdown and also with LY294002 or PTEN re-expression. Taken together, active GSK3B in low-AKT conditions may suppress NF-KB, and AKT may relieve that suppression alongside the IKK/mTOR route.
hypotheses.prediction: In PC3 cells, inhibiting or knocking down GSK3B should raise NF-KB reporter activity and target-gene expression (Bcl-2, cIAP1, XIAP, IκBα), and should at least partly rescue the loss of NF-KB activity caused by AKT2 knockdown or LY294002. A non-AKT-inhibitable GSK3B mutant should lower NF-KB activity despite high AKT. If GSK3B inhibition has no effect or reduces NF-KB activity, the hypothesis is refuted.
hypotheses.test: Run NF-KB luciferase reporter assays and RT-PCR of NF-KB target genes in PC3 and HeLa cells treated with SB-216763 or GSK3B shRNA, with and without AKT2 siRNA or LY294002, and after expressing wild-type versus constitutively active GSK3B. Follow with co-immunoprecipitation of endogenous GSK3B with RelA/p65 and an in vitro kinase assay using recombinant GSK3B and p65 to check for a direct interaction and phosphorylation.

citations.title: GSK-3 represses growth factor-inducible genes by inhibiting NF-kappaB in quiescent cells.
Phosphorylation of serine 468 by GSK-3beta negatively regulates basal p65 NF-kappaB activity.
A screen for transcription factor targets of glycogen synthase kinase-3 highlights an inverse correlation of NFκB and androgen receptor signaling in prostate cancer.
GSK-3β controls NF-kappaB activity via IKKγ/NEMO.

novelty.note: I searched for GSK3β as a negative regulator of NF-κB, for GSK3 inhibition raising NF-κB reporter/target-gene activity, and for the Akt→GSK3→NF-κB route in PTEN-null/prostate cells. Graham et al. (JBC 2010) state exactly this explanation — GSK-3 that remains active without growth-factor/PI 3-kinase-Akt signalling represses NF-κB (via IKK inhibition, blocking IκBα degradation and p65 nuclear entry), so GSK-3 inhibition raises p65 occupancy and target-gene expression — while Buss et al. (JBC 2004) give the direct substrate-level version (GSK-3β phosphorylates p65 Ser468 to hold down basal NF-κB activity), and the Oncotarget 2014 prostate screen shows GSK-3 silencing or CHIR99021 increases basal NFκB transcriptional activity in prostate cancer cells. Because the explanation and its central prediction are already published, the status is established; I note that the regulation is context-dependent, as other work reports GSK-3β is positively required for cytokine-induced NF-κB activation via NEMO phosphorylation, but that is a different stimulus setting rather than a direct negative test of this claim.

hypotheses.statement: EGFR activation drives RSK activation (phosphorylation of its ERK-dependent sites, including the hydrophobic-motif Ser380), acting upstream of RSK through ERK1/2 rather than by direct EGFR-RSK contact.
hypotheses.mechanism: The EGFR-side claims show that EGF stimulation induces ERK1/2 activation and that an ERK-output reporter decays when EGFR is inhibited, so EGFR activity sets ERK activity in these cells. The RSK-side claims state that RSK activation requires ordered phosphorylation mediated by ERK1/2, PDK1 and autophosphorylation, and that growth-factor-induced Ser380 phosphorylation is mediated by ERK. Together these imply that EGFR kinase activity should control RSK phosphorylation state and activity through ERK1/2.
hypotheses.prediction: EGF stimulation should rapidly increase RSK phosphorylation at Ser380 and Thr573 and increase RSK-specific substrate phosphorylation (rpS6 Ser235/236). An EGFR kinase inhibitor should block this increase, as should MEK/ERK inhibition; if an EGFR inhibitor does not reduce EGF-induced RSK phosphorylation, the hypothesis is ruled out.
hypotheses.test: Serum-starve HeLa or MCF-10A cells, stimulate with EGF over a 0-60 min time course with or without pretreatment with an EGFR inhibitor (e.g. erlotinib) or a MEK inhibitor, and immunoblot for phospho-RSK Ser380 and Thr573, total RSK and phospho-ERK1/2. As a complementary readout, measure rpS6 Ser235/236 phosphorylation in the presence of rapamycin (to remove the S6K contribution), with or without the RSK inhibitor BI-D1870. EGFR siRNA knockdown can serve as an orthogonal loss-of-function control.

citations.title: Stress-Induced Phosphorylation of Nuclear YB-1 Depends on Nuclear Trafficking of p90 Ribosomal S6 Kinase.
Identification of regulatory phosphorylation sites in mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK)-activated protein kinase-1a/p90rsk that are inducible by MAPK.
RAS/ERK signaling promotes site-specific ribosomal protein S6 phosphorylation via RSK and stimulates cap-dependent translation.
Phosphorylation of p90 ribosomal S6 kinase (RSK) regulates extracellular signal-regulated kinase docking and RSK activity.

novelty.note: I searched for the mechanism in plain words (growth-factor/EGF-induced RSK hydrophobic-motif Ser380 phosphorylation mediated by ERK), for the entities together (EGFR inhibitor + phospho-RSK + rpS6 Ser235/236), and for the prediction (EGF + Ser380/Thr573 + MEK inhibitors), using Europe PMC/PMC and PubMed records. The ERK-dependent ordered activation of RSK (ERK phosphorylating Thr573/Ser363 with CTKD-dependent Ser380, enabling PDK1 and full activity) and RSK-specific rpS6 Ser235/236 phosphorylation downstream of Ras/ERK are established primary findings, and a published experiment shows that the EGFR inhibitor erlotinib efficiently blocks EGF-induced RSK phosphorylation and its downstream output, i.e. EGFR acts upstream of RSK through the ERK cascade rather than requiring direct EGFR-RSK contact. Because sources state this explanation for this phenomenon, the status is established rather than partial; no source reported a negative test.

hypotheses.statement: p38 positively regulates S6K1 (RPS6KB1) under stress, acting through its downstream kinases MK2/3 to promote S6K1 activating phosphorylation (T389), in parallel to the mTORC1 input.
hypotheses.mechanism: p38α is strictly required for MK2 activation, and MK2/3 phosphorylate RSK at Ser380 in some cell types, which is offered as the route by which p38-activating stresses turn on RSK. S6K1 is, like RSK, an AGC kinase that can phosphorylate the same site on a shared substrate (CCTβ Ser260), and its activity is read out by T389 phosphorylation, which is normally rapamycin-sensitive. If the p38-MK2/3 module can act on RSK in this way, it may supply a comparable stress-driven input to the related kinase S6K1; this rests on analogy with RSK, not on any claim linking MK2/3 to S6K1.
hypotheses.prediction: p38-activating stress (e.g. UV, arsenite or sorbitol) should induce a component of S6K1 T389 phosphorylation and S6K1 activity that is blocked by SB203580, absent in p38α-deficient or MK2/3-depleted cells, and at least partly retained under rapamycin. Active MK2 should also phosphorylate kinase-dead S6K1 in vitro. If stress-induced S6K1 phosphorylation is unaffected by p38 inhibition or loss, and MK2 does not phosphorylate S6K1, the hypothesis is ruled out.
hypotheses.test: Expose cultured cells (e.g. HEK293, and p38α-deficient versus wild-type cells) to a p38-activating stress with or without SB203580, rapamycin, or MK2/3 siRNA. Immunoblot for phospho-S6K1 (T389), phospho-S6 (S240/244) and phospho-MK2 (Thr334) as a control for p38 pathway activity. In parallel, run an in vitro kinase assay with recombinant active MK2 (or p38) and immunoprecipitated kinase-dead S6K1, reading out with the phospho-T389 antibody.

citations.title: S6K1 is a multifaceted regulator of Mdm2 that connects nutrient status and DNA damage response.
A role for p38 stress-activated protein kinase in regulation of cell growth via TORC1.
Contribution of S6K1/MAPK Signaling Pathways in the Response to Oxidative Stress: Activation of RSK and MSK by Hydrogen Peroxide

novelty.note: I searched for p38/SB203580 control of S6K1 T389 under stress, for MK2/MAPKAPK2 acting on p70S6K, and for rapamycin-insensitive stress-driven T389 phosphorylation. The positive p38-to-S6K1 T389 link under stress is already published: genotoxic stress requires p38α for S6K1 T389 phosphorylation (reduced by SB203580 and in p38α-null MEFs), and p38-activating stresses such as H2O2 and anisomycin activate TORC1/S6K phosphorylation. However, both papers place the input upstream of mTOR rather than in parallel (the stress-induced signal is rapamycin/Torin-sensitive), MK2 RNAi had little effect on S6K phosphorylation in the TORC1 study, and no source tests or reports MK2/3 phosphorylating S6K1; a further study found that H2O2-induced anti-phospho-T389 signal is RSK/MSK cross-reactivity, not S6K1, so the MK2/3-mediated, rapamycin-retained arm is unsupported rather than affirmatively refuted as a whole.

hypotheses.statement: In HeLa cells, RPS6KA1 (RSK1) is an expressed RSK isoform that carries the MEK/ERK- and mTOR-dependent hydrophobic-motif (Ser380) phosphorylation, and during glucose/glutamine withdrawal this phosphorylated RSK1 is not catalytically coupled to S6 Ser235/236.
hypotheses.mechanism: HeLa cells show phospho-Ser380 RSK that is diminished by mTOR knockdown and by U0126, and that stays high under glucose/glutamine withdrawal while S6 Ser235/236 phosphorylation is abolished; these claims do not resolve the RSK isoform. Independently, Ser380 is one of the four ordered activation sites of human RSK1 (driven by ERK1/2, PDK1 and autophosphorylation), RSK1 mRNA is ubiquitous across human tissues, and RSK1/2 phosphorylate S6 at Ser235/236. Together these imply that RSK1 is a plausible carrier of the HeLa Ser380 signal, and that Ser380 phosphorylation of RSK1 in starved HeLa cells does not translate into RSK1 kinase output toward S6.
hypotheses.prediction: RSK1-specific immunoprecipitates from HeLa cells will show Ser380 phosphorylation that rises on glucose/glutamine withdrawal and is lost with U0126 or mTOR knockdown. RSK1 siRNA will substantially reduce the total phospho-Ser380 RSK band. Despite the elevated Ser380 phosphorylation, RSK1 immunoprecipitated from starved HeLa cells will show no matching increase in in vitro kinase activity toward GST-S6 (Ser235/236) compared with serum- or PMA-stimulated cells.
hypotheses.test: Culture HeLa cells in complete medium, with serum or PMA stimulation, or with glucose/glutamine withdrawal, each with or without U0126 or mTOR siRNA. Immunoprecipitate endogenous RSK1 with an isoform-specific antibody and immunoblot for phospho-Ser380 and phospho-Ser221. Run a non-radioactive in vitro kinase assay on the immunoprecipitates using GST-S6 with a phospho-Ser235/236 readout, including BI-D1870 as a specificity control. In parallel, knock down RSK1 by siRNA and blot whole lysates for phospho-Ser380 RSK and phospho-S6 Ser235/236. The hypothesis is ruled out if RSK1 knockdown leaves the phospho-Ser380 signal unchanged, or if RSK1 kinase activity toward S6 tracks Ser380 phosphorylation under starvation.

citations.title: mTORC2 Is Involved in the Induction of RSK Phosphorylation by Serum or Nutrient Starvation.
P90 ribosomal S6 kinase confers cancer cell survival by mediating checkpoint kinase 1 degradation in response to glucose stress.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the plain-words mechanism (RSK hydrophobic-motif Ser380 phosphorylation sustained under glucose/glutamine withdrawal while S6 Ser235/236 is lost), the entities together (RSK1 isoform vs pan-RSK Ser380 signal in HeLa, mTORC2/SIN1, MEK/U0126), and the prediction (RSK1 immunoprecipitate kinase activity toward GST-S6 during nutrient starvation). The uncoupling of RSK HM phosphorylation from S6 Ser235/236 in starved HeLa cells is published (Chou et al., Cells 2020), but that work uses a pan-RSK phospho-Ser380 antibody with no isoform-resolving immunoprecipitation or siRNA and performs no in vitro kinase assay, so neither the attribution of the HeLa Ser380 signal to RSK1 nor the predicted absence of RSK1 catalytic output toward S6 is stated anywhere I found. The nearest direct test of catalytic output under nutrient stress reports the opposite direction for other substrates — pan-RSK activity rises during glucose deprivation, scored by BAD Ser112 and GSK3β Ser9 and by CHK1 Ser280 — but it does not assay S6 Ser235/236 or resolve isoforms, so it neither states nor refutes this specific claim; hence partial rather than established or refuted.

hypotheses.statement: TAK1 positively regulates proinflammatory gene expression in epithelial cells, acting upstream of p38α (and of NF-κB), so that loss of TAK1 reduces stimulus-induced proinflammatory gene expression.
hypotheses.mechanism: Deleting p38α in epithelial cells reduces proinflammatory gene expression (cargnello2011:findings:006). Independently, TAK1 phosphorylates the p38 activator MKK6 and is activated by IL-1β (kojima2005:findings:001), and TAK1 activation leads to p38 MAPK activation (derynck2019:findings:030). TAK1 knockdown in HME epithelial cells also impairs IL-1/EGF-stimulated IKK, IκB and ERK phosphorylation (de2015:findings:001), so TAK1 loss should remove the p38α-dependent transcriptional output.
hypotheses.prediction: In epithelial cells, TAK1 knockdown or kinase inhibition will lower IL-1-induced proinflammatory transcripts together with p38 phosphorylation. Re-activating p38 downstream of TAK1 (e.g. constitutively active MKK6) will at least partially restore those transcripts. A scrambled control will show no such loss.
hypotheses.test: Express TAK1 shRNA or scrambled shRNA in a cultured epithelial line (e.g. HME cells) and stimulate with IL-1. Measure a panel of proinflammatory genes by RT-qPCR and phospho-p38 by Western blot. Then attempt rescue with constitutively active MKK6, and compare the effect with p38α knockdown or inhibition.

citations.title: TGF-β1-activated kinase-1 regulates inflammation and fibrosis in the obstructed kidney.
Interleukin-1 and TRAF6-dependent activation of TAK1 in the absence of TAB2 and TAB3.
Heat shock protein 27 functions in inflammatory gene expression and transforming growth factor-beta-activated kinase-1 (TAK1)-mediated signaling.

novelty.note: I searched three ways — the mechanism in words (TAK1 as the MAP3K upstream of p38/NF-κB for inflammatory gene output), the entities together (TAK1 + IL-1 + p38 + epithelial cells + knockdown), and the prediction (TAK1 loss lowering IL-1-induced proinflammatory transcripts alongside phospho-p38, and MKK6 as the intervening activator) — via PubMed and Europe PMC. Bonnet/Ma et al. in Am J Physiol Renal Physiol state and demonstrate exactly this explanation: 'TAK1 deletion in cultured tubular epithelial cells substantially inhibited IL-1 and TNF-α-induced JNK, p38, and NF-κB signaling and the proinflammatory response,' with in vivo TAK1 deletion suppressing p38/NF-κB activation and proinflammatory mRNAs; the Biochem J study shows IL-1β-stimulated p38α activation and IL-8 mRNA require TAK1 expression and kinase activity, and the JBC study places TAK1 as the most upstream common node driving MKK3/6–p38 and IL-1-induced COX-2/IL-6/IL-8 expression in HeLa epithelial cells. Nothing found reports a negative test, so the explanation is already published rather than open; only the specific constitutively-active-MKK6 rescue arm appears untested.

hypotheses.statement: SYK acts upstream of JNK, such that SYK kinase activity is required for JNK activation after Dectin-1 (ITAM-coupled receptor) ligation in myeloid cells.
hypotheses.mechanism: SYK signalling downstream of Dectin-1 drives cytokine production through ERK, NFAT and NF-κB (mcsai2010:findings:019), and the collaborative TNF response to β-glucan plus a TLR2 ligand is lost in Syk–/– macrophages (dennehy2008:findings:004). Independently, JNK is activated together with ERK, p38 and NF-κB by the same receptor-proximal module in IL-17 signalling (gaffen2014:findings:022), and by Rho/Rac/Cdc42 through MAPKKKs in a context-dependent manner (jaffe2005:findings:008). Because SYK already engages the ERK and NF-κB arms that are co-activated with JNK elsewhere, JNK is plausibly another SYK-dependent output of this receptor, though none of the cited claims shows this directly.
hypotheses.prediction: Inhibiting or depleting SYK will markedly reduce β-glucan-induced JNK activation-loop phosphorylation and c-Jun phosphorylation. JNK activation by a SYK-independent stimulus such as TNF or IL-1 will be unaffected.
hypotheses.test: In a macrophage or dendritic cell line expressing Dectin-1, stimulate with β-glucan (curdlan or zymosan) with or without a selective SYK inhibitor, or after SYK knockdown/knockout with wild-type or kinase-dead SYK re-expressed. Measure phospho-JNK (Thr183/Tyr185) and phospho-c-Jun by immunoblot over a time course, using TNF or IL-1 stimulation as the SYK-independent control and phospho-ERK as a positive control for SYK dependence.

citations.title: CR3 and Dectin-1 Collaborate in Macrophage Cytokine Response through Association on Lipid Rafts and Activation of Syk-JNK-AP-1 Pathway.
Phospholipase Cgamma2 is critical for Dectin-1-mediated Ca2+ flux and cytokine production in dendritic cells.

novelty.note: I searched for Dectin-1/Syk-dependent JNK activation in myeloid cells, for Syk-inhibitor or Syk-knockout effects on JNK/c-Jun phosphorylation after beta-glucan (curdlan/zymosan), and for the Syk-JNK-AP-1 axis, via PubMed/E-utilities and publisher full text. The PLOS Pathogens macrophage study is built on exactly this ordering: it reports that Syk inhibitors (SykI, Bay 61-3606) and Syk-deficient macrophages abolish JNK phosphorylation upon Dectin-1/CR3 engagement (Raf-1 and JNK lost, ERK/p38/Akt spared) and that the resulting Syk-JNK-AP-1 axis drives TNF and IL-6, i.e. the placement of SYK upstream of JNK at this receptor is already published. The dendritic-cell PLCgamma2 paper is the nearest supporting work, showing curdlan/zymosan-induced JNK activation depends on the Syk-proximal PLCgamma2 module; no source reported a direct negative test of Syk-dependent JNK activation.

hypotheses.statement: Phosphorylation of EGFR at Tyr992 negatively regulates the magnitude and duration of RAPTOR Ser696/Ser863 phosphorylation by recruiting RasGAP and limiting Ras/ERK output.
hypotheses.mechanism: EGFR pY992 is a RasGAP binding site, and Y992F-EGFR induces higher and more prolonged ERK1/2 activation than wild-type EGFR when SHP2 cannot dephosphorylate this site. Separately, active Ras is sufficient to drive RAPTOR phosphorylation on proline-directed sites, and ERK1/2 are required for EGF-induced RAPTOR Ser696/Ser863 phosphorylation. The pY992 status of EGFR should therefore tune how strongly and how long RAPTOR is phosphorylated after EGF.
hypotheses.prediction: In cells expressing R/E-SHP2, Y992F-EGFR will produce stronger and more sustained EGF-induced RAPTOR Ser696/Ser863 phosphorylation than wild-type EGFR. A MEK1/2 inhibitor will eliminate this difference.
hypotheses.test: Transfect NIH 3T3 cells stably expressing R/E-SHP2 with wild-type or Y992F-EGFR and run an EGF time course. Immunoblot RAPTOR phospho-Ser696 and phospho-Ser863 together with phospho-ERK1/2, with and without U0126 or PD184352, and compare signal amplitude and decay between the two EGFR constructs.

citations.title: Molecular mechanism for a role of SHP2 in epidermal growth factor receptor signaling.
ERK1/2 phosphorylate Raptor to promote Ras-dependent activation of mTOR complex 1 (mTORC1).

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the EGFR pY992/RasGAP/SHP2 mechanism with ERK duration, the Raptor Ser696/Ser863–ERK1/2–Ras axis, and the conjunction (EGFR autophosphorylation-site mutants or RasGAP/SHP2 linked to Raptor phosphorylation or mTORC1 kinetics), retrieving the Agazie/Hubbard and Carrière/Roux full texts plus RASA1–mTORC1 and SHP-2–mTOR/S6K1 literature. Each half is published separately — pY992 is a RasGAP site whose loss (Y992F) yields higher and more prolonged ERK1/2 activation, and ERK1/2 directly phosphorylate Raptor at Ser696/Ser863 in a MEK-dependent, Ras-driven manner after EGF/PMA — but no retrieved source connects EGFR pY992 status to the amplitude or decay of Raptor Ser696/Ser863 phosphorylation, and the Raptor paper never mentions Y992, RasGAP or SHP2. Hence partial rather than established, and no source reports a negative test of this specific link.

hypotheses.statement: ERK2 directly phosphorylates STAT3 on a serine residue (candidate: Ser727) in response to EGF or IL-6, modulating STAT3 DNA binding and transactivation.
hypotheses.mechanism: EGF strongly activates ERK2 (meng2005) and IL-6 activates ERK2 through gp130 Tyr759-dependent Gab1–SHP2 association (heinrich2003:010). The same two stimuli induce STAT3 phosphorylation (darnell1994), and SHP2 modulates the amplitude of STAT3 activity (heinrich2003:036). STAT3 Ser727 is a regulated serine site whose IL-6-dependent phosphorylation alters DNA binding and transactivation (heinrich2003:023), and activated ERK2 directly phosphorylates serine/threonine sites on substrates such as Raptor in vitro (carriere2010), so ERK2 is a plausible stimulus-activated serine kinase for STAT3.
hypotheses.prediction: Activated ERK2 will incorporate phosphate into wild-type STAT3 in vitro but not into a STAT3 S727A mutant. In cells, MEK1/2 inhibition or ERK2 knockdown will reduce EGF- and IL-6-induced STAT3 Ser727 phosphorylation and change STAT3-dependent reporter activity, without abolishing STAT3 tyrosine phosphorylation.
hypotheses.test: Run an in vitro kinase assay with recombinant activated ERK2 (or HA-ERK2 immunoprecipitated from stimulated cells) and purified wild-type versus S727A STAT3, read out by [γ-32P]ATP autoradiography and phospho-Ser727 immunoblot. In parallel, treat EGF- or IL-6-stimulated HepG2 or HEK293 cells with U0126 or ERK2 siRNA and measure phospho-Ser727 STAT3, phospho-tyrosine STAT3 and a STAT3-responsive (e.g. α2M promoter) luciferase reporter. Test ERK2–STAT3 association by co-immunoprecipitation.

citations.title: STAT3 serine phosphorylation by ERK-dependent and -independent pathways negatively modulates its tyrosine phosphorylation.
Serine-727 phosphorylation activates hypothalamic STAT-3 independently from tyrosine-705 phosphorylation.

novelty.note: I searched for ERK/ERK2 phosphorylation of STAT3 at Ser727 in vitro, for the EGF–ERK–Ser727 link with reporter/DNA-binding readouts, and for IL-6-dependent Ser727 phosphorylation by MAPK. Chung et al. (Mol Cell Biol 1997) provide exactly this explanation: in vitro and in vivo evidence that ERK family MAP kinases (but not JNK or p38) specifically phosphorylate STAT3 on Ser727 in response to growth factors, with S727 phosphorylation negatively modulating STAT3 tyrosine phosphorylation and thus dimerisation/DNA binding; Breit et al. (Mol Endocrinol 2015) confirm in cells that ERK-1/2 inhibition blocks EGF-induced STAT-3 Ser-727 phosphorylation and STAT-3 reporter activity. The status is established rather than partial because the central claim and its predicted readouts are already published, though note that Chung et al. explicitly report the IL-6-stimulated arm of STAT3 serine phosphorylation to be ERK-independent, contradicting the IL-6 half of the mechanism.

hypotheses.statement: RPS6KB1 (S6K1) kinase activity creates a phospho-dependent 14-3-3 docking site on Rictor at T1135, so S6K1 acts upstream of 14-3-3 recruitment to Rictor.
hypotheses.mechanism: S6K1 directly phosphorylates Rictor on T1135 in vitro, S6K1 knockdown specifically reduces this phosphorylation in cells, and the phosphorylated site is recognised by a phospho-Akt-substrate antibody; Rictor-T1135 is also reported as an mTORC1/S6K target in another cell system. Independently, 14-3-3 binding to Rictor is largely lost with the T1135A mutant, and 14-3-3 proteins bind phosphoserine/threonine motifs with upstream Arg, the same type of basophilic AGC-kinase motif through which AKT creates 14-3-3 sites on FoxO. Together these imply that S6K1 activity determines whether 14-3-3 binds Rictor.
hypotheses.prediction: Reducing S6K1 activity (S6K1 siRNA or rapamycin) should lower the amount of Rictor recovered with 14-3-3 to about the level seen with Rictor-T1135A, while S6K2 knockdown should not. A rapamycin-resistant active S6K1 should keep 14-3-3 bound to Rictor in the presence of rapamycin. Rictor phosphorylated in vitro by S6K1 should bind GST-14-3-3, whereas unphosphorylated or T1135A Rictor should not.
hypotheses.test: In HEK-293E cells expressing myc-Rictor (wild-type or T1135A), perform GST-14-3-3 pulldown and Flag-14-3-3 co-immunoprecipitation after S6K1 siRNA, S6K2 siRNA or control siRNA, and after insulin with or without rapamycin, with or without the rapamycin-resistant S6K1 mutant; immunoblot for Rictor and phospho-T1135. In parallel, phosphorylate immunopurified Rictor in vitro with immunoprecipitated S6K1 and test binding to recombinant GST-14-3-3.

citations.title: Rictor is a novel target of p70 S6 kinase-1.
mTORC1-activated S6K1 phosphorylates Rictor on threonine 1135 and regulates mTORC2 signaling.
Characterization of Rictor phosphorylation sites reveals direct regulation of mTOR complex 2 by S6K1.

novelty.note: I searched for the mechanism in plain words (S6K1 creating a 14-3-3 docking site on Rictor), for the entities together (Rictor / Thr1135 / S6K1 / 14-3-3), and for the prediction (rapamycin-sensitive, S6K1-dependent 14-3-3 binding to Rictor), then retrieved PubMed records for the three primary papers. Two independent groups beyond the corpus source state exactly this explanation: Treins et al. report that S6K1 directly phosphorylates Rictor at Thr1135 in a rapamycin-sensitive manner and that this phosphorylation mediates 14-3-3 binding to Rictor and mTORC2, and Julien et al. independently establish S6K1-dependent, rapamycin-sensitive Thr1135 phosphorylation as the mTORC1-to-mTORC2 regulatory link, with the corpus paper (Dibble et al.) itself reporting that T1135 phosphorylation stimulates 14-3-3 binding. Nothing found tests and negates the claim, so the ordering of S6K1 upstream of 14-3-3 recruitment to Rictor is already published.

hypotheses.statement: PKA directly phosphorylates GSK3B and inhibits its kinase activity, analogous to the inhibition of GSK3B by AKT.
hypotheses.mechanism: AKT inhibits GSK3β, stabilising PHLPP and prolonging NFAT nuclear residence (haeusler2018:findings:007, hogan2003:findings:006), and atypical PKC activation likewise leads to GSK3 inactivation (jaffe2005:findings:023). PKA is grouped with Akt and the PKCs as an AGC kinase sharing the turn-motif architecture (facchinetti2008:findings:004). This suggests PKA may exert the same inhibitory control over GSK3B that the related kinases do.
hypotheses.prediction: Activating PKA will increase phosphorylation of GSK3B and lower phosphorylation of GSK3-dependent sites (for example Smad3 Thr66 or GSK3-motif phosphosites), and this will be blocked by PKA inhibition but not by PI3K/AKT inhibition. Purified PKA catalytic subunit will phosphorylate recombinant GSK3B and reduce its activity toward a primed peptide substrate.
hypotheses.test: Perform an in vitro kinase assay with purified PKA catalytic subunit and recombinant GSK3B (with or without PKI), detecting GSK3B phosphorylation by mass spectrometry or phospho-blot and measuring GSK3B activity on a primed peptide afterwards. In cultured cells (e.g. HeLa or 293), raise cAMP with forskolin or CPT-cAMP with or without H89 and LY294002, then quantify GSK3B phosphorylation and a GSK3-dependent readout such as Smad3 pThr66 by Western blot.

citations.title: Phosphorylation and inactivation of glycogen synthase kinase 3 by protein kinase A.
Cyclic AMP promotes neuronal survival by phosphorylation of glycogen synthase kinase 3beta.

novelty.note: I searched for the mechanism (PKA phosphorylating and inactivating GSK3), the entities (cAMP, PKA, GSK-3β Ser9) and the prediction (forskolin-induced GSK3β phosphorylation blocked by H89 but not LY294002; purified PKA catalytic subunit in vitro). Fang et al. 2000 (PNAS) reports that PKA catalytic subunit phosphorylates GSK-3α Ser21 and GSK-3β Ser9 in vitro (blocked by PKI), inactivates both isoforms, and that forskolin/8-Br-cAMP-induced GSK-3 phosphorylation is insensitive to wortmannin or LY294002. Li et al. 2000 independently reports cAMP-driven phosphorylation and inhibition of GSK-3β at the Akt site, so the explanation and its prediction have been published since 2000.

hypotheses.statement: TGFBR1 (TβRI) activates NF-κB: TGF-β-engaged TβRI raises IKK-dependent NF-κB transcriptional activity through the AKT/mTOR-Raptor route.
hypotheses.mechanism: The TGFBR1 evidence reports that TGF-β activates AKT in a TβRI kinase-dependent manner, with the PI3K regulatory subunit p85 associating with TβRI upon TGF-β (a TRAF6-mediated route that does not need the TβRI kinase is also reported). Independently, the NF-κB evidence shows that NF-κB reporter activity, DNA binding and target-gene expression in high-Akt cells depend on PI3K, Akt2, mTOR/Raptor and IKKα, and are suppressed by LY294002, rapamycin or PTEN re-expression. If TβRI feeds AKT, it should therefore feed this Akt/mTOR/IKK-dependent NF-κB output.
hypotheses.prediction: TGF-β stimulation or a constitutively active TβRI should increase NF-κB reporter activity, NF-κB DNA binding and NF-κB target-gene expression (e.g. IκBα, cIAP1, XIAP). This increase should be lost on TGFBR1 knockdown and blunted by LY294002, rapamycin, Akt2 siRNA or IKKα siRNA. A TβRI kinase inhibitor should reduce it only to the extent that the kinase-dependent AKT route, rather than the TRAF6 route, carries the signal. If TGFBR1 knockdown or inhibition leaves TGF-β-induced and basal NF-κB activity unchanged despite reduced AKT phosphorylation, the hypothesis is ruled out.
hypotheses.test: In cultured cells such as PC3 and HeLa, transfect an NF-κB luciferase reporter and treat with TGF-β, with or without a TβRI kinase inhibitor, TGFBR1 siRNA, or a constitutively active TβRI. Measure reporter activity, NF-κB EMSA on nuclear extracts, RT-PCR of NF-κB target genes, and phospho-AKT by immunoblot. Repeat with Akt2 siRNA, IKKα siRNA, rapamycin or LY294002 to check that the TβRI effect on NF-κB needs the AKT/mTOR/IKK axis, using TNF-induced NF-κB (rapamycin-insensitive) as a specificity control.

citations.title: TGF-beta coordinately activates TAK1/MEK/AKT/NFkB and SMAD pathways to promote osteoclast survival.
TGF-β and NF-κB signal pathway cross-talk is mediated through TAK1 and SMAD7 in a subset of head and neck cancers.
TGF-{beta}1 activates two distinct type I receptors in neurons: implications for neuronal NF-{kappa}B signaling.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the plain-language mechanism (TGF-β receptor → PI3K/Akt → IKK → NF-κB), the entities together (TGFBR1/ALK5 + NF-κB + mTOR/Raptor/IKKα, incl. PC3/prostate context), and the prediction (constitutively active TβRI or TβRI knockdown/inhibitor changing NF-κB reporter, DNA binding and target genes such as XIAP/cIAP1). The general mechanism is published: Gingery et al. report that TGF-β acting through the canonical TGF-β receptor complex triggers AKT and IKK/IκB phosphorylation and NF-κB activation, with AKT and IKK/NF-κB inhibition abolishing the response, and Freudlsperger et al. show TGF-β-induced NF-κB reporter, DNA binding and target-gene transcription (via TAK1). However, no retrieved source connects TβRI to the Akt2/mTOR–Raptor-dependent, rapamycin-sensitive NF-κB output described in the corpus, and König et al. directly tested constitutively active ALK5 (TβRI) on NF-κB reporter/gelshift activity in neurons and found it failed to reproduce the TGF-β1 effect, attributing NF-κB activation to ALK1 instead — a contrary result for one arm of the prediction rather than a refutation of the Akt-route claim, so the status is partial.

hypotheses.statement: SHP2 phosphatase activity is an upstream positive regulator of MEK activation in EGF/RTK-driven cells, acting through Ras rather than on MEK directly.
hypotheses.mechanism: Claims about SHP2 place it upstream of Ras: catalytically inactive SHP2 reduces EGF-induced Ras-GTP and ERK activation, it cannot block V12-Ras-driven ERK activation, and KRASG12V restores p-ERK after SHP2 knockdown. Independent claims about MEK place its activation downstream of the Ras/Raf level (c-Raf inhibition eliminates MEK and ERK activity) and show that MEK activity is required for ERK phosphorylation. Together these imply that SHP2 loss should lower MEK activation as a consequence of lower Ras-GTP, with no SHP2 requirement once Ras is constitutively active.
hypotheses.prediction: In EGF-stimulated, RTK-dependent cells, SHP2 knockdown or expression of catalytically inactive SHP2 (C/S or R/E) will reduce and shorten activation-loop phospho-MEK in parallel with p-ERK. Wild-type but not catalytically dead SHP2 will restore phospho-MEK, and constitutively active Ras (V12-H-Ras or KRASG12V) will restore it even without SHP2. If phospho-MEK is unchanged while p-ERK falls, the hypothesis is ruled out.
hypotheses.test: In COS-1 or MDA-MB-468 cells, deplete SHP2 with inducible shRNA or express C/S-SHP2, stimulate with EGF over a time course (0-60 min), and immunoblot for phospho-MEK, total MEK, p-ERK and Ras-GTP (GST-Raf-RBD pulldown). Repeat with re-expression of shRNA-resistant WT or C459S SHP2, and with co-expression of V12-Ras, to test the epistasis.

citations.title: Molecular mechanism for the Shp-2 tyrosine phosphatase function in promoting growth factor stimulation of Erk activity.
Multiple requirements for SHPTP2 in epidermal growth factor-mediated cell cycle progression.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the mechanism in plain words (SHP2 phosphatase upstream of Ras controlling MEK/ERK after EGF), the entities together (SHP2 knockdown/catalytically-dead SHP2 with phospho-MEK and RAS-GTP readouts, including SHP099/RMC-4550 studies), and the epistasis prediction (constitutively active RAS conferring insensitivity to SHP2 loss), plus a deliberate search for a stated negative (SHP2 acting downstream of Ras / at Raf without changing Ras-GTP). Cunnick et al. (MCB 2000) already reports exactly this explanation: EGF-stimulated Ras, Raf and MEK activation are all significantly attenuated and shortened in Shp-2 mutant cells, and the authors conclude Shp-2 acts upstream of Ras, working via a Gab1 complex substrate rather than on MEK itself; Bennett et al. (MCB 1996) independently establishes the catalytic-activity requirement and the Ras epistasis (dominant-negative SHP2 blocks EGF-induced MAP kinase but not activated-Ras-driven signalling). No source tested this claim and found it fails, and the later allosteric-inhibitor literature is concordant, so this is established rather than open or refuted.

hypotheses.statement: TGFBR2 negatively regulates GSK3B: TGF-β engagement of TβRII activates PI3K/AKT, which inhibits GSK3β kinase activity and so reduces GSK3β-dependent Thr66 phosphorylation of Smad3.
hypotheses.mechanism: The PI3K regulatory subunit p85 associates constitutively with TβRII, and TGF-β activates AKT (derynck2019:findings:032). Independently, AKT is reported to inhibit GSK3β in insulin-treated cells and in T cells (haeusler2018:findings:007, hogan2003:findings:006). GSK3β phosphorylates Smad3 at Thr66 to drive its turnover, and TGF-β releases Smad3 from the Axin/GSK3β complex (guo2008:findings:018, guo2008:findings:009), which is consistent with receptor-initiated suppression of GSK3β action.
hypotheses.prediction: TGF-β stimulation should acutely increase AKT-dependent inhibitory phosphorylation of GSK3β, lower GSK3β kinase activity and lower Smad3 Thr66 phosphorylation. These effects should be lost with TGFBR2 knockdown or kinase-defective TβRII, and blocked by the PI3K inhibitor LY294002. If GSK3β activity and Smad3 pT66 do not change with TGF-β or TGFBR2 loss, the hypothesis is ruled out.
hypotheses.test: In HaCaT or HepG2 cells with or without TGFBR2 shRNA/CRISPR knockout (rescued with wild-type or kinase-defective TβRII), run a TGF-β time course with or without LY294002 or an AKT inhibitor. Immunoblot for phospho-AKT, inhibitory phospho-GSK3β and Smad3 pT66. In parallel, immunoprecipitate GSK3β and measure its activity in an in vitro kinase assay on a primed peptide or recombinant Smad3 substrate.

citations.title: Chronic TGFβ stimulation promotes the metastatic potential of lung cancer cells by Snail protein stabilization through integrin β3-Akt-GSK3β signaling.
Axin and GSK3- control Smad3 protein stability and modulate TGF- signaling.
TGFbeta intercepts nuclear glycogen synthase kinase 3beta to inhibit PDGF-induced DNA synthesis in mesangial cells.
Non-canonical Smads phosphorylation induced by the glutamate release inhibitor, riluzole, through GSK3 activation in melanoma.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the mechanism in words (TGF-β → PI3K/AKT → inhibitory Ser9 phosphorylation of GSK3β), the entities together (TGFBR2/p85, GSK3β, Smad3 Thr66, LY294002), and the prediction (loss of Smad3 pT66 upon TGF-β or receptor loss). The component links are published separately — chronic TGFβ raising Akt activity and inhibitory GSK3β Ser9 phosphorylation to stabilize a GSK3β substrate (Snail) via integrin β3, and Axin/GSK3β phosphorylating Smad3 at Thr66 to drive its degradation — but no retrieved source states that TβRII-initiated PI3K/AKT signalling suppresses GSK3β activity and thereby lowers Smad3 Thr66 phosphorylation, and the Smad3-stability paper attributes TGF-β-induced release of Smad3 from Axin/GSK3β to complex dissociation rather than to loss of GSK3β activity. Notably, the nearest direct test found the opposite sign in mesangial cells: TGF-β blocked Akt-mediated Ser9 phosphorylation and so prevented GSK3β inactivation, so the specific receptor-to-pT66 claim is neither established nor cleanly refuted.

hypotheses.statement: LPS activates mTORC1 through EGFR-dependent ERK signalling that leads to phosphorylation of Raptor by ERK1/2 (and RSK).
hypotheses.mechanism: LPS induces ERK and AKT phosphorylation in HME and A549 cells, and this requires EGFR expression and kinase activity (de2015). Separately, ERK1/2- and RSK-mediated Raptor phosphorylation raises mTORC1 kinase activity toward 4E-BP1, and MEK1/2 inhibitors abolish that activity (carriere2010, foster2009). Together these imply that LPS-driven ERK activation should feed into Raptor phosphorylation and increase mTORC1 activity.
hypotheses.prediction: LPS treatment of HME or A549 cells should increase Raptor phosphorylation at the ERK/RSK sites and raise mTORC1 output (4E-BP1 Thr37/Thr46 and S6K1 phosphorylation). This increase should be blocked by erlotinib, EGFR knockdown or a MEK1/2 inhibitor, and blunted in cells expressing the phosphorylation-deficient Raptor S3A mutant.
hypotheses.test: Stimulate A549 or HME cells with LPS over a time course and immunoblot for phospho-ERK, phospho-Raptor, phospho-4E-BP1 (Thr37/Thr46) and phospho-S6K1, with and without erlotinib, U0126 or rapamycin pretreatment. Then immunoprecipitate mTORC1 from LPS-treated cells expressing wild-type or S3A Raptor and run an in vitro kinase assay on GST-4E-BP1. No LPS-induced rise in mTORC1 activity, or a rise that is insensitive to MEK inhibition and to the S3A mutation, would rule the hypothesis out.

citations.title: LPS Induces mTORC1 and mTORC2 Activation During Monocyte Adhesion.
Cot/tpl2-MKK1/2-Erk1/2 controls mTORC1-mediated mRNA translation in Toll-like receptor-activated macrophages.
TLR4 counteracts BVRA signaling in human leukocytes via differential regulation of AMPK, mTORC1 and mTORC2.

novelty.note: I searched for LPS/TLR4-driven mTORC1 activation via MEK/ERK, for ERK/RSK-mediated Raptor phosphorylation in innate-immune settings, and for EGFR-dependence of LPS-induced mTOR signalling (erlotinib, A549/airway epithelium). The two arms exist separately in print: LPS activates mTORC1/S6K through a MEK/ERK axis (shown in monocytes, via TSC2 Ser664 with S6K as readout, no Raptor or EGFR analysis), and TLR4-driven ERK1/2 controls RSK, S6 and 4E-BP phosphorylation and cap-dependent translation in macrophages; the closest LPS-to-Raptor link found is dephosphorylation of Raptor Ser792 via MMP9, a different site and mechanism from the ERK/RSK proline-directed sites. No retrieved source states the specific chain LPS → EGFR → ERK1/2 → Raptor phosphorylation → mTORC1 output in HME or A549 cells, and none reports a negative test of it, so the mechanism is partially published but this specific prediction and connection is not.
