hypotheses.statement: RSK1 (RPS6KA1) directly phosphorylates STAT3 on a serine residue after growth-factor stimulation, thereby modulating STAT3 DNA binding and transcriptional activity.
hypotheses.mechanism: RSK1 is a serine-preferring kinase that moves from the cytoplasm to the nucleus on ERK1/2 stimulation and directly phosphorylates regulatory serines on signalling substrates such as IRS-1 Ser-1101. STAT3 is phosphorylated in response to EGF, and its DNA binding and transactivation are controlled by serine phosphorylation (Ser727, shown for PKCδ). A mitogen-activated serine kinase that enters the nucleus is therefore a candidate for STAT3 serine phosphorylation downstream of EGF, though the cited claims do not establish that any STAT3 serine matches the RSK1 consensus motif.
hypotheses.prediction: Active RSK1, but not kinase-dead RSK1, should phosphorylate recombinant STAT3 on serine in vitro, with a serine-to-alanine mutant of the target site not phosphorylated. In EGF-stimulated cells, BI-D1870 or dominant-negative RSK1 should reduce STAT3 serine phosphorylation and alter SIE-binding or STAT3 reporter activity, without the loss of STAT3 tyrosine phosphorylation that upstream receptor inhibition would cause.
hypotheses.test: Run an in vitro phosphotransferase assay with HA-RSK1 (wild-type or kinase-dead) immunoprecipitated from PMA- or EGF-stimulated HEK293 cells and recombinant GST-STAT3 (wild-type or Ser727Ala), read out by phospho-serine STAT3 immunoblot. In parallel, treat EGF-stimulated cultured cells with BI-D1870 or SL0101, or RSK1 siRNA or dominant-negative RSK1, and measure STAT3 Ser727 and tyrosine phosphorylation by Western blot and STAT3 activity by SIE bandshift or luciferase reporter. No in vitro phosphorylation, together with no change in STAT3 serine phosphorylation on RSK inhibition, would rule the hypothesis out.

citations.title: Ataxia telangiectasia mutated proteins, MAPKs, and RSK2 are involved in the phosphorylation of STAT3.
Nuclear RSK1 mediates interferon-γ-induced proinflammatory activation in human primary macrophages and humanized mice.
STAT3 serine phosphorylation by ERK-dependent and -independent pathways negatively modulates its tyrosine phosphorylation.

novelty.note: I searched PubMed and Europe PMC for RSK/p90RSK/RPS6KA1 with STAT3 and Ser727, for RSK inhibitors (BI-D1870, SL0101) with STAT3 serine phosphorylation, and for the prediction (nuclear mitogen-activated serine kinase as a STAT Ser727 kinase). Zhang et al. (2003) already place an RSK family member upstream of STAT3 Ser727: RSK2-deficient cells fail to phosphorylate STAT3 Ser727 after UVA, rescue by full-length RSK2 restores it, and RSK2-mediated Ser727 phosphorylation is required for STAT3 transcriptional activity — but that work used RSK2 and UVA rather than RSK1 and growth factor, and notably active RSK2 phosphorylated only STAT3 immunoprecipitates and not GST-STAT3 pull-downs, i.e. no clean direct phosphorylation of recombinant STAT3. The closest RSK1-specific work shows nuclear RSK1 driving STAT1 (not STAT3) Ser727 phosphorylation after IFN-γ, and the classic growth-factor work assigns STAT3 Ser727 to ERK itself; so the mechanism is published in part, while the specific RSK1/EGF-STAT3 link and direct in vitro phosphorylation remain unstated and untested, and I found no paper reporting a negative test of it.

hypotheses.statement: In HeLa cells, RPS6KA3 (RSK2) is an ERK-pathway-activated kinase whose EGF-induced nuclear import depends on Src-family-mediated tyrosine phosphorylation at Y529 and the ERK binding this promotes.
hypotheses.mechanism: Fractionation proteomics in HeLa cells found nuclear import of RPS6KA3 after EGF stimulation (itzhak2016:findings:011). Separately, EGF treatment of 293T and COS7 cells causes RSK2 Y529 phosphorylation by Src family kinases, which facilitates ERK binding to RSK2 (kang2009:context:001), and such tyrosine phosphorylation stabilises ERK1/2 binding and promotes RSK2 activation (cargnello2011:findings:059). Together these suggest the HeLa relocalisation is downstream of the same Src-to-Y529-to-ERK-binding step.
hypotheses.prediction: In EGF-stimulated HeLa cells, RSK2 becomes phosphorylated at Y529, and Src inhibition or a Y529F substitution reduces both ERK-RSK2 co-precipitation and the EGF-induced increase of RSK2 in the nuclear fraction. MEK inhibition should likewise blunt the nuclear accumulation.
hypotheses.test: Serum-starve HeLa cells and stimulate with EGF with or without the Src inhibitor PP2 or the MEK inhibitor U0126. Then perform nuclear/cytosolic fractionation with RSK2 immunoblotting and phospho-Y529 blotting. In parallel, express tagged WT and Y529F RSK2 in HeLa and compare EGF-induced nuclear localisation by immunofluorescence and ERK co-immunoprecipitation.

citations.title: Epidermal growth factor stimulates RSK2 activation through activation of the MEK/ERK pathway and src-dependent tyrosine phosphorylation of RSK2 at Tyr-529.
FGFR3 activates RSK2 to mediate hematopoietic transformation through tyrosine phosphorylation of RSK2 and activation of the MEK/ERK pathway.
Nuclear localization and regulation of erk- and rsk-encoded protein kinases.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the plain-language mechanism (Src-family tyrosine phosphorylation of RSK2 promoting ERK binding), the entities together (RSK2 Y529 + Src/PP2 + EGF + nuclear translocation, including Y529F localization), and the prediction (MEK/U0126 or Src dependence of RSK2 nuclear import) via Europe PMC and PMC. The upstream mechanism is fully published — Kang et al. show EGF-induced, Src/Fyn-dependent RSK2 Y529 phosphorylation in cells lacking FGFR3 that facilitates inactive ERK binding and RSK2 activation (PP2-sensitive), and the FGFR3 work establishes the Y529/ERK-binding step — while Chen et al. separately show that growth-factor stimulation of HeLa cells drives MAP-kinase-dependent activation and concurrent nuclear entry of RSK. However, no retrieved source connects the two, i.e. none states or tests that EGF-induced nuclear import of RPS6KA3 requires Y529 phosphorylation or Src activity (no Y529F/PP2 fractionation or localization experiment was found), and no source reports a negative test of that link, so this is partial rather than established or refuted.

hypotheses.statement: In HeLa cells, RPS6KA3 (RSK2) is a contributing isoform to the MEK/ERK-dependent RSK hydrophobic-motif phosphorylation that rises on glucose and glutamine withdrawal.
hypotheses.mechanism: In HeLa cells, RSK hydrophobic-motif phosphorylation is MEK-dependent (chou2020:findings:003) and increases on glucose/glutamine withdrawal together with ERK1/2 phosphorylation (chou2020:findings:007), but these readouts do not identify the RSK isoform. RPS6KA3 is present and signal-responsive in HeLa (itzhak2016:findings:011), and RSK2 activation is read out by S386 phosphorylation and driven by the MEK/ERK pathway (kang2009:findings:006, kang2009:context:000). This makes RSK2 a plausible carrier of part of the HeLa signal.
hypotheses.prediction: RSK2 immunoprecipitated from glucose/glutamine-starved HeLa cells shows increased, U0126-sensitive hydrophobic-motif (S386) phosphorylation. RSK2-specific knockdown measurably reduces the total phospho-hydrophobic-motif RSK band induced by nutrient withdrawal.
hypotheses.test: Withdraw glucose and glutamine from HeLa cultures with or without U0126, immunoprecipitate endogenous RSK2, and immunoblot for hydrophobic-motif phosphorylation. In parallel, knock down RPS6KA3 by siRNA (with RSK1 knockdown as comparison) and quantify the remaining phospho-hydrophobic-motif RSK signal in whole lysates.

citations.title: mTORC2 Is Involved in the Induction of RSK Phosphorylation by Serum or Nutrient Starvation.
Cellular stress induces non-canonical activation of the receptor tyrosine kinase EphA2 through the p38-MK2-RSK signaling pathway.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the mechanism in plain words (RSK hydrophobic-motif phosphorylation on glucose/glutamine withdrawal in HeLa), the entities together (RPS6KA3/RSK2 + HeLa + Ser380/Ser386 + U0126/MEK), and the prediction (isoform-specific siRNA or immunoprecipitation resolving which RSK isoform carries the pHM signal). The component parts are published — Chou et al. report MEK/U0126-dependent pHM RSK rising with ERK1/2 phosphorylation on combined glucose/glutamine withdrawal in HeLa but explicitly use a pan-reactive pS380 readout and never resolve isoforms (no RSK2/S386, no isoform knockdown), while independent work immunoprecipitates endogenous RSK1 and RSK2 separately from HeLa and shows RSK2 Ser386 is a bona fide hydrophobic-motif site downstream of upstream kinases, with the ERK-driven C-terminal-kinase route to Ser386 being canonical. No source attributes any part of the nutrient-withdrawal pHM signal to RSK2 specifically, and none reports a negative test of that attribution, so this is partial rather than established or refuted.

hypotheses.statement: Insulin (INS) activates SHP2, and SHP2 catalytic activity is required for insulin's amplification of EGF-induced Ras/ERK activation.
hypotheses.mechanism: Insulin alone barely activates ERK but enhances EGF-induced ERK, with the crosstalk located upstream of Ras and at the Ras/Raf level rather than at the receptors; insulin also drives tyrosine phosphorylation of IRS1 and GAB1. Independently, SHP2 acts upstream of Ras, its catalytic activity enhances and prolongs EGF-induced Ras-GTP and ERK activation, and it is activated about 100-fold when its tandem SH2 domains bind a ligand. The proposed link is that insulin-induced phosphotyrosine sites engage SHP2's SH2 domains and raise its activity at the same upstream-of-Ras step where insulin's synergy with EGF arises; the cited claims do not show SHP2 binding to these scaffolds, so that step is the inference under test.
hypotheses.prediction: Insulin stimulation should increase SHP2 phosphatase activity and SHP2 association with tyrosine-phosphorylated IRS1/GAB1. SHP2 knockdown or expression of catalytically inactive C/S-SHP2 should abolish the insulin-dependent increment in Ras-GTP and phospho-ERK at low EGF doses. Constitutively active V12-Ras should make ERK activation insensitive to SHP2 loss.
hypotheses.test: In HEK293 cells, stimulate with low-dose EGF, insulin, or both, after SHP2 siRNA/shRNA knockdown or expression of WT- versus C/S-SHP2 (with shRNA-resistant WT rescue). Measure Ras-GTP by GST-Raf-RBD pulldown and phospho-ERK by immunoblot, and compare the insulin-dependent increment over EGF alone across conditions. In parallel, immunoprecipitate SHP2 from cells with or without insulin, assay its in vitro phosphatase activity, and blot for co-precipitating phospho-IRS1 and phospho-GAB1.

citations.title: Systems-level interactions between insulin-EGF networks amplify mitogenic signaling.
Role of SH-PTP2, a protein-tyrosine phosphatase with Src homology 2 domains, in insulin-stimulated Ras activation.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the mechanism in plain words (insulin-induced pTyr on IRS1/GAB1 recruiting and activating SHP2 upstream of Ras), the entities together (SHP2 + insulin + EGF + ERK synergy in HEK293), and the prediction (catalytically inactive SHP2 / knockdown abolishing insulin-stimulated Ras-GTP). Borisov et al. 2009 — the corpus paper itself — explicitly names SHP2, together with GAB1 and IRS, as the critical network node that converts the insulin-induced PIP3 rise into enhanced Ras/ERK activity in exactly the HEK293 low-EGF-plus-insulin setting, i.e. it already states this explanation for this phenomenon (though its SHP2 role is model-based, with the experimental perturbations done on GAB1/IRS). Noguchi et al. 1994 independently establishes the experimental half: insulin drives SHP2 binding to IRS-1 through its SH2 domains, and the catalytically inactive Cys459Ser mutant markedly attenuates insulin-stimulated Ras and MAP kinase activation. No source was found reporting a direct negative test, so the status is established rather than refuted or open; the untested residue is only the insulin-over-EGF increment measured under SHP2 loss.

hypotheses.statement: SRC acts as an upstream positive regulator of mTORC1, with SRC activity promoting growth-factor-stimulated mTORC1 kinase activity through ERK1/2- and RSK-dependent phosphorylation of Raptor.
hypotheses.mechanism: The claims about SRC show it is required for EGF-induced ERK (and AKT) phosphorylation (SRC-family inhibition with PP2 eliminates it, and Src RNAi lowers GAB1 phosphorylation and phospho-ERK), and that Src-dependent tyrosine phosphorylation of RSK2 stabilises ERK1/2 binding and promotes RSK2 activation. Independently, the claims about mTORC1 show that RSK and ERK1/2 phosphorylate Raptor, that this phosphorylation is needed for full mTORC1 kinase activity towards 4E-BP1, and that MEK1/2 inhibition abolishes mTORC1 kinase activity. Together these imply that SRC activity sets the level of the ERK/RSK input onto Raptor and therefore of mTORC1 activity.
hypotheses.prediction: In EGF-stimulated HEK293 cells, Src knockdown or SRC-family inhibition should reduce Raptor phosphorylation at the ERK/RSK sites, 4E-BP1 Thr37/Thr46 and S6K1 phosphorylation, and Raptor-associated mTOR kinase activity in vitro. This loss should be rescued by constitutively active MEK or RSK, and Src inhibition should cause no further reduction in cells expressing the phosphorylation-deficient Raptor S3A mutant.
hypotheses.test: Treat HEK293 cells with Src siRNA or PP2 (versus controls), stimulate with EGF, and immunoblot for phospho-ERK, phospho-RSK, phospho-Raptor, phospho-4E-BP1 (Thr37/Thr46) and phospho-S6K1. Immunoprecipitate Raptor and run an in vitro mTOR kinase assay with GST-4E-BP1 as substrate. Then repeat with co-expression of constitutively active MEK/RSK, and in cells expressing wild-type versus S3A Raptor, to test whether the SRC effect on mTORC1 runs through ERK/RSK-dependent Raptor phosphorylation.

citations.title: Regulation of mTORC1 signaling by Src kinase activity is Akt1-independent in RSV-transformed cells.
Inhibition of mTORC1 by SU6656, the selective Src kinase inhibitor, is not accompanied by activation of Akt/PKB signalling in melanoma cells.
Src regulates amino acid-mediated mTORC1 activation by disrupting GATOR1-Rag GTPase interaction.

novelty.note: I searched for Src as an upstream regulator of mTORC1, for the Src→ERK/RSK→Raptor chain in plain words, and for the prediction (Src inhibition/PP2/dasatinib reducing raptor phosphorylation, 4E-BP1 Thr37/46, S6K1 and Raptor-associated mTOR kinase activity), using web search plus Europe PMC full-text queries. The component halves are published separately: Src kinase activity is reported to be required for mTORC1 signalling to S6K1 and 4E-BP1 (Akt1-independently) and Src is found associated with raptor in the mTORC1 complex, while a separate line of work places Src upstream of the Rag GTPases via GATOR1 dissociation for amino-acid-stimulated mTORC1; none of the retrieved papers attributes Src's effect on mTORC1 to ERK1/2- or RSK-dependent raptor phosphorylation, and no paper tested Src inhibition against the raptor ERK/RSK sites or the S3A mutant. Hence partial rather than established; notably the GATOR1 paper states that insulin regulation of mTORC1 was independent of Src activity, which pulls against the growth-factor framing but is not a direct test of the EGF/ERK/RSK/raptor route claimed here, so it does not amount to refutation.

hypotheses.statement: BCL2, as an NF-κB-induced gene product, inhibits prolonged TNF-induced JNK activation.
hypotheses.mechanism: Bcl-2 is reported as one of a set of NF-κB target genes whose expression falls when NF-κB activation is reduced by mTOR/Raptor knockdown. Independently, TNF-induced JNK activation is stronger and more prolonged in cells lacking NF-κB, and several NF-κB-activated gene products inhibit that JNK activation. Sustained late-phase JNK/c-Jun phosphorylation after TNF is associated with caspase-3 and PARP cleavage. Together these make BCL2 a candidate for one of the NF-κB-induced products that restrains JNK activation, though no cited claim names it as such.
hypotheses.prediction: In NF-κB-deficient cells, enforced BCL2 expression should shorten and weaken late-phase TNF-induced JNK and c-Jun phosphorylation. In NF-κB-competent cells, BCL2 knockdown or inhibition should prolong TNF-induced JNK phosphorylation. If BCL2 only acts downstream of JNK, JNK phosphorylation kinetics would be unchanged even if cell death is altered.
hypotheses.test: In a cultured cell line, block NF-κB (e.g. IκBα super-repressor or IKK inhibitor), with or without ectopic BCL2 expression. In parallel, knock down BCL2 by siRNA in NF-κB-competent cells. Stimulate with TNFα over a time course (0–8 h) and western blot for phospho-JNK, total JNK, phospho-c-Jun, and cleaved PARP/caspase-3. Include a pan-caspase inhibitor arm to separate a direct effect on JNK activation from an indirect effect via blocked caspase activity.

citations.title: Sustained JNK activation in response to tumor necrosis factor is mediated by caspases in a cell type-specific manner.
Inhibition of JNK activation through NF-kappaB target genes.

novelty.note: I searched for (a) NF-κB target gene products that restrain prolonged TNF-induced JNK activation, (b) Bcl-2 together with TNF/JNK/NF-κB, and (c) the specific prediction that enforced Bcl-2 shortens late-phase JNK in NF-κB-blocked cells. The general mechanism is well established but the canonical NF-κB-induced JNK inhibitors named in the literature are XIAP, GADD45β, A20 and c-FLIP-L, not BCL2; Tang et al. (Nature 2001) state the NF-κB-target-gene mechanism via XIAP. One paper (Wicovsky et al., JBC 2007) directly overexpressed Bcl2 in NF-κB-inhibited KB and HaCaT cells and reports that Bcl2 (like zVAD-fmk and FLIP-L) differentially blocked the transient versus sustained phases of TNF-induced JNK activation, concluding sustained JNK is caspase/ROS-mediated — i.e. the first limb of the prediction is published, but as a caspase-dependent effect rather than as Bcl-2 acting as the NF-κB-induced JNK brake, and the BCL2-knockdown limb was not found. Hence partial rather than established or refuted.

hypotheses.statement: The paradoxical increase in uORF-mRNA translation during the ISR may reflect a generic sensitivity of uORF-containing leaders to any reduction in initiation rate, rather than a mechanism specific to eIF2α Ser51 phosphorylation and eIF2B blockade.
hypotheses.mechanism: statzer2022:findings:000 shows a Patf-4(uORF)::GFP reporter is induced when translation is lowered by cycloheximide, with only a 1.5-fold change in atf-4 mRNA, so reporter gain is translational and does not require an eIF2α kinase. ivashkiv2014:findings:025 shows translation can also be lowered at a different step, by IFIT1/IFIT2 blocking eIF3-mediated preinitiation complex formation, independently of the PKR/eIF2α arm. Together they imply that lowering initiation flux by any route is sufficient for the selective uORF bypass the anomaly attributes to eIF2α-P.
hypotheses.prediction: Reducing initiation through a non-eIF2α node (eIF3/PIC formation or elongation slowdown) should induce the uORF reporter to a similar degree as eIF2α-kinase activation, and the induction should persist in eIF2α phospho-defective backgrounds.
hypotheses.test: In a cell line stably carrying the ATF4-uORF reporter plus a uORF-less control reporter, compare induction after (a) an eIF2α-kinase activator (tunicamycin or thapsigargin), (b) low-dose cycloheximide, and (c) IFIT1/IFIT2 overexpression or eIF3 subunit knockdown, each titrated to matched global translation inhibition measured by puromycin incorporation; repeat in an eIF2α-S51A knock-in clone. Equal reporter induction at matched global inhibition, retained in S51A cells, supports flux-sensing; loss of induction in S51A cells supports strict eIF2α-P dependence.

citations.title: ATF-4 and hydrogen sulfide signalling mediate longevity in response to inhibition of translation or mTORC1.
Eukaryotic Initiation Factor 5B (eIF5B) Cooperates with eIF1A and eIF5 to Facilitate uORF2-Mediated Repression of ATF4 Translation.
mTORC1 Balances Cellular Amino Acid Supply with Demand for Protein Synthesis through Post-transcriptional Control of ATF4.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the plain-language mechanism (uORF/ATF4 induction by reduced initiation independent of eIF2α-P), the entities together (ATF4/GCN4 uORF reporters with eIF3, eIF5B, eIF4E/4E-BP, cycloheximide, IFIT1), and the prediction (induction retained in eIF2α-S51A or phospho-defective backgrounds at matched global inhibition). The eIF2α-P-independent part is published: Statzer et al. report that several translation-lowering treatments (cycloheximide, ifg-1/eIF4G knockdown, tRNA synthetase knockdown) raise ATF-4 without canonical ISR induction and that the effect persists in an eIF2α phospho-defective mutant, and depletion of eIF5B/eIF1A/eIF5 de-represses ATF4 in human cells with unchanged eIF2α phosphorylation. However, no source states the generic flux-sensing claim as such or tests equal induction across nodes at matched global inhibition, and work at the eIF4F node points the other way (mTOR inhibition lowers initiation yet reduces ATF4 in a uORF-dependent manner), so the specific prediction is neither established nor directly refuted.

hypotheses.statement: An mTOR-dependent selective-translation arm may account for the eIF2α-independent portion of the paradoxical selective translation, with mTOR activity state determining which mRNAs stay translated when global synthesis falls.
hypotheses.mechanism: statzer2022:findings:023 reports that knocking down the mTORC2 subunit rict-1 suppresses global translation and raises the ATF-4 uORF reporter independently of eIF2α phosphorylation. ivashkiv2014:findings:026 reports that mTOR signalling through S6 kinase and eIF4 factors promotes translation of a select subset of mRNAs. Combined, mTOR output can both lower global synthesis and re-specify which transcripts are loaded, providing a selectivity mechanism not routed through eIF2B.
hypotheses.prediction: Pharmacological mTOR inhibition should reproduce selective uORF-reporter induction while suppressing bulk synthesis, and combining mTOR inhibition with eIF2α-kinase activation should give more than additive uORF reporter output, since the two act on different selectivity nodes.
hypotheses.test: Perform polysome profiling plus reporter quantification in cells treated with torin1, an eIF2α-kinase activator, or both; sequence polysome-associated mRNA to score whether the set of transcripts retained on polysomes under torin1 overlaps or is distinct from the set retained under eIF2α-kinase activation. Distinct retained-transcript sets with additive uORF reporter output support a separate mTOR selectivity arm; identical sets argue the two converge on one initiation-limited mechanism.

citations.title: mTORC1 Balances Cellular Amino Acid Supply with Demand for Protein Synthesis through Post-transcriptional Control of ATF4.
ATF-4 and hydrogen sulfide signalling mediate longevity in response to inhibition of translation or mTORC1.
A unifying model for mTORC1-mediated regulation of mRNA translation.
Targeted profiling of RNA translation reveals mTOR-4EBP1/2-independent translation regulation of mRNAs encoding ribosomal proteins.

novelty.note: I searched for mTOR-dependent selective translation, eIF2α-independent uORF control of ATF4, Torin1 ribosome-profiling of retained transcripts, and for combined mTOR-inhibitor plus ISR-activator experiments. The eIF2α-independent mTOR arm acting on uORF-mediated ATF4 translation is explicitly published (Park et al. 2017, via 4E-BPs, in GCN2-null cells with no change in eIF2α phosphorylation), and Torin1 ribosome profiling already defines the transcript set whose translation is mTOR-specific (Thoreen et al. 2012); the C. elegans source paper itself shows mTORC1 (raga-1/ragc-1) knockdown raising the uORF reporter while global synthesis falls, with eIF2α phosphorylation blocked. What I did not find is a test of the specific prediction — greater-than-additive uORF reporter output from mTOR inhibition plus eIF2α-kinase activation, and whether the polysome-retained sets under the two treatments are distinct — and the sign of the mTOR effect on the ATF4 uORF reporter is opposite in mammalian cells (Torin1 depletes ATF4) versus worms, so the specific prediction is unsettled rather than established.

hypotheses.statement: Whether TβRII is seen as ligand-independent homomers or as ligand-induced dimers depends on its cell-surface density, and surface density can be shifted acutely by the insulin–Akt–AS160 trafficking pathway without any change in total expression.
hypotheses.mechanism: The copatching, double-IP and sedimentation studies that found preformed TβRII homomers used transient overexpression (zhang2009a:context:000). The single-molecule imaging used near-endogenous levels, where TGF-β drives TβRII dimerization independently of TβRI, consistent with the dimeric ligand recruiting a pair of TβRII (zhang2009a:findings:006; sorrentino2008:context:001). Insulin, or silencing of AS160, rapidly raises surface TβRI and TβRII without changing total abundance (budi2015:findings:001, budi2015:findings:011). This gives a way to raise receptor density in the same cells, so the density explanation for the discrepancy can be tested directly rather than inferred by comparing studies.
hypotheses.prediction: In cells expressing near-endogenous TβRII, the ligand-independent homomeric fraction should rise when surface receptor density is raised by insulin or AS160 knockdown, and fall when density is kept low.
hypotheses.test: Stably express tagged TβRII at low levels in NMuMG cells. Treat with insulin or AS160 siRNA (with control siRNA and GDC0941 or AktVIII to block the increase), without adding TGF-β. Confirm the rise in surface receptor by cell-surface biotinylation. Then compare the fraction of TβRII homomers by membrane-impermeable crosslinking (BS3) followed by non-reducing SDS-PAGE and immunoblotting, and by antibody copatching immunofluorescence. The density hypothesis predicts more homomers when surface levels rise and no change when the rise is blocked. A density-independent model predicts no difference between conditions.

citations.title: Single-molecule imaging reveals transforming growth factor-beta-induced type II receptor dimerization.
TGF-β signalling is mediated by two autonomously functioning TβRI:TβRII pairs.
The insulin response integrates increased TGF-β signaling through Akt-induced enhancement of cell surface delivery of TGF-β receptors.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the expression-level/surface-density explanation for the conflicting TβRII oligomerization data, the single-molecule TβRII dimerization work and its reception, and the insulin–Akt–AS160 receptor-trafficking pathway combined with receptor oligomerization/crosslinking. The density (expression-level) explanation for why biochemical studies saw preformed ligand-independent TβRII homomers while single-molecule imaging at near-endogenous levels saw ligand-induced dimerization is explicitly published — the single-molecule paper itself tested expression level and concluded that expression level determines oligomerization status, and the 2011 EMBO J study restates this attribution of the discrepancy. What I found no published statement or test of is the second half: that acute, trafficking-driven shifts in surface density (insulin, or AS160 silencing, with no change in total abundance) would raise the ligand-independent homomeric fraction; the trafficking paper characterizes surface delivery and responsiveness but does not address receptor oligomeric state. Hence partial, not established, and nothing tested and negated this specific prediction.

hypotheses.statement: JAK1's 100-fold reduced mobility reflects stable, non-exchanging binding to the receptor cytoplasmic Box1/Box2 region rather than any intrinsic membrane affinity of JAK1 itself, so JAK1 effectively diffuses as part of a receptor complex.
hypotheses.mechanism: The non-receptor-binding Jak1 mutant L80A/Y81A loses membrane localization and instead distributes through the cytoplasm, showing membrane residence is conferred by receptor binding (behrmann2004:findings:010). Structurally, the receptor Box1/Box2 peptide occupies an extended groove on the JAK1 FERM-SH2 module burying ~1650 Å2 with hydrophobic insertion and salt-bridge contacts, an interface large enough to support a long-lived complex (glassman2022:findings:004). If JAK1 is essentially permanently docked on a transmembrane receptor, its diffusion coefficient must equal the receptor's, which is ~100-fold below a free cytoplasmic protein.
hypotheses.prediction: Mobility should scale with receptor occupancy: JAK1 carrying FERM-pocket or Box2-contact point mutations (e.g., disrupting the Val194/Phe247/Phe251 pocket or the Glu284–His509 salt bridge equivalent) should recover with cytoplasmic-like kinetics, while wild-type JAK1 recovery should remain indistinguishable from the receptor's, and JAK1 mobility should increase when receptor is limiting.
hypotheses.test: Perform FRAP on cells co-expressing receptor-CFP with a panel of JAK1-YFP FERM/SH2 interface point mutants of graded affinity, and independently titrate receptor expression; measure recovery half-life and mobile fraction against co-immunoprecipitation-determined binding for each mutant. A monotonic relationship between interface binding and immobility supports docking-driven immobility; mutants that lose receptor binding yet stay slow would instead indicate an intrinsic membrane anchor.

citations.title: Long term association of the cytokine receptor gp130 and the Janus kinase Jak1 revealed by FRAP analysis.

Janus kinase (Jak) subcellular localization revisited: the exclusive membrane localization of endogenous Janus kinase 1 by cytokine receptor interaction uncovers the Jak.receptor complex to be equivalent to a receptor tyrosine kinase.
Structure of a Janus kinase cytokine receptor complex reveals the basis for dimeric activation.

novelty.note: I searched for the FRAP/mobility mechanism in plain words (JAK1 diffusing as part of a receptor complex, no exchange with cytosolic pool), for the entities together (Jak1 L80A/Y81A non-binding mutant, membrane localization, gp130), and for the structural interface plus the graded-affinity prediction (single-molecule/FRAP tests of JAK1 mobility vs receptor occupancy). Giese et al. (JBC 2003, retrieved via PubMed record) reports that gp130-YFP and Jak1-YFP have equal plasma-membrane mobilities, that antibody-mediated immobilization of gp130-CFP immobilizes Jak1-YFP, and that the non-binding Jak1 mutant recovers like a free cytosolic protein — i.e. exactly the docking-driven-immobility explanation; Behrmann et al. (JBC 2004) states that Jak1 has no strong intrinsic membrane affinity and that receptor interaction alone confers membrane residence, describing the Jak–receptor complex as equivalent to a receptor tyrosine kinase. The Glassman cryo-EM structure supplies the Box1/Box2 FERM-SH2 interface but says nothing about complex lifetime or diffusion, so it is cited as the nearest structural work; only the graded point-mutant/receptor-titration scaling test remains unaddressed, which does not change that the explanation itself is published.

hypotheses.statement: Earlier reports of a freely mobile, largely cytoplasmic/nuclear JAK1 pool arose from non-specific antibody staining, so the low measured mobility is the correct behaviour of the true, membrane-restricted JAK1 population.
hypotheses.mechanism: Subcellular fractionation places Jak1 predominantly in membrane fractions, with the residual nuclear/cytoplasmic signal tracking membrane contamination marked by flotillin (behrmann2004:findings:000, behrmann2004:findings:001). The antibodies underpinning the older cytoplasmic/nuclear localization claims produced no specific staining when tested against Jak1-deficient cells (behrmann2004:findings:004). Hence the expectation of cytoplasmic-protein-like mobility was built on an artefact, and a nearly fully receptor-bound JAK1 pool would naturally show receptor-like FRAP kinetics.
hypotheses.prediction: Quantitative fractionation of untagged endogenous JAK1, after correcting for membrane carry-over, should recover essentially no genuine soluble pool, and tagged JAK1 expressed at endogenous levels should show no fast-recovering component in FRAP.
hypotheses.test: Combine careful sequential-detergent fractionation of cells expressing JAK1 at endogenous levels (quantifying JAK1 against flotillin and calnexin carry-over) with FRAP on the same cell line, and fit recovery curves for a two-component model. Absence of a detectable fast-recovering fraction that matches a soluble pool, alongside fractionation showing no contamination-free soluble JAK1, distinguishes a genuinely membrane-restricted pool from a real cytosolic reservoir missed by imaging.

citations.title: Janus kinase (Jak) subcellular localization revisited: the exclusive membrane localization of endogenous Janus kinase 1 by cytokine receptor interaction uncovers the Jak.receptor complex to be equivalent to a receptor tyrosine kinase.
Long term association of the cytokine receptor gp130 and the Janus kinase Jak1 revealed by FRAP analysis.
Nuclear Import of JAK1 Is Mediated by a Classical NLS and Is Required for Survival of Diffuse Large B-cell Lymphoma.

novelty.note: I searched for the Jak subcellular-localization controversy (membrane fractionation, flotillin contamination, antibody specificity in Jak-deficient cells), for the Jak1/gp130 FRAP mobility work, and for evidence of a genuine soluble/nuclear JAK1 pool. The explanation is stated in full by Behrmann et al. (JBC 2004), which explicitly attributes earlier nuclear/cytoplasmic Jak1 reports to non-specific antibody staining and concludes Jak1 is exclusively membrane-localized through receptor binding, while Giese et al. (JBC 2003) already concluded from FRAP that membrane-bound Jak1 diffuses like a transmembrane protein and does not exchange with a cytosolic pool. I note contrary published evidence (a classical NLS mediating constitutive nuclear import of JAK1, shown with GFP-tagged constructs and fractionation), but that work does not test or negate the antibody-artefact/membrane-restriction claim itself, so the status is established rather than refuted.

hypotheses.statement: CARD14 is a ligand-regulated scaffold whose linker-region autoinhibition is relieved either physiologically by IL-17A/Act1 engagement or constitutively by the E138A/G117S mutations, so loss-of-function and gain-of-function phenotypes report the same CBM-activating switch.
hypotheses.mechanism: Howes et al. show WT CARD14 barely binds BCL10/MALT1 while E138A, G117S, or deletion of the linker region all create constitutive BCL10/MALT1 association and NF-κB activation, and that the mutants' effect still partly depends on the LR. If the LR normally keeps CARD14 closed until an upstream receptor signal opens it, then in CARD14-deficient cells the IL-17A receptor has no scaffold to nucleate BCL10/MALT1, which is exactly the requirement Kurgyis et al. observe for CARD14 and BCL10 in IL-17A-induced TNF, CXCL5 and CSF2 expression.
hypotheses.prediction: IL-17A stimulation of keratinocytes should induce a time-dependent increase in association of endogenous (or WT-reconstituted) CARD14 with BCL10/MALT1, whereas LR-deleted or E138A CARD14 should already be bound to BCL10/MALT1 before stimulation and should drive CXCL5/CSF2/TNF expression without IL-17A.
hypotheses.test: Reconstitute CARD14-knockdown primary or HaCaT keratinocytes with WT, ΔLR, or E138A CARD14 at matched expression, then ± IL-17A: run anti-BCL10 co-immunoprecipitation time courses and qPCR for CXCL5/CSF2/TNF. The autoinhibition-release model predicts ligand-dependent CARD14–BCL10 coIP and gene induction only for WT, and ligand-independent coIP and induction for ΔLR/E138A; a model in which CARD14 is merely a constitutive stoichiometric adaptor predicts equal, IL-17A-independent CARD14–BCL10 association for all three constructs with IL-17A acting only downstream.

citations.title: Keratinocyte-intrinsic BCL10/MALT1 activity initiates and amplifies psoriasiform skin inflammation.
Gain-of-Function Mutation of Card14 Leads to Spontaneous Psoriasis-like Skin Inflammation through Enhanced Keratinocyte Response to IL-17A.
CARD14 signalosome formation is associated with its endosomal relocation and mTORC1-induced keratinocyte proliferation.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the autoinhibition/linker-release mechanism (CARD14 LR, E138A/G117S, constitutive BCL10-MALT1 binding), the entities together (CARD14 + IL-17A/Act1 + BCL10/MALT1 in keratinocytes), and the prediction (ligand-induced CARD14–BCL10/MALT1 association driving CXCL5/CSF2/TNF). The autoinhibition half is published (O'Sullivan et al. confirm E138A drives a conformational change giving BCL10/MALT1 interaction without exogenous stimulation), and CARD14 is published as an IL-17A-pathway mediator, but via direct association with ACT1–TRAF6 rather than ligand-triggered CBM nucleation (Wang et al.). Critically, Kurgyis et al. directly examined whether the BCL10/MALT1 signalosome operates in the CARD14-dependent IL-17 receptor pathway and report that it is not involved in the IL-17R-proximal pathway, acting instead as a pleiotropic amplifier of keratinocyte responses to IL-17A, IL-1β and TNF — a stated negative result against the proposed IL-17A-gated CARD14→BCL10/MALT1 nucleation step, so the unified switch as formulated does not hold.

hypotheses.statement: The requirement for CARD14 in IL-17A signaling reflects MALT1 protease activity acting on the A20 brake, so the CBM complex is needed to relieve A20-mediated inhibition rather than to transmit the activating signal itself.
hypotheses.mechanism: Kurgyis et al. show that knocking down A20 restores normal IL-17A-induced Cxcl5 and Csf2 (and raises Tnf) in Bcl10-deficient keratinocytes, meaning the CBM module is dispensable once A20 is removed. Howes et al. show that NF-κB activation by CARD14 E138A is blocked dose-dependently by the MALT1 protease inhibitor mepazine, implicating MALT1 catalytic activity in CARD14-driven output; together these imply CARD14/BCL10 act by licensing MALT1 to remove A20 restraint on the IL-17A receptor complex.
hypotheses.prediction: Mepazine should suppress IL-17A-induced CXCL5/CSF2/TNF in A20-sufficient keratinocytes but have little or no effect once A20 is knocked down, and CARD14 or BCL10 loss should likewise become inconsequential in A20-depleted cells.
hypotheses.test: In keratinocytes, cross A20 siRNA (versus control siRNA) with mepazine (versus vehicle) and with CARD14 siRNA, then stimulate with IL-17A and quantify CXCL5/CSF2/TNF mRNA and IκBα degradation. An epistatic pattern — inhibitor and knockdown effects lost in the A20-depleted arm — supports the brake-relief model; parallel, additive losses in both arms indicate CARD14/MALT1 transmit signal independently of A20.

citations.title: The paracaspase MALT1 mediates CARD14-induced signaling in keratinocytes.
MALT1 protease: a new therapeutic target in B lymphoma and beyond?
MALT1 substrate cleavage: what is it good for?

novelty.note: Searched three ways: the CBM/MALT1–A20 brake mechanism in plain words, the entity combination (CARD14/BCL10/MALT1 + A20 + IL-17A + keratinocytes), and the prediction (MALT1 protease inhibitors such as mepazine/MLT-827 blocking IL-17A-induced CXCL5/CSF2). Published work establishes the component steps — CARD14 drives MALT1 protease activity that cleaves endogenous A20, and A20 overexpression suppresses CARD14-induced NF-κB, with reviews stating that A20 cleavage inactivates this brake and amplifies NF-κB — but none of the retrieved sources frames the CARD14/BCL10 requirement in IL-17A receptor signaling as relief of A20 restraint, and none reports the epistasis prediction (MALT1-inhibitor or CBM-loss effects vanishing in A20-depleted keratinocytes). No source tested and negated this specific claim, so the integrated explanation is partially anticipated rather than established or refuted.

hypotheses.statement: CARD14 supports IL-17A-induced JNK and p38 activation through recruitment of TRAF6 and its RING-dependent K63-linked ubiquitin chains, a branch separable from the CBM–IKK branch that drives NF-κB.
hypotheses.mechanism: Deng et al. show TRAF6 RING mutants C70A and C85A/H87A lose both K63-chain assembly and NF-κB reporter activation, while Hayden and Ghosh report that a RING-less TRAF6 can fully restore IL-1-induced NF-κB but not JNK activation in TRAF6-deficient cells, and Ge et al. show LPS increases assembly of a TRAF6–TAB1–p38 complex. If CARD14 acts as the keratinocyte scaffold that docks TRAF6 near the receptor, its loss would remove the RING-dependent ubiquitin platform that feeds TAK1/TAB1 to JNK and p38 while leaving a residual TRAF6-independent route to IKK.
hypotheses.prediction: Reconstituting CARD14-deficient keratinocytes with CARD14 plus a RING-mutant TRAF6 should restore NF-κB activation by IL-17A substantially more than it restores JNK and p38 phosphorylation, and CARD14 pulldowns should recover K63-ubiquitinated TRAF6 and TAB1 in an IL-17A-dependent manner.
hypotheses.test: In TRAF6-knockdown keratinocytes reconstituted with siRNA-resistant WT or C70A TRAF6, stimulate with IL-17A and immunoblot phospho-IκBα/p65, phospho-JNK and phospho-p38 in parallel; separately, immunoprecipitate CARD14 ± IL-17A and blot for TRAF6, K63-linkage-specific ubiquitin and TAB1. Selective loss of the JNK/p38 arm with preserved NF-κB in the C70A arm distinguishes the RING-dependent branch model from a model in which CARD14 feeds a single TAK1-dependent trunk supplying all three kinases equally.

citations.title: Gain-of-Function Mutation of Card14 Leads to Spontaneous Psoriasis-like Skin Inflammation through Enhanced Keratinocyte Response to IL-17A.
CARD14 signalosome formation is associated with its endosomal relocation and mTORC1-induced keratinocyte proliferation.
TRAF6 autoubiquitination-independent activation of the NFkappaB and MAPK pathways in response to IL-1 and RANKL.

novelty.note: I searched for the CARD14–TRAF6 scaffold in keratinocytes, for CARD14/CARMA2 in IL-17A-induced NF-κB and MAPK signaling, and for TRAF6 RING/K63-chain mutants that dissociate NF-κB from JNK/p38. The scaffold half is already published: Wang et al. (Immunity 2018) report that CARMA2/CARD14 associates with the ACT1–TRAF6 complex and is required for IL-17A-induced NF-κB and MAPK activation in keratinocytes, and O'Sullivan et al. (Biochem J 2024) show CARD14 signalosomes recruit TRAF6 and assemble TRAF6-linked K63 ubiquitin chains. However, no retrieved work tests the specific prediction of a separable RING-dependent branch; where the point has been probed indirectly the published data run the other way (TRAF6 loss blocked IKK2 and MAP kinase arms alike in CARD14 signalosomes, and TRAF6 RING mutants failed both NF-κB and MAPK in IL-1/RANKL signaling), but these are not direct tests of the CARD14/IL-17A claim, so this is partial rather than refuted.

hypotheses.statement: PKCβ phosphorylation tracks light-activated Ras because PKC is engaged downstream of ERK in a positive-feedback loop onto Raf, not as a direct Ras effector.
hypotheses.mechanism: Santos et al. propose that PKC phosphorylates RKIP, releasing it from Raf-1, and that this drives an NGF-induced positive feedback in the Raf-Mek-Erk cascade. For PKC to act as a positive-feedback node, it must itself be activated downstream of the cascade. Kawakami et al. show that PKCβI (via Y662) positively contributes to Ras-GTP and ERK activation, placing PKCβ functionally within the Ras/ERK module. Together, these suggest PKCβ could be recruited by the Ras-Raf-Mek-Erk cascade that opto-SOS drives, explaining why it groups with the fast, light-tracking class II nodes rather than with the RTK-proximal class I nodes.
hypotheses.prediction: Light-induced PKCβ phosphorylation in opto-SOS cells should require Mek/Erk activity and should be lost when Mek is inhibited, even though Ras is still activated by light.
hypotheses.test: In NIH 3T3 opto-SOS cells, pretreat with a MEK inhibitor (e.g., U0126) or vehicle, then apply light. Immunoblot phospho-PKCβ, phospho-Erk and Ras-GTP (RBD pull-down) over a time course. If PKCβ phosphorylation is abolished by MEK inhibition while Ras-GTP is preserved, it is ERK-dependent feedback. If it persists, a direct Ras-proximal route is more likely. Optionally, co-express a non-phosphorylatable RKIP mutant and measure whether Erk activation kinetics change.

citations.title: MAP kinase phosphatase as a locus of flexibility in a mitogen-activated protein kinase signaling network.
A positive feedback signal transduction loop determines timing of cerebellar long-term depression.
Using optogenetics to interrogate the dynamic control of signal transmission by the Ras/Erk module.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the mechanism in words (PKC engaged downstream of ERK as a positive-feedback node onto Raf, including the RKIP route), the entities together (PKCβ + light-activated Ras/opto-SOS, PKCβII phosphorylation + MEK/ERK dependence), and the prediction (MEK inhibitor abolishing PKC phosphorylation while Ras-GTP persists). The general mechanism is well published: a MAPK→PLA2/arachidonate→PKC→Raf positive-feedback loop was modelled and tested in NIH-3T3 fibroblasts (Bhalla/Ram/Iyengar), and reciprocal MAPK-dependent PKC activation was demonstrated by kinase-inhibitor epistasis in Purkinje cells (Tanaka/Augustine); reports of phospho-PKCβII being regulated in a MEK/ERK-dependent manner also exist. However, no retrieved source states this for PKCβ in the opto-SOS system or tests whether light-induced PKCβ phosphorylation requires Mek while Ras-GTP is preserved, and no source reports a negative result for this specific claim — hence partial, with the Toettcher optogenetics paper as the nearest work to the specific prediction.

hypotheses.statement: The discrepancy between HEK-293 nuclei and neonatal rat cardiac myocytes arises because the AKAP-anchored PKA/PDE4D3 negative-feedback loop is far more active in cardiac tissue, so PKA activation itself rapidly raises local PDE4D3 Vmax and clamps nuclear cAMP below the threshold needed for resident-holoenzyme activation.
hypotheses.mechanism: In heart extracts, PKA anchored on mAKAP phosphorylates the adjacent PDE4D3 at Ser13/Ser54, raising phosphodiesterase Vmax ~3-fold and attenuating cAMP signalling, and disrupting anchoring with Ht31 cuts cAMP-stimulated PDE activity by ~47%. The same PDE4D3 co-expression lowers mAKAP-associated PKA activity by 40% in HEK293 and rolipram restores it, showing the feedback magnitude depends on how much scaffolded PDE is present, which is high in heart. A cardiac nucleus therefore buffers away the supra-threshold cAMP transient that drives fast resident-holoenzyme activation in HEK-293, making the kinetics look diffusion-limited instead.
hypotheses.prediction: Pre-treatment with a PDE4 inhibitor (rolipram) or expression of PKA-site-dead PDE4D3 (S13A/S54A) should convert the slow, apparently diffusion-limited nuclear PKA activation kinetics of cardiac myocytes into the fast HEK-293-like kinetics, while having little additional effect in HEK-293 nuclei where scaffolded PDE feedback is weaker.
hypotheses.test: Express a nuclear-targeted PKA-activity FRET reporter (AKAR-type) plus a nuclear cAMP sensor in both HEK-293 cells and cultured neonatal rat cardiac myocytes, then compare nuclear activation rise times after forskolin ± rolipram, and in myocytes expressing PDE4D3 S13A/S54A versus wild-type PDE4D3; quantify Ser54 phosphorylation of immunoprecipitated PDE4D3 in parallel to confirm the feedback loop is engaged in myocytes and not in HEK-293.

citations.title: PKA catalytic subunit compartmentation regulates contractile and hypertrophic responses to β-adrenergic signaling.
PDE4 and mAKAPβ are nodal organizers of β2-ARs nuclear PKA signalling in cardiac myocytes.
Regulation of nuclear PKA revealed by spatiotemporal manipulation of cyclic AMP.
Control of cytoplasmic and nuclear protein kinase A by phosphodiesterases and phosphatases in cardiac myocytes.

novelty.note: I searched for nuclear PKA activation kinetics in cardiac myocytes vs HEK-293, for the mAKAP/PDE4D3 PKA-phosphorylation negative-feedback loop, and for the specific prediction that PDE4 inhibition or loss of the anchored PDE feedback would speed nuclear PKA activation. Yang et al. (J Mol Cell Cardiol 2014) tested exactly this in neonatal rat cardiac myocytes: broad PDE inhibition (forskolin+IBMX) produced rapid nuclear cAMP yet still gave a ~12-fold slower nuclear than cytosolic PKA response, and the AKAP-disrupting peptide Ht31 'did not accelerate or enhance nuclear PKA dynamics', leading the authors to conclude the cytosol/nucleus difference is not due to cAMP compartmentation or AKAP-anchored PDE and instead reflects slow catalytic-subunit diffusion — a stated negative result for the specific prediction. Parts of the underlying mechanism are published (Sample et al. show AKAP-localized PDEs tune a nuclear PKA activation threshold in HEK-293; Bedioune et al. show PDE4 insulating a mAKAPβ-anchored PKA pool restrains nuclear PKA in myocytes), but the proposed explanation of the kinetic discrepancy itself has been directly tested and failed.

hypotheses.statement: The apparent enhancement of synaptic PSD-95 by Ser295 phosphorylation reflects reduced proteasomal turnover of PSD-95 rather than increased delivery to synapses.
hypotheses.mechanism: Synaptic PSD-95 is actively degraded through a ubiquitin-proteasome route, since proteasome inhibitors MG132 and lactacystin fully block activity-induced loss of total PSD-95 (colledge2003:findings:013). Because multivalent PDZ interactions can sequester PSD-95 into a dense condensed phase (case2019a:findings:014), a linker phosphorylation that favours condensation would occlude PSD-95 from ligase/proteasome access, so steady-state synaptic enrichment would increase purely through a slower degradation rate.
hypotheses.prediction: Phosphomimetic S295D PSD-95 should show a longer protein half-life and lower ubiquitylation than wild type or S295A, and the difference in synaptic enrichment between S295D and S295A should collapse when the proteasome is inhibited; conversely, if the effect were on delivery, S295D enrichment would persist or grow under proteasome inhibition.
hypotheses.test: Express equal levels of GFP-tagged PSD-95 wild type, S295A and S295D in cultured hippocampal neurons and (i) measure protein half-life by cycloheximide chase immunoblot, (ii) measure ubiquitylation by immunoprecipitation followed by anti-ubiquitin blot, and (iii) quantify synaptic puncta enrichment by immunofluorescence with and without MG132/lactacystin. Loss of the S295D-versus-S295A enrichment difference under proteasome inhibition, together with a half-life difference, distinguishes stabilization from enhanced synaptic targeting.

citations.title: Synaptic accumulation of PSD-95 and synaptic function regulated by phosphorylation of serine-295 of PSD-95.
Ubiquitination regulates PSD-95 degradation and AMPA receptor surface expression.
The DNA repair protein DNA-PKcs modulates synaptic plasticity via PSD-95 phosphorylation and stability
Ca2+-PP2B-PSD-95 axis: A novel regulatory mechanism of the phosphorylation state of Serine 295 of PSD-95

novelty.note: I searched for Ser295/JNK1-dependent synaptic accumulation of PSD-95, for phosphorylation-controlled PSD-95 protein stability/half-life, and for PSD-95 ubiquitin-proteasome turnover and condensate protection from degradation (PubMed/eutils records, PLOS ONE and EMBO Reports pages). The component mechanisms are published — PSD-95 is ubiquitylated by Mdm2 and degraded by the proteasome after NMDA receptor activation (Colledge 2003), and phosphorylation of PSD-95 at other identified residues does control its protein stability (DNA-PKcs study) — but no retrieved source attributes the Ser295 effect to slowed proteasomal turnover; the primary Ser295 papers frame the effect as synaptic accumulation/positional stability and measure pS295 relative to unchanged total PSD-95 without testing half-life or ubiquitylation of S295D/S295A. Indexing snippets suggest the original Ser295 paper argues in its discussion against a degradation mechanism, but I could not retrieve that full text (publisher 403), so I do not score this as refuted.

hypotheses.statement: The rate-limiting kinase for IL-2-dependent and constitutive STAT5 phosphorylation in these cells is JAK1 rather than JAK3, so only inhibitors that also block JAK1 (the pan-Jak compounds) suppress pSTAT5 at low concentrations, and NIBR3049 must reach concentrations where its residual JAK1 activity contributes.
hypotheses.mechanism: hornakova2009:findings:006 shows that JAK1 drives STAT5 (and STAT3) activation through a γc-family receptor complex with γc acting only as a modulator and JAK3 absent, indicating JAK1 can carry STAT5 phosphorylation in this receptor context; hornakova2011:findings:002 shows that pharmacologic block of JAK1 completely abolishes STAT5 phosphorylation in cells. Together they imply that JAK1 catalytic activity, not JAK3 activity, sets the cellular pSTAT5 readout, so a compound with >150-fold JAK3 selectivity would need 20–50-fold higher exposure to engage enough JAK1 despite matching JAK3 in vitro potency.
hypotheses.prediction: A JAK1-selective inhibitor should suppress IL-2-induced and constitutive pSTAT5 in CMK and Kit225 cells at concentrations comparable to the pan-Jak inhibitors, JAK1 knockdown should reduce pSTAT5 far more than JAK3 knockdown, and low doses of NIBR3049 combined with sub-effective JAK1 inhibition should reconstitute full pSTAT5 suppression.
hypotheses.test: In Kit225 and CMK cells, perform side-by-side siRNA/shRNA knockdown of JAK1 versus JAK3 (verified by immunoblot) and measure IL-2-induced and constitutive pSTAT5 by phosphoflow; in parallel run full dose-response curves for a JAK1-selective inhibitor, NIBR3049, and a fixed-ratio combination of the two, and compare the EC50 shift with the shift predicted from JAK3 occupancy alone. If pSTAT5 tracks JAK1 loss/inhibition and the combination is synergistic, JAK1-dependence explains the discrepancy; if JAK3 knockdown alone ablates pSTAT5, it does not.

citations.title: Essential biphasic role for JAK3 catalytic activity in IL-2 receptor signaling.
Jak1 has a dominant role over Jak3 in signal transduction through γc-containing cytokine receptors.

novelty.note: I searched for NIBR3049's cellular potency versus its enzymatic JAK3 potency, for the JAK1-vs-JAK3 rate-limiting-kinase argument in γc/IL-2 signalling, and for direct tests of whether JAK3-selective inhibition suppresses pSTAT5. The explanation itself is already published: Haan et al. (Chem Biol 2011) used analogue-sensitive JAK1/JAK3 and kinase-dead mutants to conclude that JAK1 kinase activity is dominant and JAK3 catalytic activity dispensable for IL-2-induced STAT5 phosphorylation, explicitly arguing that selective JAK3 inhibitors would therefore be weak in cells. However, Ross et al. (Nat Chem Biol 2016) performed the specific test with a >3,000-fold JAK3-selective covalent inhibitor plus an inhibitor-resistant JAK3(C905S) rescue and report that JAK3 catalytic activity is in fact absolutely required for IL-2-induced STAT5 phosphorylation (with a second, even more JAK3-sensitive wave), directly contradicting the premise that JAK3 activity cannot carry the cellular pSTAT5 readout; hence refuted rather than established.

hypotheses.statement: The constitutive STAT5 phosphorylation in these lines is maintained by JAK3-independent tyrosine kinases (e.g. a Src/JAK2-type axis) that the pan-Jak compounds cross-inhibit but NIBR3049 does not, so suppressing pSTAT5 with the selective compound requires off-target concentrations.
hypotheses.mechanism: olayioye1999:findings:011 establishes that Src-family kinases acting upstream of Jak2 can drive STAT5 phosphorylation in a pathway entirely separate from γc/JAK3 receptor signalling, and hornakova2011:findings:002 shows that direct inhibition of a non-JAK3 Janus kinase is sufficient to eliminate cellular pSTAT5. If such a route sustains the constitutive signal, potency in a purified Jak3 kinase assay would not predict cellular pSTAT5 suppression, whereas broad-spectrum Jak inhibition would work at low dose.
hypotheses.prediction: A Src-family inhibitor or a JAK2-selective inhibitor should reduce constitutive pSTAT5 in CMK cells at concentrations where NIBR3049 is inactive, and the fraction of pSTAT5 resistant to NIBR3049 should be the fraction removed by these agents.
hypotheses.test: Titrate a Src-family inhibitor and a JAK2-selective inhibitor against constitutive pSTAT5 in CMK cells by phosphoflow and immunoblot, alone and on top of a maximal non-toxic dose of NIBR3049, and confirm target engagement by blotting pJAK2 and Src autophosphorylation. Additivity of NIBR3049 with these agents to reach pan-Jak-level suppression supports a JAK3-independent kinase input; no effect of either agent argues against it.

citations.title: Jak1 has a dominant role over Jak3 in signal transduction through γc-containing cytokine receptors.
Distinct Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL)-associated Janus Kinase 3 (JAK3) Mutants Exhibit Different Cytokine-Receptor Requirements and JAK Inhibitor Specificities.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the plain-language mechanism (a non-JAK3 kinase sustaining pSTAT5 that pan-Jak but not JAK3-selective inhibitors block), the entities together (NIBR3049/TCS 21311, CMK, JAK3 A572V, constitutive pSTAT5), and the prediction (Src-family or JAK2-selective inhibitor lowering constitutive pSTAT5 in CMK; Lyn/Src-driven STAT5 in megakaryoblastic lines). The general shape of the explanation is published — Haan et al. report that a Jak3-selective inhibitor is less efficient than pan-Jak inhibitors at abolishing STAT5 phosphorylation and attribute this to the dominant requirement for the kinase activity of a different Janus kinase (JAK1), and Degryse et al. show JAK3-mutant-driven constitutive STAT5 activation depends on a functional receptor/JAK1 complex with correspondingly poor responses to JAK3-selective compounds. However, the specific claim that the NIBR3049-resistant pSTAT5 fraction in CMK is sustained by a Src-family/JAK2 axis is neither stated nor directly tested in what I retrieved (the published attribution is to JAK1, not Src or JAK2), and no source reports a negative test of the Src/JAK2 prediction, so this is partial rather than established or refuted.

hypotheses.statement: The transmembrane segment raises intracellular-domain EGFR activity not by simply tethering the kinase to membrane but by driving TM-mediated association that lets the juxtamembrane segment form the activating 'cradle' interaction, thereby mimicking enforced dimerization.
hypotheses.mechanism: lemmon2010:findings:012 states the intracellular juxtamembrane region promotes activation by cradling the Activator C-lobe to stabilize the asymmetric dimer, so a juxtamembrane-containing construct only becomes active once two intracellular domains are brought together. kiyatkin2020:findings:009 shows that an EGFR transmembrane-plus-intracellular module, when dimerized through a heterologous extracellular region, supports strong and sustained phosphorylation of the EGFR intracellular region, indicating the TM+JM module is competent to hold an activated dimer once apposed. Together they imply that in jura2009 the TM segment supplies the association step that ICD alone cannot achieve, after which the juxtamembrane cradle produces activity equivalent to the GCN4-forced dimer.
hypotheses.prediction: Disrupting the juxtamembrane cradle contacts (or deleting the juxtamembrane segment) should abolish the high autophosphorylation of TM-ICD and of GCN4-ICD, leaving them as low as ICD alone, whereas disrupting TM-TM association should lower TM-ICD activity but leave GCN4-ICD activity intact.
hypotheses.test: In COS7 cells at the same low DNA levels, transfect matched panels of ICD, TM-ICD and GCN4-ICD carrying either wild-type juxtamembrane, cradle-interface point mutations, or juxtamembrane deletion, plus a TM-ICD variant with the TM dimerization motif mutated; measure autophosphorylation by immunoprecipitation and anti-phosphotyrosine blot. Selective loss of activity in all cradle mutants but loss only in TM-ICD for the TM-motif mutant separates the juxtamembrane-cradle mechanism from a generic membrane-anchoring/local-concentration explanation.

citations.title: Mechanism for activation of the EGF receptor catalytic domain by the juxtamembrane segment.
Conformational coupling across the plasma membrane in activation of the EGF receptor.
Architecture and membrane interactions of the EGF receptor.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the plain-words mechanism (transmembrane-driven association enabling the juxtamembrane 'cradle'/latch), the entities together (TM-ICD vs GCN4-ICD, JM-A antiparallel dimer, JM-B latch, activator C-lobe), and the prediction (JM deletion or TM-motif mutation in forced-dimer versus membrane-anchored kinase constructs). The published mechanism is stated in general: Jura 2009 reports that TM-ICD autophosphorylation equals that of the GCN4-enforced dimer and that JM-A potentiates dimerization (likely an antiparallel helical dimer engaging the TM helices) while the JM-B latch clamps the activator C-lobe, and Endres 2013 and Arkhipov 2013 show that coupling through the N-terminal TM helix interface promotes/stabilizes the antiparallel JM-A dimer and is required for activation of full-length receptor. However, none of the retrieved sources performs the discriminating experiment — matched ICD / TM-ICD / GCN4-ICD panels carrying cradle-interface point mutations or JM deletions plus a TM-dimerization-motif mutant — so the specific prediction separating TM-mediated association from generic membrane tethering/local concentration is not established, and no source reports a direct negative test of it.

hypotheses.statement: The Ser939 requirement reported by Liu et al. reflects a phosphopeptide-competition assay that reports only one of several independent 14-3-3 docking sites on TSC2, whereas the dominant constitutive site in cells lies in the 1101-1320 region, so mutating S939 alone leaves binding intact.
hypotheses.mechanism: Deletion mapping localizes the principal 14-3-3 binding determinant to TSC2 residues 1101-1320, a region that excludes Ser939, and a mutant lacking all six Akt sites including S939 still binds 14-3-3 at wild-type levels. A separate paper places an MK2-phosphorylated 14-3-3 site at Ser1210, which falls inside that mapped region, giving a concrete alternative docking site that a S939 phosphopeptide competition assay would not detect.
hypotheses.prediction: S939A TSC2 retains 14-3-3 binding and anisomycin responsiveness, whereas mutating the residue(s) within 1101-1320 (e.g. S1210) or deleting that segment abolishes or strongly reduces 14-3-3 association, including the anisomycin-stimulated component.
hypotheses.test: Co-express 14-3-3 with a panel of HA-TSC2 constructs (WT, S939A, S1210A, S939A/S1210A, delta1101-1320) in HEK293 cells, with and without anisomycin, and quantify co-immunoprecipitated 14-3-3; in parallel run in vitro competition of the TSC2/14-3-3 complex with synthetic phospho-S939 versus phospho-S1210 peptides to see which peptide actually displaces binding.

citations.title: Regulation of TSC2 by 14-3-3 binding.
The p38 and MK2 kinase cascade phosphorylates tuberin, the tuberous sclerosis 2 gene product, and enhances its interaction with 14-3-3.
Identification and characterization of the interaction between tuberin and 14-3-3zeta.
14-3-3 interacts with the tumor suppressor tuberin at Akt phosphorylation site(s).

novelty.note: I searched for the 1101-1320 deletion-mapped 14-3-3 site on TSC2, for MK2/Ser1210-dependent 14-3-3 binding, and for the S939 Akt-site claim, then retrieved the Europe PMC records for the primary papers. The explanation is already published by the same group: Li et al. 2002 (the corpus's li2002) states in its abstract that phosphorylation of Ser1210 — inside the mapped 1101-1320 region — is required for 14-3-3 association, while its six-Akt-site (including S939) mutant still binds, and Li et al. 2003 shows p38/MK2 phosphorylates Ser1210 to create the 14-3-3 site and that serum/anisomycin enhancement works through Ser1210. Nellist et al. 2002 independently reports multiple 14-3-3 binding sites within tuberin, so the multi-site framing is also published; nothing found reports a direct negative test of the prediction, hence established rather than open or refuted.

hypotheses.statement: The discrepancy arises because 14-3-3 binding to TSC2 is driven by a stress-kinase-dependent phosphorylation event rather than by Akt-pathway phosphorylation, so assays that manipulate only Akt sites report a false dependence on Ser939.
hypotheses.mechanism: Pharmacological inhibition of PI3K-Akt with wortmannin (as well as PKC-delta and ERK inhibition) had no effect on the TSC2-14-3-3 interaction even though phosphatase treatment abolishes binding entirely, showing the relevant phosphate is placed by a kinase outside the Akt pathway. A stress-activated route through MK2 phosphorylating TSC2 to promote 14-3-3 binding supplies such a kinase, consistent with anisomycin (a stress-pathway activator) stimulating binding of the S939A mutant.
hypotheses.prediction: 14-3-3 binding to TSC2, and its anisomycin-induced increase, will be insensitive to Akt or PI3K inhibition but will be lost upon inhibition or depletion of the p38-MK2 stress kinase arm, in both wild-type and S939A TSC2.
hypotheses.test: Treat HEK293 cells expressing HA-TSC2 (WT or S939A) with anisomycin in the presence of a p38 inhibitor or MK2 knockdown versus wortmannin or an Akt inhibitor, and measure co-immunoprecipitated 14-3-3; a lambda-phosphatase control confirms the interaction remains phospho-dependent in each condition.

citations.title: The p38 and MK2 kinase cascade phosphorylates tuberin, the tuberous sclerosis 2 gene product, and enhances its interaction with 14-3-3.
RIP3 antagonizes a TSC2-mediated pro-survival pathway in glioblastoma cell death.

novelty.note: I searched PubMed/Europe PMC three ways: the mechanism in words (stress kinase p38-MK2 phosphorylating tuberin to create a 14-3-3 site), the entities together (TSC2 + 14-3-3 + Ser1210, and TSC2 + 14-3-3 + Ser939/Akt/wortmannin), and the prediction (anisomycin-induced, p38/MK2-dependent, PI3K-independent 14-3-3 binding). The direct follow-up study to the corpus paper, Li et al. J Biol Chem 2003 (PMID 12582162), already states this explanation: serum and anisomycin enhance TSC2-14-3-3 binding by stimulating phosphorylation of Ser1210, p38 activation is required, MK2 directly phosphorylates this site, and Ser1210 phosphorylation is essential for 14-3-3 binding — i.e. the 14-3-3 site is created by a stress kinase outside the Akt pathway; a later study independently reports a TSC2 survival pathway implicating MK2 and 14-3-3. No source was found that tested and negated the p38-MK2 arm, so this is established rather than open or refuted (work reporting Akt/Ser939-driven 14-3-3 binding and cytosolic partitioning is a competing positive claim, not a direct negative test of the stress-kinase route).

hypotheses.statement: The ~3-fold higher population phospho-ERK with NGF plus roscovitine reflects a larger fraction of PC12 cells switching into the high-ERK state of a bistable, switch-like NGF response, rather than higher ERK phosphorylation within each responding cell.
hypotheses.mechanism: Santos2007 reports that NGF produces a switch-like, bimodal distribution of phosphorylated Erk1/2 across single PC12 cells, with bistability conferred by positive feedback after maximal Erk1/2 activation. Ryu2015 reports that single-cell first-peak ERK amplitudes saturate above a threshold NGF concentration and that population-averaged kinetics arise from heterogeneous single-cell trajectories. Taken together, a large increase in immunoblot-averaged pERK could come mainly from roscovitine shifting more cells across the switching threshold, or from the high state persisting longer, rather than from a higher ceiling in each cell.
hypotheses.prediction: Single-cell ppERK distributions after NGF plus roscovitine should stay bimodal, with a larger high-mode fraction and a largely unchanged high-mode intensity compared with NGF alone. The effect should be largest at NGF doses near the switching threshold and smallest at saturating NGF.
hypotheses.test: Run phospho-ERK1/2 flow cytometry on PC12 cells treated with NGF across a dose range (below, near and above threshold), with and without roscovitine, at several time points. Compare the fraction of cells in the high mode with the median intensity of that mode. A fraction shift supports this hypothesis; a uniform rightward shift of the whole distribution, including a higher high-mode intensity, contradicts it.

citations.title: Cdk5 Modulation of mitogen-activated protein kinase signaling regulates neuronal survival.
Conversion of graded phosphorylation into switch-like nuclear translocation via autoregulatory mechanisms in ERK signalling.
Emergence of bimodal cell population responses from the interplay between analog single-cell signaling and protein expression noise.

novelty.note: I searched for (a) roscovitine/Cdk5 inhibition potentiating NGF-induced ERK phosphorylation in PC12 cells, (b) single-cell/flow-cytometry ppERK distributions in NGF-stimulated PC12 cells (bimodality, high-mode fraction vs. high-mode intensity), and (c) the general claim that population-average pERK increases reflect more cells crossing a switching threshold. The roscovitine–ERK literature I could retrieve is entirely population-level (immunoblot/immunocytochemistry showing earlier and abnormally sustained Erk1/2 activation after Cdk5 inhibition, with no single-cell distribution analysis and no dose–threshold mode-fraction analysis), and the single-cell ERK-distribution literature never uses roscovitine; one PC12/HeLa single-cell study even reports unimodal rather than bimodal ppERK distributions, which bears on the premise but is not a test of the roscovitine claim. No source states this explanation and none reports a direct negative test of it, so the status is open with the closest published work cited as nearest.

hypotheses.statement: The Syk linker tyrosines act as phospho-dependent docking sites for downstream SH2 partners rather than as determinants of catalytic output, so their mutation leaves activity toward a generic exogenous substrate such as cdb3 unchanged while abolishing physiological signalling.
hypotheses.mechanism: Phosphorylated Tyr342 and Tyr346 are reported to bind the VAV1 and PLCγ1 SH2 domains, and mutation of these residues inhibits FcεRI signalling and phenocopies SYK-deficient cytoskeletal defects, which is an adaptor-recruitment function separable from catalysis (mcsai2010:findings:012). Consistent with catalysis being substrate-context dependent rather than uniform, Syk phosphorylates a PKCβI C-terminal peptide only when it is already primed by serine phosphorylation and fails on the unprimed peptide (kawakami2003:findings:002), showing that an artificial substrate such as cdb3 need not report the reactions that matter in cells. Under this view the in vitro assay measures a docking-independent reaction and is therefore blind to the defect.
hypotheses.prediction: Wild-type and linker-tyrosine-mutant Syk will remain indistinguishable on cdb3, but will diverge sharply on substrates or reactions whose phosphorylation requires prior recruitment of an SH2-containing partner, and mutant Syk will fail to co-precipitate VAV1 or PLCγ1 after stimulation despite normal autophosphorylation-independent catalysis.
hypotheses.test: Run parallel in vitro kinase reactions with immunoprecipitated wild-type and mutant Syk on (i) cdb3 and (ii) a recombinant PLCγ1 or VAV1 fragment retaining its SH2 domain, with and without a competing free phospho-linker peptide; in the same lysates perform GST-SH2 pulldowns and reciprocal co-immunoprecipitation of VAV1/PLCγ1 with Syk. Equal activity on cdb3 combined with mutant-selective loss of activity on the SH2-bearing substrate and loss of co-precipitation supports docking loss; equal activity on both substrates points instead to a defect downstream of Syk itself.

citations.title: Phospholipase C-gamma1 interacts with conserved phosphotyrosyl residues in the linker region of Syk and is a substrate for Syk.
Phosphorylation of Tyr342 in the linker region of Syk is critical for Fc epsilon RI signaling in mast cells.

novelty.note: I searched for the Syk linker tyrosines (Y342/Y346, human numbering Y348/Y352) as SH2 docking sites versus catalytic determinants, for linker-mutant kinase activity toward exogenous substrates, and for VAV1/PLCγ co-precipitation with linker mutants. Law et al. (MCB 1996) state precisely this explanation: substitution of the linker tyrosines Y348/Y352 did not affect Syk's kinase activity but almost completely abolished binding of the PLC-γ1 C-terminal SH2 domain and Syk-induced PLC-γ1 tyrosine phosphorylation in vivo, i.e. a recruitment function separable from catalysis. A later direct test complicates part of it — Zhang, Berenstein & Siraganian report that Y342F Syk has reduced kinase activity and decreased ITAM binding, yet still reconstitutes FcεRI-induced Vav phosphorylation — so the PLCγ docking arm is established while the 'catalysis wholly unchanged' and Vav-dependence arms are contested rather than confirmed.

hypotheses.statement: Expressing Syk at roughly 10-fold over endogenous levels saturates the activation-induced Cbl/ubiquitin-dependent degradation that normally limits Syk abundance, so any difference in mutant stability or turnover is buffered out and the mutants appear expression-matched to wild type.
hypotheses.mechanism: Stimulation drives c-Cbl phosphorylation, Cbl–Syk association and a ubiquitylated Syk ladder, with up to 80% loss of Syk protein over long incubations and loss occurring even at sub-degranulating stimulus strengths (macglashan2004:findings:002, macglashan2004:findings:000). Linker and interdomain tyrosine phosphorylation governs Syk's association with ITAMs and with SH2-containing partners, with Tyr130 phosphorylation actively dissociating Syk from phosphorylated ITAMs (mcsai2010:findings:009), so mutations that change residency in the receptor complex could change exposure to the Cbl machinery. At 10-fold over endogenous levels the degradative capacity would be exceeded for all constructs, flattening such differences.
hypotheses.prediction: If expression is titrated down to endogenous levels, stimulation-induced Syk loss and the ubiquitylated Syk ladder will differ between wild-type and linker mutants, whereas at 10-fold overexpression all constructs will show similar fractional loss; proteasome inhibition should accumulate high-molecular-weight species preferentially in the constructs that turn over fastest.
hypotheses.test: Generate a graded expression series of wild-type and each linker mutant (drug-inducible or low-multiplicity transduction with sorting) spanning endogenous to 10-fold, stimulate, and quantify by immunoblot the fractional loss of p72 Syk, the intensity of the >p72 ubiquitylated ladder, and Cbl co-immunoprecipitation, each with and without a proteasome inhibitor. Expression-level-dependent divergence between wild type and mutants at low expression, collapsing at high expression, supports saturation; identical turnover at all expression levels indicates the linker mutations do not affect Syk stability.

citations.title: The non-receptor tyrosine kinase Syk is a target of Cbl-mediated ubiquitylation upon B-cell receptor stimulation.
Ubiquitination and degradation of Syk and ZAP-70 protein tyrosine kinases in human NK cells upon CD16 engagement

novelty.note: I searched for Cbl/ubiquitin-dependent Syk degradation and its saturation by overexpression, for expression-level dependence of stimulation-induced Syk loss, and for turnover/stability differences among Syk linker and interdomain mutants (PubMed/PMC, publisher pages for EMBO J, PNAS, JBC, JEM). The component mechanism is well published — BCR/FcR stimulation drives Cbl-dependent ubiquitylation and proteasomal degradation of Syk, requiring the Cbl-TKB site in the SH2-kinase linker (Tyr323), and the extent of ubiquitylation scales with the degree of Syk tyrosine phosphorylation — but no retrieved source states that expressing Syk ~10-fold over endogenous saturates this degradative capacity and thereby buffers out stability differences between wild-type and linker mutants, and none reports a direct test of that expression-level-dependent prediction (positive or negative). Hence partial rather than established, open, or refuted.

hypotheses.statement: Normal PLCγ1 phosphorylation in SykY342F cells reflects functional redundancy between the two Syk linker tyrosines, because both pTyr342 and pTyr346 engage the same PLCγ1 C-terminal SH2 domain, so either site alone suffices.
hypotheses.mechanism: mcsai2010:findings:012 states that both phosphorylated Tyr342 and Tyr346 bind the C-terminal SH2 domain of PLCγ1, whereas only pTyr342 binds the VAV1 SH2 domain; lemmon2010:findings:016 shows that PLCγ1 C-SH2 engagement of phosphosites is intrinsically weak (KD > 1 µM) relative to the N-SH2, so PLCγ1 docking is expected to be a low-affinity, multi-site interaction rather than a single dominant one. A single-site loss at Tyr342 would therefore be buffered by the remaining Tyr346 docking site, while PLCγ2 (a different isoform with different linker preference) is not buffered.
hypotheses.prediction: A Syk Y342F/Y346F double mutant, but neither single mutant, should abolish PLCγ1 recruitment to Syk and PLCγ1 tyrosine phosphorylation; recombinant PLCγ1 C-SH2 should bind Syk linker phosphopeptides containing either pTyr342 or pTyr346 with comparable affinity.
hypotheses.test: Reconstitute Syk-deficient RBL-2H3 cells with wild-type, Y342F, Y346F, and Y342F/Y346F Syk and compare PLCγ1 co-immunoprecipitation with Syk and PLCγ1 phosphorylation after FcεRI crosslinking; in parallel, measure binding of a purified PLCγ1 C-SH2 domain to synthetic Syk linker phosphopeptides (pY342, pY346, doubly phosphorylated, and non-phosphorylated) by fluorescence-polarization or peptide-pulldown immunoblot.

citations.title: Distinct roles for the linker region tyrosines of Syk in FcepsilonRI signaling in primary mast cells.
Phosphorylation of Tyr342 in the linker region of Syk is critical for Fc epsilon RI signaling in mast cells.
Distinct mechanisms of a phosphotyrosyl peptide binding to two SH2 domains.
Phospholipase C-gamma1 interacts with conserved phosphotyrosyl residues in the linker region of Syk and is a substrate for Syk.

novelty.note: I searched for the Syk linker tyrosine 342/346–PLCγ1 docking mechanism, for reconstitution experiments with Y342F/Y346F single and double mutants in mast cells, and for biophysical measurements of PLCγ1 SH2 binding to Syk linker phosphopeptides.
