The redundancy premise is contradicted by direct tests: Simon et al. reconstituted Syk-deficient primary mast cells with exactly these linker mutants and found PLCγ1 (as well as PLCγ2 and Vav1) phosphorylation strongly decreased by the Y342F single mutation alone, while Zhang et al. in Syk-deficient RBL-2H3 cells found Y342 critical and Y346 barely phosphorylated after antigen stimulation with little functional effect — i.e. the two sites are not interchangeable and single-site loss at Tyr342 is not buffered. Consistent with this, kinetic/structural analysis of the doubly phosphorylated Syk linker B peptide shows PLC-γ SH2 binds by dock-and-coalesce with pTyr342 anchoring the primary pocket (and sub-micromolar, not >1 µM, affinity), not two equivalent sites; Law et al. established the C-terminal SH2/linker interaction and the loss of binding when both tyrosines are mutated.

hypotheses.statement: PLCγ1 phosphorylation is preserved in SykY342F cells because PLCγ1 is recruited predominantly through the LAT scaffold rather than through the Syk linker region, making the Syk-linker docking site dispensable for PLCγ1 phosphorylation specifically.
hypotheses.mechanism: nicolas2022:findings:014 and nicolas2022:findings:016 show PLCγ1 is a stably conserved, stoichiometrically substantial client of phospho-LAT complexes with rapid stimulus-dependent kinetics, and good2011:findings:006 states that Syk/Zap70-family phosphorylation of LAT creates the SH2 docking sites that drive downstream assembly. If the LAT route dominates, mutating a single Syk linker tyrosine leaves LAT phosphorylation-dependent PLCγ1 recruitment intact even though direct Syk-linker binding (mcsai2010:findings:012) is lost.
hypotheses.prediction: In SykY342F-expressing cells, PLCγ1 should remain associated with LAT at near-normal stoichiometry after stimulation, and PLCγ1 phosphorylation should become Y342-dependent only when the LAT docking route is removed (LAT-deficient or LAT phospho-site mutant background).
hypotheses.test: In Syk-deficient RBL-2H3 cells reconstituted with wild-type or Y342F Syk, deplete LAT by CRISPR/siRNA or replace it with a PLCγ1-binding-site mutant, then quantify PLCγ1 co-immunoprecipitation with LAT versus Syk and PLCγ1 phosphorylation; the hypothesis predicts a Y342F phosphorylation defect appears only in the LAT-compromised background, whereas the redundancy hypothesis predicts no effect of LAT status on the Y342F versus wild-type comparison.

citations.title: Phospholipase C-gamma1 interacts with conserved phosphotyrosyl residues in the linker region of Syk and is a substrate for Syk.
Phosphorylation of Tyr342 in the linker region of Syk is critical for Fc epsilon RI signaling in mast cells.
LAT is essential for Fc(epsilon)RI-mediated mast cell activation.

novelty.note: I searched for the Syk linker Y342F/Y346 mutants and PLCγ1 phosphorylation, for LAT-dependent PLCγ1 recruitment in FcεRI signalling, and for the prediction that the Syk linker docking site is dispensable when LAT is intact. Law et al. directly tested dispensability: substituting the conserved linker tyrosines (Tyr-348/Tyr-352, i.e. the Y342/Y346 pair) left kinase activity intact but abolished PLCγ1 SH2(C) binding and completely eliminated in vivo tyrosyl phosphorylation of PLCγ1 in LAT-sufficient lymphoid cells, so the linker site is required, not bypassed by a scaffold route. The mast-cell Y342F study further reports that antigen-induced LAT phosphorylation is itself dramatically reduced in SykY342F cells (with PLCγ2 phosphorylation down ~70%), contradicting the premise that the phospho-LAT docking route remains intact in that background; Saitoh et al. show the converse arm, that LAT loss cripples PLCγ1 phosphorylation, so both routes are non-redundant rather than one being dominant.

hypotheses.statement: Normal Vav1 phosphorylation in SykY342F cells arises because Vav1 is recruited by an adaptor-mediated route (GRB2/GRAP2/SLP-76) that operates in parallel to direct pTyr342–Vav1 SH2 binding.
hypotheses.mechanism: nicolas2022:findings:006 shows the VAV1 interactome is dominated by GRB2, GRAP2 and SLP-76, which peak within 30 s of receptor stimulation, and smithgarvin2009:findings:009 shows SLP-76 tyrosine mutants retain SLP-76/Vav1 association even when downstream signalling fails, indicating that Vav1 docking onto the adaptor module is robust. Loss of the direct Syk pTyr342 site described in mcsai2010:findings:012 would then leave Vav1 recruitment and phosphorylation largely intact while removing only one of several inputs.
hypotheses.prediction: Vav1 phosphorylation in SykY342F cells should still require SLP-76/GRB2-family adaptors; depleting SLP-76 or GRAP2 should collapse Vav1 phosphorylation in Y342F cells more severely than in wild-type-Syk cells, and Vav1 should co-immunoprecipitate with SLP-76 but not with Y342F Syk.
hypotheses.test: In Syk-deficient RBL-2H3 cells reconstituted with wild-type or Y342F Syk, knock down SLP-76 or GRAP2 by siRNA and measure Vav1 tyrosine phosphorylation and Vav1 co-immunoprecipitation with Syk versus SLP-76 after FcεRI crosslinking; a selective loss of Vav1 phosphorylation upon adaptor depletion in the Y342F background distinguishes the parallel-adaptor route from a model in which Vav1 phosphorylation is simply Syk-linker-independent.

citations.title: Phosphorylation of Tyr342 in the linker region of Syk is critical for Fc epsilon RI signaling in mast cells.
Mechanism and function of Vav1 localisation in TCR signalling.
Two closely spaced tyrosines regulate NFAT signaling in B cells via Syk association with Vav.

novelty.note: I searched for the Syk linker Tyr342–Vav1 SH2 interaction, for Vav phosphorylation in Y342F-reconstituted mast cells, and for adaptor-mediated (SLP-76/GRB2/GRAP2) Vav1 recruitment and its requirement for Vav1 phosphorylation. The adaptor-docking arm of the mechanism is well published — Vav1 recruitment to SLP-76 phosphotyrosines 112/128 via its SH2/SH3B domains is required for Vav1 tyrosine phosphorylation in T cells — and the mast-cell phenomenon itself (antigen-induced Vav phosphorylation preserved in Syk Y342F transfectants, with impaired LAT/SLP-76/PLCγ2 phosphorylation) is reported, but no source I retrieved attributes the preserved Vav1 phosphorylation to a parallel GRB2/GRAP2/SLP-76 route; the Y342F mast-cell paper instead reports that Syk–Vav co-immunoprecipitation was similar in wild-type and Y342F cells, which argues against the co-IP element of the prediction without testing the adaptor-dependence claim, and a B-cell study found Y342F does attenuate Vav1 phosphorylation. Hence partial rather than established or refuted.

hypotheses.statement: GSK3B negatively regulates (inhibits) TGF-B signaling by lowering the amount and activity of Smad3 available to respond to TGF-B.
hypotheses.mechanism: GSK3-β promotes Smad3 ubiquitination and basal turnover, and it phosphorylates activated Smad3 in a way that targets it for degradation (guo2008:findings:013, derynck2019:findings:042). Cells lacking GSK3-β, or with it knocked down or inhibited, show stronger TGF-B-induced C-terminal Smad3 phosphorylation, nuclear translocation and SBE-Luc activity (guo2008:findings:016). TGF-B's own output is marked by pSMAD3 and by induction of TGF-B-responsive genes such as Ctgf and Col1a1 (biffi2018:findings:014). Together these imply that GSK3B activity limits the Smad3-dependent response to TGF-B.
hypotheses.prediction: In TGF-B-responsive cells, lowering GSK3B activity should raise total and C-terminally phosphorylated Smad3 after TGF-B treatment. It should also increase TGF-B induction of Smad3-dependent targets such as SBE-Luc, Ctgf and Col1a1, but should not change TGF-B-independent Smad2 reporter activity.
hypotheses.test: Treat cultured TGF-B-responsive cells (e.g., HaCaT or primary stellate/fibroblast cultures) with GSK3B siRNA/shRNA or a GSK3 inhibitor (SB-216763), with or without TGF-B. Measure pSmad3, total Smad3 and Smad3 half-life by CHX-chase immunoblot, SBE-Luc activity, and Ctgf/Col1a1 by qPCR. As a control, re-express Smad3(T66V) to test whether the enhanced response requires GSK3B-dependent Smad3 phosphorylation.

citations.title: Axin and GSK3- control Smad3 protein stability and modulate TGF- signaling.
Glycogen synthase kinase-3beta negatively regulates TGF-beta1 and Angiotensin II-mediated cellular activity through interaction with Smad3.
Glycogen synthase kinase-3 inhibition attenuates fibroblast activation and development of fibrosis following renal ischemia-reperfusion in mice.

novelty.note: I searched for the mechanism in plain words (GSK3-β lowering Smad3 levels/activity and thereby limiting TGF-β signaling), for the entities together (GSK3β + Smad3 + ubiquitination/Thr66 + SBE-Luc/MEF), and for the prediction (GSK3 inhibitor or knockdown raising TGF-β-induced pSmad3 and Smad3 target genes such as CTGF/Col1a1 in fibroblasts). The explanation is explicitly published: Guo et al. (Genes Dev 2008, verified via NCBI esummary) report Axin/GSK3-β-mediated Thr66 phosphorylation driving Smad3 ubiquitination and basal degradation, with reduced GSK3-β expression/activity increasing Smad3 stability and TGF-β transcriptional output while leaving Smad2 responses unaffected; Hua et al. independently describe GSK3β as a negative regulator of TGF-β1/Smad3-mediated transcription through direct interaction. The status is established rather than partial because the same explanation for the same phenomenon is stated, though I note a context caveat: in renal fibroblasts GSK3 inhibition (SB216763/TDZD) reduced rather than raised TGF-β1-induced pSMAD3 and myofibroblast/fibrotic gene expression, so the fibroblast/stellate-cell arm of the prediction runs against that report.

hypotheses.statement: mTOR (mTORC1) kinase activity negatively regulates c-Src activation, so that loss of mTOR activity releases Src into its active state.
hypotheses.mechanism: Several claims show that rapamycin blocks mTOR-dependent outputs. It abolishes insulin-induced, mTOR-targeted Raptor Ser863 phosphorylation (carriere2010:findings:011). mTOR is also one of the nodes mediating negative feedback that keeps EGF-induced ERK and AKT activation transient (borisov2009:findings:008). Independently, rapamycin increases active c-Src (pY416) and decreases inactive c-Src (pY527) (chaturvedi2009:findings:012). That rapamycin-induced Src activity is then required for the downstream EGFR Y845, ERK1/2 and RSK phosphorylation (chaturvedi2009:findings:013). Together this implies that mTOR activity restrains c-Src activation, and that the Src increase seen with rapamycin is a consequence of losing mTOR activity.
hypotheses.prediction: Reducing mTOR activity by any route should raise Src Y416 and lower Y527 phosphorylation, and PP2 should block the resulting EGFR Y845 and ERK1/2 increase. Routes include mTOR siRNA knockdown, rapamycin, or an ATP-competitive mTOR inhibitor. A rapamycin-resistant mTOR mutant should prevent rapamycin from activating Src.
hypotheses.test: In HEK293 or COS7 cells, knock down mTOR by siRNA, or treat with rapamycin or Torin1, alongside vehicle and scrambled-siRNA controls. Immunoblot for phospho-Src Y416, phospho-Src Y527, phospho-EGFR Y845 and phospho-ERK1/2, with phospho-4E-BP1 or phospho-S6 as a readout of mTOR inhibition. In parallel, express either wild-type mTOR or the rapamycin-resistant S2035I mTOR mutant and treat with rapamycin. The hypothesis is supported if the mutant abolishes rapamycin-induced Src Y416 phosphorylation. It is ruled out if knockdown or rescue fails to change Src activation state.

citations.title: mTOR Inhibition Leads to Src-Mediated EGFR Internalisation and Degradation in Glioma Cells.
Rapamycin induces transactivation of the EGFR and increases cell survival.
Combined SFK/mTOR inhibition prevents rapamycin-induced feedback activation of AKT and elicits efficient tumor regression.

novelty.note: I searched for rapamycin-induced c-Src activation with EGFR Y845, for mTOR inhibition as a negative regulator of Src family kinases, and for the specific prediction (Torin1/AZD8055 or mTOR knockdown raising Src Y416). Colella et al. 2020 in glioma cells report Src activation (pY416) after every mTOR-inhibitory stimulus tested, including the ATP-competitive inhibitors Torin1 and AZD8055 and nutrient starvation, and explicitly frame Src activation as a consequence of losing mTOR activity rather than a rapamycin off-target effect — the same explanation as the hypothesis, and an independent confirmation of the ATP-competitive-inhibitor arm of the prediction; the original Chaturvedi et al. 2009 paper already states the rapamycin-to-Src-to-EGFR link. Two caveats keep this short of a complete match: no published work uses mTOR siRNA or a rapamycin-resistant mTOR mutant to close the loop, and where the corpus predicts a Src-dependent ERK increase, Colella et al. found ERK1/2 persistently suppressed while Clark et al. 2014 saw no consistent Src activation by rapamycin in three breast cancer lines, so the downstream half of the prediction is contested rather than supported.

hypotheses.statement: p38 activates mTORC1 through RSK-mediated phosphorylation of Raptor, particularly during amino acid stimulation.
hypotheses.mechanism: RSK phosphorylates Raptor in a MEK- and RSK-dependent but rapamycin-insensitive way, and this phosphorylation is needed for full PMA-stimulated mTORC1 kinase activity (carrire2008:findings:001, carrire2008:findings:010). Separately, amino acids phosphorylate p38 while lowering ERK phosphorylation, and amino acid-induced RSK phosphorylation requires p38 or ERK, which can substitute for each other (casasterradellas2008:findings:009, casasterradellas2008:findings:002). p38-activated MK2/3 phosphorylate RSK Ser380 (cargnello2011:findings:058). Together these imply that p38 can drive RSK activity toward Raptor and so raise mTORC1 activity, with this route contributing most when ERK input is low, as it is after amino acid stimulation.
hypotheses.prediction: In amino acid-stimulated cells, p38 inhibition (especially with MEK inhibition) should reduce Raptor phosphorylation on the RSK motif and lower mTORC1 kinase activity toward 4E-BP1. This p38-dependent part of mTORC1 activity should be lost in cells expressing the phosphorylation-deficient Raptor 3A mutant, and it should not appear for insulin-stimulated mTORC1 activity.
hypotheses.test: Transfect HEK293 cells with Myc-Raptor (wild-type or 3A) plus mTOR. Starve them of amino acids, then restimulate with amino acids after pretreatment with vehicle, SB203580, U0126, both inhibitors, or the RSK inhibitor BI-D1870. Measure Raptor phosphorylation by immunoprecipitation and RXRXXpS/T immunoblot, mTORC1 kinase activity in vitro with GST-4E-BP1 and [γ-32P]ATP, and 4E-BP1 Thr37/46 phosphorylation. Also test whether a constitutively active MKK6 raises Raptor phosphorylation and mTORC1 activity in wild-type but not 3A Raptor cells.

citations.title: A role for p38 stress-activated protein kinase in regulation of cell growth via TORC1.

novelty.note: I searched for RSK-mediated Raptor phosphorylation and mTORC1, for p38/MK2-to-RSK signalling toward Raptor, and for p38 requirement in amino acid-stimulated mTORC1 activity. The published work establishes the two halves separately — RSK phosphorylates Raptor to activate mTORC1 downstream of Ras/MAPK, and p38 (via MKK3/6) is positively required for TORC1 activation by amino acids and growth factors (Cully et al.) — but the p38 study explicitly leaves the molecular mechanism unresolved, reporting that Raptor Ser863 is not dynamically regulated by p38 activation and that p38α/γ and MK2 do not appreciably phosphorylate purified TORC1, without testing the RSK-motif Raptor sites. A separate line of work attributes stress (arsenite)-induced p38 effects on Raptor to direct proline-directed phosphorylation rather than RSK, so the specific RSK-mediated link between p38 and Raptor during amino acid stimulation is neither stated nor directly tested and refuted.

hypotheses.statement: ERK2 directly phosphorylates EGFR on serine/threonine residue(s) as a feedback modification that limits EGFR tyrosine phosphorylation, analogous to its phosphorylation of FGFR1.
hypotheses.mechanism: EGFR kinase activity and its autophosphorylation sites are required for Erk1/2 activation, so ERK2 becomes active downstream of EGFR (chaturvedi2009:findings:008, chaturvedi2009:findings:009, chaturvedi2009:findings:010). Independently, activated ERK2 directly phosphorylates upstream components of its own activating pathway in vitro. This is shown for the receptor tyrosine kinase FGFR1 at S777, where blocking the site prolongs receptor tyrosine phosphorylation, and for SOS1 and Raf-1, where phosphorylation desensitises signalling (lake2016:findings:002, lake2016:findings:003, lake2016:findings:007). Together these suggest EGFR, the upstream receptor for ERK activation in these systems, may also be a direct ERK2 substrate in a comparable negative-feedback loop.
hypotheses.prediction: Recombinant active ERK2 will incorporate 32P into purified EGFR or its cytoplasmic domain in vitro, at S/T-P site(s) that are also phosphorylated in EGF-stimulated cells in a MEK-dependent manner. Blocking MEK/ERK, or mutating the mapped site(s) to alanine, will prolong EGF-induced EGFR tyrosine phosphorylation.
hypotheses.test: Run an in vitro kinase assay with recombinant activated ERK2 (versus kinase-dead ERK2) and immunopurified EGFR or recombinant EGFR intracellular domain using [gamma-32P]ATP, and detect phosphorylation by autoradiography and pS/T-P phospho-motif immunoblot. Map the sites by phosphopeptide analysis. Then, in EGF-stimulated cultured cells, compare EGFR S/T-P phosphorylation and the time course of EGFR tyrosine phosphorylation with and without U0126 or ERK1/2 siRNA, and between wild-type EGFR and the Ser/Thr-to-Ala mutant.

citations.title: Inverse correlation between Thr-669 and constitutive tyrosine phosphorylation in the asymmetric epidermal growth factor receptor dimer conformation.
Epidermal growth factor (EGF) receptor T669 peptide kinase from 3T3-L1 cells is an EGF-stimulated "MAP" kinase.
Feedback control of ErbB2 via ERK-mediated phosphorylation of a conserved threonine in the juxtamembrane domain.

novelty.note: I searched for ERK-mediated serine/threonine feedback phosphorylation of EGFR, for the historical MAP-kinase 'T669 peptide kinase' work, and for the prediction that blocking the site prolongs EGF-induced receptor tyrosine phosphorylation. This exact explanation is long published: EGFR Thr-669 in the juxtamembrane region is phosphorylated in a MEK/ERK-dependent manner after EGF stimulation, MAP kinase (ERK) phosphorylates the T669 site directly in vitro, and loss of the site or U0126 treatment increases/prolongs EGFR tyrosine phosphorylation, with the same mechanism conserved in ErbB2 (Thr-677). Because sources state the mechanism, the in vitro direct phosphorylation, the MEK dependence and the tyrosine-phosphorylation consequence for EGFR itself, the status is established rather than partial.

hypotheses.statement: SRC positively regulates (activates) ERK2 downstream of EGF by promoting GAB1 phosphorylation and GAB1–SHP2 coupling, so that ERK2 activation depends on SRC kinase activity.
hypotheses.mechanism: SRC knockdown in HEK293 cells markedly reduced EGF-induced GAB1 phosphorylation and altered phospho-ERK without affecting EGFR autophosphorylation, placing SRC between the receptor and GAB1 (borisov2009:findings:011). Independently, GAB1–SHP2 association drives ERK2 activation, and a membrane-targeted GAB1-PH–active SHP2 fusion is sufficient for constitutive MEK1/ERK2 activation (heinrich2003:findings:010, heinrich2003:findings:011). SRC inhibition with PP2 or dasatinib also abolished stimulus-induced Erk1/2 phosphorylation in several cell lines (chaturvedi2009:findings:013), consistent with SRC acting upstream of the ERK2 activation step.
hypotheses.prediction: In EGF-stimulated cells, SRC depletion or PP2 treatment (but not PP3) should reduce GAB1 tyrosine phosphorylation, GAB1–SHP2 co-precipitation and ERK2 activation-loop (TEY) phosphorylation and kinase activity. Expressing the GAB1-PH–active SHP2 fusion should restore ERK2 activation in SRC-inhibited cells.
hypotheses.test: In HEK293 cells, knock down SRC by siRNA or treat with PP2 versus the inactive analog PP3, then stimulate with EGF. Measure GAB1 pY and GAB1–SHP2 association by co-immunoprecipitation. Measure ERK2 activation by isoform-resolved phospho-ERK immunoblot and by an immunoprecipitated-ERK2 in vitro kinase assay. Repeat with the GAB1-PH–active SHP2 fusion transfected to test whether it bypasses the SRC requirement.

citations.title: EGFR-activated Src family kinases maintain GAB1-SHP2 complexes distal from EGFR.
Roles of Gab1 and SHP2 in paxillin tyrosine dephosphorylation and Src activation in response to epidermal growth factor.
Src-family tyrosine kinases, phosphoinositide 3-kinase and Gab1 regulate extracellular signal-regulated kinase 1 activation induced by the type A endothelin-1 G-protein-coupled receptor.
Regulation of the mitogen-activated protein kinase signaling pathway by SHP2.

novelty.note: I searched for the mechanism in words (Src phosphorylates Gab1 enabling SHP2 recruitment and ERK activation), for the entities together (Src + Gab1 + SHP2 + EGF/EGFR, PP2/dasatinib, HEK293), and for the prediction (Src inhibition reducing Gab1 pY, Gab1-SHP2 co-IP and ERK activation; Gab1PH-SHP2 fusion bypass), using PubMed/Europe PMC, PMC full texts and publisher pages. Furcht et al. (Sci Signal 2015) state exactly this explanation for EGF signaling: EGFR-activated Src family kinases amplify and sustain GAB1 tyrosine phosphorylation and GAB1-SHP2 association at a site distal from EGFR, with increased ERK activity as the SHP2 output; Ren et al. (2004) independently report that Src kinase inhibition abrogates EGF-stimulated Erk activation and that the Gab1-SHP2 module is required for it, and the endothelin-1 paper reports the same Src-family -> Gab1 pY -> SHP-2-dependent ERK1 chain for another receptor. Hence established; the one element not supported is the bypass step, since Cunnich/Cunnick et al. (2002), the source of the Gab1PH-active SHP2 fusion result, found that MEK1/ERK activation by that fusion is itself blocked by a Src inhibitor and by Csk, placing Src downstream rather than upstream of the Gab1-SHP2 module.

hypotheses.statement: SYK activates MAPK, driving phosphorylation of the MAPK effector kinases (ERK, p38, JNK), possibly through a non-canonical route that does not require activation of upstream MAPK-pathway kinases.
hypotheses.mechanism: In dendritic cells, curdlan-induced phosphorylation of p38, Erk and Jnk depends on Syk (leibundgutlandmann2007:findings:001). Syk can directly phosphorylate a tyrosine on a primed substrate in vitro (kawakami2003:findings:002). Separately, several overexpressed human tyrosine kinases activated the MAPK effector kinase and its downstream substrates without activating the upstream MAPK-pathway kinases (bradley2024:findings:009). Together these suggest SYK may be a proximal activator of MAPK, not only an upstream initiator of the canonical cascade. One caveat: in AML lines, Syk substrate-group enrichment did not co-occur with MEK/ERK enrichment (casado2013:findings:002), so the coupling may depend on cell context.
hypotheses.prediction: Expressing active SYK in a SYK-low cell line should increase phosphorylation of ERK, p38 and JNK and of their substrates (e.g. RSK, MK2). At least part of this increase should persist when MEK1/2 is pharmacologically inhibited. Recombinant SYK should also phosphorylate, or increase the activity of, recombinant MAPK in vitro.
hypotheses.test: Overexpress wild-type versus kinase-dead SYK in HEK293 cells, with and without a MEK inhibitor and a SYK inhibitor. Immunoblot phospho-MEK, phospho-ERK/p38/JNK and phospho-RSK/MK2. In parallel, run an in vitro kinase assay with recombinant SYK and recombinant ERK2 or p38, reading out MAPK phosphorylation by phospho-specific immunoblot and MAPK activity on a model substrate.

citations.title: The protein tyrosine kinase SYK regulates the alternative p38 activation in liver during acute liver inflammation.
T cell receptor-mediated activation of p38{alpha} by mono-phosphorylation of the activation loop results in altered substrate specificity.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the mechanism in words (SYK directly phosphorylating MAPK effector kinases / non-canonical, MEK- or MKK-independent MAPK activation), the entities together (Syk + p38/JNK/ERK phosphorylation, Syk inhibitor R406 in TNF-stimulated cells, Syk reconstitution of ERK2 activation in Lck-negative JCaM1 cells), and the prediction (recombinant SYK phosphorylating recombinant ERK2/p38 in vitro; SYK overexpression in HEK293 with MEK inhibition). The non-canonical arm is already published for p38 specifically: SYK is reported to drive the 'alternative' p38 activation pathway (p38 Tyr323 phosphorylation followed by activation-loop autophosphorylation) in hepatocytes and liver inflammation, explicitly without changes in upstream MKK3/6 or MKK4 phosphorylation, although that work used knockdown/knockout rather than a direct SYK–p38 kinase assay and routes the signal through Vav-1; the mechanistic literature on this pathway also attributes the Tyr323 event to ZAP70 and notes it was undetectable in antigen-receptor-stimulated B cells despite Syk expression. I found no source stating the broader claim — SYK as a proximal activator of ERK and JNK (and their substrates RSK/MK2) that survives MEK1/2 inhibition, or direct SYK phosphorylation of recombinant MAPKs — and no source that tested and negated it, so this is partial rather than established or refuted.

hypotheses.statement: EGFR kinase activity activates NF-κB transcriptional activity through PI3K/AKT-dependent signaling.
hypotheses.mechanism: EGF stimulation that tyrosine-phosphorylates EGFR induces AKT phosphorylation, and the PI3K inhibitor wortmannin blocks that AKT phosphorylation without affecting EGFR phosphorylation (borisov2009:findings:009). Separately, NF-κB reporter activity depends on PI3K and Akt: LY294002 reduces it, and Akt2 knockdown lowers it by about 70% in PC3 cells (dan2008:findings:008, dan2008:findings:006). Together these imply EGFR could act as an upstream input that raises NF-κB activity via the PI3K/AKT arm, in cells where NF-κB depends on Akt (dan2008:findings:019).
hypotheses.prediction: EGF stimulation should increase NF-κB reporter activity and NF-κB DNA binding. The EGFR kinase inhibitor AG1478 or EGFR siRNA should prevent this increase, and LY294002 should block the EGF-induced increase even though EGFR stays phosphorylated.
hypotheses.test: In PC3 cells transfected with an NF-κB luciferase reporter, stimulate with EGF with or without AG1478, EGFR siRNA, LY294002, or Akt2 siRNA. Measure reporter activity, NF-κB DNA binding by EMSA, and IκBα and phospho-p65 by immunoblot, and immunoblot phospho-EGFR and phospho-AKT to confirm each perturbation worked.

citations.title: Independent role of phosphoinositol-3-kinase (PI3K) and casein kinase II (CK-2) in EGFR and Her-2-mediated constitutive NF-kappaB activation in prostate cancer cells.
Distinct domains in the SHP-2 phosphatase differentially regulate epidermal growth factor receptor/NF-kappaB activation through Gab1 in glioblastoma cells.
CXCR2-driven ovarian cancer progression involves upregulation of proinflammatory chemokines by potentiating NF-κB activation via EGFR-transactivated Akt signaling.

novelty.note: I searched for the mechanism in plain words (EGF/EGFR-induced NF-κB activation via PI3K/Akt), for the entities together (EGFR + NF-κB + PI3K/Akt + PC3/prostate), and for the prediction's experimental signature (EGF-stimulated NF-κB luciferase/EMSA blocked by AG1478 or LY294002/wortmannin). The explanation is already published as such: a study in PC-3 prostate cancer cells reports that EGFR activates NF-κB specifically through the PI3K/Akt pathway with IκBα Ser32/36 phosphorylation and p65 nuclear translocation (distinct from Her-2/CK-2), and a glioblastoma study shows EGF stimulation activates NF-κB DNA binding and reporter activity through a PI3-kinase/Akt loop, with wortmannin abolishing Akt phosphorylation and reducing NF-κB activity. A further paper shows EGFR-transactivated Akt signaling potentiating NF-κB with LY294002 sensitivity, so the mechanism, cell type and inhibitor predictions are all anticipated rather than open; no source reported a direct negative test.

hypotheses.statement: EGFR kinase activity negatively regulates cell-surface TGFBR1 (TβRI) abundance by driving ERK-dependent TACE/ADAM17 ectodomain shedding of TβRI, which dampens TGF-β/Smad responsiveness.
hypotheses.mechanism: EGFR kinase activity and its autophosphorylation sites are required for ERK1/2 activation, and ERK pathway output decays when EGFR is inhibited. Loss of the pY992 RasGAP site on EGFR prolongs ERK activation. Separately, ERK activation triggers TACE/ADAM17 cleavage of TβRI but not TβRII, which lowers surface TβRI and reduces TGF-β responsiveness. Together these imply that EGFR activation should deplete surface TβRI through ERK-driven shedding.
hypotheses.prediction: EGF stimulation should reduce cell-surface TβRI but not TβRII, increase shed TβRI ectodomain, and blunt TGF-β-induced Smad2/3 C-terminal phosphorylation. AG1478, MEK inhibition or a TACE inhibitor should abolish these effects. Cells expressing Y992F-EGFR should show greater TβRI loss than cells expressing WT-EGFR.
hypotheses.test: In cultured epithelial cells, stimulate with EGF with or without AG1478, U0126 or a TACE/ADAM17 inhibitor. Measure cell-surface TβRI and TβRII by surface biotinylation and immunoblot, and TβRI ectodomain in the medium. Then measure TGF-β-induced phospho-Smad2/3 by immunoblot. Repeat in cells transfected with WT versus Y992F EGFR.

citations.title: TACE-mediated ectodomain shedding of the type I TGF-beta receptor downregulates TGF-beta signaling.

novelty.note: I searched for ERK/TACE-dependent shedding of the type I TGF-β receptor, for EGF stimulation lowering surface TβRI with unchanged TβRII, and for the predicted blunting of TGF-β-induced Smad phosphorylation. Liu et al. (Mol Cell 2009), retrieved via PMC, states exactly this explanation: EGF (and other Erk MAPK activators) decreases cell-surface TβRI but not TβRII through TACE/ADAM17 cleavage, the TβRI ectodomain is released into the medium, MEK inhibition or TAPI-1 blocks the loss, and TACE silencing restores TGF-β-induced Smad3 activation. Only the EGFR Y992F refinement of the prediction is not covered, so the core explanation counts as already published.

hypotheses.statement: EGFR activation positively regulates cell-surface TGFBR1 (TβRI) abundance through PI3K-dependent AKT activation, which relieves AS160-mediated intracellular retention of TβRI.
hypotheses.mechanism: EGF induces AKT phosphorylation, and this is prevented by PI3K inhibition without affecting EGFR tyrosine phosphorylation. Separately, AKT activation increases TβRI and TβRII at the cell surface by phosphorylating AS160, which retains TβRI intracellularly and associates with it. This happens without any change in total receptor levels and is blocked by PI3K or AKT inhibitors but not by MEK inhibition. EGFR-driven AKT activation should therefore mobilize intracellular TβRI to the cell surface, as insulin does.
hypotheses.prediction: EGF should rapidly increase cell-surface TβRI without changing total TβRI. This increase should be blocked by AG1478, GDC0941 or AKT inhibition but not by U0126, and should be absent in AS160-silenced cells, where surface TβRI is already elevated. EGF should also enhance SB431542-sensitive Smad2/3 phosphorylation.
hypotheses.test: In NMuMG cells or MEFs, treat with EGF for 15–30 min with or without AG1478, GDC0941, an AKT inhibitor or U0126, and in control versus AS160 siRNA cells. Quantify surface versus total TβRI by surface biotinylation and immunoblot, and measure SB431542-sensitive phospho-Smad2/3.

citations.title: The insulin response integrates increased TGF-β signaling through Akt-induced enhancement of cell surface delivery of TGF-β receptors.
Transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β)-induced up-regulation of TGF-β receptors at the cell surface amplifies the TGF-β response.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the plain-language mechanism (growth-factor-driven Akt relieving AS160 retention of TGF-β receptors), the entities together (EGF/EGFR + surface TβRI + PI3K/Akt + AS160 + surface biotinylation), and the prediction (EGF rapidly raising surface TβRI without changing total receptor, inhibitor-sensitivity profile, AS160 knockdown). The Akt→AS160→cell-surface TβRI/TβRII mechanism is fully published, including GDC0941/AktVIII sensitivity, U0126 insensitivity, unchanged total receptor, and elevated basal surface receptors in AS160-silenced cells (insulin and IGF-1 as ligands), and it has been extended to TGF-β itself and to BMP-4 as another Akt-activating ligand; no retrieved source states EGF/EGFR as an input to this pathway, and none reports a direct test of EGF that came out negative. The only EGF-specific literature I found concerns slower, ERK/U0126-dependent upregulation of TβRII expression rather than rapid PI3K/Akt-dependent surface mobilization of TβRI, so the mechanism is established in general but this specific EGFR connection and prediction are not.

hypotheses.statement: GSK3B positively regulates (activates) NF-κB transcriptional activity by phosphorylating PTEN at Thr-366, which reduces PTEN's suppression of Akt-dependent NF-κB activation.
hypotheses.mechanism: In PTEN-deficient Jurkat cells, PTEN-T366A lowered Akt phosphorylation more than wild-type PTEN did, indicating that GSK3 phosphorylation of Thr-366 reduces PTEN activity and so permits more Akt activity (alkhouri2005:findings:008). Independently, adding back PTEN to PTEN-null PC3 cells cut basal NF-κB activity by about 50% (dan2008:findings:007). Knocking down Akt2, or inhibiting PI3K with LY294002, also reduced NF-κB reporter activity (dan2008:findings:006, dan2008:findings:008). Together these imply that GSK3B activity should raise NF-κB output by weakening PTEN's restraint on Akt, making this a regulatory relationship mediated by PTEN rather than a physical interaction.
hypotheses.prediction: In PTEN-null cells reconstituted with wild-type PTEN, inhibiting or knocking down GSK3B should lower NF-κB reporter activity and NF-κB target gene expression, together with a drop in Akt phosphorylation. In cells reconstituted with PTEN-T366A, or in cells with no PTEN, GSK3B inhibition should have little or no effect on NF-κB activity.
hypotheses.test: Transfect PTEN-null PC3 cells with empty vector, PTEN-WT or PTEN-T366A together with an NF-κB-dependent luciferase reporter. Treat with a GSK3 inhibitor (SB-216763 or LiCl) or GSK3B siRNA. Measure reporter activity, phospho-Akt by immunoblot, and NF-κB target transcripts (IκBα, cIAP1, Bcl-2) by RT-qPCR. The hypothesis is supported only if GSK3B suppression reduces NF-κB output in the PTEN-WT condition but not in the T366A or vector conditions.

citations.title: PTEN regulation by the Akt/GSK-3β axis during RANKL signaling.
PTEN is destabilized by phosphorylation on Thr366.
GSK-3β controls NF-kappaB activity via IKKγ/NEMO.
The cross-talk between GSK-3β, RKIP, and PTEN as potential targets for therapeutic implications in cancer: a comprehensive insight.

novelty.note: I searched for GSK3-mediated PTEN Thr366 phosphorylation and its functional consequences, for GSK3β as a positive regulator of NF-κB, and for GSK3 inhibition effects on NF-κB in PTEN-null prostate lines. The load-bearing step (GSK3 phosphorylation of Thr366 lowering PTEN function so that Akt rises) has been directly tested twice with opposite or null outcomes: Maccario et al. report that mutating Thr366 does not alter PTEN phosphatase activity in vitro or in cells (it changes only protein stability), and Jang et al. show that the GSK-3 inhibitor SB216763 lowers PTEN Thr366 phosphorylation and PTEN activity while *increasing* Akt phosphorylation, with T366A showing lower, not higher, phosphatase activity — the reverse of the predicted sign. The published explanation for GSK3β support of NF-κB transcriptional activity instead runs through NEMO/IKKγ phosphorylation and is PTEN- and Akt-independent, so the PTEN-Thr366 route is both unstated and contradicted at its critical link.

hypotheses.statement: SHP2 acts directly upstream of RAF as a required activator of RAF, sustaining the Ras-GTP pool that drives RAF dimerisation and kinase activation, so RAF activation state in wild-type-BRAF cells is SHP2-dependent.
hypotheses.mechanism: The SHP2 evidence shows that catalytically active SHP2 is needed to generate and maintain EGF-induced GTP-Ras (C/S-SHP2 cuts GTP-Ras to 30-40% of control while WT-SHP2 keeps it elevated), and that SHP2 dependency segregates with RTK-driven lines and is lost in BRAF/KRAS-mutant lines, placing SHP2 upstream of the point where RAF is switched on. The RAF evidence states that RAF activation requires engagement of activated Ras, that RAF-inhibitor-bound protomers transactivate their partner only within Ras-dependent dimers, and that Raf-1/B-Raf dimer formation and phospho-ERK rebound rise when feedback is relieved. Together these imply that removing SHP2 activity should starve RAF of the Ras-GTP input it needs, directly lowering the amount of dimerised, active RAF rather than acting only on ERK output.
hypotheses.prediction: In wild-type-BRAF, RTK-driven cells, SHP2 knockdown or catalytically dead SHP2 should reduce Ras-RBD-bound Ras, reduce co-immunoprecipitated Raf-1/B-Raf dimers and RAF kinase activity, and abolish the paradoxical RAF-inhibitor-induced dimerisation and phospho-ERK rebound; the same manipulation in BRAF-mutant cells should leave RAF dimer levels and ERK output essentially unchanged.
hypotheses.test: In MDA-MB-468 (RTK-driven, wild-type BRAF) and a BRAF-mutant line such as A2058, use doxycycline-inducible SHP2 shRNA with rescue by wild-type versus C459S SHP2, then (i) GST-Raf-RBD pulldown for GTP-Ras, (ii) reciprocal B-Raf/Raf-1 co-immunoprecipitation with and without a short RAF-inhibitor pulse, and (iii) immunoprecipitated RAF in vitro kinase assay on recombinant MEK, reading phospho-MEK/phospho-ERK by immunoblot; loss of RAF dimerisation and RAF activity only in the wild-type-BRAF line upon SHP2 loss, reversed by wild-type but not C459S SHP2, supports the relationship, whereas unchanged RAF dimers and activity despite reduced Ras-GTP rules it out.

citations.title: RAS nucleotide cycling underlies the SHP2 phosphatase dependence of mutant BRAF-, NF1- and RAS-driven cancers.
Tumours with class 3 BRAF mutants are sensitive to the inhibition of activated RAS.
Combined inhibition of SHP2 overcomes adaptive resistance to type 1 BRAF inhibitors in BRAF V600E-driven high-grade glioma

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the mechanism in words (SHP2 upstream of RAS-GTP required for RAF dimerisation in RTK-driven wild-type-BRAF cells), the entities together (SHP2/SHP099 with BRAF-CRAF heterodimer co-IP, RAS-RBD pulldown), and the prediction (SHP2 loss abolishing RAF-inhibitor paradoxical dimerisation/pERK rebound, with BRAF-mutant lines unaffected). Published work establishes the upstream half — SHP2 sustains RAS-GTP via SOS1-mediated nucleotide loading and SHP2 dependence tracks with RAS-GTP-dependent (RTK-driven, class 3 BRAF, NF1-loss) contexts while class 1 BRAF-V600E lines are refractory in both RAS-GTP and pERK readouts — and separately establishes that RAF heterodimer formation and inhibitor-induced transactivation are RAS-GTP-dependent; I found no source that closes the loop by measuring Raf-1/B-Raf dimers or immunoprecipitated RAF kinase activity as a function of SHP2 catalytic activity, nor any direct negative test of it. Hence partial rather than established or refuted.

hypotheses.statement: PMA-induced phosphorylation of GSK3β in HeLa cells is MEK1-dependent, meaning MEK1 activity lies upstream of, and is required for, GSK3β phosphorylation.
hypotheses.mechanism: In HeLa cells, PMA activates ERK and RSK and, alongside these, induces GSK3β phosphorylation (casasterradellas2008:findings:010). In the same cell line, other PMA-triggered phosphorylation events (Raptor Ser696/Ser863) are completely blocked by the MEK1/2 inhibitor U0126 (carriere2010:findings:012). Activated MEK1 alone is sufficient to drive RSK-dependent substrate phosphorylation (carrire2008:findings:005). Together these suggest the PMA-induced GSK3β phosphorylation may also be routed through MEK1 rather than being MEK-independent.
hypotheses.prediction: In serum-starved HeLa cells, U0126 or PD184352 pretreatment should strongly reduce PMA-induced phospho-GSK3β. Expressing constitutively active MEK1-DD without stimulus should increase GSK3β phosphorylation, and this increase should be reversed by MEK inhibition.
hypotheses.test: In serum-starved HeLa cells, pretreat with U0126 or PD184352 (vehicle as control), stimulate with PMA, and immunoblot for phospho-GSK3β, total GSK3β and phospho-ERK. Separately, transfect MEK1-DD or empty vector, with and without MEK inhibitor, and immunoblot for phospho-GSK3β. The hypothesis is ruled out if PMA-induced GSK3β phosphorylation persists despite full loss of phospho-ERK.

citations.title: BI-D1870 is a specific inhibitor of the p90 RSK (ribosomal S6 kinase) isoforms in vitro and in vivo.

Pharmacological and genetic evaluation of proposed roles of mitogen-activated protein kinase/extracellular signal-regulated kinase kinase (MEK), extracellular signal-regulated kinase (ERK), and p90(RSK) in the control of mTORC1 protein signaling by phorbol esters.

novelty.note: I searched for PMA/phorbol-ester-induced GSK3β Ser9 phosphorylation combined with MEK inhibitors (U0126, PD184352, PD98059) and RSK, for the RSK→GSK3 Ser9 axis, and for HeLa-specific tests of the prediction. Two retrieved primary papers already perform essentially the proposed experiment: Sapkota et al. show PMA-induced GSK3α/β Ser21/Ser9 phosphorylation is blocked by the MEK inhibitor PD184352 (to the same extent as by the RSK inhibitor BI-D1870, with loss of phospho-ERK), and the JBC 2011 pharmacological/genetic evaluation reports the same MEK→ERK→p90RSK→GSK3α/β Ser21/9 dependence under PMA. The explanation is therefore published, not merely adjacent; the only gap is that these direct tests were done in HEK293 rather than HeLa cells, and no source reports a negative (MEK-independent) result.

hypotheses.statement: TGFBR2 negatively regulates epithelial cell growth by being required for TGF-β-induced, Smad-dependent growth inhibition in NMuMG cells.
hypotheses.mechanism: In NMuMG cells, TGF-β causes growth inhibition that depends on Smad signaling, since dominant-negative Smad3 or Smad7 blocked about 80% of it (bhowmick2001:findings:001). BxPc3 cells lacking Smad4 escape growth inhibition but still respond to TGF-β for RhoA, so the growth arm branches downstream of the receptor complex (bhowmick2001:findings:008). TGF-β1 and TGF-β3 bind TβRII with high affinity, while TβRI has low affinity and needs TβRII for assembly (derynck2019:findings:004), and TβRII kinase activity is regulated by autophosphorylation (derynck2019:findings:013). This places TβRII upstream of the Smad-dependent growth-inhibitory branch.
hypotheses.prediction: Depleting TβRII in NMuMG cells, or inhibiting its kinase, should abolish TGF-β1-induced suppression of thymidine incorporation and 3TP-Lux activation. Re-expressing wild-type TβRII, but not a kinase-dead mutant, should restore growth inhibition.
hypotheses.test: Knock down Tgfbr2 by siRNA in NMuMG cells, with an siRNA-resistant wild-type or kinase-dead TβRII rescue. Treat with TGF-β1 and measure thymidine or EdU incorporation, cell counts and 3TP-Lux reporter activity. Run the TβRI/TβRII inhibitor LY2109761 and a TβRI-only inhibitor in parallel to separate TβRII kinase-dependent effects on growth.

citations.title: Inactivation of the type II receptor reveals two receptor pathways for the diverse TGF-beta activities.
Signaling activity of transforming growth factor beta type II receptors lacking specific domains in the cytoplasmic region.
TGF-beta receptor-activated p38 MAP kinase mediates Smad-independent TGF-beta responses.

novelty.note: I searched for the mechanism in plain words (type II TGF-β receptor required for TGF-β growth inhibition in epithelial cells), for the entities together (TGFBR2 kinase-dead rescue, NMuMG, 3TP-Lux, Smad-dependent growth arrest), and for the prediction (Tgfbr2 knockdown/deletion abolishing antiproliferative response). The requirement of TβRII, and specifically of its intact cytoplasmic kinase domain, for TGF-β-induced growth inhibition and transcriptional activation in mammary/lung epithelial cells is long-established: kinase-defective dominant-negative TβRII selectively blocks the growth-inhibitory response while sparing matrix/other responses, and truncated TβRII that still binds ligand and recruits TβRI fails to inhibit proliferation or activate transcription; the downstream Smad dependence of the growth-arrest arm in NMuMG cells is likewise published. No source was found that tested and refuted this claim, so the verdict is established rather than open or refuted.

hypotheses.statement: ERBB2 activation increases AKT activation (phosphorylation) through the PI3K activity that ERBB2 recruits.
hypotheses.mechanism: Transactivated ErbB2 associates with p85-PI3K and raises PI3K activity in hepatoma cells (hemi2011:context:000). AKT phosphorylation in response to growth factors depends on PI3K: wortmannin blocks it after EGF or insulin (borisov2009:findings:009), and GDC0941 blocks it after insulin (budi2015:findings:006). Together these imply that ERBB2 activation should raise AKT phosphorylation in a PI3K-dependent way, making ERBB2 an upstream activator of AKT.
hypotheses.prediction: Stimuli that transactivate ErbB2 (anisomycin, TNF or glucose oxidase in Fao cells) should increase phospho-AKT. This increase should be reduced by ErbB2 knockdown and abolished by wortmannin. Total AKT should not change.
hypotheses.test: In Fao or HepG2 cells, deplete ErbB2 by siRNA and compare with control siRNA, with or without wortmannin pretreatment. Then stimulate with anisomycin or glucose oxidase, co-immunoprecipitate ErbB2 with p85, and immunoblot for phospho-ErbB2, phospho-AKT and total AKT over a time course.

citations.title: p38 mitogen-activated protein kinase-dependent transactivation of ErbB receptor family: a novel common mechanism for stress-induced IRS-1 serine phosphorylation and insulin resistance.
Transactivation of ErbB2 and ErbB3 by tumor necrosis factor-alpha and anisomycin leads to impaired insulin signaling through serine/threonine phosphorylation of IRS proteins.
HER2 Amplification in Tumors Activates PI3K/Akt Signaling Independent of HER3.
Intermolecular biparatopic trapping of ErbB2 prevents compensatory activation of PI3K/AKT via RAS-p110 crosstalk.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the plain-language mechanism (ErbB2 recruits p85-PI3K and raises phospho-AKT), the entities together (ErbB2/ErbB3 transactivation by TNF/anisomycin/glucose oxidase in Fao hepatoma cells), and the prediction (ErbB2 knockdown or PI3K inhibition lowering phospho-AKT). The Diabetes 2011 paper underlying the corpus claim itself already states that stress-induced ErbB receptor transactivation leads to 'PI3-kinase/Akt activation' in Fao cells, with ErbB2/ErbB3 Tyr phosphorylation coupled to increased PI3K association and Akt activation, and the earlier JBC study established the transactivated-ErbB2/ErbB3–p85-PI3K complex driving a PI3K cascade; independent cancer-biology work shows direct HER2–PI3K binding sustaining PI3K/AKT signalling and loss of AKT activation when ErbB2 is trapped. Since the explanation for this phenomenon is explicitly published rather than merely adjacent, the status is established, not partial.

hypotheses.statement: mTORC1 negatively regulates EGFR signalling, so that mTORC1 inhibition relieves a feedback and increases EGFR-dependent Ras-ERK activation.
hypotheses.mechanism: The claims about mTORC1 show that its inhibition by rapamycin activates ERK through Ras-Raf1-MEK1/2, and that a related feedback acts through upregulation of receptor tyrosine kinases. The claims about EGFR show that it is a receptor tyrosine kinase driving Ras-GTP/MEK/ERK responses and that ERK output depends on EGFR activity. This makes EGFR a candidate receptor through which the mTORC1 feedback reaches Ras-ERK.
hypotheses.prediction: Rapamycin treatment should increase EGFR abundance or tyrosine phosphorylation. The rapamycin-induced rise in phospho-ERK and Ser338-Raf1 phosphorylation should be reduced by EGFR inhibition or EGFR knockdown.
hypotheses.test: Treat MCF7 or HEK293 cells with rapamycin, with or without an EGFR kinase inhibitor or EGFR siRNA. Immunoblot for total EGFR, EGFR tyrosine phosphorylation, phospho-Raf1 (Ser338), phospho-ERK1/2 and phospho-RpS6 to see whether the rapamycin-induced ERK activation requires EGFR.

citations.title: Rapamycin induces transactivation of the EGFR and increases cell survival.
mTOR inhibition induces EGFR feedback activation in association with its resistance to human pancreatic cancer.

novelty.note: I searched for the mechanism in plain words (mTORC1 inhibition relieving a feedback onto EGFR), the entities together (rapamycin + EGFR tyrosine phosphorylation + ERK/Raf), and the prediction (EGFR inhibition or knockdown blocking rapamycin-induced ERK activation). Chaturvedi et al. (Oncogene 2009) report exactly this explanation: rapamycin increases EGFR tyrosine phosphorylation without added growth factor (via c-Src-dependent transactivation), and rapamycin-induced Erk1/2 activation requires EGFR, its kinase activity and intact autophosphorylation sites; a later study shows mTOR inhibition transcriptionally upregulates EGFR, whose activation feeds back to AKT and ERK and is blocked by erlotinib. Because the hypothesis's mechanism and its key prediction are both already stated and tested positively in published primary work, the status is established rather than partial or open; no source was found that tested and negated EGFR dependence of this feedback.

hypotheses.statement: LPS stimulation induces inhibitory phosphorylation of GSK3β in epithelial cells, and this depends on EGFR kinase activity and the AKT it activates.
hypotheses.mechanism: In HME and A549 cells, LPS-induced AKT phosphorylation requires EGFR expression and EGFR kinase activity: EGFR knockdown or erlotinib blocks it (de2015:findings:004, de2015:findings:006). Independently, activated AKT inhibits GSK3β, which otherwise phosphorylates PHLPP and triggers its degradation (haeusler2018:findings:007). GSK3β is also a phosphorylation target of other agonists that activate kinase cascades in cells (casasterradellas2008:findings:010). Together these imply that LPS, acting through EGFR-dependent AKT activation, should inactivate GSK3β by phosphorylation.
hypotheses.prediction: LPS treatment of A549 or HME cells should raise inhibitory phosphorylation of GSK3β (Ser9) above unstimulated levels. This increase should be blocked by erlotinib, EGFR knockdown or AKT inhibition. It should be accompanied by reduced GSK3β-dependent substrate turnover, such as increased PHLPP protein stability.
hypotheses.test: Stimulate A549 cells with LPS over a time course, with or without erlotinib, EGFR siRNA or an AKT inhibitor. Immunoblot for phospho-GSK3β Ser9, total GSK3β, phospho-AKT and PHLPP. In parallel, run a cycloheximide-chase immunoblot of PHLPP to test whether LPS stabilizes this GSK3β substrate in an EGFR-dependent way.

citations.title: IFN-beta production by TLR4-stimulated innate immune cells is negatively regulated by GSK3-beta.
Erlotinib protects against LPS-induced endotoxicity because TLR4 needs EGFR to signal.
Role of TLR4-Mediated PI3K/AKT/GSK-3β Signaling Pathway in Apoptosis of Rat Hepatocytes.
Glycogen synthase kinase-3β modulation of glucocorticoid responsiveness in COPD.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the mechanism in words (LPS/TLR4 → PI3K/Akt → inhibitory Ser9 phosphorylation of GSK3β), the entities together (LPS + EGFR + erlotinib + GSK-3β in A549/bronchial epithelial cells), and the prediction (EGFR-dependent GSK3β Ser9 phosphorylation and PHLPP stabilization). Both halves are published separately — LPS is well documented to drive PI3K/Akt-dependent GSK3β Ser9 phosphorylation in monocytes/macrophages (PMID 18981097), and LPS-induced AKT activation is EGFR- and erlotinib-dependent in HME/A549 epithelial cells (PMID 26195767) — but no retrieved source joins them by showing that LPS-induced GSK3β Ser9 phosphorylation in epithelial cells requires EGFR kinase activity, and none tests LPS-driven, GSK3β-dependent PHLPP stabilization. Nothing found reports a direct negative test of this claim, although a rat hepatocyte study reports LPS lowering rather than raising P-GSK-3β Ser9 (PMID 26770978), which is a different cell type and does not address EGFR, so the status is partial rather than established or refuted.

hypotheses.statement: EGFR kinase signaling negatively regulates TSC2 by driving ERK- and RSK-dependent inhibitory phosphorylation of TSC2 at Ser664 and Ser1798.
hypotheses.mechanism: EGFR kinase activity and its major autophosphorylation sites are required for Erk1/2 and RSK activation: kinase-dead K721M, the inhibitor AG1478 and the Y5F autophosphorylation mutant each abolish it. Independently, ERK phosphorylates TSC2 at Ser664 and RSK at Ser1798, which suppresses TSC2's GAP activity toward Rheb. Together these imply that EGFR kinase output should set the inhibitory phosphorylation state and GAP function of TSC2.
hypotheses.prediction: EGF stimulation should increase TSC2 phosphorylation at Ser664 and Ser1798 and raise Rheb-GTP loading. These increases should be absent or sharply reduced with AG1478 pretreatment, in cells expressing kinase-dead EGFR K721M or the Y5F mutant, and in EGFR-null parental B82L cells.
hypotheses.test: Compare EGFR-null parental B82L cells with B82L cells expressing wt-EGFR, K721M or Y5F EGFR. Stimulate with EGF, with or without AG1478 or a MEK inhibitor, and immunoblot for phospho-TSC2 Ser664 and Ser1798 alongside phospho-Erk1/2 and phospho-RSK. Measure TSC2 GAP output by Rheb-GTP loading or downstream phospho-S6K. EGFR-dependent loss of TSC2 Ser664/Ser1798 phosphorylation would support the hypothesis; unchanged phosphorylation would rule it out.

citations.title: Phosphorylation and functional inactivation of TSC2 by Erk implications for tuberous sclerosis and cancer pathogenesis.
Tumor-promoting phorbol esters and activated Ras inactivate the tuberous sclerosis tumor suppressor complex via p90 ribosomal S6 kinase.
Quantitative phosphorylation profiling of the ERK/p90 ribosomal S6 kinase-signaling cassette and its targets, the tuberous sclerosis tumor suppressors.
Lysosomal EGFR acts as a Rheb-GEF independent of its kinase activity to activate mTORC1.

Pharmacological and genetic evaluation of proposed roles of mitogen-activated protein kinase/extracellular signal-regulated kinase kinase (MEK), extracellular signal-regulated kinase (ERK), and p90(RSK) in the control of mTORC1 protein signaling by phorbol esters.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the mechanism in plain words (ERK/RSK inhibitory phosphorylation of TSC2 suppressing Rheb-GAP activity), the entities together (EGF/EGFR kinase, AG1478, K721M, B82L with TSC2 S664/S1798), and the prediction (EGF-stimulated S664/S1798 phosphorylation and Rheb-GTP loading blocked by EGFR/MEK inhibition). The component steps are firmly published: ERK phosphorylates TSC2 at Ser664 and RSK1 at Ser1798 to inactivate the TSC1-TSC2 complex and raise mTORC1 signaling, and phospho-profiling work used EGF as a stimulus of the ERK/RSK cassette while quantifying ERK-dependent TSC2 Ser1798 phosphorylation; however, no retrieved source tests EGFR kinase activity or its autophosphorylation sites (AG1478, kinase-dead K721M, Y5F, EGFR-null B82L) as the determinant of TSC2 Ser664/Ser1798 phosphorylation or Rheb-GTP loading. The nearest directly relevant work argues EGFR raises Rheb-GTP and mTORC1 activity through a lysosomal Rheb-GEF function independent of its kinase activity and without invoking TSC2 phosphorylation, and another study finds RSKs dispensable for mTORC1 activation by phorbol esters — related but not a direct test of this EGFR-to-TSC2 claim, so the status is partial rather than established or refuted.

hypotheses.statement: EGFR kinase activity activates STAT1 by driving its tyrosine phosphorylation and SIE/GAS DNA-binding activity in response to EGF.
hypotheses.mechanism: EGF treatment induces tyrosine phosphorylation of Stat1 or related proteins and their binding to SIE and GAS sites. In EGF-treated epithelial cells, two of the three SIE bandshift complexes (SIFB, SIFC) react with Stat1 antiserum (darnell1994). Separately, EGFR kinase activity and its autophosphorylation are required for downstream kinase activation, since AG1478 and a kinase-dead EGFR (K721M) abolish it (chaturvedi2009). Together these imply that the EGF-induced Stat1 tyrosine phosphorylation depends on, and is driven by, EGFR catalytic activity.
hypotheses.prediction: EGF-induced STAT1 Tyr701 phosphorylation and Stat1-containing SIE complexes (SIFB/SIFC) should be absent in cells lacking EGFR or expressing kinase-dead EGFR K721M. They should also be abolished by AG1478, and restored by re-expressing wild-type EGFR.
hypotheses.test: Compare EGF-stimulated B82L cells that lack EGFR, express wild-type EGFR, or express EGFR K721M, with and without AG1478 pretreatment. Measure STAT1 pY701 by immunoblot and SIE/GAS binding by EMSA with Stat1 antibody supershift. As a complement, run an in vitro kinase assay with immunopurified wild-type versus K721M EGFR and recombinant STAT1, probing for pY701, to test whether EGFR phosphorylates STAT1 directly.

citations.title: Phosphorylation and activation of the DNA binding activity of purified Stat1 by the Janus protein-tyrosine kinases and the epidermal growth factor receptor.
Roles of JAKs in activation of STATs and stimulation of c-fos gene expression by epidermal growth factor.
Constitutive activation of the EGFR-STAT1 axis increases proliferation of meningioma tumor cells.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: direct EGFR-catalysed STAT1 Tyr701 phosphorylation, EGF-induced STAT activation in cells expressing kinase-dead (K721M) EGFR, and whether EGF-induced STAT1/SIE binding depends on receptor kinase activity versus Src/JAK. Quelle et al. (JBC 1995) report that immune-complex-purified EGF receptor phosphorylates purified Stat1 at Tyr701 in vitro and that this phosphorylation is necessary and sufficient to activate Stat1 DNA binding, while Leaman et al. (MCB 1996) show that in cells expressing a kinase-negative EGF receptor there is no EGF-induced STAT activation (and it is JAK-independent), and the meningioma study shows EGF induces STAT1 pY701 within minutes and EGFR kinase inhibitors rapidly abolish it. Both the mechanism and the predicted loss of the response with kinase-dead receptor or EGFR kinase inhibition are therefore already published, so the status is established; note only that some work places Src between EGFR and Stat phosphorylation in intact cells.

hypotheses.statement: RPS6KB1 (S6K1) promotes 14-3-3 binding to Rictor by phosphorylating Rictor at Thr1135, creating a phosphorylation-dependent 14-3-3 docking site.
hypotheses.mechanism: Rictor binds 14-3-3 largely through phosphorylation at T1135, and a T1135A mutant shows greatly reduced 14-3-3 binding in pulldown and co-IP assays (dibble2009). Rictor T1135 phosphorylation is described as an mTORC1/S6K target readout (cosimo2018). Together these imply S6K1 kinase activity sits upstream of 14-3-3 engagement of Rictor. This parallels the corpus pattern of kinase-dependent phosphorylation creating 14-3-3 binding sites, such as RSK on Bad and MK2 on TSC2 (cargnello2011).
hypotheses.prediction: Recombinant active S6K1 should phosphorylate wild-type Rictor, but not a T1135A mutant, at T1135 in vitro, and this phosphorylation should confer GST-14-3-3 binding. In cells, loss of S6K1 activity should lower Rictor T1135 phosphorylation and Rictor-14-3-3 co-immunoprecipitation. Constitutively active, rapamycin-insensitive S6K1 should sustain both under rapamycin.
hypotheses.test: Run an in vitro kinase assay with purified active S6K1 and immunopurified, λ-phosphatase-pretreated wild-type or T1135A Rictor, followed by phospho-T1135 immunoblot and GST-14-3-3 pulldown. In parallel, knock down S6K1 by siRNA in HEK293 cells, or express rapamycin-resistant constitutively active S6K1 (E389 D3A/E) with rapamycin, then measure phospho-T1135 Rictor and Flag-14-3-3/Rictor co-IP by immunoblot.

citations.title: Characterization of Rictor phosphorylation sites reveals direct regulation of mTOR complex 2 by S6K1.
mTORC1-activated S6K1 phosphorylates Rictor on threonine 1135 and regulates mTORC2 signaling.

novelty.note: Searched for S6K1-mediated Rictor Thr1135 phosphorylation with 14-3-3 binding, for the Dibble/Asara/Manning 2009 characterization of Rictor phosphosites, and for independent confirmation of the S6K1-Rictor T1135 kinase relationship. The corpus paper itself (Dibble 2009, MCB) reports that Rictor T1135 is a rapamycin-sensitive, mTORC1-dependent site directly phosphorylated by S6K1 and that this phosphorylation promotes Rictor binding to 14-3-3 proteins; Julien et al. 2010 independently demonstrate direct S6K1 phosphorylation of Rictor T1135 in vitro and in vivo in a rapamycin-sensitive manner. Both the kinase-substrate link and the phospho-dependent 14-3-3 docking consequence are therefore already stated in the published literature, so the explanation is established rather than novel, and nothing found reports a negative test.

hypotheses.statement: c-Src directly tyrosine-phosphorylates IRS-1, and this Src-dependent phosphorylation is the step that converts relief of mTORC1/S6K1 feedback on IRS-1 into MAPK activation.
hypotheses.mechanism: carracedo2008 shows that rapamycin activates ERK through an S6K1–IRS-1 feedback arm, with IRS-1-activating ligands cooperating with rapamycin to superactivate MAPK, so IRS-1 is the node transmitting mTORC1 inhibition to ERK. chaturvedi2009 shows that the same rapamycin stimulus activates c-Src (increased pY416, decreased pY527) and that Src inhibition by PP2 or dasatinib abolishes rapamycin-induced ERK/RSK phosphorylation, placing Src as the required kinase in that identical feedback-to-MAPK route. If both claims describe one pathway, the simplest direct link is that the rapamycin-activated Src kinase phosphorylates IRS-1 tyrosines, which borisov2009 shows are docking sites generated upon insulin-type input rather than EGF input.
hypotheses.prediction: Rapamycin (or insulin plus rapamycin) should increase tyrosine phosphorylation of IRS-1 in a PP2/dasatinib-sensitive manner, recombinant active Src should phosphorylate purified IRS-1 directly in vitro, Src and IRS-1 should co-immunoprecipitate after stimulation, and Src knockdown should blunt rapamycin-induced ERK activation without reducing IRS-1 protein levels.
hypotheses.test: Perform an in vitro kinase assay with purified recombinant active c-Src and immunopurified or recombinant IRS-1 (kinase-dead Src and no-kinase controls), reading out anti-phosphotyrosine and site-specific pY612 immunoblots; in parallel, in cultured cells treat with rapamycin ± PP2/PP3 or Src siRNA and immunoblot IRS-1 immunoprecipitates for phosphotyrosine and co-precipitated Src, with p-ERK as the downstream readout. Loss of IRS-1 tyrosine phosphorylation upon Src inhibition/depletion plus direct in vitro phosphorylation supports the relationship; absence of in vitro phosphorylation and Src-independent IRS-1 pY rules it out.

citations.title: Insulin receptor substrate-1 as a signaling molecule for focal adhesion kinase pp125(FAK) and pp60(src).
Src-family tyrosine kinases in activation of ERK-1 and p85/p110-phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase by G/CCKB receptors.
The TSC1-2 tumor suppressor controls insulin-PI3K signaling via regulation of IRS proteins.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the mechanism in words (Src as a direct IRS-1 tyrosine kinase, in vitro kinase assays), the entities together (rapamycin/mTORC1-S6K feedback + Src + IRS-1 + ERK, via PubMed/eutils queries that returned no on-topic hits), and the prediction (rapamycin-induced, PP2/dasatinib-sensitive IRS-1 tyrosine phosphorylation). The first half of the claim is published independently: co-expression of pp60src with IRS-1 drives extensive IRS-1 tyrosine phosphorylation and increased SH2-protein binding (though that study reported enhanced PI3K activity without an effect on MAPK), and gastrin/CCKB signaling shows Src-family-dependent IRS-1 tyrosine phosphorylation alongside ERK activation; the mTORC1-S6K-IRS-1 feedback arm is likewise well established. Nothing retrieved states that rapamycin-activated c-Src phosphorylates IRS-1 tyrosines as the step converting feedback relief into MAPK activation, and no source reports a direct negative test of that specific link, so the conjunction remains partial rather than established or refuted.

hypotheses.statement: TGFBR2 (TβRII) is required upstream for TGF-β-induced JNK activation, acting through ligand-driven receptor complex assembly rather than through its kinase activity.
hypotheses.mechanism: TGF-β1 and TGF-β3 bind TβRII with high affinity, and TβRI needs TβRII to engage the ligand, so TβRII is required to form the receptor complex (derynck2019:findings:004). TGF-β activates JNK by recruiting TRAF6/TRAF4 and TAK1 to receptor complexes, without direct phosphorylation by the type I receptor kinase (derynck2019:findings:030). The L45 loop, which is essential for Smad signaling, is dispensable for this JNK activation (hata2016:findings:011). A parallel TRAF6-dependent output, Lys63-linked p85 ubiquitylation and AKT activation, persists when TβRI/TβRII kinase is inhibited (hamidi2017:findings:011, hamidi2017:findings:006). Together these suggest TβRII couples ligand binding to TRAF6–TAK1–JNK activation as a scaffold, not as a kinase.
hypotheses.prediction: Loss of TβRII should abolish TGF-β-induced JNK phosphorylation. Inhibiting TβRI/TβRII kinase activity (e.g., LY2109761), or re-expressing a kinase-dead TβRII in TβRII-depleted cells, should largely preserve TGF-β-induced JNK phosphorylation even though Smad2/3 phosphorylation is lost.
hypotheses.test: In cultured epithelial cells such as NMuMG, compare the following conditions after TGF-β1 stimulation: siRNA knockdown of TGFBR2, control siRNA, LY2109761 treatment, and TGFBR2 knockdown reconstituted with either wild-type or kinase-dead TβRII. Immunoblot for phospho-JNK, phospho-c-Jun and phospho-Smad2. In parallel, co-immunoprecipitate TRAF6 and TAK1 with TβRII to test whether the complex forms under kinase inhibition.

citations.title: Transforming growth factor-beta (TGF-beta1) activates TAK1 via TAB1-mediated autophosphorylation, independent of TGF-beta receptor kinase activity in mesangial cells.
TRAF6 mediates Smad-independent activation of JNK and p38 by TGF-beta.
The type I TGF-beta receptor engages TRAF6 to activate TAK1 in a receptor kinase-independent manner.

novelty.note: I searched for the plain-language mechanism (TGF-β type II receptor as scaffold for TRAF6/TAK1-driven JNK activation), the entities together (TGFBR2 + TRAF6 + TAK1 + JNK, kinase-dead TβRII, LY2109761/SB431542), and the prediction (receptor-kinase-independent JNK/p38 phosphorylation, TβRII-deficient DR26 cells), retrieving the Yamashita Mol Cell 2008, Sorrentino Nat Cell Biol 2008 and Kim JBC 2009 papers. The component parts are published: TRAF6 binds TβRII directly and can only engage TβRI when TβRII is co-expressed (so TRAF6 recognises the ligand-assembled complex), TAK1→p38/JNK activation is reported to proceed without receptor kinase activity, and a kinase-deficient TβRII (K277R) retains normal TAK1 association while SB431542 spares TAK1 phosphorylation but blocks Smad2/3. However, no retrieved study performs the specific test — TGFBR2 depletion abolishing TGF-β-induced phospho-JNK with rescue by kinase-dead versus wild-type TβRII — and the kinase-independence of the TRAF6 arm is contested (Yamashita et al. report TβRI kinase activity is needed for TRAF6 ubiquitylation), so this is partial rather than established or refuted.

hypotheses.statement: PTEN directly suppresses TNF-induced NF-κB activation, thereby sensitizing cells to TNF-driven apoptosis.
hypotheses.mechanism: Restoring PTEN in PTEN-null PC3 cells cuts basal NF-κB activity roughly in half and blocks mTOR-driven NF-κB induction (dan2008:findings:007), and the mTOR-linked IKKα interaction that PTEN loss enables acts on the same IKK module (dan2008:context:002) that TNF-R1 recruits and activates within minutes to turn on NF-κB (chen2002:findings:004). Because NF-κB output is what protects cells from TNF-R1's parallel caspase-8/apoptotic arm, and its absence raises susceptibility to TNF-induced apoptosis (chen2002:findings:006, chen2002:findings:001), a PTEN-imposed ceiling on NF-κB should convert TNF signalling toward death.
hypotheses.prediction: In PTEN-null cells, re-expression of wild-type PTEN will blunt the TNF-stimulated NF-κB reporter response, p65 nuclear translocation and induction of NF-κB targets such as IκB and cIAPs, and will increase TNF-induced caspase-8 activation and apoptosis; a lipid-phosphatase-dead PTEN should fail to do so.
hypotheses.test: Transfect PC3 (PTEN-null) cells with empty vector, wild-type PTEN, or a phosphatase-dead PTEN mutant, then stimulate with TNF over a time course and read out (i) NF-κB-dependent luciferase reporter activity and p65 nuclear translocation by immunoblot of nuclear fractions, (ii) IκB/cIAP target induction by qPCR, and (iii) apoptosis by caspase-8/caspase-3 activity and DNA-fragmentation ELISA; a reciprocal PTEN knockdown in a PTEN-expressing line should raise TNF-induced NF-κB output and protect against TNF-induced death.

citations.title: PTEN blocks tumor necrosis factor-induced NF-kappa B-dependent transcription by inhibiting the transactivation potential of the p65 subunit.
Suppression of PTEN expression by NF-kappa B prevents apoptosis.

novelty.note: I searched for PTEN suppressing TNF-induced NF-κB and sensitizing to TNF apoptosis, for PTEN re-expression in PTEN-null prostate (PC3) cells with NF-κB reporters, and for the phosphatase-dead PTEN/p65 transactivation angle. Mayo et al. (J Biol Chem 2002) already report exactly this explanation: reintroducing PTEN into PTEN-null prostate cells suppresses TNF-stimulated NF-κB-dependent transcription in an Akt/PI3K-reversible (i.e. lipid-phosphatase-dependent) manner and thereby sensitizes cells to TNF-induced apoptosis; Vasudevan et al. (Mol Cell Biol 2004) independently state that restoring PTEN inhibits NF-κB transcriptional activity and augments TNF-induced apoptosis as part of a reciprocal PTEN/NF-κB loop. The same Mayo paper also directly tested and excluded the proposed IKK-module route — PTEN did not block TNF-induced IKK activation, IκBα degradation, p105 processing, p65 nuclear translocation or NF-κB DNA binding — so the specific readouts predicted at the IKK/translocation level are contradicted even though the overall claim is established.

hypotheses.statement: SRC kinase activity positively regulates c-Myc protein expression through its requirement for ERK activation.
hypotheses.mechanism: Albeck2013 identifies c-Myc as an ERK effector: its expression scales with EGF-driven pathway output and becomes more variable when ERK activity is pulsatile. Chaturvedi2009 shows that Src inhibition with PP2 or dasatinib, but not the inactive analog PP3, abolishes stimulus-induced increases in Erk1/2 and RSK phosphorylation. Together these imply that removing Src activity should lower the ERK output that drives c-Myc expression, reducing c-Myc levels.
hypotheses.prediction: In EGF-stimulated MCF-10A cells, Src inhibition (PP2 or dasatinib) or Src knockdown should lower phospho-ERK and shift the single-cell c-Myc distribution toward lower intensity compared with PP3 or control siRNA. Adding MEK inhibition on top of Src inhibition should give no further reduction beyond MEK inhibition alone.
hypotheses.test: Treat MCF-10A cells with a range of EGF doses plus PP2, dasatinib, PP3 or vehicle, or transfect Src siRNA versus control siRNA. Quantify phospho-ERK and c-Myc by immunoblot and by high-content immunofluorescence at steady state. Include U0126 alone and combined with PP2 to test whether the Src effect on c-Myc depends on ERK.

citations.title: Src Inhibition Blocks c-Myc Translation and Glucose Metabolism to Prevent the Development of Breast Cancer.
A switch role of Src in the biphasic EGF signaling of ER-negative breast cancer cells.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the mechanism in words (Src inhibition lowering c-Myc via ERK), the entities together (dasatinib/PP2 + phospho-ERK + c-Myc in mammary epithelial cells), and the prediction/epistasis (Src effect on c-Myc being MEK/ERK-dependent, plus explicit searches for negative results where Src inhibitors fail to block EGF-induced ERK). Jain et al. (Cancer Res 2015) state exactly this explanation in the same cell background: in MCF10A/MCF12A-derived ER- mammary epithelial cells, Src blockade with saracatinib lowered phospho-ERK1/2-T202/Y204 and, through the ERK1/2-MNK1-eIF4E axis, reduced c-Myc protein (not mRNA) and polysomal recruitment of Myc mRNA. The specific single-cell/EGF-dose and PP2-versus-PP3 readouts are not tested there, and the Src requirement for EGF-induced ERK is cell-type-dependent in the wider literature (hence the nearest citation), but the core Src -> ERK -> c-Myc protein explanation is already published, so this is established rather than open or partial.

hypotheses.statement: SRC acts as a positive upstream regulator of BRAF-driven ERK signalling specifically under feedback relief, such that SRC kinase activity is required for the EGFR-dependent ERK reactivation that follows inhibition of mutant BRAF.
hypotheses.mechanism: The BRAF evidence states that Raf or MEK1/2 inhibition relieves ERK negative feedback and immediately upregulates EGFR (and ERBB3) activity in BRAF-mutant colon cancer and melanoma cells, which is how pathway output is restored during BRAF inhibition. Independently, the SRC evidence shows that when mTOR-directed feedback is relieved, c-Src becomes activated (pSrc Y416 up, Y527 down), phosphorylates EGFR at the c-Src site Y845, and that Src inhibition with PP2 or dasatinib abolishes the resulting increase in Erk1/2 and RSK phosphorylation; Src depletion likewise lowers EGF-driven GAB1 phosphorylation and pERK without changing EGFR autophosphorylation. Together these imply that the EGFR-to-ERK arm engaged after BRAF inhibition runs through SRC, placing SRC directly upstream of the BRAF/MEK/ERK module rather than merely alongside it.
hypotheses.prediction: In BRAF V600E cells, a Src inhibitor or SRC knockdown should leave acute (3 h) pERK suppression by vemurafenib or a MEK inhibitor unchanged and should have little effect on basal pERK, but should prevent the feedback-relief phenotype: no rise in EGFR Y845 (and blunted GAB1/ERBB3 phosphorylation) and strongly reduced pERK/pRSK rebound at 24–48 h, with correspondingly greater loss of colony formation for the combination than for either agent alone.
hypotheses.test: Treat BRAF V600E melanoma (A375) and BRAF V600E colon cancer lines with vemurafenib or PD0325901 for 0–48 h with and without PP2 (PP3 as inactive control), dasatinib, or doxycycline-inducible SRC shRNA/siRNA, and immunoblot a time course for pERK, pRSK, EGFR Y845, pGAB1, pSrc Y416/Y527; co-immunoprecipitate SRC with BRAF and EGFR to test whether the interaction is induced by BRAF inhibition, and score colony formation for single versus combined treatment. Loss of the pERK rebound and of the EGFR Y845 increase upon SRC removal, without change in acute pERK inhibition, supports the hypothesis; an unchanged rebound rules it out.

citations.title: A reversible SRC-relayed COX2 inflammatory program drives resistance to BRAF and EGFR inhibition in BRAF(V600E) colorectal tumors.
Inhibiting EGF receptor or SRC family kinase signaling overcomes BRAF inhibitor resistance in melanoma.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the mechanism in words (SRC as an upstream requirement for EGFR-driven ERK reactivation after BRAF/MEK inhibition), the entities together (SRC + EGFR Y845 + vemurafenib + BRAF V600E), and the prediction (Src inhibitor/dasatinib blocking pERK rebound and enhancing BRAFi efficacy). The kinome-screen study of adaptive SRC activation in BRAF V600E colorectal cancer directly tests this specific claim: SRC kinases are indeed activated upon BRAF ± EGFR inhibition and SRC co-targeting improves efficacy, but the authors report that SRC inhibition did not significantly impact the rebound of ERK phosphorylation, and SRC activation persisted under EGFR inhibition, placing SRC in an ERK-independent, β-catenin/COX2–PGE2-relayed arm rather than upstream of the BRAF/MEK/ERK module. The nearest supporting work (EGFR–SFK–STAT3 upregulation in BRAF-inhibitor-resistant melanoma, where dasatinib overcomes resistance) states the combination benefit but not SRC-dependence of the ERK rebound, so the mechanistic core of the hypothesis stands as a stated negative result.

hypotheses.statement: TSC2 negatively regulates cap-dependent mRNA translation by restraining mTORC1-dependent S6K and eIF4/4EBP1 signaling.
hypotheses.mechanism: The C-side evidence states that TSC2 antagonizes mTOR signaling through RHEB GTP hydrolysis, and that AKT-mediated inactivation of TSC2 is required for mTORC1 activation. It also states that MK2 phosphorylation of TSC2 may regulate mTOR-dependent protein synthesis. The A-side evidence states that mTOR signaling through p70 S6 kinase, 4EBP1 and eIF4 initiation factors promotes translation of specific mRNAs. Together these imply that TSC2 activity should limit translation, and loss of TSC2 should raise it in an mTORC1-dependent way.
hypotheses.prediction: TSC2 knockdown should increase global and cap-dependent translation under growth-factor-limited conditions, along with higher S6K and 4EBP1 phosphorylation. Rapamycin should abolish this increase. Re-expressing wild-type TSC2 in TSC2-depleted cells should lower translation.
hypotheses.test: In cultured cells (e.g., HeLa shTSC2 vs shLUC, or TSC2-null MEFs with or without TSC2 re-expression), measure: (1) nascent protein synthesis by puromycin incorporation (SUnSET) or 35S-methionine labeling; (2) cap-dependent vs IRES-driven translation using a bicistronic luciferase reporter; (3) phospho-S6K, phospho-rpS6 and phospho-4EBP1 by immunoblot. Run each measurement with and without rapamycin.

citations.title: Tuberous sclerosis complex-1 and -2 gene products function together to inhibit mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR)-mediated downstream signaling.
Tuberous sclerosis complex proteins 1 and 2 control serum-dependent translation in a TOP-dependent and -independent manner.
Inhibition of Growth of TSC2-Null Cells by a PI3K/mTOR Inhibitor but Not by a Selective MNK1/2 Inhibitor.
