novelty.note: I searched for TSC2 loss/knockdown raising cap-dependent and global translation, for TSC1/TSC2 overexpression suppressing 4E-BP1 and S6K1 signalling with bicistronic cap-versus-IRES reporters, and for serum/growth-factor-deprived TSC2-null cells with TSC2 re-expression plus rapamycin controls. The core explanation is long established: Tee et al. (PNAS 2002) show TSC1/TSC2 coexpression represses mTOR-dependent 4E-BP1 and S6K1 phosphorylation and impairs cap-dependent translation, with a patient-derived TSC2 mutant defective in this repression, while the MCB 2007 study shows TSC1/TSC2-null cells keep constitutive S6K(T389)/4E-BP1 phosphorylation and elevated polysomal translation after serum withdrawal, both reversed by TSC2 re-expression and largely rapamycin-sensitive. One sub-part of the prediction is qualified rather than supported: in TSC2-null cells clinically relevant rapamycin blocks S6/S6K but not the eIF4E-releasing 4E-BP1 Thr37/46 site, so rapamycin would not be expected to abolish the cap-dependent component entirely.

hypotheses.statement: Actin positively regulates PKC/phorbol-ester-stimulated mTOR (mTORC1) kinase activity by providing the actin-tethered ERK1/2 pool that phosphorylates Raptor.
hypotheses.mechanism: In vascular smooth muscle cells, PKC activation phosphorylates and activates an actin-associated pool of ERK. IQGAP directly tethers this ERK1/2 to actin, and knocking down IQGAP prevents its activation (brozovich2016:findings:030). Separately, PMA-driven mTORC1 activity depends on ERK1/2-mediated Raptor phosphorylation at Ser696/Ser863: MEK1/2 inhibition abolishes both the Raptor phosphorylation and mTORC1 kinase activity, and the phosphorylation-deficient Raptor S3A mutant lowers PMA-stimulated 4E-BP1 phosphorylation (carriere2010:findings:011, carriere2010:findings:015). Together these claims imply that the actin-anchored ERK pool is a source of the ERK activity that switches on mTOR after PKC stimulation, so actin would be required upstream of mTOR in this pathway.
hypotheses.prediction: Disrupting actin filaments, or releasing ERK from actin by depleting IQGAP, should reduce PMA-induced Raptor Ser863/Ser696 phosphorylation and mTORC1 kinase activity toward 4E-BP1. Insulin-stimulated, rapamycin-sensitive Raptor Ser863 phosphorylation, which the evidence attributes to mTOR itself rather than ERK, should be largely spared.
hypotheses.test: In HEK293 or cultured smooth muscle cells, pretreat with latrunculin B or cytochalasin D, or deplete IQGAP by siRNA, then stimulate with PMA or with insulin. Measure phospho-ERK1/2, phospho-Raptor Ser696/Ser863 and phospho-4E-BP1 Thr37/46 by immunoblot, and measure Raptor-immunoprecipitated mTOR kinase activity on GST-4E-BP1 in vitro. Include a Raptor S3A control to confirm that any actin-dependent effect acts through Raptor phosphorylation.

citations.title: ERK1/2 phosphorylate Raptor to promote Ras-dependent activation of mTOR complex 1 (mTORC1).
Hierarchical scaffolding of an ERK1/2 activation pathway.
Co-ordinated activation of classical and novel PKC isoforms is required for PMA-induced mTORC1 activation
A conserved role of IQGAP1 in regulating TOR complex 1.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the actin/IQGAP-tethered ERK pool with PKC stimulation, ERK-mediated Raptor Ser696/Ser863 phosphorylation and mTORC1, and actin-disruption (latrunculin/cytochalasin) effects on PMA-driven mTORC1 output. Both halves of the mechanism are published separately — IQGAP1 tethering ERK1/2 to actin filaments and being required for PKC-stimulated phosphorylation of the actin-bound ERK pool, and ERK1/2 phosphorylating Raptor at Ser8/Ser696/Ser863 to promote mTORC1 activity — but no retrieved source joins them, and none tests actin disruption or IQGAP depletion against Raptor phosphorylation or Raptor-associated mTOR kinase activity. Evidence around the junction is mixed rather than confirmatory: one study of PMA-induced mTORC1 activation reports MEK/ERK (and RSK) inhibition to be largely dispensable for the S6K readout, and the published IQGAP1–TORC1 work finds IQGAP1 attenuates rather than supports mTORC1-dependent S6K1 phosphorylation, i.e. the opposite sign from the prediction; since neither is a direct test of the actin-ERK-Raptor link, this is partial rather than refuted.

hypotheses.statement: Oncogenic BRAF (V600E) directly activates mTORC1 by driving ERK1/2-dependent phosphorylation of Raptor at Ser696/Ser863, so that mTOR kinase activity in BRAF-mutant cells is constitutively supported by the BRAF-MEK-ERK arm.
hypotheses.mechanism: Claims about BRAF establish that mutant B-Raf is constitutively active, insensitive to ERK1/2-mediated negative feedback, and is the dominant driver of steady-state doubly-phosphorylated ERK1/2 with little rebound after MEK inhibition (lake2016:findings:018, lake2016:findings:019, lito2014:findings:001). Claims about mTOR establish that ERK1/2 directly phosphorylates Raptor at Ser696/Ser863 in an mTOR-independent, MEK1/2-dependent manner and that loss of these sites lowers mTOR kinase activity toward 4E-BP1, with MEK1/2 inhibitors completely abolishing mTORC1 kinase activity (carriere2010:findings:011, carriere2010:findings:015). Because mutant BRAF supplies the constitutive, feedback-resistant ERK1/2 flux that these Raptor sites depend on, BRAF activity should set the tone of mTORC1 output directly rather than only through parallel PI3K/Akt input.
hypotheses.prediction: In BRAF V600E cells, phospho-Raptor Ser696/Ser863 and mTORC1 output (4E-BP1 Thr37/46, S6K Thr389) should be high and should fall sharply upon BRAF inhibition or BRAF knockdown, while in RAS-mutant or RTK-driven wild-type-BRAF cells the same treatment should produce a smaller and transient decrease that rebounds along with pERK; expressing the Raptor S3A mutant should render mTORC1 activity in BRAF-mutant cells largely insensitive to BRAF inhibition.
hypotheses.test: In a BRAF V600E line (e.g. A375) versus a KRAS-mutant line (e.g. A549), treat with vemurafenib or transfect BRAF siRNA and immunoblot a time course for phospho-Raptor Ser696/Ser863, pERK, phospho-4E-BP1 Thr37/46 and phospho-S6K Thr389; in parallel, immunoprecipitate myc-Raptor (wild-type versus S3A) from the same cells and measure associated mTOR kinase activity toward GST-4E-BP1 in vitro, testing whether BRAF inhibition lowers wild-type but not S3A-associated mTOR activity.

citations.title: RSK regulates activated BRAF signalling to mTORC1 and promotes melanoma growth.
ERK1/2 phosphorylate Raptor to promote Ras-dependent activation of mTOR complex 1 (mTORC1).
TORC1 suppression predicts responsiveness to RAF and MEK inhibition in BRAF-mutant melanoma.

novelty.note: I searched for the ERK-Raptor Ser696/Ser863 mechanism together with BRAF V600E, for BRAF/MEK-inhibitor effects on mTORC1 output (S6K/4E-BP1/rpS6) in BRAF-mutant cells, and for any immunoblot study of phospho-Raptor Ser863 under vemurafenib. The component parts are published — ERK1/2 directly phosphorylate Raptor at Ser8/Ser696/Ser863 to promote mTORC1 (Carriere 2010, in a Ras/PMA/EGF context with no B-Raf mutant tested), and mTORC1 output in BRAF-V600E melanoma is MAPK-dependent and collapses on RAF/MEK inhibition (Corcoran 2013), with Romeo/Roux attributing the BRAF-V600E-to-mTORC1 link to RSK-mediated Raptor phosphorylation rather than the ERK sites — but no retrieved source states that BRAF V600E sets mTORC1 tone specifically through ERK-dependent Raptor Ser696/Ser863, nor tests the S3A prediction under BRAF inhibition. Nothing found reports a direct negative test, so this is partial rather than established or refuted.

hypotheses.statement: p38 activates RSK1 (RPS6KA1) by promoting phosphorylation of its activating site Ser380, independently of ERK1/2, and thereby drives RSK1-dependent phosphorylation of its substrates.
hypotheses.mechanism: In HEK-293 and HeLa cells, amino acids induced RSK phosphorylation at the Ser380 site (homologous to S6K1 Thr389), and this required either p38 or ERK activity, with each able to compensate for the other. p38 itself was phosphorylated on amino acid stimulation, and a review attributes stress-induced RSK activation downstream of p38 to MK2/3 phosphorylating RSK Ser380. On the RSK side, Ser380 is one of four ordered sites required for RSK1 activation, and active RSK1/2 phosphorylate Raptor and rpS6 Ser235/236. Together these imply that p38 signaling can feed into RSK1 activation and its substrate output when ERK is absent.
hypotheses.prediction: When ERK1/2 is blocked (MEK inhibitor), amino-acid- or stress-induced RSK1 Ser380 phosphorylation and RSK1 kinase activity toward Kemptide should persist but be lost upon p38 inhibition (SB203580) or p38α knockdown. Under the same conditions, RSK1-dependent Raptor and rpS6 Ser235/236 phosphorylation should also be lost. Conversely, constitutively active MKK6 should raise RSK1 Ser380 phosphorylation and Raptor phosphorylation in a BI-D1870-sensitive manner.
hypotheses.test: In HEK293 cells pretreated with U0126, stimulate with amino acids or MKK6-EE expression, with and without SB203580, p38α siRNA, or an MK2 inhibitor. Immunoblot RSK1 pSer380, immunoprecipitate RSK1 and assay its kinase activity against Kemptide, and measure Raptor (RXRXXpS/T) and rpS6 pS235/236 phosphorylation, with RSK1/2 siRNA or BI-D1870 as controls. An in vitro kinase assay with recombinant active p38α or MK2 and kinase-dead RSK1 can separate direct from MK2-mediated Ser380 phosphorylation.

citations.title: Structural and functional basis for p38-MK2-activated Rsk signaling in toll-like receptor-stimulated dendritic cells.
Cellular stress induces non-canonical activation of the receptor tyrosine kinase EphA2 through the p38-MK2-RSK signaling pathway.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the plain-language mechanism (p38 activating RSK1 at Ser380 independently of ERK), the entities together (MK2/MK3 + RSK Ser380/386 + p38 + stress), and the prediction (Ser380 phosphorylation persisting under MEK inhibition and lost on p38 inhibition). Retrieved sources state exactly this explanation: in TLR-stimulated dendritic cells and macrophages, Rsk Ser380/386 phosphorylation and Rsk activity toward substrates (GSK3, filamin A, NHE1) resist MEK1/2 inhibition (PD184352) and are abolished only when p38 is additionally inhibited, with MK2/3 phosphorylating Ser380/386 in trans and bypassing the CTKD; a second study shows stress-activated p38 rather than ERK drives MK2-mediated RSK activation-site phosphorylation and RSK-dependent substrate (EphA2) phosphorylation. The statement-level mechanism is therefore already published, though the specific amino-acid-stimulated HEK293 context and the Raptor/rpS6 Ser235/236 readouts of the prediction are not covered by these reports.

hypotheses.statement: Rapamycin activates ERK2, increasing ERK2 kinase activity toward its direct substrates Raptor and Raf-1 through the Ras–Raf1–MEK1/2 route and in an EGFR/c-Src-dependent manner.
hypotheses.mechanism: Rapamycin raises ERK1/2 phosphorylation through Ras–Raf1–MEK1/2, and this requires EGFR kinase activity and c-Src (carracedo2008:findings:004, chaturvedi2009:findings:009, chaturvedi2009:findings:013). Independently, activated ERK2 phosphorylates Raptor in vitro and associates with it (carriere2010:findings:004, carriere2010:findings:006), and ERK2 directly phosphorylates Raf-1 at feedback sites (lake2016:findings:007). MAPK-driven Raptor Ser696/Ser863 phosphorylation is MEK-dependent but not blocked by rapamycin (carriere2010:findings:011), so rapamycin-induced activation of ERK2 should raise ERK2 catalytic output toward these substrates rather than being cancelled by mTORC1 inhibition.
hypotheses.prediction: In rapamycin-treated cells that express EGFR (such as HEK293, MCF7 or SW13), immunoprecipitated ERK2 should show higher in vitro kinase activity toward purified Raptor than ERK2 from vehicle-treated cells. Cellular Raptor pS/T-P phosphorylation and phosphorylation at the ERK sites on Raf-1 should also increase. These increases should be lost with ERK2 knockdown, U0126, AG1478 or PP2.
hypotheses.test: Treat cultured cells with rapamycin, with or without U0126, AG1478 or PP2, and with or without siRNA against ERK2 alone. Immunoprecipitate ERK2 and run an in vitro [γ-32P]ATP kinase assay on purified myc-Raptor. In parallel, immunoblot Raptor immunoprecipitates for pS/T-P, Ser696 and Ser863, and blot Raf-1 for phosphorylation at the ERK-dependent sites.

citations.title: ERK1/2 phosphorylate Raptor to promote Ras-dependent activation of mTOR complex 1 (mTORC1).
Inhibition of mTORC1 leads to MAPK pathway activation through a PI3K-dependent feedback loop in human cancer.
The identification of raptor as a substrate for p44/42 MAPK.
Different patterns of Akt and ERK feedback activation in response to rapamycin, active-site mTOR inhibitors and metformin in pancreatic cancer cells.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the rapamycin→MEK/ERK feedback mechanism in plain words, the entity combination (rapamycin + ERK2 + Raptor Ser696/Ser863 + Raf-1 feedback sites), and the prediction (rapamycin raising immunoprecipitated ERK2 kinase activity toward purified Raptor). The component steps are each published — mTORC1 inhibition by rapamycin activating the Ras–Raf1–MEK1/2–ERK route (Carracedo, incl. Raf-1 Ser338 and U0126 sensitivity), ERK1/2 binding and directly phosphorylating Raptor at Ser8/Ser696/Ser863 with MEK-dependent, rapamycin-insensitive Ser696 (Carriere; Langlais) — but I found no source that joins them, i.e. none reporting that rapamycin treatment increases ERK2 catalytic output toward Raptor or toward the ERK feedback sites on Raf-1, nor any EGFR/c-Src-dependence test of that output. One paper directly reports rapamycin failing to raise ERK phosphorylation in pancreatic cancer cells (unlike active-site mTOR inhibitors), which contradicts the upstream step in those cells but is not a test of this claim in the EGFR-expressing lines specified, so this is partial rather than refuted.

hypotheses.statement: mTORC2 positively regulates the output of ERK/MAPK signalling by contributing to phosphorylation of RSK at its hydrophobic motif (Ser380), which ERK also controls, so full MAPK-driven RSK activity requires mTORC2.
hypotheses.mechanism: Growth factors induce RSK hydrophobic-motif Ser380 phosphorylation, which is mediated by ERK, and mTORC2 is also reported to take part in this phosphorylation (chou2020:context:000). RSK1-3 are the ERK1/2-activated kinases that move to the nucleus upon ERK1/2 stimulation (cargnello2011:findings:020). RSK1/2 phosphorylate rpS6 at Ser235/236 in response to Ras/MAPK activation, independently of S6K1/2 (cargnello2011:findings:034). So RSK is a point where ERK and mTORC2 inputs converge, and mTORC2 would control how much ERK activity is passed on to RSK substrates.
hypotheses.prediction: With EGF-stimulated ERK1/2 phosphorylation unchanged, loss of mTORC2 activity (rictor deletion or knockdown) should reduce RSK Ser380 phosphorylation. It should also reduce RSK-dependent rpS6 Ser235/236 phosphorylation under conditions where S6K is blocked by rapamycin.
hypotheses.test: In rictor-/- versus rictor-reconstituted MEFs, or in rictor siRNA versus control cultured cells, pretreat with rapamycin to remove S6K input, then stimulate with EGF. Immunoblot for phospho-ERK1/2, phospho-RSK Ser380 and phospho-rpS6 Ser235/236. In parallel, run an in vitro kinase assay using RICTOR immunoprecipitates with purified kinase-inactive RSK as substrate to detect direct Ser380 phosphorylation.

citations.title: mTORC2 Is Involved in the Induction of RSK Phosphorylation by Serum or Nutrient Starvation.
RAS/ERK signaling promotes site-specific ribosomal protein S6 phosphorylation via RSK and stimulates cap-dependent translation.

novelty.note: I searched for mTORC2/rictor control of the RSK hydrophobic motif, for the Chou 2020 study behind the corpus claim, and for the RSK→rpS6 Ser235/236 arm plus any post-2020 follow-up on SIN1/rictor scaffolding of RSK. The Chou et al. Cells 2020 paper (PMID 32605013) already states this explanation and reports the key prediction: RSK Ser380 phosphorylation is abolished in rictor−/− cells while ERK1/2 activation remains robust, i.e. optimal MAPK-driven RSK hydrophobic-motif phosphorylation requires an intact mTORC2. One qualification rather than a refutation: in that same work Torin1 and rapamycin did not block serum-induced RSK Ser380 phosphorylation, so mTORC2 appears to act as a scaffold rather than the direct Ser380 kinase, and the rpS6 Ser235/236 arm was uncoupled from sustained RSK hydrophobic-motif phosphorylation under nutrient withdrawal; the nearest work establishing RSK-specific, mTOR-independent rpS6 Ser235/236 phosphorylation is Roux et al. 2007.

hypotheses.statement: SOS1 associates with EGFR in a manner that depends on EGFR autophosphorylation, and this association is the route by which EGFR tyrosine autophosphorylation drives EGF-induced Ras/ERK activation.
hypotheses.mechanism: EGFR kinase activity and its five major autophosphorylation sites (Y992, Y1068, Y1086, Y1148, Y1173) are required for EGFR-dependent ERK activation, even when the kinase itself remains active. SOS1 is the GEF required for nearly all EGF-induced Ras activation in HeLa cells. Prior work describes a Grb2-SOS complex that associates with, and can dissociate from, the activated EGF receptor. Together these point to SOS1 recruitment to phosphorylated EGFR as the step connecting receptor autophosphorylation to Ras activation.
hypotheses.prediction: After EGF stimulation, SOS1 should co-immunoprecipitate with wild-type EGFR but not with the kinase-dead K721M mutant or the autophosphorylation-deficient Y5F mutant. SOS1 depletion should abolish ERK activation driven by wild-type EGFR. Because ERK-dependent SOS1 phosphorylation disrupts its adaptor associations, MEK inhibition (U0126) should prolong SOS1 association with EGFR.
hypotheses.test: Express wild-type, K721M, or Y5F EGFR in EGFR-null cells (e.g., B82L). Stimulate with EGF over a time course (0-30 min), with or without U0126. Immunoprecipitate EGFR and immunoblot for SOS1, and the reverse. In parallel, knock down SOS1 by siRNA and measure EGFR-driven phospho-ERK by immunoblot.

citations.title: Epidermal growth factor regulates p21ras through the formation of a complex of receptor, Grb2 adapter protein, and Sos nucleotide exchange factor.
Regulation of epidermal growth factor receptor signaling by phosphorylation of the ras exchange factor hSOS1.
A two-component protein condensate of the EGFR cytoplasmic tail and Grb2 regulates Ras activation by SOS at the membrane.
Identification of the mitogen-activated protein kinase phosphorylation sites on human Sos1 that regulate interaction with Grb2.
Epidermal growth factor-receptor mutant lacking the autophosphorylation sites induces phosphorylation of Shc protein and Shc-Grb2/ASH association and retains mitogenic activity.

novelty.note: I searched for receptor-Grb2-Sos complex formation on autophosphorylated EGFR, for the specific Grb2/SOS docking tyrosines (Y1068/Y1086/Y1148/Y1173) as the requirement for Ras/ERK activation, and for ERK/MEK-dependent feedback phosphorylation of SOS1 controlling its association with the receptor. The explanation is the canonical published one: Buday & Downward showed Sos co-immunoprecipitates with EGFR only from EGF-stimulated cells, that Grb2 is required for activated-receptor binding to Sos, and that a phospho-Y1068 peptide blocks both complex assembly and EGF-stimulated nucleotide exchange on p21ras; Porfiri & McCormick state that hSOS1 activates Ras by forming a complex with Grb2 and the EGF receptor and that MAPK-mediated phosphorylation of hSOS1 markedly reduces that receptor association (the basis for the U0126 prediction), and Lin et al. restate phospho-tail-dependent Grb2/SOS recruitment as the route to Ras activation. I therefore score this established, while noting Gotoh et al. as a contrary caveat: an EGFR mutant lacking the major autophosphorylation sites still fully activated MAP kinase via Shc-Grb2 without Shc or Grb2 binding the receptor, so receptor-bound SOS1 is not the only route to ERK.

hypotheses.statement: MEK1 is recruited to actin, in the same IQGAP-dependent actin-tethered signaling complex that holds ERK1/2, where it phosphorylates the actin-associated ERK pool after PKC activation.
hypotheses.mechanism: In vascular smooth muscle cells, an actin-associated pool of ERK1/2 is tethered to actin by IQGAP. PKC-induced activation of this pool needs IQGAP and upstream C-raf (brozovich2016:findings:030). Separately, ERK1/2 activation-loop phosphorylation is carried out by MEK1/2 downstream of Raf, and MEK1 is the top-ranked kinase for the ERK1 Thr202/ERK2 Thr203 site (cargnello2011:findings:002, johnson2023:findings:009). Raf activation of ERK runs through MEK1/2 (carracedo2008:findings:004), so the actin-tethered ERK can only be activated if MEK1 acts on it, which implies MEK1 is present at the actin scaffold.
hypotheses.prediction: After PKC activation in cultured vascular smooth muscle cells, MEK1 should give proximity-ligation signal with actin that depends on IQGAP. MEK1/2 inhibition should abolish ERK phosphorylation specifically in the actin-associated fraction.
hypotheses.test: Treat cultured vascular smooth muscle cells with a phorbol ester, with or without IQGAP siRNA. Measure MEK1–actin proximity by PLA, co-sedimentation of MEK1 with the F-actin (cytoskeletal) fraction, and phospho-ERK in the actin-bound fraction with and without U0126 or PD0325901.

citations.title: Hierarchical scaffolding of an ERK1/2 activation pathway.
IQGAP1 is a scaffold for mitogen-activated protein kinase signaling.

novelty.note: I searched for IQGAP1 as a MEK/ERK scaffold, for actin-tethered ERK activation by PKC in vascular smooth muscle, and for MEK1 association with the actin cytoskeletal fraction. Roy, Li & Sacks (Mol Cell Biol 2005) show MEK1 and MEK2 bind IQGAP1 directly and co-immunoprecipitate with it, with MEK binding required for IQGAP1-dependent ERK activation, i.e. MEK and ERK occupy the same IQGAP1 complex; Vetterkind et al. (Cell Commun Signal 2013), the source of the smooth-muscle actin/IQGAP1/C-Raf/PLA findings, explicitly states this explanation as its model — 'the PKC-Ras-Raf-MEK-ERK pathway is broken down into two modules... the other one, (B-)Raf-MEK-ERK, is tethered to the actin cytoskeleton with the help of IQGAP1'. The explanation is therefore already published for this phenomenon, though the specific predictions (IQGAP-dependent MEK1–actin PLA, loss of actin-fraction phospho-ERK under U0126/PD0325901) were not themselves measured in either paper.

hypotheses.statement: ERK2 directly phosphorylates STAT3.
hypotheses.mechanism: IL-6 signalling through gp130 activates ERK2 via Gab1–SHP2 (heinrich2003:findings:010). Activated ERK2 directly phosphorylates several signalling proteins engaged by the same growth-factor and receptor pathways, including SOS1, Raf-1 and FGFR1 (lake2016:findings:003, lake2016:findings:007, lake2016:findings:002). ERK2 is also selective, since it fails to phosphorylate PTEN (alkhouri2005:findings:002). STAT3 is phosphorylated in response to both EGF and IL-6 (darnell1994:findings:023), the same stimuli that activate ERK2, so STAT3 is positioned to be an ERK2 substrate in these cells. The evidence for this is co-activation only; no claim shows an ERK2 site on STAT3.
hypotheses.prediction: Activated recombinant ERK2 should add 32P to purified STAT3 in vitro, while inactive ERK2 should not. In cells, the component of EGF- or IL-6-induced STAT3 phosphorylation that ERK2 mediates should be lost after MEK1/2 inhibition or ERK2 knockdown. Tryptic phosphopeptides of STAT3 from EGF-stimulated cells should include peptides that comigrate with those produced by ERK2 in vitro.
hypotheses.test: Run an in vitro kinase assay with [γ-32P]ATP using active versus inactive recombinant ERK2 and purified STAT3. Include PTEN as a negative substrate control and SOS1 or Raptor as a positive control. In parallel, stimulate cultured cells expressing tagged STAT3 with EGF or IL-6 after U0126 treatment or ERK2 siRNA. Then compare STAT3 phosphorylation between conditions by immunoblotting, and by 2D tryptic phosphopeptide mapping against the ERK2-phosphorylated STAT3 from the in vitro assay.

citations.title: STAT3 serine phosphorylation by ERK-dependent and -independent pathways negatively modulates its tyrosine phosphorylation.
Repression of Stat3 activity by activation of mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK).

novelty.note: I searched for direct ERK2 kinase assays on STAT3, for the ERK/STAT3 Ser727 pairing under EGF and IL-6, and for the predicted MEK-inhibitor-sensitive component of STAT3 phosphorylation, retrieving PubMed records via NCBI E-utilities. Chung et al. (MCB 1997) report that ERK family MAP kinases, but not JNK or p38, specifically phosphorylate STAT3 at Ser727 downstream of growth factors, and that IL-6-induced STAT3 serine phosphorylation is instead ERK-independent; Jain et al. (Oncogene 1998) report that ERK2 phosphorylates Stat3 on three serine-containing peptides, associates with Stat3 in vivo, and thereby lowers EGF-induced Stat3 tyrosine phosphorylation. The core claim of direct ERK2 phosphorylation of STAT3 is therefore already published, so the status is established (with the caveat that the published work assigns the IL-6 arm to an ERK-independent kinase).

hypotheses.statement: PKA directly phosphorylates GSK3B and inhibits its kinase activity. This mirrors the AKT-mediated inhibition of GSK3β that the corpus already states.
hypotheses.mechanism: One corpus claim states that PKA directly phosphorylates and inactivates GSK-3 in mammalian cells (fang2000:context:001). The corpus also describes GSK3β as a kinase held in check by upstream kinase phosphorylation: AKT inhibits GSK3β, which otherwise phosphorylates PHLPP to trigger its degradation (haeusler2018:findings:007). GSK3B's own activity is readable through defined substrate sites such as Smad3 Thr66 (guo2008:findings:018). In vitro, PKA and GSK3β also act on different substrates: GSK3β phosphorylates PTEN, while PKA does not (alkhouri2005:findings:002). So any PKA effect on GSK3B-dependent sites should come from inhibiting GSK3B, not from PKA phosphorylating the substrate itself.
hypotheses.prediction: Purified PKA catalytic subunit should phosphorylate recombinant GSK3B and lower its activity toward substrates in vitro. In cells, cAMP elevation should reduce GSK3B-dependent substrate phosphorylation, such as Smad3 Thr66, and this reduction should be prevented by the PKA inhibitors H89 or PKI.
hypotheses.test: Step 1: preincubate recombinant GSK3B with ATP, with or without purified PKA catalytic subunit (and with or without PKI peptide). Step 2: detect GSK3B phosphorylation by [gamma-32P]ATP incorporation or phospho-immunoblot. Step 3: measure residual GSK3B kinase activity on a primed substrate peptide or GST-Smad3. Step 4: in parallel, treat cultured cells (e.g., HaCaT or 293T) with forskolin or CPT-cAMP, with or without H89/PKI. Step 5: immunoblot for Smad3 pThr66 and total Smad3 levels.

citations.title: Phosphorylation and inactivation of glycogen synthase kinase 3 by protein kinase A.
Cyclic AMP promotes neuronal survival by phosphorylation of glycogen synthase kinase 3beta.

novelty.note: I searched for the mechanism in plain words (PKA directly phosphorylating and inactivating GSK-3), for the entities together (PKA + GSK3beta Ser9 + forskolin/H89), for the downstream prediction (cAMP/PKA effects on GSK3-dependent Smad3 Thr66), and for any report that PKA fails to phosphorylate GSK-3 directly. Bibliographic records retrieved from the Europe PMC REST service confirm Fang et al. (PNAS 2000), which reports that Ser21 of GSK-3alpha and Ser9 of GSK-3beta are PKA substrates and that PKA associates with, phosphorylates and inactivates both isoforms, and Li et al. (Mol Cell Biol 2000), which reports cAMP-driven, PKA-dependent Ser9 phosphorylation and inhibition of GSK-3beta in neurons. Because published primary work already states exactly this explanation — including the in vitro direct-phosphorylation/inactivation component and the cAMP-elevation cellular component — the status is established; the only refinement in later literature concerns anchoring proteins (AKAP220, GSKIP) that facilitate the same PKA-on-GSK3 event rather than contradicting it, and no source was found reporting a negative direct test.

hypotheses.statement: JNK1 directly suppresses cytokine production in activated T cells by phosphorylating NFATc1 and thereby limiting NFAT-dependent cytokine gene transcription.
hypotheses.mechanism: The claims about JNK1 show it binds and phosphorylates NFATc1 at Ser117/Ser172, reduces calcineurin binding and nuclear NFATc1, and inhibits IL-4 and NFAT-AP1 IL-2 reporter activity, while loss of JNK1/JNK2 raises IL-2 output after anti-CD3/anti-CD28 stimulation. Independently, the cytokine-production evidence states that NFAT family members are the transcription factors whose combined loss abolishes T-cell cytokine production. Together these imply that JNK1 activity sets the level of cytokine output by controlling how much NFATc1 reaches the nucleus, making JNK1 a direct negative regulator of cytokine production rather than merely a co-occurring signal.
hypotheses.prediction: Inhibiting or depleting JNK1 in stimulated T cells should increase secreted IL-2 and IL-4 in proportion to increased nuclear NFATc1, whereas expressing activated JNK1 should reduce cytokine secretion; a phospho-site mutant NFATc1 (Ala117/Ala172) that cannot be phosphorylated by JNK1 should render cytokine output insensitive to JNK1 manipulation.
hypotheses.test: In Jurkat or primary CD4+ T cells, pair JNK1 loss-of-function (siRNA/CRISPR or selective JNK inhibitor) and gain-of-function (activated MKK7+JNK1) with PMA-ionomycin or anti-CD3/anti-CD28 stimulation, and measure secreted IL-2 and IL-4 by ELISA alongside nuclear NFATc1 by cell fractionation immunoblot; repeat in cells reconstituted with wild-type versus [Ala117 Ala172] NFATc1 to test whether the cytokine change requires the JNK1 phosphosites, which would distinguish direct NFATc1-mediated control from JNK1 effects on cytokine production through other routes.

citations.title: c-Jun NH(2)-terminal kinase inhibits targeting of the protein phosphatase calcineurin to NFATc1.
Defective T cell differentiation in the absence of Jnk1.
JNK knockdown enhances CAR-T cell cytotoxicity through elevated NFATc1-dependent transcription in preclinical ovarian cancer models.
c-Jun NH2-terminal kinase (JNK)1 and JNK2 have similar and stage-dependent roles in regulating T cell apoptosis and proliferation.

novelty.note: I searched for the JNK1–NFATc1 Ser117/Ser172 phosphorylation mechanism, for JNK loss-of-function effects on IL-2/IL-4 in T cells, and for the prediction linking nuclear NFATc levels to cytokine output (PubMed/Europe PMC, publisher pages). The explanation is already published: Chow et al. (MCB 2000) report that JNK phosphorylates the calcineurin-docking region of NFATc1, blocking calcineurin binding, nuclear accumulation and NFAT-dependent transcription, and Dong et al. (Science 1998) had already attributed the enhanced TH2 cytokine production of Jnk1-/- T cells to increased nuclear accumulation of NFATc — i.e. JNK1 as a negative regulator of NFAT-driven cytokine output. Status is established rather than open/partial, though the cytokine-direction part of the prediction is contested rather than settled: Sabapathy et al. (JEM 2001) found reduced, not increased, IL-2 in JNK1-deficient mature T cells, and a 2025 CAR-T study found JNK knockdown suppressed helper-T-cell cytokine production even while NFATc1-dependent transcription rose, so the proportionality between nuclear NFATc1 and secreted cytokine is not supported.

hypotheses.statement: ERK2 is a direct positive regulator of MTORC1, activating the complex by phosphorylating its Raptor subunit on pS/T-P sites.
hypotheses.mechanism: Claims about ERK2 show it physically associates with Raptor in an mTOR-independent manner and that activated ERK2 increases 32P incorporation into purified Raptor in vitro, with dual ERK1/ERK2 knockdown abolishing stimulated Raptor pS/T-P phosphorylation. Independent claims about MTORC1 show that a Raptor mutant lacking these phosphosites retains normal binding to mTOR, S6K1 and 4E-BP1 yet supports lower mTOR kinase activity toward 4E-BP1, and that MEK1/2 inhibition blocks mTORC1 kinase activity. Combining the two implies ERK2 acts directly on the mTORC1 holoenzyme to raise its catalytic output rather than to assemble it.
hypotheses.prediction: In vitro, incubating immunopurified mTORC1 with active ERK2 and ATP should raise its subsequent phosphotransferase activity toward GST-4E-BP1 relative to mock or kinase-dead ERK2, and this gain should be lost when the complex contains the phosphosite-deficient Raptor mutant; conversely, selective ERK2 depletion should lower cellular 4E-BP1 Thr37/46 phosphorylation without altering mTOR-Raptor-substrate association.
hypotheses.test: Two-step in vitro kinase assay: immunoprecipitate mTORC1 from cells expressing wild-type or phosphosite-mutant Raptor, pre-incubate with recombinant active ERK2 (or kinase-dead control) plus cold ATP, wash to remove ERK2, then assay mTOR activity on GST-4E-BP1 with [gamma-32P]ATP; pair with siRNA knockdown of ERK2 alone in cultured cells and immunoblot Raptor pS/T-P and 4E-BP1 Thr37/46, plus co-immunoprecipitation to confirm complex integrity.

citations.title: ERK1/2 phosphorylate Raptor to promote Ras-dependent activation of mTOR complex 1 (mTORC1).
The identification of raptor as a substrate for p44/42 MAPK.

novelty.note: I searched for the mechanism in plain words (ERK phosphorylating Raptor to activate mTORC1), for the entities together (ERK2 + Raptor + S/T-P sites + 4E-BP1), and for a possible negative test (Raptor Ser696/Ser863 dispensable for mTORC1 activity). The Carriere et al. JBC paper states exactly this explanation — ERK1 and ERK2 interact with and directly phosphorylate Raptor on proline-directed residues Ser8, Ser696 and Ser863, and phosphorylation-deficient Raptor alleles show that these sites promote mTORC1 activity and signalling to 4E-BP1 — and Langlais et al. independently show that incubation of raptor with p42 MAPK (ERK2) significantly increases raptor phosphorylation at Ser696, MAPK-dependent and rapamycin-insensitive. No source reporting a direct negative test of this claim was found, so the status is established rather than refuted; only the specific two-step reconstitution predicted (pre-phosphorylating immunopurified mTORC1 with ERK2 before assaying it) appears not to have been performed as such.

hypotheses.statement: MAPK (ERK1/2) activity negatively regulates ERBB3 tyrosine phosphorylation, possibly by directly phosphorylating ERBB3 at an inhibitory Ser/Thr feedback site analogous to EGFR T669.
hypotheses.mechanism: Blocking the Raf-MEK-ERK axis with MEK1/2 or B-Raf inhibitors reduced phosphorylation of the EGFR feedback site T669 and increased EGFR/ERBB3 activity. Prolonged vemurafenib treatment consistently raised ERBB3 tyrosine phosphorylation and downstream Akt phosphorylation (lake2016). Separately, MAPK is EGF-activated and directly phosphorylates Ser/Thr sites on substrates such as caldesmon Ser789 (bhalla1999, brozovich2016). Together these suggest that active MAPK suppresses ERBB3 activation, and that it could do so through direct phosphorylation of ERBB3 rather than only indirectly through EGFR.
hypotheses.prediction: Active ERK1/2 should phosphorylate the ERBB3 intracellular domain in vitro at one or more Ser/Thr sites. In cells, lowering MAPK activity should reduce phosphorylation at those sites and increase ERBB3 tyrosine phosphorylation. Mutating those sites to alanine should raise basal ERBB3 tyrosine phosphorylation and make it insensitive to MEK inhibition.
hypotheses.test: Run an in vitro kinase assay with recombinant active ERK2 and purified ERBB3 cytoplasmic domain, then map the phosphosites by mass spectrometry or phospho-specific immunoblot. In cultured cells expressing wild-type or phosphosite-null ERBB3, treat with a MEK inhibitor or express constitutively active MEK1, and immunoblot ERBB3 tyrosine phosphorylation and Akt phosphorylation.

citations.title: MEK inhibition leads to PI3K/AKT activation by relieving a negative feedback on ERBB receptors.
Feedback control of ErbB2 via ERK-mediated phosphorylation of a conserved threonine in the juxtamembrane domain.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the plain-language mechanism (MEK/ERK inhibition relieving negative feedback on ERBB receptors and raising ERBB3 tyrosine phosphorylation), the entities together (ERK + ERBB3/HER3 + conserved juxtamembrane threonine analogous to EGFR T669/HER2 T677), and the prediction (ERBB3 as a direct ERK Ser/Thr substrate, phosphosite-null mutant insensitive to MEK inhibition). The general mechanism is established: Turke et al. show ERK-mediated inhibitory threonine phosphorylation of EGFR (T669) and HER2 (T677) restrains ERBB3/PI3K/AKT signalling, and alanine substitution makes that signalling unresponsive to MEK inhibition — but in EGFR/HER2, with ERBB3 hyperactivated in trans. Kiuchi et al. come nearest to the ERBB3-specific part and argue against it: the residue corresponding to EGFR Thr-669 is an aspartate (Asp-667) in ErbB3, and feedback downregulation of pY-ErbB3 is abolished by the ErbB2 T677A mutant, leading them to conclude the receiver kinase ErbB2, not the activator ErbB3, carries the feedback site; however they performed no in vitro ERK kinase assay or phosphosite mapping on the ERBB3 intracellular domain, so the specific prediction of a direct inhibitory ERK site on ERBB3 is neither stated nor experimentally tested, hence partial rather than established or refuted.

hypotheses.statement: JNK phosphorylates TSC2, and this phosphorylation inhibits TSC2's GAP activity toward Rheb, in the same way the corpus states ERK and RSK phosphorylate and negatively regulate TSC2.
hypotheses.mechanism: The corpus groups JNK with Erk and p38 as MAP kinases sharing dual-specificity MAP kinase phosphatases (alonso2004). JNK is shown to phosphorylate substrates directly after activation by stress signals and MKK7 (chow2000, dong2000). TSC2 is phosphorylated and inhibited by the MAP kinase ERK at Ser664, and it is also targeted by the stress-responsive kinase MK2 at Ser1210, which promotes 14-3-3 binding (cargnello2011). Together these suggest that TSC2 is a hub for MAPK and stress-kinase input, and that the stress MAPK JNK could be a further direct TSC2 kinase. This is inferred by analogy only. dasilva2006 shows that JNK does not substitute for ERK/p38 on at least one ERK/p38 substrate (Spry2).
hypotheses.prediction: Active JNK1 should phosphorylate recombinant or immunopurified TSC2 in vitro on one or more Ser/Thr-Pro sites. In cells, stress-induced JNK activation should increase TSC2 phosphorylation and Rheb-GTP loading, and these increases should be abolished by JNK loss or inhibition.
hypotheses.test: 1. Run an in vitro kinase assay with purified active JNK1 (MKK7-activated) and immunopurified HA-TSC2, detecting phosphorylation by radiolabel or phospho-Ser/Thr-Pro antibody and mapping sites by mass spectrometry. 2. In cultured cells, including Jnk1-/-Jnk2-/- ES cells versus wild type or cells treated with SP600125, stimulate JNK with UV. 3. In those cells, measure TSC2 phosphorylation by mobility shift or phospho-specific immunoblot, and measure Rheb-GTP loading and S6K/RpS6 phosphorylation. Include ERK and p38 inhibitors to exclude indirect effects.

citations.title: Osmotic stress regulates mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) complex 1 via c-Jun N-terminal Kinase (JNK)-mediated Raptor protein phosphorylation.
TSC2 mediates hyperosmotic stress-induced inactivation of mTORC1.

novelty.note: I searched for JNK-mediated TSC2/tuberin phosphorylation in plain mechanistic terms, for the entity pair (JNK + TSC2/tuberin + Rheb GAP activity), for the predicted in vitro kinase-assay result, and ran a PubMed query combining (JNK OR c-Jun N-terminal kinase) AND (TSC2 OR tuberin) AND phosphorylat*; no retrieved source claims JNK phosphorylates TSC2 or thereby inhibits its GAP activity toward Rheb. The closest published work is a direct stress-JNK-to-mTORC1 phosphorylation link that runs through Raptor (Ser696/Thr706/Ser863) rather than TSC2, and a study of stress-induced TSC2-dependent mTORC1 control whose surveyed TSC2 kinases are Akt, ERK, RSK, AMPK, GSK3beta and p38/MK2 with JNK absent. Since nothing states the claim and nothing I found reports a direct negative test of JNK-dependent TSC2 phosphorylation or Rheb-GTP loading, the status is open.

hypotheses.statement: TGFBR1 (TβRI) activates mTORC1 by driving ShcA–Ras–ERK signaling that phosphorylates Raptor.
hypotheses.mechanism: TGF-β-induced ERK/MAPK activation depends on p52ShcA recruited to tyrosine-phosphorylated TβRI, which promotes ShcA-Grb2-SOS complex formation and Ras activation (derynck2019:findings:028, 029). Separately, ERK1/2 and RSK phosphorylate Raptor, and this phosphorylation is needed for full mTORC1 kinase activity toward 4E-BP1, with MEK1/2 inhibitors abolishing mTORC1 activity (carriere2010:context:004, findings:015). Together these imply that TβRI-initiated ERK signaling should raise mTORC1 activity through Raptor phosphorylation.
hypotheses.prediction: TGF-β stimulation should increase Raptor phosphorylation at the ERK/RSK-dependent sites and 4E-BP1 Thr37/Thr46 phosphorylation within the time frame of ERK activation (about 5–10 min onward). This increase should be blocked by a TβRI kinase inhibitor, by MEK1/2 inhibition or by ShcA knockdown, and should be blunted in cells expressing the Raptor S3A mutant.
hypotheses.test: In cultured cells (e.g. HEK293 or fibroblasts), stimulate with TGF-β with or without a TβRI kinase inhibitor, a MEK1/2 inhibitor, or ShcA siRNA. Immunoblot for phospho-ERK, phospho-Raptor, phospho-4E-BP1 (Thr37/Thr46) and phospho-S6K1. In parallel, run in vitro mTOR kinase assays on Raptor immunoprecipitates (wild-type versus S3A) with GST-4E-BP1 as substrate.

citations.title: Transforming Growth Factor β1-induced Apoptosis in Podocytes via the Extracellular Signal-regulated Kinase-Mammalian Target of Rapamycin Complex 1-NADPH Oxidase 4 Axis.
ERK1/2 phosphorylate Raptor to promote Ras-dependent activation of mTOR complex 1 (mTORC1).
Inhibition of the ERK1/2-mTORC1 axis ameliorates proteinuria and the fibrogenic action of transforming growth factor-β in Adriamycin-induced glomerulosclerosis.
Raptor-rictor axis in TGFbeta-induced protein synthesis.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the plain-language mechanism (TGF-β receptor driving mTORC1 through ERK), the entities together (TGFBR1/ShcA/Ras/ERK/Raptor/mTORC1, including PubMed field-restricted queries for TGF-β+raptor, TGF-β+mTORC1+ERK/MEK, and Shc+mTORC1+TGF-β), and the prediction (TGF-β-induced Raptor Ser8/696/863 and 4E-BP1 Thr37/46 phosphorylation blocked by TβRI or MEK inhibition). Both halves are independently published: TGF-β1 activates mTORC1 (p70S6K, 4E-BP1) in a MEK-ERK-dependent manner that is blocked by TβRI and mTOR inhibitors and requires Raptor, and ERK1/2 (with RSK) directly phosphorylate Raptor to promote mTORC1 activity; but the published TGF-β→ERK→mTORC1 work attributes ERK activation to Smad2/3/4 rather than ShcA and never assays Raptor phosphorylation, and the Raptor-phosphorylation work uses EGF/serum/PMA and does not mention TGF-β. No source states the joined claim and none reports a negative test of it, so the status is partial rather than established, refuted or open.

hypotheses.statement: mTORC1 activity maintains cell-surface TGFBR1 (TβRI), so that mTORC1 inhibition reduces surface TβRI and Smad3 activation through ERK-triggered TACE/ADAM17 cleavage of the receptor.
hypotheses.mechanism: Rapamycin-mediated mTORC1 inhibition activates ERK via the Ras-Raf1-MEK1/2 pathway (carracedo2008:findings:004). ERK activation causes TACE/ADAM17 to cleave TβRI but not TβRII, lowering cell-surface TβRI and TGF-β-induced Smad3 activation (hata2016:findings:007; derynck2019:findings:009). The evidence also supports an opposing branch: mTORC1 inhibition activates AKT (carracedo2008:context:000), and AKT moves TβRI to the cell surface via AS160 (derynck2019:findings:010), so the net direction has to be resolved experimentally.
hypotheses.prediction: Rapamycin treatment should decrease cell-surface full-length TβRI and TGF-β-induced Smad3 phosphorylation, with TβRII surface levels unchanged. MEK1/2 inhibition or TACE inhibition or knockdown should rescue the decrease. If the AKT branch dominates instead, surface TβRI will rise and that rise will be blocked by AKT inhibition.
hypotheses.test: Treat MCF7 cells with rapamycin with or without U0126, a TACE/ADAM17 inhibitor or siRNA, or an AKT inhibitor. Quantify surface TβRI and TβRII by cell-surface biotinylation and pulldown followed by immunoblot (or flow cytometry), measure the shed TβRI ectodomain in the medium, and immunoblot phospho-Smad3 after a TGF-β pulse alongside phospho-ERK and phospho-S6 controls.

citations.title: Inhibition of mTORC1 leads to MAPK pathway activation through a PI3K-dependent feedback loop in human cancer.
TACE-mediated ectodomain shedding of the type I TGF-beta receptor downregulates TGF-beta signaling.
Novel roles of Akt and mTOR in suppressing TGF-beta/ALK5-mediated Smad3 activation.
Rapamycin potentiates transforming growth factor beta-induced growth arrest in nontransformed, oncogene-transformed, and human cancer cells.
Rapamycin activates TGF receptor independently of its ligand: implications for endothelial dysfunction.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the composite mechanism (mTORC1 inhibition → ERK → TACE/ADAM17 shedding of TβRI), the entities together (rapamycin + TGFBR1 + cell-surface/shedding + ADAM17), and the prediction (rapamycin effect on TGF-β-induced Smad3 phosphorylation and surface receptor levels), via web search plus Europe PMC/PMC retrieval. Both halves of the chain are separately published — rapamycin-induced ERK/MAPK feedback activation (Carracedo 2008) and ERK-driven TACE cleavage of TβRI but not TβRII that lowers surface TβRI and Smad3 activation (Liu/Derynck 2009) — but no retrieved source joins them or tests whether mTOR inhibition sheds TβRI. Direct tests of rapamycin on TGF-β/Smad signalling that I did find point the other way (mTOR inhibition relieves Akt-mediated suppression of Smad3, rapamycin potentiates TGF-β growth arrest without receptor-level increases, and rapamycin activates TβRI ligand-independently), so the specific predicted direction is unsupported but not directly refuted on the TACE/surface-receptor readout.

hypotheses.statement: RPS6KB1 (S6K1) positively regulates NF-κB activity, acting as a TORC1 output that mediates Akt/mTOR/Raptor-dependent NF-κB activation in PTEN-null cells.
hypotheses.mechanism: In PTEN-null PC3 cells, rapamycin and knockdown of mTOR or Raptor reduce NF-κB reporter activity, NF-κB DNA binding and NF-κB target-gene expression. Raptor is required for this NF-κB activation but not for IKKα binding to mTOR, so some other Raptor-dependent TORC1 function must be involved (dan2008:findings:008, :011, :018). Independently, S6K1 is a Raptor-bound TORC1 substrate whose phosphorylation and activity are blocked by rapamycin and by loss of TORC1 amino-acid signaling (carrire2008:findings:001, :009; barpeled2013:findings:001). This makes S6K1 a candidate Raptor-dependent effector through which TORC1 promotes NF-κB activity.
hypotheses.prediction: In PC3 cells, depleting S6K1 should lower basal and mTOR-induced NF-κB reporter activity, NF-κB DNA binding and NF-κB target-gene mRNAs (Bcl-2, cIAP1, XIAP, IκBα, cyclin D1). A rapamycin-insensitive, constitutively active S6K1 should partly restore NF-κB activity in rapamycin-treated cells. S6K1 depletion should not affect TNF-induced NF-κB activation in low-Akt cells, which rapamycin also fails to block.
hypotheses.test: In PC3 cells, knock down S6K1 with siRNA, or use a pharmacological S6K1 inhibitor, with and without mTOR overexpression. Measure NF-κB luciferase reporter activity, NF-κB DNA binding by EMSA, and target-gene expression by RT-qPCR, with GAPDH and SP1 binding as controls. In parallel, express the rapamycin-insensitive constitutively active S6K1 (E389 D3A/E) and test whether it rescues rapamycin-suppressed NF-κB reporter activity and DNA binding. As a specificity control, repeat the S6K1 knockdown in TNF-stimulated low-Akt cells.

citations.title: S6K1 negatively regulates TAK1 activity in the toll-like receptor signaling pathway.
Osteopontin selectively regulates p70S6K/mTOR phosphorylation leading to NF-kappaB dependent AP-1-mediated ICAM-1 expression in breast cancer cells.
Differential IKK/NF-κB Activity Is Mediated by TSC2 through mTORC1 in PTEN-Null Prostate Cancer and Tuberous Sclerosis Complex Tumor Cells.
A positive feedback loop involving EGFR/Akt/mTORC1 and IKK/NF-kB regulates head and neck squamous cell carcinoma proliferation.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the mechanism in words (S6K1 as the Raptor/TORC1 output driving IKK/NF-κB), the entities together (S6K1 + NF-κB + PC3/PTEN-null/prostate + rapamycin-resistant S6K1), and the prediction (S6K1 knockdown or PF-4708671 lowering NF-κB reporter/DNA binding/target genes). No source states S6K1 as the TORC1 effector for NF-κB; follow-up work from the same laboratory line (TSC2-mTORC1-IKK in PTEN-null PC3, and the EGFR/Akt/mTORC1-IKK feedback loop in HNSCC) uses S6K phosphorylation only as an mTORC1 readout and attributes the effect to direct mTORC1-IKK action without ever testing S6K1. Conversely, two studies directly tested S6K1's effect on NF-κB and report the opposite of the prediction: S6K1 knockdown in THP-1 cells markedly increased NF-κB reporter activity and NF-κB-dependent gene expression while S6K1 overexpression suppressed NF-κB (S6K1 disrupts TAK1-TAB1), and in breast cancer cells overexpression of mTOR/p70S6K (including the rapamycin-resistant construct) inhibited rather than restored NF-κB-dependent transcription while rapamycin augmented it — so the positive-regulation direction has been tested and does not hold, albeit in non-PTEN-null contexts.

hypotheses.statement: SYK is a required upstream kinase for CSF2 (GM-CSF) induction, activating CSF2 transcription through a BCL10–MALT1 signalosome in myeloid/dendritic cells stimulated via C-type lectin receptors.
hypotheses.mechanism: In keratinocytes, IL-17A-driven CSF2 induction depends on BCL10 and on MALT1 paracaspase activity, placing csf2 downstream of a CARD-adaptor–BCL10–MALT1 module (kurgyis2021:findings:008, kurgyis2021:findings:013). In dendritic cells, curdlan/dectin-1 stimulation requires SYK and CARD9 for rapid p38/Erk/Jnk phosphorylation and NF-κB activation and for the ensuing cytokine output (leibundgutlandmann2007:findings:001, leibundgutlandmann2007:findings:002). Because SYK is the proximal kinase feeding the CARD9–BCL10–MALT1 signalosome that these two independent lines converge on, CSF2 should be a direct SYK-dependent transcriptional target rather than merely a bystander of the inflammatory program.
hypotheses.prediction: Curdlan- or zymosan-depleted-stimulated Syk-/- (or SYK-inhibitor-treated) BMDCs and macrophages will show strongly reduced Csf2 mRNA and secreted GM-CSF protein relative to wild type, with the same loss produced by MALT1 protease inhibition or BCL10 knockdown, while stimuli that bypass SYK (LPS/TLR4) still induce Csf2.
hypotheses.test: Stimulate wild-type versus Syk-/- (or R406/entospletinib-treated) BMDCs and macrophages with curdlan and, in parallel, with LPS; quantify Csf2 mRNA by RT-qPCR and secreted GM-CSF by ELISA over 2–24 h. Then in wild-type cells repeat with siRNA knockdown of BCL10 or with a MALT1 paracaspase inhibitor to test epistasis, and confirm transcriptional coupling by chromatin immunoprecipitation for NF-κB p65 at the csf2 locus with and without SYK inhibition.

citations.title: Adaptor protein 3BP2 regulates gene expression in addition to the ubiquitination and proteolytic activity of MALT1 in dectin-1-stimulated cells.
Impaired RASGRF1/ERK-mediated GM-CSF response characterizes CARD9 deficiency in French-Canadians.
Gain-of-function variants in SYK cause immune dysregulation and systemic inflammation in humans and mice.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the mechanism in words (SYK/CARD9-BCL10-MALT1 driving GM-CSF), the entities together (dectin-1/curdlan/zymosan + Csf2/GM-CSF in BMDCs and macrophages), and the prediction (SYK inhibitor/R406 or MALT1 protease inhibition reducing GM-CSF, LPS-independence). Published work supports parts of the claim: Csf2 is among the dectin-1-induced genes in BMDCs in a pathway where BCL10/MALT1/CARD9 are required for NF-κB activation (3BP2 paper), CARD9 hypomorphism impairs zymosan-induced GM-CSF in human monocytes via a Syk-initiated RASGRF1/ERK branch rather than an explicitly BCL10-MALT1 route, and SYK inhibitors ablate β-glucan-induced GM-CSF release in a SYK gain-of-function system. I found no source stating that CSF2 transcription in myeloid/dendritic cells specifically requires the BCL10-MALT1 paracaspase module (the epistasis with SYK and the LPS-bypass contrast are untested), and no source reporting a direct negative test, so the status is partial rather than established or refuted.

hypotheses.statement: SRC kinase activity drives inhibitory phosphorylation of TSC2 on its ERK/RSK sites (Ser664/Ser1798), thereby suppressing TSC2 GAP activity toward Rheb.
hypotheses.mechanism: Src inhibition with PP2 or dasatinib abolishes the increase in Erk1/2 and RSK phosphorylation seen in SW13, B82L and COS7 cells (chaturvedi2009:findings:013), and Src activation directly tyrosine-phosphorylates RSK2 to stabilise ERK1/2-RSK2 binding and promote RSK2 activation (cargnello2011:findings:059); since RSK and ERK phosphorylate TSC2 at Ser1798 and Ser664 to negatively regulate its GAP activity toward Rheb (cargnello2011:findings:035), an active Src pool should set the occupancy of these inhibitory TSC2 sites.
hypotheses.prediction: Src inhibition or Src knockdown should lower TSC2 pSer664/pSer1798 and raise TSC2-dependent Rheb-GAP output (less GTP-Rheb, reduced S6K/S6 phosphorylation), while expression of constitutively active Src should raise phosphorylation at these TSC2 sites; the effect should be lost in cells depleted of RSK/ERK if it is routed through them, and persist in an in vitro kinase reaction only if Src phosphorylates TSC2 directly.
hypotheses.test: In SW13 or COS7 cells, treat with PP2 versus the inactive PP3 or with dasatinib (and in parallel siRNA-deplete Src), then immunoblot TSC2 with phospho-Ser664 and phospho-Ser1798 antibodies alongside pERK, pRSK, and pS6K; complement with a Rheb-GTP loading assay on TSC2 immunoprecipitates and an in vitro kinase assay using recombinant active Src plus purified TSC2 (with and without recombinant RSK2) to determine whether the phosphorylation is direct or RSK-dependent.

citations.title: Regulation of mTORC1 signaling by Src kinase activity is Akt1-independent in RSV-transformed cells.
Src regulates amino acid-mediated mTORC1 activation by disrupting GATOR1-Rag GTPase interaction.
SRC kinase is a novel therapeutic target in lymphangioleiomyomatosis.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the mechanism in words (Src activity setting occupancy of ERK/RSK inhibitory sites on TSC2), the entities together (Src/PP2/dasatinib + TSC2 Ser664/Ser1798 + Rheb GAP), and the prediction (Src inhibition or knockdown lowering pTSC2 and S6K output; direct Src-TSC2 in vitro phosphorylation). The component steps are well published separately — ERK/RSK phosphorylate TSC2 at Ser664/Ser1798 to suppress Rheb-GAP activity, and Src inhibitors reduce ERK phosphorylation and mTORC1 output — and Vojtechova et al. report that Src inhibition lowers bulk TSC2 phosphorylation and S6K1/S6 signaling, but they attribute the mTORC1 effect to an Akt1/TSC2-independent route and never assay the ERK/RSK sites; Pal et al. similarly find Src-dependent mTORC1 activation persists in Tsc2−/− cells but is amino acid/GATOR1-Rag-routed and measures no TSC2 phospho-sites or Rheb-GTP. Because no retrieved source states that Src activity governs TSC2 pSer664/pSer1798 occupancy, and none directly tested and negated that specific site-level claim, this is partial rather than established or refuted.

hypotheses.statement: ERK2 directly phosphorylates RPS6KB1 (S6K1) at Thr421/Ser424 in its C-terminal autoinhibitory region, in the same way the corpus reports ERK2 directly phosphorylating Raptor, SOS1, Raf-1 and FGFR1.
hypotheses.mechanism: Several papers show that activated ERK2 directly phosphorylates signaling proteins in vitro. These include Raptor at pS/T-P sites, Raf-1 at five mitogen-induced sites and SOS1 at multiple sites. Independently, amino acid-induced phosphorylation of S6K1 at Thr421/Ser424 is insensitive to rapamycin and wortmannin but requires ERK and/or p38 activity. This makes a MAPK the likely proximal kinase for these sites. The C-side evidence refers to ERK generically and shows p38 can compensate, so ERK2 acting directly on S6K1 is one candidate route to that MAPK dependence, alongside an ERK-activated intermediate kinase.
hypotheses.prediction: Purified active ERK2 should phosphorylate purified S6K1 at Thr421/Ser424 in vitro, detectable with the anti-P-T421/S424 antibody. This signal should be lost with a T421A/S424A mutant. In cells, ERK2 knockdown combined with p38 inhibition should reduce amino acid-induced Thr421/Ser424 phosphorylation, and ERK2 alone should restore it.
hypotheses.test: Run an in vitro kinase assay with recombinant activated ERK2 (±MEK inhibition of the upstream activation step) and purified wild-type or T421A/S424A HA-GST-S6K1. Read out by immunoblotting with anti-P-T421/S424-S6K1 and by [γ-32P]ATP autoradiography. Complement this with siRNA against ERK2 (vs ERK1) plus a p38 inhibitor in amino acid-stimulated HeLa or HEK-293 cells, and co-immunoprecipitate ERK2 with S6K1.

citations.title: An array of insulin-activated, proline-directed serine/threonine protein kinases phosphorylate the p70 S6 kinase.
MEK1/2 overactivation can promote growth arrest by mediating ERK1/2-dependent phosphorylation of p70S6K.
c-Raf/MEK/ERK pathway controls protein kinase C-mediated p70S6K activation in adult cardiac muscle cells.
Phosphoproteomics identification of ERK-dependent activation of Rps6kb1 in cardiac hypertrophy

novelty.note: I searched for direct ERK/ERK2 phosphorylation of p70S6K/S6K1 at Thr421/Ser424, for the autoinhibitory (SKAIPS) domain as a MAPK substrate, and for the prediction of in vitro kinase assays and ERK knockdown effects on these sites (Europe PMC, PubMed, publisher pages). The general mechanism is published: erk/MAP kinase directly phosphorylates recombinant p70 S6 kinase in vitro at proline-directed sites within and beyond the C-terminal autoinhibitory domain (Mukhopadhyay/Avruch), and cell-based work shows ERK1/2-dependent, mTOR-independent Thr421/Ser424 phosphorylation that is lost on ERK1/2 silencing or MEK inhibition (PKC/TPA in cardiomyocytes, MEK1/2 overactivation, and MEK1/ERK-coupled S418/T421/S424 phosphorylation in cardiac hypertrophy). However, I found no source that assigns Thr421/Ser424 specifically as sites phosphorylated by purified ERK2 in a direct in vitro assay, nor any that connects this to amino-acid stimulation with p38 compensation, and no source reporting a negative test, so the specific claim and prediction remain only partly anticipated.

hypotheses.statement: RAS activates RPS6KA3 (RSK2) by driving its ERK-dependent activating phosphorylation at Ser-386, without contributing to its ERK-independent Tyr-529 phosphorylation.
hypotheses.mechanism: Several claims place Ras upstream of ERK. Ras-mediated Raf activation leads to MEK-dependent ERK1/2 TEY phosphorylation (cargnello2011:findings:002). Insulin-EGF crosstalk that amplifies ERK acts upstream of Ras and at the Ras/Raf level (borisov2009:findings:013). RSK1/2 act in response to Ras/MAPK pathway activation (cargnello2011:findings:034). Independently, EGF-induced RSK2 activation (Ser-386) requires MEK/ERK, whereas Tyr-529 phosphorylation is ERK-independent (kang2007:findings:000, kang2007:findings:001). Together these imply that Ras activity controls the Ser-386 activation step of RSK2 but not the Tyr-529 priming step.
hypotheses.prediction: Expressing constitutively active Ras should raise RSK2 Ser-386 phosphorylation without EGF, and U0126 should abolish this increase. Blocking Ras should suppress EGF-induced Ser-386 phosphorylation. In both cases, RSK2 Tyr-529 phosphorylation should be largely unchanged.
hypotheses.test: Use 293T cells transfected with GST-RSK2. Co-express empty vector, V12-H-Ras or dominant-negative Ras, and treat with or without EGF and with or without U0126. Immunoblot for RSK2 phospho-Ser-386 and phospho-Tyr-529, with phospho-ERK1/2 and GTP-Ras (Raf-RBD pulldown) as pathway controls.

citations.title: RAS/ERK signaling promotes site-specific ribosomal protein S6 phosphorylation via RSK and stimulates cap-dependent translation.
Epidermal growth factor stimulates RSK2 activation through activation of the MEK/ERK pathway and src-dependent tyrosine phosphorylation of RSK2 at Tyr-529.
FGFR3 activates RSK2 to mediate hematopoietic transformation through tyrosine phosphorylation of RSK2 and activation of the MEK/ERK pathway.

novelty.note: I searched for Ras-driven RSK Ser-386/Ser-380 phosphorylation, for the combination of RSK2 Tyr-529 with Ras/constitutively active Ras, and for tests of whether active Ras or dominant-negative Ras changes each RSK2 site (web search plus Europe PMC full-text queries for 'Tyr-529'/'Y529' AND RSK2 AND Ras). The two component halves are published: Roux et al. show oncogenic Ras (61L), but not dominant-negative Ras (17N), drives RSK-dependent substrate phosphorylation in a U0126-sensitive, ERK-dependent manner, and Kang et al. show EGF-induced RSK2 Ser-386 phosphorylation is MEK/ERK-dependent while Tyr-529 phosphorylation is ERK-independent and Src/Fyn-mediated. However, no retrieved source manipulates Ras itself while blotting both RSK2 phospho-Ser-386 and phospho-Tyr-529, so the specific prediction that Ras controls the Ser-386 step without contributing to Tyr-529 is neither stated nor tested and refuted; hence partial.

hypotheses.statement: JNK1 positively regulates IFNG expression in activated CD4+ T cells, acting as an upstream kinase that de-represses the Th1/IFNγ program by phosphorylating NFATc1-a/b and excluding it from the nucleus, thereby shutting down the competing NFAT-dependent IL-4 program.
hypotheses.mechanism: The JNK1 evidence shows that activated JNK1 phosphorylates NFATc1-a/b on Ser117/Ser172, blocks calcineurin binding and calcineurin-driven nuclear accumulation, and strongly inhibits IL-4 promoter reporter activity, while loss of JNK1 leaves NFATc1 constitutively nuclear and drives CD4+ TH cells into an IL-4-secreting TH2 state. The IFNG evidence establishes that IFNγ production is the output of a mutually exclusive Th1 polarization program instructed by upstream signals (MyD88/IL-12/IL-18) and coupled to T-bet, with IFNγ and IL-4 as the discriminating cytokines whose levels move together only when the whole T cell response is suppressed. If JNK1's only documented transcriptional action in T cells is repression of the NFATc1-dependent IL-4 arm, then JNK1 activity should be a direct determinant of the reciprocal IFNG arm rather than a bystander.
hypotheses.prediction: Gain of JNK1 function in stimulated T cells should increase IFNG promoter activity and IFNγ transcript/protein while decreasing IL-4, and loss of JNK1 function (dnJNK1, knockdown, or inhibitor) should decrease IFNG output while raising nuclear NFATc1 and IL-4; the IFNG gain should be abolished if NFATc1-a is replaced with the JNK1-insensitive [Ala117 Ala172] mutant, showing the effect on IFNG runs through JNK1 phosphorylation of NFATc1 rather than through a separate pathway.
hypotheses.test: In Jurkat T cells (the system in which activated JNK1 was shown to deplete nuclear NFATc1 and repress the IL-4 reporter), co-transfect an IFNG-promoter luciferase reporter with activated JNK1 (MKK7+JNK1), dnJNK1, or vector, stimulate with PMA/ionomycin or anti-CD3, and read reporter activity in parallel with an IL-4 reporter as an internal control; confirm at the endogenous locus by qRT-PCR and ELISA for IFNγ after siRNA knockdown of JNK1 versus scrambled control, and test mechanism-dependence by repeating the activated-JNK1 arm while co-expressing wild-type NFATc1-a versus [Ala117 Ala172] NFATc1-a, with nuclear/cytoplasmic fractionation and immunoblot to verify NFATc1 relocalization in each condition. Loss of any IFNG reporter or transcript change across JNK1 gain and loss of function would rule the relationship out.

citations.title: Defective antiviral CD8 T-cell response and viral clearance in the absence of c-Jun N-terminal kinases.
Differentiation of CD4+ T cells to Th1 cells requires MAP kinase JNK2.
Defective T cell differentiation in the absence of Jnk1.
JNK is required for effector T-cell function but not for T-cell activation.

novelty.note: I searched for the JNK1→NFATc1 nuclear-exclusion mechanism, for JNK1/JNK2 loss-of-function effects on IFN-γ in CD4+ T cells, and for the reciprocal IL-4/IFNG prediction (PubMed/eutils, Immunity, Nature, PMC). The published assignment is the opposite of the hypothesis: the IFN-γ/Th1 arm is attributed to JNK2 (Yang et al. 1998; IFN-γ defect in JNK2-deficient, not JNK1-deficient, cells), the Jnk1-/- phenotype is described only as enhanced Th2 cytokines with increased nuclear NFATc, and no source connects JNK1 phosphorylation of NFATc1-a/b (Ser117/Ser172) to IFNG promoter activity. A direct measurement in JNK1-/- CD4+ T cells reports a stated null result — Th1 cytokine production including IFN-γ was normal versus wild type while JNK2-/- cells were significantly defective — which contradicts the loss-of-function prediction, so I score this refuted rather than open.

hypotheses.statement: ERK1 directly phosphorylates EGFR as a negative-feedback substrate, in the same way this corpus reports ERK1 phosphorylating the receptor tyrosine kinase FGFR1.
hypotheses.mechanism: EGFR kinase activity and its autophosphorylation sites are required for Erk1/2 activation, which places ERK1 downstream of active EGFR (chaturvedi2009:findings:008, chaturvedi2009:findings:010). With WT-EGFR, ERK1/2 activation is short-lived, which points to limiting mechanisms acting at the receptor level (agazie2003:findings:014). Independently, recombinant ERK1 phosphorylates another receptor tyrosine kinase, FGFR1, on S777; loss of that site prolongs receptor tyrosine phosphorylation (lake2016:findings:002). ERK1 also feeds back onto its own upstream activator MEK1 (lake2016:findings:010). Together these suggest active ERK1 may likewise phosphorylate EGFR directly and damp its signalling.
hypotheses.prediction: Activated ERK1 should add phosphate to EGFR in vitro. In EGF-stimulated cells, EGFR Ser/Thr-Pro phosphorylation should depend on ERK1/2. Blocking ERK1/2 should prolong EGFR tyrosine phosphorylation, and mutating any identified ERK1 target site on EGFR should do the same.
hypotheses.test: First, incubate immunopurified kinase-inactive EGFR (K721M, which rules out autophosphorylation) with recombinant activated ERK1 and [γ-32P]ATP, and read out by autoradiography and pS/T-P phospho-motif immunoblot. Second, in cultured cells, compare EGF-induced EGFR pS/T-P signal and the time course of EGFR tyrosine phosphorylation after ERK1 siRNA, ERK1/2 double knockdown, or U0126 treatment versus controls.

citations.title: Isolation and characterization of two growth factor-stimulated protein kinases that phosphorylate the epidermal growth factor receptor at threonine 669.
ERK-dependent threonine phosphorylation of EGF receptor modulates receptor downregulation and signaling.
Negative feedback regulation of the ERK1/2 MAPK pathway.
ERK-mediated negative feedback regulation of oncogenic EGFRvIII in glioblastoma cells.
Feedback control of ErbB2 via ERK-mediated phosphorylation of a conserved threonine in the juxtamembrane domain.

novelty.note: I searched for ERK1/2-mediated feedback phosphorylation of EGFR, for the specific juxtamembrane site, and for the prediction that blocking ERK prolongs/enhances EGFR tyrosine phosphorylation. This is long-established: EGFR is a direct ERK/MAP-kinase substrate at the Ser/Thr-Pro motif PL-T669-P (the two growth-factor-stimulated T669 kinases purified in 1991 being MAP2/ERT kinases), T669 phosphorylation in cells is ERK1/2-dependent, and MEK/ERK inhibition enhances and sustains EGF-induced EGFR tyrosine phosphorylation, with T669A mutants resistant to the feedback; the same conserved threonine feedback operates on ErbB2 (T677) and EGFRvIII. Every element of the stated mechanism and prediction is therefore already published, so the status is established rather than partial.

hypotheses.statement: JNK1 negatively regulates T-cell cytokine secretion (IL-4, IL-2, IFNγ) by phosphorylating NFATc1 on Ser117/Ser172 and limiting its nuclear accumulation.
hypotheses.mechanism: Jnk1-/- TH cells secrete large amounts of IL-4, and JNK-null T cells produce more IL-2. Activated JNK1 phosphorylates NFATc1-a at Ser117 and Ser172, lowers nuclear NFATc1, and represses NFAT-dependent IL-4 and IL-2 reporters, while the Ala117/Ala172 mutant escapes this repression. Separately, disrupting NFATC1 activity in T lymphocytes is linked to reduced IFNγ secretion, and activated TH cells secrete IL-2, IL-4 and IFNγ. Together these imply that JNK1 restrains NFATc1-dependent cytokine secretion.
hypotheses.prediction: In stimulated T cells, activated JNK1 should reduce the amount of secreted IL-2, IL-4 or IFNγ, and dominant-negative JNK1 should increase it. Cells expressing the Ala117/Ala172 NFATc1-a mutant should secrete more cytokine and should no longer be suppressed by activated JNK1.
hypotheses.test: In Jurkat T cells, co-express empty vector, activated JNK1 (MKK7-JNK1) or dnJNK1 with wild-type or Ala117/Ala172 NFATc1-a. Stimulate the cells with PMA/ionomycin or anti-CD3/CD28 and measure secreted IL-2 (and IL-4 or IFNγ where detectable) in the supernatant by ELISA. In parallel, confirm nuclear NFATc1 levels by cell fractionation and immunoblot.

citations.title: c-Jun NH(2)-terminal kinase inhibits targeting of the protein phosphatase calcineurin to NFATc1.
Phosphorylation of NFATc4 by p38 mitogen-activated protein kinases.

novelty.note: I searched for the mechanism in words (JNK phosphorylation of NFATc1 limiting nuclear accumulation and cytokine output), for the entities together (JNK1 + NFATc1 + Ser117/Ser172 + IL-4/IL-2), and for the prediction (activated JNK1 or dnJNK1 versus the Ala117/Ala172 mutant on cytokine output in Jurkat/T cells). The explanation is published in full as the stated conclusion of Chow et al., Mol Cell Biol 2000 (PMID 10866678), which maps JNK phosphorylation to Ser117/Ser172 in the calcineurin-targeting domain, shows loss of nuclear NFATc1 and repression of the NFAT-dependent IL-4 reporter that the Ala117/Ala172 mutant escapes, and explicitly frames this as why Jnk1-/- TH cells overproduce IL-4; a later independent MCB paper (PMID 11997522) restates that Ser172→Ala promotes NFATc1 nuclear localization and that Jnk1 disruption enhances IL-4 expression. Nothing found reports a direct negative test, and the only part not covered in the retrieved literature is the readout at the level of secreted IL-2/IFNγ protein rather than reporter/mRNA, so the core explanation counts as established rather than open.

hypotheses.statement: LPS directly antagonizes PTEN function, inactivating PTEN (via inhibitory C-terminal phosphorylation/reduced lipid phosphatase output) so that LPS-driven AKT and NF-κB signaling can proceed.
hypotheses.mechanism: LPS stimulation activates AKT and NF-κB in epithelial cells through EGFR- and SRC-family-dependent signaling (de2015:findings:004, de2015:findings:008), while PTEN is the counter-regulator of exactly these outputs: reintroducing PTEN into PTEN-null cells halves basal and mTOR-driven NF-κB activity (dan2008:findings:007), and PTEN's suppression of AKT phosphorylation is blunted when its C-terminal Thr-366 is phosphorylated, an inactivating modification on the PTEN tail (alkhouri2005:findings:008). If LPS must raise PI3K-product levels to phosphorylate AKT, the simplest direct link is that LPS-initiated kinase activity lowers PTEN's effective activity rather than merely acting upstream of PI3K.
hypotheses.prediction: LPS treatment of TLR4-competent cells (e.g. HME or A549) should increase PTEN C-terminal inhibitory phosphorylation (anti-phospho-Thr-Pro/Thr-366 reactivity on immunoprecipitated PTEN) and decrease PTEN-specific PI(3,4,5)P3 phosphatase activity within the window of LPS-induced AKT phosphorylation, with total PTEN protein unchanged; conversely, enforced expression of active PTEN (or the phospho-resistant T366A form) should blunt LPS-induced AKT phosphorylation and NF-κB reporter activity, whereas PTEN knockdown should amplify them.
hypotheses.test: In HME/A549 cells, run an LPS time course and immunoprecipitate PTEN to blot for anti-phospho-Thr-Pro (Thr-366), phospho-Ser-370 and phospho-Ser-385 plus total PTEN, and in parallel assay immunoprecipitated PTEN's phosphatase activity on PI(3,4,5)P3 by malachite-green phosphate release; then perform the reciprocal perturbations — transfect wild-type PTEN, PTEN-T366A, catalytically dead PTEN, or siPTEN — and quantify LPS-induced phospho-AKT by Western blot and NF-κB activity by luciferase reporter. Loss of PTEN activity after LPS together with PTEN-dose-dependent suppression of LPS-induced AKT/NF-κB supports the relationship; unchanged PTEN phosphorylation and activity with PTEN-insensitive LPS responses rules it out.

citations.title: Overexpression of PTEN suppresses lipopolysaccharide-induced lung fibroblast proliferation, differentiation and collagen secretion through inhibition of the PI3-K-Akt-GSK3beta pathway.
Lipopolysaccharide induces lung fibroblast proliferation through Toll-like receptor 4 signaling and the phosphoinositide3-kinase-Akt pathway.
Phosphorylation and inactivation of PTEN at residues Ser380/Thr382/383 induced by Helicobacter pylori promotes gastric epithelial cell survival through PI3K/Akt pathway.
Association between TLR4 and PTEN Involved in LPS-TLR4 Signaling Response.

novelty.note: I searched for LPS/TLR4-driven PTEN inactivation, for PTEN C-terminal inhibitory phosphorylation in response to microbial stimuli, and for the prediction that enforced PTEN blunts LPS-induced AKT/NF-κB. Published work establishes the general leg that TLR4 ligation lowers PTEN output and thereby permits PI3K–AKT signaling (LPS reduced PTEN mRNA/protein and its dephosphorylation activity in lung fibroblasts, with PTEN overexpression abolishing LPS-induced AKT phosphorylation), and pathogen-induced inactivating phosphorylation of the PTEN C-terminal Ser380/Thr382/383 cluster driving PI3K/AKT has been shown in gastric epithelial cells with Helicobacter pylori rather than LPS. However, no source reports the specific version here — LPS raising inhibitory PTEN tail phosphorylation (Thr-366) with unchanged total PTEN in TLR4-competent epithelial cells (HME/A549) plus PTEN-dose-dependent suppression of LPS-induced NF-κB; indeed the one study that directly blotted phospho-PTEN after LPS (RAW264.7) reported decreased PTEN phosphorylation with membrane recruitment and TLR4 binding, and PTEN overexpression enhanced rather than suppressed LPS-induced NF-κB, so the phospho-inactivation and NF-κB legs are unsupported and partly contradicted in a different cell type.

hypotheses.statement: Rapamycin directly increases the tyrosine phosphorylation and kinase activity of TGFBR2 (TβRII) by activating c-Src.
hypotheses.mechanism: Rapamycin activates c-Src in multiple cell lines, raising active pSrc(Y416) and lowering inactive pSrc(Y527), and drives Src-dependent phosphorylation of a receptor tyrosine (EGFR Y845) that is abolished by the Src inhibitors PP2 and dasatinib (chaturvedi2009:findings:012, chaturvedi2009:findings:013). Independently, TβRII activity is stated to be enhanced by tyrosine phosphorylation carried out by Src (derynck2019:findings:013). If rapamycin's action on Src is general rather than restricted to EGFR, TβRII should be a substrate whose activity rises upon mTORC1 inhibition.
hypotheses.prediction: Rapamycin treatment of cells expressing TβRII should increase TβRII tyrosine phosphorylation and its kinase activity (and downstream TβRI/Smad2 phosphorylation at a given TGF-β dose) with kinetics paralleling Src activation, and this increase should be abolished by PP2 or dasatinib but not by the inactive analog PP3.
hypotheses.test: Treat a cell line in which rapamycin activates Src (e.g., SW13 or COS7) with rapamycin ± PP2/PP3 or dasatinib, immunoprecipitate endogenous or epitope-tagged TβRII, and blot with a pan-phosphotyrosine antibody; in parallel run an in vitro kinase assay on the immunoprecipitated receptor and immunoblot lysates for phospho-Smad2 after a submaximal TGF-β pulse. Loss of the rapamycin-induced phosphotyrosine/activity gain under Src inhibition, or its absence in Src-knockdown cells, would confirm or rule out the relationship.

citations.title: Rapamycin activates TGF receptor independently of its ligand: implications for endothelial dysfunction.
Rapamycin induces the TGFbeta1/Smad signaling cascade in renal mesangial cells upstream of mTOR.
Src phosphorylates Tyr284 in TGF-beta type II receptor and regulates TGF-beta stimulation of p38 MAPK during breast cancer cell proliferation and invasion.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: rapamycin/mTOR inhibition acting on TGF-β receptor signalling, Src-mediated tyrosine phosphorylation of TβRII/TGFBR2 and its effect on receptor kinase activity, and the joint prediction (rapamycin + Src inhibitors PP2/dasatinib + TβRII phosphotyrosine) via PubMed and Europe PMC. Both halves exist separately in print — rapamycin/sirolimus is reported to activate TGF-β receptor signalling and Smad2 phosphorylation in a ligand-independent way (attributed to FKBP12 release from TβRI, with ROS/p38 involvement, not to Src or to the type II receptor), and Src is reported to phosphorylate TβRII on Tyr284 (though that event left Smad2/3 signalling unchanged and acted through Grb2/p38) — but no retrieved source states that rapamycin raises TβRII tyrosine phosphorylation or kinase activity, nor tests Src inhibition of such an effect. No stated negative result on this specific claim was found, so the status is partial rather than refuted or established.

hypotheses.statement: RAF kinase activity negatively regulates TSC2 by driving its inhibitory phosphorylation at the ERK site Ser664 and the RSK site Ser1798.
hypotheses.mechanism: c-Raf inhibition with GW-5074 in HEK293 cells abolishes MEK and ERK activity (borisov2009). ERK and RSK phosphorylate TSC2 at Ser664 and Ser1798, which suppresses its GAP activity toward Rheb (cargnello2011), and Ras/MAPK signalling is described as inactivating TSC2 through these kinases (carrire2008).
