Raf or MEK inhibition can also relieve ERK feedback and raise Akt phosphorylation (lake2016), and AKT inactivates TSC2 (haeusler2018), so Raf inhibition may shift TSC2 phosphorylation from ERK/RSK sites towards AKT sites rather than simply activating TSC2.
hypotheses.prediction: In growth-factor-stimulated cells, acute RAF inhibition should reduce TSC2 Ser664 and Ser1798 phosphorylation and lower Rheb-GTP loading. Prolonged RAF inhibition should raise AKT-site TSC2 Thr1462 phosphorylation as Akt activity increases. Constitutively active MEK should restore Ser664 and Ser1798 phosphorylation despite RAF inhibition.
hypotheses.test: Stimulate HEK293 cells with EGF after pretreatment with GW-5074 or vehicle, at short (15–30 min) and long (24 h) times. Immunoblot for phospho-TSC2 Ser664, Ser1798 and Thr1462, total TSC2, phospho-ERK and phospho-Akt. Measure Rheb GTP loading by nucleotide pull-down or immunoprecipitation. Include a rescue arm transfected with constitutively active MEK1 to test whether RAF's effect on TSC2 runs entirely through MEK-ERK.

citations.title: Phosphorylation and functional inactivation of TSC2 by Erk implications for tuberous sclerosis and cancer pathogenesis.
Tumor-promoting phorbol esters and activated Ras inactivate the tuberous sclerosis tumor suppressor complex via p90 ribosomal S6 kinase.
TSC2/Rheb signaling mediates ERK-dependent regulation of mTORC1 activity in C2C12 myoblasts.
Regulation of TORC1 by MAPK Signaling Determines Sensitivity and Acquired Resistance to Trametinib in Pediatric BRAFV600E Brain Tumor Models.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the mechanism in words (ERK/RSK phospho-inactivation of TSC2 at Ser664/Ser1798), the entities together (Raf/BRAF + TSC2 + Rheb + S664/S1798 via Europe PMC and web search), and the prediction (RAF/MEK inhibitor effects on TSC2 Ser664, Ser1798, Thr1462 and Rheb-GTP loading). The upstream half is firmly published: ERK phosphorylates TSC2 at Ser664 and RSK at Ser1798 to inactivate it and raise mTORC1 signalling, MEK inhibition (U0126) abolishes Ser664 phosphorylation and Rheb-dependent mTORC1 activation, and in BRAF-V600E tumour models TORC1 is described as activated through ERK-mediated inactivation of the TSC complex with MEK inhibition suppressing it. What I could not find is any study that inhibits RAF itself (e.g. GW-5074) and reads out TSC2 Ser664/Ser1798 with Rheb-GTP loading, nor any report of prolonged RAF inhibition raising the AKT site Thr1462 as Akt rebounds; hence partial rather than established, and no negative test was found.

hypotheses.statement: RAF (c-Raf/Raf-1) activity positively regulates phosphorylation of RPS6KB1 (S6K1) at Thr421/Ser424, acting as the upstream kinase input that supplies the ERK-dependent component of this phosphorylation.
hypotheses.mechanism: In HEK293 cells, inhibiting c-Raf with GW-5074 eliminated MEK and ERK activities, so ERK activity in these cells depends on Raf (borisov2009:findings:013; cargnello2011:findings:002). Separately, in HEK-293 and HeLa cells, S6K1 phosphorylation at Thr421/Ser424 requires ERK or p38 activity, is independent of rapamycin and wortmannin, and is blocked completely only when both pathways are inhibited (casasterradellas2008:findings:003, casasterradellas2008:findings:011). Together these claims imply that Raf activity should control the ERK-dependent share of S6K1 Thr421/Ser424 phosphorylation.
hypotheses.prediction: In HEK293 or HeLa cells stimulated with amino acids or insulin, Raf inhibition (GW-5074) or Raf-1 knockdown will lower phospho-ERK and reduce S6K1 Thr421/Ser424 phosphorylation. Because p38 can compensate, Raf inhibition alone will give a partial reduction, and Raf inhibition combined with p38 inhibition will abolish the phosphorylation. Rapamycin-sensitive Thr389 phosphorylation of S6K1 will be largely unaffected by Raf inhibition.
hypotheses.test: Pretreat HEK293 or HeLa cells with GW-5074, a p38 inhibitor, both together, or vehicle, or transfect Raf-1 siRNA versus control siRNA. Stimulate with an amino acid mix or insulin, then immunoblot for phospho-MEK, phospho-ERK, phospho-S6K1 Thr421/Ser424, phospho-S6K1 Thr389, total S6K1 and phospho-S6 Ser235/236. Add a MEK inhibitor (U0126) arm to confirm the effect runs through the Raf–MEK–ERK route.

citations.title: c-Raf/MEK/ERK pathway controls protein kinase C-mediated p70S6K activation in adult cardiac muscle cells.
MEK1/2 overactivation can promote growth arrest by mediating ERK1/2-dependent phosphorylation of p70S6K.

novelty.note: I searched for the plain-language mechanism (Raf as upstream input to S6K1 Thr421/Ser424), the entities together (c-Raf/MEK/ERK + p70S6K + T421/S424 + rapamycin-insensitivity), and the prediction (Raf inhibition/dominant-negative c-Raf lowering this phosphorylation while sparing Thr389), via Europe PMC and general scholarly search. A 2002 J Biol Chem study states exactly this explanation: dominant-negative c-Raf or the MEK1/2 inhibitor U0126 blocks S6K1 Thr-421/Ser-424 phosphorylation, which rapamycin leaves intact, placing c-Raf/MEK/ERK as the upstream, mTOR-independent input to these sites; a 2014 study independently shows ERK1/2 silencing suppresses p70S6K phosphorylation downstream of MEK1/2. The specific cell context (HEK293/HeLa, amino acid or insulin stimulation) and the p38-compensation part of the prediction were not found tested, but the stated explanation itself is published, so this is established rather than open or partial.

hypotheses.statement: ERK2 directly binds and phosphorylates RSK (at the ERK1/2-dependent activation sites, e.g. Thr573 and Ser363 in RSK1), thereby activating RSK.
hypotheses.mechanism: RSK isoforms form a complex with ERK1/2 in quiescent cells, and RSK activation requires ordered phosphorylation of essential sites that ERK1/2 carry out (cargnello2011:findings:018, cargnello2011:findings:023). ERK2 specifically is an active kinase after PMA stimulation that phosphorylates purified substrates in vitro, and knocking down ERK2 alone partially reduces PMA-stimulated substrate phosphorylation (carriere2010:findings:004, carriere2010:findings:002). RSK-dependent Raptor phosphorylation after PMA or EGF is almost completely blocked by MEK inhibition (carrire2008:findings:001), which places RSK activity downstream of MEK-ERK signaling. Together these claims suggest that ERK2 on its own is a direct activating kinase of RSK, although the cited claims establish this only for ERK1/2 collectively.
hypotheses.prediction: Activated recombinant ERK2 should phosphorylate kinase-inactive RSK1 at Thr573 (and Ser363) in vitro, and ERK2 should co-immunoprecipitate with RSK1 in unstimulated cells. In PMA-stimulated HEK293 cells, ERK2 knockdown should reduce RSK1 Thr573/Ser380 phosphorylation and RSK-dependent Raptor phosphorylation, and ERK1 plus ERK2 knockdown should abolish them.
hypotheses.test: Run an in vitro kinase assay with active versus unphosphorylated recombinant ERK2 and purified kinase-inactive RSK1 (K112/464R), using [γ-32P]ATP and phospho-site-specific immunoblotting, with a T573A RSK1 mutant as a control. In parallel, knock down ERK2, ERK1, or both by siRNA in HEK293 cells and immunoblot for RSK1 pThr573/pSer380 and Raptor RXRXXpS/T after PMA stimulation. Also co-immunoprecipitate HA-ERK2 with RSK1, comparing wild-type RSK1 against a D-domain docking mutant.

citations.title: Structural assembly of the signaling competent ERK2-RSK1 heterodimeric protein kinase complex.
Phosphorylation of p90 ribosomal S6 kinase (RSK) regulates extracellular signal-regulated kinase docking and RSK activity.

novelty.note: I searched for the regulatory phosphorylation sites of p90RSK inducible by MAPK, for the ERK docking (D-domain) interaction with RSK, and for direct ERK2–RSK1 complex/kinase-assay work. The PNAS 2015 structural study explicitly reconstitutes a direct ERK2–RSK1 complex in which ERK2 docks on the RSK1 linear motif and, in in vitro kinase assays with preactivated ERK2, phosphorylates RSK1 at the C-terminal-domain activation-loop site Thr573; Roux et al. (Mol Cell Biol 2003) independently show RSK1 is constitutively bound to ERK1/2 in quiescent HEK293 cells through a C-terminal docking site, with mitogen-induced dissociation. Both the direct binding and the direct ERK2-catalyzed activating phosphorylation are therefore already published, so the status is established rather than partial.

hypotheses.statement: BCL2 acts as a suppressor of TNF-induced apoptosis specifically in type II cells, where the TNF-R1 death pathway must route through mitochondria.
hypotheses.mechanism: TNF-R1 recruits TRADD/FADD and activates caspase-8 to initiate apoptosis (chen2002:findings:001), and loss of NF-κB activity increases susceptibility to this death while enforced NF-κB activation protects (chen2002:findings:006). Extrinsic apoptosis is reported to be insensitive to BCL2 overexpression in type I cells but to require CASP8-mediated BID cleavage in type II cells (galluzzi2018:findings:006), so in type II cells the anti-apoptotic BCL2 protein should intercept the TNF-R1 signal at the mitochondrial step, and pharmacological BCL2 inhibition is feasible with venetoclax (galluzzi2018:findings:049).
hypotheses.prediction: In type II-like cells, BCL2 knockdown or venetoclax should markedly lower the threshold for TNF plus cycloheximide killing and BCL2 overexpression should protect, whereas in type I-like lymphoid lines neither manipulation should change TNF-induced apoptosis.
hypotheses.test: In paired type II (e.g. hepatocyte-derived or carcinoma) and type I-like lymphoid cell lines, compare TNF+cycloheximide dose–response apoptosis (caspase-3/7 activity and DNA fragmentation) across four conditions — control, BCL2 siRNA, venetoclax co-treatment, and BCL2 overexpression — and score cytochrome c release and BID cleavage by western blot to confirm the mitochondrial step is where BCL2 intervenes.

citations.title: NF-κB activation fails to protect cells to TNFα-induced apoptosis in the absence of Bcl-xL, but not Mcl-1, Bcl-2 or Bcl-w.
Two CD95 (APO-1/Fas) signaling pathways.
Mitochondrial carrier homolog 2 is a target of tBID in cells signaled to die by tumor necrosis factor alpha.
Rejuvenating Bi(d)ology.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the plain-language mechanism (death-receptor apoptosis routed through mitochondria and blocked by BCL2 only in type II cells), the entities together (TNF/TNF-R1 + BCL2 + BID + type II + hepatocytes/HeLa), and the prediction (BCL2 knockdown or venetoclax lowering the TNF+cycloheximide killing threshold; BCL2 overexpression protecting). The type I/type II BCL2-sensitivity model itself is long established for CD95 (Scaffidi 1998) and the BCL2-family block on tBID/BAX at mitochondria is documented for the TNF pathway (Grinberg 2005, where BCL-XL is the effective blocker; Zinkel 2012 review for hepatocyte type II TNF/BID signalling). However, Casanelles et al. directly performed the loss-of-function arm of the prediction in canonical type II-like cells (HeLa, plus RD and DU-145) with NF-κB protection removed, and report that specific knockdown of Bcl-xL, but explicitly not of Bcl-2 (nor Bcl-w or Mcl-1), sensitizes cells to TNFα-induced apoptosis with caspase activation and cytochrome c release — a stated negative result for BCL2 being the suppressor at the mitochondrial step in these cells, so the claim is refuted as specified.

hypotheses.statement: Ligand-activated TLR4 positively regulates (activates) MTOR kinase activity within mTORC1, through an EGFR- and ERK-dependent route.
hypotheses.mechanism: In A549 cells, LPS stimulation of TLR4 drives ERK and AKT phosphorylation, and this requires EGFR kinase activity because erlotinib blocks it (de2015:findings:006); TLR4 knockdown also abolishes EGF-driven downstream signaling (de2015:findings:002). Separately, ERK1/2- and RSK-dependent Raptor phosphorylation is required for full mitogen-stimulated mTORC1 kinase activity toward 4E-BP1, and MEK1/2 inhibition completely blocks mTORC1 activity under Ras/MAPK stimulation (carriere2010:findings:015, carrire2008:findings:010). Taken together, TLR4-induced ERK activation should feed into ERK-dependent Raptor phosphorylation and so increase MTOR kinase output.
hypotheses.prediction: LPS stimulation of TLR4-expressing epithelial cells such as A549 should increase Raptor Ser696/Ser863 phosphorylation, 4E-BP1 Thr37/Thr46 phosphorylation and mTOR immunoprecipitate kinase activity toward GST-4E-BP1. This increase should be lost with TLR4 siRNA, erlotinib or a MEK1/2 inhibitor, and should be reduced in cells expressing the phosphorylation-deficient Raptor S3A mutant.
hypotheses.test: In A549 cells transfected with TLR4 siRNA or control siRNA, or pretreated with erlotinib or PD184352, stimulate with LPS. Then immunoblot for phospho-ERK, phospho-Raptor (Ser696/Ser863), phospho-4E-BP1 (Thr37/Thr46) and phospho-S6K1, and run an in vitro mTOR kinase assay on mTOR immunoprecipitates using GST-4E-BP1 as substrate. Repeat the LPS stimulation in cells expressing wild-type versus S3A Raptor to test whether the TLR4-driven increase in mTOR activity depends on ERK-site phosphorylation of Raptor.

citations.title: Cot/tpl2-MKK1/2-Erk1/2 controls mTORC1-mediated mRNA translation in Toll-like receptor-activated macrophages.
Activation of MTOR in pulmonary epithelium promotes LPS-induced acute lung injury.

novelty.note: I searched for the mechanism in words (TLR4/LPS activating mTORC1 through ERK and Raptor phosphorylation), for the entities together (TLR4 + EGFR + mTOR + erlotinib in A549/lung epithelium), and for the prediction (LPS raising Raptor Ser696/Ser863, 4E-BP1 Thr37/46 and mTOR immunoprecipitate kinase activity, blocked by MEK inhibition), plus a search for stated negative results. Published work separately establishes each arm: in LPS/TLR-activated macrophages the Cot/tpl2–MKK1/2–ERK1/2 module drives mTORC1 output (RSK, S6, 4E-BP1 phosphorylation, blocked by MEK inhibition, with RSK-mediated Raptor phosphorylation invoked as the link), and in mouse lung and human bronchial epithelium LPS induces MTOR phosphorylation via TLR4; EGFR-dependence of LPS-driven ERK/AKT is published but never connected to mTORC1 or to Raptor ERK-site phosphorylation. No source states the composite TLR4→EGFR→ERK→Raptor→mTOR-kinase-activity explanation or tests the S3A Raptor prediction under LPS, and none reports a negative test of it, so this is partial rather than established or refuted.

hypotheses.statement: RAS activates ERK1 by driving MEK-dependent phosphorylation of ERK1's activation-loop Thr202, so RAS acts as an upstream activator of ERK1.
hypotheses.mechanism: Constitutively active V12-H-Ras is sufficient to induce ERK1/2 activation (agazie2003:findings:003). ERK1/2 are phosphorylated by MEK1/2 in their activation-loop TEY motif downstream of Ras-mediated Raf activation (cargnello2011:findings:002). Motif scoring ranks MEK1 as the top kinase for the ERK1 Thr202 site, and MEK1's substrates are essentially restricted to ERK1 and ERK2 sites (johnson2023:findings:009; ubersax2007:findings:002). Together these imply that RAS activity is converted specifically into ERK1 Thr202 phosphorylation through MEK. Consistent with this, blocking MEK with PD98059 suppresses stimulus-induced ERK1 phosphorylation (waters1995:findings:003).
hypotheses.prediction: Expressing active RAS (V12-H-Ras) alone, without growth factor, should increase ERK1 Thr202/Tyr204 phosphorylation and ERK1 kinase activity toward a known ERK1 substrate such as Raptor or FGFR1 S777. MEK inhibition with U0126 or PD98059 should abolish this increase. Dominant-negative RAS, or interfering with RAS activation, should reduce EGF-induced ERK1 phosphorylation.
hypotheses.test: In HEK293 or COS-1 cells, transfect V12-H-Ras, empty vector, or dominant-negative RAS. Measure ERK1 activation by immunoblotting with a phospho-Thr202/Tyr204 antibody, resolving ERK1 from ERK2 by molecular weight and using ERK1-specific immunoprecipitation. Run an in vitro kinase assay of immunoprecipitated ERK1 on purified Raptor, with and without U0126 pretreatment. As a further check, knock down ERK1 by siRNA to confirm that the RAS-induced phospho-signal and kinase activity attributed to ERK1 are lost.

citations.title: Activation and function of the MAPKs and their substrates, the MAPK-activated protein kinases.
Activation of extracellular signal‐regulated kinase, ERK2, by p21ras oncoprotein.

novelty.note: I searched for the Ras→Raf→MEK→ERK1 activation-loop mechanism in plain words, for the entities together (oncogenic Ras, MEK, ERK1 Thr202/TEY phosphorylation), and for the specific prediction (activated V12/oncogenic Ras sufficient to activate ERK without growth factor; PD98059/MEK inhibition abolishing it). The retrieved review (Cargnello & Roux) explicitly states that Raf-activated MEK1/2 phosphorylate ERK1/2 on the conserved TEY activation-loop motif downstream of Ras, and the retrieved primary paper (Leevers & Marshall) reports that oncogenic p21ras alone, without growth factor, activates the 42/44 kDa ERKs via threonine and tyrosine phosphorylation. This is the canonical, long-published cascade rather than a new explanation, so the status is established; nothing found reports a negative test of it.

hypotheses.statement: mTORC1 activity negatively regulates RAF (Raf-1) activation, so that mTORC1 inhibition relieves a Ras-dependent restraint on Raf-1 and increases its activating phosphorylation and downstream MEK/ERK output.
hypotheses.mechanism: In MCF7 cells, rapamycin-mediated mTORC1 inhibition induced Raf1 Ser338 phosphorylation and ERK activation, and dominant-negative Ras (N17) blocked this, placing Raf-1 downstream of an mTORC1-restrained, Ras-dependent input. Independently, Raf-1 activity depends on plasma-membrane localisation and engagement with activated Ras, and is tuned by feedback phosphorylation. ERK1/2 in turn positively drives mTORC1 via Raptor phosphorylation, which would close a loop in which mTORC1 limits Raf-1 activation.
hypotheses.prediction: Acute mTORC1 inhibition (rapamycin or Raptor knockdown) should increase Raf-1 Ser338 phosphorylation, Raf-1 association with Ras-GTP, and Raf-1 kinase activity toward MEK. These increases should be abolished by dominant-negative Ras and should not occur with a Raf-1 mutant that cannot bind Ras.
hypotheses.test: In MCF7 or HEK293 cells, treat with rapamycin or deplete Raptor by siRNA. Measure Raf-1 Ser338 phosphorylation and phospho-MEK by immunoblot, Ras-GTP pull-down, and Raf-1 co-immunoprecipitation with Ras. Immunoprecipitate Raf-1 and run an in vitro kinase assay using recombinant inactive MEK as substrate. Compare cells co-expressing Ras N17, and compare wild-type Raf-1 with a Ras-binding-deficient Raf-1 mutant.

citations.title: Inhibition of mTORC1 leads to MAPK pathway activation through a PI3K-dependent feedback loop in human cancer
mTORC1 inhibition increases neurotensin secretion and gene expression through activation of the MEK/ERK/c-Jun pathway in the human endocrine cell line BON
Different Patterns of Akt and ERK Feedback Activation in Response to Rapamycin, Active-Site mTOR Inhibitors and Metformin in Pancreatic Cancer Cells

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the mechanism in words (mTORC1 inhibition relieving a restraint on Raf-1), the entities together (rapamycin + Raf-1 Ser338 + RasN17 + MEK/ERK), and the prediction (raptor/mTOR knockdown raising Raf-1/MEK/ERK output, Ras-GTP–Raf binding). The explanation is already published as the S6K–PI3K–Ras feedback loop: Carracedo et al. (JCI 2008) report that rapamycin induces Raf-1 Ser338 phosphorylation and ERK activation, that dominant-negative Ras N17 blocks it, and that MEK inhibition abolishes it, and Li et al. (Am J Physiol Cell Physiol 2011) independently report Raf-1/MEK1/2/ERK1/2 phosphorylation after mTORC1 inhibition by rapamycin, torin1 or mTOR/RAPTOR/S6K1 knockdown. No source directly refutes the claim, though Soares et al. (PLoS ONE 2013; now carrying an Expression of Concern) found rapamycin did not raise ERK phosphorylation in pancreatic cancer cells while active-site mTOR inhibitors did, indicating context dependence rather than refutation.

hypotheses.statement: TAK1 positively regulates EGF-stimulated cell growth (proliferation) by acting upstream of EGF-induced ERK activation.
hypotheses.mechanism: TAK1 knockdown in HME cells impaired EGF-stimulated ERK phosphorylation, which places TAK1 upstream of ERK in EGFR signalling (de2015). Transient ERK activation by EGF is associated with proliferation rather than differentiation (borisov2009), and ERK activity in full growth medium sustains the growth-associated factor Fra-1 (albeck2013). Taken together, loss of TAK1 should reduce the ERK signal that couples EGF to proliferation. The inference is indirect: the ERK-proliferation link comes from PC12 and MCF-10A cells, not from the HME cells in which TAK1 was tested.
hypotheses.prediction: In EGF-dependent epithelial cells, TAK1 depletion or inhibition should lower EGF-induced ERK phosphorylation and Fra-1 accumulation. It should also reduce EGF-stimulated proliferation. Re-expressing shRNA-resistant TAK1, or expressing constitutively active MEK, should restore proliferation.
hypotheses.test: Knock down TAK1 by shRNA in HME or MCF-10A cells, with scrambled shRNA as control. Serum-starve the cells, then stimulate with EGF. Measure pERK and Fra-1 by immunoblot or immunofluorescence, and measure proliferation by EdU incorporation and cell counts over 48–72 h. Include an shRNA-resistant TAK1 rescue and a constitutively active MEK rescue to test whether any growth defect is ERK-dependent.

citations.title: TAK1-mediated serine/threonine phosphorylation of epidermal growth factor receptor via p38/extracellular signal-regulated kinase: NF-{kappa}B-independent survival pathways in tumor necrosis factor alpha signaling.
TAK1 Phosphorylates RASSF9 and Inhibits Esophageal Squamous Tumor Cell Proliferation by Targeting the RAS/MEK/ERK Axis.

novelty.note: I searched for TAK1 as an upstream regulator of EGF-induced ERK, for TAK1 knockdown effects on EGFR-driven proliferation/Fra-1, and for TAK1/MAP3K7 in mammary and other epithelial cells (Google/PubMed/Europe PMC full-text queries). The only direct tests of the core step report the opposite: in HeLa cells TAK1 shRNA left EGF-induced MAPK/ERK activation and EGFR Ser/Thr/Tyr phosphorylation intact ("TAK1 was dispensable in ligand-induced MAPK activation"), TAK1 being required only for TNF-α-induced ERK, and in esophageal squamous cells TAK1 knockdown raised p-MEK/p-ERK and enhanced proliferation while TAK1 overexpression suppressed both, placing TAK1 as a negative regulator of RAS/MEK/ERK. No source states TAK1 as a positive upstream driver of EGF-stimulated ERK-dependent proliferation, and the ERK-dependent-growth rescue prediction is untested, so the specific mechanistic premise stands directly contradicted in the cell systems where it has been examined.

hypotheses.statement: SYK positively regulates mTORC1 kinase activity, through SYK-dependent ERK activation leading to ERK/RSK-mediated Raptor phosphorylation, in cells that engage SYK-coupled receptor signalling.
hypotheses.mechanism: Curdlan stimulation of BMDCs induces rapid, Syk-dependent phosphorylation of Erk (leibundgutlandmann2007:findings:001). Independently, in HEK293 cells, MEK/ERK-dependent phosphorylation of Raptor is required for full stimulus-induced mTORC1 kinase activity toward 4E-BP1: MEK inhibition abolishes both PMA-induced Raptor phosphorylation and mTORC1 activity, and phosphorylation-deficient Raptor mutants reduce it (carriere2010:findings:015, carrire2008:findings:001, carrire2008:findings:010). Together these imply that SYK-driven ERK activation should raise mTORC1 activity via Raptor phosphorylation, so SYK acts as an upstream positive regulator of mTORC1.
hypotheses.prediction: After SYK-coupled receptor stimulation (e.g., curdlan), Raptor RXRXXpS/T phosphorylation, 4E-BP1 Thr37/46 phosphorylation and in vitro mTORC1 activity toward GST-4E-BP1 should rise. Loss or inhibition of SYK should blunt this rise. MEK inhibition or the Raptor 3A/S3A mutant should phenocopy SYK loss, and SYK loss should add no further reduction in cells already expressing the Raptor mutant.
hypotheses.test: Use a SYK-expressing myeloid cell line stimulated with curdlan. Compare control cells with cells given siRNA knockdown or pharmacological inhibition of SYK, with U0126 and wild-type versus 3A Raptor as comparators. Measure p-ERK, Raptor phosphorylation (immunoprecipitation plus phospho-motif immunoblot), p-4E-BP1 Thr37/46 and p-S6 by immunoblot. Also run an in vitro mTOR kinase assay on Raptor immunoprecipitates with GST-4E-BP1 and [γ-32P]ATP. Include rapamycin-treated controls, because mTORC1 inhibition itself raises ERK phosphorylation (carracedo2008:findings:004); this checks the direction of the SYK–ERK–mTORC1 link.

citations.title: Syk-dependent mTOR activation in follicular lymphoma cells.
SYK regulates mTOR signaling in AML.
mTOR- and HIF-1α-mediated aerobic glycolysis as metabolic basis for trained immunity.

novelty.note: I searched for SYK as an upstream activator of mTORC1, for Dectin-1/curdlan-driven mTOR signalling in myeloid cells, and for any link between SYK, ERK/RSK and Raptor phosphorylation (PubMed/Europe PMC, PMC full texts, publisher pages). The positive-regulator half is already published: Leseux et al. show Syk-dependent mTOR activation (p70S6K/4E-BP1) in B-lymphoma cells but explicitly via PLD/PI3K-independent routes with no ERK/Raptor mechanism, and Carnevale et al. show SYK inhibition/knockdown suppresses mTOR, RPS6 and (variably) 4E-BP1 in myeloid AML cells, with MEK/ERK falling only in RAS-wild-type lines; β-glucan/Dectin-1 engagement is likewise reported to activate mTOR, but through Akt-HIF-1α. Nothing found states or tests the specific proposed connection — SYK-driven ERK/RSK-mediated Raptor RXRXXpS/T phosphorylation as the route to mTORC1 kinase activity after curdlan stimulation — so this is partial rather than established or refuted.

hypotheses.statement: mTORC1 activity acts as a negative upstream regulator of CD274 (PD-L1) expression in tumour cells, such that loss of amino-acid-driven mTORC1 signalling induces PD-L1.
hypotheses.mechanism: Blocking glutamine uptake (LAT2 inhibition/V-9302) upregulates PD-L1 via NF-κB in mouse lung cancer and CRC cells (de2024:findings:039), and amino acid availability is transduced principally through Rag-GTPase-dependent lysosomal recruitment and activation of mTORC1 (balla2013:findings:096). If the amino-acid signal that suppresses PD-L1 runs through mTORC1, then cells whose mTORC1 is constitutively lysosomal and completely insensitive to amino acid deprivation because of GATOR1 (DEPDC5/NPRL2/NPRL3) deletion (barpeled2013:findings:010) should fail to induce PD-L1 when amino acid supply is restricted.
hypotheses.prediction: Amino acid/glutamine restriction and direct mTORC1 inhibition (rapamycin/Torin1) will each raise surface PD-L1 in mTORC1-competent tumour lines, whereas GATOR1-deleted lines will show no PD-L1 induction on amino acid withdrawal or V-9302 but will regain it after re-introduction of DEPDC5/NPRL2; conversely rapamycin should still induce PD-L1 in those lines.
hypotheses.test: In paired cancer cell lines (GATOR1-null versus DEPDC5/NPRL2-reconstituted, plus a wild-type line), withdraw amino acids/glutamine or add V-9302 with or without rapamycin/Torin1 and Raptor knockdown, then quantify surface and total PD-L1 by flow cytometry and immunoblot alongside p-S6K1/p-4E-BP1 as the mTORC1 readout; concordance of PD-L1 induction with loss of mTORC1 output, and its abolition where mTORC1 cannot be switched off, would establish or exclude the direct regulatory link, with NF-κB inhibition used to test whether the effect is routed through the reported NF-κB arm.

citations.title: Inhibition of mTOR complex 1/p70 S6 kinase signaling elevates PD-L1 levels in human cancer cells through enhancing protein stabilization accompanied with enhanced β-TrCP degradation.
Searching for the real function of mTOR signaling in the regulation of PD-L1 expression.
Immunosuppression Induced by Glutamine Deprivation Occurs via Activating PD-L1 Transcription in Bladder Cancer.

novelty.note: I searched for mTOR/mTORC1 control of PD-L1 in either direction, for glutamine/amino-acid deprivation raising PD-L1 (V-9302, NF-κB), and for any GATOR1/DEPDC5/NPRL2 link to PD-L1. The general mechanism is already published: mTORC1/p70S6K signalling is reported as a negative regulator of PD-L1, with rapamycin/TORKinibs and raptor knockdown elevating PD-L1 via β-TrCP-dependent stabilization (PMID 31316145), and a review argues this negative-regulation direction is the real one while noting contradictory reports that mTOR activation drives PD-L1 (PMID 32854033). However, I found no source that routes amino-acid/glutamine restriction-induced PD-L1 through loss of mTORC1 output, nor any test in GATOR1-deleted lines: the glutamine-deprivation papers attribute PD-L1 induction to EGFR/MEK/ERK/c-Jun or Ca²⁺/NF-κB without testing mTOR (PMID 34805266), and other work reports an Asn-mTORC1 axis upregulating PD-L1, so the specific connection and prediction remain untested rather than refuted.

hypotheses.statement: SRC directly promotes cap-dependent mRNA translation by activating RSK, which phosphorylates ribosomal protein S6 at Ser235/236.
hypotheses.mechanism: Src activity is required for RSK phosphorylation downstream of EGFR Y845, since the Src inhibitors PP2 and dasatinib abolish rapamycin-induced Erk1/2 and RSK phosphorylation (chaturvedi2009:findings:013), and Src activation directly drives RSK2 tyrosine phosphorylation that stabilizes ERK1/2 binding and activates RSK2 (cargnello2011:findings:059). Independently, active RSK1/2 phosphorylate rpS6 specifically at Ser235/236, which facilitates translation preinitiation complex assembly and increases cap-dependent translation (cargnello2011:findings:034). Therefore Src should act as an upstream positive regulator of cap-dependent translation through this RSK–rpS6 step, independent of mTOR/S6K.
hypotheses.prediction: Src inhibition or knockdown should lower rpS6 Ser235/236 phosphorylation and reduce cap-dependent translation and global protein synthesis rates, while leaving other rpS6 sites (S6K-specific) relatively spared; conversely, expressing activated Src should raise Ser235/236 phosphorylation and cap-dependent translation, and this gain should be abolished by RSK inhibition.
hypotheses.test: In cultured cells, treat with PP2 (versus inactive PP3) or dasatinib, or knock down Src by RNAi, and measure (i) phospho-rpS6 Ser235/236 versus Ser240/244 by immunoblot, (ii) nascent protein synthesis by puromycin-incorporation (SUnSET) immunoblot or O-propargyl-puromycin labeling, and (iii) a bicistronic cap-dependent versus IRES luciferase reporter; then repeat in cells expressing constitutively active Src with and without an RSK inhibitor to test whether the Src effect on translation requires RSK.

citations.title: RAS/ERK signaling promotes site-specific ribosomal protein S6 phosphorylation via RSK and stimulates cap-dependent translation.
Epidermal growth factor stimulates RSK2 activation through activation of the MEK/ERK pathway and src-dependent tyrosine phosphorylation of RSK2 at Tyr-529.
SRC inhibition enables formation of a growth suppressive MAGI1-PP2A complex in isocitrate dehydrogenase-mutant cholangiocarcinoma.
Src Family Kinase Inhibitors Block Translation of Alphavirus Subgenomic mRNAs.

novelty.note: I searched for the composite chain (Src → RSK → rpS6 Ser235/236 → cap-dependent translation), for the individual links (RSK site-specific rpS6 phosphorylation; Src/SFK-dependent RSK2 activation), and for the prediction (Src inhibitor/dasatinib effects on rpS6 Ser235/236, puromycin incorporation, cap-dependent reporters). Both halves are separately published — Roux et al. show RSK alone phosphorylates rpS6 at Ser235/236 mTOR-independently and stimulates cap-dependent translation, and Kang et al. show Src/Fyn phosphorylate RSK2 at Tyr-529 to permit ERK binding and RSK2 activation — but I found no source that joins them into Src as an upstream driver of rpS6 Ser235/236 and cap-dependent translation, nor any site-selectivity test of Src inhibition. The nearest whole-pathway work reports SRC inhibition lowering S6 phosphorylation and de novo protein synthesis but attributes it to p70 S6K rather than RSK, and an SFK-inhibitor translation study confines the translational block to viral subgenomic mRNA; no retrieved source directly tested and negated the specific claim, so this is partial rather than established or refuted.

hypotheses.statement: SYK acts upstream of RAS, promoting RAS activation (GDP-RAS to GTP-RAS conversion) that mediates SYK-dependent ERK phosphorylation after Dectin-1 stimulation.
hypotheses.mechanism: Curdlan-induced Erk phosphorylation in dendritic cells requires Syk (leibundgutlandmann2007:findings:001). Independently, ERK1/2 activation-loop phosphorylation occurs through MEK1/2 downstream of Ras-mediated Raf activation (cargnello2011:findings:002), and upstream regulators of Ras-driven ERK activation have been placed by measuring GTP-Ras directly (agazie2003:findings:004). Together these suggest SYK-dependent ERK activation may pass through RAS activation, making SYK an upstream positive regulator of RAS in this setting.
hypotheses.prediction: Curdlan-stimulated GTP-RAS levels should rise in SYK-competent myeloid cells and be markedly reduced when SYK is inhibited or depleted. Constitutively active V12-RAS should restore ERK phosphorylation in SYK-inhibited cells, placing SYK upstream of RAS rather than parallel to it.
hypotheses.test: In a cultured Dectin-1-expressing myeloid cell line, treat cells with a SYK inhibitor or SYK siRNA versus control and stimulate with curdlan. Measure GTP-RAS by GST-Raf-RBD affinity precipitation and immunoblot, and measure phospho-ERK1/2 by immunoblot. In parallel, express V12-H-RAS in SYK-inhibited cells to test whether it rescues ERK phosphorylation.

citations.title: CARD9 mediates Dectin-1-induced ERK activation by linking Ras-GRF1 to H-Ras for antifungal immunity.

novelty.note: I searched for the Dectin-1/curdlan–Syk–Ras–ERK chain in plain words, for the entities together (Syk, Ras-GTP, ERK, myeloid cells), and for the specific prediction (Raf-RBD pull-down of GTP-Ras under Syk inhibition). The JEM 2014 study (retrieved via PMC4203953) states exactly this explanation: Dectin-1 engagement triggers Syk-dependent Ras-GRF1 phosphorylation, which with CARD9 recruits and loads H-Ras with GTP (shown by Raf-RBD pull-down) to drive ERK activation, and Syk inhibition with piceatannol blocks the Ras-GRF1 phosphorylation/complex formation and ERK activation. Because a published source places SYK upstream of RAS activation as the route to Dectin-1–induced ERK phosphorylation, the status is established; only the V12-Ras rescue arm of the proposed test appears not to have been performed in that work.

hypotheses.statement: RAF1 (CRAF) activates MAPK (p42/44 ERK1/2) downstream of PKC activation, so PKC-driven MAPK activation and phosphorylation of MAPK substrates depend on RAF1.
hypotheses.mechanism: The simulated PKC–MAPK network couples PKC to MAPK through a PKC→Raf step, and sustained EGF input keeps both PKC and MAPK active. Separately, in cultured vascular smooth muscle cells, PKC activation phosphorylates an actin-tethered ERK1/2 pool, and C-raf activation is specifically required upstream. In HEK293 cells, inhibiting c-Raf with GW-5074 abolished MEK and ERK activity. In cultured smooth muscle cells, p42/44 MAPK phosphorylates caldesmon at Ser789. Together these imply that RAF1 is the kinase linking PKC input to MAPK activation and to MAPK substrate phosphorylation.
hypotheses.prediction: In cultured vascular smooth muscle cells, phorbol-ester (PKC) stimulation will increase phospho-p42/44 MAPK and caldesmon Ser789 phosphorylation. RAF1 knockdown or GW-5074 treatment will largely abolish both increases, while total MAPK and caldesmon levels stay unchanged.
hypotheses.test: Treat cultured vascular smooth muscle cells with RAF1 siRNA (versus non-targeting control) or GW-5074 (versus vehicle), then stimulate with a phorbol ester. Immunoblot for phospho-ERK1/2, total ERK1/2, phospho-caldesmon Ser789 and total caldesmon. Include a rescue with siRNA-resistant RAF1 to confirm specificity.

citations.title: Hierarchical scaffolding of an ERK1/2 activation pathway.
Erk1/2 MAPK and caldesmon differentially regulate podosome dynamics in A7r5 vascular smooth muscle cells.
Raf-1 kinase regulates smooth muscle contraction in the rat mesenteric arteries.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the PKC→Raf-1→MEK/ERK→caldesmon Ser789 chain in vascular smooth muscle; the entities together (phorbol ester, Raf-1/GW-5074, ERK, VSMC); and the prediction that Raf-1 loss abolishes PKC-driven ERK and substrate phosphorylation. The RAF1/C-Raf requirement for PKC-driven ERK1/2 activation in vascular smooth muscle cells is already published (C-Raf knockdown reduces phorbol-ester activation of the cytoskeletal ERK1/2 pool, with C-Raf placed upstream of an IQGAP1/B-Raf module), and ERK-dependent caldesmon phosphorylation downstream of PKC is published separately — but no retrieved source links RAF1 loss to caldesmon Ser789 phosphorylation, so the specific prediction is unpublished. One direct test cuts the other way without refuting the whole claim: in rat mesenteric artery smooth muscle the Raf-1 inhibitor GW-5074 inhibited MEK but not PDBu-induced ERK phosphorylation, so pharmacological Raf-1 inhibition alone did not abolish PKC-driven ERK activity there; hence partial rather than established or refuted.

hypotheses.statement: RAF1 (CRAF) is required for the MAPK activation caused by rapamycin, which relieves an S6K1–PI3K feedback loop.
hypotheses.mechanism: Rapamycin activates MAPK through an S6K1–IRS-1/PI3K feedback loop that normally restrains MAPK, and rapamycin cooperates with insulin or IGF-1 to superactivate MAPK. On the RAF1 side, CRAF knockdown did not change baseline ERK signaling but removed the residual ERK signal that reappears when the pathway is pharmacologically perturbed. CRAF is also specifically required for drug-induced MEK/ERK activation. This suggests that feedback-driven MAPK reactivation, such as the rapamycin response, runs through RAF1.
hypotheses.prediction: In MCF7 cells, RAF1 knockdown or c-Raf inhibition will leave basal phospho-ERK largely unchanged. It will, however, strongly reduce the rapamycin-induced and the rapamycin-plus-insulin-induced increase in phospho-ERK, while rapamycin still suppresses phospho-RpS6.
hypotheses.test: Transfect MCF7 cells with RAF1 siRNA or control siRNA (or pretreat with GW-5074 or vehicle). Treat with rapamycin alone or with insulin or IGF-1. Immunoblot for phospho-ERK1/2, total ERK1/2, phospho-AKT and phospho-RpS6, and quantify the fold change in phospho-ERK induced by rapamycin in each condition.

citations.title: Inhibition of mTORC1 leads to MAPK pathway activation through a PI3K-dependent feedback loop in human cancer.
SHOC2 mediates the drug-resistance of triple-negative breast cancer cells to everolimus.

The PP242 mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) inhibitor activates extracellular signal-regulated kinase (ERK) in multiple myeloma cells via a target of rapamycin complex 1 (TORC1)/eukaryotic translation initiation factor 4E (eIF-4E)/RAF pathway and activation is a mechanism of resistance.

novelty.note: I searched for the rapamycin/mTORC1–S6K1–PI3K feedback to MAPK, for mTOR-inhibitor-induced ERK activation with c-Raf/RAF1 requirement (knockdown, GW-5074, Ser338/Ser289 sites), and for the MCF7 insulin/IGF-1 superactivation prediction. The corpus source itself (retrieved full text) already places rapamycin-induced ERK activation on a Ras–Raf1–MEK axis in MCF7 (rapamycin induced Ser338-Raf1 phosphorylation; dominant-negative Ras N17 and U0126 blocked the response), and other work shows mTOR-inhibitor feedback ERK activation proceeds through c-Raf (increased SHOC2–c-Raf binding after everolimus; stimulated RAF kinase activity with loss of Ser-289/296/301 inhibitory phosphorylation after PP242). No retrieved source performs the specific loss-of-function test — RAF1 knockdown or c-Raf inhibition showing unchanged basal pERK but abolished rapamycin- and rapamycin-plus-insulin-induced pERK — so the mechanism is published in general but this specific prediction is not, and nothing reports a negative test.

hypotheses.statement: Rapamycin inhibits GSK3β kinase activity in cells, as a consequence of the AKT reactivation that follows rapamycin treatment.
hypotheses.mechanism: In PC3 cells and in CLL-like cells, rapamycin raises AKT Ser473 phosphorylation, which is attributed to loss of the S6K negative feedback (dan2008:findings:013, cosimo2018:findings:004). Separately, activated AKT inhibits GSK3 (hogan2003:findings:006), and AKT-mediated inhibition of GSK3β prevents GSK3β-driven phosphorylation and degradation of its substrates (haeusler2018:findings:007). Together these imply rapamycin should lower phosphorylation of GSK3β-dependent sites such as Smad3 Thr66, a GSK3β site whose phosphorylation controls Smad3 turnover (guo2008:findings:018, guo2008:findings:013).
hypotheses.prediction: Rapamycin-treated cells should show lower Smad3 Thr66 phosphorylation, slower Smad3 turnover in a cycloheximide chase, and higher PHLPP protein levels than vehicle-treated cells. These effects should be abolished by co-treatment with a PI3K or AKT inhibitor, and should be absent in GSK3β-knockdown cells, where the GSK3β-dependent signal is already lost.
hypotheses.test: Treat HaCaT or HepG2 cells with rapamycin, with or without LY294002 or an AKT inhibitor, and with or without GSK3β shRNA. Immunoblot for pAKT S473, Smad3 pThr66, total Smad3 and PHLPP. Run a cycloheximide chase for Smad3 half-life, using SB-216763 as a positive control for GSK3β inhibition.

citations.title: S6K1 regulates GSK3 under conditions of mTOR-dependent feedback inhibition of Akt.
Convergence of the mammalian target of rapamycin complex 1- and glycogen synthase kinase 3-β-signaling pathways regulates the innate inflammatory response.
GSK3 is required for rapalogs to induce degradation of some oncogenic proteins and to suppress cancer cell growth.

novelty.note: I searched for rapamycin's effect on GSK3β Ser9 phosphorylation and kinase activity under Akt feedback reactivation, for rapamycin plus GSK3-dependent substrate degradation, and for rapamycin with Smad3/Thr66. Multiple studies directly test the rapamycin→GSK3 link and report the opposite sign: Zhang et al. show S6K1, not just Akt, phosphorylates GSK3 S9/S21 and that acute rapamycin strongly activates GSK3 (minor effect in wild-type, strong activation in Tsc2−/− cells) even as Akt is restored; Wang et al. show rapamycin attenuates GSK3β S9 phosphorylation and increases glycogen synthase S641 phosphorylation (higher GSK3 activity) via loss of p85S6K; Koo et al. report that rapamycin raises Akt S473 in every line tested yet leaves GSK3 S21/9 phosphorylation largely unchanged, and that active GSK3 is required for rapalog-induced substrate degradation. Since the central premise — that rapamycin-induced AKT reactivation inhibits GSK3β in cells — has been directly assayed and found not to hold, the dependent predictions about reduced Smad3 Thr66 phosphorylation and stabilised GSK3β substrates fail with it.

hypotheses.statement: RAF (c-Raf) activity positively regulates mTOR (mTORC1) kinase activity under Ras/MAPK pathway stimulation, via MEK/ERK-dependent phosphorylation of Raptor.
hypotheses.mechanism: In HEK293 cells, Ras/MAPK-induced Raptor phosphorylation at Ser696/Ser863 was fully abolished by the MEK1/2 inhibitor PD184352 but not by mTOR inhibitors (carriere2010:findings:011). MEK1/2 inhibitors also completely inhibited mTORC1 kinase activity, and the phosphorylation-deficient Raptor S3A mutant reduced mTOR kinase activity toward 4E-BP1 (carriere2010:findings:015). Separately, in the same cell type, c-Raf inhibition with GW-5074 eliminated MEK and ERK activity (borisov2009:findings:013), and ERK1/2 activation depends on MEK acting downstream of Raf activation (cargnello2011:findings:002). Together these place RAF upstream of the MEK/ERK input that the first paper shows is required for Ras/MAPK-stimulated mTORC1 activity.
hypotheses.prediction: In PMA- or EGF-stimulated HEK293 cells, c-Raf inhibition or knockdown should abolish Raptor Ser696/Ser863 phosphorylation. It should also reduce mTOR kinase activity toward GST-4E-BP1 in Raptor immunoprecipitates and lower in-cell 4E-BP1 Thr37/Thr46 phosphorylation. Cells expressing Raptor S3A should show little further reduction on RAF inhibition, and constitutively active c-Raf should raise wild-type Raptor-associated mTOR activity but not S3A-associated activity.
hypotheses.test: Stimulate HEK293 cells coexpressing mTOR with wild-type or S3A Raptor using PMA, with and without GW-5074 or c-Raf siRNA, and in a parallel arm express constitutively active c-Raf. Measure Raptor pSer696/pSer863 by immunoprecipitation and immunoblot. Measure mTORC1 activity by in vitro kinase assay of Raptor immunoprecipitates on GST-4E-BP1 with [γ-32P]ATP, and by immunoblot of 4E-BP1 pThr37/Thr46. Include phospho-MEK/ERK readouts to confirm pathway inhibition.

citations.title: ERK1/2 phosphorylate Raptor to promote Ras-dependent activation of mTOR complex 1 (mTORC1).
RSK regulates activated BRAF signalling to mTORC1 and promotes melanoma growth.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the plain-language mechanism (Raf/MEK/ERK-dependent Raptor phosphorylation driving mTORC1), the entities together (c-Raf/BRAF + Raptor Ser696/Ser863 + 4E-BP1 + GW-5074/PLX4720), and the prediction (Raf inhibition abolishing Raptor phosphorylation and Raptor-associated mTOR kinase activity), plus explicit searches for negative results (MEK/ERK inhibition not affecting mTORC1, Raptor site function disputed). The ERK-to-Raptor limb (ERK1/2 directly phosphorylating Ser8/Ser696/Ser863 to stimulate mTORC1 and 4E-BP1 signalling) is published, and oncogenic RAF-to-mTORC1 signalling in HEK293 cells expressing Raf(V600E) is published as ERK/RSK-dependent but without Raptor site measurements; no source I retrieved places c-Raf upstream of the Ser696/Ser863 phosphorylation or tests Raf loss against Raptor-associated mTOR kinase activity, and none reports a negative test. Hence the mechanism is established in general terms while this specific Raf-dependence prediction and the S3A epistasis remain unpublished.

hypotheses.statement: SYK is a direct proximal transducer of LPS signalling, binding phosphotyrosines generated on the LPS receptor complex (TLR4 TIR and/or associated ITAM adaptors) and amplifying LPS-induced NF-κB-dependent cytokine production.
hypotheses.mechanism: LPS signalling requires tyrosine phosphorylation of the TLR4 TIR domain (Y674/Y680) and recruits the SRC-family kinase LYN to TLR4, and SRC-family inhibition blocks LPS-induced NF-κB activation, so LPS generates SRC-family-dependent phosphotyrosine motifs at the receptor. SYK is activated precisely by binding doubly phosphorylated tyrosine motifs through its tandem SH2 domains, which are structurally flexible enough to accommodate a broad range of tyrosine spacing, and SYK-dependent signals must be integrated with TLR/MyD88 input for full TNF output. Together these imply SYK can dock on the LPS-engaged, tyrosine-phosphorylated receptor complex and feed into the ERK/NF-κB cytokine programme it drives downstream of other receptors.
hypotheses.prediction: LPS stimulation should induce SYK activation loop/linker tyrosine phosphorylation and inducible co-precipitation of SYK with TLR4 (lost with SRC-family inhibition or TLR4 Y674/Y680 mutation), and SYK loss or inhibition should reduce LPS-induced NF-κB activation and TNF/IL-6 production without abolishing it.
hypotheses.test: In macrophages (and TLR4/MD-2-expressing epithelial lines), stimulate with LPS and (i) co-immunoprecipitate SYK with TLR4 and blot SYK phosphotyrosine over a time course, with and without a SRC-family inhibitor; (ii) test direct engagement by pulling down recombinant SYK tandem-SH2 domains with synthetic TLR4 TIR peptides phosphorylated at Y674/Y680 versus unphosphorylated controls; (iii) knock out or knock down SYK, or reconstitute SH2-binding-deficient SYK, and measure LPS-induced IκB degradation, NF-κB reporter activity and TNF/IL-6 ELISA.

citations.title: Tyrosine kinase Syk associates with toll-like receptor 4 and regulates signaling in human monocytic cells.
Syk-MyD88 Axis Is a Critical Determinant of Inflammatory-Response in Activated Macrophages.
TLR4 phosphorylation at tyrosine 672 activates the ERK/c-FOS signaling module for LPS-induced cytokine responses in macrophages.
SCIMP is a transmembrane non-TIR TLR adaptor that promotes proinflammatory cytokine production from macrophages.

novelty.note: I searched for SYK–TLR4 association and LPS-induced tyrosine phosphorylation, for SYK-deficient macrophage LPS cytokine/NF-κB phenotypes, and for the SCIMP/Lyn–SYK–TLR4 axis and SYK SH2 docking on ITAM-like adaptor phosphotyrosines. The core explanation is already published: SYK associates with TLR4 and modulates LPS responses in monocytes, SYK is recruited to TLR4 via Lyn-phosphorylated SCIMP and is the most proximal kinase for LPS-induced TLR4 tyrosine phosphorylation and cytokine output, and SYK is engaged by the phosphorylated hemi-ITAM tyrosine (Y58) of MyD88 through its tandem SH2 domains to drive LPS-induced NF-κB activation and TNF/IL-6. Hence established; the one arm not directly supported is SYK SH2 docking onto phosphorylated TLR4 TIR Y674/Y680 itself (published work places SYK upstream of, not downstream of, TLR4 tyrosine phosphorylation, and some reports find enhanced rather than reduced proinflammatory cytokines in SYK-deficient macrophages).

hypotheses.statement: RPS6KB1 (S6K1) negatively regulates MEK activation through a PI3K-dependent feedback, so that loss of S6K1 activity increases MEK phosphorylation.
hypotheses.mechanism: Constitutively active, rapamycin-insensitive S6K1 reduced rapamycin-induced ERK activation, and PI3K inhibitors (LY294002, wortmannin) also reduced it. This defines an S6K1–PI3K feedback loop that negatively regulates MAPK (carracedo2008:005, :006). Rapamycin-mediated S6K inhibition also raised Akt S473 phosphorylation, consistent with S6K feedback on IRS-1/PI3K (dan2008:013). Separately, PI3K inhibition prevented insulin from enhancing MEK phosphorylation and disrupted insulin-plus-EGF amplification of Ras-GTP/MEK/ERK (borisov2009:009). This places the PI3K-dependent input at or above MEK, implying that S6K1's suppression of ERK acts on MEK activation.
hypotheses.prediction: S6K1 knockdown or rapamycin treatment should increase phospho-MEK (not only phospho-ERK) after insulin or IGF-1 stimulation. Expressing rapamycin-resistant, constitutively active S6K1 should blunt that increase, and PI3K inhibition should abolish it.
hypotheses.test: In MCF7 or HEK293 cells, compare control and S6K1 siRNA knockdown, and rapamycin treatment with and without expression of rapamycin-resistant active S6K1 (E389 D3A/E). Test each condition with and without LY294002, followed by insulin or IGF-1 stimulation. Measure phospho-MEK1/2 (Ser217/221), phospho-ERK, phospho-S6 and phospho-Akt S473 by immunoblot.

citations.title: Different patterns of Akt and ERK feedback activation in response to rapamycin, active-site mTOR inhibitors and metformin in pancreatic cancer cells.
Dual PI3K/mTOR Inhibitors Induce Rapid Overactivation of the MEK/ERK Pathway in Human Pancreatic Cancer Cells through Suppression of mTORC2.
Suppression of feedback loops mediated by PI3K/mTOR induces multiple overactivation of compensatory pathways: an unintended consequence leading to drug resistance.
Regulation of skeletal muscle insulin-stimulated signaling through the MEK-REDD1-mTOR axis.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the mechanism in words (S6K1/mTORC1 negative feedback onto MEK/ERK via PI3K), the entities together (rapamycin + phospho-MEK Ser217/221 + S6K1 knockdown + LY294002/wortmannin), and the prediction (does mTOR/S6K inhibition raise insulin-stimulated p-MEK). The phospho-MEK half of the prediction is published: mTOR inhibitors raise MEK activation-loop (Ser217/221) phosphorylation, and in vivo rapamycin improved insulin-stimulated MEK1/2 phosphorylation in mouse muscle (PMID 27913296, 25323681). However, Soares et al. directly tested this specific claim in insulin- and neurotensin-stimulated pancreatic cancer cells: rapamycin fully suppressed the S6K/S6 axis yet 'did not have any stimulatory effect on ERK activation', and the MEK/ERK hyperactivation seen with active-site mTOR inhibitors persisted under PI3K inhibition, which the authors attribute to a PI3K/S6K-independent loop (PMID 23437362); a follow-up assigns the MEK/ERK feedback to mTORC2 rather than S6K1–PI3K, with MEK/ERK rising even while PI3K is inhibited (PMID 25673820). These stated negatives on both the S6K1 dependence and the PI3K dependence make the verdict refuted, even though the p-MEK phenomenon itself is real in other settings.

hypotheses.statement: MEK1 kinase activity positively regulates (activates) RPS6KB1/S6K1 by promoting its mTORC1-dependent phosphorylation during Ras/MAPK pathway stimulation.
hypotheses.mechanism: MEK1/2 inhibitors abolish Raptor phosphorylation at Ser696/Ser863 after Ras/MAPK activation. They also completely inhibit mTORC1 kinase activity toward 4E-BP1, and a Raptor S3A mutant lowers PMA-stimulated mTORC1 activity. Separately, S6K1 is recruited by Raptor, and its phosphorylation is mTORC1-dependent and tracks Raptor Ser863 phosphorylation kinetics. Together, MEK1 output should therefore feed into S6K1 activation through the same mTORC1 step shown for 4E-BP1.
hypotheses.prediction: PMA-stimulated S6K1 phosphorylation (T389) and S6K1 activity toward S6 Ser240/244 or Rictor T1135 should be reduced by MEK1 knockdown or MEK1/2 inhibitors. Constitutively active MEK1 should raise S6K1 T389 phosphorylation in serum-starved cells, and this effect should be blunted by Raptor S3A or rapamycin.
hypotheses.test: In serum-starved HEK293 cells stimulated with PMA, compare three conditions: MEK1 siRNA or PD184352/U0126, expression of constitutively active MEK1, and co-expression of wild-type versus S3A Raptor. Readouts are immunoblotting for phospho-S6K1 (T389), phospho-S6 (Ser240/244) and phospho-Rictor (T1135), plus an in vitro kinase assay of immunoprecipitated S6K1.

citations.title: Pharmacological and genetic evaluation of proposed roles of mitogen-activated protein kinase/extracellular signal-regulated kinase kinase (MEK), extracellular signal-regulated kinase (ERK), and p90(RSK) in the control of mTORC1 protein signaling by phorbol esters.
c-Raf/MEK/ERK pathway controls protein kinase C-mediated p70S6K activation in adult cardiac muscle cells.
ERK1/2 phosphorylate Raptor to promote Ras-dependent activation of mTOR complex 1 (mTORC1).

novelty.note: I searched for MEK/ERK control of S6K1 Thr389 after phorbol ester stimulation, for the MEK–raptor–mTORC1 mechanism (Ser8/Ser696/Ser863), and for negative tests of MEK inhibition on mTORC1 readouts, using PubMed/Europe PMC records and abstracts. The explanation is already published: Fonseca et al. (2011) directly tested MEK dependence of PMA-stimulated mTORC1 signaling with PD184352 and report that in HEK293E cells S6K1 phosphorylation was completely MEK-dependent (while noting marked cell-type diversity and MEK/ERK-independent routes in other lines), and Iijima et al. (2002) showed the c-Raf/MEK/ERK pathway mediates phorbol-ester-stimulated S6K1 Thr-389 phosphorylation in an mTOR-dependent (rapamycin-sensitive) manner. Carriere et al. (2011) supplies the nearest statement of the specific raptor-phosphorylation step invoked here, so the claim is established in substance, though the S6K1-specific dependence on raptor Ser8/696/863 (S3A) was not found stated.

hypotheses.statement: RPS6KB1/S6K1 negatively regulates MEK1 activation through an IRS-1/PI3K-dependent feedback loop.
hypotheses.mechanism: Rapamycin-mediated mTORC1 inhibition activates ERK through a Ras-Raf1-MEK1/2 route that U0126 abrogates. A rapamycin-insensitive constitutively active S6K1 reduces this ERK activation, and PI3K inhibition also blunts it. S6K1 is independently described as feeding back to block IRS-1 and so restrain growth-factor-induced PI3K signalling. Together, this implies that S6K1 activity suppresses signalling upstream of MEK1.
hypotheses.prediction: S6K1 knockdown should increase MEK1 activating phosphorylation (Ser217/221) and MEK1 kinase activity toward ERK after insulin or IGF-1 stimulation. Constitutively active rapamycin-resistant S6K1 should prevent rapamycin-induced MEK1 phosphorylation. Both effects should be attenuated by PI3K inhibition.
hypotheses.test: In MCF7 or HEK293 cells stimulated with insulin, with or without rapamycin, perform S6K1 siRNA or express constitutively active, rapamycin-resistant S6K1 (with or without LY294002). Readouts are immunoblotting for phospho-MEK1 (Ser217/221) and an in vitro kinase assay of immunoprecipitated MEK1 using recombinant kinase-dead ERK2 as substrate.

citations.title: Inhibition of mTORC1 leads to MAPK pathway activation through a PI3K-dependent feedback loop in human cancer.
Inhibition of the mechanistic target of rapamycin induces cell survival via MAPK in tuberous sclerosis complex.
Different patterns of Akt and ERK feedback activation in response to rapamycin, active-site mTOR inhibitors and metformin in pancreatic cancer cells.

novelty.note: I searched for the plain-language mechanism (S6K1/IRS-1 feedback restraining MEK/ERK), the entities together (S6K1 + MEK1 + feedback; rapamycin + ERK activation + IRS-1) and the prediction (S6K1 knockdown or rapamycin raising phospho-MEK1/2 Ser217/221, PI3K dependence) via Europe PMC and web search, and retrieved the primary papers. Carracedo et al. (JCI 2008) already state exactly this explanation — mTORC1 inhibition relieves an S6K1-PI3K(IRS-1)-dependent feedback loop that negatively regulates the Ras-Raf1-MEK1/2-ERK pathway, with rapamycin-resistant active S6K1 and LY294002 both blunting ERK activation — so the explanation is published rather than new; the only untested element is the MEK1-level readout (phospho-Ser217/221 and immunoprecipitated MEK1 kinase activity) and S6K1 siRNA. A TSC study confirms mTORC1 inhibition drives MEK1-dependent MAPK activation without testing S6K1/IRS-1/PI3K, while Soares et al. report that in pancreatic cancer cells rapamycin gave no ERK stimulation and dual PI3K/mTOR-driven MEK/ERK overactivation was PI3K-independent and mTORC2-mediated, indicating context dependence but not a direct negative test of the S6K1-to-MEK1 claim.

hypotheses.statement: Insulin potentiates EGF-induced activation of ERK2, through a Gab1–SHP2-dependent route, even though insulin alone is a poor activator of ERK2.
hypotheses.mechanism: In HEK293 cells, insulin alone weakly activates ERK1/2 but enhances ERK activation by low EGF doses. This amplification is lost when PI3K is inhibited, and the crosstalk is placed upstream of Ras and at the Ras/Raf level (borisov2009). Independently, EGF-induced ERK2 activation depends largely on SHP2 recruitment to Gab1/Gab2 (meng2005), and Gab1–SHP2 association drives ERK2 activation (heinrich2003). Together these suggest that insulin's input converges on the Gab1–SHP2 node that controls ERK2 activation, raising ERK2 activity in response to EGF.
hypotheses.prediction: In cells co-stimulated with insulin and a low EGF dose, immunoprecipitated ERK2 kinase activity should exceed the sum of either stimulus alone. This synergy should be largely abolished by the SHP2-binding-defective Gab1FF mutant or by wortmannin, while ERK2 activation by EGF alone is only partly reduced.
hypotheses.test: Transfect HEK293 or T47D cells with HA-ERK2 plus empty vector or Gab1FF. Serum-starve the cells and pretreat with or without wortmannin. Then stimulate with vehicle, insulin alone (100 nM), low EGF alone (about 0.1 nM), or both. Measure HA-ERK2 activity by immunocomplex kinase assay with MBP as substrate, and blot for phospho-Gab1 and Gab1-associated SHP2.

citations.title: Systems-level interactions between insulin-EGF networks amplify mitogenic signaling.
Participation of both Gab1 and Gab2 in the activation of the ERK/MAPK pathway by epidermal growth factor.

novelty.note: I searched for insulin potentiation of EGF-induced ERK via Gab1–SHP2, for insulin–EGF crosstalk with wortmannin/PI3K in HEK293, and for direct tests of Gab1–SHP2 dependence of the synergy. The Borisov et al. study whose page I retrieved does state the mechanism in part (insulin-driven PIP3 increases membrane recruitment of Grb2–SOS and SHP2 by GAB1/IRS, and wortmannin abolishes the amplification), but it also directly tested the Gab1 dependence of the synergy and reports the opposite of the prediction: with GAB1 depletion the EGF+insulin phospho-ERK peak 'decreases only slightly' whereas EGF-alone ERK activation drops markedly, i.e. insulin 'endows the mitogenic EGFR pathway with increased robustness towards GAB1 downregulation', and simulated disruption of GAB1–SHP2 interactions shortens EGF-induced ERK signalling while the insulin-plus-EGF synergy is retained. Meng et al. independently establish only the EGF-alone arm (Gab1FF/Gab2F block EGF-induced ERK2), with no insulin co-stimulation, so the specific Gab1–SHP2-dependent synergy claim stands tested and negative.

hypotheses.statement: mTOR kinase activity directly inhibits FOXO1 by driving its phosphorylation (T24/S256) and cytoplasmic sequestration, so that mTOR catalytic inhibition restores nuclear FOXO1 and its transcriptional output.
hypotheses.mechanism: Claims from separate papers state that mTORC2 kinase activity is required for phosphorylation of FOXO1/3a at the AKT sites while other AKT substrates (TSC2, GSK3b) are unaffected, and that the ATP-competitive mTOR inhibitor AZD8055 — but not rapamycin — reduces pFOXO1-T24, shifts FOXO1 from cytoplasm to nucleus, and raises FOXO1 DNA-binding with corresponding target-gene changes (CCND2, BCL2L1 down; BCL2L11 up). Since phosphorylation at these residues creates 14-3-3 motifs that export FOXO1 and attenuate its program, mTOR catalytic output is positioned as the upstream requirement for FOXO1 inactivation rather than a parallel input. The corpus also links this axis functionally, with FOXO1 protein high yet target genes deregulated as if FOXO1 were inactive in cells with active mTOR signalling.
hypotheses.prediction: Loss of mTOR catalytic function (kinase-dead mTOR, mTOR or RICTOR knockdown, or ATP-competitive inhibition) should reduce pFOXO1-T24/S256, decrease FOXO1/14-3-3 association, increase the nuclear FOXO1 fraction, and increase FOXO1 DNA-binding and derepression of FOXO1 targets (CDKN1A/CDKN1B up, CCND2 and BCL2L1 down), whereas rapamycin at doses that block S6 phosphorylation should leave pFOXO1 and FOXO1 localisation largely unchanged; the effect should persist under conditions where GSK3 phosphorylation is unaffected.
hypotheses.test: In a cultured cell line, compare siRNA knockdown of MTOR and of RICTOR (with non-targeting control) and rescue with kinase-dead mTOR, against matched treatment with an ATP-competitive mTOR inhibitor versus rapamycin, then read out by immunoblot pFOXO1-T24/S256 and pGSK3 (specificity control), by subcellular fractionation and immunofluorescence the nuclear/cytoplasmic FOXO1 ratio, by FOXO1 co-immunoprecipitation the amount of bound 14-3-3, and by ELISA-based DNA-binding assay plus qPCR of CDKN1A, CDKN1B, CCND2, BCL2L1 and BCL2L11 the transcriptional consequence; a FOXO1 T24A/S256A mutant should be refractory to all mTOR manipulations, which would rule out indirect routes.

citations.title: mTORC2 Is the Major Second Layer Kinase Negatively Regulating FOXO3 Activity.
SIN1/MIP1 maintains rictor-mTOR complex integrity and regulates Akt phosphorylation and substrate specificity.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the mechanism in plain words (ATP-competitive mTOR kinase inhibition reducing FOXO1 T24/S256 phosphorylation and restoring nuclear FOXO1 where rapamycin does not), the entities together (mTORC2/RICTOR + FoxO1/3a Thr24/Ser256 + 14-3-3 + AKT substrate selectivity vs TSC2/GSK3), and the prediction (mTOR/RICTOR loss increasing nuclear FOXO1 and FOXO target-gene output such as CDKN1A/B, CCND2, BCL2L1, BCL2L11). A retrieved primary study (Molecules 2022, PMID 36080182) reports that inhibitors of mTOR kinase activity, but not rapamycin up to 100 nM, potently reduce FOXO S253/AKT-S473 phosphorylation and drive nuclear translocation of FOXO3 and also FOXO1/FOXO4, concluding mTORC2 is the major kinase layer negatively regulating FOXO activity; Jacinto et al. (PMID 16962653) independently show that loss of the mTORC2 subunit SIN1 abolishes AKT-S473 and selectively impairs FoxO1/3a phosphorylation while TSC2 and GSK3 are unaffected. Because published work states this same explanation (mTOR catalytic output as the upstream requirement for FOXO1 phospho-inactivation and cytoplasmic sequestration, rapamycin-insensitive), the status is established; no source was found that tested and negated it, though the 14-3-3 co-immunoprecipitation and full target-gene panel remain less directly documented outside the corpus papers.

hypotheses.statement: MEK activates MTORC1 by driving ERK-dependent phosphorylation of Raptor at Ser696 and Ser863, which increases MTORC1 kinase activity toward 4E-BP1.
hypotheses.mechanism: Two independent studies found that MEK inhibition (U0126) abolished PMA- or EGF-stimulated Raptor phosphorylation at Ser696/Ser863 but not at Ras/MAPK-independent sites (carriere2010:findings:010, foster2009:findings:007). In the MTORC1 evidence, a phosphorylation-deficient Raptor S3A mutant reduced MTORC1 kinase activity toward 4E-BP1 without affecting complex assembly or substrate binding, and MEK1/2 inhibitors fully blocked MTORC1 kinase activity (carriere2010:findings:015, carriere2010:findings:014). Together these place MEK upstream of MTORC1 catalytic activity through Raptor phosphorylation, not through complex assembly.
hypotheses.prediction: Acute MEK inhibition should lower Raptor Ser696/Ser863 phosphorylation and MTORC1 kinase activity toward 4E-BP1 in growth-factor- or PMA-stimulated cells. Constitutively active MEK1 should raise both. Neither effect should occur in cells expressing phospho-deficient Raptor (S696A/S863A), and MTORC1 composition (mTOR, S6K1 and 4E-BP1 co-precipitation) should not change.
hypotheses.test: In HEK293 cells expressing wild-type or S696A/S863A myc-Raptor, compare three conditions: PMA/EGF stimulation with or without U0126/PD0325901, and transfection with constitutively active MEK1. Readouts are phospho-Raptor (Ser696, Ser863) immunoblots, an in vitro kinase assay of Raptor-immunoprecipitated MTORC1 on GST-4E-BP1, cellular 4E-BP1 Thr37/46 phosphorylation, and co-immunoprecipitation to confirm unchanged complex assembly.

citations.title: ERK1/2 phosphorylate Raptor to promote Ras-dependent activation of mTOR complex 1 (mTORC1).
Regulation of mTOR complex 1 (mTORC1) by raptor Ser863 and multisite phosphorylation.

novelty.note: I searched for the mechanism in plain words (MEK/ERK phosphorylating Raptor to activate mTORC1), the entities together (Raptor Ser696/Ser863, U0126, 4E-BP1 kinase activity), and the prediction (MEK inhibition lowering mTORC1 catalytic activity without altering complex assembly), then retrieved the full texts. The Carriere et al. JBC paper states exactly this explanation: ERK1/2 downstream of MEK1/2 phosphorylate Raptor at Ser8/Ser696/Ser863, U0126 and PD184352 block it, the phospho-deficient S3A mutant lowers mTORC1 kinase activity toward 4E-BP1 in vitro and in vivo, and S3A Raptor still binds mTOR normally so assembly is unaffected; Foster et al. independently report EGF/PMA-driven, U0126-sensitive Ser863 phosphorylation with reduced 4E-BP1 phosphorylation by phospho-defective raptor. Searches for contradictory work turned up only ERK-independent mTORC1 inputs in other contexts (mitosis, mechanical stimulation, TSC2), not a negative test of this claim, so the status is established rather than partial or refuted.

hypotheses.statement: MEK1 kinase activity is required for sustained PKC activation after EGF stimulation, acting through MEK1-dependent ERK activation that feeds back onto PKC.
hypotheses.mechanism: MEK1/2 phosphorylate ERK1/2 on the TEY activation-loop motif downstream of Raf (cargnello2011:findings:002), and MEK1 is the top-ranked kinase for the ERK activation sites (johnson2023:findings:009). In the PKC-MAPK loop model, sufficient EGF drives MAPK and PKC activity that persists after the signal is withdrawn (bhalla1999:findings:001). That persistence rests on a bistable MAPK-to-PKC feedback (bhalla1999:findings:002), and blocking the feedback returns PKC activity to baseline (bhalla1999:findings:006). Removing MEK1 output should therefore cut the MAPK arm and collapse sustained PKC activity.
hypotheses.prediction: In EGF-stimulated cells, MEK1/2 inhibition should leave the initial PKC response largely intact but abolish PKC activity that persists after EGF washout. Cells should then return to basal PKC activity rather than holding the high steady state.
hypotheses.test: Express the CKAR2 PKC FRET reporter in cultured cells and stimulate with 5 nM EGF for 100 min, then wash out. Compare PKC reporter activity over time after washout with and without PD184352 or U0126, confirmed with MEK1 siRNA knockdown and p-ERK immunoblots. Loss of persistent PKC activity specifically in the MEK-inhibited or MEK1-depleted cells would support the hypothesis.

citations.title: A positive feedback signal transduction loop determines timing of cerebellar long-term depression.
Down-regulation of Cdx2 in colorectal carcinoma cells by the Raf-MEK-ERK 1/2 pathway.
MAP kinase phosphatase as a locus of flexibility in a mitogen-activated protein kinase signaling network.

novelty.note: I searched for the ERK→PKC feedback arm in plain terms (ERK/MEK-dependent sustained PKC), for the entity combination (MEK inhibitor + sustained PKC + EGF/CKAR live-cell reporters), and for experimental tests of the Bhalla–Iyengar bistable PKC–MAPK loop. Tanaka & Augustine directly demonstrate the prediction's shape in Purkinje neurons: U0126 blocked the persistent phase of PKC activation while leaving the initial stimulus-evoked PKC response unaffected, in an explicitly reciprocal PKC–MAPK positive feedback loop; the Cdx2 paper independently shows MEK/ERK-dependent phosphorylation of PKC isoforms at activation sites. However, no retrieved source tests this for EGF-stimulated cultured cells with EGF washout, and the experimental test of the bistable growth-factor network (Bhalla, Ram & Iyengar) probed the PKC→MAPK direction and MAPK phosphatase rather than MEK dependence of persistent PKC, so the specific EGF prediction remains unaddressed.

hypotheses.statement: PKC activates MEK1 by acting upstream of Raf in the Ras-Raf-MEK-ERK cascade.
hypotheses.mechanism: The PKC-MAPK network model includes a PKC-to-Raf input, and PKC and MAPK activity mutually sustain each other (bhalla1999:findings:001, bhalla1999:findings:002). Independent evidence places MEK1/2 directly downstream of Raf activation (cargnello2011:findings:002), with ERK activation running through a Ras-Raf1-MEK1/2 route (carracedo2008:findings:004). PKC-driven Raf activation should therefore increase MEK1 activation-state phosphorylation and MEK1 kinase activity toward ERK.
hypotheses.prediction: Activating PKC should raise MEK1 activation and its phosphorylation of ERK Thr202/Tyr204. Pharmacological PKC inhibition or PKC knockdown should reduce MEK1 activation and ERK phosphorylation in EGF-stimulated cells.
hypotheses.test: Treat cultured cells with a PKC activator, or stimulate with EGF with or without a PKC inhibitor or PKC isoform siRNA. Immunoprecipitate MEK1 and measure its kinase activity in vitro against recombinant kinase-dead ERK2, alongside immunoblots for phospho-MEK1 and phospho-Raf1. As a specificity control, co-express dominant-negative Raf to test whether the PKC effect on MEK1 requires Raf.

citations.title: Protein kinase C alpha activates RAF-1 by direct phosphorylation.
Activation of the mitogen-activated protein kinase/extracellular signal-regulated kinase pathway by conventional, novel, and atypical protein kinase C isotypes.

novelty.note: I searched for PKC phosphorylating or activating Raf-1, for PKC isotypes activating MEK/ERK, and for Raf-dependent versus Raf-independent PKC signalling to MEK. Kolch et al. (1993) showed that PKCα directly phosphorylates and activates Raf-1. Schönwasser et al. (1998) showed that constitutively active PKC isotypes activate MEK-1 and p42 MAPK, with conventional and novel PKCs acting through c-Raf1. The core claim, that PKC activates MEK1 upstream of Raf, is therefore already published. One caveat: atypical PKC-ζ activates MEK without Raf, and neither paper, as far as their abstracts show, specifically tests PKC inhibition in EGF-stimulated cells.

hypotheses.statement: SRC acts as a direct upstream tyrosine kinase for LAT, phosphorylating LAT tyrosine motifs to generate SH2-docking sites.
hypotheses.mechanism: LAT signalling depends on phosphorylation of its cytoplasmic tyrosine motifs, which create SH2-domain docking sites and license assembly of GRB2/SOS1-containing clusters (good2011:findings:006; case2019a:findings:006). Independently, SRC-family kinase activity is reported to phosphorylate the cytoplasmic tyrosines of an unrelated membrane scaffold to create SH2-binding pYDXV motifs (case2019a:findings:011), and LAT resides in the same detergent-resistant membrane fraction that concentrates SRC-family kinases after receptor activation (sezgin2017:findings:015), placing an active SRC-type kinase in the same membrane compartment as an available tyrosine-motif substrate.
hypotheses.prediction: Purified active SRC should phosphorylate recombinant LAT cytoplasmic domain on multiple tyrosines in vitro, and the resulting pLAT should acquire GRB2 binding; increasing SRC activity in cells should raise LAT pTyr stoichiometry and LAT-GRB2 association, while SRC inhibition or knockdown should lower basal/induced LAT pTyr independently of ZAP-70.
hypotheses.test: Run an in vitro kinase reaction with recombinant purified SRC (and a kinase-dead SRC control) plus purified LAT cytoplasmic domain on liposomes, and read out LAT tyrosine phosphorylation by anti-pTyr immunoblot and site assignment by MS; couple this to a cell-based arm in a LAT-expressing cell line where SRC is knocked down or inhibited and LAT pTyr plus LAT-GRB2 co-immunoprecipitation are quantified, using a LAT tyrosine-to-phenylalanine mutant to confirm site specificity.

citations.title: An electrostatic selection mechanism controls sequential kinase signaling downstream of the T cell receptor.
Lck promotes Zap70-dependent LAT phosphorylation by bridging Zap70 to LAT.

novelty.note: I searched for Src-family kinase phosphorylation of LAT, for Lck/Fyn vs ZAP-70/Syk substrate assignment, and for the prediction that SFK activity would raise LAT pTyr and LAT-GRB2 association independently of ZAP-70. Two retrieved primary papers report direct negative tests of exactly this claim: Shah et al. measured Lck and ZAP-70 specificity on TCRζ/LAT/SLP-76 phosphosites and found 'ZAP-70 efficiently phosphorylates LAT and SLP-76, but not TCRζ ITAMs, while Lck is an efficient kinase for ITAMs, but not for LAT or SLP-76', attributing the exclusion to Lck's intolerance of the aspartate at the -1 position of LAT sites; Lo et al. state 'Lck cannot phosphorylate the substrates of Zap70, namely the adaptors LAT and SLP76' and show catalytically dead Lck (K273R) still enhances Zap70-mediated LAT phosphorylation, i.e. the SFK contribution to LAT pTyr is an SH2/SH3 bridging function rather than direct catalysis. Because the specific kinase-substrate relationship and its ZAP-70-independent prediction were tested and came out negative, this is refuted rather than merely unsupported.

hypotheses.statement: SYK is directly recruited to and required for signalling by ligand-engaged TLR4, joining the LPS-activated TLR4 complex and contributing to its NF-κB/cytokine output.
hypotheses.mechanism: LPS stimulation recruits the Src-family kinase LYN into a complex with TLR4 (de2015:findings:010), and SYK in myeloid cells is activated by association with receptor-proximal complexes whose ITAM adaptors (DAP12/FcRγ) are phosphorylated by Src-family kinases (mcsai2010:findings:016). Independently, SYK deficiency abolishes the collaborative TNF response that requires integration of the SYK arm with the TLR/MyD88 arm, leaving TNF at the level of TLR ligation alone (dennehy2008:findings:004), implying SYK acts at or on the TLR module itself rather than only in a parallel pathway.
hypotheses.prediction: After LPS treatment of macrophages, SYK should co-immunoprecipitate with TLR4 (in a LYN-dependent, LPS-inducible manner), and SYK loss or catalytic inhibition should reduce LPS-induced IKK/IκB phosphorylation and TNF secretion without changing surface TLR4 levels.
hypotheses.test: In a macrophage cell line, immunoprecipitate TLR4 at 0/5/15/30 min after LPS and blot for SYK and LYN (reciprocal SYK IP blotted for TLR4 as control); then compare LPS-induced phospho-IKK/phospho-IκB and TNF ELISA in cells treated with a SYK inhibitor or SYK siRNA versus control, with surface TLR4 quantified by flow cytometry to exclude receptor loss.

citations.title: Tyrosine kinase Syk associates with toll-like receptor 4 and regulates signaling in human monocytic cells.
The SYK side of TLR4: signalling mechanisms in response to LPS and minimally oxidized LDL.
Syk-MyD88 Axis Is a Critical Determinant of Inflammatory-Response in Activated Macrophages.
The tyrosine kinase Syk differentially regulates Toll-like receptor signaling downstream of the adaptor molecules TRAF6 and TRAF3.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: SYK–TLR4 co-immunoprecipitation in LPS-stimulated macrophages/monocytes, SYK requirement for LPS-induced NF-κB/IKK and TNF output, and Src-family (LYN)/ITAM-adaptor coupling of SYK to TLR4. The explanation is already published: Chaudhary et al. report that SYK associates with TLR4 in monocytic cells, that TLR4 is inducibly tyrosine-phosphorylated on LPS engagement with SYK in the same MyD88/IRAK-1-containing complex, and Miller et al. review this as constitutive SYK binding to the TLR4 cytoplasmic domain that increases with LPS-driven TLR4 dimerisation/phosphorylation; the Syk–MyD88 paper further reports that LPS-induced NF-κB activation is abolished in Syk-deficient macrophages, i.e. the functional requirement is also stated. Status is established rather than open/partial, but the specific cytokine prediction is contested: Chaudhary et al. found SYK inhibition had no effect on LPS-induced TNF, IL-6 or IL-1β release, and Lin et al. found Syk-deficient macrophages show enhanced TAK1 activation and increased proinflammatory cytokines (with reduced type I IFN), the opposite direction to the prediction.
