hypotheses.statement: EGFR activity positively regulates RSK activation, so the magnitude and duration of EGFR signaling, including the RasGAP-binding site pY992, set the extent and duration of RSK hydrophobic-motif (Ser380) phosphorylation.
hypotheses.mechanism: EGFR drives ERK1/2 activation: an ERK-output reporter decays when EGFR is inhibited, and Y992F-EGFR, which cannot bind the RasGAP SH2 domain, gives higher and more prolonged ERK1/2 activation than WT-EGFR. Independently, RSK activation requires ordered ERK1/2-mediated phosphorylation, and growth-factor-induced RSK Ser380 phosphorylation is mediated by ERK. Together these imply that EGFR-derived ERK1/2 activity determines RSK activation state, with pY992 acting as a negative modulator of that signal. This link is inferred through ERK1/2 and is not a demonstrated physical EGFR-RSK interaction.
hypotheses.prediction: EGF stimulation should increase RSK Ser380 and Thr573 phosphorylation, and EGFR kinase inhibition should abolish this. Cells expressing Y992F-EGFR should show higher and longer-lasting RSK Ser380/Thr573 phosphorylation than cells expressing WT-EGFR. MEK/ERK inhibition should block the EGF-induced RSK phosphorylation.
hypotheses.test: Transfect NIH 3T3 cells with WT-EGFR or Y992F-EGFR and serum-starve them. Stimulate with EGF with or without an EGFR kinase inhibitor or a MEK inhibitor. Run a time course (0-120 min) of immunoblots for phospho-RSK Ser380 and Thr573, total RSK, and phospho-ERK1/2. Compare the amplitude and duration of RSK phosphorylation across constructs and inhibitor conditions.

citations.title: Epidermal growth factor (EGF) regulates α5β1 integrin activation state in human cancer cell lines through the p90RSK-dependent phosphorylation of filamin A.
Phosphoproteomics-based modeling defines the regulatory mechanism underlying aberrant EGFR signaling.
Phosphorylation of p90 ribosomal S6 kinase (RSK) regulates extracellular signal-regulated kinase docking and RSK activity.

novelty.note: Searched three ways: the EGF→EGFR→MEK/ERK→RSK Ser380 cascade in plain words, EGFR Y992/RasGAP-site mutants and ERK activation duration, and the joint prediction (Y992F plus RSK Ser380/Thr573 time course). The generic arm is clearly established — EGF induces p90RSK Ser380 phosphorylation within minutes in A431 cells, the EGFR inhibitor AG1478 blocks the downstream output and the MEK inhibitor PD184352 completely blocks EGF-induced p90RSK phosphorylation (PMID 23007402) — and Y992F-EGFR is independently reported to convert transient ERK1 activation into sustained activation (PMID 21085658), but that phosphoproteomic study stops at ERK1 and presents no RSK data. No retrieved source states or tests the specific connection that the pY992/RasGAP site sets the amplitude and duration of RSK hydrophobic-motif phosphorylation, and nothing reports a negative test of it, so the mechanism is published in general while this particular prediction is not.

hypotheses.statement: NGF activates MEK1 in PC12 cells, and MEK1 is required for the sustained ERK1/2 activation that NGF produces.
hypotheses.mechanism: MEK1 is the kinase that phosphorylates ERK1/2 on their activation-loop TEY motif (Thr202/Thr203), a site nearly every other profiled human kinase selects against, so ERK1/2 activation-loop phosphorylation should report MEK1 activity. NGF produces sustained ERK activation in PC12 cells lasting hours, whereas EGF produces only transient activation. Because MEK1 is the kinase specific to that ERK site, NGF's sustained ERK phosphorylation implies that NGF drives sustained MEK1 activity, which in turn phosphorylates ERK.
hypotheses.prediction: In PC12 cells, NGF should produce MEK1 activation that persists for hours and tracks the sustained phospho-ERK1/2 time course, while EGF gives only transient MEK1 activation. Blocking MEK1 should abolish both the early and the sustained NGF-induced ERK1/2 phosphorylation.
hypotheses.test: Stimulate serum-starved PC12 cells with NGF (50 ng/ml) or EGF (25 ng/ml) over a 0–5 h time course. Immunoprecipitate MEK1 and measure its kinase activity toward recombinant inactive ERK2 in vitro, and immunoblot lysates for phospho-ERK1/2 (Thr202/Tyr204). In parallel, pretreat cells with U0126 or PD184352, or deplete MEK1 by siRNA, and test whether NGF-induced sustained phospho-ERK1/2 and neurite outgrowth are lost.

citations.title: Sustained activation of the mitogen-activated protein (MAP) kinase cascade may be required for differentiation of PC12 cells. Comparison of the effects of nerve growth factor and epidermal growth factor.
Activation of MAP kinase kinase is necessary and sufficient for PC12 differentiation and for transformation of NIH 3T3 cells.
LAMTOR2-mediated modulation of NGF/MAPK activation kinetics during differentiation of PC12 cells.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the mechanism in words (NGF sustained MEK activation underlying sustained ERK in PC12), the entities together (MEK1 immunoprecipitation kinase-activity time course NGF vs EGF PC12), and the prediction (MEK1 blockade/knockdown abolishing NGF-induced sustained phospho-ERK and neurite outgrowth). Traverse et al. 1992 directly measured immunoprecipitated MAPKK (MEK) activity toward inactive MAP kinase in serum-starved PC12 cells and reported NGF gives >20-fold activation sustained for at least 90 min while EGF peaks at 2 min and returns to baseline by 60–90 min, concluding explicitly that the differing MEK activation kinetics underlie the transient versus sustained MAP kinase activation; Cowley et al. 1994 showed interfering MEK1 mutants block growth-factor-induced PC12 differentiation while activated MEK1 is sufficient, and the LAMTOR2 study confirms MEK inhibition blocks NGF-driven ERK-dependent differentiation. Both the claim and its central prediction are therefore already stated in the literature, so the status is established rather than partial.

hypotheses.statement: SRC kinase activity positively regulates endocytosis, promoting the internalization and endosomal processing of membrane-associated cargo such as EGFR.
hypotheses.mechanism: In contractile vascular smooth muscle cells, zyxin and VASP undergo Src-dependent endosomal processing (brozovich2016:findings:084), which places SRC upstream of cargo entry into endosomes. Separately, SRC-family inhibition with PP2 greatly diminishes EGF-induced EGFR phosphorylation (de2015:findings:008). Clathrin-mediated EGFR internalization depends on phosphorylation of EGFR and of Rab5 effectors (cuadrado2010:findings:054). Together these claims suggest that loss of SRC activity should reduce phosphorylation-dependent entry of EGFR and other cargo into the endocytic pathway.
hypotheses.prediction: Depleting or inhibiting SRC should reduce the rate and extent of ligand-induced EGFR internalization and reduce endosomal accumulation of internalized cargo. Restoring wild-type SRC, but not a kinase-dead SRC, should rescue internalization.
hypotheses.test: In HEK293 or A549 cells, knock down SRC by siRNA or treat with a SRC-family inhibitor such as PP2. Measure internalization of fluorescent EGF, or surface-biotinylated EGFR, over a time course by flow cytometry or a surface-biotinylation internalization assay, with confocal colocalization against an early-endosome marker. Include a rescue with siRNA-resistant wild-type versus kinase-dead SRC, and use fluid-phase dextran uptake as a control for general endocytic capacity.

citations.title: EGF receptor signaling stimulates SRC kinase phosphorylation of clathrin, influencing clathrin redistribution and EGF uptake.
Epidermal growth factor receptor translocation to the mitochondria: regulation and effect.
Effect of tyrosine kinase inhibitors on clathrin-coated pit recruitment and internalization of epidermal growth factor receptor.

novelty.note: I searched for the mechanism in plain words (Src kinase promoting clathrin-mediated EGFR internalization), the entities together (Src + clathrin heavy chain phosphorylation + EGF uptake), and the prediction (PP2/SU6656 or Src siRNA effects on EGFR internalization with kinase-dead rescue). Wilde et al. (Cell 1999) states exactly this explanation: EGFR-activated SRC phosphorylates clathrin heavy chain, and in SRC-deficient cells or cells treated with a SRC-family inhibitor clathrin redistribution fails and EGF endocytosis is delayed; Demory et al. (JBC 2009) similarly report that c-Src catalytic activity (PP2-sensitive, reduced by kinase-defective c-Src) and clathrin-mediated endocytosis are required for EGF-stimulated EGFR trafficking. Status is established rather than refuted, although Sorkina et al. (JBC 2002) is a partly discordant direct test in which the selective SFK inhibitor SU6656 did not affect EGFR internalization and PP2's moderate inhibition persisted in SFK-null cells, arguing the pharmacological effect is off-target; this qualifies the magnitude of the SRC requirement rather than the existence of the published explanation.

hypotheses.statement: The GRB2 SH2 domain directly binds one or more autophosphorylated tyrosines on activated SYK, recruiting GRB2 to SYK.
hypotheses.mechanism: GRB2 consists of a single SH2 domain flanked by two SH3 domains. It was cloned by its binding to a tyrosine-autophosphorylated receptor tail, and it docks on newly phosphorylated tyrosines of signaling proteins such as Spry1/2 and phospho-LAT. SYK carries ten autophosphorylation tyrosines, several of which (Tyr342, Tyr346, Tyr624) are phosphorylated after receptor stimulation and serve as docking sites for the SH2 domains of VAV1, PLCγ1 and SLP65. Activated SYK therefore presents several phosphotyrosine SH2-docking sites of the kind GRB2's SH2 domain engages. This inference is general: none of the cited claims shows that GRB2's SH2 domain recognizes any specific SYK site, so the hypothesis is speculative.
hypotheses.prediction: GRB2 should co-precipitate with SYK only when SYK is tyrosine-phosphorylated (activated or autophosphorylated). The binding should be lost with an SH2-inactivating GRB2 mutation, or with tyrosine-to-phenylalanine mutation of the responsible SYK autophosphorylation site(s).
hypotheses.test: Express wild-type or kinase-dead SYK in HEK293 cells, or autophosphorylate purified SYK in vitro. Pull down with GST-GRB2-SH2 (wild-type versus an SH2 phosphotyrosine-binding-dead mutant) and immunoblot for SYK. In parallel, screen biotinylated phospho- versus non-phospho-peptides covering each SYK autophosphorylation tyrosine for GRB2-SH2 binding (peptide pulldown or fluorescence polarization), then confirm hits by Y→F mutation in co-immunoprecipitation.

citations.title: Differential effect of the inhibition of Grb2-SH3 interactions in platelet activation induced by thrombin and by Fc receptor engagement.
Once phosphorylated, tyrosines in carboxyl terminus of protein-tyrosine kinase Syk interact with signaling proteins, including TULA-2, a negative regulator of mast cell degranulation.

novelty.note: I searched for GRB2 SH2 binding to SYK phosphotyrosines, phospho-dependent SYK–GRB2 co-precipitation, and SYK autophosphorylation-site (Y342/Y346/Y624) docking partners, plus GRB2 pYXN specificity screens. Published work shows an activation-dependent association of a GST-Grb2-SH2 construct with Syk in thrombin-stimulated platelets (alongside β3 integrin, Shc, Src, SHP1), but does not demonstrate directness or map a SYK autophosphorylation site; separately, a phosphopeptide study of the SYK C-terminal tail tyrosines precipitated Grb2 from mast cell lysates yet far-Western showed direct binding only for Nck-1 and SHIP-1, so Grb2's recovery there was attributed to indirect complex formation. Thus the general mechanism and a phospho-dependent SYK–GRB2-SH2 association are published, but the specific direct-docking claim and site assignment are not established (and the one site directly probed gave no direct Grb2 binding), giving partial rather than established or refuted.

hypotheses.statement: IL-17 directly activates JNK1 through the IL-17RA–ACT1–TRAF6 module, and this IL-17-driven JNK1 activity phosphorylates NFATc1-a/b to drive its nuclear exit and repress NFAT-dependent IL-4 promoter activity.
hypotheses.mechanism: Claims about IL-17 state that ACT1 recruits and ubiquitinates TRAF6 to trigger canonical MAPK activation including JNK, that CARD14/Bcl10/MALT1 is required for IL-17A-induced JNK1/2 signaling in keratinocytes, and that A20 feedback specifically dampens IL-17-induced JNK. Independently, claims about JNK1 establish that JNK1 binds and phosphorylates NFATc1-a/NFATc1-b at Ser117/Ser172, reduces calcineurin binding, blocks calcineurin-stimulated nuclear accumulation, and thereby inhibits IL-4 reporter expression. If IL-17 is an upstream activator of the same JNK1 pool, its receptor-proximal signaling should be transmitted onto the NFATc1 substrate and produce the JNK1-characteristic loss of nuclear NFATc1 and IL-4 promoter output.
hypotheses.prediction: IL-17A stimulation of IL-17RA/ACT1-competent cells expressing NFATc1-a should increase JNK1 activity and Ser117/Ser172 phosphorylation of NFATc1-a, shift NFATc1-a from nucleus to cytoplasm after calcium/calcineurin stimulation, and reduce IL-4 reporter activity; all of these effects should be abolished by ACT1 or TRAF6 knockdown, by JNK1 knockdown or dominant-negative JNK1, and by the non-phosphorylatable [Ala117 Ala172] NFATc1-a mutant, which should remain constitutively nuclear and IL-17-insensitive.
hypotheses.test: In an IL-17-responsive cell line co-transfected with NFATc1-a (wild type or [Ala117 Ala172]) and an IL-4 luciferase reporter, stimulate with PMA/ionomycin ± IL-17A and measure (i) in vitro/immunoprecipitation JNK1 kinase activity, (ii) phospho-Ser117/Ser172 NFATc1-a by immunoblot, (iii) nuclear versus cytoplasmic NFATc1-a by cell fractionation and immunofluorescence, and (iv) reporter activity; repeat under siRNA knockdown of ACT1, TRAF6, or JNK1 and with dominant-negative JNK1 to establish whether the IL-17 effect requires the receptor-proximal module and JNK1 itself, with loss of the effect on the [Ala117 Ala172] mutant serving as the decisive substrate-level control.

citations.title: c-Jun NH(2)-terminal kinase inhibits targeting of the protein phosphatase calcineurin to NFATc1.
IL-17 Signaling: The Yin and the Yang.
Differential expression of interleukin-17A and -17F is coupled to T cell receptor signaling via inducible T cell kinase.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the mechanism in words (IL-17 Act1/TRAF6 activating JNK feeding onto NFATc1 nuclear exit), the entities together (IL-17 + NFATc1 + JNK1 + Act1; IL-17 + NFATc1 + nuclear export + IL-4, via Europe PMC full-text queries), and the prediction (IL-17A suppressing NFAT-dependent IL-4). Each half is separately published — JNK1 phosphorylation of NFATc1α at Ser117/Ser172 blocking calcineurin targeting, nuclear accumulation and NFAT-dependent output, and Act1/TRAF6-dependent JNK activation downstream of IL-17RA — but no retrieved source places IL-17 upstream of the JNK1–NFATc1-a/b–IL-4 axis, and none reports a negative test of that link; the closest IL-17/NFATc1 work runs the opposite direction (NFATc1 acting on the Il17a promoter). Hence partial rather than established or open.

hypotheses.statement: NTRK1 (TrkA) directly drives MAPK (ERK) activation in a receptor-autonomous manner, and the amplitude and duration of MAPK activity scale with the level of NTRK1 activation.
hypotheses.mechanism: MAPK is activated downstream of ligand-stimulated receptor tyrosine kinase signalling, as in EGF-driven MAPK activation (bhalla1999:findings:000). Independently, NGF-stimulated NTRK1 produces a dose-graded, sustained ERK signal that the EGFR inhibitor gefitinib does not block (sparta2015:findings:002, sparta2015:findings:003). Lowering TrkA receptor number converts sustained ERK activation into transient activation (marshall1995:findings:005). Together these imply that NTRK1 activity itself sets MAPK activation amplitude and persistence, rather than acting through EGFR transactivation.
hypotheses.prediction: Titrating NTRK1 expression (e.g., graded doxycycline induction) at fixed NGF should monotonically increase both the peak and the sustained level of MAPK phosphorylation. Inhibiting NTRK1 kinase activity should abolish NGF-induced MAPK activation even when EGFR is fully functional, whereas EGFR inhibition should leave it intact.
hypotheses.test: In MCF10A (or similar) cells with doxycycline-inducible NTRK1, apply a range of doxycycline doses and a fixed NGF dose. Measure phospho-ERK1/2 by western blot or with an ERK FRET reporter over 0–12 h. In parallel, treat with an NTRK1 kinase inhibitor or NTRK1 siRNA versus gefitinib, and compare how each treatment affects phospho-ERK.

citations.title: Receptor Level Mechanisms Are Required for Epidermal Growth Factor (EGF)-stimulated Extracellular Signal-regulated Kinase (ERK) Activity Pulses.
Prediction and validation of the distinct dynamics of transient and sustained ERK activation.
Specificity of receptor tyrosine kinase signaling: transient versus sustained extracellular signal-regulated kinase activation.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the plain-words mechanism (TrkA/NGF driving ERK autonomously, amplitude vs. duration coding), the entities together (TrkA + receptor number + sustained/transient ERK; TrkA + inducible expression + ERK amplitude; K-252a selectivity for trk over EGFR), and the prediction (graded receptor/ligand level scaling peak and sustained pERK; NGF-to-ERK requiring EGFR transactivation). The explanation is already in print: Sparta et al. report that ERK activation through a heterologous TrkA receptor in MCF10A cells is non-pulsatile and amplitude-modulated and that receptor-level mechanisms set ERK activation characteristics, Sasagawa et al. show NGF-stimulated sustained ERK amplitude is set by NGF concentration via TrkA-proximal signalling, and Marshall reviews that TrkA receptor number determines whether ERK activation is sustained or transient. No source was found that tested and negated NGF/TrkA-driven, EGFR-independent ERK activation, so the status is established rather than refuted; the only element lacking a direct published demonstration is titration of TrkA expression itself at fixed ligand.

hypotheses.statement: TGFBR1 (TβRI), through its kinase activity, activates RhoA in response to TGF-β, independently of Smad signaling.
hypotheses.mechanism: TGF-β rapidly and selectively activates RhoA over Rac1/Cdc42 in epithelial cells, within about 5 min (bhowmick2001:findings:005, derynck2019:findings:035). The RhoA-dependent lamellipodia response to TGF-β1 does not require the Smad pathway (edlund2002:findings:000). TGF-β signaling requires TβRI to join TβRII in a receptor complex (derynck2019:findings:004), and TβRI directly starts several Smad-independent branches by recruiting adaptors such as ShcA and p85, with ERK activation on a similar fast timescale (derynck2019:findings:028, derynck2019:findings:032). Together these suggest that TβRI, not a Smad-dependent transcriptional route, is the receptor component that triggers rapid RhoA activation.
hypotheses.prediction: Blocking TβRI kinase activity or depleting TGFBR1 should abolish the rapid (≤5–10 min) increase in GTP-bound RhoA after TGF-β stimulation. Depleting Smad2/3/4 should leave it intact. Restoring wild-type TβRI, but not kinase-dead TβRI, should rescue RhoA activation.
hypotheses.test: In NMuMG cells, knock down TGFBR1 by siRNA or pretreat with a selective TβRI kinase inhibitor. Stimulate with TGF-β1 and measure GTP-RhoA over 0–30 min by rhotekin-RBD pull-down and immunoblot. Include Smad4 knockdown as a control for Smad independence, and re-express wild-type versus kinase-dead TβRI in the knockdown background to test for rescue.

citations.title: TGF-beta-mediated activation of RhoA signalling is required for efficient (V12)HaRas and (V600E)BRAF transformation.
Transforming growth factor-beta1 mediates epithelial to mesenchymal transdifferentiation through a RhoA-dependent mechanism.
TGFβ-induced early activation of the small GTPase RhoA is Smad2/3-independent and involves Src and the guanine nucleotide exchange factor Vav2.

novelty.note: I searched for Smad-independent rapid RhoA activation by TGF-β, for TβRI/ALK5 kinase dependence of RhoA activation, and for the specific prediction (receptor-kinase inhibitor or receptor-deficient cells abolishing early GTP-RhoA). Fleming et al. (Oncogene 2009) states exactly this explanation: TGF-β-mediated RhoA activation is dependent on ALK5 kinase activity and ALK5 maintains RhoA-ROCK signalling independently of Smad2, Smad3 and Smad4; the source corpus paper itself (Bhowmick 2001) additionally reports that TβRI-deficient R1B cells show little or no TGF-β-induced RhoA activation, and Papadimitriou et al. (2011) independently documents the Smad2/3-independence of the ≤5-min RhoA/RhoB response. Status is established; note one caveat, that in the Papadimitriou JEG3 system the TβRI inhibitor SB431542 did not prevent the early RhoA/B activation, so the kinase-dependence arm of the prediction appears cell-context dependent rather than universally confirmed.

hypotheses.statement: ZAP70 directly phosphorylates the tyrosine motif(s) of the CD28 cytoplasmic tail, acting alongside Lck as a kinase that licenses CD28's SH2-docking function.
hypotheses.mechanism: CD28's tail functions as a membrane-tethered tyrosine substrate whose phosphorylation creates an SH2 docking site that recruits the PI3K regulatory subunit (hui2017:findings:004; smithgarvin2009:findings:021), and its phosphorylation has so far been assayed only with Lck as the kinase in reconstituted liposomes (hui2017:findings:008). ZAP70, recruited to phosphorylated CD3ζ upon TCR clustering, is the kinase that phosphorylates tyrosine motifs on membrane-proximal proteins such as LAT and SLP-76 to generate SH2 docking sites (good2011:findings:006; smithgarvin2009:findings:003), so it is positioned in the same membrane compartment and with the same substrate preference as the CD28 tail. If CD28 is within ZAP70's substrate range, part of CD28 tail phosphorylation and downstream p85 recruitment would depend on ZAP70 rather than Lck alone.
hypotheses.prediction: Purified activated ZAP70 will phosphorylate the CD28 cytosolic tail on liposomes/bilayers in the absence of Lck, and p85 recruitment to CD28 will follow; conversely, blocking or removing ZAP70 in T cells will reduce CD28 tail phosphorylation and CD28-associated p85 after receptor engagement even when Lck activity and CD3ζ phosphorylation are preserved. If false, ZAP70 addition will not raise CD28 phosphorylation above the Lck-only baseline and ZAP70 loss will leave pCD28 unchanged.
hypotheses.test: Reconstitute His-tagged CD28 cytosolic tail on large unilamellar vesicles or supported bilayers with purified ZAP70 (pre-activated with phospho-ITAM peptide or a phosphomimetic/constitutively active variant) with and without Lck, add ATP, and quantify CD28 phosphotyrosine by immunoblot plus fluorescently labeled p85-SH2 binding by FRET/TIRF; in parallel, in a ZAP70-deficient versus reconstituted T cell line (or with an acute ZAP70 inhibitor), stimulate with anti-CD3/anti-CD28, immunoprecipitate CD28 and blot for phosphotyrosine and associated p85, using pCD3ζ as a control that upstream Lck activity is intact.

citations.title: p56Lck and p59Fyn regulate CD28 binding to phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase, growth factor receptor-bound protein GRB-2, and T cell-specific protein-tyrosine kinase ITK: implications for T-cell costimulation.

novelty.note: I searched for ZAP-70 as a kinase for the CD28 cytoplasmic tail, for CD28 YMNM/Tyr-191 phosphorylation with candidate kinases (Lck, Fyn, ZAP-70, ITK) driving p85/PI3K SH2 recruitment, and for reconstituted/liposome CD28 phosphorylation work and ZAP-70 substrate specificity. Raab et al. (PNAS 1995) directly tested this exact claim by coexpressing CD28 with candidate kinases: p56Lck and p59Fyn phosphorylated CD28 primarily at Tyr-191 of the YMNM motif and induced a 3- to 8-fold increase in p85 and GRB-2 SH2 binding, whereas "in contrast to Src kinases, ZAP-70 and ITK failed to induce these events." That is a stated negative result for ZAP-70 both as a CD28-tail kinase and as a licensor of p85 docking, so the hypothesis is refuted rather than merely unsupported; consistent with this, other searches found CD28-proximal phosphorylation events reported as ZAP-70-independent and ZAP-70 described as a narrowly selective kinase.

hypotheses.statement: GM-CSF (CSF2) signals through JAK2, which is directly required to transduce GM-CSF receptor engagement into STAT phosphorylation and GM-CSF-dependent myeloid proliferation/differentiation.
hypotheses.mechanism: JAK2 is reported to be physically attached to the IL-3 and erythropoietin receptors and to be tyrosine phosphorylated upon IL-3, erythropoietin and growth hormone stimulation, i.e. it is the kinase coupled to this class of haematopoietic cytokine receptors, and JAK2 V617F confers hypersensitivity to low IL-3 with pronounced STAT5 phosphorylation (darnell1994:findings:025, kralovics2005:findings:009, kralovics2005:findings:011). Independently, GM-CSF signalling in human CD14+ monocytes is suppressed by SOCS1, a JAK/STAT feedback inhibitor induced by TLR signals, implying GM-CSF acts through a SOCS-restrained JAK module (yoshimura2007:findings:017). Together these imply the GM-CSF receptor uses JAK2 as its proximal kinase, explaining both its STAT-type output and its SOCS1 sensitivity.
hypotheses.prediction: GM-CSF stimulation of monocytes/bone-marrow myeloid progenitors should induce rapid JAK2 tyrosine phosphorylation and downstream STAT5 phosphorylation; depleting or inhibiting JAK2 should abolish GM-CSF-induced STAT5 phosphorylation and block GM-CSF-driven proliferation and GM-CSF-dependent dendritic cell/macrophage outgrowth, while enforced SOCS1 expression should phenocopy this loss, and constitutively active JAK2 V617F should render such cells able to proliferate at limiting or zero GM-CSF.
hypotheses.test: In a GM-CSF-responsive myeloid line (or GM-CSF-cultured bone-marrow cells), stimulate with GM-CSF and immunoprecipitate JAK2 for anti-phosphotyrosine blotting to test receptor-proximal activation; then compare CRISPR/shRNA JAK2-knockout versus control cells for GM-CSF-induced pSTAT5 by immunoblot and for proliferation by a tetrazolium/viability dose-response across GM-CSF concentrations, with rescue by re-expressed wild-type JAK2 and gain-of-function testing by expressing JAK2 V617F to score cytokine-independent growth. Kinase-dependence can be confirmed pharmacologically with the JAK1/JAK2 inhibitor ruxolitinib, using IL-3 or another receptor as a specificity control.

citations.title: JAK2 associates with the beta c chain of the receptor for granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor, and its activation requires the membrane-proximal region.
Roles of JAK kinases in human GM-CSF receptor signal transduction.
The granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor receptor: linking its structure to cell signaling and its role in disease.
SOCS-1 mediates ubiquitylation and degradation of GM-CSF receptor.

novelty.note: I searched for GM-CSF receptor–JAK2 coupling, for JAK2 requirement in GM-CSF-induced STAT5 phosphorylation/proliferation, and for SOCS1 restraint of GM-CSF signalling. Quelle et al. (1994) show JAK2 physically associates with the GM-CSF receptor βc chain and is tyrosine-phosphorylated and catalytically activated within minutes of GM-CSF stimulation, with the membrane-proximal βc region required and activation correlating with mitogenesis; Watanabe et al. (1996) show dominant-negative JAK2 blocks GM-CSF-induced c-fos/c-myc activation and proliferation, concluding JAK2 is the primary kinase for GM-CSF activities; the Hercus et al. Blood review states JAK2 is the proximal kinase whose dimerisation in the receptor dodecamer drives activation, and Bunda et al. document SOCS-1 attenuation of GM-CSF receptor signalling. The explanation is therefore already published rather than novel, and no source tested and negated it.

hypotheses.statement: LPS activates EGFR signalling (transactivation) in LPS-responsive cells through p38 MAPK-dependent phosphorylation of TACE/ADAM17 and shedding of TGFalpha-family ligands.
hypotheses.mechanism: LPS acts as an inflammatory stimulus on TLR4-expressing myeloid cells. In these cells it engages p38 MAPK, which drives histone H3 Ser10 phosphorylation at inflammatory promoters and is then dephosphorylated by acetylated MKP1. Independently, p38 MAPKs phosphorylate TACE/ADAM17 on Thr735 in response to inflammatory stimuli, and that phosphorylation is required for TGFalpha-family ligand shedding and the resulting EGFR signalling. p38alpha also phosphorylates EGFR and Rab5 effectors to drive EGFR internalization after inflammatory stimulation. Together, these claims imply LPS should act upstream of EGFR activation and trafficking through the p38–TACE axis.
hypotheses.prediction: LPS stimulation of TLR4-competent cells should increase soluble TGFalpha-family ligand in the medium and raise EGFR tyrosine phosphorylation, followed by EGFR internalization. These effects should be abolished by p38 inhibition, by a TACE/ADAM17 inhibitor or a Thr735-nonphosphorylatable TACE mutant, or by a ligand-neutralizing antibody.
hypotheses.test: Treat TLR4-expressing cultured cells (e.g., RAW264.7 macrophages, or epithelial cells co-expressing TLR4/MD2/CD14) with LPS, with and without a p38 inhibitor, a TACE inhibitor, or anti-TGFalpha/EGFR-blocking antibody. Measure shed TGFalpha in conditioned medium by ELISA, EGFR phosphorylation by immunoblot, and surface EGFR loss by surface biotinylation or flow cytometry.

citations.title: Helicobacter pylori-induced gastric mucosal TGF-α ectodomain shedding and EGFR transactivation involves Rac1/p38 MAPK-dependent TACE activation.
Multiple TLRs activate EGFR via a signaling cascade to produce innate immune responses in airway epithelium.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the mechanism in words (LPS → p38 → TACE/ADAM17 Thr735 → TGF-alpha shedding → EGFR), the entities together (LPS/TLR4 + ADAM17 + TGF-alpha + EGFR in macrophages and epithelium), and the prediction (blockade by SB203580, metalloprotease inhibitors, TACE knockdown, ligand neutralization), plus an explicit search for negative tests. Slomiany & Slomiany (Inflammopharmacology 2016) state exactly this explanation for LPS: LPS stimulation causes p38 phosphorylation and Rac1-GTP membrane translocation that recruits active p38 to phosphorylate TACE on Thr735, producing soluble TGF-alpha release and EGFR transactivation; Koff et al. independently show LPS and other TLR ligands drive TACE-dependent TGF-alpha shedding and EGFR phosphorylation in airway epithelium. No source was found reporting a direct test with a negative outcome, so the explanation counts as already published rather than open; the EGFR-internalization arm of the prediction is the least directly covered part.

hypotheses.statement: ERK2 negatively regulates TGFBR1 (TβRI) by driving loss of cell-surface TβRI, forming a negative feedback loop on TβRI-initiated ERK signaling.
hypotheses.mechanism: TβRI recruits p52ShcA and promotes ShcA-Grb2-SOS complex formation, Ras activation and ERK/MAPK signaling (derynck2019:findings:028). Erk MAPK activation in turn causes TACE/ADAM17 to cleave TβRI but not TβRII, which reduces cell-surface TβRI and downstream Smad3 signaling (hata2016:findings:007, derynck2019:findings:009). ERK2 separately acts as a feedback kinase on upstream components of its own activating pathways, including the receptor FGFR1, SOS1, Raf-1 and MEK1, and this feedback attenuates their signaling (lake2016:findings:002, lake2016:findings:003). Together these claims imply that ERK2 is the Erk isoform that mediates activity-dependent downregulation of TβRI.
hypotheses.prediction: Stimuli that activate ERK, including TGF-β itself, should reduce cell-surface TβRI and increase shed TβRI ectodomain. This reduction should be lost or strongly blunted by ERK2 knockdown or MEK1/2 inhibition. Expressing constitutively active ERK2 without a stimulus should be enough to lower surface TβRI in a TACE-dependent manner, while leaving TβRII unchanged.
hypotheses.test: In a cultured cell line expressing endogenous TβRI and TβRII: (1) knock down ERK1, ERK2, or both by siRNA; (2) stimulate with PMA, EGF or TGF-β, with or without U0126; (3) quantify cell-surface TβRI and TβRII by surface biotinylation followed by immunoblot, and measure TβRI ectodomain in conditioned medium. As a gain-of-function arm, express constitutively active ERK2 with or without a TACE/ADAM17 inhibitor and measure surface TβRI. Finally, read out TGF-β-induced Smad3 phosphorylation to confirm functional attenuation.

citations.title: TACE-mediated ectodomain shedding of the type I TGF-beta receptor downregulates TGF-beta signaling.
TACE activation by MAPK-mediated regulation of cell surface dimerization and TIMP3 association.
TRAF6 ubiquitinates TGFβ type I receptor to promote its cleavage and nuclear translocation in cancer.

novelty.note: I searched for ERK/MAPK-driven TACE/ADAM17 cleavage of TβRI, for ERK-isoform-specific negative feedback on receptors, and for a TGF-β→ERK→surface-TβRI feedback loop. The core mechanism is published: Liu et al. show Erk MAP kinase pathway activation (PMA/serum, blocked by U0126/PD98059) drives TACE-mediated shedding of TβRI but not TβRII, lowering surface TβRI and TGF-β-induced Smad3 signaling, and Xu et al. give the MAPK-dependent TACE dimerization/TIMP3 step; TGF-β itself is also known to trigger TACE cleavage of TβRI, but via TRAF6/PKCζ rather than ERK (Mu et al.). No retrieved source resolves ERK1 versus ERK2 for this event (no isoform siRNA or constitutively active ERK2 arm) or frames it as a feedback loop closing on TβRI-initiated ERK signaling, so the isoform attribution and loop closure remain unpublished rather than refuted.

hypotheses.statement: SYK kinase activity is directly required upstream for IL-17 production by T cells responding to fungal stimuli, such that SYK inhibition or loss suppresses IL-17 induction.
hypotheses.mechanism: SYK signalling downstream of the fungal lectin receptors CLEC7A/CLEC6A/CLEC4E drives a distinct dendritic-cell cytokine program dominated by IL-2, IL-10 and IL-23 that yields potent TH17 responses, and SYK-deficient DCs are more profoundly blocked in this program than receptor-deficient DCs (mcsai2010:findings:021, mcsai2010:findings:022). Independently, human loss of the IL-17/Th17 axis — including CARD9 mutations that sit immediately downstream of SYK in this same pathway — produces reduced Th17 frequency and chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis, and IL-17/IL-17R-deficient mice are selectively susceptible to Candida (gaffen2014:findings:032, gaffen2014:findings:031). Together these imply that SYK is the proximal kinase whose activity sets the level of IL-17 output, rather than merely a parallel antifungal arm.
hypotheses.prediction: Pharmacological or genetic ablation of SYK in myeloid antigen-presenting cells stimulated with zymosan/heat-killed Candida should reduce IL-23 (and IL-2) secretion and, in co-culture, proportionally reduce IL-17A production and RORγt+ frequency in responding CD4+ T cells; adding exogenous IL-23 should rescue IL-17 despite continued SYK blockade, while SYK inhibition applied only to the purified T cells should leave IL-17 largely intact.
hypotheses.test: Stimulate wild-type versus Syk-knockdown (siRNA/CRISPR) bone-marrow-derived DCs or a human monocyte-derived DC line with zymosan or heat-killed Candida in the presence or absence of a SYK inhibitor, quantify IL-23/IL-2/IL-10 by ELISA, then co-culture the DCs with naive CD4+ T cells and measure IL-17A by ELISA and intracellular cytokine flow cytometry plus Il17a/Rorc qPCR; include an IL-23 add-back arm and a parallel arm where the inhibitor is applied only to T cells to localize the SYK requirement to the DC compartment.

citations.title: Syk- and CARD9-dependent coupling of innate immunity to the induction of T helper cells that produce interleukin 17.
Tyrosine phosphatase SHP-2 mediates C-type lectin receptor-induced activation of the kinase Syk and anti-fungal TH17 responses.
Syk signaling in dendritic cells orchestrates innate resistance to systemic fungal infection.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the mechanism in words (Syk/CARD9 innate signalling instructing IL-17-producing T helper cells), the entities together (Syk-deficient or Syk-inhibited DCs + zymosan/heat-killed Candida + IL-23/IL-2/IL-10), and the prediction (loss of Syk in myeloid APCs reducing IL-17A/Th17 output). The Dectin-1–Syk–CARD9 paper in Nature Immunology states exactly this explanation — Syk-dependent signalling in DCs drives IL-23 (with little IL-12) and instructs Th17 differentiation, with Candida-induced Th17 responses dependent on this pathway — and it is corroborated by the SHP-2/Syk scaffold study (impaired Syk signalling in DCs/macrophages abolishes IL-1β/IL-6/IL-23 and anti-fungal TH17 responses to C. albicans) and by DC-specific Syk deletion abrogating IL-23p19 production and antifungal resistance. Because published primary work already asserts the SYK-upstream-of-IL-17 requirement for fungal stimuli, the status is established; the finer sub-predictions (IL-23 add-back rescue, T-cell-restricted inhibitor arm) were not found as separate direct tests.

hypotheses.statement: TGFBR2 is a required upstream positive regulator of IL-17 expression in CD4+ T cells, such that TGFBR2 kinase signaling licenses the RORγt-dependent IL-17 program.
hypotheses.mechanism: T cell-specific loss of TGFBR2 reduces TH17 cell numbers and protects from EAE (massagu2023:findings:014), indicating that receptor-level TGF-β input is needed for cells that make IL-17; independently, IL-17 expression is driven by a RORγt/p300 complex whose activity is opposed by FOXP3 (gaffen2014:findings:017), and TGFBR2-dependent SMAD signaling is what induces FOXP3 with STAT5/NFAT (massagu2023:findings:016). Together these imply that TGFBR2 signaling acts directly on the IL-17-transcribing T cell, with the balance between FOXP3 induction and RORγt-driven IL-17 output set by how much TGFBR2 signal is received alongside inflammatory cues.
hypotheses.prediction: Naive CD4+ T cells in which TGFBR2 is deleted or its kinase inhibited will fail to upregulate RORγt and will produce little or no IL-17 under polarizing conditions, even with IL-6/IL-23 present, while the same cells given graded TGFBR2 signaling will show a dose-dependent switch from FOXP3-high/IL-17-low to RORγt-high/IL-17-high; conversely, re-expressing wild-type but not kinase-dead TGFBR2 will restore IL-17 production.
hypotheses.test: CRISPR-delete TGFBR2 (versus non-targeting guide) in primary naive CD4+ T cells, polarize in vitro with IL-6 plus IL-23 with or without added TGF-β, and quantify IL-17 by intracellular flow cytometry and ELISA plus RORγt and FOXP3 by qPCR/immunoblot; then rescue the knockout by transducing wild-type TGFBR2 or a kinase-dead (or Ser213-mutant) TGFBR2 and score restoration of IL-17, with a TGFBR1/II kinase inhibitor titration in wild-type cells as an orthogonal loss-of-function arm.

citations.title: Generation of pathogenic T(H)17 cells in the absence of TGF-β signalling.
Transforming growth factor beta is dispensable for the molecular orchestration of Th17 cell differentiation.
TGFbeta in the context of an inflammatory cytokine milieu supports de novo differentiation of IL-17-producing T cells.

novelty.note: I searched for the receptor-level requirement (TGFBR2/TGFβRII conditional deletion and Th17/RORγt), for the plain-language mechanism (TGF-β licensing the RORγt–IL-17 program versus FOXP3), and for the specific prediction (no IL-17 under IL-6/IL-23 polarization without TGF-β signaling). Two primary papers directly tested this and report the opposite: Ghoreschi et al. generated IL-17-producing cells from naive precursors independently of TGF-β signaling using IL-6/IL-23 plus IL-1β, with epigenetic remodeling of the Il17a, Il17f and Rorc promoters and co-expression of RORγt (and T-bet) proceeding without TGF-β1, and those cells were pathogenic in EAE; Das et al. report TGF-β had no effect on RORγt expression and that IL-6 alone sufficed for robust Th17 differentiation in Stat6-/-T-bet-/- mice, concluding TGF-β acts permissively by suppressing Th1/Th2 rather than being required for IL-17. The nearest supporting work (Veldhoen et al.) states the positive TGF-β-plus-IL-6 mechanism but frames TGF-β as redirecting lineage choice rather than as an obligatory licensing input, so the strong requirement claim and its central prediction are contradicted by direct test.

hypotheses.statement: Insulin positively regulates (enhances) activation of the kinase RSK1 (RPS6KA1) by potentiating EGF-driven ERK1/2 signalling, rather than by activating RSK1 on its own.
hypotheses.mechanism: In HEK293 cells, insulin alone barely activates Ras/ERK. However, it enhances ERK activation by low physiological EGF doses. This amplification requires PI3K: wortmannin abolishes insulin's enhancement of MEK/ERK. RSK1 activation requires ordered phosphorylation mediated by ERK1/2 and PDK1. In HEK293 cells, RSK1 activity toward tuberin is fully MEK-dependent (U0126-sensitive). So insulin's amplification of EGF-induced ERK1/2 should carry through to greater RSK1 activation.
hypotheses.prediction: In HEK293 cells, insulin plus a low EGF dose should produce more RSK1 activating-site phosphorylation (e.g. Ser380, Thr573) and more RSK-specific downstream phosphorylation (rpS6 Ser235/236, tuberin RXRXXpS/T) than EGF alone. Insulin alone should produce little RSK1 activation. The insulin-dependent increment should be lost with wortmannin or U0126 pretreatment.
hypotheses.test: Serum-starve HEK293 cells and stimulate with a low EGF dose (~0.1 nM), saturating insulin, or both, with or without 100 nM wortmannin or U0126 pretreatment. Collect a time course and immunoblot for phospho-ERK1/2 (T202/Y204), phospho-RSK1 (Ser380, Thr573), and RSK substrates (rpS6 Ser235/236 in rapamycin-treated cells, and tuberin RXRXXpS/T). In parallel, knock down RSK1 by siRNA to confirm that the insulin-enhanced substrate phosphorylation depends on RSK1.

novelty.note: I searched for insulin/EGF ERK amplification in HEK293, for insulin-driven RSK1 activating-site phosphorylation (Ser380/Thr573) and RSK readouts (rpS6 Ser235/236, tuberin RXRXXpS/T), and for combined insulin+low-EGF effects on RSK. The component steps are published separately: Borisov et al. report insulin's PI3K/GAB1/IRS-dependent amplification of low-dose EGF-driven Ras/ERK in HEK293 but measure only up to ERK (no RSK or RSK substrates), while Shahbazian et al. show in HEK-type cells that insulin cannot activate the ERK1/2 cascade and that insulin-stimulated phosphorylation of a shared RSK/S6K substrate is rapamycin-sensitive and U0126-insensitive, consistent with insulin alone not engaging RSK. No source I retrieved states the specific extension that insulin amplifies EGF-induced RSK1 activation or that the increment is wortmannin/U0126-sensitive; conversely Smadja-Lamère et al. report insulin alone does activate RSK in muscle and hepatic cells, so the claim is neither established nor directly refuted in this setting.

hypotheses.statement: JAK1 directly phosphorylates STAT5 on its activating tyrosine, acting as an upstream kinase for STAT5 when JAK1 is recruited to and activated at a cytokine receptor box1/box2 motif.
hypotheses.mechanism: JAK1 is a receptor-associated tyrosine kinase that, once dimerized on a receptor Box1/Box2 module, presents outward-facing TK catalytic clefts and becomes activation-loop phosphorylated, and in the same setting it directly activates a STAT family member (STAT3) downstream of a receptor it constitutively binds (glassman2022:findings:002, glassman2022:findings:003, derynck2019:findings:034). STAT5 is a STAT-family substrate whose activating tyrosine phosphorylation is driven by a JAK-family kinase at a cytokine receptor (kralovics2005:findings:011), and STAT family members are broadly interchangeable as substrates in such receptor contexts (villarino2017:findings:010). Together these imply that an activated JAK1 dimer can phosphorylate STAT5 directly rather than only STAT3.
hypotheses.prediction: Activating JAK1 (e.g. via the EpoR-IFNλR1 Box1/Box2 chimera or the V657F allele) should produce tyrosine-phosphorylated STAT5 in cells, and recombinant active JAK1 kinase domain should phosphorylate purified STAT5 on its C-terminal activating tyrosine in vitro; conversely, JAK1 loss or selective JAK1 inhibition should reduce ligand-induced STAT5 phosphorylation in cells that depend on JAK1 for signaling.
hypotheses.test: Two complementary assays in cultured cells and in vitro: (1) an in vitro kinase reaction combining purified recombinant active JAK1 (wild-type or V657F) with recombinant STAT5, reading out STAT5 activating-tyrosine phosphorylation by phospho-specific immunoblot with kinase-dead JAK1 and JAK1-inhibitor arms as controls; (2) in JAK1-deficient fibrosarcoma cells versus the parental line reconstituted with wild-type or kinase-dead JAK1, stimulate the EpoR-IFNλR1 Box1/Box2 chimera with Epo and immunoblot for phospho-STAT5 alongside phospho-JAK1, with a STAT5 co-immunoprecipitation from the same lysates to test direct JAK1-STAT5 association.

JAK1 and Tyk2 activation by the homologous polycythemia vera JAK2 V617F mutation: cross-talk with IGF1 receptor.
Constitutive association of JAK1 and STAT5 in pro-B cells is dissolved by interleukin-4-induced tyrosine phosphorylation of both proteins.

novelty.note: I searched for JAK1-mediated STAT5 Tyr694 phosphorylation, for the requirement of JAK1 catalytic activity in cytokine-induced STAT5 activation (JAK1-deficient/kinase-dead reconstitution), and for the activating JAK1 V657F/V658F allele plus JAK1–STAT5 physical association, using PubMed records and their abstracts. The published literature already states this explanation: kinase-inactive JAK1 completely abolishes γc-cytokine-induced STAT5 phosphorylation while kinase-inactive JAK3 does not (JAK1 dominant as the STAT5-activating kinase), the pseudokinase-domain JAK1 V658F allele drives cytokine-independent constitutive STAT5 activation, and JAK1 is reported in constitutive complex with STAT5 with both becoming tyrosine-phosphorylated upon receptor stimulation. No source was found that tested and negated JAK1 as an upstream kinase for STAT5, so the status is established rather than partial or refuted.

hypotheses.statement: Oncogenic KRAS directly activates MEK1, making MEK1 catalytic activity the obligate step through which KRAS drives ERK1/2 activation and KRAS-mutant cell growth.
hypotheses.mechanism: The MEK1 evidence places MEK1/2 as the kinase that phosphorylates the ERK1/2 TEY activation-loop motif downstream of Ras-mediated Raf activation, with MEK1 the top-scoring kinase for the ERK activation-loop site and MEK1/2 inhibition sufficient to abolish essentially all ERK-dependent substrate phosphorylation in cells. The KRAS evidence independently shows that mutant/amplified KRAS signals through this axis: a MEK inhibitor prevents resistance driven by KRAS/NRAS copy-number gain, and a KRAS-G12C-selective covalent inhibitor blocks the RAS-RAF interaction and downstream signalling. Together these imply a direct upstream-activator relationship in which KRAS-GTP output converges on MEK1 to phosphorylate ERK.
hypotheses.prediction: In KRAS-mutant cells, MEK1 activation-loop phosphorylation and MEK1 in vitro kinase activity toward ERK1/2 should be elevated and should fall rapidly upon KRAS silencing or KRAS-G12C inhibition; conversely, selective MEK1 depletion or a catalytically dead MEK1 should collapse ERK TEY phosphorylation and colony formation in KRAS-mutant but not in KRAS-wild-type, RTK-driven lines, and constitutively active MEK1 should restore ERK signalling and growth after KRAS knockdown.
hypotheses.test: In a KRAS-G12C-mutant cell line, (i) treat with the covalent G12C compound or doxycycline-inducible KRAS shRNA and immunoblot for phospho-MEK1 (S218/S222) and phospho-ERK1/2 (TEY), plus immunoprecipitate MEK1 and assay its in vitro kinase activity on recombinant kinase-dead ERK2; (ii) perform the reciprocal epistasis test with siRNA/CRISPR knockout of MEK1 (MEK2 intact) and rescue with wild-type, kinase-dead, or constitutively active MEK1, reading out ERK TEY phosphorylation and crystal-violet colony formation, with an RTK-driven KRAS-wild-type line as the specificity control.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the biochemistry of the MEK1 activation loop and its direct upstream kinase, isoform-selective MEK1 versus MEK2 depletion in RAS/KRAS-mutant cells, and the KRAS-to-ERK dependency axis in KRAS-mutant tumours. The general axis is long established but with RAF, not RAS, as the direct MEK1 activator: Alessi et al. identified Ser217/Ser221 of MEK1 as sites phosphorylated directly by p74raf-1 downstream of Ras, so no direct KRAS-MEK1 activation step is supported. The isoform-specific prediction has been directly tested and failed: in human colon carcinoma cells (a KRAS-mutant-rich setting) silencing MEK2 suppressed proliferation whereas MEK1 inactivation had only weak effects, and genetic loss of Mek1 stabilises rather than collapses Mek2/Erk phosphorylation, so MEK1 catalytic activity is not the obligate node the hypothesis requires.

hypotheses.statement: MTOR kinase activity positively regulates the lipid biosynthetic process, acting upstream of SREBP1c-driven de novo lipogenesis.
hypotheses.mechanism: Independent evidence on lipid biosynthesis shows that de novo lipid synthesis depends on mTORC1 and on mTORC2. The lipogenesis in TSC2-deficient cells is rapamycin-sensitive, loss of either complex's scaffold (raptor or rictor) reduces SREBP-1c activity and lipogenesis, and combined mTORC1/2 blockade reduces glucose-to-lipid conversion (manning2017:findings:040, szwed2021:findings:036, szwed2021:findings:073). Independent evidence on MTOR places SREBP1c regulation downstream of mTOR, and shows that mTOR inhibition suppresses mTOR-motif and p70S6K substrate phosphorylation (haeusler2018:findings:021, bekkerjensen2020:findings:016). The kinase itself is the one component shared by both complexes, so lipid synthesis should depend directly on MTOR catalytic activity.
hypotheses.prediction: Acute loss of MTOR protein or MTOR catalytic activity should lower SREBP1c processing and lipogenic gene expression (e.g., FASN). It should also cut incorporation of labeled glucose or acetate into newly synthesized lipids. This reduction should exceed that from rapamycin alone, because it also removes the mTORC2-dependent contribution. A kinase-dead MTOR should fail to rescue lipogenesis in MTOR-depleted cells, while wild-type MTOR should restore it.
hypotheses.test: In cultured hepatocyte-derived or TSC2-null fibroblast cell lines: (1) deplete MTOR by siRNA, or treat with an ATP-competitive mTOR inhibitor (e.g., Torin1) versus rapamycin; (2) measure de novo lipogenesis by [14C]-acetate or [13C]-glucose incorporation into the lipid fraction; (3) immunoblot precursor and nuclear SREBP1 and measure FASN mRNA by qPCR; (4) re-express siRNA-resistant wild-type versus kinase-dead MTOR to test whether catalytic activity is required.

citations.title: SREBP activity is regulated by mTORC1 and contributes to Akt-dependent cell growth.
Activation of a metabolic gene regulatory network downstream of mTOR complex 1.
mTOR complex 1 regulates lipin 1 localization to control the SREBP pathway.
mTORC2 Promotes Tumorigenesis via Lipid Synthesis.

novelty.note: I searched for the mechanism in plain words (mTOR kinase activity upstream of SREBP1c and de novo lipogenesis), the entities together (Torin1/rapamycin, SREBP-1 processing, FASN, TSC2-null cells, raptor/rictor), and the specific prediction (ATP-competitive mTOR inhibition exceeding rapamycin; mTOR depletion lowering lipogenic gene expression). Multiple primary papers already state this explanation: Porstmann et al. place SREBP-dependent lipogenesis downstream of mTOR in the Akt pathway, Düvel et al. show TSC2-null, rapamycin-sensitive activation of SREBP and de novo lipid biosynthesis, Peterson et al. show that the ATP-competitive inhibitor Torin1 (but not rapamycin) drives lipin 1 nuclear relocalization and strongly downregulates SREBP target genes — i.e. the predicted catalytic-activity requirement and the Torin1>rapamycin differential — and Guri et al. document an mTORC2-dependent lipid synthesis arm. Hence the explanation and even its distinguishing prediction are published, though the same literature notes rictor loss did not phenocopy raptor loss for Akt-driven SREBP-1 activation.

hypotheses.statement: TRAF6 is required for activation of MAPK14 (p38α), specifically its dual Thr180/Tyr182 activation-loop phosphorylation, in TGFβ receptor signalling, and this depends on TRAF6's RING-dependent K63-linked ubiquitin ligase activity.
hypotheses.mechanism: The corpus states that TRAF6 is required for TGFβ-receptor-induced activation of p38 MAPKs. That requirement works through TRAF6 auto-ubiquitination and TAK1 activation, independent of the canonical Smad pathway and of type I receptor kinase activity (cuadrado2010:findings:052, derynck2019:findings:030). TRAF6 RING mutants lose K63-linked polyubiquitin chain assembly (deng2000:findings:009). Separately, p38α is the ubiquitously expressed p38 isoform, is activated by dual Thr-Gly-Tyr phosphorylation, and fully accounts for MK2 activation (cuadrado2010:findings:000, cuadrado2010:findings:001, cargnello2011:findings:068). Together these imply that the p38 activation TRAF6 controls includes p38α and requires TRAF6's ligase activity, although the corpus names only p38 MAPKs generally.
hypotheses.prediction: Cells lacking TRAF6, or expressing only a RING-dead TRAF6 (C70A), should fail to induce TGFβ-stimulated p38α Thr180/Tyr182 phosphorylation. MK2 phosphorylation at the p38α-dependent sites (Thr222, Ser272, Thr334) should also fail. Wild-type TRAF6 re-expression should restore both.
hypotheses.test: Knock out or knock down TRAF6 (CRISPR or siRNA) in a TGFβ-responsive cultured cell line. Reconstitute with empty vector, wild-type TRAF6, or TRAF6 C70A. Stimulate with TGFβ. Immunoprecipitate p38α with an isoform-specific antibody and immunoblot for phospho-Thr180/Tyr182, and blot lysates for phospho-MK2 Thr334. Use SB203580-treated cells as a control confirming that the MK2 readout is p38-dependent.

citations.title: TRAF6 mediates Smad-independent activation of JNK and p38 by TGF-beta.
The type I TGF-beta receptor engages TRAF6 to activate TAK1 in a receptor kinase-independent manner.
TTRAP Is a Novel Component of the Non-Canonical TRAF6-TAK1 TGF-β Signaling Pathway

novelty.note: I searched for the mechanism in plain words (TRAF6 requirement for TGF-β-induced p38 activation via TAK1 K63 ubiquitination), for the entities together (TRAF6 RING C70A mutant + phospho-p38 Thr180/Tyr182), and for negative reports (TRAF6-independent TGF-β p38 phosphorylation). Yamashita et al. (Mol Cell 2008) report that TRAF6 is specifically required for Smad-independent TGF-β activation of p38, that a RING-deleted TRAF6 curtails TGF-β/TβRI-induced p38 phosphorylation, and that wild-type but not RING-mutant TRAF6 (C70A) rescues signalling in TRAF6-deficient MEFs; Sorrentino et al. (Nat Cell Biol 2008) independently show TRAF6 E3 activity and K63-linked polyubiquitylation drive TAK1–p38/JNK activation independently of TβRI kinase activity. This matches the hypothesis' core explanation, so the status is established; the only elements not directly published are the isoform-resolved p38α immunoprecipitation readout and the MK2 Thr222/Ser272/Thr334 predictions, and no source tested and negated the claim.

hypotheses.statement: MAPK signaling regulates MTOR activity through its MAPK-activated protein kinase MK2, which phosphorylates the MTOR regulator TSC2 at Ser1210 and promotes 14-3-3 binding, so that MTOR-dependent phosphorylation outputs change in response to MAPK activation under stress.
hypotheses.mechanism: MK2 is classified as a member of the MAPK-activated protein kinase family, placing it downstream of MAPK (cargnello2011:findings:021). MK2 phosphorylates TSC2 at Ser1210, which promotes 14-3-3 binding and may regulate MTOR-dependent protein synthesis under certain stresses (cargnello2011:findings:077). In EGF-stimulated RPE1 cells, EGF-regulated site occupancies are enriched for MAPK signaling (bekkerjensen2020:findings:014), and MTOR inhibition specifically lowers MTOR-motif and p70S6K substrate sites (bekkerjensen2020:findings:016), which gives measurable readouts for testing whether the MAPK branch feeds into MTOR output.
hypotheses.prediction: Under a stress that activates the MAPK/MK2 branch, TSC2 Ser1210 phosphorylation and TSC2–14-3-3 association should increase. MTOR-motif and p70S6K substrate phosphorylation should change in the same direction. Blocking MK2, or mutating TSC2 Ser1210 to alanine, should abolish both the 14-3-3 binding and the MTOR-output change without affecting the MTOR response to direct MTOR inhibition.
hypotheses.test: In cultured cells (e.g. RPE1 or HEK-293T) exposed to a MAPK/MK2-activating stress, compare cells treated with or without an MK2 inhibitor or MK2 siRNA. Also compare cells re-expressing wild-type versus S1210A TSC2 on a TSC2-knockdown background. Measure TSC2 Ser1210 phosphorylation by immunoblot, TSC2–14-3-3 binding by co-immunoprecipitation, and MTOR output by immunoblot of S6K1 Thr389 and 4E-BP1 phosphorylation (or by targeted phosphoproteomics of MTOR-motif sites). Include an MTOR inhibitor as a reference control.

citations.title: The p38 and MK2 kinase cascade phosphorylates tuberin, the tuberous sclerosis 2 gene product, and enhances its interaction with 14-3-3.
p38 regulates the tumor suppressor PDCD4 via the TSC-mTORC1 pathway.

novelty.note: I searched for the mechanism in plain words (MK2 phosphorylating TSC2 Ser1210 creating a 14-3-3 site), for the entities together (MAPKAPK2 + TSC2 + mTORC1/S6K), and for a direct negative test (S1210A or MK2 inhibition failing to change mTORC1 output). The primary report of this exact explanation is Li et al. 2003 (JBC), which shows anisomycin/serum stimulate Ser1210 phosphorylation via the p38–MK2 cascade, that MK2 phosphorylates Ser1210 directly, that this creates the 14-3-3 binding site, and that 14-3-3 binding impairs the TSC1/TSC2 complex's inhibition of S6 kinase phosphorylation; a later study extends the same p38–MK2→TSC→mTORC1 axis to a downstream mTORC1-dependent output. No source was found that tested this specific claim and reported it does not hold, so the status is established rather than partial or refuted.

hypotheses.statement: MAPK (ERK1/2) signaling activates MTORC1 by inactivating the TSC1/TSC2 complex, directly and through its downstream kinase RSK.
hypotheses.mechanism: laplante2012 states that ERK1/2 and RSK1 directly phosphorylate and inactivate TSC1/TSC2, the Rheb GAP, and that this activates mTORC1. cargnello2011 places RSK1/2 downstream of Ras/MAPK activation as MAPK-activated protein kinases. EGF stimulation drives MAPK activation (bhalla1999, bekkerjensen2020), and mTORC1 output is read out as S6K1 Thr389 and 4E-BP1 phosphorylation (gu2017). Together these claims imply that MAPK activity should raise mTORC1 activity through a TSC2-dependent route.
hypotheses.prediction: In EGF-stimulated cells, blocking MAPK activation should reduce mTORC1-specific substrate phosphorylation (S6K1 Thr389, 4E-BP1 Ser65). This reduction should be absent in TSC2-deficient cells. cargnello2011 reports that RSK phosphorylates rpS6 Ser235/236 independently of S6K, so that site is not an mTORC1 readout here; the prediction concerns the S6K1 Thr389 and 4E-BP1 readouts only.
hypotheses.test: Stimulate cultured wild-type and TSC2-knockout (CRISPR) cells with EGF, with or without a MEK or ERK inhibitor, and optionally with an RSK inhibitor. Immunoblot for phospho-ERK1/2, phospho-TSC2, S6K1 Thr389 and 4E-BP1 Ser65. As a gain-of-function arm, express constitutively active MEK and measure the same mTORC1 readouts, with and without rapamycin as a control.

citations.title: Tumor-promoting phorbol esters and activated Ras inactivate the tuberous sclerosis tumor suppressor complex via p90 ribosomal S6 kinase
Phosphorylation and Functional Inactivation of TSC2 by Erk
TSC2/Rheb signaling mediates ERK-dependent regulation of mTORC1 activity in C2C12 myoblasts.

novelty.note: I searched for ERK/RSK phosphorylation of the TSC1/TSC2 complex, for the Roux/Blenis RSK–tuberin work, and for MEK-inhibitor effects on S6K1 Thr389 in TSC2-dependent settings. Multiple primary papers state exactly this explanation: RSK1 phosphorylates tuberin at Ser1798 downstream of Ras/MAPK to inhibit the complex and increase mTOR signaling; ERK phosphorylates TSC2 (Ser664) causing TSC1–TSC2 dissociation and loss of mTOR inhibition; and a myoblast study shows MEK/ERK-driven S6K1 Thr389 phosphorylation is mediated through TSC2/Rheb. Nothing found reports a direct negative test, so the status is established rather than partial or refuted.

hypotheses.statement: MEK1 kinase activity positively regulates (activates) mTORC1 signaling in growth-factor-stimulated cells, through ERK1/2-mediated inactivating phosphorylation of the TSC1/TSC2 complex.
hypotheses.mechanism: MEK1 phosphorylates the ERK1/2 activation-loop TEY motif, and ERK sites are top-ranked for MEK1 (cargnello2011:findings:002, johnson2023:findings:009). Separately, ERK1/2 is reported to directly phosphorylate and inactivate TSC1/TSC2, the Rheb GAP, which activates mTORC1 (laplante2012:findings:002). This link parallels the stated AKT-TSC2-RHEB route (haeusler2018:findings:027). Together these claims imply that MEK1 output should feed positively into mTORC1 activity. That positive effect may be partly masked by the feedback relief of PI3K/Akt that follows MEK1/2 inhibition (lake2016:findings:025).
hypotheses.prediction: Acute, selective MEK1/2 inhibition in serum- or EGF-stimulated cells should lower mTORC1 substrate phosphorylation (S6K1 Thr389, 4E-BP1) together with ERK-dependent TSC2 phosphorylation. The reduction should be lost in TSC2-depleted cells. With prolonged inhibition, the reduction should be blunted as Akt phosphorylation rises. Expressing constitutively active MEK1 should raise mTORC1 substrate phosphorylation in a TSC2-dependent way.
hypotheses.test: In HeLa cells or fibroblasts stimulated with growth factor, treat with PD0325901, verified with U0126, over a time course. Immunoblot phospho-ERK1/2, ERK-site phospho-TSC2, phospho-Akt, and phospho-S6K1 Thr389 / phospho-4E-BP1. Run control versus TSC2 siRNA cells, with and without a PI3K or Akt inhibitor to remove the compensatory Akt input. Complement this with transfection of constitutively active MEK1 and a kinase-dead MEK1.

The Ras-ERK and PI3K-mTOR pathways: cross-talk and compensation.

novelty.note: I searched for ERK-mediated TSC2 phosphorylation activating mTORC1, for MEK-inhibitor effects on S6K1 Thr389 together with TSC2 phospho-sites, and for reported negative results on MEK inhibition and mTORC1 substrates. The proposed explanation is already published in full: Ma et al. (Cell 2005) map ERK sites on TSC2 (including Ser664), show ERK phosphorylation dissociates TSC1-TSC2 and impairs its ability to inhibit mTOR signaling, and Miyazaki et al. (FEBS Open Bio 2017) directly perform the predicted experiment, showing U0126 blocks TSC2-Ser664 phosphorylation and reduces stimulated S6K1 Thr389 phosphorylation with Rheb dependence; the Life Science Alliance 2022 paper further resolves ERK1/2- versus Akt-biased control through a single TSC2 serine, and the Mendoza/Er/Blenis review states the MEK-ERK-to-TSC2-mTORC1 link alongside the Akt feedback-relief caveat invoked in the mechanism. Status is established rather than partial because these sources assert the same explanation for the same phenomenon, including the MEK-inhibition prediction; some contexts report MEK inhibition not lowering mTORC1 substrates, but those are cell-type-specific quantitative differences rather than a direct negative test of the ERK-TSC2 link.

hypotheses.statement: RAF1 (CRAF) directly phosphorylates and activates MEK1, placing MEK1 as the immediate kinase substrate of RAF1 in the Ras-Raf1-MEK-ERK cascade.
hypotheses.mechanism: Independent evidence places MEK1/2 immediately downstream of Raf. MEK1/2 phosphorylates ERK1/2 downstream of Ras-mediated Raf activation, and rapamycin-induced Raf1 Ser338 phosphorylation drives ERK activation through a Ras-Raf1-MEK1/2 route. For RAF1 itself, pharmacological inhibition of c-Raf eliminates MEK activity, and CRAF's isolated catalytic domain gives Ras-independent MEK phosphorylation. Washed CRAF immunoprecipitates also show kinase activity read out as pMEK. Together these suggest RAF1 catalytic activity acts on MEK1 without an intervening kinase.
hypotheses.prediction: Purified or immunoprecipitated catalytically active RAF1 (e.g., the catC catalytic domain) should phosphorylate recombinant kinase-dead MEK1 in a cell-free reaction. Kinase-dead RAF1 or RAF1 inhibitor treatment should abolish this phosphorylation. In cells, RAF1 depletion should reduce MEK1 phosphorylation when other RAF isoforms cannot compensate.
hypotheses.test: Run an in vitro kinase assay. Incubate recombinant kinase-dead MEK1 with ATP and either immunopurified wild-type RAF1 catalytic domain or a kinase-dead RAF1 mutant, with and without a RAF inhibitor. Detect MEK1 activation-loop phosphorylation by phospho-MEK immunoblot or 32P incorporation. Using kinase-dead MEK1 excludes MEK autophosphorylation. As a complementary check, knock down RAF1 by siRNA in HEK293 cells and immunoblot phospho-MEK1 after growth factor stimulation.

citations.title: Raf-1 activates MAP kinase-kinase.
Identification of the sites in MAP kinase kinase-1 phosphorylated by p74raf-1.
Reconstitution of the Raf-1-MEK-ERK signal transduction pathway in vitro.

novelty.note: I searched for direct Raf-1 phosphorylation of MEK1 activation-loop serines, for the 1992-era 'Raf-1 activates MAP kinase kinase' primary literature, and for cell-free reconstitution with purified/kinase-inactive MEK, retrieving records via Europe PMC and NCBI E-utilities. The claim is classic, long-established biochemistry: Kyriakis et al. identified MAPK-K as the first physiological substrate of the c-raf-1 product, Alessi et al. mapped Ser217/Ser221 of MAPKK1 as sites phosphorylated directly by p74raf-1, and Macdonald et al. reconstituted the pathway in vitro with purified recombinant proteins (including kinase-inactive MEK), concluding MEK is a direct substrate of Raf-1 and that Raf-1 phosphorylation is sufficient for MEK activation. This matches both the stated mechanism and the proposed cell-free test, so the hypothesis is anticipated rather than open.

hypotheses.statement: RSK positively regulates (activates) MTOR kinase signaling in mTORC1 downstream of Ras/MEK/ERK, by relieving TSC2 inhibition and by modifying the mTORC1 complex.
hypotheses.mechanism: RSK phosphorylates TSC2 at Ser1798 (and at S939/T1462). This negatively regulates TSC2 GAP activity toward Rheb and is linked to mTORC1 induction. RSK also phosphorylates Raptor, a component of mTORC1 (cargnello2011:findings:035, manning2017:findings:028). On the MTOR side, loss of TSC1 function is associated with activated mTOR signaling and rapalog sensitivity (fruman2017:findings:044). Inhibitory phosphorylation of TSC2 by a related kinase, MK2, is proposed to regulate mTOR-dependent protein synthesis (cargnello2011:findings:077). Together these imply that RSK activity should feed into MTOR kinase output. The MTOR readouts used here are p70S6K substrates and S6K1 phosphorylation (bekkerjensen2020:findings:016, gu2017:findings:012).
hypotheses.prediction: In mitogen-stimulated cells, blocking RSK should reduce mTORC1-dependent phosphorylation of S6K1 and 4EBP1 and reduce the kinase activity of immunoprecipitated MTOR, even though ERK phosphorylation stays intact. A TSC2 Ser1798A mutant, a Raptor mutant at the RSK site, or both should blunt this RSK-dependent increase in mTORC1 activity.
hypotheses.test: Stimulate HeLa or HEK-293T cells with EGF or PMA after RSK1/2 siRNA knockdown or treatment with BI-D1870 or FMK. Immunoblot S6K1 Thr389, 4EBP1 and phospho-ERK, and run an in vitro kinase assay on MTOR immunoprecipitates. In parallel, re-express wild-type versus RSK-site phospho-deficient TSC2 (S1798A) or Raptor in knockdown cells to test whether the RSK effect on MTOR output requires these sites. Avoid rpS6 Ser235/236 as a readout, because RSK phosphorylates those sites directly.

citations.title: Tumor-promoting phorbol esters and activated Ras inactivate the tuberous sclerosis tumor suppressor complex via p90 ribosomal S6 kinase.
