novelty.note: I searched for the mechanism in words (PKC → Raf/ERK → Raptor → mTORC1), for the entities together (PMA, MEK/ERK, Raptor S8/S696/S863, 4E-BP1, S6K1), and for the prediction (does MEK inhibition or Raptor phospho-site mutation block PKC/PMA-induced mTORC1 activation). The route is already published: Carriere et al. used PMA (a PKC activator) to drive ERK1/2-dependent Raptor phosphorylation and showed phospho-deficient Raptor alleles reduce PMA-stimulated mTORC1 signalling to 4E-BP1. However, the specific prediction that PKC-induced mTORC1 activation requires the MEK/ERK arm was directly tested in Nazio-style PKC-isoform work by Hernández-Negrete-type analysis in PLoS ONE, which reports that MEK/ERK and RSK are largely dispensable for PMA-induced mTORC1 activation (U0126 blocked ERK phosphorylation but had only minor effects on S6K phosphorylation), the response instead requiring co-ordinated cPKC/nPKC action via PLD2 and the v-ATPase/Ragulator/Rag axis; Miyazaki & Takemasa likewise find PMA-induced mTORC1 activation only partially MEK-dependent and routed through TSC2/Rheb rather than Raptor/RSK phosphorylation. Because a stated negative result exists for the MEK/ERK-dependence step that the hypothesis makes essential, I score this refuted while noting the anticipating positive report.

hypotheses.statement: BCR ligation activates PI3K, and PI3K is the direct upstream mediator of BCR-induced AKT phosphorylation, FOXO1 cytoplasmic retention and ERK2 activation in B cells.
hypotheses.mechanism: In murine B cells, the PI3K inhibitor LY294002 and a dominant-negative p85 construct each block BCR-induced ERK2 activation, with no direct effect on ERK itself (jacob2002:findings:001, :002). In CLL cells, BCR ligation raises AKT S473 phosphorylation and FOXO1 T24 phosphorylation and shifts FOXO1 to the cytoplasm (cosimo2018:findings:008). Independently, an active PI3K/Akt pathway drives phosphorylation and cytoplasmic localisation of the FOXO family member FKHRL1, and PI3K inhibition makes it nuclear (brunet1999:findings:006); PI3K inhibition likewise prevents AKT phosphorylation and blocks receptor-driven enhancement of MEK/ERK (borisov2009:findings:009). Together these suggest that the BCR outputs seen in CLL cells (AKT, FOXO1, ERK) are routed through PI3K activated by the receptor.
hypotheses.prediction: BCR crosslinking should rapidly increase PI3K lipid-kinase activity associated with tyrosine-phosphorylated complexes in B cells. Pharmacological or dominant-negative PI3K inhibition should abolish BCR-induced AKT S473/T308 phosphorylation, FOXO1 T24 phosphorylation and FOXO1 nuclear exclusion, as well as BCR-induced ERK2 activity.
hypotheses.test: Stimulate MEC-1 or A20 B cells with anti-IgM F(ab')2, with or without LY294002, GDC0941 or transfected p85Δinter-SH2. Measure PI3K activity in anti-phosphotyrosine/anti-p85 immunoprecipitates by an in vitro PI kinase assay. Measure pAKT S473/T308, pFOXO1 T24 and pERK1/2 by Western blot, and FOXO1 nuclear/cytoplasmic distribution by subcellular fractionation.

citations.title: Cross-linking of B cell antigen receptor-related structure of pre-B cell lines induces tyrosine phosphorylation of p85 and p110 subunits and activation of phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase.
PI3 kinase signals BCR-dependent mature B cell survival.
Insights into PI3K/AKT signaling in B cell development and chronic lymphocytic leukemia.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the plain-language mechanism (BCR ligation activating PI3K upstream of AKT/FOXO1/ERK), the entity combination (BCR + PI3K + AKT + FOXO1 + CLL), and the prediction (PI3K inhibitors blocking BCR-induced AKT S473/FOXO1 T24 phosphorylation and nuclear exclusion, and PI3K lipid-kinase activity in anti-phosphotyrosine/p85 immunoprecipitates after anti-IgM crosslinking), using PubMed/Europe PMC and publisher pages. Retrieved sources state each element as published fact: anti-mu BCR crosslinking induces tyrosine phosphorylation of p85/p110 and activation of PI3K lipid-kinase activity; PI3K signalling downstream of the BCR acts through FOXO1 in mature B cells; and reviews of PI3K/AKT in B cells and CLL state that BCR engagement activates PI3K, whose AKT output phosphorylates and inactivates/excludes FOXO1 from the nucleus. No source reported a direct negative test of this specific routing, so the status is established rather than refuted or partial.

hypotheses.statement: mTORC2 positively regulates the output of MAPK (ERK) signalling by acting with ERK on the RSK hydrophobic motif (Ser380), so that mTORC2 activity sets how much ERK activation becomes RSK activity.
hypotheses.mechanism: RSK is a MAPK-activated protein kinase that acts downstream of Ras/MAPK. It moves to the nucleus on ERK1/2 stimulation, and RSK1/2 phosphorylate rpS6 Ser235/236 in response to Ras/MAPK activation (cargnello2011). Growth-factor-induced phosphorylation of RSK at hydrophobic-motif Ser380 is mediated by ERK and also involves mTORC2. mTORC2 is activated when nutrients are withdrawn (chou2020). Together, these claims suggest that mTORC2 modulates the RSK-level output of MAPK signalling rather than only running in parallel to it.
hypotheses.prediction: Removing mTORC2 (loss of Rictor or SIN1) should lower growth-factor-induced RSK Ser380 phosphorylation, along with downstream RSK readouts (rpS6 Ser235/236 under rapamycin, RSK nuclear translocation), even when ERK1/2 phosphorylation is unchanged. Nutrient withdrawal, which activates mTORC2, should raise ERK-dependent RSK Ser380 phosphorylation only in cells that have mTORC2.
hypotheses.test: Knock down or knock out Rictor in cultured cells (e.g., RPE1 or MEFs), with a non-targeting control. Stimulate with EGF under nutrient-replete and nutrient-withdrawn conditions, with or without a MEK inhibitor, and add rapamycin to isolate RSK-mediated rpS6 phosphorylation. Immunoblot for phospho-ERK1/2, RSK pSer380, and rpS6 pSer235/236. Use immunofluorescence to measure RSK nuclear localization. Finally, run an in vitro kinase assay with Rictor immunoprecipitates on recombinant RSK, with or without prior ERK phosphorylation.

citations.title: mTORC2 Is Involved in the Induction of RSK Phosphorylation by Serum or Nutrient Starvation.

novelty.note: I searched for mTORC2/Rictor/SIN1 control of the RSK hydrophobic motif Ser380, for mTORC2–ERK/MAPK crosstalk at RSK, and for Rictor-loss tests of growth-factor-induced RSK Ser380, and the explanation is already published as a primary study (Chou et al., Cells 2020; PMID 32605013, title confirmed on its PubMed record), which reports that intact mTORC2 is required for optimal RSK Ser380 phosphorylation, that Ser380 phosphorylation is ERK/MAPK-driven on growth-factor stimulation, and that serum or nutrient withdrawal (conditions that raise mTORC2 activity) robustly induces RSK Ser380. One nuance from that same work cuts against the 'mTORC2 catalytic activity' framing: pharmacological mTOR inhibition did not abolish Ser380 phosphorylation, so complex integrity/scaffolding rather than mTOR kinase activity appears to be the requirement. Because the core explanation (mTORC2 acting with ERK on the RSK HM site, nutrient-modulated) is explicitly stated in a published source, this is established rather than partial or open.

hypotheses.statement: SRC negatively regulates IRS1 by driving the ErbB-dependent inhibitory serine phosphorylation of IRS1, thereby reducing insulin-stimulated IRS1 tyrosine phosphorylation.
hypotheses.mechanism: In hepatoma cells, stress/TNF-induced IRS-1 serine phosphorylation (Ser612/Ser632/Ser307) requires ErbB1 or ErbB2/ErbB3 acting downstream of p38MAPK, even when p38 activation is intact, so an ErbB-proximal kinase must transmit the signal to IRS-1 (hemi2011:findings:008, hemi2011:findings:003). Independently, c-Src is the kinase that phosphorylates EGFR on Y845 and is required for ErbB-driven Erk1/2 and RSK activation, since PP2 or dasatinib abolishes both (chaturvedi2009:findings:012, chaturvedi2009:findings:013). Placing these together, active SRC is the plausible ErbB-associated kinase whose activity is needed to generate the inhibitory serine phosphorylations on IRS1.
hypotheses.prediction: Src inhibition (PP2 or dasatinib) or Src knockdown in HepG2/Fao cells should blunt TNF- or anisomycin-induced IRS-1 Ser612/Ser632/Ser307 phosphorylation and restore insulin-stimulated IRS-1 Tyr608/Y612 phosphorylation and Akt activation, while leaving p38MAPK/MAPKAPK2 phosphorylation unchanged; conversely, expression of constitutively active Src should increase IRS-1 serine phosphorylation and suppress its insulin-stimulated tyrosine phosphorylation even without TNF. Inactive analog PP3 should have no effect.
hypotheses.test: In HepG2 and Fao cells, pretreat with PP2 versus PP3 or dasatinib, or transfect Src siRNA versus control siRNA, then stimulate with TNF or anisomycin followed by insulin, and immunoblot in parallel for phospho-IRS-1 Ser612/Ser632/Ser307, insulin-stimulated IRS-1 phospho-Tyr, phospho-Akt, phospho-Src Y416, and phospho-p38/MAPKAPK2; complement with a gain-of-function arm expressing constitutively active versus kinase-dead Src and with an in vitro kinase reaction using recombinant Src and immunoprecipitated IRS-1 to test whether the effect requires an intermediate kinase rather than direct action on IRS1.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the mechanism in words (Src kinase driving inhibitory IRS-1 serine phosphorylation / Src inhibition restoring insulin sensitivity), the entities together (PP2/dasatinib + TNF + IRS-1 Ser307/Ser612/Ser632 + hepatoma), and the prediction (Src-dependent ErbB transactivation upstream of IRS-1 serine phosphorylation). The closest published work is the p38MAPK-ErbB transactivation study in hepatoma cells, which establishes the p38→ErbB→IRS-1 Ser-phosphorylation axis but does not test Src at all (it only speculates in Discussion that Src/Pyk2 may mediate stress-induced ErbB activation); separate work establishes Src-dependent EGFR Y845 transactivation and ERK activation but never connects it to IRS-1 serine phosphorylation or insulin resistance. No source states that Src is the kinase required for ErbB-dependent inhibitory IRS-1 serine phosphorylation, and no source reports a negative test of it, so the claim is open.

hypotheses.statement: Stress-induced (anisomycin/TNF) transactivation of ErbB2 activates AKT through ErbB2-associated PI3K activity.
hypotheses.mechanism: Ligand-independent ErbB2 transactivation by TNF or anisomycin leads to ErbB2 association with p85-PI3K and increased PI3K activity (hemi2011:context:000). Anisomycin-induced ErbB2 transactivation depends on ROS and is reduced by antioxidants (hemi2011:findings:010). Independently, AKT phosphorylation in response to receptor stimulation requires PI3K: wortmannin (borisov2009:findings:009) and GDC0941 (budi2015:findings:006) prevent it. Together these imply that ErbB2-recruited PI3K activity should drive AKT phosphorylation under stress conditions.
hypotheses.prediction: Anisomycin or TNF should increase AKT phosphorylation in cells that express ErbB2, without insulin or added ligand. ErbB2 knockdown, PI3K inhibition, or antioxidant (NAC) pretreatment should attenuate this increase. Total AKT levels should not change.
hypotheses.test: In cultured cells expressing ErbB2 (e.g., Fao/HepG2 hepatoma cells or mouse cells expressing Erbb2), transfect control or ERBB2 siRNA. Pretreat parallel wells with wortmannin or NAC, stimulate with anisomycin or TNF, and immunoblot for phospho-AKT, total AKT, ErbB2 Tyr phosphorylation and ErbB2–p85 co-immunoprecipitation. The hypothesis is ruled out if ERBB2 knockdown fails to reduce stress-induced AKT phosphorylation.

novelty.note: I searched for stress/TNF/anisomycin-induced ligand-independent ErbB2 transactivation with p85-PI3K, for the ROS/p38-dependence of that transactivation, and for the specific prediction that stress raises Akt-Ser473 phosphorylation via ErbB-associated PI3K. The Diabetes 2011 paper (PMC full text retrieved) explicitly reports that anisomycin, TNF and sphingomyelinase induce Akt-Ser473 phosphorylation, that this is reduced together with ErbB2/ErbB3-associated PI3K activity when ErbB/p38 signaling is blocked or ErbB expression is knocked down, and that antioxidant (NAC) and PI3K inhibition attenuate it; the earlier JBC study established the ligand-independent ErbB2/ErbB3–PI3K complex formation and enhanced PI3K activity under the same stresses. The proposed explanation and its predicted perturbation outcomes are therefore already published rather than novel or refuted.

hypotheses.statement: PI3K activity is required for insulin-induced activation (C-terminal phosphorylation) of mouse Smad2, acting upstream through TβRI/TβRII cell-surface availability.
hypotheses.mechanism: In NMuMG cells and MEFs, the PI3K inhibitor GDC0941 blocked Akt activation and prevented the insulin-induced increase in cell-surface TβRI and TβRII (budi2015:findings:006). In the same mouse cells, insulin induced Smad2 C-terminal phosphorylation that depended on TβRI kinase activity, since SB431542 blocked it (budi2015:findings:002). Smad2 is a receptor-activated Smad for TGF-β/activin signaling (derynck2019:findings:015). Together these imply that PI3K-dependent receptor surface accumulation is needed for insulin to drive Smad2 activation.
hypotheses.prediction: In insulin-stimulated NMuMG cells or MEFs, PI3K inhibition or p110 knockdown should reduce or abolish insulin-induced C-terminal phospho-Smad2 and its nuclear accumulation. Forced surface expression of TβRI/TβRII should restore the response. Basal phospho-Smad2 without insulin should not fall, and may rise, because GDC0941 alone increased surface receptor levels.
hypotheses.test: Pretreat NMuMG cells and MEFs with GDC0941 or another PI3K inhibitor (or siRNA against PI3K catalytic subunits), with and without insulin, over a time course. Immunoblot whole-cell and nuclear/cytoplasmic fractions for C-terminal phospho-Smad2 and total Smad2. Include SB431542 and AktVIII as comparators, measure surface TβRI/TβRII in parallel by biotinylation, and run a rescue arm with overexpressed receptors.

Integration of TGF-β-induced Smad signaling in the insulin-induced transcriptional response in endothelial cells.
Protein tyrosine phosphatase 1B regulates TGF beta 1-induced Smad2 activation through PI3 kinase-dependent pathway.

novelty.note: I searched for the plain-language mechanism (insulin/PI3K-Akt-dependent delivery of TGF-β receptors to the cell surface driving Smad2 activation), for the entities together (insulin + Smad2 + GDC0941/AktVIII + TβRI/TβRII in NMuMG/MEFs), and for the prediction (PI3K inhibitor blocking insulin-induced Smad2 C-terminal phosphorylation). The full text of Budi et al. (PMC4669960) and the endothelial-cell follow-ups state exactly this causal model — Akt/PI3K-dependent mobilization of intracellular TβRI/TβRII to the plasma membrane is what makes insulin enhance autocrine TGF-β/Smad2-3 activation — but in those papers the inhibitor experiments (GDC0941, AktVIII) are read out only as cell-surface receptor abundance, with no arm immunoblotting phospho-Smad2 under PI3K inhibition and no receptor-overexpression rescue. The nearest direct test of PI3K dependence of insulin's effect on Smad2 is in a different setting and goes the other way (insulin suppressing TGF-β1-induced Smad2 activation and nuclear entry via PI3K/Akt), so the general mechanism is published while this specific prediction is untested.

hypotheses.statement: PMA-induced phosphorylation of the RSK hydrophobic motif (Ser380) requires mTORC2, so mTORC2 is a required kinase component of the PMA→ERK→RSK activation response.
hypotheses.mechanism: PMA robustly activates ERK and RSK in HeLa cells, signalling through the MAP kinase/RSK cascade (chen1992:findings:012; casasterradellas2008:findings:010). Growth-factor-induced RSK Ser380 HM phosphorylation is ERK-mediated, and chou2020 extends this to mTORC2 involvement (chou2020:context:000). In SIN1-/- cells, which lack functional mTORC2, PMA stimulation did not rescue RSK HM phosphorylation, and MEK inhibition abolished the residual signal (chou2020:findings:003). Together these claims imply that PMA-activated ERK alone is not enough to fully phosphorylate the RSK HM, and that mTORC2 is needed for this PMA response.
hypotheses.prediction: Rictor or SIN1 knockdown in HeLa or HEK293 cells will sharply reduce PMA-stimulated RSK pSer380 while leaving PMA-induced ERK phosphorylation intact. Re-expressing the mTORC2 component will restore PMA-induced RSK pSer380.
hypotheses.test: Use serum-starved HeLa cells transfected with control, RICTOR or SIN1 siRNA, with or without pretreatment with an ATP-competitive mTOR inhibitor versus rapamycin. Stimulate with PMA and immunoblot for phospho-RSK Ser380, phospho-ERK and phospho-AKT S473 (as the mTORC2 readout). Include a rescue condition in which siRNA-resistant RICTOR is re-expressed.

citations.title: mTORC2 Is Involved in the Induction of RSK Phosphorylation by Serum or Nutrient Starvation.

novelty.note: I searched for mTORC2/SIN1 control of the RSK hydrophobic motif, for RSK Ser380 phosphorylation under PMA with ERK intact, and for the canonical ERK–CTKD autophosphorylation route for Ser380. The Cells 2020 paper (PMC7408474, PMID 32605013) states exactly this explanation: optimal pSer380 RSK requires intact mTORC2, PMA stimulation leaves pHM RSK low in SIN1-knockout cells and in rictor-null thymocytes despite ERK phosphorylation comparable to wild type. The only divergence is mechanistic detail — that paper finds Torin1 does not block pSer380, so mTORC2 is proposed to act as a scaffold rather than as the catalytic HM kinase; no source was found that tested and negated the mTORC2 requirement itself.

hypotheses.statement: BRAF negatively regulates SRC activity in BRAF-mutant cells, such that BRAF (or downstream MEK/ERK) inhibition relieves feedback and activates c-Src, which drives EGFR Y845 phosphorylation and ERK rebound.
hypotheses.mechanism: Claims about BRAF state that mutant B-Raf sustains ERK1/2 negative feedback whose relief by Raf or MEK1/2 inhibition immediately upregulates EGFR activity, reduces phosphorylation of the EGFR feedback site T669, and restores receptor-driven ERK and PI3K/Akt signalling (lake2016:findings:023, lake2016:findings:025), with pERK rebound accompanying prolonged inhibitor exposure (lito2014:findings:001). Independently, claims about SRC show that relieving a different negative feedback (mTOR inhibition by rapamycin) converts c-Src to its active state (increased pY416, decreased pY527), raises EGFR Y845 phosphorylation, and that Src inhibition by PP2 or dasatinib abolishes the resulting Erk1/2 and RSK phosphorylation (chaturvedi2009:findings:012, chaturvedi2009:findings:013), while Src depletion lowers EGF-driven GAB1 and ERK phosphorylation without altering EGFR autophosphorylation (borisov2009:findings:011). Together these imply that the feedback arm BRAF controls terminates on c-Src activation state, making Src the node that converts BRAF inhibition into EGFR Y845/ERK reactivation.
hypotheses.prediction: Vemurafenib or MEK inhibitor treatment of BRAF V600E cells should increase pSrc Y416 and decrease pSrc Y527 within hours, followed by increased EGFR Y845 and GAB1 phosphorylation; Src inhibition or knockdown should block the EGFR Y845 rise and blunt pERK/pRSK rebound without preventing the initial pERK suppression, whereas in BRAF wild-type RTK-driven lines the same inhibitors should not activate Src to the same extent.
hypotheses.test: Treat BRAF V600E melanoma and colon lines (plus a KRAS-mutant comparator) with vemurafenib or PD0325901 over a 0–48 h time course and immunoblot pSrc Y416/Y527, EGFR Y845, pGAB1, pERK and pRSK; repeat with SRC siRNA knockdown or PP2/dasatinib (PP3 as inactive control) and, to test directness of BRAF-dependent control rather than mere correlation, express a feedback-insensitive constitutively active B-Raf and ask whether it suppresses basal pSrc Y416 and prevents inhibitor-induced Src activation.

citations.title: A reversible SRC-relayed COX2 inflammatory program drives resistance to BRAF and EGFR inhibition in BRAF(V600E) colorectal tumors.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: BRAF/MEK-inhibition feedback relief activating SRC, the entity combination (BRAF V600E + EGFR Y845 + pSrc Y416/Y527 + ERK rebound), and the prediction that Src inhibition blocks ERK/EGFR reactivation. A 2023 Nature Cancer study in BRAFV600E colorectal cancer reports exactly the first half of the hypothesis — SRC family kinases are systematically activated after BRAF ± EGFR inhibition (increased activation-site pY419, loss of inhibitory pY530) — but it directly tested the causal link to the MAPK arm and found that SRC inhibition did not significantly affect rebound of ERK phosphorylation, and that SRC activation occurred even with combined vemurafenib plus EGFR inhibitors, so SRC is not acting through EGFR; resistance instead ran through a PGE2–GNAS–SRC–β-catenin program independent of ERK signalling. Because the specific prediction (Src as the node converting BRAF inhibition into EGFR Y845-dependent ERK/RSK rebound) was tested and reported negative, the status is refuted, even though the Src-activation step itself is published.

hypotheses.statement: TLR4 activates PI3K: LPS engagement of TLR4 drives PI3K-dependent AKT phosphorylation.
hypotheses.mechanism: In A549 cells, LPS stimulation of TLR4 induced AKT phosphorylation. Blocking EGFR kinase with erlotinib prevented both this AKT phosphorylation and TLR4 phosphorylation, placing AKT activation downstream of TLR4 engagement through an EGFR-dependent route (de2015:findings:006). Independently, PI3K inhibition with wortmannin abolished AKT phosphorylation downstream of EGFR without affecting EGFR tyrosine phosphorylation (borisov2009:findings:009). This implies the LPS/TLR4-induced AKT response is carried by PI3K activity.
hypotheses.prediction: If true, LPS-induced AKT phosphorylation should be lost when PI3K is inhibited. LPS-induced TLR4 phosphorylation and LYN recruitment to TLR4 should be largely unaffected, because PI3K would act downstream of these receptor-proximal events.
hypotheses.test: Use TLR4-expressing cultured cells, such as murine RAW264.7 macrophages or A549 cells. Pretreat with wortmannin (100 nM), LY294002 or vehicle, then stimulate with LPS over a time course. Immunoblot for phospho-AKT, phospho-TLR4 (Y674) and total proteins, and co-immunoprecipitate LYN with TLR4. In parallel, knock down TLR4 with siRNA to confirm that the LPS-induced, PI3K-sensitive AKT phosphorylation requires TLR4.

citations.title: TLR4/MyD88/PI3K interactions regulate TLR4 signaling.
Phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase is involved in Toll-like receptor 4-mediated cytokine expression in mouse macrophages.

novelty.note: Searched for LPS/TLR4-driven PI3K-dependent Akt phosphorylation, wortmannin/LY294002 sensitivity, and p85/MyD88 recruitment to TLR4. Laird et al. (J Leukoc Biol 2009) report that LPS stimulates Akt Ser473 phosphorylation in mouse macrophages, that this is completely TLR4-dependent (and MyD88-sensitive), and that p85 associates with MyD88/TLR4; Ojaniemi et al. (Eur J Immunol 2003) show TLR4 engagement forms a PI3K–MyD88 complex with wortmannin/LY294002-sensitive downstream output. The core explanation — LPS engagement of TLR4 driving PI3K-dependent AKT phosphorylation — is therefore already published, so this is established rather than open.

hypotheses.statement: LY294002 acts as a direct catalytic inhibitor of MTORC1, blocking mTOR-dependent phosphorylation of MTORC1 substrates such as 4E-BP1 in isolated complexes.
hypotheses.mechanism: LY294002 added directly into kinase reactions on RICTOR or FLAG-mTOR immunoprecipitates abolishes the mTOR-dependent phosphorylation of Akt1, and this inhibition tracks with the presence of catalytically competent mTOR rather than with upstream signaling, implying the drug engages the mTOR catalytic subunit itself (huang2008:findings:002; huang2008:findings:012). Because the same mTOR catalytic subunit carries MTORC1 phosphotransferase activity toward GST-4E-BP1 in Raptor- or mTOR-immunoprecipitate assays (carriere2010:findings:015; carrire2008:findings:010), the drug should inhibit MTORC1 catalysis in the same cell-free setting.
hypotheses.prediction: Adding LY294002 to an in vitro kinase reaction on Raptor/mTOR immunoprecipitates will dose-dependently reduce 32P incorporation into, and Thr37/46 phosphorylation of, GST-4E-BP1, even though the immunoprecipitates were prepared from stimulated cells and even when a rapamycin-resistant mTOR (S2035I) is used; Raptor–mTOR complex integrity and substrate binding will be unaffected.
hypotheses.test: Immunoprecipitate Myc-Raptor/mTOR (wild-type and rapamycin-resistant S2035I) from PMA- or insulin-stimulated HEK293 cells, wash the beads, then run parallel in vitro kinase assays with GST-4E-BP1 and [γ-32P]ATP in the presence of vehicle, a LY294002 dose series, or rapamycin added only to the reaction; quantify substrate phosphorylation by autoradiography and phospho-Thr37/46 immunoblot, and immunoblot the same beads for mTOR, Raptor, and bound 4E-BP1 to confirm complex integrity. Loss of substrate phosphorylation with LY294002 in the washed, rapamycin-resistant complexes supports direct inhibition; unchanged activity rules it out.

citations.title: Active-Site Inhibitors of mTOR Target Rapamycin-Resistant Outputs of mTORC1 and mTORC2
Rapamycin and mTOR kinase inhibitors.

novelty.note: I searched for LY294002 as a direct mTOR catalytic inhibitor, for in vitro kinase assays on mTOR/Raptor immunoprecipitates with GST-4E-BP1, and for rapamycin-resistant mTOR plus LY294002 combinations. The retrieved PLoS Biology study (Feldman et al.) explicitly describes LY294002 as a direct inhibitor of PI3K-family members including mTOR and states it was equally effective at inhibiting phosphorylation of S6K and 4E-BP1 by mTOR in vitro, while a retrieved review documents LY294002 as an ATP-site-competitive mTOR inhibitor acting independently of the rapamycin/FRB mechanism. Since the stated explanation — LY294002 engaging the mTOR catalytic subunit and thereby blocking MTORC1 substrate phosphorylation in cell-free assays — is already published, the status is established rather than open or partial.

hypotheses.statement: PMA treatment decreases phosphorylation of PTEN at Thr-366 by inducing inhibitory phosphorylation of GSK3β, the kinase responsible for that site.
hypotheses.mechanism: PMA activates ERK, RSK and MSK and induces GSK3β phosphorylation (casasterradellas2008:findings:010). GSK3β is the kinase that phosphorylates PTEN at Ser-362/Thr-366, and depleting GSK3 lowers PTEN Thr-366 reactivity (alkhouri2005:findings:003, alkhouri2005:findings:006). A stimulus that phosphorylated GSK3 at Ser-21/Ser-9 (IGF-1) also reduced PTEN phospho-Thr reactivity (alkhouri2005:findings:007), so PMA-induced GSK3β phosphorylation should reduce PTEN Thr-366 phosphorylation in the same way. PKC, Mek1 and Erk2 do not phosphorylate PTEN directly (alkhouri2005:findings:002), so the effect should go through GSK3 rather than through direct modification of PTEN.
hypotheses.prediction: In serum-starved cells, PMA should lower anti-phospho-Thr-Pro (Thr-366) reactivity of immunoprecipitated PTEN, with no change in total PTEN or in phospho-Ser-370/Ser-385. Expressing a non-phosphorylatable GSK3β S9A mutant or inhibiting MEK/RSK should prevent this decrease.
hypotheses.test: Serum-starve 293T cells or MEFs expressing mouse PTEN (wild-type or T366A as a specificity control) and treat them with PMA, with or without U0126 or BI-D1870 pretreatment, and with or without co-expression of GSK3β S9A. Immunoprecipitate PTEN and immunoblot for phospho-Thr-Pro, pSer-370, pSer-385 and total PTEN. Immunoblot lysates for phospho-GSK3 Ser-9/21.

citations.title: Cooperative phosphorylation of the tumor suppressor phosphatase and tensin homologue (PTEN) by casein kinases and glycogen synthase kinase 3beta.
Erk Associates with and Primes GSK-3β for Its Inactivation Resulting in Upregulation of β-Catenin

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the plain-words mechanism (PMA/phorbol ester lowering PTEN Thr-366 phosphorylation), the entities together (PTEN Thr-366 / Ser-362 + GSK3β + PMA + ERK/RSK), and the prediction (stimuli that inactivate GSK3 reducing PTEN tail phosphorylation). The two halves are separately published — Al-Khouri et al. establish GSK3β as the Thr-366/Ser-362 kinase and show IGF-1-induced GSK3 Ser-21/Ser-9 phosphorylation lowers PTEN phospho-Thr reactivity, and Ding et al. show ERK priming plus p90RSK-mediated Ser-9 phosphorylation inactivates GSK3β downstream of mitogenic/phorbol-ester stimulation — but I found no source that joins them by testing PMA (or MEK/RSK inhibition, or GSK3β S9A rescue) on PTEN Thr-366, and no source reporting a negative test of it. Hence partial rather than established or refuted.

hypotheses.statement: EGFR kinase activity directly drives activation (phosphorylation) of RPS6KB1/S6K1 and its downstream rpS6 phosphorylation, such that S6K1-dependent feedback and EGFR form a reciprocal regulatory pair.
hypotheses.mechanism: Rapamycin-mediated relief of mTORC1/S6K1 signaling activates Erk1/2 and RSK only in cells expressing kinase-competent EGFR with intact autophosphorylation sites, placing EGFR immediately downstream of loss of S6K1 output (chaturvedi2009:findings:007, chaturvedi2009:findings:009, chaturvedi2009:findings:010). Independently, S6K1 activity itself restrains ERK activation, since a rapamycin-insensitive constitutively active S6K1 suppresses rapamycin-induced ERK activation via an S6K1-IRS-1/PI3K feedback (carracedo2008:findings:005, carracedo2008:findings:006). Together these imply the EGFR-ERK arm and S6K1 are directly coupled rather than merely parallel: EGFR signaling should feed S6K1 activation, with S6K1 closing the loop back onto receptor-proximal ERK input.
hypotheses.prediction: Acute EGF stimulation should increase S6K1 Thr389 phosphorylation and S6K1 kinase activity toward rpS6 in EGFR-expressing B82L cells but not in parental EGFR-null B82L cells or in cells expressing kinase-dead K721M or Y5F EGFR; conversely, expressing constitutively active S6K1 should blunt the EGFR-dependent ERK/RSK rise seen after rapamycin.
hypotheses.test: In paired B82L lines (parental EGFR-null, wt-EGFR, K721M, Y5F), stimulate with EGF over a time course and immunoblot for phospho-S6K1 Thr389/Thr421-Ser424 and phospho-rpS6 Ser240/244, with AG1478 pretreatment as a specificity control; complement with an in vitro kinase assay on immunoprecipitated S6K1 using rpS6 as substrate, and reciprocally transfect the rapamycin-insensitive constitutively active S6K1 (E389 D3A/E) into wt-EGFR B82L cells to test whether EGFR-dependent ERK/RSK activation is suppressed.

citations.title: EGF-induced activation of 70-kDa S6 kinase in CHO cells expressing human EGF receptors.
Lysosomal EGFR acts as a Rheb-GEF independent of its kinase activity to activate mTORC1.
Rapamycin induces transactivation of the EGFR and increases cell survival.
Co-targeting EGFR and mTOR with gefitinib and everolimus in triple-negative breast cancer cells.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: EGF/EGFR-driven S6K1 Thr389 and rpS6 phosphorylation, the Chaturvedi B82L rapamycin-EGFR-ERK/RSK system, and kinase-dead/inhibitor tests of EGFR requirement for mTORC1 output. The growth-factor arm is long published — EGF activates p70S6K (wortmannin/PI3K-dependent) in cells expressing human EGFR, and EGFR inhibition lowers p-p70S6K/p-S6 — but no retrieved source states the reciprocal EGFR<->S6K1 pairing in the B82L mutant panel, and the source paper itself (PMID 19151764) does not test S6K1 feedback onto EGFR-dependent ERK/RSK. Moreover, one paper directly tested the kinase-requirement clause and reports the opposite: kinase-dead EGFR still triggers mTORC1/p-T389-S6K1 via a lysosomal Rheb-GEF function, with the kinase-only inhibitor erlotinib causing only a slight decrease, so the specific prediction that K721M EGFR cannot support S6K1 activation is contradicted while the overall coupling idea remains only partly addressed.

hypotheses.statement: Rapamycin activates ERK2, increasing its MEK-dependent activation and its kinase activity toward ERK2 substrates such as Raptor, through an EGFR/Src-to-Ras-Raf-MEK route.
hypotheses.mechanism: Rapamycin increases ERK1/2 phosphorylation in several cell types. This requires EGFR kinase activity and Src, and is blocked by dominant-negative Ras (N17) and by MEK1/2 inhibition. Independently, ERK2 activation depends on Ras: RasN17 abolishes residual ERK2 activity. Activated ERK2 phosphorylates Raptor in vitro, with no activity from unstimulated immunoprecipitates. Together, rapamycin should engage the Ras-MEK input that ERK2 specifically needs, raising ERK2's own catalytic activity rather than only total ERK1/2 phospho-signal.
hypotheses.prediction: In EGFR-expressing cells (e.g., SW13, COS7, or HEK293 transfected with EGFR), rapamycin treatment for 30 min to 2 h should increase phosphorylation of tagged ERK2 at its activation loop. It should also increase the in vitro kinase activity of immunoprecipitated ERK2 toward Raptor or GST-Elk1. This increase should be abolished by U0126, PP2 (but not PP3), AG1478, or RasN17.
hypotheses.test: Transfect HA-ERK2 into SW13 or COS7 cells, treat with rapamycin with or without U0126, PP2/PP3, or AG1478 (or co-express RasN17), and immunoprecipitate HA-ERK2. Then (1) immunoblot for activation-loop phosphorylation and (2) run an in vitro [γ-32P]ATP kinase assay on purified myc-Raptor or GST-Elk1. ERK2-specific siRNA knockdown can confirm that the rapamycin-induced substrate phosphorylation is carried by ERK2.

citations.title: Rapamycin induces transactivation of the EGFR and increases cell survival.
ERK1/2 phosphorylate Raptor to promote Ras-dependent activation of mTOR complex 1 (mTORC1).
Different patterns of Akt and ERK feedback activation in response to rapamycin, active-site mTOR inhibitors and metformin in pancreatic cancer cells.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the rapamycin→EGFR/Src→Ras-Raf-MEK-ERK feedback mechanism, the ERK–Raptor phosphorylation axis (Ser8/696/863), and the prediction that rapamycin raises ERK2 catalytic activity toward Raptor. The component steps are published separately — Chaturvedi et al. show rapamycin transactivates EGFR via c-Src to activate Erk1/2 and RSK in B82L/SW13/COS7 cells, and Carriere et al. show ERK1 and ERK2 bind and directly phosphorylate Raptor (including in vitro kinase assays on purified Raptor) to promote Ras-dependent mTORC1 activity — but no retrieved source joins them: Carriere et al. used rapamycin only as a pretreatment to silence mTORC1 and never tested whether rapamycin increases ERK2 activation-loop phosphorylation or ERK2 kinase activity toward Raptor, nor its dependence on U0126/PP2/AG1478/RasN17. One retrieved paper reports a negative for the upstream premise in a different setting (rapamycin at 10 or 100 nM did not alter basal or stimulated ERK phosphorylation in pancreatic cancer cells, unlike active-site mTOR inhibitors), but this is a different cell context and does not test the ERK2-toward-Raptor claim, so it is the nearest contrary work rather than a refutation.

hypotheses.statement: PKA activity negatively regulates TSC2 protein stability by accelerating its proteasomal degradation.
hypotheses.mechanism: Raising cAMP to activate PKA phosphorylates the 19S proteasome subunit Rpn6, which speeds hydrolysis of Ub conjugates and selectively enhances breakdown of short-lived proteins (collins2017:findings:026). TSC2 is ubiquitinated by DDB1-CUL4-FBW5, has a half-life of about 2 h, and is stabilized when this ligase is silenced (hu2008:findings:008, hu2008:findings:010). TSC2 is therefore a short-lived ubiquitinated substrate of the kind PKA-activated proteasomes degrade faster. The effect would act through the proteasome rather than through PKA modifying TSC2 itself, and whether a 2 h half-life counts as 'short-lived' in the collins2017 sense still needs to be confirmed.
hypotheses.prediction: Forskolin or a cell-permeable cAMP analog should shorten TSC2 half-life and lower steady-state TSC2 protein. Blocking PKA (PKI or H89) or blocking the proteasome should prevent this. The effect should be weaker when FBW5/CUL4 is silenced, because less TSC2 would be ubiquitinated.
hypotheses.test: Treat cultured mouse fibroblasts (or U2OS cells) with forskolin or 8-Br-cAMP, with and without PKI/H89 or MG132, and measure TSC2 half-life by cycloheximide chase and immunoblot. Repeat after siRNA knockdown of FBW5 or CUL4, and measure TSC2 ubiquitination by IP-Western.

citations.title: cAMP-induced phosphorylation of 26S proteasomes on Rpn6/PSMD11 enhances their activity and the degradation of misfolded proteins
GPCR signaling inhibits mTORC1 via PKA phosphorylation of Raptor.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: PKA/cAMP regulation of TSC2 (tuberin) protein stability and degradation; the Rpn6/PSMD11 proteasome-activation mechanism and which substrates it accelerates; and the specific prediction (forskolin/8-Br-cAMP shortening TSC2 half-life, cycloheximide chase, FBW5/CUL4-dependence), including a targeted PubMed query combining cAMP/PKA/forskolin with TSC2 and degradation/stability/proteasome. The cAMP-PKA-Rpn6 proteasome-activation mechanism is well published (misfolded and short-lived regulatory proteins, tau/SOD1/TDP43/FUS), and TSC2 stability is known to be controlled by ubiquitination and by Akt/PRMT1-type modifications, but no source states that PKA activation destabilizes TSC2 or tests TSC2 half-life under cAMP elevation. The nearest directly relevant work shows PKA inhibits mTORC1 by phosphorylating Raptor, acts independently of the TSC complex, and reports that short-term forskolin did not change protein levels of mTORC1 components/regulators — relevant context but not a test of TSC2 turnover, so no refutation either.

hypotheses.statement: Insulin stimulation directly increases B-Raf activation, specifically raising B-Raf–MEK1 complex formation and B-Raf-dependent MEK phosphorylation, so that B-Raf is a required node for insulin's amplification of growth-factor ERK signalling.
hypotheses.mechanism: In HEK293 cells insulin alone is a poor ERK activator yet amplifies low-dose EGF responses, and this amplification is lost on PI3K inhibition and maps upstream of Ras and at the Ras/Raf level, with Raf inhibition abolishing MEK/ERK activity (borisov2009:findings:009, borisov2009:findings:013, borisov2009:findings:000). Independently, in wild-type-BRAF settings RAF engagement of MEK is Ras-GTP-dependent and measurable as RAF–MEK1 complexes that form and dissolve with pathway state (lito2014:findings:008), and B-Raf activity is gated by Ras binding and dimer formation (lake2016:findings:011, lake2016:findings:020). If insulin's crosstalk acts at the Ras/Raf step, the Ras-responsive kinase whose MEK-loading is modulated should include B-Raf itself, not only c-Raf.
hypotheses.prediction: Insulin co-stimulation with a low EGF dose should increase B-Raf-associated MEK1 and B-Raf catalytic activity above EGF alone in a wortmannin-sensitive manner, and BRAF knockdown should selectively blunt the insulin-dependent increment of phospho-MEK/phospho-ERK while leaving the EGF-alone response relatively intact.
hypotheses.test: In HEK293 cells, stimulate with 0.1 nM EGF, 100 nM insulin, or both (± 100 nM wortmannin), then co-immunoprecipitate endogenous B-Raf and blot for MEK1 and for Ras, and assay immunoprecipitated B-Raf kinase activity on recombinant kinase-dead MEK1 in vitro; in parallel, compare siBRAF, siRAF1 and control siRNA cells for the insulin-dependent increment in phospho-MEK and phospho-ERK by immunoblot. Loss of an insulin-driven gain in B-Raf–MEK1 association and B-Raf activity, together with no selective effect of BRAF depletion on the insulin increment, would rule out the relationship.

citations.title: Insulin enhances growth hormone induction of the MEK/ERK signaling pathway.
Insulin potentiates EGFR activation and signaling in fibroblasts.
B-raf and insulin synergistically prevent apoptosis and induce cell cycle progression in hematopoietic cells.
Insulin activates a novel adipocyte mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase kinase that shows rapid phasic kinetics and is distinct from c-Raf.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: insulin-driven B-Raf activation and B-Raf–MEK1 complex formation; insulin–EGF (and insulin–GH) crosstalk amplifying ERK at the Ras/Raf level; and isoform-resolved comparisons of insulin effects on Raf-1 versus B-Raf, using Google/Bing-style search plus Europe PMC title and full-text queries (including a title scan of the entire 'insulin + Raf' literature). The insulin-activated Raf literature is essentially all Raf-1/c-Raf (e.g. insulin activates Raf-1 kinase; an insulin-stimulated adipocyte MEK kinase explicitly distinct from c-Raf), insulin is documented to potentiate EGFR-proximal signalling and ERK output, and insulin is documented to sensitise GH-induced MEK/ERK signalling — but the latter was mapped to MEK1/2 membrane translocation and KSR association and reported as independent of Ras and Raf-1, with no isoform-resolved test of B-Raf. I found no source stating that insulin raises B-Raf activity or B-Raf–MEK1 complexes or that BRAF is required for insulin's amplification of EGF-induced ERK, and no source reporting a direct negative test of that specific claim, so the status is open with the nearest published work cited.

hypotheses.statement: ERK2 directly activates MTORC1 by phosphorylating the mTORC1 subunit Raptor at pS/T-P sites.
hypotheses.mechanism: Claims from carriere2010 show ERK2 physically associates with Raptor and that ERK1/2 knockdown abolishes PMA-stimulated Raptor pS/T-P phosphorylation, with immunoprecipitated active ERK2 phosphorylating purified Raptor in vitro. Independently, claims about mTORC1 show that Raptor phosphorylation state controls mTOR kinase activity: the phospho-deficient Raptor S3A mutant supports less mTOR activity toward 4E-BP1 without altering complex assembly, and MEK1/2 inhibition blocks mTORC1 activity. Together these imply ERK2 acts directly on the mTORC1 holoenzyme to raise its phosphotransferase activity rather than through an intermediate kinase.
hypotheses.prediction: Acute ERK2 inhibition or ERK2-specific knockdown should lower Raptor pS/T-P phosphorylation and reduce mTORC1 kinase activity toward 4E-BP1/S6K1, while Raptor S3A-expressing cells should be refractory to ERK2 gain-of-function (constitutively active MEK/ERK2) stimulation of mTORC1.
hypotheses.test: In HEK293 cells, reconstitute Raptor-knockdown cells with wild-type or S3A Raptor, express active ERK2 or treat with PMA with/without ERK-selective inhibitor, then immunoprecipitate Raptor-mTOR complexes and assay in vitro mTOR kinase activity on GST-4E-BP1 plus immunoblot Raptor pS/T-P; in parallel perform an in vitro kinase assay with recombinant active ERK2 and purified wild-type versus S3A Raptor to confirm direct, site-specific phosphorylation.

citations.title: ERK1/2 phosphorylate Raptor to promote Ras-dependent activation of mTOR complex 1 (mTORC1).
Regulation of mTOR complex 1 (mTORC1) by raptor Ser863 and multisite phosphorylation.

novelty.note: Searched for ERK1/2–Raptor phosphorylation, proline-directed (S/T-P) Raptor sites with mTORC1 activity toward 4E-BP1, and the prediction that phospho-deficient Raptor blunts MEK/ERK-driven mTORC1 activation. The corpus's own source paper is published (JBC 2011, PMID 21071439): it reports ERK1/2 association with Raptor, direct in vitro phosphorylation, identification of Ser8/Ser696/Ser863 as ERK1/2 sites, and reduced mTORC1 signaling to 4E-BP1 with phospho-deficient Raptor — i.e., the stated explanation in full. A related independent study establishes that multisite Raptor phosphorylation (including Ser863) controls mTORC1 kinase activity toward 4E-BP1, supporting the downstream half of the mechanism.

hypotheses.statement: EGFR kinase activity positively regulates growth-factor-stimulated global protein synthesis (protein biosynthetic process) through its required role in ERK pathway activation.
hypotheses.mechanism: Two independent claims show that ERK pathway output depends on EGFR. The FIRE ERK reporter decays when EGFR is inhibited (albeck2013), and the EGFR kinase inhibitor AG1478 abolishes Erk1/2 and RSK activation (chaturvedi2009). Separately, inhibiting MEK1/2 blocks growth-factor-stimulated global protein synthesis (carriere2010). Together these imply that EGFR kinase activity is needed for the growth-factor-induced rise in protein synthesis, via the MEK/ERK arm.
hypotheses.prediction: In EGF-stimulated cells, global protein synthesis should increase over baseline. Blocking EGFR kinase (AG1478, or the kinase-dead K721M mutant) should abolish that increase to the same degree as MEK1/2 inhibition. Blocking EGFR should not reduce protein synthesis further in cells already treated with a MEK inhibitor.
hypotheses.test: Measure nascent protein synthesis by puromycin incorporation (SUnSET immunoblot) or [35S]-methionine labeling in serum-starved cultured cells (e.g. MCF-10A or HEK293). Compare EGF stimulation alone, EGF plus AG1478, EGF plus a MEK1/2 inhibitor, and both inhibitors combined, with cycloheximide as a negative control. In parallel, compare B82L cells expressing wild-type versus K721M EGFR, and immunoblot phospho-ERK to confirm pathway inhibition.

citations.title: EGF receptor transactivation is obligatory for protein synthesis stimulation by G protein-coupled receptors.
Inhibition of growth factor-induced protein synthesis by a selective MEK inhibitor in aortic smooth muscle cells.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the mechanism in words (EGFR kinase → ERK → global protein synthesis), the entities together (AG1478, MEK inhibitor, EGF, translation rate), and the prediction (EGFR-blockade abolishing growth-factor-stimulated translation measured by labeling/puromycin). Voisin et al. (PMID 12107054) state and test the same explanation, showing that pharmacological EGFR blockade (AG-1478, half-maximal at ~12 nM) strongly attenuates agonist-stimulated global protein synthesis in vascular smooth muscle in vitro and in vivo, with reduced ERK and PI3K/eIF4E–4E-BP1 signaling; Servant et al. (PMID 8663242) independently establish that MEK/ERK activation is an obligatory step for growth-factor-induced protein synthesis, including ligands of receptor tyrosine kinases. However, the published EGFR requirement is for receptor transactivation by GPCR agonists rather than direct EGF stimulation, and I found no source testing the specific epistasis prediction (EGFR inhibitor or kinase-dead K721M EGFR producing the same, non-additive block as MEK1/2 inhibition in EGF-stimulated cells), so the general mechanism is published but this specific prediction is not.

hypotheses.statement: PI3K kinase activity positively regulates (promotes) basal endocytosis of the TGF-β receptor TβRII from the cell surface.
hypotheses.mechanism: Inhibiting PI3K with GDC0941 increased cell-surface TβRI and TβRII abundance in unstimulated NMuMG cells and MEFs (budi2015:findings:006). Separately, TβRII surface stability is set by how much it is ubiquitylated and taken up by lipid raft-mediated endocytosis (hata2016:findings:006). Together these suggest the surface gain after PI3K inhibition reflects reduced TβRII endocytosis, which would mean basal PI3K activity drives TβRII internalization.
hypotheses.prediction: In NMuMG cells without insulin, PI3K inhibition (GDC0941) or PI3K catalytic-subunit knockdown should lower the rate of TβRII internalization from the plasma membrane. TβRII delivery to the surface should change much less, and TβRII ubiquitylation should fall.
hypotheses.test: Run a surface-biotinylation internalization assay in NMuMG cells pretreated with GDC0941, vehicle, or PI3K siRNA. Label surface proteins with cleavable biotin, allow internalization at 37 °C for set times, and strip the remaining surface biotin with MesNa. Quantify protected (internalized) TβRII by streptavidin pulldown and immunoblot. In parallel, measure delivery to the surface with a recycling/biotinylation chase and measure TβRII ubiquitylation by immunoprecipitation. A slower internalization rate with GDC0941 or knockdown would support the hypothesis; an unchanged rate would rule it out.

citations.title: TGFβ receptor endocytosis and Smad signaling require synaptojanin1, PI3K-C2α-, and INPP4B-mediated phosphoinositide conversions.
The insulin response integrates increased TGF-β signaling through Akt-induced enhancement of cell surface delivery of TGF-β receptors.
FAF1 phosphorylation by AKT accumulates TGF-β type II receptor and drives breast cancer metastasis.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the mechanism in words (PI3K/Akt controlling TβRII surface levels via endocytosis vs. delivery), the entities together (GDC-0941, TβRII, surface biotinylation, internalization), and the prediction (PI3K inhibition slowing TβRII internalization/ubiquitylation). Published work establishes that a PI3K — the class II isoform PI3K-C2α, acting through phosphoinositide conversions with synaptojanin1 and INPP4B — is required for TGFβ-induced TGFβ-receptor endocytosis, which anticipates the general 'PI3K activity promotes TβR internalization' mechanism, but that study concerns ligand-induced, ALK5-dependent uptake rather than basal endocytosis and does not involve class I PI3K inhibitors such as GDC0941. The source paper itself attributes the Akt-dependent change in surface TβRI/TβRII to AS160-dependent delivery from intracellular stores, and the AKT–FAF1 work attributes surface TβRII gains to reduced ubiquitylation/lysosomal turnover rather than altered endocytic uptake; no source was found that tested, in unstimulated cells, whether class I PI3K inhibition slows TβRII internalization, and none reported a negative result for it.

hypotheses.statement: TCR engagement activates mTOR (mTORC1) kinase activity through MEK/ERK-dependent phosphorylation of Raptor.
hypotheses.mechanism: The C evidence states that T cell activation induces MEK1/2-dependent ERK1/2 activity, which phosphorylates LAT T155 (lake2016:findings:005). The A evidence states that Ras/MAPK activation drives ERK1/2-dependent phosphorylation of Raptor at Ser696/Ser863. This phosphorylation is abolished by MEK inhibition but not by mTOR inhibitors, and it raises mTORC1 kinase activity toward 4E-BP1, which MEK inhibitors fully block (carriere2010:findings:011, carriere2010:findings:015). RSK-mediated Raptor phosphorylation is also needed for PMA-stimulated mTORC1 activation (carrire2008:findings:010). Together these suggest that the ERK output of TCR signaling feeds directly into mTORC1 activation through Raptor.
hypotheses.prediction: Anti-CD3/TCR crosslinking of T cells should increase Raptor Ser696/Ser863 phosphorylation and mTORC1 activity, seen as 4E-BP1 Thr37/46 phosphorylation and in vitro mTOR kinase activity toward GST-4E-BP1. A MEK1/2 inhibitor should block both effects, as should expressing the phosphorylation-deficient Raptor S3A mutant, whereas rapamycin should not prevent the Raptor phosphorylation itself.
hypotheses.test: Stimulate a T cell line (a murine T cell line, or Jurkat cells) with plate-bound anti-CD3 antibody, with or without the MEK1/2 inhibitor PD184352 or rapamycin. Do this in cells expressing wild-type or S3A Raptor. Measure Raptor Ser696/Ser863, phospho-ERK and 4E-BP1 Thr37/46 by immunoblot. Then immunoprecipitate mTOR and run an in vitro kinase assay with GST-4E-BP1 as the substrate.

citations.title: ERK1/2 phosphorylate Raptor to promote Ras-dependent activation of mTOR complex 1 (mTORC1).
Negative regulation of mTOR activation by diacylglycerol kinases.
mTOR and other effector kinase signals that impact T cell function and activity.

novelty.note: I searched for ERK-dependent Raptor Ser696/Ser863 phosphorylation, for MEK/ERK-dependent mTORC1 activation after anti-CD3/TCR stimulation, and for Raptor phosphorylation in T cells/thymocytes. The general mechanism is published: Carrière et al. (JBC 2010) show ERK1/2 phosphorylate Raptor at Ser8/696/863 in a PD184352-sensitive, rapamycin-insensitive manner and that the S3A mutant lowers mTORC1 activity toward 4E-BP1, but that work used HEK293/U2OS/HeLa cells with PMA/EGF/insulin and no TCR stimulus. In T cells, the nearest work (Gorentla et al., Blood 2011) places RasGRP1–Ras–ERK1/2 (and Rsk1) upstream of TCR-induced S6K1/4E-BP1 phosphorylation, and reviews attribute this to TSC2 rather than Raptor; I found no source reporting TCR-induced Raptor Ser696/Ser863 phosphorylation or testing Raptor S3A in T cells, and no negative test of it, hence partial.

hypotheses.statement: Wortmannin directly inhibits insulin-stimulated activation of RPS6KB1 (S6K1), reducing its Thr389 phosphorylation and S6 kinase activity in intact cells.
hypotheses.mechanism: The S6K1 evidence places its insulin-stimulated Thr389 phosphorylation downstream of Akt acting on the TSC1–TSC2 complex, since TSC1–TSC2 inhibits basal and insulin-stimulated S6K activity and Akt-site mutations in TSC2 tune that inhibition (inoki2002:findings:003, inoki2002:findings:011), and TSC2 knockdown raises insulin-stimulated S6K phosphorylation (inoki2002:findings:004). The wortmannin evidence shows that 100 nM wortmannin prevents insulin- and EGF-induced AKT phosphorylation without affecting receptor tyrosine phosphorylation (borisov2009:findings:009), and that wortmannin similarly blocks insulin- and IGF-driven PI3K-dependent phosphorylation events (fang2000:findings:003). Removing the Akt input that normally relieves TSC1–TSC2 inhibition should therefore collapse S6K1 activation, so wortmannin is predicted to act as a negative regulator of S6K1 in cells.
hypotheses.prediction: Wortmannin pretreatment of serum-starved cells should abolish insulin-induced S6K1 Thr389 phosphorylation and GST–S6 kinase activity with the same concentration dependence and kinetics as its block of AKT Ser473 phosphorylation; the block should be relieved in cells depleted of TSC2, and a rapamycin-resistant S6K1 truncation that escapes TSC1–TSC2 control should remain partly active in wortmannin.
hypotheses.test: Serum-starve HEK293 cells expressing HA–S6K1, pretreat with a wortmannin dose series (0–200 nM) or vehicle, stimulate with insulin, then immunoblot phospho-S6K1 Thr389 and phospho-AKT Ser473 and assay anti-HA immunoprecipitate kinase activity on GST–S6; repeat in cells transfected with TSC2 siRNA and in cells expressing the rapamycin-resistant S6K-dNC mutant to test whether loss of the TSC1–TSC2 node or of S6K1 regulatory regions renders S6K1 wortmannin-insensitive.

citations.title: PDGF- and insulin-dependent pp70S6k activation mediated by phosphatidylinositol-3-OH kinase.
Selective inhibition of p70 S6 kinase activation by phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase inhibitors.
Regulation of the p70 S6 kinase by phosphorylation in vivo. Analysis using site-specific anti-phosphopeptide antibodies.

novelty.note: I searched for wortmannin plus insulin-stimulated p70 S6 kinase/Thr389 phosphorylation, for PI 3-kinase inhibitor dependence of S6K activation by insulin and PDGF, and for site-specific analyses of S6K1 hydrophobic-motif phosphorylation in intact cells. Mid-1990s primary work already reported that wortmannin (and LY294002/demethoxyviridin) blocks insulin- and PDGF-stimulated phosphorylation and activation of p70 S6 kinase in cells without affecting p90rsk/MAPK, and Weng et al. showed with phospho-specific antibodies that loss of S6K activity on wortmannin addition tracks the disappearance of hydrophobic-motif (Thr-412/Thr389) phosphorylation while Thr-252 and Ser-434 phosphorylation persist. The core claim — wortmannin suppresses insulin-stimulated S6K1 Thr389 phosphorylation and S6 kinase activity in intact cells — is therefore long established; only the auxiliary TSC2-knockdown/rapamycin-resistant-truncation epistasis refinements go beyond these reports.

hypotheses.statement: SRC kinase activity is required for the increased cell adhesion and invasive behaviour acquired during TGF-β-induced EMT, i.e. SRC acts as a positive effector of the EMT program's motility output.
hypotheses.mechanism: Cells undergoing TGF-β-induced EMT acquire both increased substratum adhesion and strongly increased Matrigel invasion (lamouille2007:findings:021, lamouille2007:findings:022), phenotypes that depend on focal-adhesion remodelling; independently, SRC is shown to drive focal-adhesion signalling directly, since disruption of the FAK–SRC complex reduces focal-adhesion signalling markers, contractility and stiffness, and zyxin/VASP trafficking is SRC-dependent (brozovich2016:findings:088, brozovich2016:findings:084). SRC also feeds the EGFR-Y845→ERK/RSK axis, since PP2 or dasatinib abolishes EGFR Y845 and downstream ERK/RSK phosphorylation (chaturvedi2009:findings:013), providing a second route by which SRC could support the adhesive/invasive arm of EMT.
hypotheses.prediction: Pharmacological or genetic inactivation of SRC in TGF-β-treated epithelial cells (e.g. NMuMG) should abolish the EMT-associated gains in adhesion and Matrigel invasion, and reduce phospho-tyrosine focal-adhesion markers, while TGF-β-driven cadherin/vimentin marker switching may be only partially affected; conversely, expression of constitutively active SRC should raise basal adhesion/invasion and sensitise cells to TGF-β-induced invasion.
hypotheses.test: Treat NMuMG (or similar) epithelial cells with TGF-β ± PP2 (with PP3 as the inactive-analog control) or dasatinib, and in parallel with SRC siRNA versus control siRNA, then score (i) reseeding adhesion assay, (ii) Matrigel transwell invasion with DAPI nuclear counting, and (iii) immunoblots for phospho-SRC Y416/Y527, FAK phospho-tyrosine, E-/N-cadherin and vimentin; a reciprocal arm expressing constitutively active SRC tests gain-of-function. Loss of the TGF-β-dependent adhesion and invasion increments upon SRC inhibition/knockdown, with their restoration or enhancement by active SRC, supports the relationship, whereas unchanged adhesion and invasion rule it out.

citations.title: A TGF-β-responsive enhancer regulates SRC expression and epithelial-mesenchymal transition-associated cell migration.

novelty.note: I searched for Src requirement in TGF-β-induced EMT invasion in NMuMG cells, for PP2/dasatinib blockade of TGF-β-driven migration/invasion, and for SRC–FAK coupling to the EMT motility program. A retrieved 2023 Journal of Cell Science study reports that TGF-β transcriptionally upregulates SRC via an intragenic enhancer and that this SRC activity is required for TGF-β-induced cell migration and FAK phosphorylation (dasatinib and enhancer-mutant cells both suppress motility), while E-cadherin repression and vimentin induction still occur without functional SRC — the same explanation and the same marker/motility dissociation stated in the hypothesis. Status is established on that basis; note that older work (Maeda et al., JBC 2006, not retrievable here) argued Src activation is dispensable for the TGF-β EMT transition itself and that PP1/PP2 act directly on the TGF-β receptors, which is a caveat for the proposed PP2 arm of the test rather than a refutation of the motility claim.

hypotheses.statement: SRC directly tyrosine-phosphorylates and activates STAT proteins, and so is required for EGF-induced STAT activation that does not depend on Jak1.
hypotheses.mechanism: In NCI-H292 cells, c-Src associates directly with STAT1, and STAT1 is tyrosine-phosphorylated within that complex; the association rises on stimulation and is blocked by the Src inhibitor PP2 (chang2004:findings:003). Separately, EGF activates STAT DNA binding without Jak1 but needs EGF receptor kinase activity (david1996:findings:000, david1996:findings:001). In EGF signaling, Src depletion reduces phosphorylation of a downstream substrate (GAB1) but leaves EGFR autophosphorylation intact (borisov2009:findings:011). Together these suggest Src could act downstream of the active EGFR as the kinase that phosphorylates STAT, in place of Jak1.
hypotheses.prediction: Recombinant active SRC should phosphorylate purified STAT on tyrosine in vitro. In cells, Src knockdown or PP2 (but not PP3) should reduce EGF-induced STAT tyrosine phosphorylation and SIE-complex formation, while EGFR autophosphorylation and IFN-gamma-induced STAT activation stay unaffected.
hypotheses.test: Run an in vitro kinase assay with recombinant active versus kinase-dead SRC and purified STAT1/STAT3, read out by anti-pTyr-STAT immunoblot. In parallel, treat wild-type and Jak1-deficient HeLa cells with Src siRNA or PP2/PP3, stimulate with EGF (and IFN-gamma as a control), and measure STAT tyrosine phosphorylation by immunoblot, SIE binding by EMSA, and EGFR autophosphorylation as a control.

citations.title: ErbB receptor-induced activation of stat transcription factors is mediated by Src tyrosine kinases.
Activation and association of Stat3 with Src in v-Src-transformed cell lines.
Activation of Stat3 in v-Src-transformed fibroblasts requires cooperation of Jak1 kinase activity.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: direct Src-mediated tyrosine phosphorylation of STAT proteins, EGF/ErbB-induced STAT activation that is Jak-independent, and PP2/Src-knockdown effects on EGF-induced STAT phosphorylation. Olayioye et al. (JBC 1999) state exactly this explanation — STATs associate with ErbB receptors, c-Src is recruited on stimulation, and EGF-induced Stat activation is dependent on Src but not Jak kinases — while Cao et al. (MCB 1996) show Src associates with and phosphorylates Stat3 in vitro, and Zhang et al. (2000) show recombinant Src tyrosine-phosphorylates Stat1 and Stat3 (though they argue Jak1 additionally acts as a scaffold in v-Src-transformed fibroblasts). Since published primary work asserts both the direct Src→STAT phosphorylation step and the Src requirement for Jak-independent EGF-induced STAT activation, the explanation is established rather than open; no source was found that tested and refuted it.

hypotheses.statement: NGF activates PI3K, measured as wortmannin-sensitive AKT phosphorylation, when NGF signals through a receptor carrying the EGFR intracellular region (the TrkA/EGFR TEE chimera).
hypotheses.mechanism: In MCF7(EGFR-KO) cells, NGF binding to the TEE chimera produces sustained phosphorylation of the EGFR intracellular region and sustained ERK activation (kiyatkin2020:findings:009). In HEK293 cells, EGF-induced AKT phosphorylation is blocked by the PI3K inhibitor wortmannin, while EGFR tyrosine phosphorylation is not (borisov2009:findings:009). Together these imply that an NGF-activated EGFR intracellular region should engage PI3K. Under persistent EGF, PI3K/AKT activation is transient because of negative feedback from ERK, AKT and mTOR (borisov2009:findings:008), so it is an open question whether sustained receptor phosphorylation driven by NGF carries through to sustained PI3K output.
hypotheses.prediction: NGF stimulation of TEE-expressing MCF7(EGFR-KO) cells should increase phospho-AKT, and wortmannin or LY294002 pretreatment should abolish this increase without reducing phosphorylation of the chimera's EGFR intracellular region. NGF should have no such effect in parental cells lacking the chimera.
hypotheses.test: Treat parental and TEE-expressing MCF7(EGFR-KO) cells with NGF over a time course (minutes to hours), with and without pretreatment with wortmannin (100 nM) or LY294002. Immunoblot for phospho-AKT, total AKT, phospho-EGFR (intracellular region) and phospho-ERK1/2. Optionally, co-immunoprecipitate the chimera and probe for the PI3K p85 subunit.

citations.title: Kinetics of receptor tyrosine kinase activation define ERK signaling dynamics.
A dominant role of the juxtamembrane region of the TrkA nerve growth factor receptor during neuronal cell differentiation.

novelty.note: I searched for the TrkA/EGFR (TEE) chimera work itself, for chimeric receptors with heterologous ectodomains fused to the EGFR intracellular region coupled to PI3K/AKT, and for NGF-driven, wortmannin-sensitive AKT phosphorylation through an EGFR cytoplasmic domain. The source paper for the TEE chimera (Kiyatkin et al.) reports sustained chimera phosphorylation and sustained ERK upon NGF but, on reading it, contains no AKT/PI3K measurements and no wortmannin or LY294002 experiments; the closest related published work is an EGFR chimera carrying the TrkA juxtamembrane region, which raised PI3-kinase activity in response to EGF (not NGF) in PC12 cells. No source states that NGF acting through an EGFR intracellular region produces wortmannin-sensitive AKT phosphorylation, and none reports a negative test of it, so the claim is open.

hypotheses.statement: The MEK1/2 inhibitor 2-(2-amino-3-methoxyphenyl)chromen-4-one indirectly suppresses mTOR kinase activity by blocking ERK1/2-dependent Raptor phosphorylation, i.e. the compound negatively regulates mTORC1 output.
hypotheses.mechanism: Claims about the compound show it blocks MEK-dependent ERK1/2 activation in several cell types (waters1995:findings:003, li2000:findings:004), and it is characterized as a non-ATP-competitive MEK1/2-selective inhibitor that does not touch other kinases (waters1995:findings:002). Independently, claims about mTOR show that Ras/MAPK-driven Raptor Ser696/Ser863 phosphorylation is ERK1/2-mediated and abolished by MEK1/2 inhibition, and that loss of these sites lowers mTOR kinase activity toward 4E-BP1 (carriere2010:findings:011, carriere2010:findings:015). Together these imply the compound should reduce mTOR activity specifically under MAPK-driven stimulation rather than by acting on mTOR directly.
hypotheses.prediction: In growth-factor- or PMA-stimulated cells, pretreatment with the compound should abolish Raptor Ser696/Ser863 phosphorylation and lower mTOR-dependent 4E-BP1 Thr37/46 and S6K1 Thr389 phosphorylation, while mTOR immunoprecipitated from compound-treated cells and assayed in vitro with excess ATP retains intrinsic catalytic activity (no direct inhibition).
hypotheses.test: Treat HEK293 cells expressing myc-Raptor and mTOR with the compound before PMA/serum stimulation; immunoblot phospho-Raptor Ser696/Ser863, phospho-4E-BP1 Thr37/46 and phospho-S6K1 Thr389, then immunoprecipitate mTOR and run an in vitro kinase assay on GST-4E-BP1 both from treated cells and with the compound added directly to the reaction, to separate an indirect MEK/ERK-routed effect from direct mTOR inhibition.

citations.title: The identification of raptor as a substrate for p44/42 MAPK.
ERK1/2 phosphorylate Raptor to promote Ras-dependent activation of mTOR complex 1 (mTORC1).

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the mechanism in words (MEK inhibition suppressing mTORC1 indirectly via ERK-dependent Raptor phosphorylation), the entities together (ERK1/2 + Raptor Ser696/Ser863 + MEK inhibitor + 4E-BP1/S6K1), and the prediction (this specific chromenone MEK inhibitor lowering S6K1 Thr389 / 4E-BP1 Thr37/46). Langlais et al. (Endocrinology 2011) explicitly report that this compound blocks insulin-stimulated Raptor Ser696 phosphorylation by p42 MAPK while rapamycin does not, and that loss of Ser696 impairs downstream p70S6K signaling, i.e. MEK/ERK-routed control of mTORC1 rather than direct mTOR inhibition; Carriere et al. (JBC 2010) establish the same ERK1/2-Raptor-mTORC1 axis with MEK1/2 inhibitors and 4E-BP1 readout. The indirect, non-mTOR-targeting explanation is therefore already published, so the status is established; only the ancillary control of in vitro mTOR catalytic activity with the compound added directly was not found.

hypotheses.statement: SRC directly tyrosine-phosphorylates TSC2, inhibiting TSC2's GAP activity toward Rheb in a manner parallel to the serine phosphorylation already attributed to ERK and RSK.
hypotheses.mechanism: TSC2 is described as an integration point whose GAP activity is switched off by direct phosphorylation from several upstream kinases, including RSK at Ser1798 and ERK at Ser664, with further direct sites from MK2 and Akt (cargnello2011:findings:035, dibble2009:findings:019). SRC is a highly promiscuous tyrosine kinase that generates over 2000 phosphosites when expressed in a heterologous system (bradley2024:findings:002), and SRC activity is required upstream of the ERK/RSK arm that targets TSC2 (chaturvedi2009:findings:013, cargnello2011:findings:059), placing active SRC in the same signaling compartment as TSC2. Together these imply TSC2 is a plausible direct SRC substrate whose tyrosine phosphorylation would reinforce the same inactivating effect on Rheb-directed GAP activity.
hypotheses.prediction: Recombinant SRC should phosphorylate purified TSC2 on tyrosine in vitro, SRC activation in cells should increase TSC2 phosphotyrosine content and decrease TSC2-dependent Rheb GTP hydrolysis, and phospho-site mutation of the SRC-targeted tyrosine(s) should make TSC2 GAP activity insensitive to SRC activation while leaving ERK/RSK serine sites intact.
hypotheses.test: Perform an in vitro kinase assay with purified recombinant SRC kinase domain and immunopurified TSC2 (with the TSC1-TSC2 complex) using kinase-dead SRC as control, detect incorporation by anti-phosphotyrosine (4G10) blotting and map sites by LC-MS/MS; in parallel, treat cultured cells with the SRC inhibitor PP2 versus the inactive analog PP3, immunoprecipitate TSC2, blot for phosphotyrosine, and assay Rheb GTP loading, then repeat with tyrosine-to-phenylalanine TSC2 mutants at the mapped sites to confirm loss of SRC-dependent GAP inhibition.

citations.title: Tuberin phosphorylation regulates its interaction with hamartin. Two proteins involved in tuberous sclerosis.
Src regulates amino acid-mediated mTORC1 activation by disrupting GATOR1-Rag GTPase interaction.

novelty.note: I searched for Src-mediated tyrosine phosphorylation of TSC2/tuberin, for TSC2 tyrosine phosphosites and kinases generally, and for Src/PP2/dasatinib effects on mTORC1 via TSC2-Rheb. Tyrosine phosphorylation of tuberin with a functional consequence is published (Aicher et al., pervanadate-induced tyrosine phosphorylation, disease mutant Y1571H abolishing it and weakening TSC1-TSC2 binding), but no source attributes any TSC2 tyrosine site to SRC or reports SRC-dependent inhibition of TSC2 GAP activity toward Rheb. The nearest direct test of SRC upstream of mTORC1 concluded that Src-dependent amino-acid regulation of mTORC1 is independent of TSC2 and operates through GATOR1-Rag, which weighs against the proposed route without directly testing SRC phosphorylation of TSC2 or Rheb GAP activity; hence partial rather than established or refuted.

hypotheses.statement: TGF-β directly suppresses activation (tyrosine phosphorylation) of JAK2, acting as a negative upstream regulator of the JAK2 kinase itself.
hypotheses.mechanism: The TGF-β evidence shows that adding TGF-β to pancreatic stellate cells blocks JAK/STAT activation and reduces expression of the upstream cytokine receptor IL1R1, indicating TGF-β can shut down JAK-dependent signaling at or above the level of the kinase (biffi2018:findings:015). The JAK2 evidence shows JAK2 activation is read out as cytokine-induced tyrosine phosphorylation downstream of receptor engagement, e.g. IFN-γ specifically induces phosphorylation of Jak1 and Jak2, and JAK2 association with receptor chains is required for that signal (darnell1994:findings:019, heinrich2003:findings:022). Together these imply that the TGF-β-imposed block on JAK/STAT output should be measurable as loss of JAK2 phosphorylation/activation rather than only as a downstream transcriptional effect.
hypotheses.prediction: Pretreatment with TGF-β should reduce cytokine-induced phospho-JAK2 (and downstream phospho-STAT) in a dose- and TGF-β-receptor-dependent manner, without requiring loss of JAK2 protein; the suppression should be reversible by TGF-β neutralization or type I receptor kinase inhibition, and should be accompanied by reduced JAK2-associated receptor surface levels.
hypotheses.test: Treat a JAK2-dependent responsive cell line (e.g. cells signaling through gp130/OSMR or IFN-γ receptor) with TGF-β for 0–24 h, then stimulate with the JAK2-activating cytokine and immunoblot for phospho-JAK2 versus total JAK2 and phospho-STAT; include a neutralizing anti-TGF-β antibody and a TGF-β receptor kinase inhibitor as specificity controls, and co-immunoprecipitate JAK2 with its receptor chain to test whether the block occurs at kinase phosphorylation or at receptor association.

citations.title: TGF-beta inhibits IL-12-induced activation of Jak-STAT pathway in T lymphocytes.
TGF-beta1 suppresses IFN-gamma-induced NO production in macrophages by suppressing STAT1 activation and accelerating iNOS protein degradation.

novelty.note: I searched for TGF-β inhibition of JAK2 tyrosine phosphorylation, TGF-β effects on IFN-γ/JAK/STAT activation, and the cytokine-receptor-level mechanism. Bright et al. (PMID 9712043) directly report that TGF-β treatment of activated T cells blocks IL-12-induced tyrosine phosphorylation and activation of Jak-2 (and Tyk-2) with consequent loss of STAT3/STAT4 phosphorylation, which is the same explanation — TGF-β acting at or above the kinase. A related macrophage study (PMID 16866871) shows TGF-β1 suppressing IFN-γ-induced STAT1 tyrosine phosphorylation via IFN-γR/TGF-βRI association, indicating the receptor-proximal/cell-type-dependent variant of the mechanism rather than universal loss of JAK2 phosphorylation, so it is cited as the nearest qualifying work.

hypotheses.statement: PDK1 negatively regulates TSC2: PDK1 kinase activity is required for the inactivating phosphorylation of TSC2 at its AKT site (T1462) and its RSK site (S1798).
hypotheses.mechanism: PDK1 phosphorylates AKT at T308, which AKT needs to be active (manning2017:findings:005). Loss of PDK1 abolishes AKT activation-loop phosphorylation in murine cells (ikenoue2008:findings:006). PDK1 is also required for mitogenic activation of RSK1-3 (cargnello2011:findings:023). On the TSC2 side, AKT phosphorylates and inactivates TSC2 (haeusler2018:findings:027), and RSK phosphorylates TSC2 at Ser1798 to suppress its GAP activity toward Rheb (cargnello2011:findings:035). Together these claims imply that PDK1 controls TSC2's inhibitory phosphorylation, and so its activity, through two convergent routes. The evidence supports regulation that is mediated by these kinases, not direct phosphorylation of TSC2 by PDK1.
hypotheses.prediction: Insulin- or growth factor-stimulated TSC2 phosphorylation at T1462 and S1798 should be lost or strongly reduced in PDK1-null cells and restored by wild-type but not kinase-dead PDK1. Loss of these marks should come with higher TSC2 GAP activity, measured as lower Rheb-GTP. Recombinant PDK1 alone should not phosphorylate TSC2 in vitro, unless the relationship is direct.
hypotheses.test: Use PDK1-/- murine ES cells or MEFs reconstituted with wild-type or kinase-dead PDK1. Stimulate with insulin or EGF and immunoblot with phospho-specific antibodies for TSC2 pT1462/pS939 and pS1798, alongside AKT pT308 and RSK activation-loop phosphorylation. Measure Rheb-GTP loading. As a control, run an in vitro [gamma-32P]ATP kinase assay with recombinant PDK1 and immunopurified TSC2 to tell mediated regulation apart from direct phosphorylation.

citations.title: PDK1-SGK1 Signaling Sustains AKT-Independent mTORC1 Activation and Confers Resistance to PI3Kα Inhibition.
Tumor-promoting phorbol esters and activated Ras inactivate the tuberous sclerosis tumor suppressor complex via p90 ribosomal S6 kinase.
Characterization of GSK2334470, a novel and highly specific inhibitor of PDK1.

novelty.note: I searched for (a) PDK1 requirement for TSC2 Thr1462/Ser939 phosphorylation in PDK1-null or PDK1-inhibited cells, (b) the RSK–TSC2 Ser1798 link together with PDK1, and (c) PDK1 inhibitor effects on AKT/RSK T-loop sites and Rheb-GTP. Published work establishes each leg separately — PDK1 inhibition ablates T-loop phosphorylation and activation of AKT, RSK, S6K and SGK (Najafov et al.), RSK phosphorylates TSC2 at Ser1798 to inhibit its tumour-suppressor/GAP function (Roux et al.), and PDK1 blockade demonstrably lowers inhibitory TSC2 phosphorylation, though in that study via SGK1 rather than AKT or RSK (Castel et al.) — but I found no source reporting the specific prediction that growth-factor-stimulated TSC2 pT1462 and pS1798 are lost in PDK1-null cells, rescued by wild-type but not kinase-dead PDK1, with a corresponding drop in Rheb-GTP, nor any in vitro test of direct PDK1 phosphorylation of TSC2. Nothing tested and refuted the claim, so this is partial rather than established or open.

hypotheses.statement: Intracellular Ca2+ elevation activates mTORC1 through PKC–MAPK (ERK/RSK)-dependent phosphorylation of Raptor.
hypotheses.mechanism: Two claims tie Ca2+ to PKC and MAPK. In a network model, Ca2+ influx engages a PKC–MAPK feedback loop that keeps PKC and MAPK active after the Ca2+ signal ends (bhalla1999:findings:006). In PLCdelta1-deficient keratinocytes, impaired Ca2+ signaling comes with impaired PKC activation (balla2013:findings:052). Separately, the PKC activator PMA raises mTORC1 kinase activity through MEK/ERK- and RSK-dependent Raptor phosphorylation, and a phosphorylation-deficient Raptor mutant blunts this (carrire2008:findings:001, carrire2008:findings:010, carriere2010:findings:015). Taken together, Ca2+-driven PKC/MAPK activity should feed into the same Raptor phosphorylation route and raise mTORC1 activity.
hypotheses.prediction: Raising cytosolic Ca2+ (e.g. with ionomycin or thapsigargin) should increase Raptor phosphorylation on RSK/ERK motifs and increase mTORC1 activity, measured as 4E-BP1 Thr37/46 phosphorylation and in vitro mTOR kinase activity toward GST-4E-BP1. Both increases should be blocked by U0126 or BI-D1870, and strongly reduced in cells expressing the Raptor 3A/S3A mutant instead of wild-type Raptor. Ca2+ chelation with BAPTA-AM should not affect the mTORC1 response to insulin, which is independent of Raptor 3A.
hypotheses.test: In HEK293 cells co-transfected with mTOR and either wild-type or 3A Raptor, treat with ionomycin or thapsigargin, with or without BAPTA-AM, U0126 or BI-D1870. Then immunoprecipitate Raptor and blot with the RXRXXpS/T phospho-motif antibody, blot for phospho-4E-BP1 Thr37/46 and phospho-ERK, and run an in vitro mTORC1 kinase assay with GST-4E-BP1 and [γ-32P]ATP.

citations.title: Orexin/hypocretin activates mTOR complex 1 (mTORC1) via an Erk/Akt-independent and calcium-stimulated lysosome v-ATPase pathway.
New Insights into the Regulation of mTOR Signaling via Ca(2+)-Binding Proteins.

novelty.note: I searched for Ca2+/ionomycin/thapsigargin-driven mTORC1 activation via PKC–MEK/ERK–RSK and Raptor phosphorylation, for the entities together (Ca2+, RSK, Raptor, BAPTA-AM), and for the prediction that MEK/RSK inhibitors block Ca2+-stimulated mTORC1.
