The closest published work directly tested this dependence: in orexin/OX1R-expressing neuronal cells, ionomycin and thapsigargin activate mTORC1 (S6K/S6 phosphorylation, BAPTA-AM-sensitive), yet the MEK inhibitors U0126 and AZD6244 and the pan-RSK inhibitor BI-D1870 abolished ERK1/2 and RSK phosphorylation without affecting the calcium-dependent mTORC1 activation, which instead required the lysosomal v-ATPase; a recent review of Ca2+-binding-protein control of mTOR likewise describes only CaM/hVps34, TRPML1 and TSC2 routes and no Ca2+–PKC/ERK/RSK–Raptor route. Because a stated negative result exists for the specific prediction that U0126/BI-D1870 should block Ca2+-induced mTORC1 activation, I score this refuted, noting that separate work on amino-acid sensing reports a positive Ca2+–ERK1/2–mTORC1 link, so the refutation is system-specific.

hypotheses.statement: MEK1 associates with the actin cytoskeleton, where it phosphorylates the IQGAP-tethered, actin-associated pool of ERK1/2 after PKC activation.
hypotheses.mechanism: In cultured vascular smooth muscle cells, PKC activation phosphorylates and activates a pool of ERK1/2 that IQGAP tethers directly to actin. This activation needs IQGAP and caveolin-dependent upstream C-raf activation (brozovich2016:findings:030). Independent evidence identifies MEK1/2 as the kinase for the ERK1/2 activation-loop TEY motif downstream of Raf (cargnello2011:findings:002), and MEK1 as the top-ranked kinase for the ERK1 Thr202/ERK2 Thr203 site (johnson2023:findings:009). Together these imply that MEK1 must reach the actin-tethered ERK pool, so MEK1 should be found in, and act within, an actin-associated signaling complex.
hypotheses.prediction: After PKC activation, MEK1 (including phospho-MEK1) should co-sediment with F-actin and give proximity-ligation signal with actin. Inhibiting MEK1/2 should abolish phosphorylation of the actin-associated ERK pool. Depolymerizing actin or knocking down IQGAP should reduce MEK1's actin association and its access to tethered ERK.
hypotheses.test: In cultured vascular smooth muscle cells stimulated with a phorbol ester, ± U0126 or PD0325901, ± latrunculin, ± IQGAP siRNA: (1) prepare F-actin co-sedimentation (high-speed pellet) fractions; (2) immunoblot for total and phospho-MEK1 and phospho-ERK1/2; (3) run MEK1–actin proximity ligation assays. As a direct-binding check, perform an in vitro F-actin co-sedimentation assay with purified MEK1, with and without IQGAP.

citations.title: Hierarchical scaffolding of an ERK1/2 activation pathway.
IQGAP1 is a scaffold for mitogen-activated protein kinase signaling.
Stimulus-Specific Activation and Actin Dependency of Distinct, Spatially Separated ERK1/2 Fractions in A7r5 Smooth Muscle Cells

novelty.note: I searched for IQGAP1 as a MEK/ERK scaffold, for MEK1 association with actin filaments and co-sedimentation, and for PKC/phorbol-ester activation of actin-associated ERK in smooth muscle. The IQGAP1 scaffold literature already establishes direct IQGAP1 binding to MEK1 and MEK2 (and to ERK1/2 and actin) with functional effects on MEK/ERK activation (Roy et al.), and the smooth-muscle study that defines the actin-tethered ERK pool explicitly proposes a model in which a B-Raf–MEK–ERK module is scaffolded by IQGAP1 downstream of caveolin-1/PKC — but its full text includes MEK only in the inferred model and presents no data on MEK in the cytoskeletal fraction or MEK–actin proximity. Hence the mechanism is published in general while the specific prediction (phospho-MEK1 co-sedimenting with F-actin, MEK1–actin PLA, MEK-dependence and IQGAP1/actin-dependence of the actin-associated ERK pool) remains untested; nothing found reports a negative test.

hypotheses.statement: S6K1 (RPS6KB1) acts as a negative upstream regulator of EGFR activation, such that loss of S6K1 kinase activity increases EGFR phosphorylation (notably the c-Src site Y845) and downstream ERK/RSK output.
hypotheses.mechanism: In EGFR-expressing cells, rapamycin raises EGFR Y845 phosphorylation and activates c-Src, ERK1/2 and RSK in a manner strictly requiring EGFR kinase activity and its autophosphorylation sites (chaturvedi2009:findings:012, chaturvedi2009:findings:008, chaturvedi2009:findings:010); independently, the same rapamycin treatment is characterized primarily as blocking S6K T389 phosphorylation/TORC1 output (dan2008:findings:017, dan2008:findings:013). If the relevant rapamycin target for this EGFR effect is S6K itself, then S6K activity normally restrains EGFR phosphorylation, and the partial recovery of S6K phosphorylation when RSK is inhibited (chaturvedi2009:findings:006) implies a closed S6K–EGFR–ERK/RSK feedback loop rather than a one-way cascade.
hypotheses.prediction: Selective depletion or kinase-inhibition of S6K1 alone, without inhibiting mTORC1 broadly, should increase EGFR Y845 (and Y1173) phosphorylation and phospho-ERK1/2 in EGFR-expressing cells but not in EGFR-null parental cells; conversely, expressing a rapamycin-insensitive S6K should blunt rapamycin-induced EGFR Y845 phosphorylation.
hypotheses.test: In B82L cells expressing wt-EGFR (with EGFR-null parental cells as control), compare siRNA knockdown of RPS6KB1 (and a selective S6K inhibitor) against rapamycin by immunoblot for phospho-EGFR Y845/Y1173, phospho-Src Y416, phospho-ERK1/2 and phospho-S6K T389; then co-express the rapamycin-resistant S6K-dNC mutant and test whether it abolishes the rapamycin-induced rise in EGFR Y845 phosphorylation, which would place S6K activity causally upstream of EGFR.

citations.title: Inhibition of mTORC1 leads to MAPK pathway activation through a PI3K-dependent feedback loop in human cancer.
Inhibition of p70S6K does not mimic the enhancement of Akt phosphorylation by rapamycin.
Rapamycin induces transactivation of the EGFR and increases cell survival.

novelty.note: I searched for rapamycin-induced EGFR Y845/c-Src transactivation, for S6K1 acting as a negative upstream regulator of EGFR phosphorylation, and for the prediction that S6K1 depletion alone raises EGFR/ERK phosphorylation. The general mechanism is published: Carracedo et al. show that mTORC1 or S6K1 inhibition relieves a feedback brake and activates PI3K and ERK via an S6K–PI3K–Ras route, and the broader literature documents S6K1-mediated feedback onto receptor tyrosine kinase signaling (IRS-1/Grb10). However, no retrieved source attributes the rapamycin-induced rise in EGFR Y845 (or Y1173) phosphorylation and c-Src activation to loss of S6K1 activity specifically, nor tests S6K1 knockdown or a rapamycin-resistant S6K against that readout in EGFR-expressing versus EGFR-null cells; a directly adjacent study found that p70S6K inhibition does not reproduce rapamycin's feedback effect on Akt, so the S6K-centred attribution is unsettled rather than refuted for EGFR.

hypotheses.statement: PDK1 is required for growth-factor-induced inhibitory phosphorylation of GSK3 at Ser21/Ser9, so PDK1 negatively regulates GSK3 activity in growth-factor signalling, but not in cAMP/PKA signalling.
hypotheses.mechanism: IGF-1- and insulin-induced GSK3 Ser21/9 phosphorylation depends on PI3K and occurs together with increased Akt phosphorylation (fang2000:findings:003, alkhouri2005:findings:007). PDK1 phosphorylates AKT T308, which is required for AKT activity (manning2017:findings:005). PDK1 is also required for mitogenic activation of RSK1-3 (cargnello2011:findings:023), and GSK3α/β Ser21/9 is listed among RSK targets (chou2020:findings:015). The cAMP-induced GSK3 phosphorylation instead runs through PKA and is independent of PI3K (fang2000:findings:001, fang2000:findings:003), so it should not need PDK1.
hypotheses.prediction: Without PDK1, IGF-1 or insulin should fail to increase GSK3α/β Ser21/9 phosphorylation, and GSK3 substrate phosphorylation should stay elevated. Forskolin- or 8-Br-cAMP-induced GSK3 Ser21/9 phosphorylation should be unaffected. Recombinant PDK1 alone should not phosphorylate GSK3 Ser21/9 in vitro, which would show the dependence acts through AKT/RSK rather than direct phosphorylation.
hypotheses.test: Compare PDK1-/- and wild-type murine ES cells, or HEK293 cells treated with PDK1 siRNA or a selective PDK1 inhibitor. Stimulate them with IGF-1 versus forskolin and immunoblot for phospho-GSK3α/β Ser21/9, phospho-AKT T308 and phospho-RSK. In parallel, run an in vitro kinase assay of recombinant PDK1 with recombinant GSK3β, with and without AKT, to tell direct phosphorylation from relayed phosphorylation.

citations.title: Further evidence that the inhibition of glycogen synthase kinase-3beta by IGF-1 is mediated by PDK1/PKB-induced phosphorylation of Ser-9 and not by dephosphorylation of Tyr-216.
The role of 3-phosphoinositide-dependent protein kinase 1 in activating AGC kinases defined in embryonic stem cells.

novelty.note: I searched for PDK1-dependence of growth-factor-induced GSK3 Ser21/Ser9 phosphorylation, for PDK1-null/knockout models with insulin or IGF-1 readouts, and for PI3K/PKA-independent cAMP-driven GSK3 Ser9 phosphorylation. Shaw, Cohen & Alessi (FEBS Lett 1997) state exactly this explanation in their title and results — IGF-1 inhibition of GSK3beta is mediated by PDK1/PKB-induced phosphorylation of Ser-9 rather than Tyr-216 dephosphorylation — and Williams et al. (Curr Biol 2000) show in PDK1-/- ES cells that IGF1 fails to phosphorylate the PKB T-loop and that PKB, p70 S6K and p90 RSK activation is compromised while PKA, MSK1 and AMPK remain functional, which is the same PDK1->AKT/RSK relay plus PDK1-independence of the PKA arm. (A FEBS Lett 2005 muscle-PDK1-knockout paper covering the insulin/GSK3/glycogen synthase prediction exists but is retracted, so it is not cited.) Nothing found tests and negates the claim, so the status is established rather than partial or refuted.

hypotheses.statement: MAP2K1 (MEK1) negatively regulates MTORC2 kinase output toward AKT Ser473 through mTORC1-dependent phosphorylation of the MTORC2 subunit Rictor.
hypotheses.mechanism: PMA-induced Rictor phosphorylation on RXRXXpS/T sites is blocked by the MEK1/2 inhibitor U0126 and by rapamycin, placing MEK1/2 upstream of mTORC1-dependent Rictor phosphorylation (julien2009:findings:001). MEK1/2 inhibitors also abolish mTORC1 kinase activity (carriere2010:findings:015), and constitutively active MEK1-DD drives Raptor phosphorylation without growth factors (carrire2008:findings:005). Rictor within MTORC2 is phosphorylated in an mTORC1-dependent manner (dibble2009:findings:004), and the non-phosphorylatable Rictor-T1135A mutant raises insulin-stimulated AKT Ser473 phosphorylation (dibble2009:findings:018). Together these imply that MEK1 activity, acting through mTORC1, restrains MTORC2 output.
hypotheses.prediction: Expressing MEK1-DD or stimulating with PMA should increase Rictor phosphorylation within MTORC2. It should also lower MTORC2 kinase activity toward AKT Ser473, and U0126 or rapamycin should prevent both effects. Cells reconstituted with Rictor-T1135A should be resistant to the MEK1-induced reduction in MTORC2 activity.
hypotheses.test: In cultured Rictor-/- MEFs reconstituted with wild-type Rictor or Rictor-T1135A, and in HEK293 cells, express MEK1-DD or treat with PMA, with or without U0126 or rapamycin. Measure Rictor phosphorylation by immunoprecipitation and phospho-motif immunoblot. Measure MTORC2 activity with an in vitro kinase assay on anti-Rictor immunoprecipitates using inactive Akt1 as substrate, plus immunoblots for AKT Ser473.

citations.title: mTORC1-activated S6K1 phosphorylates Rictor on threonine 1135 and regulates mTORC2 signaling.
Characterization of Rictor phosphorylation sites reveals direct regulation of mTOR complex 2 by S6K1.

novelty.note: I searched for the MEK1/2–mTORC1–Rictor axis, for Rictor Thr1135 phosphorylation as a negative regulator of mTORC2/Akt-Ser473, and for ERK/RSK-driven feedback onto mTORC2, then read the two primary papers underlying the corpus claims. Julien et al. (MCB 2010) publishes both halves of the chain — PMA-induced, rapamycin-sensitive Rictor RXRXXS/T phosphorylation is strongly inhibited by U0126, and S6K1-mediated Thr1135 phosphorylation dampens mTORC2-directed Akt-Ser473 phosphorylation — while Dibble et al. independently establish mTORC1/S6K1-dependent Thr1135 phosphorylation restraining Akt-Ser473 (and report that insulin/EGF-stimulated Rictor phosphorylation was resistant to MEK inhibition). However, no retrieved source states MEK1 itself as a negative regulator of mTORC2 output or tests MEK1-DD/PMA for reduced mTORC2 activity with Rictor-T1135A rescue; notably Julien's in vitro kinase assay on anti-Rictor immunoprecipitates found no difference in activity toward kinase-inactive Akt between wild-type and T1135A/T1135D Rictor, so that element of the prediction is already disfavoured without the MEK arm having been tested.

hypotheses.statement: ERK2 directly binds RSK and phosphorylates it on ERK-dependent activating sites, thereby activating RSK.
hypotheses.mechanism: RSK isoforms bind ERK1/2 in quiescent cells, and RSK activation requires ordered phosphorylation of essential sites mediated partly by ERK1/2 (cargnello2011:findings:018, :023). Independently, ERK2 is a PMA-activatable kinase that phosphorylates protein substrates in vitro (carriere2010:findings:004). MEK inhibition with U0126 nearly abolishes PMA-induced Raptor phosphorylation, which is RSK-dependent (BI-D1870-sensitive), placing ERK activity upstream of RSK output (carrire2008:findings:001). Together these suggest ERK2 itself is a direct RSK-activating kinase and binding partner.
hypotheses.prediction: Purified active ERK2 should phosphorylate kinase-inactive RSK1 in vitro on ERK-dependent activation-site residues, and unstimulated or inactive ERK2 should not. ERK2 should co-immunoprecipitate with RSK1 in quiescent cells, with the complex reduced after mitogen stimulation. Selective ERK2 knockdown should reduce PMA-induced RSK activation-site phosphorylation and RSK-dependent Raptor phosphorylation.
hypotheses.test: Run an in vitro kinase assay with [γ-32P]ATP using active versus inactive recombinant or immunoprecipitated ERK2 and immunopurified kinase-dead RSK1 (K112/464R). Read out 32P incorporation and site-specific phospho-immunoblots, including a RSK1 mutant lacking the ERK-dependent sites. Complement this with HA-ERK2/RSK1 coimmunoprecipitation in quiescent versus PMA-stimulated HEK293 cells, and with ERK2 siRNA followed by immunoblotting of RSK activation sites.

citations.title: Identification of regulatory phosphorylation sites in mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK)-activated protein kinase-1a/p90rsk that are inducible by MAPK.
Phosphorylation of p90 ribosomal S6 kinase (RSK) regulates extracellular signal-regulated kinase docking and RSK activity.
Structural assembly of the signaling competent ERK2-RSK1 heterodimeric protein kinase complex.

novelty.note: I searched for direct ERK2 phosphorylation of RSK1 activation sites with in vitro kinase assays, for the ERK–RSK complex in quiescent cells that dissociates on mitogen stimulation, and for structural/biochemical work on the ERK2–RSK1 pair. All three elements are already published: Dalby et al. identified MAPK(ERK)-inducible sites on p90rsk and showed MAPK phosphorylates the activation-loop Thr574 (Thr573 in RSK1 numbering) to trigger the ordered autophosphorylation cascade; Roux, Richards and Blenis showed RSK1 is complexed with ERK1/2 in resting cells and dissociates after stimulation via Ser749 phosphorylation; and Alexa et al. solved a precatalytic ERK2–RSK1 complex in which the RSK1 activation loop faces the ERK2 catalytic site. Since published sources state exactly this explanation (direct binding plus direct activating phosphorylation by ERK2), the status is established rather than partial or open.

hypotheses.statement: mTORC1 negatively regulates SRC activity, such that mTORC1 inhibition directly relieves suppression of c-Src and increases its activating autophosphorylation.
hypotheses.mechanism: The mTORC1 evidence establishes that mTORC1 inhibition by rapamycin/RAD001 triggers feedback activation of the Ras-Raf1-MEK1/2-ERK cascade and upregulation of receptor tyrosine kinase signaling (carracedo2008:findings:004, carracedo2008:context:000, carracedo2008:findings:002). Independently, the SRC evidence shows that rapamycin raises active c-Src (pSrc Y416) and lowers inactive c-Src (pSrc Y527) while increasing the c-Src-dependent EGFR Y845 site, and that Src inhibition abolishes rapamycin-driven ERK/RSK phosphorylation (chaturvedi2009:findings:012, chaturvedi2009:findings:013). Taken together, the ERK/RTK feedback attributed to loss of mTORC1 activity and the c-Src activation state change upon the same perturbation imply that c-Src is itself the node whose activity mTORC1 restrains, placing SRC directly downstream of mTORC1 rather than merely parallel to it.
hypotheses.prediction: Acute, selective loss of mTORC1 catalytic output (not just rapamycin treatment) should increase the pSrc Y416/pSrc Y527 ratio and in vitro Src kinase activity within minutes to a few hours, and conversely restoring or hyperactivating mTORC1 should suppress basal Src activation; the ERK/Raf1 Ser338 feedback seen after mTORC1 inhibition should be lost when Src is depleted, whereas Src activation after mTORC1 inhibition should persist when MEK is blocked, placing Src upstream of the ERK arm.
hypotheses.test: In a cultured line such as MCF7, COS7 or HEK293, compare vehicle, rapamycin, and a direct mTOR kinase inhibitor, each with and without RAPTOR knockdown (and with a rapamycin-resistant mTOR mutant as specificity control), then immunoblot pSrc Y416, pSrc Y527, p-Raf1 Ser338 and p-ERK, and immunoprecipitate Src for an in vitro kinase assay on a peptide substrate; epistasis is resolved by repeating with siRNA against SRC versus MEK inhibition, which should respectively abolish or spare the Src activity change.

citations.title: mTOR signaling feedback modulates mammary epithelial differentiation and restrains invasion downstream of PTEN loss.
Inhibition of mTORC1 leads to MAPK pathway activation through a PI3K-dependent feedback loop in human cancer.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the mechanism in words (mTORC1 as a negative regulator of Src / feedback relief), the entities together (rapamycin + c-Src Y416/Y527 autophosphorylation), and the prediction (active-site mTOR kinase inhibitors raising Src activity, Src-dependence of ERK feedback). A Cancer Research study of PTEN-null mammary epithelium states exactly this explanation: both rapamycin and the active-site inhibitor AZD8055 increase c-SRC tyrosine phosphorylation, 'markedly upregulated SRC Y416 phosphorylation', and the authors frame it as mTORC1 inhibition releasing negative feedback that triggers a marked increase in SRC activity — i.e. loss of mTORC1 catalytic output, not a rapamycin-specific off-target effect. Because the statement is published for this phenomenon (with the published mechanism routing through relieved RTK/EGFR feedback rather than a strictly direct mTORC1–Src link), I score this established, citing the MAPK-feedback paper as the nearest work for the ERK-arm portion; no source reporting a negative test of mTORC1-dependent Src activation was found.

hypotheses.statement: PI3K activity is required for insulin-induced accumulation of GTP-bound (active) RHEB, acting through AKT-mediated inactivation of TSC2's GAP activity toward RHEB.
hypotheses.mechanism: Inhibiting PI3K with wortmannin or GDC0941 blocks insulin-induced AKT phosphorylation and activation in HEK293 cells, NMuMG cells and MEFs (borisov2009:findings:009, budi2015:findings:006). Separately, insulin acting via AKT phosphorylates and inactivates TSC2 and releases it from the lysosome. Because TSC2's GAP activity otherwise keeps RHEB GDP-bound, this stabilizes GTP-bound RHEB (haeusler2018:findings:027, manning2017:findings:017, laplante2012:findings:002). Together these imply that PI3K activity sets RHEB's nucleotide state, with AKT and TSC2 as intermediates.
hypotheses.prediction: In insulin-stimulated wild-type MEFs, PI3K inhibition should lower the RHEB-GTP/RHEB-GDP ratio to the serum-starved baseline and keep TSC2 at the lysosome. In Tsc2-null MEFs, RHEB-GTP should stay high and largely insensitive to PI3K inhibition.
hypotheses.test: Serum-starve wild-type and Tsc2-null MEFs, pretreat with wortmannin (100 nM), GDC0941 or vehicle, then stimulate with insulin. Measure RHEB nucleotide loading by immunoprecipitating RHEB and resolving bound GTP/GDP by HPLC or TLC, or by an active-RHEB pull-down. In parallel, immunoblot p-AKT and p-TSC2 at the AKT sites and S6K1 T389, and image TSC2/LAMP2 colocalization by immunofluorescence.

citations.title: Insulin activation of Rheb, a mediator of mTOR/S6K/4E-BP signaling, is inhibited by TSC1 and 2.
Spatial control of the TSC complex integrates insulin and nutrient regulation of mTORC1 at the lysosome.
Rheb GTPase is a direct target of TSC2 GAP activity and regulates mTOR signaling.

novelty.note: I searched for insulin/wortmannin-dependent Rheb-GTP loading, for Rheb nucleotide state in TSC2-null cells, and for AKT-driven TSC2 release from the lysosome permitting Rheb-GTP loading. Garami et al. (Mol Cell 2003) directly report that TSC1/2 is a Rheb-GAP and that insulin stimulates Rheb (GTP loading) in a PI3K-dependent manner, and Menon et al. (Cell 2014) show wortmannin-sensitive, Akt-phosphorylation-dependent dissociation of the TSC complex from lysosomal Rheb that permits Rheb-GTP loading; Inoki et al. establish TSC2 GAP activity toward Rheb with constitutive Rheb-GTP elevation when TSC2 is lost. Since published primary work states this same explanation (PI3K→AKT→TSC2 GAP inactivation→Rheb-GTP), the hypothesis is established rather than open, and no source reported a negative test.

hypotheses.statement: PI3K activity positively regulates cell cycle progression (G1/S commitment) when cells are stimulated with insulin plus EGF, in part by sustaining the ERK activity that cell cycle progression requires.
hypotheses.mechanism: In MCF-10A cells, ERK activity is absolutely required for cell cycle progression, and the fraction of pERK+ cells reflects the time each cell spends in ERK-on pulses during a cycle (albeck2013:findings:006, albeck2013:findings:009). In HEK293 cells, PI3K inhibition with wortmannin abolished the synergistic amplification of Ras-GTP/MEK/ERK by insulin plus EGF, and insulin could not enhance MEK or ERK without PI3K (borisov2009:findings:009). PI3K and mTOR inhibitors also reduced proliferation of AML cell lines (casado2013:findings:017). Together these claims suggest that PI3K is upstream of the ERK input that drives cell cycle entry when insulin and EGF are co-present.
hypotheses.prediction: In insulin plus EGF–stimulated epithelial cells, PI3K inhibition should lower the frequency or duty fraction of ERK activity pulses. It should also lower the fraction of pRb+ or S-phase cells and delay the rise of CDK2 activity relative to vehicle. These effects should be markedly weaker under EGF alone, where insulin–ERK synergy is absent.
hypotheses.test: Treat MCF-10A cells expressing an ERK FRET reporter (EKAR-EV) and a CDK2 translocation reporter with a PI3K inhibitor (e.g. wortmannin or LY294002) or vehicle. Stimulate with EGF alone, insulin alone, or EGF plus insulin. Quantify ERK pulse frequency and CDK2 activity rise by live imaging, then fix and score pRb and EdU incorporation by immunofluorescence. As a rescue arm, test whether a constitutively active MEK restores pRb+/EdU+ fractions under PI3K inhibition.

citations.title: Spatiotemporal control of ERK pulse frequency coordinates fate decisions during mammary acinar morphogenesis.
Cell cycle dependence of ERK activation dynamics is regulated by PI3K and PAK1 signaling.
Disentangling Pro-mitotic Signaling during Cell Cycle Progression using Time-Resolved Single-Cell Imaging.
Akt and ERK control the proliferative response of mammary epithelial cells to the growth factors IGF-1 and EGF through the cell cycle inhibitor p57Kip2.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: (i) PI3K inhibition and ERK pulse frequency / S-phase entry in MCF-10A, (ii) insulin+EGF synergistic amplification of Ras-GTP/ERK and its PI3K dependence, and (iii) the prediction itself (PI3K inhibition lowering pRb/CDK2 and ERK duty fraction, weaker under EGF alone). Individual legs are published: PI3K gain-of-function raises ERK pulse frequency in MCF10A and pulse frequency tracks proliferation (PMID 36113484); PI3K-dependent PAK1 signaling governs sustained vs. transient ERK dynamics and correlates with division rate (PMID 40731057); and in untransformed mammary epithelium both ERK and PI3K activity are separately required for cell-cycle entry, with PI3K inhibition suppressing S-phase entry while only transiently attenuating ERK (PMID 32294432). However, no source states the specific causal chain that PI3K sustains the ERK duty fraction that licenses G1/S selectively when insulin is co-present with EGF; the nearest work on insulin/IGF-1 + EGF synergy in MCF10A instead places Akt and ERK as parallel, partly antagonistic inputs converging on p57Kip2 (PMID 22394561), so the status is partial rather than established, and nothing reports a direct negative test.

hypotheses.statement: ERK2 directly phosphorylates RAF as a negative-feedback kinase-substrate relationship that reduces RAF kinase activity.
hypotheses.mechanism: Two independent papers state that activated ERK2 directly phosphorylates upstream signaling proteins in vitro. It phosphorylates hSos1 at the same sites seen in vivo (corbalangarcia1996:findings:000), and it phosphorylates Raptor at S/T-P sites (carriere2010:findings:004). Separately, the RAF evidence states that MAPK/ERK feedback-phosphorylates Raf, which reduces Raf kinase activity and downstream MAPKK/MAPK phosphorylation (lemmon2010:findings:022). It also states that this ERK-mediated phosphorylation disrupts Raf–KSR binding and shuts down pathway activation (good2011:findings:004). Finally, blocking ERK-dependent feedback induces activating pCRAF-S338 (lito2012:findings:011). Together these suggest the ERK2 isoform is itself a direct Raf kinase in this feedback loop.
hypotheses.prediction: Activated ERK2 should add 32P to purified RAF in vitro, and this should be blocked by an ERK2 kinase-dead mutant or by U0126 pretreatment of the cells the ERK2 is taken from. In cells, ERK2 knockdown should reduce growth-factor-induced phosphorylation of RAF at S/T-P sites. It should also prolong RAF kinase activity and RAF–KSR association after EGF stimulation.
hypotheses.test: Run an in vitro [γ-32P]ATP kinase assay using immunoprecipitated or recombinant activated ERK2 (wild-type versus kinase-dead) with immunopurified RAF. Confirm the phosphorylated sites by phospho-S/T-P immunoblotting or phosphopeptide mapping. Then, in HEK293 cells, knock down ERK2 with siRNA (alone and together with ERK1). Measure RAF S/T-P phosphorylation, RAF immunoprecipitate kinase activity toward MEK, and RAF–KSR coimmunoprecipitation over an EGF time course.

citations.title: Regulation of Raf-1 by direct feedback phosphorylation.
Impact of feedback phosphorylation and Raf heterodimerization on normal and mutant B-Raf signaling.
Identification of novel ERK-mediated feedback phosphorylation sites at the C-terminus of B-Raf.

novelty.note: I searched for ERK-to-Raf feedback phosphorylation in plain terms, for the specific entities (ERK2, Raf-1/B-Raf, S/T-P proline-directed sites, in vitro 32P kinase assay), and for the predicted consequences (loss of Raf activity, Raf–KSR/Ras disengagement). Dougherty et al. (Mol Cell 2005) identify six mitogen-induced Raf-1 downregulatory sites, five of them proline-directed sites phosphorylated directly by activated ERK2 in vitro with MEK-dependent phosphorylation in cells, and show hyperphosphorylation desensitizes Raf-1 and blocks Ras/Raf-1 interaction; Ritt et al. and Brummer et al. report the equivalent ERK-mediated feedback sites on B-Raf and their impact on Raf complexes. The stated kinase–substrate negative-feedback explanation is therefore already published, so the status is established rather than partial.

hypotheses.statement: PTEN directly negatively regulates the cell-surface abundance of TGFBR1 (TβRI), limiting autocrine TGF-β/Smad2/3 signaling, through its lipid phosphatase activity that lowers PIP3 and thereby Akt activity.
hypotheses.mechanism: Evidence about PTEN shows that expressing PTEN in PTEN-deficient cells lowers Akt phosphorylation and that its tumor-suppressive function depends on the lipid (D3-phosphoinositide) phosphatase activity. Independently, evidence about TGFBR1 shows that PI3K and Akt1/2 inhibition raises basal surface TβRI and blocks the insulin-induced increase, and that AKT drives surface delivery of TβRI by phosphorylating the RabGAP AS160 to relieve intracellular retention. If PTEN sets the PIP3/AKT tone upstream of this trafficking step, then PTEN status should itself dictate how much TβRI reaches the plasma membrane.
hypotheses.prediction: PTEN loss or knockdown should increase basal cell-surface TβRI (with higher AS160 phosphorylation and elevated basal phospho-Smad2/3), while re-expression of wild-type PTEN should reduce surface TβRI and blunt insulin/growth-factor-induced TβRI surface delivery; the lipid-phosphatase-dead G129E mutant should fail to do so.
hypotheses.test: In NMuMG cells or MEFs, knock down Pten by siRNA and separately re-express wild-type PTEN versus G129E in a PTEN-null line, then quantify surface TβRI by cell-surface biotinylation/streptavidin pulldown and immunoblot (total TβRI as control), alongside phospho-AKT, phospho-AS160 and phospho-Smad2/3 blots with SB431542 as specificity control.

citations.title: Transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β)-induced up-regulation of TGF-β receptors at the cell surface amplifies the TGF-β response.
Activation of Akt signaling in prostate induces a TGFβ-mediated restraint on cancer progression and metastasis.
Endometrial PTEN Deficiency Leads to SMAD2/3 Nuclear Translocation.

novelty.note: I searched for PTEN control of TGFBR1 surface abundance, PTEN/AKT/AS160 receptor trafficking, and PTEN loss with elevated Smad2/3, across PubMed/PMC and publisher pages. The upstream and downstream halves are published separately — AKT-driven delivery of intracellular TβRI/TβRII to the surface (PMID 30948511) and PTEN loss or constitutive AKT increasing TGFβ pathway activity in prostate (PMID 23995785, attributed to raised Tgfbr2/Smad4 expression, not trafficking) — but no source states that PTEN's lipid-phosphatase activity sets surface TβRI via PIP3/AKT/AS160, and none tests G129E in this context. Notably, one study directly tested receptor dependence of PTEN-loss Smad2/3 activation and reports SB431542 failed to restore cytoplasmic SMAD2/3, concluding the effect is TGF-β-receptor-independent (PMID 34638474), which argues against the autocrine-receptor arm of the prediction though surface TβRI itself was not quantified; hence partial rather than established or refuted.

hypotheses.statement: mTOR (as mTORC1) positively regulates SMAD-dependent transcription and is required for insulin's enhancement of TGF-β/Smad-induced gene expression.
hypotheses.mechanism: In HEK293 cells, insulin stimulates mTORC1: it induces rapamycin-sensitive Raptor Ser863 phosphorylation and robust mTORC1 kinase activity toward 4E-BP1 (carriere2010:findings:011, carrire2008:findings:010). In NMuMG cells, insulin enhances TGF-β/Smad-induced Snai1, Serpine1 and Fn1 expression at low TGF-β, and SB431542 prevents this enhancement (budi2015:findings:023). If mTORC1 is the insulin-activated effector that potentiates the Smad output, then mTOR activity should be needed for the insulin effect on Smad-dependent transcription.
hypotheses.prediction: In NMuMG cells given low-dose TGF-β (0.2 ng/ml) plus insulin, blocking mTOR with rapamycin or Torin1, or knocking down MTOR or Raptor, should abolish insulin's enhancement of Snai1, Serpine1 and Fn1 induction and of Smad-responsive reporter activity. TGF-β alone should induce these genes to the same extent with or without mTOR inhibition. Insulin-enhanced Smad2/3 C-terminal phosphorylation or Smad nuclear accumulation should also be reduced by mTOR inhibition.
hypotheses.test: Treat NMuMG cells with TGF-β (0.2 ng/ml) with or without insulin, in combination with rapamycin or Torin1 or with siRNA against Mtor or Rptor. Include an SB431542 control. Measure Snai1, Serpine1 and Fn1 mRNA by qRT-PCR, a Smad-binding-element luciferase reporter, and phospho-Smad2/3 and nuclear Smad by immunoblotting and fractionation. Confirm mTORC1 inhibition by phospho-S6K1 Thr389 and phospho-4E-BP1 Thr37/46. The hypothesis is ruled out if insulin still enhances Smad-dependent output when mTORC1 is fully inhibited.

citations.title: The insulin response integrates increased TGF-β signaling through Akt-induced enhancement of cell surface delivery of TGF-β receptors.
Distinct roles for mammalian target of rapamycin complexes in the fibroblast response to transforming growth factor-beta.
PI3K/mTORC2 regulates TGF-β/Activin signalling by modulating Smad2/3 activity via linker phosphorylation.
Enhanced TGF-β Signaling Contributes to the Insulin-Induced Angiogenic Responses of Endothelial Cells.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the insulin→TGF-β/Smad enhancement mechanism (Budi/Derynck work), mTORC1/rapamycin requirement for Smad-dependent transcription, and the prediction that mTOR inhibition abolishes TGF-β-induced Snai1/Serpine1/Fn1 and SBE-reporter output. The source paper's own mechanism is Akt→AS160-dependent trafficking of TGF-β receptors to the cell surface with no mTOR or rapamycin involvement (PMID 26420907, and the follow-up endothelial study PMID 30684493), so the proposed mTORC1 requirement is not published. The nearest direct tests of the mTOR arm go the other way: rapamycin blocked TGF-β-driven anchorage-independent growth 'without affecting TGF-beta transcriptional responses or extracellular matrix protein induction' in fibroblasts (PMID 19117990), and the one demonstrated PI3K-to-Smad link is mTORC2-mediated Smad2/3 linker phosphorylation that shortens rather than potentiates Smad activity (PMID 25998442). Because the specific insulin-plus-low-dose-TGF-β combination in NMuMG cells was not itself tested with mTOR inhibition or MTOR/Raptor knockdown, this is partial rather than refuted.

hypotheses.statement: TGFBR2 negatively regulates (inhibits) cell growth: ligand binding to TGFBR2 and its kinase activity are required for TGF-β-induced, Smad-dependent growth inhibition.
hypotheses.mechanism: In NMuMG cells, dominant-negative Smad3 or Smad7 blocked about 80% of TGF-β-induced growth inhibition, so the antiproliferative response runs through Smad signaling. Ligand sequestration away from TβRII prevented Smad2 activation, showing that ligand binding to TβRII is needed to start the cascade. Smad7 associated only with receptor complexes containing kinase-competent TbR-II, so TbR-II kinase activity is needed to engage the Smad machinery. Separately, removing surface TβRI downregulated TGF-β-mediated Smad3 activation and antiproliferation, placing the receptor complex upstream of the growth-inhibitory output.
hypotheses.prediction: Removing TGFBR2, or replacing it with a kinase-dead mutant (K277R), should abolish TGF-β-induced Smad2/3 phosphorylation and the TGF-β-induced drop in proliferation. Restoring wild-type TGFBR2 should restore growth inhibition.
hypotheses.test: In TGF-β-responsive NMuMG cells, knock down TGFBR2 by siRNA/CRISPR and rescue with wild-type or kinase-dead K277R TGFBR2. Treat with TGF-β1, then measure thymidine/EdU incorporation and cell counts, with phospho-Smad2/3 immunoblot and a 3TP-Lux reporter as pathway readouts.

citations.title: Growth inhibition by transforming growth factor beta (TGF-beta) type I is restored in TGF-beta-resistant hepatoma cells after expression of TGF-beta receptor type II cDNA.
Restoration of TGF-beta signalling reduces tumorigenicity in human lung cancer cells.
A kinase-defective transforming growth factor-beta receptor type II is a dominant-negative regulator for human breast carcinoma MCF-7 cells.
TGF-beta receptor-mediated signalling through Smad2, Smad3 and Smad4.

novelty.note: I searched for kinase-dead/K277R TβRII effects on Smad2/3 phosphorylation and growth arrest, for restoration of TβRII in receptor-deficient cells, and for the requirement of TβRII kinase activity in Smad activation. Multiple primary papers already state this explanation: TβRII loss abolishes TGF-β growth inhibition and re-expression of wild-type TβRII restores both Smad2/3 phosphorylation and antiproliferation, while truncated/kinase-defective TβRII acts dominant-negatively to block growth inhibition, and Smad2/3 engagement of TβRI requires a kinase-competent TβRII. The hypothesis and its prediction are therefore pre-existing established knowledge rather than novel.

hypotheses.statement: ERK2 directly phosphorylates SOS (hSos1) within its C-terminal domain, and this phosphorylation uncouples SOS from Grb2 as a negative feedback on Ras activation.
hypotheses.mechanism: Tryptic phosphopeptide maps of hSos1 from serum-stimulated cells comigrate with maps from in vitro ERK2 phosphorylation of hSos1. This places ERK2, or a kinase with identical site specificity, at the in vivo SOS sites (corbalangarcia1996:findings:000). Independent evidence on SOS states that MAPK phosphorylation of Sos impairs Sos/Grb2 interaction and reduces Sos membrane recruitment, dampening Ras activation (lemmon2010:findings:022). It also describes ERK-mediated inhibitory phosphorylation of Sos as the feedback that makes the EGFR response transient (kiyatkin2020:context:001). Together these imply a direct ERK2→SOS phosphorylation that controls SOS–Grb2 coupling.
hypotheses.prediction: Purified active ERK2 should phosphorylate recombinant SOS1 C-terminal domain in vitro, and this should be lost in a phosphosite-mutant SOS1. In cells, depleting ERK2 or inhibiting MEK should reduce stimulus-induced SOS1 phosphorylation and prevent serum- or EGF-induced dissociation of SOS1 from Grb2.
hypotheses.test: Run an in vitro [γ-32P]ATP kinase assay with recombinant active ERK2 and purified wild-type versus phosphosite-mutant SOS1 C-terminal domain. In parallel, use siRNA knockdown of ERK2, alone and with ERK1, or U0126 treatment in EGF-stimulated cultured cells, followed by SOS1 phospho-mobility shift and SOS1–Grb2 co-immunoprecipitation.

citations.title: Regulation of epidermal growth factor receptor signaling by phosphorylation of the ras exchange factor hSOS1.
Identification of the mitogen-activated protein kinase phosphorylation sites on human Sos1 that regulate interaction with Grb2.
Desensitization of Ras activation by a feedback disassociation of the SOS-Grb2 complex.

novelty.note: I searched for ERK/MAPK phosphorylation of the SOS1 proline-rich C-terminal domain, for the SOS1–Grb2 uncoupling prediction, and for the Grb2-SOS dissociation feedback literature on PubMed/publisher pages. Porfiri & McCormick (1996) report that MAPK phosphorylates hSOS1 in the carboxyl-terminal proline-rich domain in vitro and in EGF-stimulated cells and that this markedly reduces hSOS1 association with the EGF receptor via Grb2, i.e. exactly the proposed direct ERK2→SOS feedback; the companion Corbalan-Garcia et al. (1996) paper maps the specific MAPK sites (S1132/S1167/S1178/S1193) that regulate Grb2 binding, and Waters et al. (1995) had already established feedback disassembly of the SOS-Grb2 complex. The explanation is therefore published rather than open, so the status is established (a caveat exists that in insulin-receptor settings a non-ERK kinase was implicated, but that does not negate the ERK-driven mechanism).

hypotheses.statement: Actin positively regulates PKC/phorbol-ester-stimulated mTORC1 activation by scaffolding, via IQGAP, the ERK1/2 pool that phosphorylates Raptor.
hypotheses.mechanism: In vascular smooth muscle cells, IQGAP tethers ERK1/2 to actin, and IQGAP knockdown prevents phosphorylation and activation of this actin-associated ERK pool after PKC activation (brozovich2016:findings:030). In HEK293 cells, PMA-stimulated mTORC1 kinase activity depends on ERK/RSK-mediated Raptor phosphorylation: the phospho-deficient Raptor mutants (S3A/3A) lower mTORC1 activity toward 4E-BP1, and MEK1/2 inhibition abolishes mTORC1 kinase activity (carriere2010:findings:015, carrire2008:findings:010). If the PKC-responsive ERK that reaches Raptor comes from the actin-tethered pool, then the actin scaffold is an upstream requirement for PKC-driven mTORC1 activation. Insulin-stimulated mTORC1 activity does not depend on these Raptor sites (carrire2008:findings:010), so insulin-driven activation should not need the actin scaffold.
hypotheses.prediction: Disrupting actin filaments or removing the IQGAP-actin tether should reduce PMA-induced Raptor phosphorylation, 4E-BP1 Thr37/46 phosphorylation and Raptor-associated mTOR kinase activity toward GST-4E-BP1. Insulin-induced mTORC1 activity should stay largely intact. The effect on PMA-induced mTORC1 activity should be lost in cells expressing the S3A Raptor mutant.
hypotheses.test: In cultured HEK293 cells or vascular smooth muscle cells, pretreat with latrunculin B or cytochalasin D, or knock down IQGAP by siRNA. Then stimulate with PMA or with insulin. Measure ERK phosphorylation in actin-associated versus soluble fractions, Raptor phosphorylation (Raptor immunoprecipitation with RXRXXpS/T or phospho-site antibodies), 4E-BP1 Thr37/46 and S6K1 phosphorylation by immunoblot, and mTOR kinase activity in Raptor immunoprecipitates using GST-4E-BP1 and [γ-32P]ATP. Run the same comparison in cells expressing wild-type versus S3A Raptor.

citations.title: Codependencies of mTORC1 signaling and endolysosomal actin structures.
A conserved role of IQGAP1 in regulating TOR complex 1.
Shigella Effector OspB Activates mTORC1 in a Manner That Depends on IQGAP1 and Promotes Cell Proliferation

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the mechanism in words (actin cytoskeleton required for ERK/Raptor-dependent mTORC1 activation), the entities together (IQGAP1 + ERK1/2 + actin + mTORC1), and the prediction (latrunculin/cytochalasin effects on PMA-stimulated 4E-BP1/S6K and Raptor phosphorylation). The component steps are published separately — actin polymerization inhibition impairs mTORC1 activity and mTOR/RAGC endolysosomal association (PMID 37703363), IQGAP1 is a conserved regulator of TORC1 (PMID 22328503), and IQGAP1 is required for effector-driven mTORC1 activation with the authors explicitly raising IQGAP1-bound ERK1/2 as the possible conduit (doi 10.1371/journal.ppat.1005200) — but no retrieved source states that the IQGAP-actin tether supplies the ERK pool phosphorylating Raptor, nor tests the PKC/PMA-specific, S3A-Raptor-dependent prediction with insulin as the insensitive control. Nothing found reports a direct negative test of this specific claim, so it is not refuted; hence partial.

hypotheses.statement: IL-17 activates the kinase JNK1 in human IL-17-responsive cells through ACT1/TRAF6 signaling, and A20 limits this activation.
hypotheses.mechanism: IL-17 signaling recruits TRAF6 via ACT1, which leads to MAPK activation explicitly including JNK. This activation is impaired without ACT1 or TRAF6 (gaffen2014:findings:022). IL-17-induced A20 deubiquitinates TRAF6 and particularly downregulates JNK activation (gaffen2014:findings:027). JNK1 is one of the conventional JNK group MAPKs (cargnello2011:findings:000), so the JNK activity that IL-17 triggers should include direct activation of JNK1.
hypotheses.prediction: In human IL-17-responsive cells, IL-17 stimulation should increase JNK1 activating phosphorylation and JNK1 kinase activity. The increase should be abolished by ACT1 or TRAF6 knockdown and enhanced and prolonged by A20 (TNFAIP3) knockdown.
hypotheses.test: Stimulate a human IL-17-responsive fibroblast or epithelial cell line with recombinant IL-17A over a time course. Immunoprecipitate JNK1 with an isoform-specific antibody, then measure phospho-JNK1 by immunoblot and kinase activity by an in vitro c-Jun phosphorylation assay. Compare control cells with cells given siRNA against ACT1, TRAF6 or TNFAIP3.

citations.title: The deubiquitinase A20 mediates feedback inhibition of interleukin-17 receptor signaling.
IL-17RC is critically required to maintain baseline A20 production to repress JNK isoform-dependent tumor-specific proliferation.

novelty.note: I searched for A20/TNFAIP3 feedback on IL-17 receptor signaling, for ACT1–TRAF6-dependent JNK activation in fibroblasts, and for JNK1-isoform-specific IL-17 responses with c-Jun kinase assays. The ACT1/TRAF6-dependent MAPK (including JNK) arm and A20's restraint of IL-17-induced JNK phosphorylation are published, including in human fibroblast-like synoviocytes and A20-deficient MEFs (PMID 23737552), and A20 levels have been linked to differential JNK1 versus JNK2 activation downstream of IL-17RC (PMID 28562353). However, no retrieved source resolves the IL-17-induced signal to JNK1 specifically by isoform-selective immunoprecipitation/kinase activity in human IL-17-responsive cells, nor combines ACT1, TRAF6 and TNFAIP3 knockdowns against that isoform-specific readout, so the mechanism is established in general but the specific prediction is not.

hypotheses.statement: ERK activity positively regulates (promotes) the buildup of CDK2 activity that precedes S-phase entry, with the cumulative time a cell spends in the ERK-on state setting when CDK2 activity rises.
hypotheses.mechanism: In MCF-10A cells, ERK pulse length rises sharply about 12 h before S-phase entry only in the sister cell that commits, and time spent in the ERK-on state, rather than pulse number, tracks the S-phase decision (albeck2013:findings:010, :012). Independently, CDK2 activity in MCF10A cells stays low for about 8 h after mitogen restimulation and then builds up at variable times; S phase begins when the reporter ratio reaches about one, and some cells never build up CDK2 activity (spencer2013:findings:003). Both readouts mark the same variable-timing S-phase commitment step in the same cell type, which implies that ERK-on time is an upstream determinant of when CDK2 activity starts to build up.
hypotheses.prediction: In single cells co-imaged for ERK and CDK2 activity, an increase in ERK-on time (longer pulses) should precede the onset of CDK2 activity buildup. Reducing ERK output with low EGF or MEK inhibition should delay CDK2 buildup and enlarge the fraction of CDK2-low cells. Acute CDK1/2 inhibition should not change the ERK pulse pattern, which would show the dependence runs from ERK to CDK2.
hypotheses.test: Make MCF10A cells that express both an ERK FRET reporter (EKAR-EV) and the DHB-based CDK2 activity reporter, and image them by time-lapse after restimulation from mitogen starvation. Titrate EGF, and add a MEK inhibitor (PD) at defined times before and after the CDK2 rise. Quantify the timing and slope of CDK2 Cyt/Nuc buildup against each cell's preceding ERK-on fraction. In a reciprocal arm, measure ERK pulse statistics after adding a CDK1/2 inhibitor.

citations.title: Temporal integration of mitogen history in mother cells controls proliferation of daughter cells.
Predicting Individual Cell Division Events from Single-Cell ERK and Akt Dynamics
CDK2 activity crosstalk on the ERK kinase translocation reporter can be resolved computationally.
Mitogen signaling strength and duration can control cell cycle decisions.

novelty.note: I searched for ERK–CDK2 co-imaging, ERK-on time or integrated ERK and the timing of the CDK2 rise, and the effect of MEK inhibition on CDK2 buildup in MCF10A cells. Min et al. 2020 showed that short MEK-inhibitor pulses in mother cells lower the share of daughter cells that build up CDK2 activity and delay their commitment, and a bioRxiv preprint cites earlier work showing that time-integrated ERK partly predicts when cells enter S phase. A 2024 Cell Systems study found that CDK2 inhibition leaves real phospho-ERK unchanged. None of these sources imaged ERK and CDK2 in the same cells to show that ERK-on time sets when CDK2 activity starts to rise, so the general link is published but this specific prediction is not.

hypotheses.statement: SYK kinase activity is required upstream of CSF2 (GM-CSF) expression, such that dectin-1/SYK signalling in dendritic cells drives CSF2 induction both in the DCs themselves and in the T cells they prime.
hypotheses.mechanism: Curdlan stimulation of BMDCs induces maturation and a cytokine program including IL-23, and both this program and the resulting accumulation of IL-17-producing T cells strictly require SYK in the DCs (leibundgutlandmann2007:findings:002, leibundgutlandmann2007:findings:004). Independently, IL-23 exposure is what renders Th17 cells pathogenic and co-expressing GM-CSF, with IL-23-induced BLIMP1 acting directly at the csf2 locus together with RORγt and STAT3 (gaffen2014:findings:010, gaffen2014:findings:020). Because the SYK-dependent DC output contains the very signal that licenses csf2 transcription, SYK activity should sit directly upstream of CSF2 expression in this axis rather than merely correlating with it.
hypotheses.prediction: Loss or pharmacological inhibition of SYK during dectin-1 stimulation should abolish Csf2 transcript and GM-CSF protein induction in the stimulated dendritic cells, and DCs lacking SYK activity should fail to elicit GM-CSF from co-cultured antigen-specific CD4+ T cells, while GM-CSF output is restored by adding exogenous IL-23 to the SYK-blocked cultures.
hypotheses.test: Stimulate bone marrow-derived dendritic cells with curdlan in the presence or absence of a SYK inhibitor (or after SYK knockdown by siRNA), and measure Csf2 mRNA by RT-qPCR and GM-CSF protein by ELISA at 6-24 h; in parallel, co-culture the same DCs with antigen-specific CD4+ T cells and quantify T cell GM-CSF by ELISA and intracellular cytokine flow cytometry, with and without recombinant IL-23 add-back to test whether the SYK requirement for CSF2 is bypassed downstream. A chromatin immunoprecipitation or reporter assay on the csf2 locus in SYK-inhibited versus control cells distinguishes a transcriptional requirement from a secretion defect.

citations.title: Syk signaling in dendritic cells orchestrates innate resistance to systemic fungal infection.
Fungal sensing by dectin-1 directs the non-pathogenic polarization of T(H)17 cells through balanced type I IFN responses in human DCs.

novelty.note: I searched three ways — dectin-1/SYK signalling and CSF2/GM-CSF induction in dendritic cells, curdlan-stimulated DCs priming GM-CSF-producing T cells, and the Candida/CARD9–IL-23–GM-CSF axis. The closest published work (PMID 25033445) does establish SYK in DCs as strictly upstream of GM-CSF output via SYK-dependent IL-23p19, which is the core logic of the hypothesis, but the GM-CSF comes from NK cells rather than from the DCs themselves or from primed CD4+ T cells, and no IL-23 add-back bypass of SYK blockade for CSF2 is reported. A human dectin-1/TH17 study (PMID 36456734) shows curdlan-stimulated DCs polarise TH17 subsets that differ in CSF2 expression and uses SYK silencing in DCs, but only for the IFN-β arm, never testing DC-intrinsic Csf2 or T cell GM-CSF; so the mechanism is partly published while the specific prediction is not.

hypotheses.statement: mTORC1 activity negatively regulates RAF (Raf-1) activation, so inhibiting mTORC1 activates Raf-1 kinase in a Ras-dependent manner.
hypotheses.mechanism: In MCF7 cells, rapamycin inhibition of mTORC1 increased Raf-1 Ser338 phosphorylation, and the resulting ERK activation was blocked by dominant-negative Ras (N17) or MEK inhibition, placing the effect at the Ras-Raf1 step. Raf-1 activity depends on engaging activated Ras at the plasma membrane. In HEK293 cells, inhibiting c-Raf with GW-5074 eliminated MEK and ERK activity, so Raf is the required node through which a change in mTORC1 activity would reach MEK/ERK.
hypotheses.prediction: Rapamycin or raptor knockdown should increase Raf-1 Ser338 phosphorylation, Raf-1 association with Ras-GTP, and Raf-1 kinase activity measured in vitro. These increases should be abolished by Ras N17. ERK activation induced by mTORC1 inhibition should be prevented by pharmacological Raf inhibition.
hypotheses.test: Treat MCF7 or HEK293 cells with rapamycin or raptor siRNA, with or without Ras N17 expression or GW-5074. Measure p-Raf-1 S338, p-MEK, p-ERK and p-S6 by western blot. Immunoprecipitate Raf-1 for an in vitro kinase assay using recombinant MEK1 as substrate. Use Ras-binding-domain pulldown, or co-immunoprecipitation of Raf-1 with Ras, to quantify Ras-Raf-1 engagement.

citations.title: Inhibition of mTORC1 leads to MAPK pathway activation through a PI3K-dependent feedback loop in human cancer.
Opposite feedback from mTORC1 to H-ras and K-ras4B downstream of SREBP1.
mTORC1 inhibition induces pain via IRS-1-dependent feedback activation of ERK.

novelty.note: I searched three ways: the plain-language mechanism (mTORC1 inhibition relieving a feedback that activates Raf), the entities together (rapamycin + Raf-1 Ser338 + Ras N17 + raptor knockdown), and the prediction (Raf-1 activity/Ras engagement increase after mTORC1 inhibition, and refutation-style queries for Raf-independent rapamycin-induced ERK). The explanation is published: Carracedo et al. (JCI 2008) report that mTORC1 inhibition activates the MAPK pathway through an S6K-PI3K-Ras-dependent feedback loop, including rapamycin-induced Ser338-Raf1 phosphorylation and loss of ERK induction with dominant-negative Ras; Posada et al. independently show Raptor or S6K1 knockdown raises Ras activity/nanoclustering and pERK, and Melemedjian et al. show mTORC1-inhibition feedback ERK activation via IRS-1 in a different system. No source was found that tested and negated Raf dependence, so the status is established rather than partial or refuted, although the in vitro Raf-1 kinase-activity and Ras-GTP pulldown measurements specified in the prediction were not found as such.

hypotheses.statement: RAF positively regulates mTORC1 kinase activity in mitogen (PMA/EGF)-stimulated cells, through MEK/ERK/RSK-dependent phosphorylation of Raptor.
hypotheses.mechanism: PMA- and EGF-induced Raptor phosphorylation depends on MEK and RSK, and ERK1/2 also directly phosphorylate Raptor. Phosphorylation-deficient Raptor mutants reduce mTORC1 kinase activity toward 4E-BP1, and MEK inhibitors completely inhibit mTORC1 kinase activity. Because c-Raf inhibition eliminates MEK and ERK activity, Raf sits upstream of this Raptor-dependent input to mTORC1.
hypotheses.prediction: Raf inhibition or knockdown should reduce PMA- or EGF-induced Raptor phosphorylation and mTORC1 activity in vitro toward GST-4E-BP1. This reduction should not occur in cells expressing the Raptor phosphorylation-deficient (3A/S3A) mutant. Insulin-stimulated mTORC1 activity should be largely unaffected.
hypotheses.test: In HEK293 cells expressing wild-type or 3A Raptor, pretreat with GW-5074 or c-Raf/B-Raf siRNA, then stimulate with PMA, EGF or insulin. Immunoprecipitate Raptor and immunoblot with the RXRXXpS/T phospho-motif antibody. Measure mTORC1 kinase activity in immunoprecipitates using GST-4E-BP1 and [γ-32P]ATP, alongside cellular p-4E-BP1 Thr37/46 and p-ERK.

citations.title: RSK regulates activated BRAF signalling to mTORC1 and promotes melanoma growth.
Oncogenic MAPK signaling stimulates mTORC1 activity by promoting RSK-mediated raptor phosphorylation.
ERK1/2 phosphorylate Raptor to promote Ras-dependent activation of mTOR complex 1 (mTORC1).

novelty.note: I searched for the mechanism in words (MEK/ERK/RSK-dependent Raptor phosphorylation activating mTORC1), for the entities together (Raf/B-Raf + Raptor + mTORC1 + 4E-BP1 + RSK), and for the prediction (Raf inhibition or knockdown reducing mitogen-induced Raptor phosphorylation with insulin unaffected). The MEK/ERK/RSK-to-Raptor input to mTORC1 is firmly published (RSK phosphorylates Raptor on RXRXXS/T sites; ERK1/2 phosphorylate Ser8/696/863; phospho-deficient Raptor lowers mTOR activity toward 4E-BP1), and one study reports that oncogenic Ras and Raf constitutively activate mTOR with RSK partly required — so the Raf-upstream positioning is anticipated in the oncogenic-Raf setting. However, I found no work that directly tests Raf inhibition or c-Raf/B-Raf knockdown as the requirement for PMA/EGF-induced Raptor phosphorylation and in vitro mTORC1 activity, nor the epistasis with the Raptor 3A/S3A mutant and insulin specificity, so the specific prediction remains unaddressed.
